It sounds like he has a chance to continue handling a high-volume workload in the coming weeks, though the game script could hurt him if he fails to increase his passing game usage.

items.name: Jauan Jennings
items.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Jennings missed the past two games with the calf injury. A full practice today puts him on track to return for a revenge game against the 49ers. Jordan Addison is sidelined with a thumb injury, meaning Jennings will likely return to the No. 2 receiver role. He is worth a look in deeper formats, though he’s still a high-risk WR5 for Week 11.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Hockenson missed Week 10 with the wrist issue. He was also dealing with a chest injury, though the team didn’t bother listing that today. Hockenson will be reunited with Kirk Cousins on Sunday, and the Vikings will be without Jordan Addison. That could free up a few extra targets for the tight end. If healthy, Hockenson will be in the TE2 streaming conversation.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Williams would not normally be a name to monitor, but he tallied seven targets in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to Buffalo. Williams was forced to take on more work after Omar Cooper Jr. went down with an ankle injury. We suspect the Jets would lean on their 12-personnel alignment if Williams and Cooper are out for Week 11. That would finally get first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq on the field more.

items.name: Taliese Fuaga
items.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

items.name: Talanoa Hufanga
items.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is practicing on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Hufanga nearly played pre-bye in Week 9 against the Panthers, but he was unable to do so. He has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in Week 5 against the Chargers. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Riley Moss (concussion) are also practicing. Check back on Friday for their official statuses.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Douglas is a little banged up coming out of Week 10, but a limited practice means he’s still on track to suit up this week. Douglas caught three of his eight targets for 71 yards last week. He has hit 70 yards in three of his past four appearances. Barring a setback, Douglas will be a boom/bust WR3 for Week 11.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Saints coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson suffered the chest injury in Week 10 against the Panthers. The fact that he is limited is a great sign for his availability against the Bears. Tyson belongs in fantasy football lineups on a weekly basis at this point.

items.name: Christian Benford
items.headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Benford is the Bills’ No. 1 perimeter cornerback. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) and LB Dorian Williams (calf) were also sidelined to begin Week 11. The Bills face the Dolphins this weekend. Bills C Connor McGovern (neck) is practicing in full.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the ankle issue for a few weeks. We expect the same for Week 11, though he hasn’t been a strong fantasy option at any point this year, healthy or not. He will remain in the WR4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants on Sunday.

items.name: Keon Coleman
items.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Coleman should be able to face Miami this weekend. The Bills will likely employ a run-heavy approach, though with Kyle McCord starting on the other side. Coleman is only a boom-bust FLEX at this time.

items.name: Antoine Winfield
items.headline: Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Winfield missed a handful of games earlier this year because of a rib injury. A DNP today puts him at risk of missing more time with a new issue. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters they will find out more about Winfield’s injury over the next two days. EGDE Yaya Diaby (knee) got in a limtied practice. He has a shot at returning for Week 11 after missing just one game.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Kincaid played through the ankle injury last week, catching two passes for 58 yards. The thumb injury is new and likely happened in-game. Kincaid has successfully played through multiple injuries this season, so we are optimistic about his availability for the Bills’ Week 11 game against the Dolphins, though Buffalo may be able to run out the clock with ease on Sunday.

items.name: Kerby Joseph
items.headline: Lions activated S Kerby Joseph (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
items.analysis: Joseph was designated to return from the PUP list exactly three weeks ago, so they had to activate him today. He got in a full practice last week but did not travel to Germany with the team. Practicing in full once again, Joseph looks likely to make his 2026 debut in Week 11.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Last Monday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters that Ferguson would likely miss “multiple weeks.” We do not expect him to play in Week 11 against the Titans. Check back on Friday for an official update.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: Joey Porter (ankle/foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Fellow starting CB DaRon Bland will miss time with injuries in both ankles, but at least Porter’s health is trending upward. Cowboys OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), OG Tyler Booker (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Skattebo returned to action last week after missing one game with the hamstring injury. He ran for 78 yards and scored twice while adding 44 yards on three grabs. Whether they want to or not, the Giants are treating Skattebo like a workhorse back once again. He is pushing to the top of the RB2 ranks heading into his Week 11 matchup with Jacksonville.

items.name: DaRon Bland
items.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said DaRon Bland (ankle) will “miss some time.”
items.analysis: Bland entered the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers with a left ankle injury. Unfortunately, he suffered a high-ankle sprain in his right ankle mid-game and could miss “the bulk” of the remaining schedule. Bland’s absence will make this weak defense even weaker.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Tuten has been playing through the pair of injuries for the past two weeks. He was held out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday last week, so a limited session today is a notable improvement. Coming off a 29-touch outing, Tuten is flirting with an RB1 ranking heading into his Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Rodriguez has been playing through the hand issue for a few weeks. This time should be no different. Coming off a four-carry outing in a blowout win over the Titans, Rodriguez is tumbling into the RB4 ranks for Week 11 against the Giants.

items.name: Kyler Gordon
items.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Gordon missed time earlier this season with a calf issue. He played in Week 9 before the team’s bye but got banged up. Head coach Ben Johnson called him day-to-day earlier this week. Gordon has four sacks, two forced fumbles, and one pass breakup this year. Losing him would make this an easier matchup for Tyler Shough and the Saints.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Monangai has been out since Week 4 because of the toe issue. He returned to practice late last week but wasn’t ready to suit up after just one session. A full practice today all but guarantee he will be on the field this week. Monangai was splitting work with D’Andre Swift before suffering the toe injury. We suspect his role will be scaled back in his return to action, keeping him in the RB3 ranks despite the good matchup.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: It’s unclear if Spears aggravated his knee issue on Sunday or if this is just a maintenance day. Spears missed three weeks because of the knee issue before returning to action in week 10. He was held to five touches. Healthy or not, he is not on the fantasy radar ahead of Week 11.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Montgomery is good to go after logging three full practices this week. With Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out for Week 11, Montgomery will likely return to a three-down role. Facing a toothless Colts team, he is back in the RB2 mix after missing over a month.

items.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
items.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Wednesday.
items.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, this is the first time Stribling has worked off to the side at practice since injuring his ankle in Week 1. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant, but this is still a great sign for his availability in the coming weeks. Stribling must be rostered in 10-team leagues.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) returned to practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Tate missed Week 8 because of the shoulder issue. He got the bye week to recover but still wasn’t able to suit up in Week 10. Robert Saleh told reporters on Monday that he is hoping Tate is ready to go for Sunday’s game. Even a limited practice today puts him on track to play. With Wan’Dale Robinson on IR, Tate will return to an elite target share, even if he’s not fully healthy. He will be in the WR3 mix if the team clears him for Week 11.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Waller is sometimes given Wednesdays often, so this could just be precautionary. Panthers backup TE Tommy Tremble (knee) was also listed as a non-participant. Hopefully, one of them is good to go for this week’s game against the Ravens.

items.name: Mike Jackson
items.headline: Mike Jackson (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters that he thinks Jackson, his team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, is “ready” to return. He will slightly upgrade the Panthers’ secondary if so. Jackson has been sidelined since injuring his groin in late September.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Panthers listed Brooks as a full participant for two practices last week before amending his participation to limited at the end of the week. We doubt they’ll do that again. Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters today that he thinks Brooks is “ready.” He can be speculatively stashed in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young (foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Young has played through lower-body injuries for much of the season already. Late in October, coach Dave Canales admitted that Young’s knee issue may be limiting his mobility. While we fully expect Young to play this week, he may be a little less likely to scramble than he normally would. Regardless, it doesn’t alter his ranking much. Today, Canales said Young’s “foot was sore coming out of the game Sunday, but it’s been getting better and better.”

items.name: Danielle Hunter
items.headline: Texans ruled out Danielle Hunter (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Hunter will now miss his second game due to a hamstring injury. He is replaced in the lineup by veteran pass rusher Jadaveon Clowney. Fortunately, Will Anderson returned from his ankle injury last week. Kamari Lassiter (wrist) is expected to play.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Texans ruled out Marvin Harrison (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Unfortunately, the Texans’ mid-season acquisition will miss another game. Harrison’s absence helpfully condenses the pass-catching corps for fantasy football purposes, though. Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson will likely lead their position group, followed by Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Texans ruled out Woody Marks (concussion) for Week 11 against the Colts.
items.analysis: David Montgomery (groin) is expected to return for tomorrow’s game. Emari Demercardo will serve as Montgomery’s backup. The Texans’ run game has been unable to establish itself as a reliable unit, but Montgomery’s workload and matchup against the Colts’ defense put him in the RB2 tier. The Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Should Marks return to action, he will likely be relegated to PPR FLEX status.

items.name: Mason McCormick
items.headline: Steelers placed LG Mason McCormick (ankle) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports this morning that McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle but not a fracture. That gives him a shot at returning in the postseason, though he will miss at least the rest of the regular season. Spencer Anderson took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and will likely do so going forward.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Steelers designated Michael Pittman (foot) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Wilson has been out for exactly a month because of the finger issue. He will return to practice today and has a chance at suiting up for Sunday’s game against the Eagles. Wilson has six grabs for 134 yards and two touchdowns before leaving Week 6 early with the finger injury. He is worth a stash in deeper leagues.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Steelers designated Michael Pittman (foot) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Roman Wilson was also designated to return. Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters earlier this week that he was hopeful both Pittman and Wilson would be able to return this week. Getting back on the practice field is a step in the right direction. Pittsburgh now has 21 days to officially activate both wideouts from IR. The return of either one will likely remove an already-slumping Germie Bernard from the FLEX mix.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Bowers unsuccessfully tried to return to the Raiders’ Week 11 game against the Seahawks multiple times after injuring his ankle. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak described the issue as a “significant” injury, but not as bad as the team initially thought. In his first season as a head coach, Kubiak has already downplayed various injuries multiple times. Bowers’ practice participation will likely give us a clearer picture of his injury than Kubiak will. Bowers’ fantasy managers should make backup plans at this time. After practice, Kubiak told reporters that Bowers remains day-to-day and said he doesn’t need to practice to play on Sunday against the Broncos.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Murray was out last week because of the hamstring issue and will likely miss Week 11 versus the 49ers. Carson Wentz will back up Kirk Cousins on Sunday.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will not be placed on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Addison underwent successful surgery on his thumb after suffering a “freak” injury in practice last week. He is still expected to miss multiple games, but not placing him on IR means the Vikings don’t foresee him missing an entire month. He will be out for Week 11 and likely Week 12, but fantasy managers should still try to hold onto him ahead of the fantasy postseason. Myles Price and Tai Felton will be in the mix for extra targets if Jauan Jennings remains out this week.

items.name: Bo Richter
items.headline: Vikings placed EDGE Bo Richter on injured reserve with a foot injury.
items.analysis: Richter is a capable special teams player. Hopefully, he can return later this year. The Vikings also signed WR Jeshaun Jones to the active roster and WR D’Wayne Eskridge to the practice squad.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Evans is still dealing with the Achilles tendinitis issue that has been bothering him for weeks. He looks unlikely to suit up in Week 11 against the Vikings. With Deebo Samuel healthy and Keenan Allen in the mix, the 49ers can afford not to rush Evans back.

items.name: Anthony Gould
items.headline: Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable for Week 11 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Gould was upgraded to a full practice on Wednesday before receiving the questionable tag. We expect him to suit up tomorrow. He led the team with four targets last week, though Gould only turned that into two grabs for 28 yards. The Colts simply don’t have a wide receiver worth a look in even deep fantasy leagues.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable for Week 11 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Gardner did not practice at all this week, which usually guarantees that a player will not suit up. However, the Colts playing on Thursday night instead of Sunday makes things a bit murkier. The team has already ruled out Charvarius Ward because of a knee injury. Expect C.J. Stroud to keep cooking this week, even if Gardner manages to suit up.

items.name: Bernhard Raimann
items.headline: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) will not play in Week 11 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Right tackle Jalen Travis is also out with a knee injury. That’s both of Indy’s starting tackles on ice for their date with the Texans. While Houston’s defense has been one of the most disappointing units of the season, this looks like a get-right spot for Demeco Ryans’ squad.

items.name: Tyrell Shavers
items.headline: Bills activated WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
items.analysis: Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs last year and began the season on the PUP list. He was active for all 17 games last year and played a mix of offense and special teams. Shavers caught 23 passes for 245 yards and a touchdown in 2025. He will mix in as a depth option for Buffalo over the second half of the season.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Chris Bell (knee) is considered “day-to-day.”
items.analysis: Bell was playing through some soreness in his surgically repaired knee until he was forced to sit last week. He was suited up for practice today, though we expect it to be a limited session for the rookie. The Dolphins will need to see how he responds to a week of practice before making a decision on his Week 11 availability.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he feels “pretty good” about Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) returning for Week 11 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: The bigger headline is that Sirianni said this about DeVonta Smith as well. Wicks was making the occasional splash play before going down with the ankle injury. That, however, was while Jalen Hurts was healthy. We don’t expect him to be a consistent fantasy option with Joe Milton now under center for the Eagles.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he feels “pretty good” about DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returning for Week 11 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Sirianni also included Dontayvion Wicks in his comments. Smith hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. In the midst of a lost season, the Eagles almost certainly didn’t feel the need to rush him back. He will return to a team down to its third-string quarterback in Joe Milton. Smith will be in the WR2 mix if he’s cleared for Week 11.

items.name: Joe Milton
items.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni announced Joe Milton will start in Week 11 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Milton struggled in the Eagles’ loss to the Giants before their bye. Maybe an extra week of prep will result in a better performance, though we don’t have our hopes up. Milton threw for 169 scoreless yards on 34 attempts. He took seven sacks and lost a fumble. On the bright side, Milton added 64 yards with his legs. That will keep him in the QB2 mix for Superflex purposes this week, but nothing more.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Ken Walker (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: It’s looking more and more like Walker will miss a second straight game with his groin issue. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Tuesday that he wouldn’t be surprised if Walker sat again in Week 11 against the Cardinals. “He had a sore groin (last week). It’s getting better,” head coach Andy Reid said. “We just don’t want to do something stupid. ... He’s feeling better.” Emmett Johnson, fresh off a monster outing in Week 10, would get another start and profile as a top-5 fantasy option. Johnson will face a Cardinals defense allowing the fifth lowest fantasy points per opportunity to running backs this season.

items.name: Frank Reich
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said offensive coordinator Frank Reich would continue calling plays.
items.analysis: Glenn was asked about whether he had considered switching play callers after the Jets went nine straight quarters without a touchdown. “I have a lot of confidence in Frank,” Glenn said. Since Week 7, the Jets rank 19th in EPA per play and 11th in offensive success rate. They have a league-low 38 percent red zone touchdown rate on the season. This week they play an improving Chargers defense.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: NFL insider Dianna Russini reports Brandon Aiyuk passed the 49ers’ physical.
items.analysis: “He’s 100% healthy right now, in shape, and working out full force,” Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk’s agent, told Russini. Passing the team’s physical was a key step in the two sides parting ways after years of conflict. Aiyuk reportedly hopes to sign with another team once the 49ers release him. Whether that happens in the coming weeks is anyone’s guess. Aiyuk had been linked to the Commanders in the summer before a series of questionable social media posts from Aiyuk squelched those rumors.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Cooper, who picked up his latest injury last week against the Bills, appears to be a long shot for Week 11 against the Chargers. That would leave Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the clear top targets for Geno Smith, if Smith is able to play through his own ankle injury. Wilson and Mitchell last week combined for 87 percent of the Jets’ air yards and 51 percent of the team’s targets.

items.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
items.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season.
items.analysis: Robinson’s Week 10 ankle injury will end a disappointing 2026 campaign in a low-octane Tennessee offense. Robinson over nine games managed 32 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He had just three games with more than 50 receiving yards. His absence will open up more snaps and routes from Xavier Restrepo, while Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate — who could be back soon from a shoulder issue — remain the team’s top two wideouts.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Fox Sports’ Greg Auman said Mayfield “came out in street clothes, shoes, no wrap or boot on foot” while Jalon Daniels took first-team reps ahead of Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys. If Mayfield is unable to log a practice tomorrow or Friday, Daniels will get another start for the Bucs in a plus matchup against Dallas. Daniels will be usable in superflex formats, while Bucs pass catchers will be nothing more than desperation options.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would not say if Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11.
items.analysis: Smith suffered the ankle injury in last week’s loss to Buffalo and appears to be iffy for Sunday against the Chargers. Smith on Wednesday was a limited participant in practice, which is usually good news for a player’s Sunday availability. If Smith is sidelined against the Bolts, look for Cade Klubnik to get the start. Klubnik last week completed 11 of his 20 attempts for 137 yards and an interception. His aDOT was 11.3, the third highest of Week 10.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan will see “heavy usage” in Week 11 against the Texans.
items.analysis: A week after the Colts went ultra run-heavy in a win over the Dolphins — they were 9.3 percent below their expected pass rate — Boyd anticipates a similar approach on Thursday night against Houston. Taylor and McGowan over the past two games have split carries, 29-18, while Taylor takes on almost all the pass-catching work out of the backfield. “It doesn’t matter what I envision. It’s effective,” Taylor said of sharing the backfield workload with McGowan. “It helped us get a win. If we gotta win doing that and that’s what it takes, then I’m all for it. Seth has been growing each and every single day.” McGowan over the past two weeks has the highest EPA per rush in the NFL while Taylor ranks 44th. Unless the Colts face runaway negative game script against the Texans, look for McGowan to see around a dozen touches. Houston ranks 14th in running back fantasy points per opportunity allowed.

items.name: Christian Parker
items.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker will cede play-calling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.
items.analysis: After getting thrashed by Brock Purdy and the 49ers in Week 10, the Cowboys now allow the second highest yards per play and the highest EPA per play. The Dallas defense has given up a touchdown on 31 percent of their opponents’ offensive possessions this season, the third highest rate in the NFL. Pettine will try to stop the bleeding beginning this week against a Titans offense that has shown signs of life in recent weeks. Pettine was last a defensive coordinator with the Packers in 2020, when Green Bay allowed the fewest points in the league and the fifth fewest yards.

items.name: Robert Hainsey
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Jaguars C Robert Hainsey (knee) is considered week to week.
items.analysis: Jacksonville could be without its starting center for at least a few weeks. Fowler said Hainsey’s knee issue is likely not the season-ending variety though. Through Week 10, the Jaguars rank 18th in run block win rate and 12th in pass block win rate. The Jags this week take on a Giants defense that ranks 23rd in sack rate.

items.name: Fred Johnson
items.headline: Chiefs signed Fred Johnson, formerly of the Eagles, to the team’s practice squad.
items.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Johnson would likely be bumped up to KC’s active roster in the coming days. Johnson could help the Chiefs plug some holes while they deal with offensive line injuries. The Chiefs this season rank sixth in run block win rate and 22nd in pass block win rate.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said he’s “hoping” Carnell Tate (shoulder) returns for Sunday’s game against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Tate last played in Week 7. Saleh made the disclosure at Monday morning’s press conference, one day before Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) landed on injured reserve. Tate’s return would be just in the nick of time, as the Titans have a dream defensive matchup and Cam Ward is suddenly playing the best football of his career. Especially with six teams on bye and Robinson sidelined, Tate would immediately return to the WR2 ranks. We will get our first Titans practice report of the week on Wednesday.

items.name: Adrian Martinez
items.headline: Seahawks released Adrian Martinez from the practice squad.
items.analysis: Martinez was added for scout team reps after Sam Darnold (quad) was injured two weeks ago. The Seahawks have a bye in Week 11, so Martinez’s release indicates Darnold is at least trending to practice after the bye.

items.name: Anthony Gould
items.headline: Anthony Gould (toe) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Gould is dealing with a toe injury and was listed as limited for the Colts’ first two practice reports of the week. He finished the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins and starts out limited, indicating he is in line to play Thursday against the Texans. Gould is suddenly the Colts’ starting slot receiver but should only be rostered in 14-team leagues with deep benches.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) did not practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: Both Gardner and Charvarius Ward (knee) were listed as DNP on Tuesday after DNPs on Monday. They suffered the injuries in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins and are trending out for a Thursday game this week. Texans receivers get a boost for Week 11 against the Colts.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot strain.
items.analysis: He didn’t go as far as to rule out Mayfield this week, but between the Buccaneers signing Cooper Rush to the practice squad and elevating Easton Stick to the 53-man roster, they have already signaled that there’s a real chance Mayfield misses Week 11. Rapoport said it “seems to be trending towards” Jalon Daniels suiting up under center for the Bucs against Detroit on Sunday.

items.name: Jalon Daniels
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports it “seems to be trending towards” Jalon Daniels playing this week.
items.analysis: Rapoport said that he wouldn’t rule out Baker Mayfield, who is dealing with a foot strain, but he phrased it in a way that didn’t exactly inspire a ton of confidence in Mayfield playing. Daniels can be picked up off waiver wires in superflex leagues ahead of a reasonable matchup against the Lions.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes “it would be a surprise” if Drake Maye (ankle) played again this year.
items.analysis: Rapoport said that Maye would not play for the “foreseeable future” and noted that though the Patriots have not confirmed that Maye fractured his ankle, almost all of the reporting points to that reality. We’re all waiting for the Patriots to actually confirm this, which won’t happen any time soon because they’re on bye, but Maye can be dropped with little fear in shallow redraft leagues.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if Kenneth Walker sat in Week 11 to make sure that his groin is fully healed.
items.analysis: The crux of this appears to be that Emmett Johnson did so well that there’s no need to rush Walker back to the field. We’ll see how the practice reports trend, but a pop-up groin injury on Friday to a rule-out Saturday never felt like something that assured Walker was playing in Week 11. This will be one to monitor on the practice reports all week, especially with six teams on bye.

items.name: Ronnie Bell
items.headline: Cardinals signed WR Ronnie Bell to their practice squad.
items.analysis: That makes five practice-squad wideouts for the Cardinals, with Bell joining Zay Jones (who was active last week), Phillip Dorsett (really, that one), James Proche II and Shedrick Jackson. And we’re not sure that those five are any worse than the four that are on their active roster. It’s far from an ideal situation as Arizona tries to evaluate Carson Beck in the desert.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be sidelined for Week 11’s TNF game after back-to-back missed practices. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell should be the main fantasy beneficiaries of Harrison’s absence. This will make two weeks in a row on the shelf for Harrison and no practices since ahead of Week 9’s game, making it feel dicey that he’ll be able to get active for Week 12 as well.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: His ruleout on Wednesday is basically just a formality at this point. David Montgomery looks likely to lead the Texans backfield against the Colts on Thursday night. Marks should have a real chance to suit up for Week 12.

items.name: Daniel Carlson
items.headline: Dolphins signed K Daniel Carlson to their practice squad.
items.analysis: With Zane Gonzalez banished on Monday, Carlson projects to be Miami’s kicker this week against the Bills based on the fact that he’s currently the only kicker on either the roster or the practice squad. The 31-year-old went 8-of-12 with the Saints before being waived earlier in November.

items.name: Jamree Kromah
items.headline: Browns claimed EDGE Jamree Kromah off waivers from the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Kromah, who played 27 snaps for the Bears in Weeks 6 and 7, managed to get on the field for just two snaps as a Dolphin. Now on his third team of the season, he’s trying to speedrun the Josh Johnson career.

items.name: Jaydon Blue
items.headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue from their practice squad to their active roster.
items.analysis: This is the second time Blue has been added to the active roster. He’s played eight offensive snaps this year. Much like the character Blue in Degrassi , with Saquon Barkley healthy and the health of the Eagles running back room trending in a better direction, Blue can be safely cordoned off as a sideplot at this point in fantasy leagues.

items.name: Xavier Restrepo
items.headline: Titans promoted WR Xavier Restrepo from the practice squad.
items.analysis: He’ll take Wan’Dale Robinson’s place. Restrepo caught three balls for 31 yards last week as an elevation and is worth monitoring and perhaps even picking up in deeper leagues given how the Titans offense seems to be lurching towards fantasy competence.

items.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
items.headline: Titans placed WR Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four games. Even in moderate-sized leagues, Robinson is likely a cut candidate at this point given how his playing time and target share have been reduced. This should help out Carnell Tate (once he returns from his shoulder injury) and Elic Ayomanor in the target department.

items.name: Harrison Mevis
items.headline: Ravens released K Harrison Mevis from the practice squad.
items.analysis: He’ll be free to ply his wares again as it appears Riley Patterson has taken hold of the Ravens’ kicking gig. Mevis, 24, will continue to wander the kicking tryout circuit for another chance.

items.name: Jordan Phillips
items.headline: Dolphins placed DT Jordan Phillips (biceps) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: He tore his biceps and will miss the remainder of the season. The 2025 fifth-rounder — and notably not the older defensive tackle also named Jordan Phillips — had played 326 snaps this year with a 57.4 PFF grade as an interior lineman.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) is “trending in the right direction” of playing on Thursday Night.
items.analysis: He officially got in a second-straight full practice on Tuesday. Montgomery should see the vast majority of the Texans run attack volume if he’s able to go, relegating Emari Demercado back to the bench outside of a few third-down plays here or there. It’s hard to trust that anything good will come of this given how the team has played this year, but Montgomery on volume would fit in as a low-end RB2 on a week with six teams on bye.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the team expects TJ Hockenson (wrist/chest) “to progress” ahead of Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: We’ll be monitoring practice participation for Hockenson after he missed all three practices last week. Should he miss another game, Gavin Bartholomew caught a touchdown in his absence and would be a reasonable TE2.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Commanders designated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Ben Standig reports that he’s expecting Croskey-Merritt to be active for Monday night barring a setback. We’re expecting a pass-happy Commanders offense as they try to keep pace with Cincinnati’s high-flying offense, but given how many teams are on bye there’s certainly worse FLEX starts out there than a returning “Bill.”

items.name: Luther Burden
items.headline: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Luther Burden III has cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol.
items.analysis: Burden had the Bears’ bye week to recover from the head injury, and it looks like he’ll be a full go for Week 11 against the Saints — barring a setback, of course. Burden has been an elite producer of late, piling up 283 receiving yards over his past three outings while being targeted on a strong 30 percent of his pass routes. Burden over that span has averaged nearly 11 yards after the catch per reception, the third highest mark in the NFL.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was seen practicing Tuesday.
items.analysis: Montgomery looks to be in line for a full workload in Thursday night’s game against the Colts, who have struggled mightily against the rush in recent weeks. Woody Marks, who sustained a concussion in Week 10 against the Browns, will very likely miss Thursday night as he works through the league’s concussion protocol. Montgomery will be a floor-based RB2/3 against the Colts.

items.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
items.headline: Texans placed Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Al-Shaair has been playing through a serious groin issue for weeks. He was sidelined in Week 10 against the Browns and will now miss extended time. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander said Al-Shaair is “likely to miss more than four games but has not been ruled out for the season.” The Texans this season have allowed the 13th highest EPA per play and the tenth lowest offensive success rate. Their defense will be a little more vulnerable with Al-Shaair sidelined.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’s “hopeful” Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman, Jr. (foot) can return in Week 11.
items.analysis: Wilson and Pittman, after being sidelined for about a month, could return to a Steelers offense in desperate need of pass-catching help. Before his finger injury, Wilson was interesting for fantasy purposes, seeing 14 percent of the team’s targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards with a solid 23 percent targets per route rate. Pittman, meanwhile, was targeted on a lowly 13 percent of his routes over the season’s first few games. Their return could be a major issue for Germie Bernard, who’s had three straight quiet games, including a zero in Week 10 against the Bengals. Bernard won’t be playable in 12-team formats when Wilson returns to action.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: Aidan Hutchinson (ACL) will miss the remainder of the season.
items.analysis: Lions head coach Dan Campbell confirmed the news Tuesday morning during a radio interview. Hutchinson went down last week against the Patriots while celebrating a sack. His knee buckled and Hutchinson crumbled tot he turf in pain. He is just the latest NFL player to injure himself while celebrating on the field. Without Hutchinson, Detroit’s defense might struggle to pressure the passer. Headed into Week 11 they rank second in pressure rate and 10th in quick pressure rate. Hutchinson will end his 2026 season with six sacks and six tackles for loss.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku was not targeted in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Njoku briefly saw his role in the offense grow after fellow tight end Oronde Gadsden departed in the first quarter with an eye injury. Gadsden would return in the second half after the team deemed him questionable earlier, shifting Njoku back to a complimentary role behind Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. Njoku’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy score comes in Week 11 against the Jets, although fantasy managers are better off leaving him on waivers.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 3-of-5 targets for 42 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
items.analysis: Bateman saw his route structure altered with the change at quarterback, running a high percentage of his routes over the middle of the field. He was able to run free in the intermediate areas against the heavy zone coverage rates of the Chargers for much of the game, with Brissett instead targeting tight end Mark Andrews and alpha wide receiver Zay Flowers at elevated rates. Bateman remains a shaky Flex play ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

items.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
items.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
items.analysis: Lane handily led the team with 11 targets but struggled through inconsistent play, the most glaring of which came on a drop on a routine target inside the five. It won’t be often that lane leads the team in targets while playing alongside Zay Flowers and the recent resurgence of tight end Mark Andrews, the latter of whom should benefit greatly from the historically high tight end target rate from new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Lane is an upside Flex ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-7 targets for 74 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
items.analysis: Flowers carried only two receptions on two targets into the fourth quarter as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching fire in the final frame before losing a costly fumble on the team’s penultimate possession with under three minutes remaining in a three-point game. Even so, it was a solid rebound effort after Flowers had struggled mightily with poor quarterback play the previous weeks, with veteran Jacoby Brissett providing enough stability for Flowers to remain an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

items.name: Mark Andrews
items.headline: Mark Andrews caught all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
items.analysis: The presence of Jacoby Brissett and his elevated tight end target rate benefited Andrews, leading to a season-high 82 receiving yards on eight receptions. Andrews suddenly has the profile of a back end TE1 after nine weeks of poor performances and gets a solid matchup against the reeling Panthers in Week 11.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers, adding 10 yards on five receptions.
items.analysis: It was the fifth straight game in which Henry was held to 58 yards on the ground or fewer, all five of which were Baltimore losses. Henry salvaged an otherwise poor showing with two rushing scores and a season-high five receptions, marking his 35th career game with multiple touchdowns in the loss. Now playing with Jacoby Brissett under center, Henry has fallen to a middling RB2 in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a more enticing matchup against the Panthers in Week 11.

items.name: Jacoby Brissett
items.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 33-of-49 passes for 340 yards and one interception in the Ravens’ 23-20, Week 10 loss to the Chargers, adding two yards on two carries.
items.analysis: Brissett and the Ravens played from behind throughout against the only team without a win through the first nine weeks of the 2026 season, but the veteran’s performance through the air kept the team within striking distance late into the fourth quarter. The defense did its job and gave the ball back to the Ravens with under three minutes remaining and Brissett had the team driving the field down by three before a Zay Flowers fumble cost them the game. For his part, Brissett settled into the game in the second quarter after three straight three-and-out possessions, ultimately falling just short in the defeat. Brissett will remain the starter under center for the next 6-10 weeks as Lamar Jackson recovers from surgery on his thumb, with his next opportunity to return a viable fantasy outing coming in Week 11 against the Panthers in what is a must-win game for the Ravens, losers of five straight.

items.name: Quentin Johnston
items.headline: Quentin Johnston caught his only target for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Johnston was a complete afterthought in a game quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the team playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. Fellow receiver Tre’ Harris handily led the team with five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards, with no other pass catcher seeing more than three looks, catching more than two passes, or going for more than 16 yards. Johnston is completely off the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris caught all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Harris’ five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards were all team highs on a night quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the Chargers playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. The highlight of the game on either side was Harris’ 31-yard reception in the first quarter, with the veteran receiver shaking free on a deep crosser and getting his hand under the ball on a sliding catch. Fantasy managers will want to track the status of Ladd McConkey entering a Week 11 meeting with the Jets as a return to action could send Harris back to the nether realm as far as fantasy value is concerned.

items.name: Omarion Hampton
items.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding one reception for zero additional yards.
items.analysis: Hampton tallied just his second game of 100 yards from scrimmage in the team’s first win of the season, which was also his first game this year hitting the century mark on the ground. The only other game in which Hampton surpassed 100 yards came against the Raiders way back in Week 2, which was also the only other game this season with 20 or more touches. The typically backfield timeshare tilted heavily in Hampton’s favor through positive game script, hinting at his upside potential in games the Chargers are able to control, something that has not been routine this season. Hampton could carry legitimate RB2 upside against the Jets in Week 11, pending the status of quarterback Geno Smith.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert completed 12-of-18 passes for 129 yards in the Chargers’ 23-20, Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding 51 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
items.analysis: Herbert was not called on often after the Chargers jumped out to a 10-point lead in the first quarter, attempting under 30 passes for the fifth time this season. Two key turnovers were the difference in this one, the first a deflected pass off a Los Angeles defender that fell into the arms of linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips and the second a fourth quarter fumble recovery after Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers with under three minutes to play. Herbert padded his counting stats with a 22-yard touchdown run on the team’s first possession but it still wasn’t enough for the veteran signal caller to return his first QB1 week of the season. Herbert remains a fantasy dud ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

items.name: Oronde Gadsden II
items.headline: Oronde Gadsden (eye) is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Gadsden was injured on a run-blocking rep in the first quarter. He was checked out in the medical tent before being taken to the locker room after appearing to be poked in the eye, eventually deemed questionable to return by the team. Expect David Njoku to operate as the primary pass catching tight end for the Chargers as they look to steal their first win of the season. Gadsden was not targeted prior to departing.

items.name: Oronde Gadsden II
items.headline: Oronde Gadsden (eye) caught his only target for seven yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Gadsden was injured on a run-blocking rep in the first quarter. He was checked out in the medical tent before being taken to the locker room after appearing to be poked in the eye, eventually deemed questionable to return by the team. He would return in the second half to catch his lone target for a meager seven yards in a game in which quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes. Gadsden remains off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: It appears highly likely that Harrison Jr. will miss his second consecutive game with a hamstring injury considering the team is on a short week. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte are likely to continue forward as the top two wide receivers behind Nico Collins, with Tank Dell likely to be held around half of the offensive snaps in this third game back from over a year of missed time.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: It is highly unlikely that Marks will clear concussion protocol on a short week, likely leaving Emari Demercado to split work with David Montgomery, the latter of whom was listed as a full participant as he aims to return from his own injury. Fantasy managers can consider Demercado a viable waiver target in a plus matchup.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: So, too, was Charvarius Ward with a knee injury, the latter of whom departed the team’s Week 10 contest and did not return. The team has already announced quarterback Daniel Jones as the starter for Thursday Night Football, with no other massive news early in a short week.

items.name: Charvarius Ward
items.headline: Charvarius Ward (knee) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: Ward departed the team’s Week 10 win over the Dolphins with a shin injury and did not return, listed as a non-participant one day later on the team’s estimated practice report. It would appear unlikely he is able to play on a short week against the Texans on Thursday Night Football.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: ESPN’s Courtney Cronin reports Kyle Monangai is back at practice and “on track” for Week 11.
items.analysis: Monangai has missed the previous five games while dealing with thumb and toe injuries, with the team’s Week 10 bye appearing to have provided enough time for the electric youngster to return following five missed games. He should be expected to step back into a strict timeshare with D’Andre Swift after earning 31 percent to 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps through the first four weeks of the 2026 season. Monangai returns to a viable Flex profile and downgrades Swift from weekly RB1 status to a borderline RB2.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Chargers declared WR Ladd McConkey, S Kendall Williamson, CB Isas Waxter, OLB Bud Dupree, WR Brenen Thompson, and DL Justin Eboigbe inactive for Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: McConkey entered the weekend listed as questionable but was downgraded to out Saturday, while rookie Brenan Thompson will miss his seventh consecutive game. The reeling Chargers look to pick up their first win through an upset of a Ravens team without its top two quarterbacks, having recently signed veteran Jacoby Brissett for the final half of the regular season.

items.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
items.headline: Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, G/T Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Chandler Rivers, and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive for Week 10 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: No surprises here as Hawkins had already been ruled out earlier in the week, with the remaining five players all normal healthy inactives. The Ravens look to right a sinking ship against the only remaining winless team in the league, with quarterback Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center.

items.name: Christian Parker
items.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, asked directly about Christian Parker’s status as defensive coordinator and if changes are being made, said “I’m not saying that.”
items.analysis: “I’m saying we’re still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today,” Schottenheimer concluded, notably not conclusively answering the question after the Cowboys allowed 46 points to the 49ers in what has been another lost season purely due to defensive lapses. The 34-year-old Parker was regarded as a hot coaching prospect, but the early returns have been rough. The Cowboys have allowed 282 points, the third-most in the league, and are allowing a league-worst 5.2 yards per rushing attempt.

items.name: Jordan Burch
items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jordan Burch (knee) will miss the remainder of the season.
items.analysis: Burch suffered an MCL injury in Week 10’s loss to the Rams and will now miss the remainder of the season. The second-year linebacker and former third-rounder has appeared on 235 defensive snaps this season, totaling nine pressures and one sack while earning a PFF defensive grade of 54.8. Assuming his recovery goes well, he should be in line to return in time for training camp.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending in the right direction” to practice this week.
items.analysis: Quinn declined to commit to opening “Bill’s” 21-day return window, but sounded optimistic about doing so later in the week. The Commanders’ RB1 has missed the last four games with a groin injury he picked up in Week 5 and would be eligible to return as early as Week 11 if he were to be designated to return this week. The Commanders have struggled on the ground without JCM this season, as their running backs have combined to average just 3.7 YPC since Week 6 while finding the end zone once. If he’s able to play against the Bengals, JCM would have some appeal as an RB3/FLEX in a week that has six teams on bye.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: Chargers activated TE David Njoku from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Njoku will try to fight for fantasy relevancy going forward, but there’s no need to pretend he has it at the moment with all three Chargers tight ends healthy. They also activated LB Denzel Perryman off the same list and sent G/T Branson Taylor to injured reserve in their place.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers (ankle) is day-to-day.
items.analysis: He called the injury “significant” but “not as bad as we thought.” OK then. We would call Bowers’ status for Week 11 up in the air at this point, the practices will be guiding lights. Fantasy managers reliant on Bowers may want to look into a backup plan on this run of waivers.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik Willis (groin) is not having surgery at this time but a final decision has not been made on if he’ll have it.
items.analysis: “We’ll see how he feels,” Hafley said. “If he needs surgery, he will have surgery.” Well, hard to make it less complex than that. Willis is definitely out for the next three games and it sounds like there’s at least a reasonable chance he’ll be done for the season. In the meantime, Kyle McCord will play the role of bottom-five superflex starter.

items.name: Laremy Tunsil
items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said it’s too early to know if Laremy Tunsil (triceps) will return this season.
items.analysis: Quinn said Tunsil is progressing well in his recovery from the torn triceps he suffered in training camp and has moved on to the next phase of his recovery. Tunsil was always expected to miss all or most of the season with his injury, so it’s no surprise to hear that Quinn is unsure if he will be able to return with eight weeks left to go in the regular season. We’ll likely get more updates on his status in the coming weeks, but until the Commanders designate him for return, we can safely assume he will be out for the foreseeable future.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “that’s my plan” when asked if Micah Parsons (knee) could return in Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: LaFleur did note that his plan has “been different than everybody else’s” throughout Parsons’ recovery, and said the star pass-rusher still has “a couple more hurdles” to clear before they can commit to him returning. Parsons has been practicing with the team since November 4th and would need to come off injured reserve by Week 12 in order to avoid being shut down for the season. With the Packers now entering their Week 11 bye, we will likely get more news on Parsons’ Week 12 status closer to the weekend.

items.name: Cam Ward
items.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said the Titans shifted the offensive philosophy to give Cam Ward “an opportunity” to prove he’s a franchise quarterback.
items.analysis: “A few weeks ago we made a shift on how we’re letting Cam Ward run the offense, let him be a field general. ... He’s looking more comfortable, his footwork is improving, and he’s doing a nice job playing quarterback. Still things he can clean up,” Saleh added. Ward over the last two weeks has four touchdown passes and his two highest passing-attempt totals of the season. We’re not exactly excited to fire up Ward as a QB1 streamer at this point, even against the Cowboys in Week 11, but given how many NFL offenses are currently trending down it’s worth pointing out that the Titans are actually taking a step forward of late.

items.name: George Holani
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports George Holani (knee) has an MCL sprain and is week-to-week.
items.analysis: The “hope” is that Holani is not an IR candidate. His absence left Zach Charbonnet playing most of the third-down snaps yesterday, adding to his RB2 case going forward. Holani can be dropped in most leagues ahead of Seattle’s Week 11 bye.

items.name: Aaron Glenn
items.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn revealed that DC Brian Duker called defensive plays on Sunday.
items.analysis: Last February, Glenn said that calling plays was his “superpower.” The Jets are 28th in defensive DVOA per FTN and have allowed the most rushing attempts in the league along with 1,353 yards on the ground, third-most in the league. Glenn did not say whether he or Duker would call plays going forward. We’re not sure it really matters. The second-year coach is running out of road as the Jets have stumbled to a 2-8 start.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will undergo surgery and could miss “a few weeks.”
items.analysis: He called it a “freak” injury and didn’t dismiss the possibility of Addison heading to short-term injured reserve. Fantasy managers in a rough bye week squeeze without injured reserve spots can move on from Addison if need be. He hasn’t cleared 100 yards in a game all season.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Eagles designated RB Will Shipley (foot) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: With Shipley’s 21-day return window officially opened, the third-year back can resume practicing with the team and is eligible to be activated from the injured reserve list at any time. It’s only Week 11, but this offense has struggled mightily without Jalen Hurts (blood clots), making it hard to imagine anybody offering much fantasy value at this point. Shipley has rushed 20 times for 57 yards and one touchdown this season and has caught five passes for 31 scoreless yards. There’s no reason to rush to add Shipley, even when he is activated. In another move, the Eagles also signed TE Zach Ertz to the and OT John Ojukwu to the 53-man roster.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aidan Hutchinson (knee) tore his ACL and will miss the rest of the season.
items.analysis: This was expected based on what we’d been hearing but this is official confirmation that the Lions have lost their best pass rusher for the remainder of the season. Hutchinson, 26, may have a rough time making it back for the start of the 2027 season based on the timing of this injury. As has become the norm in this era, the Lions defense just can’t seem to have all their best players be healthy at the right time.

items.name: Drake London
items.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Drake London was evaluated for a concussion against the Chiefs and cleared the protocol.
items.analysis: We didn’t mention this in the blurb streets yesterday as it happened late in the fourth quarter. London should be fine to start in Week 12 after Atlanta’s Week 11 bye.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will start in Week 11 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Steichen said on Monday during his media session that Jones knows he needs to play better, which is good news. Whether or not he plays better is to be determined, as Jones has seemingly known for weeks that he needs to play better but seldom does so on game days. In fairness to Jones, the Colts parted with a few key offensive players in recent weeks, including wide receiver Josh Downs, but the 29-year-old quarterback is also part of why the Colts chose to be sellers at this year’s trade deadline. It feels like it’s only a matter of time before the Colts consider giving another QB a look, but given the short turnaround to prepare for Thursday’s game against the Texans, it makes some sense for the Colts to stick with Jones for at least one more week.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said he is “really optimistic” that Sam Darnold (quad) will be able to start after the team’s Week 11 bye.
items.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Macdonald also reaffirmed Darnold as the starter after Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10’s win over the Raiders. Lock has been solid for the Seahawks in four games this season, throwing for 837-7-0 while completing a career-high 73.1 percent of his passes. With the Seahawks now entering their bye, Macdonald said he his hopeful Darnold can log enough reps in time to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. We’ll see where things stand a week from now, but it’s clear there will be no QB controversey in Seattle whenever Darnold is ready to go.

items.name: Jimmy Garoppolo
items.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Patriots “are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week.”
items.analysis: According to Schultz, the Patriots could look into free agents like Jimmy Garoppolo and may also consider signing a QB from a team’s practice squad. Garoppolo, who last threw a regular-season pass in Week 18 of the 2024 season, worked with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels from 2014 to 2017 during their time together in New England, and also spent the 2023 season with McDaniels during a brief stint with the Raiders. It’s hard to imagine Garoppolo coming off the couch to save the Patriots’ season, but he could offer a little more upside than Tommy DeVito did in relief of Drake Maye during Sunday’s loss to the Lions. For now, DeVito is expected to start in Week 12 when the Patriots return from their bye, but it wouldn’t be surprising if they considered an upgrade. Head coach Mike Vrabel said later that the team will “have conversations” about the possibility of bringing in outside help, but said he’s “ excited for the challenge ” of seeing what the team can do with DeVito under center.

items.name: Cooper Rush
items.headline: Buccaneers signed QB Cooper Rush, formerly of the Falcons.
items.analysis: Rush’s signing comes a day after it was reported that Baker Mayfield could miss Week 11’s game against the Lions due to a leg injury he suffered in Week 9. The decision to sign Rush suggests Mayfield is trending in the wrong direction early in the week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when they take the practice field. Rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels would be the favorite to start in the event Mayfield is sidelined, but Rush could be in line to serve as his backup. The 32-year-old vet struggled during his brief stint in Atlanta, throwing for 229-1-4 in two games while completing only 56.4 percent of his passes.

items.name: Zane Gonzalez
items.headline: Dolphins waived K Zane Gonzalez.
items.analysis: Shortly after being named the Dolphins’ full-time kicker, Gonzalez is once again looking for work. The 31-year-old had a rough outing against the Colts, going 1-for-3 on field goal attempts, missing on 47 and 51-yard attempts. He also missed an extra point in the 24-22 defeat. Gonzalez has made 6-of-10 field goals on the season and is 6-for-7 on extra-point tries. It wouldn’t be surprising if he found work elsewhere at some point in the season.

items.name: Tyler Booker
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cowboys RG Tyler Booker will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain he suffered in Week 10’s loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Rapoport reports that while this injury usually results in a 4-6 week absence, the Cowboys hope Booker “can be back within that four-week window.” If he can return within four weeks, it’s possible the 22-year-old avoids a stint on injured reserve, but the team will likely make a final determination on that later in the week. T.J. Bass was the next man up to fill in for Booker and will presumably takeover as the starter for however long Booker is sidelined.

items.name: Jordan Watkins
items.headline: Jordan Watkins caught 2-of-3 targets for 49 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: After going for 4-86-1 in Week 9’s win over the Raiders, Watkins returned back to earth against the Cowboys. Watkins’ role as a field stretcher resulted in gains of 22 and 27 yards in this one, but it also highlights why he’s a weekly boom-or-bust option. His 22 routes run were one more than Keenan Allen saw in his 49ers’ debut, but Allen immediately led all Niners receivers with seven targets. Watkins can’t be counted on in Week 11 against the Vikings and can be dropped in most leagues.

items.name: Kaelon Black
items.headline: Kaelon Black rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: It was another week of steady involvement for Black, who has now seen double-digit rush attempts in three straight games. The rookie third-rounder broke off an impressive 25-yard touchdown run in the third quarter of Sunday’s win over the Cowboys, running through multiple defenders to the end zone while staying upright through contact. Black’s volume has him firmly in the conversation as a deeper league FLEX play, but he’s too touchdown-dependent to be viewed as anything more than a fringe RB3/RB4.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11 against the Chargers if he is healthy.
items.analysis: Smith is having tests on his ankle after getting banged up in Week 10’s loss to the Bills. Smith was briefly evaluated for a concussion in Sunday’s game, only to return to the field and be knocked out in the third quarter with his ankle injury. Smith has struggled as of late, failing to throw a touchdown in his last two games while throwing for just 313 yards. Rookie Cade Klubnik, who threw for 137 yards and one interception while also taking three sacks, didn’t fare much better in Smith’s absence, but Smith is undoubtedly the better of the two QBs on the roster. All Jets pass-catchers would receive a slight downgrade next week if Smith is sidelined against the Chargers.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders believe Brock Bowers (ankle) avoided a major injury in Week 10’s loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Bowers is expected to undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but Rapoport said the Raiders believe they will have him back “sooner rather than later.” Bowers had his ankle rolled up in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss and did not return to the field after making a trip to the locker room. His absence will be felt by a Raiders offense that has relied heavily on him since drafting him in 2024, and leaves rookie QB Fernando Mendoza without a valuable outlet in the passing game. Backup tight end Michael Mayer, who is in the midst of a career year, could have some value as a fringe TE1/TE2 in any games Bowers misses.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Lions believe Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in Week 10’s win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: Hutchinson will have an MRI to confirm, but things have been trending in this direction ever since it was reported on Sunday night that the team was “very concerned” about the star pass-rusher’s injury. Hutchinson landed awkwardly on a play when he jumped to celebrate a sack on Drake Maye and did not return to the field. If the worst is confirmed, it would be Hutchinson’s second season-ending injury since 2024.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: According to Schefter, Maye stayed overnight in Germany to undergo testing and determine whether or not he would need surgery. For now, Maye is out indefinitely, but the 24-year-old QB and 2025 MVP runner-up could be looking at missing the rest of the season for the now 5-5 Patriots. His absence would force the Patriots to start Tommy DeVito in Week 12 against the Chargers, which would all but spell disaster for all Patriots skill players from a fantasy perspective. DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday’s loss and has a career passing line of 1,450-9-4 in 15 career games.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports it’s “possible” Drake Maye (lower leg) misses the rest of the season.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time.” It’s devastating news for Patriots fans and fantasy managers. While Maye has had his ups and downs this year, the team was nonfunctional without him on Sunday. Tommy DeVito took over for an injured Maye early in the first quarter and threw for 81 yards at 3.4 yards per attempt. The Pats also have seventh-round rookie Behren Morton on the roster. We suspect DeVito will get another shot at the starting job, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see Morton under center at some point this year. With A.J. Brown also banged up and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Pats are shaping up to be a fantasy wasteland over the second half of the season.

items.name: Samaje Perine
items.headline: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 25 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: Perine’s 10 touches dwarfed in comparison to the 18 of lead back Chase Brown, the latter of whom found the end zone twice for his second and third scores of the season. Low weekly volume in the pass-first Cincinnati offense leaves Perine nothing more than a desperation Flex without an injury ahead of him on the depth chart.

items.name: Mike Gesicki
items.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
items.analysis: Gesicki caught the first pass from scrimmage for nine yards before completely disappearing the rest of the game, which was easy to do considering Ja’Marr Chase erupted for the third highest receiving total in a game in his career with 231 yards. The Steelers just had no answer for the elite alpha receiver, leaving little scraps leftover for the rest of the Cincinnati offense. The only thing Chase didn’t do was find the end zone, with the touchdowns accounted for by Chase Brown (two), Samaje Perine, Dohnte Meyers, and Drew Sample. Gesicki remains a touchdown-dependent TE2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Dohnte Meyers
items.headline: Dohnte Meyers caught both targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
items.analysis: Meyers capped off the second quarter with a touchdown reception from 15 yards out and only nine seconds remaining before the half. He would not be targeted again as the Bengals leaned heavily on Ja’Marr Chase on their way to a blowout win, with their defense holding the Steelers to 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters of play. Meyers remains a desperation Flex ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
items.analysis: Higgins’ six targets finished third on the team behind Ja’Marr Chase (14) and Chase Brown (nine) while his receiving output was dwarfed by the 231 yards of Chase. The matchup against the zone-heavy Steelers likely played a significant role in the target breakout, with Higgins much more dangerous against man coverage this season. Higgins remains an elite WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Chase Brown
items.headline: Chase Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 39 yards and two touchdowns on eight receptions.
items.analysis: Brown continues to see a modest workload on the ground playing in the offense leading the league in pass rate over expectation while averaging almost 38 pass attempts per game. The pass game usage isn’t reliable on a weekly basis despite the veteran back seeing nine or more targets on three separate occasions this season. This was also his first game with a trip to the end zone since Week 1 despite working as a borderline workhorse this season, leaving Brown as an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup against the pass-funnel Commanders, where he’ll likely require elite pass game utilization to return a usable score on that valuation.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
items.analysis: It was the second consecutive game in which Chase went over 140 yards in the first half alone, eventually notching the third most receiving yards in a game in his illustrious career with 231 while blowing by the century mark for the third consecutive contest. Chase was the primary point of emphasis from the first kick against the Steelers, working mostly the short-to-intermediate areas of the field before bomb on a sluggo route in the second quarter. He worked behind primary coverage on three separate instances but was ushered out of bounds on all three occasions, any of which would have further inflated his counting stats had they turned into touchdowns. Chase and the Bengals now get a long week of preparation for the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11, where he will remain an elite WR1.

items.name: Joe Burrow
items.headline: Joe Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 38-18, Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding eight yards on one carry.
items.analysis: Burrow cruised to his fifth consecutive game of four total touchdowns or more, passing for 302 yards and three scores in the first half alone. The Steelers were completely unable to move the ball consistently while managing only 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters, allowing Burrow and the Bengals to build an insurmountable lead through the first 45 minutes of play. The win sends Cincinnati to the top of the AFC North with a 7-2 record after splitting the season series with the Steelers, now in the driver’s seat for the division title with two months remaining in the regular season. Burrow will look to keep the elite play going in a Week 11 meeting with the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football, where he remains a top tier QB1 in fantasy circles.

items.name: Germie Bernard
items.headline: Germie Bernard did not catch any of his three targets in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, gaining 10 yards on one carry.
items.analysis: Bernard has now had three modest fantasy showings after his breakout game against the Buccaneers, failing to eclipse 30 yards in all three outings since Week 6. His output against the Bengals is more a microcosm of the performance from the entire Pittsburgh offense, a unit that gained only 23 yards of total offense through the first 45 minutes of play while losing 17 yards on two third quarter possessions. Fantasy managers that thought they found a hidden gem on the waiver wire a month ago have little to show for it and must question whether to start the rookie receiver in a middling matchup against the reeling Eagles in Week 11.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
