items.analysis: This was one to forget for the entire Pittsburgh offense, who managed to gain just 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters of play, limiting the fantasy production of all parties involved. Freiermuth was one of two fortunate ones to salvage his fantasy day with a fourth quarter touchdown when the game was already well out of reach, although the modest reception and yardage totals were far too familiar for Freiermuth’s fantasy managers. He’ll remain a touchdown-or-bust TE2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Eagles.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Metcalf was blanked through three quarters as the offense was held to a paltry 23 yards of total offense in the first 45 minutes of play. He salvaged his fantasy day with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown on the team’s first possession of the final frame, tacking on a two-point conversion for good measure. Even so, Metcalf has been one of fantasy’s bigger disappointments this season, with just 432 yards and two touchdowns through nine games played, while also catching under 50 percent of his targets. Even worse is the fact that he has only three receptions of 20 yards or more this season. Metcalf will remain a shaky FLEX ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Eagles.

items.name: Jaylen Warren
items.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, adding 26 yards on five receptions.
items.analysis: The end results were obviously far from encouraging for the talented veteran, although they were overshadowed by the fact the Steelers managed just 23 yards of total offense through three quarters of play. Even worse, the team lost a total of 17 yards in the third quarter after gaining just 40 yards of total offense before the break. Warren has a solid opportunity to rebound in Week 11 against the hapless Eagles, where he’ll return to RB2 status in fantasy circles.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, adding eight yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: Dowdle played sparingly in the first half as the Steelers were completely incapable of moving the ball. In fact, Pittsburgh managed just 40 yards of total offense in the first half before losing 17 yards in the third quarter, leaving them with a putrid 23 yards of total offense through three quarters. The extremely negative game script clearly limited the backfield’s opportunities and production, with Dowdle unable to escape the onslaught. His next opportunity to return usable counting stats comes in Week 11 against the Eagles, where he’ll remain off the fantasy radar.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 15-of-29 passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Steelers’ 38-18, Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: The final score doesn’t seem as bad as it was for Rodgers and the Steelers, who managed just 23 yards of total offense through three quarters as they fell to their division rivals in a game that decided the current division leader. Rodgers failed to complete his first eight passes, a mark that tied the longest stretch of incompletions to start a game of his illustrious career. Two fourth quarter touchdowns with the game already well out of reach padded Rodgers’ counting stats as well as making the game appear slightly closer than it played. The abysmal performance drops the Steelers to 6-3 and one game behind the Bengals for the lead in the AFC North, with the fact that the two teams split the season series the only saving grace as the Steelers look to make a second half push toward the postseason. Up next for Rodgers and the Steelers are the reeling Eagles on the road in Week 11, where Rodgers will remain a middling QB2 in fantasy circles.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers will be reevaluated on Monday after suffering an ankle injury in Las Vegas’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Kubiak told reporters that the team has not yet determined the injury’s severity. Tomorrow’s tests will provide more info. Bowers injured his ankle in the first quarter and was taken into the blue medical for examination. He managed to return for Fernando Mendoza’s 10-yard touchdown run, but was taken to the locker room after that. Bowers then returned to the field early in the second quarter, catching a 12-yard pass on third down. Unfortunately, his ankle wasn’t feeling right and he was again taken back to the locker room before later being ruled out. His day ended with two catches for 18 yards. The Raiders face the Broncos and Browns before going on bye in Week 13. Hopefully, he is able to return before then. Michael Mayer will be a TE1 if Bowers misses time.

items.name: Ryan Flournoy
items.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 6-of-7 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the Niners.
items.analysis: Flournoy’s seven targets were good for third-most among all Cowboys pass-catchers in this one. The third-year receiver hauled in a 23-yard catch in the third quarter, and broke free from his defender in the end zone on a fourth-and-six in the fourth quarter for an 11-yard touchdown as the Cowboys were hoping to mount a comeback. Flournoy continues to prove himself as a reliable option whenever Dak Prescott looks his way, but his usage remains hard to predict as long as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are healthy. Fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance entering Week 11 against the Titans.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 16 times for 59 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Mason’s 16 carries and 59 yards both led all Vikings players. It was his first double-digit touch game since Week 7 against the Colts, but despite the encouraging touch share, he still lacked the high-value touches near the goal line. Aaron Jones handled all four of the Vikings’ goal-to-go rush attempts, leaving Mason to rely on long scores. Mason will be hard to trust as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

items.name: Devaughn Vele
items.headline: Devaughn Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: Vele’s cold streak continued in a miserable game for Tyler Shough, who averaged 5.3 yards per attempt with an average depth of target of 4.5. The emergence of Jordyn Tyson, who led the Saints with 13 targets against Carolina, is going to take away targets from Vele. He might hold some PPR appeal in Week 11 against the Bears, but not much. Vele has more than four catches in a game just once in the past five weeks.

items.name: Tucker Kraft
items.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-4 targets for 19 yards in the Packers Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: That makes it back-to-back one-catch weeks for Kraft, who has totaled just two receptions for 20 yards on seven targets. While this can partly be blamed on a tough matchup against a stout Vikings defense, it’s worth remembering that Kraft often produces for fantasy managers despite lacking elite volume at times. His 52 routes run over the last week are tied with Dalton Schultz for 11th-most among tight ends, but the ball just hasn’t been finding him as of late. Despite the frustrating usage, he should be in the mix when the Packers return from their bye as a fringe TE1 in Week 12 against the Rams.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-2 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Shaheed ran a route on 17 of 25 Seattle drop backs but was again not a part of the passing attack. Cooper Kupp and Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught touchdowns from Drew Lock as Shaheed ran empty routes. Headed into the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye, Shaheed has two games on the season with more than three receptions and he has not scored a receiving touchdown.

items.name: Myles Price
items.headline: Myles Price caught 4-of-4 targets for 49 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings Week 10 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Price scored his first career touchdown in the first quarter when he hauled in a 38-yard pass from Kirk Cousins on a third-and-23 to put the Vikings up 10-0. Cousins displayed good anticipation on the throw to Price, who found a hole between three defenders. Price hauled in the pass, bounced off a defender, and turned upfield for the long score to give Cousins his first touchdown pass in a Vikings uniform since 2023. Price has now run 20-plus routes in back-to-back weeks while lining up in the slot over 70 percent of the time. He won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 11 against the 49ers.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnson in the flailing New Orleans offense. Johnson, who doesn’t have more than 40 yards in a game since Week 4, ran a pass route on 31 of 46 Saints drop backs. His involvement hasn’t led to much in the way of production. Johnson should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 11.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Meanwhile, Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for a meager 18 yards and again took all the pass-catching work out of the Raiders backfield. Washington will see decent rush volume when the Raiders see neutral or positive game script. How often that will happen in the coming weeks is another matter entirely. Washington should not be played in most fantasy formats next week against the Broncos.

items.name: Michael Mayer
items.headline: Michael Mayer caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: The Vegas passing attack was snuffed out from start to finish by an elite Seattle defense. Mayer could see a marked increase in targets if Brock Bowers misses time with the ankle injury he sustained in the first quarter. Mayer, who was productive earlier this season when Bowers was sidelined with injury, would be a legit streaming option in Week 11 against Denver if Bowers is out. The Broncos allow the tenth most fantasy points per target to tight ends this season.

items.name: Mason McCormick
items.headline: Mason McCormick (lower leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 10 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: McCormick stayed down on the field with his head in his hands following a pass protection rep late in the second quarter against the Bengals. Training staff placed an air cast on his lower leg and loaded him onto the cart to be removed from the field. He was immediately taken to the locker room for x-rays and is likely looking at an extended absence.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for 18 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, adding four catches for 46 yards.
items.analysis: Jeanty was the Raiders’ leading receiver with Brock Bowers sidelined with an ankle injury. His 38-yard catch and run was by far the biggest play of the day for a lifeless Vegas offense with Fernando Mendoza under center for his first start of his NFL career. As usual, Jeanty operated as the primary pass catcher out of the backfield, running 26 routes to just eight routes for Mike Washington, who had a meager 23 yards on eight carries. Jeanty will be a top-24 PPR option next week against Denver.

items.name: Coleman Shelton
items.headline: Coleman Shelton did not return to the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals after suffering a hamstring injury in the second quarter.
items.analysis: Shelton and his backup, Dylan McMahon (knee), both suffered injuries today, causing the Rams to shuffle their offensive line personnel. The Rams are on bye in Week 11. Hopefully at least one of them can return in time for the Rams’ Week 12 game against the Packers.

items.name: Fernando Mendoza
items.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 17-of-29 attempts for 143 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, adding six rushes for 22 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Mendoza was thrown directly into the meat grinder of the elite Seahawks defense and lost his superstar tight end, Brock Bowers, to a potentially serious ankle injury in the first quarter. After a first quarter rushing score on a draw play, Mendoza and the Raiders couldn’t get anything going against Seattle. Mendoza, who was sacked six times, posted a -6.8 EPA while Drew Lock had an EPA of 7. Mendoza was about 7 percent under his expected completion rate. Things won’t get much easier for the 2026 No. 1 overall pick in Week 11 when the Raiders take on the Broncos. Mendoza for now is strictly a superflex option.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed five times for 14 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: The Cardinals’ coaching staff gave Allgeier the chance to be the team’s lead rusher today. He botched it, eventually ceding carries to Bam Knight late in the game. Knight barely outplayed him. Allgeier failed to catch his lone target. He is just a FLEX option next week against the Chiefs.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Zach Charbonnet had 20 rushes for 94 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Charbonnet again led the Seattle backfield in another run-heavy outing. Jadarian Price, however, scored a touchdown on his nine rushing attempts. Charbonnet rumbled for a few impressive, tough runs against a miserable Raiders defense that appeared worn down in the second half. His long play came on a 24-yard rush in the second half. Though Charbonnet led the Seahawks backfield in routes, he did not see a target. When the Seahawks return from bye in Week 12, Charbonnet will profile as a high-floor RB2 option.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Bam Knight rushed five times for 19 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Knight missed the Cardinals’ Week 9 game due to a concussion, but he had been working as the team’s primary rusher before that. Today, Tyler Allgeier handled that role, but his poor play resulted in more carries for Knight as the game progressed. Early in the fourth quarter, Knight snuck past his coverage defender on a route out of the backfield, running down the left sideline. Carson Beck slightly overthrew him, but Knight should have attempted to dive for what could have been roughly a 25-yard catch. It’s possible he lost the pass in the stadium lights. He earned two targets on the day, catching neither. Knight is a touchdown-dependent FLEX against the Chiefs in Week 11.

items.name: Simi Fehoko
items.headline: Simi Fehoko caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Fehoko caught his lone catchable pass for a 21-yard play-action gain on the opening drive. His second target was off-target and resulted in an incompletion. Fehoko does not need to be rostered for the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs.

items.name: Devin Duvernay
items.headline: Devin Duvernay caught 2-of3 targets for 35 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Duvernay briefly got going on the Cardinals’ second drive, taking a screen pass for four yards before producing a 31-yard catch on a corner route. Unfortunately, on the Cardinals’ fifth drive, he twirled to the ground while trying to catch a pass and ended up flipping the football right into Rams S Kam Kinchens’ hands for an interception. Duvernay should not be trusted to return FLEX value against the Chiefs next week.

items.name: Tre Tucker
items.headline: Tre Tucker caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: The Raiders had a meager 146 passing yards in Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start. Tucker, the leading Vegas wideout headed into Week 10, wasn’t targeted until the fourth quarter against the elite Seahawks secondary. The loss of Kirk Cousins in a trade to the Vikings last week might be the end of Tucker’s fleeting fantasy relevance unless Mendoza improves in the coming weeks. If Brock Bowers (ankle) misses time, Tucker could see a slight uptick in targets.

items.name: AJ Barner
items.headline: AJ Barner caught all three of his targets for 19 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Running a pass routes on 18 of the team’s 23 drop backs, Barner again had nice involvement in the Seattle offense but not much in the way of usage. Barner now has more than two receptions in just four games on the season. That puts him out of streaming contention in most fantasy leagues.

items.name: Trey McBride
items.headline: Trey McBride caught 5-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Initially, it looked like McBride might not experience much of a drop-off with Carson Beck at the helm, catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the opening drive. The Cardinals’ offense then began to falter, and the Rams jumped out to a 17-6 lead by the end of the first half. From there, the Rams’ defense focused on flustering Beck, and the Cardinals’ rushing attack was unable to make them pay. McBride led the team in targets and will still be a TE1 next week against the Chiefs. As he and Beck hone their connection, his box score results may fluctuate more than we’d like in the coming weeks, though.

items.name: Jadarian Price
items.headline: Jadarian Price had nine rushes for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for eight yards.
items.analysis: It was Price’s first touchdown of the season, and it came on a 12-yard rush around the left edge against a Vegas run defense that has collapsed in recent weeks. Zach Charbonnet, meanwhile, led the backfield with 20 carries for 94 scoreless yards. Charbonnet ran 15 routes to seven routes for Price. When the Seahawks return from bye in Week 12, Price will be a deep league flex option in the run-first Seattle offense.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Carson Beck completed 11-of-18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions in the Cardinals’ 6-34, Week 10 loss to the Rams and lost one fumble.
items.analysis: Beck’s performance wasn’t quite as bad as the box score suggests, but it wasn’t good either. The rookie quarterback went 7-of-9 through the Cardinals’ first three drives, but the game script suddenly became pass-heavy late in the second quarter, allowing the Rams’ defense to play single-mindedly. Reggie Virgil let what could have been a 29-yard touchdown pass go off his hands on a free play, and Zay Jones fell over backward while trying to secure what should have been an easy 40-yard reception. Beck’s first interception, on the Cardinals’ fifth drive, was not his fault. Devin Duvernay twirled to the ground as he attempted to secure the pass, but his momentum got the better of him and he accidentally flung the ball into Rams S Kam Kinchens’ hands. Beck’s second interception was a poorly timed checkdown attempt to Tyler Allgeier, which a Rams defender timed perfectly as he jumped the route, ripping the ball away from Allgeier’s outstretched hands on the Cardinals’ seventh drive. Beck’s lost fumble was the result of a clean punch-out from a Rams defender while Beck was attempting to scramble for a first down. Life won’t get any easier for Beck against the Chiefs next week. He’s a QB2/3.

items.name: Cooper Kupp
items.headline: Cooper Kupp caught his only target for a 34-yard touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Kupp was the recipient of a highlight reel throw from Drew Lock, who had two touchdown tosses on the day. It was Kupp’s third touchdown on the season. With only three games this season with more than three catches, Kupp should not be rostered in most fantasy formats ahead of Seattle’s Week 11 bye.

items.name: Ronnie Rivers
items.headline: Ronnie Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Rivers functioned exclusively as a special teams player right up until the Rams’ final drive, which began with 12 minutes and 15 seconds remaining in the game, at the Rams’ four-yard line. Rivers ran the ball on 15 consecutive plays, with carry results ranging from minus-one to 16 yards, while taking exactly 11 minutes off the clock. Matthew Stafford knelt it out from there. Rivers will not be on the fantasy radar in Week 12 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye, but it was an encouraging performance for the team’s No. 3 running back.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-10 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Smith-Njigba, as usual, accounted for well over half of the Seahawks’ receiving yardage, with no other Seattle pass catcher seeing more than three targets on the day. JSN’s catch-and-run touchdown came on a perfectly placed ball from Drew Lock after he was flushed out of the pocket. This marked JSN’s eighth 100-yard receiving performance in 2026; he has at least ten targets in all but two games this season. JSN has the strongest fantasy profile in quite some time. The Seahawks are on bye in Week 11.

items.name: Tutu Atwell
items.headline: Tutu Atwell caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Atwell’s lone catch came via a crisp corner route from the slot on the Rams’ first drive. His gaffe came via a post route on the Rams’ fifth drive that probably should have resulted in a 32-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, Atwell bricked it, mimicking a volleyball set while trying to high-point the pass inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line. He will be a boom-bust FLEX in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: CJ Daniels
items.headline: CJ Daniels caught 1-of-2 targets for 22 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Daniels earned an end zone target on the Rams’ first drive, but Matthew Stafford unfortunately overthrew him. Daniels then snagged a 22-yard catch via a nine-route down the left sideline on the following drive. Unfortunately, his biggest impact on the game was a false start penalty that erased a five-yard receiving touchdown from Kyren Williams on the Rams’ fourth drive. The rookie wide receiver does not need to be held on rosters through the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock completed 14-of-17 attempts for 240 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders, adding six rushes for 20 yards.
items.analysis: Lock, as he has been in every spot start this season, was efficient in the run-first Seattle offense, averaging 14.1 yards per attempt and finishing 15 percent over his expected pass rate against a Raiders defense that ranks among the NFL’s worst. Lock fought through an elbow issue and an oblique injury in another win as Sam Darnold works his way back from injury. Visibly grimacing at time, Lock was his usual aggressive self, connecting with Cooper Kupp and Jaxson Smith-Njigba for touchdowns. Seattle has its bye in Week 11.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding two receptions for nine yards.
items.analysis: Williams was the clear-cut starter, as usual, touching the ball on the first four plays, but Blake Corum played so well that Rams coach Sean McVay just kept calling his number. Williams had a five-yard receiving touchdown called back due to a false start committed by rookie WR CJ Daniels. Williams’ five targets also led the pass-catching corps. The Rams go on bye in Week 11, but Williams will be back in the RB1 ranks against the Packers in Week 12.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-7 targets for 61 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Despite a short week to acclimate himself to his new team, Allen made a seamless transition to his new team. He caught 2-of-3 targets on third down for 31 yards, with one of those plays resulting in a 23-yard gain while Brock Purdy was scrambling around to extend the play. Allen’s 21 routes run narrowly trailed Deebo Samuel (27) and Jordan Watkins (22), but it wouldn’t be surprising if he saw more involvement going forward. Still one of the premier receivers in the league when it comes to finding separation and getting open, Allen already looks like a perfect fit in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. He will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next Week against the Vikings.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports A.J. Brown (hamstring) will undergo further testing this week.
items.analysis: Brown’s imaging will take place once the Patriots return from Germany, potentially as early as Monday. Florio referred to the Patriots’ Week 11 bye as “good news” for Brown, which could indicate he has a chance to play in Week 12 against the Chargers, but we really don’t know for sure. We should learn more once the imaging is complete. Stay tuned.

items.name: George Kittle
items.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-9 targets for 74 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Kittle’s nine targets led all Niners players in this one. His 20-yard touchdown on the Niners’ opening drive set Deebo Samuel up nicely for an 11-yard touchdown on a screen pass on the following play, and in the fourth quarter, Kittle caught a 10-yard pass to move into the Cowboys’ red zone and positioned Christian McCaffrey for a 16-yard touchdown run soon after. Kittle continues to impress in his return from a late-season Achilles injury. He has gone for 58 or more yards in four straight games while averaging 8.5 targets per game over that span. He draws a tough Week 11 matchup against the Vikings, but will still profile as a low-end TE1.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown, adding three carries for 78 yards and one touchdown.
items.analysis: Samuel, 30, turned back the clock to score not one, but two touchdowns in the Niners’ route of the Cowboys. Samuel would find the end zone on an 11-yard bubble screen in the first quarter to give the Niners their first points of the day. Then, in the third quarter, Samuel took an end around 70 yards upfield for a touchdown, and at one point had to walk a tightrope along the sidelines to stay in bounds before finding a clear path to the end zone. The run set a new career-high for Samuel, whose previous long was a 51-yard run back in 2022. Things went about as well as they could have for Samuel, who was playing in his first game since Week 5. Despite the strong outing, Samuel has averaged just 6.0 opportunities per game in his last three games, and his three targets in this one tied Jordan Watkins for fourth-most on the team. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a WR4 next week against the Vikings.

items.name: CeeDee Lamb
items.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-13 passes for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t be disappointed with the end result, but this was a frustrating game for Lamb. It became apparent early on that he would be taking a backseat to George Pickens, who saw six targets on the Cowboys’ first two drives of the game. Lamb saw nine of his 13 targets in the second half, and he was particularly productive in the fourth quarter, catching five passes for 49 yards and hauling in a one-yard touchdown pass with less than a minute to go in regulation. Despite Lamb needing every last second of this one to hit his expectations from a fantasy perspective, we don’t expect that to be the case for him most weeks. He’ll remain in the high-end WR1 conversation next week against the Titans.

items.name: Javonte Williams
items.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers, adding one reception for four additional yards.
items.analysis: Williams wasn’t particularly efficient in this one, averaging just 3.9 YPC, with his longest run coming on a nine-yard gain late in the game. Williams saw half of his rush attempts come on the Cowboys’ first two drives of the game, but was mainly an afterthought in the second half when the Cowboys entered the fourth quarter trailing 31-19. The negative game script certainly didn’t help Williams in this one, but his volume continues to keep him in the RB2 conversation. He’ll look for better results in Week 11 when the Cowboys take on the Titans.

items.name: Blake Corum
items.headline: Blake Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 19 yards.
items.analysis: Corum was the star of today’s show. He got involved partway through the Rams’ first drive, lining up in a two-running back set alongside Kyren Williams. The Rams’ immediate successes out of this formation led to a whole lot of it for the rest of the game. The shifty third-year running back hogged touches for stretches, playing so well as a rusher and receiver that having an eight-yard run erased by a penalty was a non-issue for fantasy purposes. Corum is a locked-in RB2 with RB1 upside. Treat him accordingly against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that Aidan Hutchinson (knee) will undergo imaging, and the Lions are “very concerned.”
items.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hutchinson is expected to be out “for the foreseeable future.” Although nothing is concrete yet, Florio’s report generally supports Rapoport’s sentiment. The Lions precariously sit atop the NFC North at 7-2. Both the Vikings and Bears share that record, while the Packers sit in fourth at 6-4. Losing Hutchinson would make this team even more reliant on explosive offensive performances than it already is.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 1-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: LaPorta’s slump continued with another quiet outing today. Backup tight end Brock Wright out-produced him in PPR formats with two catches for 11 yards, albeit on just two targets. He has nine catches for 99 yards over his past four appearances. With so many mouths to feed in the Detroit offense, LaPorta is increasingly looking like the odd man out. He will get one more week in the TE1 ranks. If things don’t turn around versus the Bucs in Week 11, fantasy managers might need to explore other options.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that the Patriots expect Drake Maye (ankle) to be sidelined for “a while.”
items.analysis: Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter against the Lions today and was unable to return. We expect more updates to follow after Maye undergoes further testing once the team returns from Germany. The Patriots go on bye in Week 11, but it sounds like the early indications are that Maye will be sidelined beyond that. They face the Chargers in Week 12 and the division-rival Bills in Week 13.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Parkinson was barely involved today, though he nearly scored a touchdown on the Rams’ sixth drive. He successfully high-pointed a red zone pass, but tumbled out of bounds at the one-yard line, tangled up with a Cardinals defender. Parkinson will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Tyler Higbee
items.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 3-of-4 targets for 17 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Higbee earned an end zone target on the Rams’ opening drive, but Matthew Stafford overthrew him, resulting in an incompletion. The two did manage to link up for a score on the Rams’ fourth drive, though. Rams coach Sean McVay dialed up a play where Higbee motioned from in-line to out wide on the left side. He ran right past his coverage defender, and Stafford hit him streaking toward the back of the end zone for a five-yard touchdown. Higbee will likely be a low-end TE1 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Davis Allen
items.headline: Davis Allen caught 1-of-1 targets in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Allen played a small role, but made a big impact today, scoring from 19 yards out on a nice catch-and-run on the Rams’ seventh drive. Allen lined up in-line on the right side before slipping across the field mid-play, seemingly without any Cardinals defenders noticing. He easily hauled in the pass and turned upfield for the score. Allen will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, post-bye, in Week 12.

items.name: Xavier Smith
items.headline: Xavier Smith caught 2-of-2 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Smith could have scored a 72-yard touchdown on the Rams’ third drive, but he was brought down by a shoestring tackle while trying to turn upfield. He made up for it with a 22-yard screen pass touchdown on the Rams’ fifth drive, in which he weaved through the middle of the field before cutting north into the end zone. The Rams go on bye next week, before facing the Packers in Week 12. He does not qualify as a much-stash player at this time.

items.name: Konata Mumpfield
items.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 3-of-4 targets for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Mumpfield had a decent game today, producing catches of 10, 27 and 45 yards, notably adding decent yardage post-catch on his two longest receptions. He was also targeted on Matthew Stafford’s interception, but it was simply an off-target throw. Mumpfield generated his longest gain with a slick hitch-and-go, leaving his defender in the dust on the false step. The Rams go on bye in Week 11 and face the Packers in Week 12. Davante Adams (hamstring) is targeting a Week 13 return. Mumpfield should be FLEX-viable in Week 12, though he will likely become quite volatile when Adams returns.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens caught 11-of-18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: In his first game since owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys needed to focus more on getting the ball to Pickens, the 25-year-old receiver saw passes funneled to him early and often. Pickens was targeted six times on the Cowboys’ first two drives and capped the second drive with a 35-yard touchdown to give the Cowboys their first touchdown of the day. Pickens would find the end zone two more times in this one, with his second score coming on a 39-yard play on a long catch-and-run. His last score would come on a five-yard pass from Dak Prescott as the Cowboys aimed to keep pace with the Niners late in the fourth quarter, but it ultimately proved to not be enough in the end. Despite his struggles at various points this season, Pickens was far from an underutilized receiver, as he entered the day averaging a solid 7.8 targets per game. It goes without saying that we shouldn’t expect this kind of performance every week from Pickens, but he will be on the fantasy radar next week as a mid-to-high-end WR2.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and one touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys, adding four receptions for 161 yards and two touchdowns.
items.analysis: McCaffrey was at his best in what can only be described as a legacy game for the 30-year-old running back. A relatively pedestrian line on the ground (12-62-1) proved to be nothing but a footnote in the box score for McCaffrey, who needed just four catches to set a new career high with 161 receiving yards. McCaffrey ripped off scores of 74 and 66 yards through the air, doing most of his damage after the catch. Of his 161 receiving yards, 141 of those yards came after the ball was in his hands, and his second score went virtually uncontested by a helpless Von Miller in man coverage. McCaffrey’s 223 yards from scrimmage were just 14 off his career high, and marked the fifth time in his career that he has gone for 200-plus yards from scrimmage. He will look to follow up this elite performance in Week 11 when the Niners “host” the Vikings in Mexico City.

items.name: Dak Prescott
items.headline: Dak Prescott completed 30-of-51 passes for 343 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 46-40, Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Facing a Niners offense that scored a touchdown on six of its 11 possessions, Prescott and the Cowboys needed to be nearly perfect if they hoped to keep pace. Dak orchestrated an 11-play, 71-yard drive on the Cowboys’ second drive of the game, capping it with a 35-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens, who found the end zone a career-high three times in this one. Prescott’s two touchdown passes in the first half had the Cowboys trailing 17-16 at halftime, but after being outscored 14-3 in the third quarter, Prescott and the company aired it out 24 times in the fourth quarter as they aimed to keep pace. Prescott threw a five-yard touchdown to Pickens to get the Cowboys within seven points, and responded on the following drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy to cut the Niners’ lead to 38-32. Unfortunately, that would be as close as the Cowboys would get, as the 49ers would need just two plays to go up by double digits, which proved to be too much for Dallas to overcome, even after a one-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb. This is the kind of game the Cowboys are capable of posting any given week, especially if they are being pushed by the opposing team. We wouldn’t expect Cam Ward and the Titans to push them next week in the way the Niners did this week, but Prescott will be in the QB1 mix in what looks to be a plus matchup at home.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy completed 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 46-40, Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Facing a porous Cowboys defense, Purdy and the Niners delivered just about everything fantasy managers could have hoped for in this one. Despite taking five sacks on the day, Purdy was nearly perfect, throwing just six incompletions while coming up with multiple big plays. Purdy’s first touchdown pass came on an 11-yard bubble screen to Deebo Samuel, with his other two coming on long catch-and-runs by Christian McCaffrey. In the second quarter, Purdy tossed a 14-yard pass to McCaffrey, which CMC immediately turned upfield for a 74-yard score, and in the fourth quarter, another six-yard pass to CMC in the face of a blitz resulted in a 66-yard score after the Cowboys left Von Miller in coverage against McCaffrey. Purdy’s three touchdowns resulted in 151 passing yards, but came on passes that combined for just 20 air yards. That’s the benefit of playing with elite playmakers like CMC. Purdy and the Niners will get a true test in Week 11 when they take on the Vikings in Mexico City. We cautiously project Purdy as a QB1 despite the tough matchup on paper.

items.name: Matthew Stafford
items.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 18-of-26 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Rams’ 34-6, Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Rams lost two centers to injury today, but Stafford navigated the resulting offensive line shuffling without issue, completing passes to nine different pass catchers. Stafford probably should have had a fourth touchdown added to his box score, but he overthrew Tyler Higbee and CJ Daniels in the end zone on the opening drive, which ultimately resulted in a field goal. A touchdown pass thrown to Kyren Williams was called back due to a false start on the Rams’ fourth drive, but Stafford linked up with Higbee for a score a couple of plays later. A similar sequence occurred in which Stafford threw a touchdown pass to Xavier Smith on the following drive, after Tutu Atwell failed to secure what should have been a 32-yard touchdown. Stafford’s second-drive interception was on him. He threw an off-target pass to Konatha Mumpfield, which a Cardinals defender easily caught. All in all, Stafford dealt with the Rams’ offensive personnel issues well. He will be a low-end QB1 against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Joey Slye
items.headline: Joey Slye converted all three of his field goal attempts in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Slye also connected on both of his PATs. Most importantly, he laid out Josh Cameron in kick coverage. The bone-crunching hit knocked the ball out of Cameron’s hands, though the Jags ultimately fell on the loose ball. Slye isn’t a reliable fantasy option, but he deserves his flowers for two combined tackles and a forced fumble on top of the solid kicking performance.

items.name: DeShon Elliott
items.headline: Steelers declared QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar ,RB Eli Heidenreich, S DeShon Elliott, and CB Sean Murphy-Bunting inactive for Week 10 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Elliott suffered a knee injury in warmups and was announced as out just 15 minutes prior to inactives being released. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback while rookie running back Eli Heidenreich is inactive for the seventh consecutive contest. The absence of Elliott is a massive blow, leaving defensive coordinator Patrick Graham to scramble to adjust his game plan mere hours before first kick.

items.name: Landon Robinson
items.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, T Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 10 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and the team is missing contributing tight ends, but the Bengals enter the second half of the season as one of the healthier teams in the league. The winner of this game will move into sole possession of the division lead in what has become the most competitive division in the AFC.

items.name: Andrew Armstrong
items.headline: Andrew Armstrong caught a 43-yard touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Armstrong’s fourth quarter score was his only target, and just his third catch of the season. It was certainly notable in that it came on a freelance, somewhat broken play with Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs really had their down-field attack cooking in Atlanta, and it could remain a theme for Week 11 against the Cardinals. Fun for fantasy, but 26-year-old, second-year UDFA Armstrong remains nothing more than a deep, deep Dynasty league curiosity.

items.name: Cyrus Allen
items.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: The Chiefs finally got their deep passing attack going and Allen was a big part of it, catching a 39-yard touchdown where he took advantage of a “stutter and go” to beat A.J. Terrell in 1-on-1 coverage. It was the kind of play the Chiefs have been dying for from one of their role players since Tyquan Thornton was lost for the season. Allen, Rashee Rice, and Andrew Armstrong all had long “air yards” conversions this afternoon, perhaps signaling the arrival of a new-look attack with Josh Downs’ addition hopefully improving the Chiefs’ spacing and timing. Good stuff for them, but not terribly relevant for Allen in fantasy, who remains miles from 12-team league relevance.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Although this was only Dotson’s second three-catch performance of the season, this has rather amazingly become something of his weekly statline. Not that it is amounting to anything in fantasy football. It definitely won’t when the Falcons come off bye to face the Vikings in Week 12. Dotson can remain firmly affixed to 12-team league waiver wires.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Kelce missed large chunks of the first and second quarter with injury, but returned to finish the game without incident. It initially appeared Kelce aggravated his pre-existing ankle issue, but coach Andy Reid said afterward it was a calf ailment. That likely means cramps. That also means it’s not a big concern for Week 11 against the Cardinals, but with Josh Downs in tow to finally provide another legitimate target for Patrick Mahomes, Kelce’s TE1 floor is probably lowering for the stretch run.

items.name: Zane Gonzalez
items.headline: Zane Gonzalez converted 1-of-3 field goal attempts in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
items.analysis: Gonzalez just recently became the Dolphins’ full-time kicker, but he missed two field goals and one extra point against the Colts. He had the opportunity to kick the go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter, but missed from 51 yards. He also missed a 47-yarder earlier in the game while making a 53-yarder and missing an extra point in the third quarter. In a game the Dolphins lost by two points, Gonzalez leaving seven points on the field certainly contributed towards the outcome of this game. If he is still on the team next week, Gonzalez should not be a fantasy option in Week 11.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard rushed nine times for 33 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars, adding eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Pollard was bottled up on the ground throughout this contest, but Cam Ward leaned on him for easy completions as the Titans played from behind. Pollard eventually cashed in on one of them with a 32-yard score on a simple check-dowk. Pollard broke several tackle attempts from Jagaurs defenders that could only be descried as effortless. The return of Tyjae Spear had no impact on his role, though that could change as Spears gets healthier. Pollard remains a volume-based RB2 for his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

items.name: Xavier Worthy
items.headline: Xavier Worthy was held without a reception on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: With Josh Downs making his Chiefs debut, Patrick Mahomes had his best game since 2022. Worthy, sadly, could not get in on the fun, turning in his first 2026 “zero ball” while only really popping up during the broadcast when he failed to corral a fourth quarter onside kick attempt. Worthy was playing through a hamstring injury, but he did not look much worse for the wear. Today was sad confirmation that what little WR4 value Worthy had left is probably now gone with Downs’ arrival. That includes even for plus dates like next week’s contest with the Cardinals.

items.name: DaRon Bland
items.headline: Cowboys S DaRon Bland (ankle) will not return in Week 10’s game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Bland could be seen having his right ankle tended to on the sideline in the second quarter of Sunday’s game. The 27-year-old corner was ruled out at the beginning of the second half and entered the game with an ankle injury that had him listed as questionable entering the weekend. Hopefully this isn’t an issue that plagues him for too long, as Dallas can ill-afford to lose its top defenders.

items.name: Daniel Bellinger
items.headline: Daniel Bellinger caught 2-of-3 targets for six yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Belinger caught a goal line touchdown in the second quarter. It was his first touchdown as a Titan. It was also the first receiving touchdown for any Titans tight end this year. Bellinger isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 11, but his presence should preent fantasy managers from having interest in Gunnar Helm.

items.name: George Holani
items.headline: George Holani (knee) has been ruled out in Week 10.
items.analysis: Holani picked up the knee injury in the first half against the Raiders and did not return. The Seattle rushing offense has revolved around Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price in recent weeks, leaving Holani out of the backfield fold. He can remain on waivers ahead of Week 11.

items.name: Kyle Pitts
items.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 4-of-5 targets for 50 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: The four catches were Pitts’ most in three weeks, while the 50 yards were his second most of the season. Unfortunately, that latter stat tells you all you need to know about Pitts’ TE1 viability right now — he doesn’t have any. He’s also now been held scoreless in 7-of-10 appearances. Headed on bye before returning against the Vikings’ shutdown defense, Pitts is a drop candidate in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: Tyler Shough completed 25-of-35 attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panther, adding six rushes for 25 yards.
items.analysis: Shough continued his wildly inefficient ways. He faced constant pressure from a Carolina front seven that entered the week with the league’s sixth lowest QB pressure rate, and missed short and intermediate throws throughout. Shough had a miserable aDOT of 4.5 and had a -8 total EPA on the day. The disjointed Saints offense doesn’t make things easy for Shough, but his total inability to make routine throws is having a real impact on Saints pass catchers. Shough should be considered a superflex-only option in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.name: Chimere Dike
items.headline: Chimere Dike caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Coming off a 5-71-1 receiving line versus the Bengals, Dike appeared to be taking on a larger role in the absence of Carnell Tate. That wasn’t the case versus Jacksonville and he finished fifth on the team in targets. Even desperate fantasy managers can send him back to the waiver wire ahead of Week 11.

items.name: Gunnar Helm
items.headline: Gunnar Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Helm is up to 16 catches over his past four games, but he’s still looking for his first touchdown of the year. Daniel Bellinger stole a short score in this game. Helm also has just one game over 30 yards to his name. He’s developed a modest PPR floor, but there’s no ceiling to be had headed into his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

items.name: Kevin Coleman
items.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 1-of-6 targets for six yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
items.analysis: Coleman was second on the Dolphins with six targets on the day, though he caught just one for six yards. He also drew a key defensive pass interference against Sauce Gardner in the second quarter. With Chris Bell (knee) out, Coleman was No. 3 in wide receiver snaps for the Dolphins. He can be rostered in 14-team leagues as a desperation boom-or-bust play for Week 11 against the Bills.

items.name: Elic Ayomanor
items.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 5-of-10 targets for 79 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Ayomanor didn’t do much in Carnell Tate’s absence the last time he took the field. He stepped up as the Titans’ clear WR1 in this game. Ayomanor led the team in all receiving categories except touchdowns. He nearly led the way in scoring as well, but the Jags tracked him down inside the five-yard line on his 50-yard catch. Ayomanor will move into the FLEX mix if Tate remains out for Week 11 against the Cowboys.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara had two rushes for four yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 10 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Kamara somehow came up with both Saints touchdowns on the day even with Travis Etienne returning from injury and operating as the de facto RB1. Kamara didn’t even lead the backfield in routes, logging 13 pass routes to 14 for Etienne, who had three grabs for 20 yards. Fantasy managers would do well not to chase Kamara’s Week 10 touchdown production when the Saints take on the Bears in Week 11.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich failed to catch either of his two targets in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
items.analysis: Dulcich saw just two targets on the day but did not reel either of them in. Kyle McCord targeted him on a red zone fourth down in the second quarter, but the ball was tipped and fell incomplete. Six teams going on bye in Week 11 means Dulcich still nets low-end TE2 consideration against the Bills.

items.name: Drake London
items.headline: Drake London caught 6-of-12 targets for 109 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: London also drew an 18-yard DPI. The 100-yard game was somehow London’s first in five weeks. It was also just his third of the season. After starting off on a high note with Michael Penix, London has been reduced to scrounging for volume of late. Things aren’t going to get any better coming off the Falcons’ bye in Week 12, where they must venture to Minnesota to take on the Vikings’ elite defense. That figures to be more of a WR2 day for London before the WR1 times are good again in Week 13 vs. the Lions.

items.name: Jalen Tolbert
items.headline: Jalen Tolbert caught 2-of-2 targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
items.analysis: Tolbert caught the Dolphins’ sole receiving touchdown of the day on a trick play pass from Malik Washington. He was wide open for a 34-yard score in the second quarter. Tolbert caught his only other target and was otherwise quiet with just 11 offensive snaps. Despite the score, Tolbert should be left on fantasy benches heading into Week 11 against the Bills.

items.name: Audric Estime
items.headline: Audric Estime had seven rushes for six yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding one catch for one yard.
items.analysis: Estime was shockingly ineffective a week after he led the Saints backfield with 15 rushing attempts for 72 yards and a touchdown. Travis Etienne returned from injury this week and operated as the nominal RB1 for the disastrous New Orleans offense. Estime won’t hold any fantasy value as long as Etienne is healthy and active.

items.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
items.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-4 targets for 10 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Robinson struggled to stand out in a Titans receiving room that was without Carnell Tate today. He logged a measly 10 percent target share and was relegated to check-down duties. Robinson has yet to hit 60 yards in a game this year and the PPR volume is not materializing. He will be buried in the WR4/5 range when the Titans take on the Cowboys next week.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington caught 3-of-3 targets for 50 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, completing his sole passing attempt for 34 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Washington led all Dolphins wide receivers in snaps, but fell behind Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman in targets. He caught all three of his targets, including a circus catch to reel in a dangerous throw from Kyle McCord in the third quarter. The Dolphins also dialed up some trickery in the second quarter with Washington taking a toss and finding Jalen Tolbert downfield for a 34-yard passing touchdown. Ultimately, Washington is on the field a lot for the Dolphins and still ranks in the WR4 range for Week 11 against the Bills.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Spears didn’t gain any yards on his only catch of the day. Tony Pollard, on the other hand, caught eight passes and rushed nine times. Spears missed three weeks with a knee issue and likely had his snaps limited by the team today. On the other hand, Pollard has played well this year and the team chose to hold onto him at the trade deadline despite receiving some interest. Spears is likely stuck in a backup role headed into Week 11. He will be an RB4 when the Titans take on the Cowboys.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 3-of-8 targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
items.analysis: Douglas and Malik Washington led the Dolphins in wide receiver snaps on the day and Douglas paced the pass-catching group with eight targets and 71 total yards. He was a key target for Kyle McCord in the second half, making a 38-yard reception in the third quarter. He also drew a defensive pass interference and added a leaping 22-yard grab in the fourth quarter. Douglas is the clear WR1 in the Dolphins’ offense and McCord has shown he can keep the 23-year-old rookie involved in the offense. With a Week 11 matchup against the Bills on the horizon, Douglas is a fantasy WR3.

items.name: Bijan Robinson
items.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Robinson added four receptions for six yards. The Chiefs’ defense wasn’t set on Robinson’s three-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. Robinson has now found the end zone in back-to-back games after somehow previously going four straight weeks without a score. So it goes in what is becoming an increasingly dysfunctional offense. Robinson and company are now headed on bye before returning in Week 12 against the imposing Vikings. You won’t be benching Robinson for that one, of course, but you will be limiting your high-end RB1 expectations.

items.name: Cam Ward
items.headline: Cam Ward completed 28-of-39 passes for 231 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Titans’ 40-23, Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Ward also led the Titans with 39 rushing yards. He got off to an ugly start by throwing an interception to Travis Hunter. Ward attempted a throw across his body to a receiver with very little separation. He didn’t lead Elic Ayomanor enough and Hunter made a great play on the ball. Ward improved throughout the contest, but not enough to make this an awfully competitive game. Still, he threw two touchdown passes for the second time this year. The first was in Week 8 before Tennessee’s bye. Ward will be worth a look as a streamer when he takes on the Cowboys next week, though only as a low-end QB2.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: Travis Etienne had eight rushes for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 20 yards.
items.analysis: The Saints wasted a few first half plays trying to get Etienne involved in his first game back from an extended injury absence. Those plays predictably went nowhere, and it was Alvin Kamara who had the big fantasy day, scoring both Saints touchdowns — one through the air, the other on the ground. Etienne logged 13 routes to 12 routes for Kamara. The Saints backfield is among the least appealing for fantasy purposes and has been for some time. Etienne will be a desperation deep league option in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.name: Josh Cameron
items.headline: Josh Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Cameron was on the receiving end of a pair of deep shots from Trevor Lawrence. The first was a long contested catch on the boundary and the second was a layup touchdown. Cameron was completely uncovered for a 25-yard touchdown strike. It was his third score of the year. Cameron is a better real-life player than a fantasy option, but he’ll at least be on the radar as a high-risk FLEX play for Week 11 against the Giants.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed 3 times for a loss of two yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding 2 receptions for 17 yards.
items.analysis: Wright is still the Dolphins’ backup running back, though this has led to limited opportunities behind Ollie Gordon. He saw 12 snaps on the day and only has fantasy value as a handcuff to Gordon moving forward.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 3-of-7 targets for 35 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
items.analysis: None of the Carolina pass catchers did much in a game that saw the Panthers go ultra run-heavy. McMillan led the team in targets but was never on the same page with Bryce Young, who had one of his worst games of the season. On the season McMillan has four games with at least 75 yards, along with five games of at least five receptions. McMillan will be a WR2 option in Week 11 against a shaky Ravens secondary.

items.name: Ollie Gordon
items.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding four receptions for 39 yards.
items.analysis: Gordon continues to operate as the Dolphins’ workhorse back, getting 20-of-23 running back carries on the day. He also saw five targets out of the backfield, operating as a useful target in the flats for Kyle McCord. Passing game utilization as a an easy-button target elevated his fantasy production on a day he did not score a touchdown. Gordon will continue to see a heavy workload en route to RB2 fantasy viability for Week 11 against the Bills.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Michael Penix completed 23-of-43 passes for 286 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception in the Falcons’ 35-13, Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Michael Penix completed 23-of-43 passes for 286 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception in the Falcons’ 35-13, Week 10 loss to the Chiefs, adding four rushes for 29 yards.
items.analysis: Penix now has just one total score over his past three starts. Although the 286 yards look nice in the box score, Penix had only 86 at the break. A huge chunk of his production came with the Falcons in frantic fourth quarter comeback mode, and the “comeback” was never particularly realistic. No longer looking like a solid matchup-based streamer, Penix now goes on bye before coming off the open date vs. the Vikings’ ferocious defense. Things do get better in Week 12 against the Lions, but that’s a long time from now.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) has been ruled out in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: A player rolled on Bowers’ ankle in the first quarter and after a trip to the blue medical tent, he was not able to return to action. The injury-marred Bowers could be in for yet another absence, making Michael Mayer a viable fantasy option in most formats. Bowers had one catch for six yards before he suffered the ankle injury.

items.name: Tommy Tremble
items.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-5 targets for 48 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
items.analysis: Darren Waller, meanwhile, caught two of his four targets for 24 yards and nearly came down with a long touchdown in the first half. Tremble ran a route on 18 of 37 Carolina drop backs in a Carolina offense that has increased its two tight end usage. Tremble now has eight receptions over his past two games. He plays the Ravens in Week 11.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Tyler Warren caught 2-of-3 targets for one yard in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding one carry for three yards.
items.analysis: Warren was non-existent in the Colts’ passing game, converting three targets into just one yard. He did get a third-and-short carry that he took for three yards, but four total yards is an immensely disappointing day for the Colts’ supposed new No. 1 pass-catcher. Still on the field for nearly every offensive snap, Warren will see better days of utilization. His ceiling is capped in the Colts offense, but Warren sits on the TE1/2 borderline for Week 11 against the Texans.

items.name: Travis Hunter
items.headline: Travis Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans, adding one rush for three yards.
items.analysis: Hunter’s highlight of the day came on defense when he made a diving interception in the first quarter. He played sparingly on offense once again. Hunter is a starting corner who sees a few snaps on offense every week. He is not on the fantasy radar for his Week 11 game against the Giants.

items.name: Brenton Strange
items.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for nine yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Strange saved an otherwise bust of a fantasy outing with a touchdown in the third quarter. Liam Coen schemed him open via a rub route at the goal line for an easy three-yard score. Strange has seven targets over his past three games. After a promising start to the year, he’s fallen to the middle of the TE2 pack headed into Week 11.

items.name: Ashton Dulin
items.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Dulin saw two targets, catching one for an explosive 30-yard gain. He led all Colts pass-catchers in receiving yardage. Dulin saw just 13 offensive snaps and is a boom-or-bust fantasy play. He does not need to be rostered until further notice.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers exited the Raiders’ Week 10 game with an ankle injury.
items.analysis: A player rolled on Bowers’ ankle in a first quarter rushing play and after a trip to the blue medical tent, Bowers was helped to the locker room in the second quarter. The oft-injured Bowers seems unlikely to return. He would end his day with one catch for six yards, possibly looking at yet another injury stint.

items.name: J. Michael Sturdivant
items.headline: J. Michael Sturdivant caught 2-of-4 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Sturdivant found the end zone in the third quarter when Jordan Love connected with him on a 32-yard score. Sturdivant broke free behind his defender and found a hole to secure the long catch, giving the rookie UDFA his first career touchdown. Sturdivant was the only Packers player to score in a game that was dominated by the Vikings’ defense for most of the afternoon. He won’t be on the fantasy radar when the Packers return from their bye in Week 12 to face the Rams.

items.name: Kaleb Johnson
items.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed 10 times for 42 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Johnson’s 10 carries and 42 rushing yards both led the Packers, who also mixed in MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks throughout the day. While Johnson failed to replicate the 14-68-1 performance he had in Week 9 against the Patriots, his 10 carries were more than double those of the next closest back. The Packers are now entering their Week 11 bye, but if Josh Jacobs (thumb) is unable to go in Week 12 against the Rams, Johnson could have some boom-or-bust RB3/Flex appeal.

items.name: Anthony Gould
items.headline: Anthony Gould caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Gould operated as the Colts’ starting slot receiver, replacing Josh Downs. He led all Indy pass-catchers with a meager four targets, converting them into two receptions for 28 yards. Gould was shaken up after getting hit hard on a punt return, but he stayed in the game. The Colts’ pass-catchers don’t offer much fantasy upside but Gould is a desperation WR5 for Week 11 against the Texans.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: A week after breaking out for 171 yards and a score, Watson and the rest of the Packers’ explosive passing game were grounded by the physical Vikings defense. Jordan Love and company failed to generate many downfield plays on the day and were instead forced to settle for more short and intermediate throws, which the Vikings immediately shut down. Watson’s biggest play came on a 15-yard reception in the first quarter on a drive that ended with a missed field goal by Trey Smack. He will be on the fantasy radar as a high-end WR2 in Week 12 when the Packers return from their bye week to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

items.name: Chris Olave
items.headline: Chris Olave caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: Jordyn Tyson, in his second NFL game, took over for at least one week as the team’s clear WR1, drawing 13 targets and finishing with 80 yards on 11 grabs. Olave, who did not record a reception until late in the third quarter, saw nothing downfield as Tyler Shough was under constant duress against a Carolina defense that entered the week with one of the lowest QB pressure rates in the NFL. Olave entered Week 10 with a 27 percent target share and a 47 percent air yards share. Tyson’s emergence could be a major issue for Olave if this sort of usage continues in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.name: Laquon Treadwell
items.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Treadwell is the de factor WR1 for the Colts with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen dealt at the trade deadline. He led all receivers in snaps while scoring the team’s sole receiving touchdown in the red zone towards the end of the second quarter. The Colts passing game won’t generate many scoring opportunities with a depleted receiving corps and Daniel Jones’ constant struggles. However, Treadwell is the best bet to roster for fantasy purposes. He is a fantasy WR4 for Week 11 against the Texans.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Week 10 will be one for Meyers to forget. He dropped a deep shot from Trevor Lawrence on a trick play. Lawrence, admittedly, underthrew the ball, forcing Meyers to turn around and fight through contact at the catch point. Meyers dropped another touchdown later in the game that was more than catchable. Meyers hasn’t scored since Week 3 and has caught more than five passes in two games this year. He’s struggling to provide even WR4 value ahead of the Jags’ Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
items.analysis: Waller ran a route on 27 of the team’s 38 drop backs and should have caught what would have been a 30-yard touchdown in the first half. Coming off a big game in Week 9 against the Broncos, Waller was fourth on the team in targets as the Panthers turned hard toward the run. Tommy Tremble had more targets, receptions, and yards than Waller on the day. Waller’s red zone role and the Panthers usual pass heaviness should keep him viable as a streaming option in Week 11 against Baltimore.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-2 targets for 3 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Sadiq is becoming buried on the Jets’ depth chart. He did run a route on 23 dropbacks in this one, compared to 28 for Mason Taylor, but Taylor played 23 more snaps, and Sadiq also has to compete with three receivers for targets. He can’t be trusted in fantasy leagues right now and should not be on redraft rosters unless there’s an injury.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: BTJ split the WR3 duties with Josh Cameron once again. Cameron, however, racked up 67 yards and a touchdown on three grabs. Thomas hasn’t even topped 40 yards in a game this year. He’s a part-time decoy who spends most of his routes clearing out space for Parker Washington. With the trade deadline in the rearview mirror, fantasy managers can safely send BTJ to the waiver wire on the upcoming run.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: Schultz’s only grab of the game was Houston’s only score of the second half, a ball C.J. Stroud lofted over zone coverage in the end zone to find Schultz at the back of it. It was a low-end outcome for Schultz, who had his lowest target count of the season. He’ll remain a high-end TE2 play against the Colts in Week 11 on Thursday.

items.name: Seth McGowan
items.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: McGowan eclipsed his previous career-high with 12 carries in the Colts’ win. He continues to be involved, eating into Jonathan Taylor’s workload with a few red zone carries and a four-yard rushing touchdown to open the second quarter. McGowan was not involved in the passing game and Taylor still saw 23 more snaps. However, it seems like McGowan is here to stay as a playmaker for the Colts offense with a rushing score for the second straight game. He should be on fantasy rosters as a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 11 against the Texans.

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Taylor played 52 of the team’s 70 snaps in this game, with Kenyon Sadiq only playing 29. Sadiq did run a route on 23 dropbacks compared to 28 for Taylor, but it’s clear that Taylor is the top tight end on the Jets. It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

items.name: Tank Dell
items.headline: Tank Dell caught 3-of-4 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: He added a zero-yard carry. His longest catch was for 29 yards. That about sums up his other four targets. Dell wasn’t able to shake man coverage very often and the Browns put the clamps on in the second half. He managed just 33-of-67 snaps. He’ll remain on the FLEX line against the Colts on Thursday night in what should be a more zone-heavy game.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed four times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Rodriguez spent most of the day watching Bhayshul Tuten rack up a career-high 29 touches, 26 of which were carries. Tuten also saw all the goal line work and eventually found the end zone late in the fourth quarter. With Tuten’s role on the rise, fantasy managers can likely cut ties with Rodriguez ahead of Week 11. He will be buried in the RB4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Williams stepped into a bigger role with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) leaving this game after the Jets’ first offensive play. The 25-year-old could have had a bigger day, but a long catch-and-run was called back due to offsetting penalties. If Cooper Jr. were to miss Week 11, Williams could be a deep league FLEX option against the Chargers, but he’s likely not in for a huge role.

items.name: Xavier Hutchinson
items.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-9 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: His touchdown catch came on a misdirection play where he camped out and waited for the Browns to react to the initial action before getting a wide-open path to the end zone. After Tank Dell returned and the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., there remained Hutchinson, now with three touchdowns in three games after the bye. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts this week with six teams on bye.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington caught 7-of-9 targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Washington was unstoppable in the first half with three gains of 30 or more yards plus a short touchdown. He entered halftime with six grabs for 148 yards. The fact that he was on pace for nearly 300 yards and finished with “only” 152 is a slightly disappointing outcome, but there wasn’t much of a reason for the Jags to keep airing it out in the second half. The Titans weren’t putting up much of a fight on offense and the Jags leaned on their ground game, preventing Washington from having a truly insane day. Fantasy managers will have to live with their 28.2 PPR points. Washington is pushing for a WR1 ranking as he heads into a Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: One of the incomplete passes was one that hit Mitchell in the hands, and he had two feet in bounds, but he let go of the ball to readjust his grip and was unable to remain in bounds, wiping out a 15-yard gain. With Omar Cooper Jr. leaving this game with an ankle injury, Mitchell could have a more dependable role next week against the Chargers, which would put him on the FLEX radar.

items.name: Nico Collins
items.headline: Nico Collins caught 9-of-16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 win over the Browns.
items.analysis: Despite the fun line, it wasn’t exactly a game that left you feeling great about Collins. He looked heavily fatigued at times, notably grabbing his shoulder after one sideline collision, and also managed to cut short a route that led to C.J. Stroud’s only interception and cost the Texans at least three points at the end of the first half. Assuming he’s healthy, he’ll be in the WR1 mix again next week against the Colts on Thursday night.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-14 targets for 106 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: No other Jets player had more than seven targets, so Wilson was the clear focus of the passing attack. That continued when Cade Klubnik came into the game as well. Wilson made a few tough catches and was targeted twice in the end zone as well. Unfortunately, the wide receiver was also charged with a fumble on a botched hook-and-ladder play where he was hit as he was attempting the pitch, which went astray and was recovered by the Bills. Wilson remains the clear top option in this passing attack and could still be a low-end WR2 with Klubnik under center next week against the Chargers.

items.name: Emari Demercado
items.headline: Emari Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: 13 of those yards came on one carry. Demercado saw the bulk of the opportunities with Woody Marks (concussion) sidelined in the third quarter.
