Both Demercado’s history and the broader history of Texans running backs over the past several years would tell you there’s little fantasy value in him next week assuming that he becomes their main ballcarrier. Nevertheless, with six teams on bye, he’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts if David Montgomery remains sidelined.

items.name: C.J. Stroud
items.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 20-of-38 passes for 211 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in Houston’s 27-24, Week 10 loss to the Browns.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion caught 3-of-8 passes for 21 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans, adding a six-yard touchdown rush on his only carry.
items.analysis: He dropped a perfectly-placed deep ball in the first quarter and was seen riding an exercise bike on the sideline afterwards, but he got off the bench and scored on a misdirection touchdown play in the third quarter. With a 129-yard game and two touchdowns mixed among his last four games, Concepcion should likely remain in the WR3 mix as we hit his bye week.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Kincaid had one huge play in the third quarter, with a 54-yard catch down the sideline. There wasn’t much else to his day, but he was targeted in the end zone on a play that wound up being called defensive pass interference. He remains more of a high-end TE2 in a crowded passing attack in Buffalo.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker did not catch any of his four targets in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
items.analysis: Coker had one rush for three yards but was otherwise invisible. The usually pass-first Panthers went mega run-heavy against the Saints, limiting targets for every Carolina pass catcher. Coker, who ran a route on 33 of 36 Panthers drop backs, was seen yelling in frustration on the sideline in the second half. Coker has done almost nothing since his Week 1 explosion against the Bears. He has four or fewer receptions in five games this season. Coker will be a deep league flex in Week 11 against Baltimore.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Daniel Jones completed 11-of-22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Colts’ 24-22, Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding five carries for nine yards.
items.analysis: With a pass-catching group depleted after the trade deadline, the Colts offense did just enough to beat the Dolphins. Jones was nearly intercepted on the first pass of the game while he fumbled out of bounds on the Colts’ second possession. He threw a fourth-down interception in the second quarter, but recovered with a touchdown pass to Laquon Treadwell towards the end of the first half. The Colts offense faltered yet again in the second half, with Jones throwing a pick-six in the third quarter and failing to connect with pass-catchers downfield. Colts fans booed the offense off the field nearly every fourth quarter possession. The Colts defense was responsible for one of the team’s touchdowns, with the offense only posting a field goal in the second half. Jones is not a quarterback that needs to be rostered for fantasy purposes; he should only be a desperation play for Superflex leagues for Week 11 against the Texans.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: He did manage some good punt returns, but the Browns weren’t able to get their deep-ball offense going and mostly let Derek Stingley take Boston out of the game. Boston isn’t necessarily a must-hold through shallow leagues at the bye, as he’s been held under 50 yards in five of his last six games, but the target count has been stronger than this dud generally, and he was likely playing hurt here.

items.name: Chuba Hubbard
items.headline: Chuba Hubbard had 27 rushes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding five catches for 72 yards.
items.analysis: The entire Carolina offense revolved around Hubbard in this one, as the Panthers ditched their pass-heavy approach for an ultra run-heavy offense against a middle New Orleans defense. Hubbard had a couple long plays and a touchdown called back on penalties too. He plodded along for much of the game before exploding for a long gain on a well-designed screen play late in the fourth quarter. Hubbard, who now has seven games with at least 17 rushes, has been one of the most reliable running backs in fantasy this season. That might change a bit when Jonathon Brooks returns from injury, perhaps in Week 11 against the Ravens.

items.name: Jerry Jeudy
items.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 74 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: He had a 65-yard field-flipper to get Cleveland their first score of the game. That was about the only deep pass the Browns connected on, but it got them going. Jeudy’s been a reasonable third wideout for the Browns this year but nobody you should consider keeping on fantasy rosters through a bye unless you’re in a very, very deep league.

items.name: Keon Coleman
items.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-3 passes for 11 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Coleman did make an impressive second catch in traffic, but the play was called back due to an illegal shift penalty. He also took a hit to his helmet on the same play and had to go into the blue medical tent. He was eventually cleared and returned to play, but it’s a situation to watch at practice this week.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin caught 7-of-9 targets for 91 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: Fannin appeared to be dinged up at some point in the third quarter, but came back no worse for the wear as he played on 59-of-68 Browns snaps. After spending the last two weeks on the injury report a Week 11 bye should help him get ready for the stretch run in Cleveland.

items.name: Khalil Shakir
items.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards receiving in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Shakir also added 29 yards rushing on three carries, but two of those were simply screens thrown backwards, so they counted as runs. When you factor that in, Shakir had five targets in this one, which was the second-most of any receiver on the Bills. He remains a safe floor option because of his consistent role in the offense, but there isn’t a big fantasy ceiling here unless he breaks multiple tackles after a short completion.

items.name: Kyle McCord
items.headline: Kyle McCord completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 24-22, Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding two carries for four yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Making his first career start in his NFL debut, McCord had a mix of explosive plays and turnover-worthy plays while taking three sacks on the day. The Dolphins offense committed a false start on the first snap and McCord briefly had his throwing hand looked at after hitting it on a helmet on the Dolphins’ first possession. He missed Greg Dulcich on a fourth down in the red zone in the first half and fumbled for a Colts touchdown to open the second half. McCord was able to hit more explosive plays in the fourth quarter with the Colts’ top two cornerbacks out with injury. He rushed for a touchdown to open the fourth quarter and get the Dolphins within two points. The Dolphins could not finish the comeback, mainly due to kicking woes. McCord showed the desire to put the ball in danger to hunt explosive plays in the second half, a good sign that he can keep a player like Caleb Douglas fantasy-relevant. With six teams on bye, McCord can be considered a QB2 against the Bills for Week 11.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans, adding three catches for 25 yards.
items.analysis: Tuten spent most of Sunday running into crowded boxes and churning out low-wattage gains. He was also stuffed at the goal line twice. Both were on different drives. Fantasy managers were finally rewarded for their persistence with a six-yard stroll into the end zone inside the two-minute warning. Tuten easily set a new career-high in carries while Chris Rodriguez was limited to a measly four attempts. After seeing 29 touches today, Tuten will continue to push for an RB1 ranking when he takes on the Giants next week.

items.name: Dylan Sampson
items.headline: Dylan Sampson rushed four times for six yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans, adding four catches for 31 yards on six targets.
items.analysis: Sampson outsnapped Quinshon Judkins 35-32 as the Browns had to dig their way out of a 17-0 hole against the Texans defense. Since returning from injured reserve Sampson has generated 12 catches for 121 yards through the air, not unusable numbers even if they’re not exactly a PPR scam. Sampson can be dropped in shallower leagues during Cleveland’s Week 11 bye.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore caught 4-of-6 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Bills saw twice as many targets as the next most-targeted player on the Bills, and connected with Josh Allen on a deep 45-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter. When he’s been healthy, Moore has been a really solid weapon in this Buffalo offense, and should be a high-end WR2 next week against the Dolphins.

items.name: Emmett Johnson
items.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons, adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns.
items.analysis: Making a spot start in place of Kenneth Walker III (groin), fifth-round rookie Johnson was electric from the opening whistle, routinely tacking on extra yardage by either dragging tacklers or simply juking them out of their cleats. Johnson almost never took a negative play, and was so, so slippery in the open field or with any steam whatsoever. He was the Chiefs’ No. 2 receiver with 6/70/2, and actually the most targeted with seven looks. It was the kind of all-around performance we knew was possible from Johnson’s pre-draft profile but that we just have not seen because of Walker’s dominance. With Walker truly questionable for Week 11 against the Cardinals until we hear otherwise, Johnson would be an RB1 if given another start against the lowly Birds. Even if Walker goes, Johnson’s FLEX standing is now on much firmer ground.

items.name: James Cook
items.headline: James Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: The Bills leaned on Cook heavily in this one, not showing much of a belief that the Jets were going to pile up many points on offense. It was a solid day overall for Cook, but he then ripped off a career-high 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter that not only sealed the win for the Bills but also made it a big fantasy day for Cook. The 27-year-old could have had an even bigger day, but he dropped what likely would have been a 15-yard touchdown catch. Cook should be a rock-solid RB1 next week against the Dolphins as well.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 35-13, Week 10 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Breaking Josh Downs into the Chiefs’ undermanned receiver corps, Mahomes ended up having his first five-score passing effort since Week 1 of the 2022 season. Heavens to Betsy. The 348 yards were also his fourth most since that MVP campaign for years ago. All this when the only addition was Josh Downs. Of course, it helped that Mahomes was facing a downtrodden, disinterested Falcons side, but it really did seem like the presence of another legitimate wideout was creating more space for everybody. That even included Rashee Rice, who caught a legitimate down-field bomb, and Andrew Armstrong, who housed a late 43-yard score where Mahomes just kind of chucked it up. Two of Mahomes’ touchdowns went to spot-starting running back Emmett Johnson, who was electric in the open field. This had the feel of a sort of deliverance for the Kansas City side, and it should continue in Week 11 against the Cardinals. The schedule stiffens after that, if not really the opposing defenses. Mahomes is back to every-week QB1 status, and should frequently be a high-end option.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: He added three catches for 33 yards on five targets as part of a robust screen game. Judkins has continued to see reasonable usage on the ground for a team that runs plenty, but he has yet to crack 100 yards in a game and this was just his fourth touchdown of the season. He actually was outsnapped by Dylan Sampson today, though it’s clear that happened because the Browns fell behind 17-0 before making their comeback. He’ll head into the bye as a borderline RB2.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young completed 17-of-30 attempts for 200 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding one rush for one yard.
items.analysis: It was one of Young’s worst performances of the season considering the middle competition. Young posted a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent under his expected completion rate against New Orleans. His statistical day would have been a little less bleak if Darren Waller had been able to hang on to what would have been a 30-yard score in the first half. Young, who regular missed open wideouts in the intermediate areas, has struggled for most of the past month. Young will be a superflex option in Week 11 against the Ravens.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordyon Tyson caught 7-of-13 targets for 80 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: The Saints ramped up Tyson’s snaps and routes in his second game of the season, as the rookie ran a route on 32 of the team’s 47 drop backs on the day and easily led all New Orleans pass catchers in targets and receiving yards. Chris Olave, meanwhile, was limited to three catches for 30 yards on five targets. Tyson was targeted both in the short and intermediate areas, and nearly came up with a couple downfield grabs on poorly-thrown balls from Tyler Shough. The Saints saw fit to target Tyson twice on backfield screen looks in the second half. That kind of usage suggests Tyson could be an outsized part of the Saints offense going forward. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.name: Cade Klubnik
items.headline: Cade Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards and an interception in the Jets’ 31-12, Week 10 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Klubik also added 26 yards rushing on the day. The rookie from Clemson looked pretty good for most of the second half, with no problem driving the ball down the field to his receivers. Some of those passes sailed on him, and he held onto the ball too long at times, but he has the arm and the ability to make enough throws to move the ball down the field and keep the Jets’ receivers relevant for fantasy football. He may have to start next week against the Chargers with Geno Smith (head/ankle) leaving this game early.

items.name: Josh Allen
items.headline: Josh Allen completed 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Bills’ 31-12, Week 10 win over the Jets, adding two rushing touchdowns on the ground.
items.analysis: The Bills leaned heavily on James Cook in this one, with Allen dropping back to pass just 21 times. When the Bills did pass, they took a few big shots down the field, which resulted in a long touchdown pass to D.J. Moore, but also a long interception on third down in what was ultimately an “arm punt.” Of Allen’s two rushing touchdowns, only one of them was on a tush push. The Bills quarterback has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in four straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a quarterback in NFL history, and he has 324 total touchdowns in his career, which is now the most by any player in their first 10 seasons in NFL history. He will look for another big fantasy day in Week 11 against the Dolphins.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden caught 5-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 9-of-13 targets for 74 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 11 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Jones was out-rushed by Jordan Mason in this one, but he still managed to get 12 touches and found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. It was the first touchdown for Jones since Week 5, which was also the last time he rushed for more than 26 yards in a game. His lone target in the passing game resulted in an eight-yard gain, but this was an otherwise forgettable performance for Jones were it not for the touchdown to get fantasy managers over the hump. Jones has not been the reliable pass-catcher fantasy managers have come to count on over the years and shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a fringe RB2/RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love completed 17-of-27 passes for 220 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 30-10, Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Love was under relentless pressure for most of this one. According to the early data from PFF, Love was pressured 19 times on his 35 dropbacks, which feels about right for a player who was sacked a season-high eight times. Love and the Packers went three-and-out on two of their offensive drives and also saw a promising drive late in the second quarter end after giving up back-to-back sacks after two long completions to Matthew Golden. Love and the Packers would eventually string together a 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive in the third quarter, with the lone touchdown coming on a 32-yard pass to rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, but that was as close as the Packers would come to mounting any sort of a comeback. Love and the Packers now head into their bye week and will return in Week 12 to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

items.name: Kirk Cousins
items.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Vikings’ 30-10, Week 10 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Cousins didn’t exactly stuff the box score in this one, but his performance provided a noticeable upgrade for the Vikings’ passing game. Getting the start on a short week following his trade to the Vikings, Cousins struggled early on, but eventually found his footing on the road against a solid Packers defense. His first big play of the game came on a 38-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price, where he placed the ball perfectly between three defenders to find Price, who then turned the ball upfield for the long score. In the fourth quarter, Cousins would connect with Gavin Bartholomew for his second touchdown pass of the day, which all but put the game out of reach for the Packers. With a full week to get ready for Week 11’s game against the Niners, we would expect Cousins and the offense to look a little more in sync. Cousins profiles as a mid-QB2 next week.

items.name: Christian Benford
items.headline: Christian Benford has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 10 with a groin injury.
items.analysis: Benford was questionable to play in Week 10 with a wrist injury but was cleared to go. He then injured his groin in the fourth quarter and will not return to the game. The Bills are set to face the Dolphins in Week 11 before facing the Chiefs the following week, so there is a chance that they hold their top cornerback out for next week. We’ll have to see if he is able to practice at all during the week.

items.name: Dorian Williams
items.headline: Dorian Williams is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Jets due to a calf injury.
items.analysis: Williams was hurt at the beginning of the fourth quarter and was taken to the blue medical tent. The Bills are up 24-12 with under eight minutes to go, so they may hold Williams out even if he is cleared to return.

items.name: Dee Alford
items.headline: Dee Alford was ruled out of Week 10 against the Jets with a concussion.
items.analysis: Alford was first evaluated for a concussion after he was hit by tight end Mason Taylor on an illegal pick play. He was cleared to return, but then, in the second quarter, he made a nice pass break-up and almost secured a one-handed interception, but his head slammed into the turf. His status for Week 11 against the Dolphins will be up in the air.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Gardner exited the game with a leg injury in the third quarter. He headed to the locker room and the Colts listed him as questionable to return. Gardner had dealt with a calf injury earlier this season, so it is possible he is dealing with a re-aggravation of the same injury.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith went to the locker room with an ankle injury during Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Smith was evaluated for a concussion during halftime but cleared to return. On his first drive back in the third quarter, he took another big hit from safety Cole Bishop and limped off the field into the blue medical tent. He then went into the locker room, which will leave Cade Klubnik as the Jets’ only healthy quarterback on the roster. If Smith is done for the day, he will have completed 12-for-21 passes for 148 yards during his two quarters of play. The Jets will hope he can return next week against the Chargers.

items.name: Eli Raridon
items.headline: Eli Raridon caught his only target for six yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Coming off a six-target game in Week 9, Raridon’s role all but evaporated today. He could pop up for another TE2 week down the line, but fantasy managers don’t need to hold him through the Pats’ Week 11 bye.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Henry couldn’t get anything going while catching passes from Tommy DeVito for the better part of four quarters. DeVito averaged 3.4 yards per attempt on 24 throws in the blowout loss. Henry would tumble down the TE2 ranks if DeVito starts the Pats’ next game. With a bye week on tap, the hope will be that Drake Maye is available when New England takes on the Chargers in Week 12.

items.name: Dont'e Thornton
items.headline: Raiders declared WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, G Bryce Cabeldue and DT Thomas Booker IV inactive for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers will function as the only viable pass catchers for Fernando Mendoza in his first NFL start against a tough Seattle defense. The Raiders will be without two key safeties, making the matchup slightly better for Drew Lock and his pass catchers.

items.name: Emanuel Wilson
items.headline: Seahawks declared RB Emanuel Wilson, QB Sam Darnold, CB Avery Smith, LG Quenton Nelson, LT Charles Cross, NT Deven Eastern, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Wilson will be a healthy scratch once again now that Zach Charbonnet is healthy. Both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price profile as legit fantasy plays against a Raiders rush defense that has been the worst in the league by most metrics over the past six weeks. Look for the Seahawks to be particularly run heavy with Drew Lock banged up.

items.name: Charvarius Ward
items.headline: Charvarius Ward (shin) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Ward went down with a leg injury after a couple of pass-breakups in the third quarter. He limped to sideline and was later carted to the locker room. The Colts declared Ward questionable to return.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith cleared concussion protocol and returned to Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Smith took a big hit on the Jets’ last play of the first half and was evaluated for a concussion at halftime. Rookie Cade Klubnik played the first drive and led the Jets on a 61-yard drive that ended in a field goal. However, with Smith cleared to return, Klubnik will head back to the bench.

items.name: DeMario Douglas
items.headline: Demario Douglas caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Douglas finished third among the team’s wideouts in targets behind A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins. Brown left the game with a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter and did not return. His absence could open up more work for Douglas, but the Pats are on bye after their trip to Germany. Fantasy managers don’t need to hold Douglas through their week off.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion evaluation) left Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns and was ruled out.
items.analysis: He was sandwiched between a pair of defenders on a third-quarter run and eventually walked off between trainers. Marks had 65 total yards before leaving, including one catch for 15 yards. With the short week ahead of them, the Texans will likely not have Marks available on Thursday night, leaving fantasy managers ignoring Emari Demercado and Dare Obungowale unless David Montgomery can play.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Garrett and Aaron Donald should have productive outings against a Cardinals offensive line that will be playing with a third-string left tackle and a backup center. Rookie QB Carson Beck will also be making his first career start. The Rams D/ST unit should put up points today.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: McDuffie sat out in Week 9 after injuring his back in Week 8. He missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury. Getting him back in the lineup provides the Rams’ secondary with a serious boost. He should play very well against a Cardinals wide receiver corps made up of backups. Myles Garrett (knee) and S Kam Curl (toe) are also active. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, S Maximus Pulley, LS Joe Cardona, OLB Darryl Peterson, OL Steve Avila, OL Keagen Trost and OLB Desjuan Johnson. Simpson will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Trent Williams
items.headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is active for the 49ers’ Week 10 game against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Williams is active despite only logging one limited practice this week. The future Hall of Famer will man his normal spot at bookend left tackle against the Cowboys. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw is also active, giving the Niners two of their key starters in this one. The 49ers have declared QB Kurtis Rourke, WR Mike Evans, OL Enrique Cruz Jr., LB Tatum Bethune, and WR Brandin Cooks inactive for Week 10.

items.name: Mack Hollins
items.headline: Mack Hollins caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: A.J. Brown left this game late with a hamstring injury but was struggling before getting banged up. With the WR1 doing nothing, Hollins stepped up with team-highs in catches and yards. He was, however, catching passes from Tommy DeVito, who took over for an injured Drake Maye. Hollins could see more work if Romeo Doubs remains on IR and Brown is out once again, but we won’t know much about either player until after the Pats’ upcoming bye week.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is active for the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Porter and fellow corner DaRon Bland are both active for this one, giving the Cowboys their top two corners against a good 49ers offense. We’ll see if Porter and Bland can slow Brock Purdy and company at home in Jerry World as the Cowboys look to move to 5-5 this season. The Cowboys ruled out S P.J. Locke, LB Donovan Ezeiruaku, WR Jonathan Mingo, S Juanyeh Thomas, OT Ajani Cornelius, TE Jake Ferguson, and DB Derion Kendrick.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Cooper Jr. was injured on the Jets’ first play of the game when Breece Hall was tackled into the back of his leg. Cooper Jr. has been battling an ankle injury throughout the season, so there is some concern that this could lead to an extended absence.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: McConkey is not taking the team flight to Baltimore, hence the Sunday rule-out. This has become a(nother) lost season for McConkey, who has gone from supposedly not even being injured entering Week 9 pre-game warmups to now missing back-to-back contests. McConkey’s own poor health coupled with Justin Herbert’s stunningly dreadful play is conspiring to make Ladd a WR4 we are no longer even sure about keeping around on our 12-team league benches. He’s a tough drop because of how little talent there is behind him in L.A., but it’s so difficult to envision McConkey contributing when it matters most during the fantasy playoffs.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith is being evaluated for a concussion in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Smith took a huge hit on the final offensive play of the second quarter when he was rolling out of the pocket. He was down on the field for a while before heading into the medical tent. Cade Klubnik is in the game for the Jets.

items.name: Roy Lopez
items.headline: Roy Lopez (toe/ankle) is active for Week 10 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Lopez, the Cardinals’ starting nose tackle, will play through a questionable designation after suffering toe and ankle injuries last week. The Rams’ ground game should still play well, but Lopez will make them work a little harder for yardage than they otherwise might have had to. Cardinals S Andrew Wingard (groin) and CB Max Melton (knee/hand) are also active. The Cardinals declared QB Joey Aguilar, CB Starling Thomas, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines and C Hjalte Froholdt inactive for Week 10 against the Rams. Playing without Froholdt, their starting center, and Williams, their current starting left tackle, is unfortunate.

items.name: Lan Larison
items.headline: Lan Larison caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Larison, New England’s third-string running back today, only ran the ball once. He found the end zone on a 20-yard catch-and-run late in the fourth quarter, but the play was nullified by a penalty. Refusing to be denied, Larison got in on a 10-yard checkdown from Tommy DeVito a few plays later. Larison will see a handful of weekly snaps with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, but we don’t foresee him being a relevant fantasy option afte New England’s upcoming bye week.

items.name: Corey Kiner
items.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 10 times for 25 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Kiner was the first Patriots running back to touch the ball, even with Rhamondre Stevenson active. He out-carried Stevenson 10-6, though New England pulled Stevenson in the fourth quarter. Kiner saw three rush attempts in the final frame, though it was third-string running back Lan Larison who found the end zone. Stevenson’s role should improve after the Patriots’ Week 11 bye. Kiner will tumble to the back of the RB3 ranks when he takes on the Chargers in two weeks.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for four yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Stevenson was initially expected to miss multiple weeks because of the knee injury he suffered in Week 9, so it was rather surprising that he suited up at all today. He was on the field for the Pats’ first play of the game but then immediately gave way to Corey Kiner, who went on to tally 10 carries. The team eventually pulled Stevenson entirely once the game was out of hand. He did not play a snap in the fourth quarter. Stevenson should see more work after resting over the bye week, but he may be relegated to committee duties for a few more weeks. Stevenson will be a low-end RB2 when he takes on the Chargers.

items.name: Tommy DeVito
items.headline: Tommy DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Patriots’ 35-10, Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: DeVito took over for an injured Drake Maye in the first quarter. He could not get anything going despite facing a Detroit defense that has been extremely beatable this year. DeVito threw a ghastly interception right at Roger McCreary late in the second quarter. He had Kyle Williams wide open for a touchdown but didn’t see him sprinting down the field uncovered. DeVito did eventually find the end zone on a check-down to Lan Larison late in the fourth quarter. DeVito would be the next man up if Drake Maye isn’t healthy after New England’s Week 11 bye, though we hope it doesn’t come to that.

items.name: Trey Smith
items.headline: Chiefs RG Trey Smith suffered a concussion in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and will not return.
items.analysis: Smith took a big hit in the first quarter and was ruled out in the second. Mike Caliendo, who is a significant downgrade, will finish the game on Patrick Mahomes’ right side.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: The Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan reports A.J. Brown (hamstring) left the Patriots’ locker room with a limp after the team’s Week 10 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Brown declined to speak to the media after the game. Head coach Mike Vrabel could only say he was unable to finish the game and the team will learn more when they get back from Germany. Brown injured his hamstring late in the team’s loss to Detroit. He briefly tried to play through it but eventually left for the locker room and did not return. With a Week 11 bye on tap, we might not get concrete information on his injury for a little while.

items.name: Dylan Parham
items.headline: Dylan Parham is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Bills with a knee injury.
items.analysis: The Jets’ starting left guard went down with a knee injury in the second quarter. The injury didn’t look good, but he was able to walk off the field and into the blue tent on his own. We’ll see what further testing reveals, but he’s been one of the Jets’ best linemen.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle, questionable) returned for the second quarter of Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Kelce ended up missing about a quarter of action. He figures to be on a snap count for the rest of the afternoon, but we would have to imagine he will be a point of targets emphasis when he is on the field.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is expected to be out “for the foreseeable future.”
items.analysis: Hutchinson injured his knee while celebrating a sack in the first quarter of Detroit’s Week 10 win over the Patriots. He jumped into the air and his right knee buckled as he landed. He will undergo more testing, but it looks like the Lions will be without their top pass-rusher for a while. Hutchinson has six sacks in nine games this year.

items.name: Bernhard Raimann
items.headline: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) was ruled out of Week 10 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Raimann headed to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion in the first half of the Colts’ Week 10 game agains the Dolphins. The Colts promptly ruled him out for the game later in the second quarter. Luke Tenuta comes in at left tackle for Raimann.

items.name: Isaac TeSlaa
items.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: TeSlaa beat his man off the line of scrimmage for a 12-yard score early in the second quarter. He was surprisingly involved in this contest, logging just his third game with more than three targets on the year. TeSlaa hadn’t seen more than two targets in a game since Week 4. We don’t expect this to be the new norm, so fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance on waivers.

items.name: Sione Vaki
items.headline: Sione Vaki rushed six times for 28 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: Vaki operated as the RB2 once again. Three of his carries came on the Lions’ penultimate drive, though Jared Goff was still on the field. Dan Campbell pulled his starters for the team’s final possession and Jacob Saylors closed out the game. Vaki is the backup fantasy managers should roster as Jahmyr Gibbs insurance, but he doesn’t hold any standalone fantasy value.

items.name: Jameson Williams
items.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 50 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: Williams didn’t post an elite box score, but he did earn his highest target total since Week 7. The speedster earned a healthy 22 percent target share and finished second on the team in receptions, tied with Amon-Ra St. Brown. Williams has generally been a boom/bust wideout, but he has at least 40 yards in all but two games this year. He’ll remain at the top of the WR3 ranks when he takes on the Bucs next week.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Bills due to an ankle injury.
items.analysis: On the Jets’ first play of the game, Cooper Jr. was blocking for Breece Hall when Hall was tackled into the back of Cooper Jr.'s legs. The wide receiver bent back awkwardly and limped off the field before heading into the locker room. Cooper Jr. was on the IR earlier this season with an ankle injury and was questionable coming into this week with an ankle injury, so this is a tough break for the 22-year-old.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff completed 20-of-31 passes for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Lions’ 35-10, Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: The Lions’ offense faced almost no resistance from New England. Goff averaged 9.8 yards per attempt and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for seven yards per carry. Goff did, however, force two throws that simply weren’t there. Both came in the second quarter, and the second pick was in the back of the end zone, costing the Lions at least three points. On the whole, it was still business as usual for one of the league’s best offenses. Goff gets a tough matchup versus the Bucs next week, but that won’t knock him out of the QB1 ranks.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and is questionable to return.
items.analysis: Already nursing an ankle issue, Kelce got rolled up at the end of a first quarter reception and hobbled gingerly to the sideline. He tried to re-enter, but ran off the field after briefly checking back in. He then headed to the locker room. We would assume veteran Kelce is genuinely questionable, and that he could get taped up/receive a pain-killing injection and return.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-5 targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: St. Brown got things started early with a 56-yard catch-and-run that saw him make nearly half of the New England defense miss. Not content with one score, St. Brown plowed into the end zone on a 22-yard screen early in the third quarter. It was an electric homecoming of sorts for ARSB, who spent part of his childhood in Germany and holds German citizenship. St. Brown hadn’t scored since Week 3, so the double-dip today will be much appreciated by fantasy managers. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when Detroit takes on Tampa Bay next week.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots, adding seven catches for 99 yards.
items.analysis: Gibbs gashed the Pats for chunk gains at will, averaging seven yards per carry and over 14 yards per catch. The Lions’ line bludgeoned New England and Gibbs was untouchable in open space. Gibbs could have posted even better numbers had the Patriots’ offense pushed the pace of this game more. Even without much pushback from New England, Gibbs racked up 44.2 PPR points, which is just shy of the highest mark in a single game this year. He’s running away with the RB1 overall crown, especially with Kenneth Walker banged up. Per usual, Gibbs will be the top-ranked option at his position when he takes on the Bucs next week.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Brown tried to gut it out through this issue early in the fourth quarter, but he ultimately walked off the field and into the locker room, likely ending his day. Even though he’s listed as questionable, we don’t expect him to return in a blowout loss. He will have a Week 11 bye to get healthy, though it’s looking like a lost season for the former superstar. Brown missed a month with a high-ankle injury early in the year, and now his lingering knee issue won’t go away, even as he tries to play through it.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Mitchell was expected to play, but now we have confirmation that he will. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also active, it’s unclear which Jets receiver will be most productive in a good matchup. That makes Mitchell a boom-or-bust FLEX option in fantasy leagues.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker (groin), DT Peter Woods, OT Jaylon Moore, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, CB Melvin Smith, and RB Jaydn Ott inactive for Week 10 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Walker was ruled out on Saturday, paving the way for rookie Emmett Johnson to potentially see a bell cow role in a plus matchup against the Falcons. Walker should be considered no better than week to week after getting injured in Friday’s practice, but the team has expressed hope that this is nothing more than a one-week injury. We will be monitoring his status all of next week, when the Chiefs begin prepping for Week 11 against the Cardinals.

items.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
items.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, RB AJ Dillon, DT TeRah Edwards, C Sam Hecht, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee, and LB Bobby Okereke inactive for Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Sanders will be out against the Saints, meaning Tommy Tremble will get a decent number of snaps and routes. He’ll be the TE2 behind Darren Waller, coming off his biggest game of the season. The Saints this season have allowed the third highest fantasy points per target to opposing tight ends.

items.name: Will Mallory
items.headline: Colts declared QB Riley Leonard, LS Luke Rhodes, LB Jaylon Carlies, OT Jalen Travis, TE Will Mallory, and DT Jerry Tillery inactive for Week 10 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The Colts already declared several players out prior to Sunday’s game against the Dolphins. Leonard will be the emergency third quarterback while Rhodes (hamstring), Carlies (neck), Travis (knee), Tillery (calf) and Mallory (hamstring) are dealing with injuries.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is officially active against the Bills in Week 10.
items.analysis: That means all of Cooper Jr., Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell will be active. This is a good matchup against the Bills’ secondary in a game where the Jets figure to be trailing and needing to throw; however, it’s hard to predict which of the Jets’ wide receivers will deliver in that one. That makes Cooper Jr. a risky FLEX option. The Jets declared WR Tim Patrick, TE Jelani Woods, EDGE Nate Lynn, LB Trevin Wallace, and CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. inactive for Week 10 against the Bills.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Spears is active for the first time since Week 6. He will pick up some work on passing downs but isn’t much more than an RB4 for fantasy purposes. Inactive for the Titans are WR Carnell Tate, LB Anthony Hill Jr., LB Cody Barton, RB Nick Singleton, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, and CB Jaylon Jones, and DL Jackie Marshall.

items.name: Christian Benford
items.headline: Christian Benford (wrist) is active for Week 10 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Benford was questionable due to a wrist injury suffered in last week’s game against the Vikings. With Jordan Hancock also coming off the injured list, the Bills have a fully healthy secondary, including the addition of safety Amani Hooker. The Bills declared QB Shane Buechele, OT Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Dolphins declared Chris Bell (knee) inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Bell entered the weekend doubtful after re-aggravating his knee in practice and not practicing on Thursday or Friday. Despite the absence of Bell, no Dolphins pass-catchers get a boost with Kyle McCord at quarterback. Dolphins also declared OL Aaron Brewer, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, WR Jared Wayne, and OL Caedan Wallace inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Bell entered the weekend doubtful after re-aggravating his knee in practice and not practicing on Thursday or Friday. Despite the absence of Bell, no Dolphins pass-catchers get a boost with Kyle McCord at quarterback. Dolphins also declared OL Aaron Brewer, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, WR Jared Wayne, and OL Caedan Wallace inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.

items.name: Will Anderson
items.headline: Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) is active for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Anderson was questionable and did not practice on Friday, so he’s presumably gutting it out as the Texans go without Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) in what looks like a must-win game. Also ruled out on Friday and Saturday were Marvin Harrison (hamstring), TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), C/G Keylan Rutledge (neck) and David Montgomery (groin), and they’re joined by G Wyatt Teller (back/illness) on the inactives list.

items.name: Zachariah Branch
items.headline: Falcons declared WR Zachariah Branch, QB Andy Dalton, LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell WR, QB Jack Strand, CB Robert Longerbeam and OL Cameron Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: It has been a disappointing rookie season for third-rounder Branch, who seemed like he might be in line for some first-year targets. Instead he has under 100 yards receiving and is now injured. A first-year washout like this makes Branch something of a dicey long-term prospect in Dynasty leagues.

items.name: Robert Hainsey
items.headline: Jaguars C Robert Hainsey (consussion) is active for Week 10 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Hainsey cleared concussion protocol earlier this week and is good to go. Inactive for the Jags are S Jessie Bates III, WR CJ Williams, DT Jordan Davis, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis.

items.name: Chris Brooks
items.headline: Chris Brooks is active for the Packers’ Week 10 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Running backs Josh Jacobs (thumb) and Pierre Strong are both out for this one, meaning the Packers will rely on the trio of Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson to handle backfield duties against a stout Vikings defense. Johnson “broke out” for 14-68-1 on the ground in last week’s win over the Patriots, but will be hard to trust this week given the multiple injuries it took for him to become fantasy relevant in Week 10. It could be best to avoid this situation altogether, especially with the Packers boasting one of the most explosive passing games in the league. The Packers declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OG Kevin Zeitler, and OL Sean Rhyan inactive for Week 10.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Week 10 against the Packers.
items.analysis: After injuring his thumb in Friday’s practice, Addison has officially been ruled out for Sunday’s pivotal NFC North tilt against the Packers. With Jauan Jennings (calf) and T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) also sidelined, Kirk Cousins will be forced to rely on Myles Price, Tai Felton, and Jeshaun and his other receivers behind Justin Jefferson. Jefferson could be in line for a big day in his first game with Cousins since 2023. The Vikings also ruled out QB Kyler Murray, QB Max Brosmer, LB Blake Cashman, and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins for Sunday’s game.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is active for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
items.analysis: He got in just one practice and was spotted in a boot at times before being dubbed questionable, but will be a reasonable WR3 play against a Texans defense missing a few pieces. Inactive for the Browns are S Ronnie Hickman (concussion), C Parker Brailsford, QB Dillon Gabriel (third quarterback), QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Ignioghene and LB Justin Jefferson.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Baker Mayfield (leg) could miss Week 11 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Mayfield suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9 against the Bears. He played through it then, but clearly it became a bigger issue after the adrenaline wore off. The Bucs are currently on bye, giving him some extra time to recover, but it may not be enough. Mayfield’s absence would give us another round of Jalon Daniels. The UDFA rookie made three starts earlier this year. He topped out at 189 passing yards and one touchdown.

items.name: Spencer Brown
items.headline: Spencer Brown (ankle) will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Brown had been questionable to play after not getting in any full practices during the week. The Bills’ right tackle went through an extensive pre-game workout before he and the team declared himself good to go. The Bills will have their full offensive line healthy for this matchup against the Jets.

items.name: Dalton Risner
items.headline: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Offensive tackle Myles Hinton is also questionable with an illness. It looks like something is going around the Cincy locker room.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

items.name: Morgan Moses
items.headline: Morgan Moses (knee) returned to the Patriots’ Week 10 game against the Lions.
items.analysis: Moses limped off the field in the first quarter and immediately left for the locker room. He was briefly listed as questionable to return but managed to get back on the field in the second quarter.

items.name: Morgan Moses
items.headline: Morgan Moses (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Things are going from bad to worse for the Pats. Drake Maye left the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Moses then followed him to the locker room a few minutes later. Both are questionable to return.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Maye’s ankle rolled while he was being sacked early in the first quarter. He initially appeared ready to play through it, but Maye walked to the locker room at the start of the Pats’ next drive. The fact that Maye was able to walk off under his own power, albeit with a slight limp, is at least a good sign. Tommy DeVitto is under center for the Pats.

items.name: Aidan Hutchinson
items.headline: Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Hutchinson jumped in the air to celebrate a sack in the first quarter. His right knee buckled when he landed and the star pass-rusher stayed on the field for a while. He was eventually able to walk off under his own power but headed straight into the locker room. Hutchinson would be a massive loss for a Detroit defense that hasn’t played particularly well this year.

items.name: Trent Williams
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Trent Williams (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Williams injured his shoulder during Thursday’s practice. The team then held him out of Friday’s session before listing him as questionable. It was likely a precautionary move as Williams is good to go for today’s game, which is great news for a 49ers offense that is very banged up otherwise.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Spears hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the knee issue. He practiced in full this week but was still listed as questionable on Friday. He should be good to go for pass-catching duties in a game that will likely see the Titans throw a lot. Spears is a low-ceiling FLEX play in PPR leagues this week.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Denzel Boston (toe) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Boston will likely go through a workout in the morning to determine his status, but he appears to be on the right side of questionable for now. He was held out of the Browns’ first two practices of the week before getting in a limited session on Friday. Barring a setback ahead of kickoff, Boston is back in the WR3 mix for Week 10.

items.name: Gardner Minshew
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL and will undergo season-ending surgery.
items.analysis: This was the expectation after Minshew severely injured his elbow in Week 9 against the Seahawks. His season is over after one incomplete start. Minshew threw for 354 yards and three scores in 2026. The surgery could sideline Minshew for over a year, meaning he may not play in 2027.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Patrick Mahomes suffered a “very small sprain of his UCL” and a muscle strain in Week 9 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Mahomes’ right arm was clobbered by a Jets defender while attempting to throw a pass late in the first half of Week 9. It looked like a serious issue at first, but he managed to finish the game and didn’t even miss any practice time this week. Per Schefter, the Chiefs consulted with physicians from the Rangers and Royals, who are among the world’s best doctors when it comes to shoulder and elbow injuries. Both doctors cleared him to play.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: There’ll be no Corey Kiner SZN then. I’ll tell the children. Stevenson is somewhat shockingly active after injuring his knee in Week 9. Initial reports had him missing multiple weeks. Instead, he’s good to go, though we should still expect Kiner to mix in for a few touches. Inactive for the Pats are QB Behren Morton, OG Ben Brown, OG Walter Rouse, OT Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis, and S Brenden Schooler.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 10 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: No surprise here. St. Brown is good to go as a mid-range WR1 for Week 10. Sione Vaki is also active. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, C Cade Mays, DB Keith Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DT Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Rhamondre Stevenson is also active. Brown made the trip to Germany and was limited in all three practices this week. He has been dealing with knee issues for several years, and we’re sure this isn’t the last we will hear of it in 2026. Still, he has been cleared for action today, meaning fantasy managers should get him in their lineups. We’re treating him as a volatile WR2.

items.name: Fernando Mendoza
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza “in the next few weeks” even if Kirk Cousins had not been traded.
items.analysis: With games against the Seahawks and Broncos on tap for Mendoza’s first two starts, the Raiders may have wanted to throw Cousins to the wolves for those games before getting the No. 1 overall pick under center against Cleveland. Instead, the Vikings offered Vegas a third-round pick for Cousins and the Raiders couldn’t say no. Mendoza will make his first NFL start at home versus Seattle today. We expect him to be in the QB2 mix at some point this year, but it might take a few weeks given Vegas’s tough schedule.

items.name: Kirk Cousins
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
items.analysis: Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Phillips hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. One of Carolina’s biggest offseason additions, Phillips was off to a solid start to the year before going down. He had 2.5 sacks in five games, two of which he left early. Getting Phillips back will be a big win for the Panthers’ defense.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is “trending towards playing” in Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Fellow Dallas cornerback Daron Bland is also expected to play. We don’t foresee the Cowboys putting up much of a fight against the 49ers offense, but having both corners available will at least help them slow San Francisco down a bit. Porter has appeared in four games for the Cowboys this year. He has three pass breakups and eight combined tackles.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jordan Addison (thumb) “will have his status determined closer to game time.”
items.analysis: Addison injured his thumb in practice on Friday and the team listed him as questionable for today’s game. The team elevated wide receiver Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad yesterday, casting some doubt on Addison’s availability. With Jauan Jennings also out, Tai Felton and Myles Price could be in line for larger roles today.

items.name: Will Anderson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Will Anderson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Anderson was added to the injury report on Thursday, then downgraded to a DNP on Friday. He was on the report earlier this year with the ankle injury. We suspect it flared up on him mid-week. The good news for Texans fans is that it won’t stop him from facing the Browns. With 9.5 sacks to his name through eight games, Anderson is in the midst of another elite season.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Garrett Wilson cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Wilson missed Week 9 because of the concussion but has cleared the league’s concussion protocol ahead of today’s game. Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday he expected Wilson to play, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In a potential shootout with the Bills, Wilson will push for a high-end WR2 designation this week.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: St. Brown played through the rib injury last week. He remained limited in all three practices before this week’s game. He’s likely not at full strength, but there was never much risk of him missing today’s game. He remains a high-end WR1.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: A.J. Brown is also expected to play. We will get confirmation from the team within the hour, but fantasy managers who are already rising and grinding can get Stevenson and Brown back in their lineups. Stevenson will shuffle back into the RB2 mix. We will expect to see some Corey Kiner touches to keep Stevenson fresh.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: McConkey heads into Monday Night Football listed as questionable after failing to practice through Friday. The veteran receiver missed Week 9 when it was revealed he had been dealing with back spasms during warmups. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers play in the final game of the week.

items.name: Chris Brooks
items.headline: Packers activated RB Chris Brooks and WR Skyy Moore from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Brooks returns to a backfield once again without Josh Jacobs, appearing likely to serve as the preferred passing down back while Kaleb Johnson handles early-down duties. Moore remains unlikely to be consistently involved in the offense but brings a sizable boost to the special teams unit. The top duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should continue to dominate targets through the air for one of the most pass-heavy offenses in the league.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Henderson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, after missing the previous two, with what the team is calling neurological symptoms. Whatever it is that Henderson is currently going through is clearly bigger than football. Rhamondre Stevenson is currently listed as questionable for Week 10 but is not expected to play, leaving the backfield in the hands of Corey Kiner in the immediate future. Here’s hoping for a speedy recovery for the electric running back.

items.name: Xavier Legette
items.headline: Panthers activated WR Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Legette will make his return to a passing offense currently dominated by Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, and tight end Darren Waller, unlikely to return a usable fantasy score in his first game since Week 2. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the plus matchup against the Saints.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Panthers downgraded Jonathon Brooks (core) to out for Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game as he attempts to return from a core muscle injury. He managed a week of limited sessions before initially being listed as doubtful, ultimately ruled out. Chuba Hubbard will again serve as a legitimate workhorse in a plus matchup against the Saints and can be treated as a back-end RB1 in Week 10.

items.name: Tyler Goodson
items.headline: Cowboys placed RB Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: It’s yet another blow to the depth of a backfield devastated by injuries this season, leaving lead back Javonte Williams again positioned well to see a workhorse role against the 49ers. The team elevated running back Israel Abanikanda in an associated move, who is likely to serve as the primary change of pace option in Week 10.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 10 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Montgomery entered the weekend listed as questionable after missing the previous three games plus the team’s Week 8 bye. Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for his return, while Woody Marks retains viable FLEX status playing as the top option alongside recent signee Emari Demercado.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report Saturday as questionable with an illness. A mid-range TE2 when healthy, Freiermuth’s potential absence likely wouldn’t change much for Darnell Washington’s fantasy outlook. Fantasy managers counting on Freiermuth will need to be proactive about alternative options as the Steelers play the Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Omar Cooper (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Cooper seemed to be trending in the right direction this week as he got in a full practice on Friday. Now he’s expected to play against the Bills, according to Zenitz. Cooper led the Jets in targets last week and will be in the WR3 mix against Buffalo this week.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is out for Week 10’s game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is questionable for Tampa Bay’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield got in two limited sessions after missing Wednesday with the injury. Todd Bowles spoke to reporters earlier today and said that he was “trending in the right direction” to start this week. He seems to be on the optimistic side of questionable, Jalon Daniels would grab the start if Mayfield is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (foot) is “trending” in the right direction to start in Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield reportedly looked good in Friday’s practice and logged back-to-back practices to close out the week. We should have an update on his official game status soon, but all signs are pointing to him starting this week against a Lions team that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards this season. We will check back in with an official update when the team provides it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield will close out the week with back-to-back practices, which should give him a decent chance at playing in Week 11’s game against the Lions. Things looked doubtful for Mayfield earlier in the week, especially after the Bucs signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad on Monday. We should get official word on Mayfield’s status shortly, but it’s safe to say he is trending in the right direction at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield did not practice Wednesday after injuring his foot ahead of the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. It initially looked like he would miss his Week 11 game against the Lions. Now he might be on the right side of questionable. Mayfield was spotted going through ball security drills and hopping over pads early in the practice. He certainly looked like a quarterback who was preparing to play in a few days. Mayfield hasn’t been all that productive this year, but he would still be an upgrade over Jalon Daniels. This is a situation to monitor heading into the weekend. After his limited practice today, Mayfield told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on Sunday, though the team has not made an official ruling. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Fox Sports’ Greg Auman said Mayfield “came out in street clothes, shoes, no wrap or boot on foot” while Jalon Daniels took first-team reps ahead of Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Lions. If Mayfield is unable to log a practice tomorrow or Friday, Daniels will get another start for the Bucs in a plus matchup against Detroit. Daniels will be usable in superflex formats, while Bucs pass catchers will be nothing more than desperation options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: He didn’t go as far as to rule out Mayfield this week, but between the Buccaneers signing Cooper Rush to the practice squad and elevating Easton Stick to the 53-man roster, they have already signaled that there’s a real chance Mayfield misses Week 11. Rapoport said it “seems to be trending towards” Jalon Daniels suiting up under center for the Bucs against Detroit on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers signed QB Cooper Rush, formerly of the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Rush’s signing comes a day after it was reported that Baker Mayfield could miss Week 11’s game against the Lions due to a leg injury he suffered in Week 9. The decision to sign Rush suggests Mayfield is trending in the wrong direction early in the week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when they take the practice field. Rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels would be the favorite to start in the event Mayfield is sidelined, but Rush could be in line to serve as his backup. The 32-year-old vet struggled during his brief stint in Atlanta, throwing for 229-1-4 in two games while completing only 56.4 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Baker Mayfield (leg) could miss Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9 against the Bears. He played through it then, but clearly it became a bigger issue after the adrenaline wore off. The Bucs are currently on bye, giving him some extra time to recover, but it may not be enough. Mayfield’s absence would give us another round of Jalon Daniels. The UDFA rookie made three starts earlier this year. He topped out at 189 passing yards and one touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 18-of-32 passes for 243 yards with two interceptions in the Buccaneers’ 27-24, Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Well, it was infinitely better than last week. Mayfield made two long connections; a 44-yarder to Kenny Gainwell to set up a field goal, and a beautiful 58-yard lob to Tez Johnson that was followed by Bucky Irving score. Unfortunately, his only scoring pass went the wrong way as it was a 67-yard pick-six from Jaylon Johnson that made it a two-score game. He did at least run in a two-point conversion that tied the game at 24-24, but the Bears were able to pull out the win on a last-second field goal. Mayfield also looked to be uncomfortable on the sidelines, as the Bears generated pressure throughout the contest. The Bucs get a needed bye next week, and Mayfield will be a QB2 for Week 11 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) recovery timeline “does not match up” with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua is currently on injured reserve, recovering from MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury. He will also serve a three-game suspension on injured reserve, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye. The superstar wide receiver underwent surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday, and Rapoport believes we have “almost certainly” seen the last of Nacua in the 2026 season. He is set to enter free agency this offseason, and it is unclear whether the Rams will extend him, franchise tag him or allow him to walk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua will undergo surgery on his MCL and will be out “a couple months.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Shortly after it was reported that Nacua “will undergo” surgery, we learned that the star receiver actually had surgery on Tuesday. We don’t know exactly how long Nacua will miss, but it’s safe to assume his only path back for the 2026 season would be if the Rams make a run in the postseason. Even then, his recovery timeline could be too long for a late-January/early-February return. The 25-year-old receiver was in the midst of another stellar season for the Rams, catching 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in. Nacua is in the final year of his four-year rookie contract and is on track to receive a lucrative payday this offseason, presumably from the Rams. An offseason marred by off-the-field issues and a stint at a rehab facility likely delayed the decision to extend him before training camp, but Nacua continues to play at an elite level on the field. If all goes well, it sounds like he should be healed well ahead of training camp next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy while on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Schefter notes that the timing of Nacua’s suspension “could potentially save him a substantial amount of money.” Suspended players are not paid, and Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract. Serving the suspension now “will cost him a lot less than serving it on his next contract, which is expected to be far more lucrative.” Schefter does not say whether he thinks the Rams will be the team that pays him, but a big payday is apparently still expected. Players are required to miss four games on injured reserve. Nacua has already missed one game. The Rams are on bye this week. He will spend the remainder of his injured reserve stint while also serving his suspension, and he will be eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys. Nacua will be allowed to rehab his injuries at the Rams’ facility for the suspension’s final two weeks.
