https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) return timeline has not changed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: A few days ago, McVay told reporters that Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve due to transaction limitations, so it was a bit surprising to see him land there yesterday. The move prompted some concern. He was initially expected to return in Week 14 or 15, and he will officially be eligible to return on the latter date against the Cowboys. As of today, he is on track to do so, just in time for the fantasy football playoffs. Nacua should not be dropped in any format. He will be a WR1 upon returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not be placed on injured reserve for roster mechanics reasons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The Rams are running out of return from IR designations. Putting Nacua on injured reserve would prevent another player from coming back later in the season, so he will simply take up a 53-man roster spot while he recovers. McVay made it clear that Nacua will still be out for a while. Nacua is expected to return at some point this year, though whether or not the Rams are still in the playoff hunt once he’s healthy could factor into the timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Puka Nacua (knee) will undergo an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Rams fans and fantasy managers will be holding their collective breath as they await the results of tomorrow’s MRI. According to Garafolo, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game when he took a rush attempt for five yards before the Rams punted the ball away. Nacua took a low hit from Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves, but didn’t appear to suffer a serious injury in real time. Garafolo reports, “the team does not believe [Nacua] suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more.” It goes without saying that the Rams can ill-afford to lose another receiver, especially one of Nacua’s caliber. We will be sure to check back in with any updates on his injury as they come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bud Dupree has requested his release from the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: Fowler also reveals that Dupree asked to be released in the offseason, but the Chargers have been unwilling to grant it. Dupree is playing infrequently and has just two quarterback pressures and one tackle. Releasing him would reduce their depth, but he is not a critical defender for this 1-8 squad. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Chargers signed EDGE Bud Dupree to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: After a productive first season with the Chargers, Dupree signed an extension to stick around for an additional season. The deal is for one year and worth up to $6 million, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. The 32-year-old finished last season with a 47.1 PFF grade, good for No. 188 among edge rushes; he totaled six sacks and an interception in the regular season. Dupree will play next to Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu again as part of the Chargers’ pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Chargers met with free agent EDGE Bud Dupree.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: In addition to the Chargers, Dupree has also met with the Falcons and Steelers. Dupree spent last season with the Falcons, amassing 39 tackles and 6.5 sacks, and was with the Steelers from 2015 until 2020. The veteran pass rusher has totaled 53 sacks over his nine-year career and was tied with Calais Campbell for the most sacks for the Falcons last season. Dupree can still provide plenty of help on passing downs but shouldn’t be counted on too heavily as an every-down player heading into his 10th season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Falcons EDGE Bud Dupree said he is “100% recovered” from a torn pectoral muscle he suffered late last season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: That means we’ll be expecting Dupree at OTAs. He, Calais Campbell, and Arnold Ebiketie will likely be the top three pass rushers for Atlanta in 2023. Dupree played just 22 games for the Titans in two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Falcons signed LB Bud Dupree, formerly of the Titans, to a one-year contract worth up to $5 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: Widely expected to return to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons in Pittsburgh, Dupree sided with Atlanta, which has made a series of defensive signings this offseason. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said the Steelers “were heavily in the mix ... but Dupree preferred a one-year deal. Steelers typically do two-year deals on veteran contracts of substance, and it appears they held firm to that here.” Dupree, 30, saw his play fall off during two injury-plagued years with the Titans, totaling just seven sacks in 22 games. Dupree joins an Atlanta defense graded by PFF as last season’s second worst pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports free agent LB Bud Dupree is scheduled to meet with the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: It was reported near the start of free agency that the Steelers had interest in reuniting with Dupree, who the team drafted in the first round of the 2015 NFL Draft. In six seasons with the Steelers, Dupree totaled 39.5 sacks, which included an 11.5 sack season in 2019. After spending the last two seasons with the Titans, Dupree, 30, is back on the market and could be heading back to the Steel City. Despite ending last season on injured reserve, Dupree is reportedly healthy and ready to prove he’s still capable offering meaningful contributions to a team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: CBS Sports’ Josina Anderson reports the Steelers have interest in bringing back free agent LB Bud Dupree.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: Dupree was released two years into a five-year deal with the Titans this offseason. Returning to the Steelers may be the best fit for Dupree, who spent the first six years of his career in Pittsburgh. After missing 12 games the last two seasons, Dupree will need to prove he’s healthy before signing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Titans released EDGE Bud Dupree.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: Dupree has not been officially released as of yet, but it is a foregone conclusion. Dupree ranked just 126th in Pro Football Focus’ defensive grades among EDGE players in 2022. Entering his age-30 season, he cannot be relied upon for anything more than solid depth at this point in his career. His release will save the Titans $9.4 million in cap space.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Titans placed Bud Dupree (chest) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: Dupree ends the season with four sacks and nine quarterback hits in 11 starts. He’s played just 22 games and has only seven sacks for the Titans in the regular season -- though he did add a playoff sack of Joe Burrow to that tally in 2021. Dupree will have a $20.2 million cap hit in 2023 that the Titans can move on from, and given that he’s missed time in each of his two seasons in Tennessee, he’s probably more likely to be cut or traded than not at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.headline: Titans EDGE Bud Dupree (chest) left Week 16’s game against the Texans and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bud-dupree.analysis: He was videoed throwing his gloves into the crowd, so we’d be surprised if he returned. Dupree came up awkwardly after a rush. He had one quarterback hit before leaving. Tennessee’s EDGE depth will have to continue to come through against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Mike Evans (Achilles) “is trending in the right direction” for Week 11 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Rapoport does note, however, that Evans is “a little sore” after returning to practice on Thursday. The 49ers will make a decision on Evans’ Week 11 status on Saturday. If active, Evans will carry some re-injury risk, but reports have consistently indicated that the 49ers learned a lot from Christian McCaffrey’s bilateral Achilles tendinitis in 2024. It seems safe to assume that if Evans is active, his Achilles tendon is in good shape. Evans may not immediately return to his pre-injury form against the Vikings’ elite defense, but he should be in fantasy football lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (Achilles) was questionable for San Francisco’s Week 11 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: We don’t have a practice status yet, but the 49ers said they’d make a decision on Evans’ status on Saturday. If active, he’ll be a reasonable WR3 bet due to the risk of in-game injury management risk and the tax the Vikings defense enacts on opposing passing games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Vikings. If active, Evans should be in fantasy football lineups. Re-injury risk is possible, but the 49ers have handled this issue smartly. We should have a decent indication as to whether he will make his return by tomorrow evening. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said “there’s a chance” Mike Evans (Achilles) practices on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: We’ll know more in a few hours, but even a chance at practicing is a small step in the right direction for Evans. The veteran wideout hasn’t played since Week 6 because of his Achilles tendinitis. We still expect this to be a ramp-up week of practice for him before returning in Week 12, but there’s at least an outside shot of him suiting up on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans is still dealing with the Achilles tendinitis issue that has been bothering him for weeks. He looks unlikely to suit up in Week 11 against the Vikings. With Deebo Samuel healthy and Keenan Allen in the mix, the 49ers can afford not to rush Evans back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Losing Evans for this one is a bummer. The 49ers’ and Cowboys’ offenses should facilitate a high-scoring game environment. Regardless, the 49ers are smartly prioritizing Evans’ long-term health. Whenever he returns, he is likely to be full-go. Keep him stashed on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: At this point, Evans seems like a long shot to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys. The 49ers allowed Christian McCaffrey to try to play through his Achilles tendinitis and it did not go well. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan indicated they learned from the experience and will let Evans get fully healthy before allowing him to retake the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The 49ers are smartly allowing Evans to fully recover from his Achilles tendinitis rather than allowing him to try to play through it. On Sunday, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Evans was “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys. He should probably be considered doubtful to play at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers declared WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, LB Tatum, Bethune, and DL Khalid Kareem inactive for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans will miss at least one game with his lingering Achilles injury. Look for the Niners to be careful with their WR1 in the coming weeks. Demarcus Robinson, coming off an injury, will return to the lineup against Vegas and likely operate as the Niners’ top wideout. Robinson will be flex-viable against a porous Vegas secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Mike Evans (Achilles) is “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The 49ers bungled Christian McCaffrey’s Achilles tendinitis in 2024 and are determined to get it right this time around with Evans. That means taking an extra cautious approach with his return to the field. He’s already been ruled out for Week 9 and now Week 10 sounds like a long-shot. Demarcus Robinson, who returned from injured reserve earlier this week, is somehow the team’s WR1 for today’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Patriots and Ravens are “potential landing spots” for Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones seemingly has decent odds of passing through waivers unclaimed, but he would be free to sign with any team after that. Rapoport adds that Jones is “still working his way back” from last year’s Achilles tendon rupture in his right, plant leg. Jones had a $10 million injury guarantee in his contract that is said to have been a factor in his release. Were he to sign with the Patriots, he could compete for the starting role with Tommy DeVito. Jacoby Brissett would probably be able to fend him off initially, were he to land in New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts waived QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Well, the Colts apparently evaluated everything, as they said they would last night. Wow. Jones makes it 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract. He will be subject to waivers since the trade deadline has passed. It’s possible — though we’d be hard-pressed to say likely given the $2 million owed this season, $10 million next year and $38 million in non-guaranteed 2027 cash — that someone takes a chance on the deal. If not, he’ll be free to sign anywhere for the rest of the season. Minnesota would probably take a gamble on him again after they scooped him up in this same exact manner a few years ago, but that’s just speculation on our part. It’s stunning in the sense that it happened in-season, but this was obviously the way things had been trending as Indianapolis’ offense simply hasn’t been able to operate with Jones. Anthony Richardson will take over as the starting quarterback for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he will “evaluate everything” at QB after Daniels Jones’ poor outing in Week 11’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Steichen didn’t commit to Jones as the Colts’ Week 12 starter for next week’s game against the Giants. Anthony Richardson replaced Jones late in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, but the Colts have been reluctant to bench Jones, despite a disastrous season in which he has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. It feels like a switch to Richardson is inevitable at some point. With some extra time to prep him for next week’s game, now could be the time to make the move back to the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 26-3, Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding three yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones led the Colts to only 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play against the Texans, also taking a sack in the end zone for a safety, before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. This is the second game in the previous four weeks in which Richardson has come on in relief of an underperforming Jones in the fourth quarter. When you add that to the continuous questions fielded by head coach Shane Steichen surrounding the quarterback position moving forward, pressure appears to be mounting toward a potential change under center in a lost season. For what it’s worth, Richardson came on and immediately threw a pass that should have been intercepted during a quick three-and-out possession, which were the only three plays he ran as the Texans controlled the ball to run out the clock. Fantasy managers should not have held on for this long, but it is safe to say that Jones can be returned to the waiver wire from whence he came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Colts want their next general manager to have a say in Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones’ futures with the team.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The Colts have faced scrutiny for their decision to keep Taylor and Jones on the roster, rather than trading one or both away for draft picks. Palmer said this is about empowering their next general manager. The team has reportedly compiled a preliminary list of candidates, potentially putting the team in position to make a hire quickly after the season. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that the Colts have a “package of plays in the playbook” for Anthony Richardson, but it is unclear whether they will “ever” use them.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Holder stops short of making any declarative statements, but today’s article implies that some in the Colts’ organization may be wondering why their 24-year-old quarterback hasn’t at least been used as a situational player. Holder compares Daniel Jones’ poor play to positive remarks made by Colts defenders regarding Richardson’s explosive dual-threat abilities. Holder does note that the Colts have at least considered using Richardson’s “electric running ability” to give them “a spark,” but for whatever reason, that hasn’t happened yet. Richardson could be worth stashing in superflex leagues, though there is no guarantee that he will take the field on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will start in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Steichen said on Monday during his media session that Jones knows he needs to play better, which is good news. Whether or not he plays better is to be determined, as Jones has seemingly known for weeks that he needs to play better but seldom does so on game days. In fairness to Jones, the Colts parted with a few key offensive players in recent weeks, including wide receiver Josh Downs, but the 29-year-old quarterback is also part of why the Colts chose to be sellers at this year’s trade deadline. It feels like it’s only a matter of time before the Colts consider giving another QB a look, but given the short turnaround to prepare for Thursday’s game against the Texans, it makes some sense for the Colts to stick with Jones for at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 11-of-22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Colts’ 24-22, Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding five carries for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: With a pass-catching group depleted after the trade deadline, the Colts offense did just enough to beat the Dolphins. Jones was nearly intercepted on the first pass of the game while he fumbled out of bounds on the Colts’ second possession. He threw a fourth-down interception in the second quarter, but recovered with a touchdown pass to Laquon Treadwell towards the end of the first half. The Colts offense faltered yet again in the second half, with Jones throwing a pick-six in the third quarter and failing to connect with pass-catchers downfield. Colts fans booed the offense off the field nearly every fourth quarter possession. The Colts defense was responsible for one of the team’s touchdowns, with the offense only posting a field goal in the second half. Jones is not a quarterback that needs to be rostered for fantasy purposes; he should only be a desperation play for Superflex leagues for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Colts informed Daniel Jones that they are not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones successfully returned from last year’s season-ending Achilles tendon rupture, but his play has been negatively impacted by it. With two young quarterbacks on the roster, it would seemingly make sense to trade Jones to get an extended look at either Riley Leonard and/or Anthony Richardson. Apparently, the Colts disagree. We have no way of knowing whether Pelissero’s report is a hardball negotiation tactic by the Colts’ front office, but we will have an answer to that question in the next couple of days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban believes Josh Johnson will “probably” start in Week 11 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms again, so recently signed journeyman Johnson will likely get the start this week. Urban notes that Johnson “played significant snaps for LaFleur in two games for the Jets in 2021, " completing 55-for-81 passes for 621 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions. With six teams on bye, Johnson, 40, is in the low-end QB2 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals signed QB Josh Johnson from the Bengals’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: In the wake of trading away Jacoby Brissett and the UCL injury to Gardner Minshew, the Cardinals spring into action to add veteran depth behind rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck, the latter of whom is expected to start for the remainder of the season in Arizona. Beck will be thrust into action without the team’s starting left tackle and alpha wide receiver in Michael Wilson but will get much needed experience as the Cardinals decide the trajectory of their franchise in the final half of the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals signed QB Josh Johnson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: It really strains the limits of credulity to have a 40-year-old practice squad player, but here we are. johnson remains QB3 in Cincinnati after being released at last cuts. Also on Cincy’s practice squad are: RB Kentrel Bullock, QB Sean Clifford, DT Howard Cross, DE Isaiah Foskey, LB Joe Giles-Harris, LB Shaka Heyward, DB Bralyn Lux, RB Kendall Milton, WR Jordan Moore, WR Noah Thomas and DB Russ Yeast.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals released QB Josh Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Johnson was signed before the Bengals knew they’d be getting Joe Flacco back, but with Flacco in the fold they’ve decided to move on from the 40-year-old. Johnson looked solid enough in the preseason to find a role elsewhere, hopefully on a team he hasn’t been on before for Immaculate Grid purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes the Bengals are “waiting on” Joe Flacco.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Flacco has been searching for an unlikely path to a starting job, but one doesn’t seem like it will materialize any time soon. The Bengals brought in Josh Johnson as a backup, but Dehner believes he’s just a hedge in case Flacco is able to find more reps elsewhere. Our nation’s great Flacco free-agency scuttlebutt will continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals agreed to terms with QB Josh Johnson on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: The well-traveled quarterback turns 40 on Sunday and heads back to Cincinnati for his third stint with the team after agreeing to terms on a one-year contract. He’ll have a good chance to earn the backup role behind franchise quarterback Joe Burrow considering the only other quarterback on the roster is Sean Clifford. Johnson has spent time with 16 NFL franchises during his sprawling career, amassing 11 professional starts across 50 appearances, most recently starting two games for the Commanders in 2025 in relief of the injured Jayden Daniels. The financials of the contract were not yet made available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Josh Johnson completed 14-of-22 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Commanders’ 24-17, Week 18 win over the Eagles, adding nine carries for 45 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Career journeyman Josh Johnson made two starts for the Commanders, both at the end of the season after Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota were ruled out due to injuries and Washington was eliminated. The 39-year-old passed for 372 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions over two starts and five games, adding 55 yards and a touchdown on the ground. A touch pass to John Bates in the fourth quarter of Week 18 against the Eagles was Johnson’s first touchdown pass since 2021. Johnson has been in the NFL for 18 seasons as a backup quarterback. He could certainly find work in a quarterback room once again for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga has not played since Week 5. He nearly returned in Week 9, pre-bye, but was unable to do so. His return could be helpful for a Broncos’ defense that struggles to cover tight ends. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) is questionable to play, and CB Riley Moss (concussion) is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga nearly played pre-bye in Week 9 against the Panthers, but he was unable to do so. He has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in Week 5 against the Chargers. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Riley Moss (concussion) are also practicing. Check back on Friday for their official statuses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos are hopeful Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Per Fowler, he remains a game-time decision. Hufanga logged two limited practices this week before receiving a questionable designation. Before going down with the injury, Hufanga had one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which he took to the end zone. Getting him back would be a big win for the Denver defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The Broncos’ talented safety might need another week to get his ankle healthy. Hufanga only logged two limited practice sessions this week. He has been sidelined since mid-October.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The Broncos’ safety now has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Panthers, though it is possible he still needs another week. Getting Hufanga back in the lineup will help improve a Broncos defense that has somewhat underperformed this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Talanoa Hufanga is expected to miss “about 2-3 weeks” with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The former second-team All-Pro safety left last week’s game against the Chargers with the injury. Hufanga has been one of the biggest havoc creators in the league this year with one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. His absence will be a big blow to the Broncos’ defense, which is already without Patrick Surtain II, Jonathon Cooper, and potentially Riley Moss for their Week 6 matchup against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Moss was ruled out of Week 5 against the Chargers but has a chance to play Week 6 against the Seahawks with back-to-back limited practice listings. Meanwhile, S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was a DNP for the second straight day. With Patrick Surtain (ankle) still out in the short term, the Broncos’ banged-up secondary may have a tough time against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and company on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar had not practiced either of the first two days of the week before this sudden Friday revival. We’d be surprised if he ultimately played coming off a short week, but no Chargers tight end is ultimately compelling with or without Kolar in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar seemingly came out of the Chargers’ first win of the season with a concussion, though he was on the field up until making the game-sealing catch on the last drive. He will need to clear concussion protocol in order to be eligible for Week 11 against the Jets. Also not practicing was WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring). Neither player has fantasy impact, though Kolar’s blocking is important for a Chargers team with a banged-up offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Justin Herbert gave Gadsden a chance to get going downfield early on, but the pass clanged off his hands. The incompletion may ultimately have been erased by a penalty. Herbert looked his way again later, on the Chargers’ late two-point conversion attempt, but it failed. Charlie Kolar, meanwhile, caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and rushed once for three yards. Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlies Kolar caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar ran 28 routes on the day while Oronde Gadsden II ran 24 routes and also had five targets from Justin Herbert. The division of pass-catching duties for LA’s tight ends make both players unplayable for fantasy outside the deepest formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar caught 3-of-4 targets for 37 yards with a lost fumble in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar tied for the team lead in catches, and finished with the most receiving yards. Unfortunately, 19 of those came on the first play, and were followed by a fumble. Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch his only target and Hayden Rucci had just one catch — for a touchdown, to be fair — so Kolar sadly appears to be the one “reliable” receiving target for the Chargers’ tight end room. That doesn’t mean he’s a great fantasy play for Week 6 against the Chiefs, however. On the contrary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar has missed a few weeks with a broken forearm after having surgery on it; he appears close to returning. The Chargers are perhaps wondering, looking at their offensive line, if he can play tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: In addition to Johnston, TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad) were also limited. Johnston has played in every game this season, but pops up on the practice report with a chest issue on Wednesday. He is not yet in danger of missing Week 5, barring setbacks later in the week. Neither Thompson nor Kolar have played since Week 2 but both have a chance to return this week against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing, Johnston may have fantasy value as the Chargers’ No. 1 wideout this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Daiyan Henley (knee) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley infamously was sent back to the Chargers after a reported trade with Denver fell through due to a failed physical. He returned to play in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, but now misses the first practice of the week with a knee issue. Given he has been playing through soreness, Henley’s absence may just be load management after a Monday game. Henley still has a chance to play in Week 11 with practices later in the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Broncos have revoked their trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley because of a failed physical.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The move, or lack thereof, was announced by Denver around midnight, and Rapoport later gave the reasoning. Henley has been playing through a knee issue for multiple weeks, though he has also dealt with other injuries that could have caused the Broncos to back out. Denver originally agreed to give fourth- and fifth-round picks to acquire Henley. He will now return to the Chargers. As Rapoport points out, the 0-8 Chargers now officially made zero trades ahead of the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Broncos acquired LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers finally make a move, dealing a player who was considered a burgeoning star a few years ago away for a light deadline return. Henley had a career-worst 38.3 PFF coverage grade this year but is still a good tackler and should give the Broncos some oomph on run defense down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 3 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: It’s kind of surprising that the illness has lasted this long — Henley drew another DNP in practice on Friday after also missing Wednesday — and even despite him playing through it on Monday Night it’s certainly possible he sits this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley was added to the Chargers’ injury report prior to their Monday night game with an illness. He played in the team’s win over the Raiders, so a missed practice two days later is a surprise, but not concerning yet. Henley is still on track to play in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Week 2’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers announced on Monday that Henley will be added to the injury report due to an illness. The third-year linebacker totaled eight tackles and a sack in the team’s Week 1 win over the Chiefs, and would join fellow linebacker Denzel Perryman on the sideline if he is unable to play. It’s not often we see players miss games due to illnesses, so we would still expect to see Henley suit up despite this late development.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley said he has fully recovered from offseason shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley played through a torn labrum for four months while breaking out in his second NFL season last year. The 25-year-old totaled 92 tackles, 13 quarterback pressures, six pass breakups and one interception. He now has ample time to ramp up ahead of the 2025 NFL season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (shoulder) expects to be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley had surgery to repair a torn labrum that he played through for the final four months of the season. Henley told ESPN’s Kris Rhim that he expects to be “100 percent” before training camp. If for whatever reason Henley is slow coming back, it could be an opening for 2024 third-rounder Junior Colson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley expects to undergo surgery on his injured shoulder this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley told The Athletic’s Daniel Popper that he suffered a torn labrum in his shoulder during the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs. Henley nonetheless finished with 49 tackles in run defense and 50 in coverage this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was limited in each of the first two sessions this week and was a shadow docket rule out in Week 9 while being a straight inactive in Week 10. Actually practicing ahead of this game is a sign things are better, but he’ll be no more than a WR3 in this dilapidated passing attack between the re-injury risk and the lack of upside. Yes, even against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver is tentatively on track to play in Week 11 against the Jets, but ideally he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Chargers have been willing to run the passing offense through McConkey when he is active. He is a WR2, albeit with some re-injury risk, if he suits up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey has been dealing with the back injury for two weeks now, sitting out the Chargers’ last two games. He continues to deal with a various set of injuries and is a wild card when it comes to playing on game days. A limited designation at least gives fantasy managers hope that he will play in Week 11 against the Jets, though McConkey has fallen to unreliable WR3 status at this point of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers declared WR Ladd McConkey, S Kendall Williamson, CB Isas Waxter, OLB Bud Dupree, WR Brenen Thompson, and DL Justin Eboigbe inactive for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey entered the weekend listed as questionable but was downgraded to out Saturday, while rookie Brenan Thompson will miss his seventh consecutive game. The reeling Chargers look to pick up their first win through an upset of a Ravens team without its top two quarterbacks, having recently signed veteran Jacoby Brissett for the final half of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is not taking the team flight to Baltimore, hence the Sunday rule-out. This has become a(nother) lost season for McConkey, who has gone from supposedly not even being injured entering Week 9 pre-game warmups to now missing back-to-back contests. McConkey’s own poor health coupled with Justin Herbert’s stunningly dreadful play is conspiring to make Ladd a WR4 we are no longer even sure about keeping around on our 12-team league benches. He’s a tough drop because of how little talent there is behind him in L.A., but it’s so difficult to envision McConkey contributing when it matters most during the fantasy playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey heads into Monday Night Football listed as questionable after failing to practice through Friday. The veteran receiver missed Week 9 when it was revealed he had been dealing with back spasms during warmups. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers play in the final game of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: This is unfortunate. McConkey is no stranger to playing through injury, but his availability for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game appears to be in jeopardy. If active, McConkey would be a WR2, but backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The back spasms that sidelined McConkey in Week 9 against the Texans evidently remain an issue. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 10’s Thursday Night Football game. The rest of the receiving corps is too unreliable for a WR3-level pivot if he is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not play in Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups. The Chargers kept that info under wraps until their first drive was underway, following an opening-drive touchdown by the Texans. We aren’t exactly sure how the Chargers were allowed to do this, but they did it, and fantasy managers who started him are stuck with 0.0 points in the box score. If he can face the Ravens next week, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Immediately after the Chargers’ second play from scrimmage, the broadcast booth announced that McConkey experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups, describing the announcement as a “developing” story. It is unclear why this wasn’t announced pre-game, but here we are. Hopefully, McConkey can take the field at some point, but he could end up missing the contest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely sat out on Friday after practicing in full, injury-free, on Wednesday and Thursday. With six teams on bye and very few reliable tight end options in fantasy, Likely remains in the TE1 tier. Monitoring his status throughout the weekend will be worthwhile. Hopefully, we continue to get positive reports on his groin injury. Likely notably dealt with a groin injury back in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) is dealing with a “minor” injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was noticeably absent from Friday’s practice, but Harbaugh said he expects his tight end to be okay. We assume that means he will be fine for Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, but we will need to wait to see where things stand when the team releases its final injury report on Friday. We should have a better sense of what he is dealing with soon, but in the event he can’t go, Theo Johnson would be the next man up to replace Likely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 9-of-11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely as clearly the going-in game plan in a game expected to be heavily influenced by weather. The rain cleared in the first half but Likely remained the featured option through the air, likely influenced by heavy blitz rates and unrelenting pressure from the Washington defense. The 11-target game was the fifth time this season that the veteran tight end hit double-digit targets but the first time doing so with J.J. McCarthy under center. Likely remains a surefire TE1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Jaguars in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Although it was another down day in the yardage department by his recent standards, Likely got the fantasy job done with his score and five receptions. It also wasn’t a bad outcome in a contest where J.J. McCarthy missed time with a hip injury and the Giants attempted only 27 throws vs. a reeling Eagles team. Likely’s touchdown was a five-yarder where he took advantage of mass defensive confusion at the goal line. It is unclear if McCarthy will be ready for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Likely will remain a high-end QB1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) expressed confidence that he’ll be fine after the bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was spotted limping at times during Week 7’s win over the Texans, which helps explain his subpar production. We’ll keep an eye on this one coming out of the bye, but we’re certainly not expecting anything serious here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: It was his first game with fewer than five targets all season. New York’s passing game simply targeted Houston outside the numbers and they ran the ball effectively enough that they didn’t need to feed Likely. He’ll be on the TE1 line in Week 9 against the Eagles once the Giants return from their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely scored his fifth touchdown of the season and third over the last two games. He also caught a two point conversion, with all his scoring coming in the fourth quarter from J.J. McCarthy. The pass-heavy game script helped Likely salvage his fantasy day late in the game as he saw double-digit targets for the third straight game and fourth time this season. Now averaging 9.8 targets per game, Likely is squarely in the fantasy TE1 ranks heading into a tough Week 7 matchup against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Matt Gay (hip) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Kansei Matsuzawa is on the Raiders’ practice squad and would presumably be elevated if the team rules out Gay. Neither player seems especially likely to be a good fantasy bet this week against the Broncos with a rookie quarterback under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Raiders agreed to terms with K Matt Gay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: The Raiders continue the free agency splurge, adding a kicker to the influx of new names in Las Vegas. Matt Gay kicked for both the Commanders and 49ers last season, making 17-of-23 field goals and all 26 extra points. The 31-year-old will replace Daniel Carlson as the Raiders’ starting kicker heading into the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: 49ers released K Matt Gay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Gay made four field goals and four extra points without missing a kick in two games for the 49ers. But starter Eddy Pinero is healthy enough to be active again, and so the 49ers will move on. Gay joins the workout kicker circuit again and figures to get a third opportunity at some point in the last month of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: 49ers declared K Eddy Pineiro, LB Tatum Bethune, DE Sam Okuayinonu, RB Jordan James, WR Jordan Watkins, OL Connor Colby, and DT Kevin Givens inactive for Week 13 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Pineiro missed practice this week with a hamstring issue and will miss a second straight game. Matt Gay, who made both of his field goal tries and both extra point attempts in Week 12 against the Panthers, will kick for the Niners against the Browns. He’s not a great fantasy option considering the weather conditions expected in Cleveland on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: 49ers signed K Matt Gay, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Eddy Piñeiro suffered a hamstring injury in Week 11 and is expected to miss some time. Gay will take his place in the lineup for now. The Commanders cut Gay on Monday after he missed two field goals versus Miami. Gay has missed six field goals on 19 attempts this year. All but one of his misses have come from 50 yards out, so the 49ers may only send him onto the field for short kicks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Commanders waived K Matt Gay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Gay was already on the hot seat entering Week 11’s game against the Dolphins. The veteran kicker has gone 9-for-10 on field goal attempts inside of 50 yards this season, but is just 4-for-9 on kicks of 50-plus yards this season. His two missed field goals in Sunday’s loss to the Dolphins were the final straw, with his last miss coming on a wide right attempt from 55 yards out that had plenty of distance to get through. Gay signed a one-year contract with the Commanders this offseason after spending the last two years with the Colts. With the Commanders now entering their bye week, we would expect them to bring on a handful of players to compete for the kicking job ahead of Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Commanders K Matt Gay (back) is not on Washington’s final Week 9 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: He has re-assumed kicking duties after missing last week’s game against the Chiefs due to a back injury. Matthew Wright was released earlier this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Commanders released K Matthew Wright.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: It’s a good sign for Matt Gay’s availability for Week 9. Wright did not attempt a field goal against the Chiefs on Monday night as the Commanders scored seven points and went for two fourth downs with Marcus Mariota under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Matt Gay (back) will not play in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: This move was expected after the Commanders signed K Matthew Wright to the practice squad and then elevated him to the roster for Monday night’s game. Any fantasy managers who have Gay in their lineup can pivot to Wright in hopes of avoiding a goose egg in the kicker slot. Wright has converted 87.5 percent of his field goals in his career and is 42-of-44 on extra points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.headline: Commanders elevated K Matthew Wright from the practice squad ahead of Week 8’s game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matt-gay/6.analysis: Matt Gay was a late addition to the Commanders’ injury report after suffering a back injury on Friday. The decision to elevate Wright ahead of Monday night’s game against the Chiefs suggests Gay could be sidelined for Week 8, putting any fantasy managers who may be counting on him in a tough spot. If Gay is unable to go, Wright becomes the plug-and-play option you can rely on in a pinch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: With Bhayshul Tuten not on the report either, Rodriguez looks likely to reprise his role as a clear backup against the Giants. He will not be worth gambling on in the FLEX spot without dramatic Tuten news ahead of Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions. The veteran backup would slide into an enviable spot if Bhayshul Tuten were unable to go after Tuten’s Thursday DNP, but we’d be surprised if it wound up that way after Tuten played through these injuries the last few weeks. If Tuten is active, Rodriguez is just a rough FLEX play, even with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez has been playing through the hand issue for a few weeks. This time should be no different. Coming off a four-carry outing in a blowout win over the Titans, Rodriguez is tumbling into the RB4 ranks for Week 11 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed four times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez spent most of the day watching Bhayshul Tuten rack up a career-high 29 touches, 26 of which were carries. Tuten also saw all the goal line work and eventually found the end zone late in the fourth quarter. With Tuten’s role on the rise, fantasy managers can likely cut ties with Rodriguez ahead of Week 11. He will be buried in the RB4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez had three limited sessions ahead of this week and, should the Jaguars bludgeon the Titans, would profile to get some between-the-tackles work with Bhayshul Tuten dealing with ankle and foot injuries and not getting in much practice time. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez played through the hand injury without issue last week, totaling 10 carries and two receptions on Thursday night. He should again handle a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans in Week 10, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) managing something.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was limited last week and played through the hand injury in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. He was limited again to open Week 10 but is still trending to play against the Titans. With Bhayshul Tuten still dealing with ankle and foot injuries, Rodriguez is a good bet to split touches this week and achieve FLEX value against a weak Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez split time with lead back Bhayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained limited all week, as did many Jaguars on the Week 9 injury report. It seems likely that the team simply took a conservative approach to their Thursday Night Football preparation. Rodriguez could end up being the Jaguars’ starter this week, with Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) labeled a game-time decision after failing to practice all week. Rodriguez warrants RB2 treatment if this is the case. Add him everywhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (heel) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Mid-week additions to the injury report are generally a bad sign for a player’s availability. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is also practicing in full, potentially pushing White into the droppable tier once tomorrow’s official injury report is released. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 47 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White started in name only, playing the first two drives before splitting backfield duties with fellow veteran Austin Ekeler for the remainder of the game. The two backs ended with the same number of opportunities while also splitting red zone work, with White narrowly missing a touchdown in the second quarter on his second longest run of the evening, a seven-yard scamper up the gut that was stopped at the one. His lone explosive run went for 18 yards, with those two carries accounting for more than 50 percent of his yardage total on the ground. White has fallen into a strict timeshare in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt and brings little fantasy upside ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 28 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding two receptions for 41 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White’s 28 rushing yards led all Commanders running backs, but his biggest play of the game came through the air. In the second quarter, White turned a short screen pass upfield for a 45-yard gain, positioning the Commanders for a touchdown, which came on the following play when Van Jefferson found the end zone for a seven-yard score. White’s only other catch went for a four-yard loss, but the 41 receiving yards still set a new season-high for him. The 27-year-old free agent signee has three touchdowns this season and hasn’t totaled more than 80 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He will be a fringe RB2/RB3 against the Giants, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) still sidelined for a few more weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding five yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White averaged just over two yards per carry on his first eight attempts before breaking loose for a 33-yard gain entering the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. He would find the end zone two plays later to salvage an otherwise underwhelming fantasy outing while operating in a three-way timeshare with Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols. Although White’s fantasy value is clearly higher in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, his performance in Week 8 goes down as his first fantasy-viable start through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers are likely better off exploring alternatives ahead of a poor matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie against the Giants, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White continued to serve as the RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and led the backfield with 11 snaps on third down. While his role remained largely the same, even with Austin Ekeler active, White offered nothing of fantasy value in this one. He saw only one target on the afternoon, and could continue to have his fantasy upside limited as long as Jayden Daniels is scrambling away from pressure rather than dumping it off to his checkdown options. Fantasy managers should avoid White in Week 6 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: In addition to White, the Commanders will also get RG Sam Cosmi back after missing the last two games with a concussion. White will likely return to his role as the team’s third-down/pass-catching back, but could be at risk of having Austin Ekeler eat into some of his workload. Fantasy managers hoping for White to return to the 10.3 touches/gm he was averaging before his injury may want to temper expectations and leave him on the bench while we wait to see how Ekeler is factored into the game plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers got in three limited sessions and will continue to play through this ailment. The Jaguars haven’t been tested enough to get him out of the WR4 ranks for the last few weeks, but if the Giants come to play on offense on Sunday, perhaps that will change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been rolling through this ankle issue the last few weeks and the fact that he remains limited shouldn’t be considered worrisome. He’ll be a fringe WR3 with six teams on bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the ankle issue for a few weeks. We expect the same for Week 11, though he hasn’t been a strong fantasy option at any point this year, healthy or not. He will remain in the WR4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Week 10 will be one for Meyers to forget. He dropped a deep shot from Trevor Lawrence on a trick play. Lawrence, admittedly, underthrew the ball, forcing Meyers to turn around and fight through contact at the catch point. Meyers dropped another touchdown later in the game that was more than catchable. Meyers hasn’t scored since Week 3 and has caught more than five passes in two games this year. He’s struggling to provide even WR4 value ahead of the Jags’ Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers will be in line for a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans. The good news is that the over/under has climbed to 46.5 after last week’s date with Joey Fagnano, leaving Meyers as a more viable touchdown threat in Week 10 than he was in a limited passing workload against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was limited at today’s practice.
