He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, but played through them in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. It is discouraging that he did not practice after a mini-bye, but the good news is that he only has the ankle designation now, no hamstring. Meyers is not yet in jeopardy of missing Week 10, but will need to practice in some fashion for fantasy managers to feel confident about his chances of playing against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The Jaguars keep many of their injured players limited all week, Meyers included. The move was likely just a conservative measure, given the short practice week. The Jaguars will likely take a run-heavy approach against a Ravens team playing with their QB3. Meyers is just a FLEX, given the expected game script.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The veteran receiver played through both ailments in Week 8 but was limited to only 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in a blowout win. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days, with the expectation that he continues to play through the injuries against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten got in a limited session on Wednesday, a DNP on Thursday while working with trainers, and appeared to do much the same on Friday before getting an official “limited” designation. Clearly gutting his way through the injury at this point, Tuten will remain a high-end RB2 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was seen practicing on the side field on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: This will presumably result in a DNP for Tuten this week, but we’ll see what the team announces when it releases its final injury report. According to Jaguars beat writer Ryan O’Halloran, Tuten was on the field with his helmet to stretch with teammates during warmups but then went to the side field. If he is listed as a DNP, it would be the second straight day Tuten failed to get on the practice field, but he could still receive a questionable designation entering the weekend. We will check back in with a final status update once the team announces it in a few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: He was spotted on the sideline with trainers, and he has played through this injury each of the last two weeks. That makes us optimistic that a rug pull won’t be forthcoming on Friday. Still, the Friday practice participation line has yet to be written and it is a negative trend after Wednesday’s limited session.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten has been playing through the pair of injuries for the past two weeks. He was held out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday last week, so a limited session today is a notable improvement. Coming off a 29-touch outing, Tuten is flirting with an RB1 ranking heading into his Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans, adding three catches for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten spent most of Sunday running into crowded boxes and churning out low-wattage gains. He was also stuffed at the goal line twice. Both were on different drives. Fantasy managers were finally rewarded for their persistence with a six-yard stroll into the end zone inside the two-minute warning. Tuten easily set a new career-high in carries while Chris Rodriguez was limited to a measly four attempts. After seeing 29 touches today, Tuten will continue to push for an RB1 ranking when he takes on the Giants next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: He practiced on Friday in a limited session, and as it was last week, he’s active despite not much actual work in a move that signals the Jaguars are clearly just trying to get their lead back some rest. He’ll be an upside RB2 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten sat out all three practices before playing in last week’s Thursday Night Football game, totaling 12 carries in the process. We tentatively expect him to play in Week 10 against the Titans, and he should be in fantasy football lineups even if he sits out or is limited on Friday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten was listed as DNP with the same ankle/foot injuries he played through last Thursday. He was clearly limited in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens and it is a bit discouraging that he starts out Week 10 not practicing after a mini-bye. It’s still early in the week, so this may just be injury maintenance for the 23-year-old. A practice later in the week will ease fantasy managers’ concerns, but a split in touches with Chris Rodriguez is certainly on the table again for Week 10 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is “good to go” after completing his pre-game workout for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jaguars have routinely killed the clock with their efficient ground game this season, oftentimes pulling Trevor Lawrence early. With the Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) tonight, the Jaguars should again enjoy a run-heavy game script, expectedly playing with a lead. Tuten is an RB1, having avoided suffering a setback this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: This could just be a rest day. Burks played through the injury last week, logging just one limited session, and he was clearly limited by the injury in-game. He still has a chance to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, but he would be a terribly volatile FLEX if so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks missed Week 9 and played through this injury in Week 10, and it seems like the extra rest after Thursday Night Football has done him some good. If he can overtake Chig Okonkwo as the No. 2 target in Washington’s passing game down the stretch, perhaps there’s some reasonable fantasy value to be had.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks got in a limited session on Tuesday, but was held out of practice on Monday and Wednesday. It is entirely possible that the Commanders are just exercising caution and Burks will play his normal allotment of snaps, but this sure seems like a scenario where he could end up being a decoy. Burks should be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX with a very low floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he expected Treylon Burks (foot) to be active for Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks, according to Quinn, did not practice Wednesday in preparation for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. He missed Week 9 against the Rams with a foot injury. The Commanders’ best downfield threat with Terry McLaurin sidelined, Burks profiles as a high-variance WR4 option this week. The Giants have faced deep passes at the league’s 16th highest rate this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: It’s an upgrade from an estimated DNP on Monday. Dan Quinn has previously said that he’s optimistic Burks will play, but it’s likely that he’ll hit the questionable line tomorrow barring a full practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders listed Treylon Burks (foot) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Hours after head coach Dan Quinn said he was “optimistic” that Burks would play in Week 10 against the Giants, the Commanders listed him as an estimated DNP for Monday. While they didn’t formally practice, the fact that the team is saying he wouldn’t have gotten on the field today isn’t an encouraging sign for a player who missed all of last week’s practices as well. The good news is there are still more practices to go, meaning Burks could still be upgraded before Thursday night’s game. We’ll see if his status changes on Tuesday when the Commanders take the practice field for the first time on the short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he is “optimistic” that Treylon Burks (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks sat out in Sunday’s loss to the Rams due to a foot injury that kept him off the practice field all week. Quinn’s optimism suggests he will at least be listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report and will get on the field in some capacity on Tuesday and Wednesday. Burks has been a solid downfield threat for the Commanders this year, catching 12 passes for 233 yards and two touchdowns. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him outside of deeper leagues, where he could be a viable desperation play as a WR4. In addition to Burks, Quinn also said he was hopeful CB Amik Robertson (ankle) would be ready to play on Thursday against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders declared WR Treylon Burks, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, and OG Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders find themselves incredibly thin at receiver with Burks (foot), Terry McLaurin (knee), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined for this one. Stefon Diggs, along with rookie Antonio Williams could both be in line for busy days against a Rams secondary that will be without CB Trent McDuffie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Zack Baun (back) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Baun didn’t practice at any point this week and could be in rough shape for a short-week Thanksgiving game against the Cowboys as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Baun is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers. If he is unable to play, the Steelers’ rushing attack should have a slightly easier time moving the ball. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Zack Baun (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Baun watched practice from the sidelines in street clothes today. He was briefly the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but nothing materialized. Baun will play if healthy this week, but we don’t expect him to be rushed back in the midst of a lost season for the team. He has 65 combined tackles, two sacks, and five pass breakups this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman believes trading Saquon Barkley “could be a tougher debate” for the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: GM Howie Roseman has seen some quick turnarounds and loves to deal. Should the Eagles continue to spiral, they will certainly be willing to trade players like CB Riq Woolen and TE Dallas Goedert on expiring contracts. But Berman frames it as a real question on “aging stars who might be part of their 2027 plans” like Barkley and Zack Baun. Barkley, still sidelined with a hamstring injury, could be a home-run swing for some team as the trade deadline nears. ESPN’s Ben Solak suggested a trade to the Texans in his Tuesday column, also adding the Seahawks, Packers and Vikings as potential fits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: He cleared concussion protocol and will, judging by online comments about the Eagles offense, spend 40 minutes Sunday morning throwing himself at Jaguars running backs who are trying to kill clock. Jihaad Campbell (knee) was also cleared.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: This is Baun’s second limited practice this week. Fellow LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and S Marcus Epps (groin) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Baun entered the league’s concussion protocol last week and was unable to practice at all. His return means he is making progress through the protocol and should be able to play in Week 5. On the other hand, fellow lineback Jihaad Campbell is not expected to practice with an unknown injury. It’s still a net positive injury report for Philly, but far from ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Not ideal timing as they gear up to try to stop Kyren Williams and Blake Corum on the ground. Baun did not practice all week and his availability for Week 5 is in some question as things stand. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will likely get extra reps next to Jihaad Campbell, though Campbell is also questionable with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Eagles WLB Zack Baun is in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: It’s less than ideal news for the Eagles’ every-down ‘backer with the team on a short week against the Rams. Teams seem to be getting players through the protocol faster than ever of late, but the Eagles’ six-day work week has play-making Baun firmly on the wrong side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.headline: Eagles RB Will Shipley (oblique) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zack-baun/.analysis: Shipley should resume No. 2 running back duties and can be stashed as a high-upside player in re-draft formats. Stud RT Lane Johnson (stinger) practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. The Eagles lost star OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) to injured reserve earlier this week. He will be eligible to return after missing four games. They got good news on LB Zack Baun (knee), LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and backup QB Tanner McKee (right thumb), though. All three are good to go. Unfortunately, CB Adoree’ Jackson (groin) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) is questionable for Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Illness was an added designation today. While it normally probably wouldn’t matter, since Shipley is already on injured reserve, the Eagles can afford to take it slow with him if they’d like to. If active, Shipley won’t be a FLEX play with Saquon Barkley healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley could need another week to fully recover from his injured reserve-worthy foot injury. Shipley partially tore his plantar fascia just over a month ago. Once he is active, he will likely serve as the Eagles’ No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: With Shipley’s 21-day return window officially opened, the third-year back can resume practicing with the team and is eligible to be activated from the injured reserve list at any time. It’s only Week 11, but this offense has struggled mightily without Jalen Hurts (blood clots), making it hard to imagine anybody offering much fantasy value at this point. Shipley has rushed 20 times for 57 yards and one touchdown this season and has caught five passes for 31 scoreless yards. There’s no reason to rush to add Shipley, even when he is activated. In another move, the Eagles also signed TE Zach Ertz to the and OT John Ojukwu to the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Eagles placed Will Shipley (foot) on injured reserve.

Shipley was diagnosed with a partially torn plantar fascia and was set to miss multiple weeks per reporting, so this makes sense. By the time he comes back, Saquon Barkley should be healthy, so he’s not a must-keep in short-bench leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” in Week 5’s loss to the Jaguars.

Saquon Barkley, who missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury, could be back as early as Week 6 against the Panthers, but if he’s unable to play, the Eagles could be looking at Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue as their top two backs. Shipley totaled 13 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on six touches before going down yesterday.

He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.

He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: The Eagles will drop their official injury report later today, but this can be chalked up as a DNP for Barkley. He was already considered week-to-week after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday, so today’s DNP doesn’t come as a surprise. He is a long-shot to play in Week 5. With Tank Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley will lead the backfield versus Jacksonville. He profiles as a low-end RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: He got in full sessions each of the last two days to clear the report. With Joe Milton under center, Smith is more of a WR3 than a WR2 at this point, but with six teams on bye fantasy managers can’t be choosy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.

Although he will be trying to catch passes from erratic QB Joe Milton, Smith’s target volume should keep him in the WR2 tier. It is possible that the team keeps him on a snap count, but he will be featured when he is on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: It sounds like Smith is on track to play in Week 11 against the Eagles, but it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow or Friday. Smith also told reporters today that he was 100 percent healthy for the Eagles’ Week 6 game against the Panthers, but he managed to strain his hamstring again anyway. If active, he will be a WR2 with six teams on bye, catching passes from Joe Milton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he feels “pretty good” about DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returning for Week 11 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Sirianni also included Dontayvion Wicks in his comments. Smith hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. In the midst of a lost season, the Eagles almost certainly didn’t feel the need to rush him back. He will return to a team down to its third-string quarterback in Joe Milton. Smith will be in the WR2 mix if he’s cleared for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, LB Jihaad Campbell, CB Jonathan Jones, S Michael Carter II and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith has now been active just one time since Week 3. With the Eagles no longer particularly interested in the 2026 season, we would consider Smith no better than 50-50 to return following the team’s Week 10 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: As expected, Smith will miss another week after not being able to practice due to his ankle troubles. The 27-year-old wideout could be an option after the Week 10 bye, but nothing is certain. The Eagles’ passing attack should be completely avoided for their divisional showdown with New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith will almost certainly miss the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants. Philadelphia goes on bye next week, so fantasy managers will likely have to wait until Week 11 to get Smith back in their lineups. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith has been out since Week 6, which was his first game back from a two-week absence. In the middle of a lost season, there’s no reason for the Eagles to rush their star receiver back. We don’t expect him to play this week and it’s possible he’s out for a while longer. Makai Lemon will likely operate as the team’s WR1 once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, LB Jihaad Campbell, WR Dontayvion Wicks, CB Jonathan Jones, OL Jake Majors , and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles continue to trudge on without key contributors as they enter Week 8 down their top two wide receivers and starting quarterback. Running back Saquon Barkley is active after being removed from the injury report Friday, with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue on hand for change of pace duties. Covey’s absence is primarily a hit to the Philadelphia special teams unit, who will continue to require alternate contributions to kick returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: He has not practiced since Week 6. It’s hard to count on Smith to be up for Week 9, though we obviously can’t say anything beyond him being questionable. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye and it might be preferable for them at this point if Smith sat through that — though that is just our speculation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck completed 11-of-18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions in the Cardinals’ 6-34, Week 10 loss to the Rams and lost one fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck’s performance wasn’t quite as bad as the box score suggests, but it wasn’t good either. The rookie quarterback went 7-of-9 through the Cardinals’ first three drives, but the game script suddenly became pass-heavy late in the second quarter, allowing the Rams’ defense to play single-mindedly. Reggie Virgil let what could have been a 29-yard touchdown pass go off his hands on a free play, and Zay Jones fell over backward while trying to secure what should have been an easy 40-yard reception. Beck’s first interception, on the Cardinals’ fifth drive, was not his fault. Devin Duvernay twirled to the ground as he attempted to secure the pass, but his momentum got the better of him and he accidentally flung the ball into Rams S Kam Kinchens’ hands. Beck’s second interception was a poorly timed checkdown attempt to Tyler Allgeier, which a Rams defender timed perfectly as he jumped the route, ripping the ball away from Allgeier’s outstretched hands on the Cardinals’ seventh drive. Beck’s lost fumble was the result of a clean punch-out from a Rams defender while Beck was attempting to scramble for a first down. Life won’t get any easier for Beck against the Chiefs next week. He’s a QB2/3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck will start for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew out because of a UCL injury, the Cardinals are already down to their third-string quarterback. It was almost a given that Beck would start at some point this year, though we imagine head coach Matt LaFleur didn’t think it would be this soon. Beck played well in his lone preseason appearance, throwing for 188 yards and a score. While he’s not much of a streaming option this week, he should be good enough to keep Trey McBride at the top of the TE1 ranks, especially with Michael Wilson done for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he did not consider benching Gardner Minshew for Carson Beck at any point in Arizona’s Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: We don’t believe him. But it really doesn’t matter because Beck will get his chance at some point in the coming weeks. The Cardinals’ rookie looked good in the preseason Hall of Fame game, though it is unclear whether he can do enough to warrant QB2 treatment as a pure pocket passer. The Cardinals’ schedule softens after matchups against the Rams and Chiefs over the next two weeks. Beck should have a chance to play in Week 12 against the Commanders, if not sooner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback has been dealing with back spasms in recent weeks, likely delaying his rookie season debut. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck threw the ball well on Tuesday. Today, they will see how things go. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned about the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season. He was officially listed as questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks got in three limited sessions, but notably had the “foot” ailment attached to him after it only being listed as an “ankle” the last two days. It’s possible this is nothing major and the Eagles are just taking it easy with him, but a new injury should be on the radar. Wicks has little fantasy utility either way at this stage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks is stuck in the questionable column, but he still has a chance to play. With QB3 Joe Milton at the helm, Wicks would only be a WR4/5 against the Steelers in Week 11. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Donatyvion Wicks (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
