Unfortunately for both wideouts, they will rejoin an offense now led by Joe Milton. With Smith commanding a massive target share and Makai Lemon in the mix for opportunities, Wicks will be relegated to the WR5 ranks if he suits up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he feels “pretty good” about Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) returning for Week 11 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: The bigger headline is that Sirianni said this about DeVonta Smith as well. Wicks was making the occasional splash play before going down with the ankle injury. That, however, was while Jalen Hurts was healthy. We don’t expect him to be a consistent fantasy option with Joe Milton now under center for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: At this point, fantasy managers should expect Wicks to take the field next in Week 11, following the Eagles’ Week 10 bye. He does not need to be held on 12-team rosters at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks hasn’t played or practiced since Week 6. It doesn’t look like he has much of a shot at suiting up this week. With a Week 10 bye up next, fantasy managers in even the deepest of leagues can cut Wicks loose.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and has not practiced since the build up to Week 6. As with colleague DeVonta Smith, Wicks enters next week questionable to play and with the Eagles having a Week 10 bye, we wouldn’t be surprised if Wicks sat that game out as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has not practiced since before Week 6’s loss to the Panthers and should be seen as doubtful heading into Friday’s practice session. We’d be surprised if he played in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets ruled out Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: This is unfortunate. Williams had a chance to play a larger role with Omar Cooper (ankle) sidelined. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell benefit from these players’ absences, though they will be catching passes thrown by a hobbled Geno Smith (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams could have been in line for a decent workload given that Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) has been ruled out, but the 25-year-old receiver will join Cooper on the sidelines for this one. Veteran Tim Patrick, who ran 22-plus routes in Weeks 5 and 6 when the Jets were shorthanded at the position, could be next in line for playing time, but he should probably be avoided even on a week with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams’ injury is unfortunate because Omar Cooper (ankle) is seemingly unlikely to play. If Williams were able to go this weekend, he would enter the boom-bust FLEX tier with six NFL teams on bye. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams would not normally be a name to monitor, but he tallied seven targets in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to Buffalo. Williams was forced to take on more work after Omar Cooper Jr. went down with an ankle injury. We suspect the Jets would lean on their 12-personnel alignment if Williams and Cooper are out for Week 11. That would finally get first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq on the field more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams stepped into a bigger role with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) leaving this game after the Jets’ first offensive play. The 25-year-old could have had a bigger day, but a long catch-and-run was called back due to offsetting penalties. If Cooper Jr. were to miss Week 11, Williams could be a deep league FLEX option against the Chargers, but he’s likely not in for a huge role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a three-yard rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Fill-in No. 2 wideout Williams is stuck on just four catches in three games during Adonai Mitchell’s surprisingly lengthy absence with a finger injury. The fact that Mitchell was not placed on I.R. suggests the Jets were not expecting more than a three-game absence, so Mitchell could be back as soon as Week 6 against the Patriots. Either way, Williams has not shown enough to earn a spot on 12-team league benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 2-of-3 targets for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams, once again subbing for Adonai Mitchell (finger), had the lone big play of the day for the lifeless New York offense. He caught a 58-yard score from Geno Smith after outrunning the Chicago secondary in the fourth quarter. Williams, who ran a route on 17 of the team’s 19 drop backs, will be a deep league flex option in Week 5 against the Browns if Mitchell remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams was technically the team’s No. 2 receiver today because of the absence of Adonai Mitchell. The role amounted to almost no presence in the box score as Geno Smith simply peppered his tight ends with the targets left behind by Mitchell. Williams is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4 despite the uptick in snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught all six of his targets for 34 yards in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams operated as the clear third wide receiver, playing on 61 of the team’s 74 snaps and running a route on 43 of their 50 dropbacks, which was actually more than Adonai Mitchell. Almost all of Williams’ work is on screen passes and quick slants where he can use his speed, but if he’s going to be on the field this much, he could be a sneaky deep league play against the Lions in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) will not play in Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield, who popped up with this injury on Wednesday, did not practice at any point this week. Yaya Diaby (knee) is questionable but probably on the optimistic side of it after getting in a full session on Friday. Tristan Wirfs practiced in full all week and is not on the final injury report with his toe ailment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ stud safety is trending toward a Week 11 absence. His team faces the Lions this week. Fortunately, Buccaneers LT Tristan Wirfs (toe) is practicing in full and should be good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield missed a handful of games earlier this year because of a rib injury. A DNP today puts him at risk of missing more time with a new issue. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters they will find out more about Winfield’s injury over the next two days. EGDE Yaya Diaby (knee) got in a limtied practice. He has a shot at returning for Week 11 after missing just one game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield Jr. will return in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield has missed the last three games due to fractured ribs he suffered in Week 4. Winfield has earned a 76.8 defensive grade per PFF this season while racking up 24 tackles. The Panthers’ secondary held up fairly well during his three-game absence, allowing only 235.0 passing yards per game, but his return will be a welcomed one for Bowles and his defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Antoine Winfield (ribs) for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield’s absence is consequential. The centerfield prowler makes an impact when he is in the game. The Steelers should have a slightly easier time moving the ball against the Buccaneers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield (ribs) has a fracture and will miss 2-4 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: That timeline makes it possible he’ll be sent to injured reserve before Week 5’s Thursday Night Football game against the Cowboys. Winfield missed only five snaps in Tampa’s loss to the Packers; this would appear to open a pretty deep hole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers S Antoine Winfield (toe) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: He and Lavonte David (knee/rib) both upgraded to full practices on Friday and were removed from the report. The Buccaneers will have their back-seven leaders ready for a divisional matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs S Antoine Winfield (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: It seems like, with Wednesday’s practice being a walkthrough, the Buccaneers opted to go easy on some of their veterans. Lavonte David (knee/rib) and Winfield both upgraded from DNPs to limited sessions on Thursday, putting them in line to play. The same can’t be said for EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee), who remained a DNP and could be in line to miss more weeks. We’re a little surprised Todd Bowles didn’t rule out Reddick when he said that Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin weren’t going to play this week, but he did say they were still waiting for the results of his MRI when asked about it on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Several Tampa Bay defenders did not practice on Wednesday. Lavonte David and Antoine Winfield are among the most notable names on the list. David is dealing with knee and rib issues while Winfield has a toe injury. Coming off a Monday night game, the Bucs might be giving their veterans some maintenance days because of the short week. Still, it’s notable just how many big names they have on the injury report. A banged-up Bucs defense could help Spencer Rattler get back on track after throwing three interceptions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers restructured S Antoine Winfield Jr.'s contract to free up 2025 cap space.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield had a $21 million base salary that was shifted to a minimum salary and bonus, with the Bucs also adding a void year. He signed a four-year, $84.1 million contract last offseason and now Tampa Bay frees up $15.86 million in cap space for 2025 by restructuring a contract that ends in 2027. The Bucs also restructured WR Mike Evans’ contract, though it was not for any cap savings. Evans had some compensation moved forward to pay him sooner, but cap space was not created.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The Jets’ rookie wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable. He appears to be likely to miss this week’s game against the Chargers. Ankle issues have bothered him for some time. Perhaps taking a week off would benefit him in the long run. He remains a worthwhile hold at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper, who picked up his latest injury last week against the Bills, appears to be a long shot for Week 11 against the Chargers. That would leave Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the clear top targets for Geno Smith, if Smith is able to play through his own ankle injury. Wilson and Mitchell last week combined for 87 percent of the Jets’ air yards and 51 percent of the team’s targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper Jr. was injured on the Jets’ first play of the game when Breece Hall was tackled into the back of his leg. Cooper Jr. has been battling an ankle injury throughout the season, so there is some concern that this could lead to an extended absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Bills due to an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: On the Jets’ first play of the game, Cooper Jr. was blocking for Breece Hall when Hall was tackled into the back of Cooper Jr.'s legs. The wide receiver bent back awkwardly and limped off the field before heading into the locker room. Cooper Jr. was on the IR earlier this season with an ankle injury and was questionable coming into this week with an ankle injury, so this is a tough break for the 22-year-old.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is officially active against the Bills in Week 10.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: That means all of Cooper Jr., Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell will be active. This is a good matchup against the Bills’ secondary in a game where the Jets figure to be trailing and needing to throw; however, it’s hard to predict which of the Jets’ wide receivers will deliver in that one. That makes Cooper Jr. a risky FLEX option. The Jets declared WR Tim Patrick, TE Jelani Woods, EDGE Nate Lynn, LB Trevin Wallace, and CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. inactive for Week 10 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Omar Cooper (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper seemed to be trending in the right direction this week as he got in a full practice on Friday. Now he’s expected to play against the Bills, according to Zenitz. Cooper led the Jets in targets last week and will be in the WR3 mix against Buffalo this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. The team listed him as questionable for a reason, but he is likely on the right side of questionable at this time. With Adonai Mitchell (knee) suddenly ailing, Cooper could warrant WR3 treatment against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Assuming all goes well, Cooper will likely be removed from the injury report before the end of the day, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Bills. Cooper caught eight passes for 58 yards in Week 9’s loss to the Chiefs, but that was with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. While we wouldn’t expect another 11-target outing from Cooper with Wilson expected to be active for Week 10, he could have some FLEX appeal after yet another strong showing. We will check back in with a final status update on Cooper when the team announces it later in the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith (ankle) is not on the Jets’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets’ starting quarterback was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. Smith has turned in a couple of decent games this season, but he’s currently on a two-game skid in which he has failed to beat 165 passing yards and/or throw a touchdown. He is stuck in the QB2 tier despite six teams being on bye this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) is trending toward playing in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: We should have the final word on Smith’s status shortly, but Glenn said his QB1 will log another practice on Friday, which should be enough for him to play on Sunday against the Chargers. Smith has struggled in recent weeks, throwing for 313 scoreless yards, but could have a chance to bounce back against a woeful Chargers defense that has allowed the 10th-most passing yards and the fifth-most net yards per attempt this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith is tentatively on track to play in the Jets’ Week 11 game against the Chargers, though his mobility could be somewhat impacted if this is indeed the case. Smith would warrant QB2 treatment if active. He is backed up by Cade Klubnik.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would not say if Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith suffered the ankle injury in last week’s loss to Buffalo and appears to be iffy for Sunday against the Chargers. Smith on Wednesday was a limited participant in practice, which is usually good news for a player’s Sunday availability. If Smith is sidelined against the Bolts, look for Cade Klubnik to get the start. Klubnik last week completed 11 of his 20 attempts for 137 yards and an interception. His aDOT was 11.3, the third highest of Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11 against the Chargers if he is healthy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith is having tests on his ankle after getting banged up in Week 10’s loss to the Bills. Smith was briefly evaluated for a concussion in Sunday’s game, only to return to the field and be knocked out in the third quarter with his ankle injury. Smith has struggled as of late, failing to throw a touchdown in his last two games while throwing for just 313 yards. Rookie Cade Klubnik, who threw for 137 yards and one interception while also taking three sacks, didn’t fare much better in Smith’s absence, but Smith is undoubtedly the better of the two QBs on the roster. All Jets pass-catchers would receive a slight downgrade next week if Smith is sidelined against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith went to the locker room with an ankle injury during Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith was evaluated for a concussion during halftime but cleared to return. On his first drive back in the third quarter, he took another big hit from safety Cole Bishop and limped off the field into the blue medical tent. He then went into the locker room, which will leave Cade Klubnik as the Jets’ only healthy quarterback on the roster. If Smith is done for the day, he will have completed 12-for-21 passes for 148 yards during his two quarters of play. The Jets will hope he can return next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith cleared concussion protocol and returned to Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith took a big hit on the Jets’ last play of the first half and was evaluated for a concussion at halftime. Rookie Cade Klubnik played the first drive and led the Jets on a 61-yard drive that ended in a field goal. However, with Smith cleared to return, Klubnik will head back to the bench.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith is being evaluated for a concussion in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith took a huge hit on the final offensive play of the second quarter when he was rolling out of the pocket. He was down on the field for a while before heading into the medical tent. Cade Klubnik is in the game for the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 attempts for 162 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding one rush for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The 36-year-old Smith was as immobile as ever, taking five sacks on the day and narrowly avoiding a half dozen others. Some of that was the Jets offensive line being overwhelmed against an elite KC pass rush; some of it was Smith refusing to get rid of the ball as the pocket collapsed. Smith playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion) was irate on the sideline in the fourth quarter with the Jets down multiple scores, barking at coaches and teammates alike. He had a negative EPA per drop back on the day. Smith should be seen as a matchup-dependent fantasy play. He will be streamable in Week 10 against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 20-of-32 passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Jets’ 38-33, Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Facing his former team, Smith had just his third multi-score start of the season. His 9.1 yards per attempt were his second most. A renewed connection with deep threat Adonai Mitchell was partly to thank even as Mitchell’s 7/142/1 included an awful deep drop. Smith also looked Garrett Wilson’s way a team-leading 12 times, though wideout and quarterback again had trouble getting on the same page. They were mere inches away from several more catches, including one in the end zone. Not great, but the duo at least appears headed in the right direction. The same was not true of Smith and rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr., whom Smith surprisingly did not target despite his back-to-back 100-yard efforts. This is sort of the long way of saying that Smith has a lot of excellent options in the passing game. That keeps him in the streamer mix, but he will not be a preferred QB2 for Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: He got in limited sessions all three practice days this week and seems to be trending in a good direction after missing Week 9 and Week 10 with this hip injury. He’s probably best-regarded as a game-time decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions declared RT Blake Miller, LG Christian Mahogany, CB Keith Abney, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, CB Ennis Rakestraw, LB Jimmy Rolder and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Losing Miller and Mahogany for this one is unfortunate, especially with C Cade Mays (wrist) on injured reserve. The Bills, however, lost DT Ed Oliver to a pre-game hip injury. This should be a high-scoring, fantasy-friendly game environment tonight. Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (foot) is questionable for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed was a mid-week addition to the injury report because of his foot issue. He was limited for the final two practices of the week. Reed is likely on the optimistic side of questionable, but we won’t know for sure until the Lions release their inactives 90 minutes before kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: He was a surprise addition to the report on Tuesday. The Lions secondary, already starting a wave of low-level veteran free agents like Rock Ya-Sin, Avonte Maddox, and Chuck Clark, can ill-afford to lose Reed before taking on the Bills on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (hamstring) is active for Week 12 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed, a critical part of the Detroit secondary, will suit up for the first time since sustaining a serious hamstring injury in early October and landing on injured reserve. It’s not the best development for Jameis Winston and the Giants pass catchers. The Giants were massively run heavy in Week 11 against the Packers. Lions declared CB Terrion Arnold, RB Craig Reynolds, CB Nick Whiteside, DL Quinton Jefferson, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (elbow) is not on Detroit’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Good thing, too, because the entire rest of the Lions defense found their way on to this report. Terrion Arnold (concussion), Kerby Joseph (knee) and Josh Paschal (back) were all ruled out. D.J. Reed (hamstring) and Amik Robertson (hamstring) are questionable. Both A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith should see slight matchup uggrades given the CB injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions S Brian Branch (foot) is scheduled to undergo an MRI after he was limited in practice for the second straight day on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: The Detroit Free Press’ Dave Birkett reports that Branch “worked out on the side during individual drills at practice Wednesday and had a noticeable limp as he left the locker room Thursday.” The Lions’ secondary could be extremely short-staffed against the Chiefs on Sunday night. Birkett notes that starting CBs, D.J. Reed and Terrion Arnold, are out indefinitely with hamstring and shoulder injuries. The Lions placed backup CB Khalil Dorsey on injured reserve this week and No. 3 safety Avonte Maddox “showed up on the injury report Thursday with a hamstring injury.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said CB D.J. Reed will be “out indefinitely” with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Fellow cornerback Terrion Arnold is also expected to miss significant time with a shoulder injury, leaving the team extremely shorthanded on the back end ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Chiefs. Safety Kerby Joseph has been tending to a knee injury as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: It seems rather unlikely that Mays will be able to get up off the mat for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game as well on a short week. Juice Scruggs will continue to start for the Lions for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: He did not travel to Munich with the team and has not practiced since injuring his ankle in Week 8. Juice Scruggs will continue to fill in at center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The Lions are at their best when the offensive line is in good health. Mays missed multiple games early in the year with a wrist injury. He is now sidelined by an ankle injury. Hopefully, he can resume practicing before long. Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Brian Branch (hip) were both limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays went down with the injury in the second quarter. His absence will make it even tougher for the Detroit offense to navigate the Vikings’ complex blitzing schemes. Mays has dealt with injuries for much of the past month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is active for Week 7 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Detroit will get back it’s highly-paid free agent acquisition from this past offseason after a preseason wrist injury. The Lions declared TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, C Seth McLaughlin, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DE Ahmed Hassanein inactive against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions C Cade Mays (wrist) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays seems likely to be activated off injured reserve ahead of the game given Dan Campbell’s public statements on the matter, him giving a presser today, and the trend to full sessions following the team’s Week 6 bye. It should be an upgrade for Detroit’s offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs ruled out RG Trey Smith (concussion) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Smith and RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) will both miss this week’s game against the Cardinals, but the Chiefs should be able to manage the situation. There is a decent overall talent gap between the two teams. Kansas City faces the Bills next week. Hopefully, the right side of the offensive line is ready for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs RG Trey Smith suffered a concussion in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Smith took a big hit in the first quarter and was ruled out in the second. Mike Caliendo, who is a significant downgrade, will finish the game on Patrick Mahomes’ right side.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs restructured Trey Smith’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Per Over the Cap’s Jason Fitzgerald, the move clears up $12.5 million in cap space. It also makes the Chiefs camp compliant ahead of the regular season, with some room to spare. Smith remains under contract through the 2028 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs G Trey Smith (ankle) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 18 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Smith suffered an ankle injury that kept him out of Weeks 13-15, coinciding with the Chiefs losing their grip on a wild card spot. He had the worst season of his career per PFF grading, making it to just a 68.5 overall grade. He did notably play worse with the ankle injury in Weeks 12, 16, and 17. Smith remains a long-term building block for Kansas City’s line, but this ends a rough season for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs ruled out RT Jawaan Taylor (triceps/knee) in Week 15 against the Chargers,
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: The Chiefs will also be without RG Trey Smith (ankle). Taylor remained sidelined all week. Smith practiced fully on Wednesday before being downgrade to limited on Thursday and an absence on Friday. The Chiefs have also lost multiple left tackles this season, with fill-in OT Wanya Morris rupturing a patellar tendon in his knee just last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs RT Jawaan Taylor (triceps/knee) is doubtful to play in Week 14 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Chiefs RG Trey Smith (ankle) is also doubtful, and Chiefs LT Josh Simmons (wrist) was recently placed on injured reserve. The Texans’ pass rush generates pressure at the NFL’s second-highest rate (42.4 percent). This is a tough break for QB Patrick Mahomes. Expect him to funnel targets to WR Rashee Rice and TE Travis Kelce on short routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs RT Jawaan Taylor (triceps/knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Taylor picked up the triceps injury in Week 13 against the Cowboys. He has missed both practices since then. The Chiefs are already without LT Josh Simmons (wrist) and RG Trey Smith (ankle) has also been sidelined over the last two days. The Chiefs face the Texans’ elite pass-rush unit on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs RT Jawaan Taylor (tricep/knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: The tricep injury, suffered in Week 13 against the Cowboys, is what will prevent Taylor from playing this week if he is ruled out. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for now. Right guard Trey Smith missed Wednesday’s practice with an ankle injury. Left tackle Josh Simmons underwent wrist surgery and was placed on injured reserve. That’s three starting linemen unlikely to play or explicitly ruled out for a must-win game versus Houston. Expect Patrick Mahomes to get the ball out quickly as often as possible on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: Chiefs declared RG Trey Smith, TE Noah Gray, S Chris Roland-Wallace, RB Elijah Mitchell, WR Jalen Royals, OT Esa Pole and CB Kristian Fulton inactive for Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Losing Smith for this one is unfortunate. The capable pass blocker will be missed against an ascending Cowboys pass-rush unit. Both Mitchell and Royals are healthy scratches. Gray was unable to practice this week, due to a concussion. This matchup should produce a high-scoring game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chiefs G Trey Smith (ankle) won’t play in Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-smith.analysis: Smith sustained two sprains on the same ankle in the team’s Week 12 game against the Colts and did not practice Tuesday ahead of KC’s Thanksgiving matchup with the Cowboys. It’s a blow to the Chiefs offense, as Pro Football Focus grades Smith as the NFL’s tenth best pass-blocking guard this season. The Dallas front seven has been much improved over the past three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears hit the questionable line with this knee injury in Week 10, Week 7 and Week 6 before this latest one. Given how similar the pathing looks to last week’s — as he also got in a full session ahead on Friday here — we think he’s more likely to play than not. He’s probably only a desperation FLEX play in a good matchup against the Cowboys busted run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. The Cowboys/Titans game has been looking like it’ll be a shootout if the Titans can keep up their end of the bargain, and six teams are on bye. Even with that, we still can’t muster much FLEX excitement for Spears as Tony Pollard’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It’s unclear if Spears aggravated his knee issue on Sunday or if this is just a maintenance day. Spears missed three weeks because of the knee issue before returning to action in week 10. He was held to five touches. Healthy or not, he is not on the fantasy radar ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears didn’t gain any yards on his only catch of the day. Tony Pollard, on the other hand, caught eight passes and rushed nine times. Spears missed three weeks with a knee issue and likely had his snaps limited by the team today. On the other hand, Pollard has played well this year and the team chose to hold onto him at the trade deadline despite receiving some interest. Spears is likely stuck in a backup role headed into Week 11. He will be an RB4 when the Titans take on the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears is active for the first time since Week 6. He will pick up some work on passing downs but isn’t much more than an RB4 for fantasy purposes. Inactive for the Titans are WR Carnell Tate, LB Anthony Hill Jr., LB Cody Barton, RB Nick Singleton, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, and CB Jaylon Jones, and DL Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the knee issue. He practiced in full this week but was still listed as questionable on Friday. He should be good to go for pass-catching duties in a game that will likely see the Titans throw a lot. Spears is a low-ceiling FLEX play in PPR leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: If Spears can play, this is theoretically the kind of blowout game script that sets him up for FLEX value via PPR scam. We wouldn’t advise chasing it, but we wouldn’t be surprised if it happened. Spears got in a full practice today, which would seem to leave him on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears was listed as a limited participant on today’s injury report, theoretically giving him a chance to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars’ elite run defense. Spears’ potential return could lower Tony Pollard’s snap share a tad, though Spears does not need to be rostered in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears’ lingering knee issue appeared to get worse a few weeks ago when the team scratched him for Week 7. He was held out the following week and even their recent bye doesn’t seem to have done the trick. Tony Pollard will continue to see a glut of touches until Spears gets healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears had three DNPs and has not practiced since last Thursday. Michael Carter filled down as the third-down back last week, though all that actually meant is that Tony Pollard got full-time workload. We expect that to continue in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: The big news here is that he got in a full session on Friday after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. The long layoff is still a little bit concerning, but a full session likely inches him over to the optimistic side of questionable in what looks to be a shootout. Tate will have high-end WR3 appeal if he’s able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions, though the fact that he’s coming off three weeks lost (two games, bye) leaves us a little unsure if we should say he’s “trending” towards playing. A full session would be nice to see and we’d be surprised if he cleared the questionable line on Friday without one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate missed Week 8 because of the shoulder issue. He got the bye week to recover but still wasn’t able to suit up in Week 10. Robert Saleh told reporters on Monday that he is hoping Tate is ready to go for Sunday’s game. Even a limited practice today puts him on track to play. With Wan’Dale Robinson on IR, Tate will return to an elite target share, even if he’s not fully healthy. He will be in the WR3 mix if the team clears him for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said he’s “hoping” Carnell Tate (shoulder) returns for Sunday’s game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate last played in Week 7. Saleh made the disclosure at Monday morning’s press conference, one day before Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) landed on injured reserve. Tate’s return would be just in the nick of time, as the Titans have a dream defensive matchup and Cam Ward is suddenly playing the best football of his career. Especially with six teams on bye and Robinson sidelined, Tate would immediately return to the WR2 ranks. We will get our first Titans practice report of the week on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: It’s a little concerning considering the Titans are coming off their bye week. Tate suffered the shoulder injury three weeks ago, and unless he can log a practice tomorrow or Friday, he’s likely to miss this week’s game against the Jaguars. His absence would make Wan’Dale Robinson viable in PPR formats, along with Chimere Dike, who led the Titans in receiving against the Bengals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is out for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate’s game-day designation comes on the heels of three missed practices this week. His absence leaves behind an alpha’s target share to go claimed by the remaining pass catchers, most notable of whom is slot man Wan’Dale Robinson. Robinson also draws the top matchup on paper against he inside-funnel nature of the Cincinnati defense, appearing to have a clear path to leading the team in targets and receiving. Fantasy managers can start Robinson as a viable WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was a DNP all week and is at risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Bengals. The team will announce his official status shortly, but if he is unable to go, Wan’Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor would be the early favorites to see an uptick in targets against a Bengals secondary that ranks 18th in points allowed to opposing receivers this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate has now missed two practices with the shoulder issue, making him truly questionable for Sunday’s game versus the Bengals. Tate has been operating as the Titans’ clear WR1, meaning there would be plenty of opportunities up for grabs if he can’t go. Wan’Dale Robinson could be in line for more targets, but his slot-only role doesn’t have much overlap with Tate’s job. Second-year wideout Elic Ayomanor might be the best bet to see more work if Tate is out this week, though that would only move him into the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: He got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. Hopefully his return will help calm down the interior of the Baltimore offensive line. The Ravens will need all the pass protection help they can get if they keep playing as they did on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ talented rookie guard continues to practice and play through two difficult injuries. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) remains sidelined through two Week 11 practices. Ioane should be able to face the Panthers this weekend. Madubuike could be sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane should have no issue playing against the Chargers on Monday night, nor should S Kyle Hamilton (hip), who has practiced in full in each of the last two days. Having Ioane on the field will be a big help for Jacoby Brissett in his first start for Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens declared WR Elija Sarratt FS Jaylinn Hawkins, CB Chandler Rivers, OG Emery Jones, OG Vega Ioane, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens will be without rookie guard Vega Ioane, who suffered a knee injury in last week’s loss to the Bengals. While it’s yet another blow to an already banged-up offensive line, the Ravens do have Lamar Jackson returning from his three-game absence after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. Hopefully, Jackson’s return can provide a much-needed spark to an offense that has managed just 23 points combined in its last two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Vega Ioane suffered an MCL injury and will miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane went down with a knee injury on Sunday against the Bengals and did not return to the game. Though Rapoport said the injury is not considered long term, Ioane — an impressive rookie — will be sidelined for a while. Baltimore’s offensive line ranks 20th in pass block win rate and 19th in run block win rate, according to ESPN.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: He’ll play against the Bills. It’s not exactly a smash play after he missed last week’s game with some soreness in his surgically-repaired knee, but it’s certainly plausible that Bell will be in the fantasy discussion in Week 12 if he proves healthy and able this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell reportedly hyperextended his knee last week, hence his day-to-day labeling this week. Bell had been limited from time to time already this year by soreness in his surgically repaired knee. The fact that this is unrelated is actually good news. He has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Chris Bell (knee) is considered “day-to-day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell was playing through some soreness in his surgically repaired knee until he was forced to sit last week. He was suited up for practice today, though we expect it to be a limited session for the rookie. The Dolphins will need to see how he responds to a week of practice before making a decision on his Week 11 availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell entered the weekend doubtful after re-aggravating his knee in practice and not practicing on Thursday or Friday. Despite the absence of Bell, no Dolphins pass-catchers get a boost with Kyle McCord at quarterback. Dolphins also declared OL Aaron Brewer, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, WR Jared Wayne, and OL Caedan Wallace inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful for Miami’s Week 10 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: He did not practice Thursday or Friday after aggravating his surgically repaired knee in practice on Wednesday. The Dolphins have no reason to push Bell, so we’d be stunned if he played. Not that you were looking for reasons to lean into a Kyle McCord start, but Bell’s injury should free up targets for Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas on the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The Dolphins were regularly limiting Bell’s practice reps earlier this season, so this may just be routine maintenance. The rookie wide receiver was limited yesterday. Bell has not yet established himself as a fantasy-relevant player, and he is unlikely to do so in Kyle McCord’s first start, especially if his surgically repaired knee is bothering him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: With nine targets over his previous two games, Bell looked to be building some momentum headed into Week 9. Instead, he posted the dreaded goose egg. The good news is that Bell ran a route on 77 percent of Malik Willis’s dropbacks. He’s running as the team’s WR3, but there’s barely enough passing volume to keep the WR1 in the FLEX mix. Bell remains an interesting dynasty stash, but he is not on the redraft radar headed into Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The third-round rookie was limited to short-area work in today’s loss to the Patriots, but his five targets and four receptions both tie for career highs. He also lost two yards on a run play. Bell has had a few gaffes this year, but he is seemingly recovering well from last year’s ACL surgery. He is a player worth stashing on benches in many 12-team leagues, and could warrant WR5 treatment against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.

Though Bell is the field more, he has yet to be a key part of the Dolphins offense and will see less opportunities once Caleb Douglas (ankle) returns. https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dee-alford.analysis: Defensive lineman Sam Roberts is questionable to return because of an ankle injury. He was a key target for Kyle McCord in the second half, making a 38-yard reception in the third quarter. He also drew a defensive pass interference and added a leaping 22-yard grab in the fourth quarter. Douglas is the clear WR1 in the Dolphins’ offense and McCord has shown he can keep the 23-year-old rookie involved in the offense. With a Week 11 matchup against the Bills on the horizon, Douglas is a fantasy WR3.

He also had his fair share of rookie blunders. Douglas dropped a pass on fourth down late in the fourth quarter. Detroit was able to run out the clock after getting the ball back. Douglas was also the intended target on Malik Willis’s lone interception of the day. Willis told reporters after the game that it was the result of a miscommunication between the two. The good news for Douglas is that the Dolphins are in development mode. Growing pains are part of the process and Douglas’s errors shouldn’t cost him playing time going forward. He will be in the WR3 mix when Miami takes on the Colts.

He caught two more passes in the second half, seemingly injuring his right ankle while being tackled on the first. He managed to return for the next drive and helped set up Kevin Coleman’s 35-yard touchdown with a 12-yard reception. Douglas should be rostered in most 12-team leagues. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions next week.

Douglas turned his second catch of the day, a short out route, into a 63-yard touchdown by toe-tapping his way along the sideline for a game-sealing score. His role is only going in one direction after the breakout performance. He will be in the WR3 mix when the Dolphins take on the Pats next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker sliced through a low-energy Jets defense time and again in the first half. He was more involved than usual in the pass game, taking over as KC’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield after Emmett Johnson’s big PPR performance in Week 8 against Denver. Walker would have likely had a bigger day if the Chiefs hadn’t benched their starters in the fourth quarter, up my multiple scores. Walker will remain a high-end fantasy play in Week 10 against the Falcons.

Walker is now coming off his two worst rushing performances of the year in tandem with the Chiefs’ first two losses. It’s safe to assume the two are related. With a down-bad Jets defense on deck, we fully expected Walker to get back on track as a top-end RB1 in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: He can be fired up as a low-end TE1 with Jordan Addison (finger) out for the foreseeable future. Hockenson got in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday before a full session on Friday tipped him past the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson has a chance to return from his wrist injury for the Vikings’ Week 11 game against the 49ers. It would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, Hockenson will likely qualify as a low-end TE1 with six NFL teams on bye this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson missed Week 10 with the wrist issue. He was also dealing with a chest injury, though the team didn’t bother listing that today. Hockenson will be reunited with Kirk Cousins on Sunday, and the Vikings will be without Jordan Addison. That could free up a few extra targets for the tight end. If healthy, Hockenson will be in the TE2 streaming conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the team expects TJ Hockenson (wrist/chest) “to progress” ahead of Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: We’ll be monitoring practice participation for Hockenson after he missed all three practices last week. Should he miss another game, Gavin Bartholomew caught a touchdown in his absence and would be a reasonable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson didn’t practice at any point this week and his status for Week 11 is likely in question as well. Gavin Bartholomew has picked up the slack this year when Hockenson has sat and will be a reasonable low-end TE2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson still has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Packers, but at this point, it seems likely that he will miss at least one game. Hockenson’s potential absence would likely allow Jordan Addison to earn a little more work than he has in recent weeks. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Both injuries are new for the veteran tight end. He presumably suffered them in the Vikings’ Monday loss to the Bills, though it’s unclear exactly when in the game he got hurt. Gavin Bartholomew would be the next man up, though we doubt he’s the best option off the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson struggled along with the rest of a Minnesota offense that managed only 178 yards of total offense, only 126 of which were accounted for with Carson Wentz under center. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the beleaguered veteran on the team’s final possession an nearly led the only touchdown drive of the game, ultimately coming up short on fourth down in the red zone. Hockenson and the rest of the Minnesota pass catchers are surely better off with any other quarterback than is currently on the roster, and there is the potential for the team to address the poor under-center play in the coming hours ahead of Tuesday’s 4 pm ET trade deadline. Hockenson would be a tough fantasy start against the Packers in Week 10 if the situation remains the same.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: TJ Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: It was Hockenson’s third touchdown grab of the season, as he remains Kyler Murray’s most trusted target in the run-heavy Vikings offense. He now has at least four receptions in four games this year. Hockenson, who came into Week 8 ranked tenth among tight ends in expected fantasy points per game, should remain in all lineups next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson operated as the Vikings’ No. 2 pass-catcher on the day, seeing a lot of Kyler Murray’s targets in the flats. He caught a five-yard touchdown in the second half and finished with 35 receiving yards. Two of his targets came in the end zone, giving him a solid floor as a red zone receiver. Hockenson’s red zone usage is a good sign for his fantasy value; he is in the low-end TE1 range for Week 8 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: He’ll return to his pass-blocking role for the Saints, assuming they want him active, in Week 11. No fantasy value here for the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The passing-down blocking back’s absence should create more opportunities for Alvin Kamara and, possibly, Travis Etienne in the passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: On the plus side, Donaldson is no longer listed with a concussion. Audric Estime played well last week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) is practicing now, though. Donaldson could be phased out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The pass-protecting back looks likely to continue to mix in and limit snaps for the fantasy-valuable members of the backfield in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and was cleared off the report for Week 11’s game against the Bears. He’ll be an upside WR3 after last week’s 13-target breakout against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Tyson, leaving him likely on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice sessions. Tyson will be an upside WR3 against the Bears in Week 11 based on the volume he was commanding last week so long as he avoids any unexpected setbacks on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Saints coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson suffered the chest injury in Week 10 against the Panthers. The fact that he is limited is a great sign for his availability against the Bears. Tyson belongs in fantasy football lineups on a weekly basis at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Chris Olave caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Jordyn Tyson, in his second NFL game, took over for at least one week as the team’s clear WR1, drawing 13 targets and finishing with 80 yards on 11 grabs. Olave, who did not record a reception until late in the third quarter, saw nothing downfield as Tyler Shough was under constant duress against a Carolina defense that entered the week with one of the lowest QB pressure rates in the NFL. Olave entered Week 10 with a 27 percent target share and a 47 percent air yards share. Tyson’s emergence could be a major issue for Olave if this sort of usage continues in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyon Tyson caught 11-of-13 targets for 80 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints ramped up Tyson’s snaps and routes in his second game of the season, as the rookie ran a route on 32 of the team’s 47 drop backs on the day and easily led all New Orleans pass catchers in targets and receiving yards. Chris Olave, meanwhile, was limited to three catches for 30 yards on five targets. Tyson was targeted both in the short and intermediate areas, and nearly came up with a couple downfield grabs on poorly-thrown balls from Tyler Shough. The Saints saw fit to target Tyson twice on backfield screen looks in the second half. That kind of usage suggests Tyson could be an outsized part of the Saints offense going forward. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett reports that the Saints had Jordyn Tyson work with doctors at the University of Wisconsin to address his recurring hamstring issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has dealt with recurring hamstring injuries since October 2025, and was most recently sidelined by a hamstring strain suffered on August 13th. According to Triplett, the Saints sent Tyson to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team, which received a $4 million research grant from the NFL in 2021 to study hamstring issues, twice during his three-month rehab program. Dr. Heiderscheit successfully treated Packers WR Christian Watson’s recurring hamstring injuries in 2024. According to Triplett, the specialists “determined that something was a little small” in Tyson’s hamstring fascia, which allowed the Saints’ training staff to update Tyson’s exercise regimen with needed alterations. Per Tyson, the changes have allowed the tissue “to fire better.” Given Dr. Heiderscheit’s track record, Tyson’s odds of remaining healthy for the rest of the season are trending upward. He warrants WR3/FLEX treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson should get “a healthy dose more” snaps in Week 10 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Moore adds that the Saints will continue to increase Tyson’s usage over time, “to a point where he’s not limited.” This is great to read. Tyson isn’t even listed on the Saints’ injury report this week. He earned four targets on 16 snaps last week and should be expected to increase his workload this week, potentially to a FLEX-worthy level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson caught 4-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was activated from injured reserve over the weekend and made his NFL debut today. He got off to a nightmare start by fumbling his first career reception inside the five-yard line. The Saints didn’t go away from him after the rookie mistake and rotated him onto the field rather sporadically for the rest of the game. He was deployed as the team’s WR3, running 16 routes compared to 44 for Devaughn Vele. Those two numbers should converge in the coming weeks, but it might take some time for Tyson to overtake Vele as the team’s WR2. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for Week 10 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.
