https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Simmons practiced in full on Friday after being limited with a knee listing the last two days. It wouldn’t be surprising if he continued to be limited in practice after this game given the quick turnaround to Chicago’s Week 12 Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports Giants HC John Harbaugh called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for DT Jeffery Simmons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: With Giants GM Joe Schoen stonewalled, Harbaugh broke with traditional NFL trade-talk norms and called the Titans owner himself. Unfortunately for the Giants, the message was the same, that Simmons was off limits in trade talks. Previous reporting from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer stated that Bears GM Ryan Poles’ long-standing relationship with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi played a huge role in Simmons ending up in Chicago. Poles and Borgonzi first met in 2007 when Poles was a guard at Boston College and Borgonzi was a recruiting assistant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Bears acquired DT Jeffery Simmons and a fifth-round pick from the Titans in exchange for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: The Titans’ fourth-round pick is in 2027 and the fifth-round pick heading back to Chicago is in 2028. It’s a massive haul for a Titans team that is once again staring down the barrel of a lost season. Simmons has been the subject of trade rumors for a while, but an offseason extension quieted the murmurs this year. Tennessee inked him to a three-year, $106 million extension in June. Simmons has consistently been one of the league’s best interior pass-rushers. He racked up a career-high 11 sacks last year and already has four to his name in 2026. Though the Titans clearly wanted Simmons to be around for years to come, they couldn’t pass on the chance to hoard draft picks as they prepare for another rebuild. With Caleb Williams healthy and playing at an elite level, the Bears are going all in on this current window. They currently rank 14th in EPA per play allowed, a mark that will certainly improve in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (back) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: He went from a Wednesday DNP to a Friday full session and should see his normal allotment of snaps and havoc-causing against Houston’s beleaguered interior offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Robert Saleh has been liberal with rest days for veterans, so this could be nothing. It’s still notable that the centerpiece of his defense did not practice today. Simmons has two sacks on 12 pressures this year. The defense wasn’t necessarily good with him in the lineup, but it would be even more of a disappointment if he does miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans signed DT Jeffery Simmons to a three-year, $105.8 million extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the contract makes Simmons, 28, the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history and includes $100 million guaranteed. Per PFF, Simmons led NFL defensive tackles with 12 sacks last season, while ranking in the top three in both quarterback pressures (64) and TFLs (12). His 43 solo tackles tied for sixth. Through seven NFL seasons, Simmons has appeared in four Pro Bowls, while earning two second-team All-Pro spots and one first-team All-Pro spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans WR Calvin Ridley (hamstring) is active for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Ridley’s hamstring injury kept him down from Weeks 7-9, not including a Week 10 bye. He’ll be on the WR4/WR5 line in a tough matchup against a good Texans pass defense. Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) and Arden Key (quad) are also active. Inactive for the Titans are: S Xavier Woods (hamstring), S Jerrick Reed II, G Drew Moss and T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Titans DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Simmons hasn’t played since Week 7. It looked like he would be out again this week when the Titans held him out of practice on Wednesday. However, he returned for two limited sessions and a questionable designation entering the weekend. It sounds like the Titans will have their top pass-rusher back versus Davis Mills and the Texans. Simmons has 4.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: The 1-7 Titans will be without their defensive leader in a matchup against one of the league’s top offenses. It’s a tough break for a team that will also be without its WR1, as Calvin Ridley will miss a third-straight game with a hamstring injury of his own. Simmons has totaled 21 tackles and 4.5 sacks in seven games this season and will likely be replaced by C.J. Ravenell, who is listed behind him on the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) will not play in Chicago’s Week 11 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: He was ruled out after three straight missed practices following the Week 10 bye. It does not look especially likely he’ll be able to turn it around next week and play in Chicago’s Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon missed time earlier this season with a calf issue. He played in Week 9 before the team’s bye but got banged up. Head coach Ben Johnson called him day-to-day earlier this week. Gordon has four sacks, two forced fumbles, and one pass breakup this year. Losing him would make this an easier matchup for Tyler Shough and the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (calf) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, the team’s starting slot cornerback, and Tyrique Stevenson (hip), the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, are both questionable. Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) has been ruled out. This defense is banged up, boding positively for the Falcons’ fantasy football outlook.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon (calf) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon practiced in full all week, so he is seemingly ready to play. The Bears could give it another week, though. Bears LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are also questionable this week. Both players practiced in full over the last two days and are likewise returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears ruled out CB Kyler Gordon (calf) for Week 4 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are all in the process of returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. None of them will play this week. Fill-in starting DB Cam Lewis (hip) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears activated CB Kyler Gordon (calf) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: This does not necessarily mean Gordon will play in Week 4 against the Jets, but he is certainly getting closer to making his 2026 debut. The Bears’ pass defense has been a fantasy-friendly unit thus far. If Gordon can return to form, he could help slow down opposing slot receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Bears CB Kyler Gordon (calf) is working out on his own with a trainer to “accelerate his recovery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Let’s hope he doesn’t find Joe Mixon’s trainers. Rapoport reports the “plan” is for Gordon to return a few weeks into the season and begin practicing shortly thereafter. He’s probably looking at a midseason timetable to return at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears placed DB Kyler Gordon on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: The Bears also placed LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and DL Shemar Turner (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. All three players must miss at least four games to begin the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Kyler Gordon (calf) has a timeline to return of “unknown.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: It certainly looks like Gordon will hit reserve/PUP or injured reserve before the start of the season while he deals with this long-term calf injury. This makes both the Bears coach and GM telling you they’re frustrated with the situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) is not on Chicago’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: He’ll return to FLEX plausibility as the Bears take on the Saints in a game where a crockpotting run-heavy attack is certainly in the range of possibilities. Monangai has not played since Week 4, but has fully recovered from a turf toe injury and practiced in full all three days this week. He shouldn’t have any limitations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai has been out since Week 4 because of the toe issue. He returned to practice late last week but wasn’t ready to suit up after just one session. A full practice today all but guarantee he will be on the field this week. Monangai was splitting work with D’Andre Swift before suffering the toe injury. We suspect his role will be scaled back in his return to action, keeping him in the RB3 ranks despite the good matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: ESPN’s Courtney Cronin reports Kyle Monangai is back at practice and “on track” for Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai has missed the previous five games while dealing with thumb and toe injuries, with the team’s Week 10 bye appearing to have provided enough time for the electric youngster to return following five missed games. He should be expected to step back into a strict timeshare with D’Andre Swift after earning 31 percent to 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps through the first four weeks of the 2026 season. Monangai returns to a viable Flex profile and downgrades Swift from weekly RB1 status to a borderline RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Malik Muhammad, RB Kyle Monangai, LB Keyshaun Elliott and DT Jayden Loving inactive for Week 9 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai will miss one more week with the expectation being that the 24-year-old tailback will be good to go after the bye in Week 10. Keenum will be the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 9 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Per Rapoport, Monangai is expected to return after Chicago’s Week 10 bye. Monangai has been out since Week 4. He finally returned to practice earlier this week, but it was for a single, limited session on Friday. He should be back in a 1B role when the Bears take on the Saints in two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) returned to practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: The Bears are calling the tailback questionable for Week 9 against the Buccaneers. It’s the first time that Monangai has been able to practice picking up the injury a month ago against the Jets. It seems extremely unlikely that the 24-year-old will be able to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday night, but he appears to be on track to return after the Week 10 bye for the final stretch. Malik Muhammed and Tyrique Stevenson are also questionable for the Sunday Night showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: It’s back-to-back missed practices for the 24-year-old ahead of Week 9’s contest against the Buccaneers. It seems more than likely that Monangai comes back for Week 10 after the bye, but if he can get a full session in, there’s a chance he rolls against Tampa Bay come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai was an estimated DNP on Wednesday, still not practicing in any capacity since Week 4. He has missed four consecutive games and is trending to miss a fifth one in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. In any injury taking this long for a return, a full practice is the best indicator of a return but the Bears may just wait until after their Week 10 bye to bring Monangai back. D’Andre Swift is in line for a workhorse game once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, QB Case Keenum, DB Malik Muhammad, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and OL Jordan van den Berg inactive for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: No real surprises here after Monangai was ruled out for Week 8 on Saturday, leaving D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson to handle backfield duties in a difficult matchup against the Seahawks. The two had operated in a loosely split backfield before Week 7, during which Swift saw workhorse usage in a tight game against the Patriots. It would appear likely that Swift will once again see the bulk of the work considering the opponent, making him a surefire RB2 with RB1 upside to cap the Week 8 festivities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is out for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: No surprise here as Monangai hasn’t practiced since Week 4. He’s set to miss his fourth consecutive game against the Seahawks in Week 8. Roschon Johnson figures to continue to serve as the Bears’ RB2 with Monangai sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Taliese Fuaga (knee) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 11 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Asim Richards (knee) was also ruled out, leaving the Saints with 24-year-old UDFA Mason Murphy as a potential Week 11 starter at tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Tailese Fuaga (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has a knee sprain, per Kellen Moore. It sounds like a short-term thing and Moore has said he won’t need to go on injured reserve. Asim Richards and Mason Murphy are the backup tackles and Richards played left tackle while Kelvin Banks was sidelined earlier this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 14 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga played in Week 13, but appears to have injured his other ankle — this is not the same ankle he was on the report for earlier in the year — somewhere along the way despite playing 100 percent of the snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints declared S Ugo Amadi, CB Rejzon Wright, RB Audric Estime, OT Taliese Fuaga, DT John Ridgeway III, and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 12 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has been sidelined with an ankle injury for the last few weeks. He was a limited practice participant on Friday, but is still not yet ready to go. Estime is also inactive in the backfield with Alvin Kamara (ankle) good to go for Week 12 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints ruled out OT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ depleted offensive line is in rough shape. Fuaga has a long way to go in his development, having allowed 22 quarterback pressures and three sacks this season, but downgrading to his backup, OT Asim Richards, won’t be any better. They face the Panthers this weekend, who field a solid defensive tackle unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) has a high-ankle sprain and is unlikely to play this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Ditto Jack Stoll. Fuaga has played through multiple injuries this year, with a knee and back listing. The second-year tackle has played up to his form last year, with a 65.0 PFF rating in 473 dropbacks. Asim Richards replaced him for the final two snaps of Week 9’s loss to the Rams and would be next man up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (knee/back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle is now firmly on track to suit up in Week 4 against the Bills. Fuaga entered Week 2 with a knee injury and exited Week 2 with a back injury as well. The 23-year-old was unable to play in Week 3 against the Seahawks. Saints EDGE Chase Young (calf) and OG Dillon Radunz (toe) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (knee/back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga missed Week 3 with the pair of injuries. Trevor Penning was active but did not play. Penning was upgraded to a full participant in Wednesday’s practice and could be ready to make his first start by Sunday. Getting both linemen back in the trenches would be a notable boost for Spencer Rattler as he searches for his first NFL win.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that A.J. Brown (hamstring) is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: According to Reiss, Brown would normally be a candidate to land on injured reserve, but the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve. The Patriots are on bye this week. Were Brown to be placed on injured reserve, he would be eligible to return for the Patriots’ Week 16 game against the Jets after missing four games. Although he will remain on the active roster, Reiss’ comments suggest Week 16 could be Brown’s expected return date. For fantasy leagues with an injured reserve spot, Brown is worth holding onto. For leagues that lack an injured reserve spot, it might make sense to drop him for a fill-in starter at the running back spot, or a player of equivalent value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports A.J. Brown (hamstring) will undergo further testing this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown’s imaging will take place once the Patriots return from Germany, potentially as early as Monday. Florio referred to the Patriots’ Week 11 bye as “good news” for Brown, which could indicate he has a chance to play in Week 12 against the Chargers, but we really don’t know for sure. We should learn more once the imaging is complete. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: The Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan reports A.J. Brown (hamstring) left the Patriots’ locker room with a limp after the team’s Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown declined to speak to the media after the game. Head coach Mike Vrabel could only say he was unable to finish the game and the team will learn more when they get back from Germany. Brown injured his hamstring late in the team’s loss to Detroit. He briefly tried to play through it but eventually left for the locker room and did not return. With a Week 11 bye on tap, we might not get concrete information on his injury for a little while.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown tried to gut it out through this issue early in the fourth quarter, but he ultimately walked off the field and into the locker room, likely ending his day. Even though he’s listed as questionable, we don’t expect him to return in a blowout loss. He will have a Week 11 bye to get healthy, though it’s looking like a lost season for the former superstar. Brown missed a month with a high-ankle injury early in the year, and now his lingering knee issue won’t go away, even as he tries to play through it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Rhamondre Stevenson is also active. Brown made the trip to Germany and was limited in all three practices this week. He has been dealing with knee issues for several years, and we’re sure this isn’t the last we will hear of it in 2026. Still, he has been cleared for action today, meaning fantasy managers should get him in their lineups. We’re treating him as a volatile WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Two limited practices would seem to have him with a real chance to play in Munich, and the fact that he made the trip at all makes it seem likely he’ll have a real chance to go. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown traveled to Germany with the team and is already practicing to start the week, giving him a shot at suiting up on Sunday morning. Given his lengthy history of knee issues, it still wouldn’t surprise us if he gets another week off. Brown would be in line for a strong workload and WR2 fantasy numbers if active. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team plans to bring A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) to Germany ahead of Week 10’s game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This doesn’t mean Brown will suit up against the Lions, but it is an indicator that the team thinks he has a chance to play if he can have a good week of practice. Brown has missed the Patriots’ last two games after a knee injury flared up following Week 7’s game against the Bears. He did not get on the practice field at all last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an improvement for the 29-year-old receiver. In three games this season, Brown has caught just 9-of-20 targets for 101 scoreless yards. That said, if he’s healthy enough to play in Week 10, he could be primed for a breakout against a lowly Lions secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye fractured his fibula and it is expected to sideline him “deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye is being given the Jaxson Dart Memorial Puncher’s Chance of returning, but it doesn’t look likely that he’ll return this year and, if you were holding out hope for whatever reason, he can be dropped in most re-draft leagues at this time. Maye won’t have to undergo surgery and there was no additional ligament damage. The Patriots may choose to not put Maye on injured reserve because they are already near the limit of how many players they can designate to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes “it would be a surprise” if Drake Maye (ankle) played again this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Rapoport said that Maye would not play for the “foreseeable future” and noted that though the Patriots have not confirmed that Maye fractured his ankle, almost all of the reporting points to that reality. We’re all waiting for the Patriots to actually confirm this, which won’t happen any time soon because they’re on bye, but Maye can be dropped with little fear in shallow redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: According to Schefter, Maye stayed overnight in Germany to undergo testing and determine whether or not he would need surgery. For now, Maye is out indefinitely, but the 24-year-old QB and 2025 MVP runner-up could be looking at missing the rest of the season for the now 5-5 Patriots. His absence would force the Patriots to start Tommy DeVito in Week 12 against the Chargers, which would all but spell disaster for all Patriots skill players from a fantasy perspective. DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday’s loss and has a career passing line of 1,450-9-4 in 15 career games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports it’s “possible” Drake Maye (lower leg) misses the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Per Rapoport, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time.” It’s devastating news for Patriots fans and fantasy managers. While Maye has had his ups and downs this year, the team was nonfunctional without him on Sunday. Tommy DeVito took over for an injured Maye early in the first quarter and threw for 81 yards at 3.4 yards per attempt. The Pats also have seventh-round rookie Behren Morton on the roster. We suspect DeVito will get another shot at the starting job, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see Morton under center at some point this year. With A.J. Brown also banged up and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Pats are shaping up to be a fantasy wasteland over the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that the Patriots expect Drake Maye (ankle) to be sidelined for “a while.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter against the Lions today and was unable to return. We expect more updates to follow after Maye undergoes further testing once the team returns from Germany. The Patriots go on bye in Week 11, but it sounds like the early indications are that Maye will be sidelined beyond that. They face the Chargers in Week 12 and the division-rival Bills in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s ankle rolled while he was being sacked early in the first quarter. He initially appeared ready to play through it, but Maye walked to the locker room at the start of the Pats’ next drive. The fact that Maye was able to walk off under his own power, albeit with a slight limp, is at least a good sign. Tommy DeVito is under center for the Pats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 16-of-20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ 24-19, Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding eight rushes for five yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s two-yard touchdown run was a thing of beauty. The Patriots quarterback took off to the right side of the field, faking a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson, which caused a Dolphins defender to fully bite on it, running right past Maye while the Patriots’ quarterback darted into the end zone. Maye’s first touchdown pass was thrown to Kyle Williams on a post route. It was well-placed, allowing Williams to secure the ball in stride just before entering the end zone. Maye later linked up with DeMario Douglas via play action for his second score. The Patriots’ quarterback is a QB1 against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Christian Benford (groin) will not play in Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Neither will Dorian Williams (calf) who also missed practice most of the week. Neither player is regarded as having a long-term injury, per Brady, so they should have a chance to get up for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford and Bills LB Dorian Williams (calf) remained sidelined today. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but he is still firmly in the questionable camp. The Bills can probably sneak past the Dolphins if a few of their defenders are absent, but having them on the field is obviously ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford is the Bills’ No. 1 perimeter cornerback. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) and LB Dorian Williams (calf) were also sidelined to begin Week 11. The Bills face the Dolphins this weekend. Bills C Connor McGovern (neck) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 10 with a groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford was questionable to play in Week 10 with a wrist injury but was cleared to go. He then injured his groin in the fourth quarter and will not return to the game. The Bills are set to face the Dolphins in Week 11 before facing the Chiefs the following week, so there is a chance that they hold their top cornerback out for next week. We’ll have to see if he is able to practice at all during the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (wrist) is active for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford was questionable due to a wrist injury suffered in last week’s game against the Vikings. With Jordan Hancock also coming off the injured list, the Bills have a fully healthy secondary, including the addition of safety Amani Hooker. The Bills declared QB Shane Buechele, OT Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) is not on the Bills’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are both good to go this weekend. Bills RT Spencer Brown (ankle) is unfortunately doubtful to play. Overall, the Bills’ offensive line health is trending in the right direction, though. Bills CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (toe) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford has a chance to return for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Rams. That said, his play declined last year, and it hasn’t exactly rebounded. If active, Benford should not dissuade anyone from treating the Rams’ wide receivers as they normally would.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said CB Christian Benford (toe) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Despite the questionable listing, Benford did not appear in the media portion of practice on Friday. At best, he’ll be listed as limited later today. Benford seems to be on the pessimistic side of questionable for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Bills’ No. 1 cornerback is on the wrong side of questionable through two Week 4 practices. Fortunately, the Patriots’ wide receiver corps is nothing to write home about.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 11 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Madubuike did not practice all week after injuring the hamstring on Monday night. A prolonged absence wouldn’t be surprising, but the Ravens have been tight-lipped about it so far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: The Ravens’ talented rookie guard continues to practice and play through two difficult injuries. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) remains sidelined through two Week 11 practices. Ioane should be able to face the Panthers this weekend. Madubuike could be sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) isn’t on Baltimore’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Questionable with this ailment last week, Hendrickson played in Week 2 with a cast. It seems like that will be the plan going forward. Hendrickson got in a full session today. Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was also not on the injury report and is slated to make his season debut in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Zay Flowers (hamstring) has a “good shot” to play in Week 3 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Flowers is one of multiple injured players who Minter said could play in Week 3. Flowers missed Week 2’s game against the Saints after reaggravating his hamstring injury in Week 1 against the Colts, but he was able to practice in a limited capacity to close out the week. We’ll see how he fares this week when the Ravens release their first injury report, but it sounds like the star receiver is trending in the right direction. In addition to Flowers, Minter also said DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and LB Teddye Buchanan (knee) could also return agains the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) is questionable for Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Hendrickson managed to upgrade to a limited showing in practice Friday after missing the previous two days, opening the door for him to be active on Sunday. The perennial tradition of the Ravens experiencing significant defensive injuries seems to be making an appearance early this year, with Nnamdi Madubuike and T.J. Tampa already ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said the team will evaluate DL Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) at the end of the week to determine whether he can play in Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Madubuike sat out in Week 1 after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Prior to his neck injury, he was a pivotal player on the Ravens’ defensive line. It seems as though he is still ramping up after a lengthy recovery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens HC Jesse Minter said DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) will not play in Week 1 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Despite being a limited participant in practice all week, the Ravens will continue to exercise caution with Madubuike, who is attempting to return from what was once believed to be a career-ending neck injury. The 28-year-old lineman has had an encouraging offseason and training camp and could find himself on the field soon, but the Ravens will give him at least one more week to prepare. We’ll see if he’s able to suit up for Week 2 when the Ravens play host to the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Madubuike is seemingly on track to debut with his teammates, though his limited practice participation could result in limited snaps on game day. The interior game-wrecker is returning from a serious neck injury. Even playing on a snap count, Madubuike can make his presence felt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Madubuike joined team drills last week, and is technically on track to play in Week 1 against the Colts. If active, the stud defensive tackle will likely be on a snap count, though the team could opt for a conservative approach and hold him out for this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) resumed participating in team drills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-mad.analysis: Ravens coach Jesse Minter labeled Madubuike as “day-to-day” heading into Week 1. This does not necessarily mean Madubuike will take the field against the Colts next week, but it is a step in the right direction. Madubuike racked up 10 quarterback pressures, two sacks and three tackles in just two games played last year. Getting him back, even in a limited capacity, is a big deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful for Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid has not practiced yet this week and we’re guessing from this designation he won’t be heading to the field on Friday either. This has, sadly, become pretty standard for Kincaid as he simply has to be managed week-to-week on the injury report. Dawson Knox should join the TE2 ranks for Week 11 assuming Kincaid is out, though it’s plausible Kincaid’s fantasy managers can do better on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: This is a little concerning. Backup plans should be made at this time. Kincaid played through the ankle injury in Week 10 against the Jets, but evidently picked up a thumb injury along the way. Dawson Knox would only be a TE2 if Kincaid sits, but the Dolphins’ defense is hardly imposing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid played through the ankle injury last week, catching two passes for 58 yards. The thumb injury is new and likely happened in-game. Kincaid has successfully played through multiple injuries this season, so we are optimistic about his availability for the Bills’ Week 11 game against the Dolphins, though Buffalo may be able to run out the clock with ease on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid had one huge play in the third quarter, with a 54-yard catch down the sideline. There wasn’t much else to his day, but he was targeted in the end zone on a play that wound up being called defensive pass interference. He remains more of a high-end TE2 in a crowded passing attack in Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) is not on the Bills’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: With Kincaid’s multi-year knee injury behind him, the Bills’ tight end put together a great offseason and has proven to be a reliable player even when banged up this season. Kincaid is firmly in the TE1 ranks for this divisional showdown against the Jets in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: After two limited sessions we don’t have a lot of doubt that Kincaid will be ready to play in Week 10’s game against the Jets. He may be managed a bit, though, as he toughs it out. He’ll remain a TE1 play regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid has successfully played through a couple of injuries this season, and we expect that to be the case again this week, when the Bills face the Jets. Kincaid’s early-week limited participation puts him on track to play. He is a TE1 in this divisional showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught all three targets for 28 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was asked to block at an increased rate against a Minnesota defense that currently holds the NFL record for highest blitz rate, heavily influence both his route rate and volume. Normal TE3 Keleki Latu caught his first professional touchdown on a broken play near the end of the first half, which was the only touchdown thrown from quarterback Josh Allen. Kincaid has been one of fantasy’s biggest disappointments considering his lofty draft capital this summer, now held to four receptions or fewer in five of eight games to start the 2026 season. He’ll be a high end TE2 against the Jets in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid remained limited in all three practices last week, so today’s return to full participation is great to see. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense often requires tight ends to stay in line to block, which could hurt Kincaid’s route volume. Regardless, he is too talented to be removed from the TE1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. It’s a tough matchup, and he could be asked to block more than usual. Still, Kincaid warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his talent, usage and quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will start in Week 12 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: The surprising release of Daniel Jones immediately thrusts Richardson back into the QB1 role, a role he hasn’t held since 2024. The former No. 4 overall pick now has a chance to make the most of what is a lost season for the Colts, who are fresh off a 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Richardson has played sparingly this season, completing 2-of-4 passes for eight yards while rushing three times for six yards. Playing in an offense that’s devoid of weapons at receiver, the Colts would benefit from leaning into Richardson’s ability as an athlete by utilizing him in the ground game. Richardson’s rushing upside could eventually put him on the radar as a decent QB2, but we will conservatively project him as a low-end QB2/QB3 in his first start in over two years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he will “evaluate everything” at QB after Daniels Jones’ poor outing in Week 11’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Steichen didn’t commit to Jones as the Colts’ Week 12 starter for next week’s game against the Giants. Anthony Richardson replaced Jones late in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, but the Colts have been reluctant to bench Jones, despite a disastrous season in which he has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. It feels like a switch to Richardson is inevitable at some point. With some extra time to prep him for next week’s game, now could be the time to make the move back to the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that the Colts have a “package of plays in the playbook” for Anthony Richardson, but it is unclear whether they will “ever” use them.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Holder stops short of making any declarative statements, but today’s article implies that some in the Colts’ organization may be wondering why their 24-year-old quarterback hasn’t at least been used as a situational player. Holder compares Daniel Jones’ poor play to positive remarks made by Colts defenders regarding Richardson’s explosive dual-threat abilities. Holder does note that the Colts have at least considered using Richardson’s “electric running ability” to give them “a spark,” but for whatever reason, that hasn’t happened yet. Richardson could be worth stashing in superflex leagues, though there is no guarantee that he will take the field on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will start in Week 9 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: After taking some time to evaluate his quarterback room, Steichen has decided to stick with Jones, saying he believes Jones gives the Colts “the best chance to win right now.” Jones has struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts and is now sitting on a 1,542-5-9 passing line this season, and he tossed two picks in Week 8’s 42-7 blowout loss to the Jaguars. He was pulled in favor of Anthony Richardson late in the game, but he will get at least one more start against a woeful Cowboys defense that is fresh off blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead to the Cardinals in a comeback that was orchestrated by Gardner Minshew. With only two teams on bye this week, Jones is nothing more than a desperation streamer in 2QB/superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports that Joe Fagnano (undisclosed) said he thinks he is healthy enough to play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: According to Zrebiec, Fagnano “was hobbled by game’s end, after he took a low and penalized hit” from Bills DL Ed Oliver. Fagnano said he and the team will have to wait and “see” how he is feeling in the coming days, noting that “you’re always going to have bumps and bruises” after a football game. Lamar Jackson (thumb) is already headed to injured reserve and Tyler Huntley will undergo an MRI tomorrow to assess a potential turf toe injury. Zrebiec rightly writes that the Ravens “will almost certainly have to bring in at least one quarterback, if not two,” this week. He lists Anthony Richardson and Tua Tagovailoa as potential trade targets. At this point, it is unclear who will start for the Ravens on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts Shane Steichen said he is “going to evaluate everything, every position going forward.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: This is the first time this season that Steichen has left open the possibility of replacing Daniel Jones as the team’s official starter. Anthony Richardson replaced him in-game today, with just under 12 minutes remaining. It seems as though Richardson, or even fellow backup Riley Leonard, could end up playing next week against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson’s status with the team after being charged with a misdemeanor for marijuana possession has not changed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: This is presumably good news for Richardson, who could be an injury or benching of Daniel Jones away from seeing his first action in 2026. Richardson was cited for marijuana possession earlier this month and said after Week 7’s loss to the Vikings that he doesn’t “really regret a lot of things I do” when asked about it after the game. Steichen said he had conversations with Richardson, which will remain private, but it sounds like his status as the Colts’ QB2 remains intact heading into Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said he has not thought about a change at quarterback and he has “a ton of faith” in Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Always a good sign for the quarterback when the coach has to defend his plan to keep starting said quarterback in back-to-back postgame availabilities. While we empathize with the Indianapolis media that clearly has seen enough of Jones, we’re not sure what exactly they think will go differently with Anthony Richardson — who spent his press availability on Sunday noting that he doesn’t “really regret a lot of things I do” after a citation for marijuana possession — under center. Richardson’s in the final year of his rookie contract. The Colts remain a mess after firing Chris Ballard. Jones probably won’t play this poorly next week against a non-Vikings defense, but it’s hard to deny that he’s playing poorly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: FOX59’s Tyler Haughn reports Colts QB Anthony Richardson was charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana earlier this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: According to reports, Richardson was stopped on October 12th for having a registration on his car that had expired and was assigned to a different vehicle. The officer reported noticing the “odor of marijuana” coming from Richardson’s car, and the former first-round pick admitted to smoking in the car; a “small mason jar containing a substance believed to be marijuana and an opened bag of THC-infused gummies” were found in his vehicle during a search. Richardson is scheduled to have a bench trial on January 4th, 2027. While the NFL no longer suspends players for testing positive for THC, it’s possible Richardson faces some kind of penalty from the league with this being a legal issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts HC Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson (groin) will be good to go for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson will be dressed to back up Daniel Jones in Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Richardson tweaked his groin while lifting earlier this week, per head coach Shane Steichen, but he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday. He’s probably best regarded as a true question mark, though nobody’s fantasy lineup should be riding on him being inactive or not. Tremble would be a reasonable TE2 play if he were able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble, who had 48 yards last week against the Saints, is probably the preferred TE2 play between himself and Darren Waller if both players make it to Sunday’s game against the Ravens healthy. Each of them logged a limited session on Thursday after missing Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Darren Waller (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Waller is sometimes given Wednesdays often, so this could just be precautionary. Panthers backup TE Tommy Tremble (knee) was also listed as a non-participant. Hopefully, one of them is good to go for this week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-5 targets for 48 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Darren Waller, meanwhile, caught two of his four targets for 24 yards and nearly came down with a long touchdown in the first half. Tremble ran a route on 18 of 37 Carolina drop backs in a Carolina offense that has increased its two tight end usage. Tremble now has eight receptions over his past two games. He plays the Ravens in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Waller ran a route on 27 of the team’s 38 drop backs and should have caught what would have been a 30-yard touchdown in the first half. Coming off a big game in Week 9 against the Broncos, Waller was fourth on the team in targets as the Panthers turned hard toward the run. Tommy Tremble had more targets, receptions, and yards than Waller on the day. Waller’s red zone role and the Panthers usual pass heaviness should keep him viable as a streaming option in Week 11 against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, RB AJ Dillon, DT TeRah Edwards, C Sam Hecht, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee, and LB Bobby Okereke inactive for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Sanders will be out against the Saints, meaning Tommy Tremble will get a decent number of snaps and routes. He’ll be the TE2 behind Darren Waller, coming off his biggest game of the season. The Saints this season have allowed the third highest fantasy points per target to opposing tight ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-6 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers liked something in their middle of the field matchups with the Broncos’ defense, targeting Tremble and Darren Waller 16 combined times. Both seam stretchers scored, with Tremble’s TD his first since Week 6. Tremble’s name has come up in the box score more than expected this year, but he has yet to have a 50-yard day and has three total touchdowns. He remains waiver-wire fodder in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught all four of his targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers seemed a little concerned about the Eagles’ pass rush since Tremble played on 54 of the team’s 79 snaps. He also was on the field for more than half of their dropbacks, but a large chunk of those were in pass-blocking situations. Still, he was schemed wide open on both touchdown passes, which led to a great fantasy day. It’s just not something we would recommend chasing next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person believes the Panthers could target TE Kenyon Sadiq in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Person said the Panthers, who hold the 19th pick in the 2026 draft, could target two Oregon players: Sadiq, who had 51 receptions for 560 yards and eight touchdowns in his final collegiate season, and safety Dillon Thieneman, one of the most sought-after secondary options in this year’s draft. The team would likely have to trade up to make sure they have a shot at Sadiq, who would join Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders in the Carolina tight end room if he lands with the Panthers. The Panthers in 2025 targeted the tight end position at a 21 percent clip, the seventh lowest mark in the NFL. “Could that change with Brad Idzik taking over the play calling and the addition of offensive specialist Darrell Bevell, who was in Seattle with Canales when the Seahawks traded for All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham?” Person said. “Possibly.” Sadiq, who ranks 11th in yards per route run among tight ends in the 2026 draft class, would probably be a rotational player in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 3-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Carolina’s Wild Card Round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers failed to establish a full-time TE1 for most of this year, with Tremble only going over 75.4 percent of the snaps in the final two games of the regular season. He played 54-of-67 snaps versus the Rams. Tremble caught more than one ball in six of his 18 games played this season. He’s low-end TE2 fodder at best entering the final year of his contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He got in two limited practices on Thursday and Friday. You’re probably not planning to play either he or fellow questionable tight end Tommy Tremble as anything more than a TE2 either way. If both players were somehow ruled out, Mitchell Evans would take their place in the pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He didn’t practice Wednesday, so this is a good sign for his availability. With Tommy Tremble also practicing though, we may remain in the Panthers TE Stasis where both players are taking too much volume off the table for you to want to start either of them in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller is sometimes given Wednesdays often, so this could just be precautionary. Panthers backup TE Tommy Tremble (knee) was also listed as a non-participant. Hopefully, one of them is good to go for this week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller ran a route on 27 of the team’s 38 drop backs and should have caught what would have been a 30-yard touchdown in the first half. Coming off a big game in Week 9 against the Broncos, Waller was fourth on the team in targets as the Panthers turned hard toward the run. Tommy Tremble had more targets, receptions, and yards than Waller on the day. Waller’s red zone role and the Panthers usual pass heaviness should keep him viable as a streaming option in Week 11 against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 8-of-10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: By far the best game of Waller’s first season in Carolina came as Tommy Tremble also found the end zone. The duo combined for 12 catches as Bryce Young flooded the middle of the field with looks. Good stuff if you were forced to take a TE2 dart throw, but this is the first time since Week 3 Waller has seen genuine volume. We would consider it a one-off spiked week heading into an admittedly plus Week 10 date in the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller scored a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller’s second quarter touchdown came after he beat a linebacker on a post route. It was also one of just two targets in a game the Panthers went on to lose 43-13. Waller’s score was the only black and teal tally before garbage time. Nice, though Waller had previously not found the end zone since Week 2. He has 14 total catches through six games. The limited overall workload has made Waller difficult to trust as a TE2 because of his zero-point floor. He will have some big-play potential Thursday against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller did not have a catch on two targets in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Initial reports have Waller playing on 36 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 21 of their 46 dropbacks. Tommy Tremble, the other tight end, ran a route on 14 dropbacks, so Waller is technically the primary option in the passing game of the two. However, Tremble scored two touchdowns this week. We don’t recommend chasing either guy in fantasy right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) is not on Carolina’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He upgraded to a full practice today. Waller will be a low-end TE2 with Jalen Coker (quad) playing in Week 6 against a Jalen Hurts-less Eagles outfit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He appears to be trending towards playing, though Waller is old enough that we probably shouldn’t count it as a sure thing that he’ll get off the questionable line. Waller would be a reasonable TE2 if he plays against the Eagles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: The Panthers should have their veteran receiving tight end on the field when they take on the Eagles this week. Waller remains a viable TE1, albeit as a somewhat volatile producer. We expect him to be practicing in full by the end of the week, coming off a restful bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks practiced in full all three days this week and we’ve seen players pacing to be activated off injured reserve be given this soft questionable listing several times this year. Expect Brooks to play as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. He’ll likely be brought along slowly in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: The Panthers listed Brooks as a full participant for two practices last week before amending his participation to limited at the end of the week. We doubt they’ll do that again. Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters today that he thinks Brooks is “ready.” He can be speculatively stashed in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers downgraded Jonathon Brooks (core) to out for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game as he attempts to return from a core muscle injury. He managed a week of limited sessions before initially being listed as doubtful, ultimately ruled out. Chuba Hubbard will again serve as a legitimate workhorse in a plus matchup against the Saints and can be treated as a back-end RB1 in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (core) is doubtful for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks was previously listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, only for head coach Dave Canales to announce on Friday that Brooks was working with the scout team, not the 53-man roster, meaning he was actually limited throughout the week. After logging three limited practices, Brooks appears unlikely to play in Week 10 given the doubtful designation. With his return window opened earlier this week, the Panthers could delay his return by two more weeks before having to either rule him out for the season or activate him from injured reserve. We will see how things go for him next week ahead of Week 11’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers designated Jonathon Brooks (core) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks practiced in full, giving him a shot at suiting up this week. However, it won’t surprise us if they give him another week of practice before putting him back on the field because of his lengthy injury history. With Chuba Hubbard excelling in his workhorse role this year, Brooks will likely be stuck with change-of-pace duties once healthy. He is only worth stashing in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the team is weighing whether or not to open Jonathon Brooks (core) return window this week
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Canales said the oft-injured Brooks still has “some things to clear recovery-wise” but noted that he could still have his practice window opened this week. Brooks suffered a core muscle injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and handled just 11 touches in his first two games of the year. Given his injury history, it’s hard to know how close he could truly be to dressing on game day, but even when he does return, we would still expect Chuba Hubbard to handle the majority of touches given how efficient he has been this season. In addition to Brooks, Canales said the team is also weighing when to open the return window for Xavier Legette, who has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jonathon Brooks is expected to have core muscle surgery and will be placed on IR.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks will be sidelined for at least six weeks. It opens the door for Chuba Hubbard to dominate the Carolina backfield for the next month and a half, with AJ Dillon chipping in as a breather back. Through two game Hubbard leads the Panthers backfield with 22 rushes for 102 yards. He’s run a route on 50 percent of the team’s drop backs and have five targets. The Panthers, meanwhile, have the second highest pass rate over expected through Week 2. Hubbard will be a locked-in top-20 option going forward. Dillon can be stashed in case Hubbard gets dinged up while Brooks is recovering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is “gathering information” on Jonathon Brooks’ groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: He’s undergoing tests to determine the severity. That’s not normally the sort of story that ends with “and Brooks played a full allotment of snaps in Week 3,” but we’ll see. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Brooks is “considered week to week.” Brooks should be regarded as a drop candidate in shallow leagues on snaps and opportunities alone, but if he’s not healthy, that may expand to more leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jonathon Brooks aggravated his groin injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and is considered “day to day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: The good news is that this is unrelated to Brooks’ history of knee injuries and it sounds like he has a shot at suiting up for Week 3. The bad news is that Brooks originally suffered this groin injury during training camp and is still dealing with it two weeks into the season. Brooks only had five carries and one catch before exiting Week 2’s win over Atlanta. Even if he is healthy for next week’s game, Brooks is barely on the fantasy radar right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable to return in Week 2 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks went down on a routine tackle in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. He eventually left for the locker room with a towel over his head. Brooks missed time late in training camp with the groin issue and it seemingly flared up against the Falcons. He had five carries for 16 yards before leaving the game. AJ Dillon will back up Chuba Hubbard if Brooks is unavailable for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said “there is a possibility” Davante Adams (hamstring) plays in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported last week that the Rams were “hopeful” this would be the timeline for Adams’ return. McVay somewhat confirmed that optimism while speaking to the media on Friday, but noted that the star receiver isn’t “ready quite yet.” This follows McVay announcing that Puka Nacua (knee) will miss the next few months after MCL surgery, so it’s safe to assume the Rams will be thin at receiver in Week 12 when they take on the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams are “hopeful” that Davante Adams (hamstring) will return for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Over the next three weeks, the Rams face the Cardinals, go on bye and then face the Packers. While his potential return ahead of the fantasy football playoffs is helpful, we still have a long way to go before he returns, and even then, his status for Week 13 is still uncertain. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels appear to be in line for 11 personnel duties at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) successfully underwent surgery, and his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: If Adams hit the absolute soonest return date, week-wise, he theoretically could face the Chiefs in Week 13, but that game takes place on Thursday night. We suspect facing the 49ers in Week 14 is more likely, though nothing is guaranteed for a 33-year-old player. Adams should be stashed in injured reserve spots, where possible. He makes for a tough cut in leagues without them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.
