https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack. Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 4-of-9 targets for 32 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams was the victim of a bad Matthew Stafford ball or two in rainy Philadelphia conditions, but he sadly immediately reverted to clear No. 2 wideout status with Puka Nacua back in the lineup. Nacua went off for 9/125. Adams now has seven catches for 58 scoreless yards in two games with Nacua in the lineup compared to 15/332/2 in two games without. Hopefully that trend normalizes a bit for a potential Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson’s three targets were a product of a game environment dominated by the Houston defense, with no player seeing more than the five targets accounted for by alpha wide receiver Nico Collins. Fantasy managers that were riding the recent production from Hutchinson were surely left disappointed in the down performance, with his next opportunity to return a usable fantasy outing coming in a Week 14 meeting with the Ravens. It remains to be seen whether Marvin Harrison Jr. will make it back in time for that contest, something that could influence the upside of Hutchinson in a zone-heavy matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-9 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: His touchdown catch came on a misdirection play where he camped out and waited for the Browns to react to the initial action before getting a wide-open path to the end zone. After Tank Dell returned and the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., there remained Hutchinson, now with three touchdowns in three games after the bye. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts this week with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 29 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: The Texans’ run-blocking specialist isn’t going anywhere. He capped off the Texans’ opening drive with an 18-yard touchdown on third down, and came up clutch with a tough catch to pick up a first down on the ensuing drive. He later let a pass go off his fingertips 38 yards downfield, near the Texans’ 25-yard line. Had he caught it and landed on his feet, he probably could have scored. He had the secondary beat. Hutchinson cannot be trusted to return FLEX value against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding two carries for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: One of the carries came on Houston’s last goal-to-go sequence of the game, where they wound up setting up what looked like a Hutchinson pass only to see him tuck the ball and run. We got nothing. With Tank Dell back and Marvin Harrison Jr. looking for work as well, it would seem that Hutchinson’s days as a FLEX option are over. But we would have said that before this game as well, and Hutchinson wound up with more wideout snaps than anyone but Nico Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He managed to get his finger underneath a sideline ball for a 21-yarder, and the replay booth upheld the ruling of catch on the field. He also managed fewer targets than Xavier Hutchinson (five), as well as 10 fewer yards, despite Hutchinson playing 16 snaps to Boutte’s 32. The Nick Caley WR platoon will continue until morale improves, making nobody much of a FLEX play against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 51 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson left the game after catching a 28-yarder in the fourth quarter and visited the blue medical tent. The Texans never announced a status for him, so it’s something to monitor. He lead the team in targets and yards. We guess that’s just where things are for the Texans now. If Hutchinson is healthy and Nico Collins is not in Week 4, he’ll have fringe FLEX/WR4 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Through two games, Hutchinson has 15 targets and 69 yards. If you’re going to be this bad, you at least want the meme number. Hutchinson let a (admittedly hard to reel in) C.J. Stroud ball hit him in the hands in the end zone before dropping it and repeatedly struggled to finish contested catches, as he did in Week 1. Hutchinson is a fine depth receiver who has been pushed into a role he simply can’t do at the NFL level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if Texans WR Jaylin Noel is more involved in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Rapoport adds that Noel is “really talented.” We agree, but the Texans have consistently played WR Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him. Noel, 24, is an explosive player, and the Texans will be looking for playmakers to contribute with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined this week. Noel is officially on the boom-bust FLEX radar in Week 2 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell was blanked in the first half before seeing three consecutive plays drawn up for him in the third quarter, catching all of them for his complete yardage total on the evening. The team continues to take a conservative approach with the young speedster after he missed more than a year with one of the more gruesome injuries you will see, holding his fantasy value in check in the process. Dell can likely be stashed for the potential he sees his route rate increase later in the season but is likely best left on fantasy benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught 3-of-4 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He added a zero-yard carry. His longest catch was for 29 yards. That about sums up his other four targets. Dell wasn’t able to shake man coverage very often and the Browns put the clamps on in the second half. He managed just 33-of-67 snaps. He’ll remain on the FLEX line against the Colts on Thursday night in what should be a more zone-heavy game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The diminutive speedster got in back-to-back full practices and should see a reasonable workload against the Browns. He’s a low-end WR3 or high-end FLEX play at this point, with more upside possible if he’s able to repeat last week’s target share.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell is firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns. He led the team with nine targets last week, catching four passes for 105 yards and one touchdown. The coaching staff reportedly drew up a play just to get him over the century mark. He is a FLEX starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans’ diminutive wide receiver led the team with nine targets last week, and evidently got a little banged up in the process. Dell’s early-week participation puts him on track to face the Browns this weekend though. He is a FLEX starter, assuming he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught 4-of-9 targets for 105 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans seemed fairly comfortable using Dell in this one, getting him going with a screen pass on the opening drive. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard touchdown via a go route, in which he simply ran past his coverage defender down the right sideline. CJ Stroud hit Dell in stride and he continued on down the field and into the end zone. Dell managed to earn an end zone target on the Texans’ 11th drive, but was unable to secure it. Dell is officially on the WR3/FLEX radar for Week 10 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M Alexander reports Jaylin Noel (toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: It’s a rough blow for Noel, who had been extremely efficient on his targets. It does clear up space for some of Houston’s other receivers. The recently-activated Tank Dell and recently-acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. will benefit a bit from one fewer mouth to feed after the Texans come off bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught his only target for 43 yards in Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He added a two-yard rush on an end around. While it was good to see him back on the field, it should be noted that it looked like his 43-yard catch glanced off Jaylin Noel’s hands and seemed to immaculately find it’s way into Dell’s as he scampered off for some yards after the catch. Dell further confounded the Houston Wideout Situation, playing just 14 snaps. We have no idea what to trust here beyond Nico Collins. Dell seemed to be running just fine, though it sounded like at times his delay in getting up to speed was about recovery. We’ll all get the Week 8 bye to sort this one out. Dell isn’t a must-roster through it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee) will play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell will make his long-awaited return next week against the Giants. By the time he takes the field in Week 7, Dell will have been more than 22 months removed from his last regular-season game, which came in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell suffered a torn ACL, LCL, and MCL, along with a dislocated knee, in that game against the Chiefs and has been on a long road to recovery. He’ll join a crowded receiver room that recently acquired Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel has posted a solid 17-334-2 line through the first six weeks of the season and topped 100 yards in Sunday’s win over the Jaguars. Targets could be hard to come by for Dell, but his return next week is an impressive feat on its own given the injury he had to work through.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans ruled out Tank Dell (knee) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans depart for London tonight to face the Jaguars on Sunday, and Dell will remain in Texas. He is currently practicing in full, but the team has not yet cleared him for game-day activities. Dell does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught both targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte’s two targets were a product of minimal pass volume in a game the Texans were able to control with their defense. He made the most of the modest volume by coming down with a touchdown in the second quarter on a dime delivered by quarterback C.J. Stroud to the middle of the end zone from 24 yards out, catching the ball with the defender draped around his midsection. Boutte remains a shaky fantasy bet as nothing more than the third option through the air, with the team expecting to get back newcomer Marvin Harrison Jr. from a hamstring injury in short order. That could come as early as Week 12 considering the Texans now get a long week of preparation ahead of a meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: He managed to get his finger underneath a sideline ball for a 21-yarder, and the replay booth upheld the ruling of catch on the field. He also managed fewer targets than Xavier Hutchinson (five), as well as 10 fewer yards, despite Hutchinson playing 16 snaps to Boutte’s 32. The Nick Caley WR platoon will continue until morale improves, making nobody much of a FLEX play against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 2-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte played 35-of-52 snaps, and if that sounds low, it actually lead the team in Nick Caley’s absolutely bizarre WR platoon situation where it seems like he is trying to find someone who he trusts. Boutte looks the best of the bunch, but we can’t recommend trying to eat these non-existent fantasy points. Jaylin Noel (2/17 on two targets) and Jared Wayne (1/20 on four targets including an inexcusable drop) continue to haunt the situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Expected to be “used a lot” by Ian Rapoport’s reporting, Boutte was on the field for 53-of-76 snaps. He either didn’t look completely comfortable with the offense yet or wasn’t fully integrated, depending on how nice you want to be about it — C.J. Stroud’s one near-pick was in his area on a ball he wasn’t expecting and it was clear he and Dalton Schultz weren’t on the same page. Boutte’s role should continue to grow next week assuming Nico Collins remains out but the Texans haven’t really embraced his talents yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Texans WR Kayshon Boutte could be used “a lot” in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Rapoport’s full quote is winding and hyperbolic, but it sounds like Boutte will be a featured receiver if the Texans believe he is ready to handle that role with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined. Rapoport notes that Boutte played in “the same” offensive scheme during his time with the Patriots, so adjusting to his new team’s playbook theoretically should have been easy. That said, Boutte caught just one pass last week. He can be treated as a volatile but viable FLEX starter in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte managed just 36-of-79 snaps, third-most among Texans wideouts, as they ran weird platoons that had Jared Wayne, Jaylin Noel, and Xavier Hutchinson all on the field for at least 24 snaps. Until someone conclusively wins this job, or at least we start getting some juice that someone might win the job, it’ll be hard to start any of these receivers in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Speaking on Monday, Ryans said Boutte has been “picking up the playbook really well.” The fourth-year receiver was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24th and is expected to have an immediate role in the offense after the Texans lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL earlier this offseason. Boutte has served primarily as a field stretcher during his first three years in the league and shouldn’t be trusted in start/sit leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Texans placed WR Tank Dell on injured reserve, designated to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: The designation to return means that Dell is expected to contribute in some capacity this season, although he appears a ways off still. With Jaylin Noel still nursing an injury after experiencing a setback and Jayden Higgins lost for the season, recent acquisition Kayshon Boutte has all the runway to operate as the WR2 opposite Nico Collins to start the season. Xavier Hutchinson should also see an uptick in opportunities while tight end Dalton Schultz should see a significant boost in weekly volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Texans acquired WR Kayshon Boutte from the Patriots in exchange for S Jaylen Reed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero was the first to report the transaction. Boutte now gets a fresh start in Houston after being phased out of the Patriots’ offense following the additions of Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown this offseason. The 24-year-old receiver is in the final year of his rookie contract and has a chance to step into an immediate role for the Texans after they lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL last week. Boutte totaled 33 receptions for 551 yards and six touchdowns last season and has averaged 15.0 YPR in his last two seasons. He’s been used primarily as a field stretcher by the Patriots and will likely see a similar role in Houston, which could make meaningful fantasy production hard to come by.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins caught two passes, one of which went for his 42-yard touchdown, on the team’s second possession before being subject to modest pass volume due to increasingly positive game script. His touchdown grab will most certainly make an appearance on highlight reels for some time, mostly due to quarterback C.J. Stroud’s performance on the play. Stroud shrugged off a strong-side pass rusher to quickly reset his feet and deliver a strike downfield to Collins, turning a potential sack into a touchdown with the flick of his wrist. He appeared to effortlessly heave the ball 50 yards through the air without being able to step into the throw, placing the football where only Collins could catch it over the defender. Collins remains one of the league’s top talents at wide receiver but is subject to performances like this when the Texans are able to control games with their defense, which is exactly what transpired here. Up next for Collins and the Texans are the Ravens in Week 12, where the veteran receiver will remains an upside WR2 due to modest volume expectations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 9-of-16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Despite the fun line, it wasn’t exactly a game that left you feeling great about Collins. He looked heavily fatigued at times, notably grabbing his shoulder after one sideline collision, and also managed to cut short a route that led to C.J. Stroud’s only interception and cost the Texans at least three points at the end of the first half. Assuming he’s healthy, he’ll be in the WR1 mix again next week against the Colts on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 4-of-4 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins delivered a 19-yard catch-and-run on the Texans’ opening drive. He played particularly well running curl route today. His one-handed touchdown has to be seen to be believed. He and his coverage defender went vertical in the end zone and Collins somehow underhanded the pass around the other player’s body, briefly pinning it to the defender’s torso to secure it. Collins is a locked-in WR1 against the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He did draw a defensive pass interference and a defensive holding, so at least he helped in points per penalty leagues. The Giants had defenders draped all over Collins for the majority of the game, and he was punished when he did catch the ball. It was Collins’ worst box score return since his rookie season, and one of only four games in his career where he was targeted and did not return at least 13 yards. The Texans wideout situation is complicated, but we’d still bet on Collins returning from the bye as a low-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 76 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He added a long defensive pass interference penalty drawn on Travis Hunter to set up Houston’s second third-quarter touchdown. Collins also took an end around in the red zone for five rushing yards. Close, but ultimately not the line that fantasy managers were hoping for. Collins will remain in the low-end WR1 region against the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He went for 3/45 in the first half and was mostly managed down with the Texans not really threatened in a major way after he sealed a block for their first touchdown in the third quarter. Collins took a hard fall after a leaping grab and did look a little worse for the wear on the sideline. We wouldn’t be surprised if he saw injury report time this week. That said, he looked good and the Texans simply didn’t need to throw the ball much late in this one. It’s back to the low-end WR1 line next week against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He immediately busted out of the gates with a 45-yarder, caught a touchdown to end that drive, then found the end zone a second time in the second half when he worked to the other side of zone coverage and C.J. Stroud was able to find him on an improvised throw. Pretty good player. Collins handled 36-of-53 snaps, highest on the team. He’ll be a low-end WR1 against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He got in a full session and will escape the line. Collins doesn’t play the same amount of snaps that most of the league’s top wideouts play anyway, so even if he is managed a bit, he can be trusted as a low-end WR1 in what looks to be a smash spot against a bad Cowboys pass defense, though one that is integrating new trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr. against Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: We’re still waiting for the final injury report to drop, but Collins appears set to return in Week 4 after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury. Collins was listed as limited in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices and has been trending in the right direction all week. We’ll check back in when the Texans officially confirm Collins’ status ahead of the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Nico Collins (hamstring) was “optimistic” about playing in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Alexander caught up with Collins after the Texans’ star player logged his second consecutive limited practice. Collins should probably still be treated as sitting somewhere in the questionable-to-probable range, but this is great to hear. Collins is a WR1, as usual, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery shook off a relatively slow start to reach 100 yards on the ground for the first time as a member of the Texans, doing so with Woody marks inactive due to a concussion. Veteran journeyman Emari Demercado handled just seven touches as the primary change of pace option. Montgomery churned out consistently positive yardage but managed just one explosive run, a 15-yard scamper to ice the game late in the fourth quarter. No longer a featured back at this point in his career, the 100-yard showing could go down as his top fantasy performance of the season with Marks expected back from injury when the Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Treat Montgomery as a potential Flex option in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery is good to go after logging three full practices this week. With Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out for Week 11, Montgomery will likely return to a three-down role. Facing a toothless Colts team, he is back in the RB2 mix after missing over a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) is “trending in the right direction” of playing on Thursday Night.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: He officially got in a second-straight full practice on Tuesday. Montgomery should see the vast majority of the Texans run attack volume if he’s able to go, relegating Emari Demercado back to the bench outside of a few third-down plays here or there. It’s hard to trust that anything good will come of this given how the team has played this year, but Montgomery on volume would fit in as a low-end RB2 on a week with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was seen practicing Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery looks to be in line for a full workload in Thursday night’s game against the Colts, who have struggled mightily against the rush in recent weeks. Woody Marks, who sustained a concussion in Week 10 against the Browns, will very likely miss Thursday night as he works through the league’s concussion protocol. Montgomery will be a floor-based RB2/3 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: It is highly unlikely that Marks will clear concussion protocol on a short week, likely leaving Emari Demercado to split work with David Montgomery, the latter of whom was listed as a full participant as he aims to return from his own injury. Fantasy managers can consider Demercado a viable waiver target in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 10 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery entered the weekend listed as questionable after missing the previous three games plus the team’s Week 8 bye. Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for his return, while Woody Marks retains viable FLEX status playing as the top option alongside recent signee Emari Demercado.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery got in a full practice for the first time since returning from his groin injury. It’s certainly possible he’s back, but given a likely snap count in his return, it’d be hard to trust him as more than a what-the-heck FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery was mostly working out with a trainer, but DeMeco Ryans said they were “pleased with the progress he was making.” It’s possible this goes down as a DNP still on the official report, but it is real progress that he’s back on the field and he now has a non-zero chance to suit up for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans declared David Montgomery, S Reed Blankenship, TE Cade Stover, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery will miss another week with his groin injury, allowing Woody Marks to qualify as a low-end, volume-based RB2. Montgomery did not practice at all this week. His status for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns is up in the air. Fortunately for the Texans, S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) is making his return this week. Rookie TE Marlin Klein will also play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-27 passes for 194 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Texans’ 26-3, Week 11 win over the Colts, adding 27 yards on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud’s lone mistake came on the team’s first possession of the game when a poorly thrown ball over the middle of the field intended for Nico Collins was picked off. He would go to work from there, completing nine of his next 10 passes while throwing two touchdowns before the half. A 17-3 lead at the break saw a slight uptick with a safety on the defense’s first time on the field in the second half, with Stroud tacking on his third touchdown throw on the following possession. The team would go into coast mode from there, eventually chasing Daniel Jones from the game with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, with Stroud finishing with three or more touchdown passes for the fourth time in his last five appearances. Stroud and the Texans get the floundering Ravens in Week 12, where he will remain a back end QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 20-of-38 passes for 211 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in Houston’s 27-24, Week 10 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: What had started off as a fun 17-0 lead melted away into a dispiriting, likely season-ending loss to the Browns to fall to 3-6. Stroud managed to go just 5-of-19 for 21 yards in the second half as his receivers were blanketed in man coverage and their run game, as usual, was dead on arrival. Especially after Woody Marks left with a concussion. Stroud will probably retain low-end QB1 value against what looks to be a dire Colts defense in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception in the Texans’ 44-22, Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding two rushes for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud was nonchalantly excellent today, linking up with four different pass catchers for five touchdowns. He capped off the opening drive with a 17-yard, third-down touchdown strike to Xavier Hutchinson. Tank Dell hauled in Stroud’s second touchdown in stride, beating his coverage defender and racing into the end zone for a 63-yard score. Kayshon Boutte bagged two, including one against Chargers CB Duke Shelley, who Stroud picked on for much of the Texans’ seventh drive. He hit Nico Collins for an improbable one-handed score, in which Collins briefly pinned the football against his coverage defender’s torso to secure the catch. Stroud’s lone mistake was an off-target interception that one Chargers defender tipped to another. Stroud should remain in fantasy football lineups as a QB1 next week against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said he expects to eventually reach a deal on a contract extension with C.J. Stroud.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Caserio said that “nobody is discouraged” with how negotiations with Stroud and his agent have gone thus far, saying that the two sides just “couldn’t quite come to an agreement” yet. Stroud is in the fourth year of his rookie contract and had his fifth-year option picked up by the team earlier this offseason. He will be under contract through the 2027 regardless of how negotiations go, but we would expect him to sign a long-term extension at some point next offseason to avoid this becoming an issue come training camp. Despite the Texans’ 2-5 start to the season, Stroud has been mostly solid, throwing for 1,867 yards, 11 touchdowns, and one interception while completing 64.8 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 17-of-28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 27-21, Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The Texans seemed to always be playing from well behind the sticks today with 10 penalties and Stroud was let down by a ghastly drop from Marvin Harrison Jr. with someone in his face in the fourth quarter. The Giants did a better job than other teams had at getting interior pressure on Stroud. Still, it wasn’t a bad game outside of an immediate overtime three-and-out, one that was punctuated by a dropped pick by Kayvon Thibodeaux. Stroud heads into the bye as a reasonable high-end QB2 with a Week 9 matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 24-of-34 passes for 312 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Houston’s 34-31, Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The Texans running game was mostly abandoned until the fourth quarter, leaving Stroud to wail on an overmatched Jaguars secondary. His best throw was probably on Houston’s final possession of the first half, as he dotted a 50-yard throw with a defender in his face to Jaylin Noel, eventually setting up (checking notes) Foster Moreau’s second touchdown of the day. Stroud has now thrown for six touchdowns and gone over 260 yards in each of his last three games; he’s suddenly in the high-end QB2 competition with bye weeks hitting as the Texans host the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-34 passes for 261 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 26-3, Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: He added a rushing touchdown on a goal-to-go red zone keeper. The Texans offense continues to bog down with penalties and bad runs — they went into half with four field goals — but Stroud was able to pilot the ship well enough to keep things reasonable until the Titans defense broke in the second half. He’ll head to London next week to face the Jaguars, yet another team that should keep him throwing given how good their run defense is, so he’ll be a mid-range QB2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-31 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 34-30, Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Well, hard to blame much of this on him. Stroud was turnover-free for the third time in four games and peppered the returning Nico Collins with targets while also finding a 52-yarder to Jaylin Noel and several chunk gains to the tertiary receivers. The Texans had a 30-27 lead at the two-minute warning. For once, the defense gets to pick up the slack. The Texans have the mother of all get-right games in an 0-4 bowl against the Titans next week. Given how poorly the run offense is going, Stroud may continue to let it rip here and could be on the high-end QB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said he is open to leaning more into the passing game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: “The thing for me about offensive football is you have to make sure you move the ball and try to score as many points as possible,” Ryans is quoted as saying by the Houston Chronicle. “How that looks to me, it really doesn’t matter. You can think or want to be a certain thing. But if you’re shown that that’s not the case and it’s not getting done, then you have to adjust. That’s where we are.” The Texans already abandoned the run against the Bengals in Week 2, throwing the ball 55 times. Perhaps Nico Collins’ return this week will raise all ships, but if it was as simple as the Texans needing to throw more, they probably would have scored more than six points against the Bengals. C.J. Stroud has a streamable matchup against the Cowboys this week if it all comes together.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 16-of-27 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 19-17, Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: It was turnover-free football despite three sacks. Simply put: The Texans just don’t look like an NFL offense right now. Two of Stroud’s three deep balls in this game could have been intended for any of four different receivers, one of them hit off Jaylin Noel’s hands. Nobody has taken the reins. Texans OC Nick Caley deserves to be on the hot seat. Stroud passes the eye test when you watch these games, but the design of this offense — especially the run offense — is brutal. Stroud is near the bottom of the superflex QB2 ranks against the Cowboys next week, though the potential return of Nico Collins merits some consideration that better things could happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 1-of-5 targets for 22 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: The poor showing comes on the heels of a two-catch, one-yard performance in Week 10, leaving fantasy managers scratching their heads following the departures of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Warren briefly departed in the second quarter after being shaken up on his lone reception but returned to do absolutely nothing else for the remainder of the game. The Colts gained only 165 yards of total offense with Daniel Jones under center through almost 53 minutes of play, something that has become a routine occurrence of late. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before considering entering Warren into lineups. Even so, there appears to be no good option currently on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 2-of-3 targets for one yard in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding one carry for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was non-existent in the Colts’ passing game, converting three targets into just one yard. He did get a third-and-short carry that he took for three yards, but four total yards is an immensely disappointing day for the Colts’ supposed new No. 1 pass-catcher. Still on the field for nearly every offensive snap, Warren will see better days of utilization. His ceiling is capped in the Colts offense, but Warren sits on the TE1/2 borderline for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren wasn’t targeted in the first half as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching his first ball on the team’s second possession of the third quarter. The Colts limp toward Tuesday’s trade deadline with numerous key players the subject of trade speculation, of which quarterback Daniel Jones, wide receiver Josh Downs, and running back Jonathan Taylor are amongst. Which is to say, Warren’s fantasy expectations could be heavily influenced by the team’s actions in the coming days, potentially setting the second-year tight end up to be the team’s top option during the second half of the season. Warren would appear to be in a solid spot on paper against the Dolphins in Week 10, where his fantasy value will be dependent on who remains with the team through Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-10 targets for 18 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was active for the first time since Week 5 after recovering from a groin injury. As if that inefficiency was not enough, Warren also batted a late second quarter target into the air for an “interception” that turned into a 92-yard Jaguars touchdown. Brutal stuff, not that it’s anything new in a season where Warren has only two touchdowns and is averaging an abysmal 6.8 yards per reception. Daniel Jones is not playing well, but his seemingly inevitable benching would only make things worse with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard as the “alternatives.” Warren will be a low-end TE1 for Week 9 against the Cowboys. That is at least an A+ matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Tyler Warren (groin) is “good to go” for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was limited in practice on Thursday and Wednesday and will return to a rough receiver corps against a Jaguars defense coming off bye. Warren remains a startable TE1, but it’s hard to forge much of a ceiling case for him at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: It was his second consecutive limited showing following two missed games, with his level of activity Friday likely to be telling as it pertains to a potential return in Week 8. Warren’s absence has been felt hard by a Colts offense that has struggled to move the football consistently. He would likely return to a sizable role over the middle of the field against the pass-funnel Jaguars, if active in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: This is Warren’s first practice in two weeks, indicating he’s close to making a return. With Josh Downs failing to step up in his absence, the Colts desperately need Warren back in the lineup as their de facto WR1. Downs has also requested a trade, which would open up even more work for him. If all goes well in practice this week, Warren will be back in the TE1 mix for his Week 8 matchup with the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts declared TE Tyler Warren, LB Bryce Boettcher, LB CJ Allen, CB Sauce Gardner, TE Tyler Warren, WR Anthony Gould, G Dalton Tucker, and QB Riley Leonard inactive for Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was declared out earlier in the week due to a groin injury. Sauce Gardner (calf) and Anthony Gould (concussion) were also already declared out while Bryce Boettcher (groin) and CJ Allen (ankle) were declared out after having a questionable tag. Riley Leonard will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was a DNP throughout the week and has now been ruled out for this week’s game against the Vikings. This will be the second straight missed game for Warren, who first suffered the injury in last Friday’s practice. The Vikings have allowed the fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season, meaning fantasy managers are best off avoiding Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox as streaming options this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: He’s firmly on the wrong side of questionable. The media attention in Indianapolis this week has been spent on the firing of Chris Ballard rather than chasing down Warren’s status, but he does seem very unlikely to play and hasn’t practiced since last Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Both of Dulin’s receptions came on the opening possession of the game, with a 25-yard catch down the sideline sparking the drive that led to the team’s only points. The Colts remain a veritable disaster at present, leaving nobody on the weekly fantasy radar - Dulin most certainly included.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin saw two targets, catching one for an explosive 30-yard gain. He led all Colts pass-catchers in receiving yardage. Dulin saw just 13 offensive snaps and is a boom-or-bust fantasy play. He does not need to be rostered until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Chiefs acquired WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: It was an obvious fit. Downs will slot in as Kansas City’s No. 2 wideout behind Rashee Rice and his fantasy stock receives a slight upgrade — though we felt like we’ve spent all year saying that and never seeing any actual returns for it — while Xavier Worthy moves back to the undesirable FLEX shadow zone. The Colts had to make this trade as Downs was a free agent at year’s end, but it has left them with a completely indecipherable wideout room. Ashton Dulin is perhaps the No. 1 target Daniel Jones has outside of Tyler Warren and Jonathan Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin’s lone reception went for a 55-yard touchdown on a simple screen late in the third quarter to bring the Colts within three, but it likely came with the veteran journeyman sitting on waiver wires. Dulin is a name to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline as his role could be growing, pending what the team does with Josh Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 5 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: After dealing with an ankle injury that sidelined him most of the first three weeks, Dulin picked up a hamstring injury and did not practice all week before being ruled out ahead of this game. Laquon Treadwell prayer starts remain on the fantasy football menu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin made his 2026 debut in Week 4 after missing the first three games of the year with an ankle injury. He’s now at risk of returning to the bench because of this hamstring injury. With Keenan Allen back at practice, Dulin’s role was going to decline either way. Laquon Treadwell would be the team’s No. 3 receiver if he is ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 3-of-6 targets for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 4
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin was active for the first time this year. His return could not have come at a better time with Keenan Allen ruled out over the weekend. Dulin took on a starting role and wound up leading the team in targets, tied with Laquon Treadwell. The Colts couldn’t get much going through the air and settled for spreading the ball around instead of peppering their top pass-catchers with targets. It’s hard to imagine them taking that approach again in Week 5. Even if they do, Dulin is more of a thorn in the sides of Tyler Warren and Josh Downs than a FLEX option in his own right.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (ankle) will play in Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Keenan Allen ruled out and Alec Pierce on IR, Dulin is now in line to be the Colts’ No. 2 receiver in his season debut. The passing attack will run through Josh Downs, putting him comfortably inside the WR2 ranks. Inactive for the Colts are WR Keenan Allen, WR Darius Slayton, RB DJ Giddens, QB Riley Leonard, EDGE George Gumbs, and OG Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould played sparingly despite the recent wide receiver departures, with his team-leading 48 yards more a statement on the current state of the offense than anything else. Nobody on this sinking team deserves fantasy consideration, a sentiment that extends to its depth pieces.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (toe) is active for Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould will play through his toe injury this evening, but he is on a boom-bust WR5. The Colts are playing without both of their starting offensive tackles, and Gould is not a replacement-level starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable for Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould was upgraded to a full practice on Wednesday before receiving the questionable tag. We expect him to suit up tomorrow. He led the team with four targets last week, though Gould only turned that into two grabs for 28 yards. The Colts simply don’t have a wide receiver worth a look in even deep fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (toe) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould is dealing with a toe injury and was listed as limited for the Colts’ first two practice reports of the week. He finished the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins and starts out limited, indicating he is in line to play Thursday against the Texans. Gould is suddenly the Colts’ starting slot receiver but should only be rostered in 14-team leagues with deep benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould operated as the Colts’ starting slot receiver, replacing Josh Downs. He led all Indy pass-catchers with a meager four targets, converting them into two receptions for 28 yards. Gould was shaken up after getting hit hard on a punt return, but he stayed in the game. The Colts’ pass-catchers don’t offer much fantasy upside but Gould is a desperation WR5 for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould will play slot receiver after Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: With Downs shipped out, the slot role will go to Gould, who has four receptions for 45 yards over three seasons with the Colts. Downs had accounted for 18 percent of the team’s targets and 24 percent of the team’s air yards through Week 9. The Colts use three wideout sets on 59 percent of their offensive plays, the 12th highest rate in the NFL. They rank 29th in EPA per pass attempt with three receivers on the field. Gould should be rostered in deeper formats based on route volume alone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (concussion) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The biggest news for fantasy purposes with the Colts inactives is simply that Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs are up, but that isn’t exactly surprising. Gould practiced in full the last two days of the week before being ruled out and stands a chance at being ready for Week 8. Inactive for the Colts are: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), TE Pharaoh Brown, DT Kevin Givens, T Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback) and CB Justin Walley (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts ruled out RT Braden Smith (concussion/neck) for Week 15 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The Colts will be without their starting right tackle for Sunday’s road game against a stout Seahawks defense. Backup Jalen Travis is expected to draw the start in his place and will be tasked with keeping one of either Riley Leonard or Philip Rivers upright. In addition to Smith, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (ankle) and CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: WR Adonai Mitchell caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Colts’ preseason game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Mitchell started in place of injured slot receiver Josh Downs (high-ankle sprain), though Mitchell was curiously subbed out for fellow rookie Anthony Gould on third downs, as noted by PFF’s Nathan Jahnke. Mitchell promisingly logged perimeter snaps opposite Alec Pierce in 12 personnel with the second-team offense. Gould averaged 22.0 yards per return on three total kickoff returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding six yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor went as the rest of the offense went in this one, with the team gaining just 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play with Daniel Jones under center before the veteran signal caller was replaced by Anthony Richardson. The only points mustered for the duration of the contest came on the opening possession of the game, sparked by a 25-yard completion to Ashton Dulin down the sideline. Taylor again rotated with Seth McGowan in a 1A-1B situation until the latter was forced from the game with a hamstring injury sustained on a kick return to end the first half. The team has no reason to run Taylor into the ground in a lost season, significantly capping his fantasy value in the process. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the starting quarterback for the Colts entering a Week 12 meeting with the Giants before inserting Taylor into lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Colts want their next general manager to have a say in Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones’ futures with the team.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: The Colts have faced scrutiny for their decision to keep Taylor and Jones on the roster, rather than trading one or both away for draft picks. Palmer said this is about empowering their next general manager. The team has reportedly compiled a preliminary list of candidates, potentially putting the team in position to make a hire quickly after the season. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan will see “heavy usage” in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: A week after the Colts went ultra run-heavy in a win over the Dolphins — they were 9.3 percent below their expected pass rate — Boyd anticipates a similar approach on Thursday night against Houston. Taylor and McGowan over the past two games have split carries, 29-18, while Taylor takes on almost all the pass-catching work out of the backfield. “It doesn’t matter what I envision. It’s effective,” Taylor said of sharing the backfield workload with McGowan. “It helped us get a win. If we gotta win doing that and that’s what it takes, then I’m all for it. Seth has been growing each and every single day.” McGowan over the past two weeks has the highest EPA per rush in the NFL while Taylor ranks 44th. Unless the Colts face runaway negative game script against the Texans, look for McGowan to see around a dozen touches. Houston ranks 14th in running back fantasy points per opportunity allowed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor totaled 103 yards from scrimmage against the Dolphins, officially eclipsing 10,000 scrimmage yards for his career. Despite staying with the team after the trade deadline, Taylor still ceded many backfield opportunities to Seth McGowan. He saw 23 more snaps but just four more carries while McGowan scored a red zone touchdown. Taylor fumbled in the second quarter; it would have been the 27-year-old’s fifth lost fumble of the season if the Colts did not recover. He was also stuffed at the one-yard line on a second quarter goal-line carry. Taylor still sees an elite workload, but the Colts offense does not generate many scoring opportunities and McGowan is cutting into red zone work. Facing the Texans in Week 11, Taylor is still a fantasy RB1, though he does not carry the same top-five ceiling that managers drafted him for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes the Colts could receive “an 11th-hour offer” for Jonathan Taylor that convinces Indianapolis to trade him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Holder’s sources are currently telling him that there is “not a strong indication” that the Colts will be busy making deals at Tuesday’s trade deadline, but he adds that “you can’t rule this out with Taylor.” The Colts already received an offer including a second- and a fifth-round pick. Holder wonders aloud whether a second- and a third-round pick could be enough for Indianapolis to trade him away. Reading between the lines, that could be the Colts leaking an asking price to him. We’ll find out for sure in less than 48 hours. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 18 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor also lost a key fumble in the fourth quarter following the team’s second takeaway of the game, leaving fantasy managers wanting more in what could have been his final game in Indianapolis. Taylor has been the subject of significant trade speculation and rumor as we head toward Tuesday’s trade deadline, although teams will need to take on his recently-signed contract extension that ties him to the Colts through the 2028 season. Things started off rough as Taylor was subbed out on third-and-goal from the two, watching from the sideline as Seth McGowan punched it in for the team’s only rushing score of the game. It did not get better from their for Taylor’s fantasy managers as the Colts played through consistently negative game script, limiting his volume in the process. Taylor’s next opponent remains uncertain, although he currently lines up to take on the reeling Dolphins in Week 10, at least as long as he remains with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts RB Jonathan Taylor “most likely” won’t be traded.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: An earlier report from the Athletic’s Jonathan Jones listed the Vikings and Giants as the favorites to trade for Taylor while the Seahawks, Packers and Broncos are still in the mix. Pelissero threw cold water on all of that by reporting no team has come close to offering what the Colts want for Taylor. Maybe that changes after Week 9, but if Taylor is stuck in Indianapolis, that’s probably the worst-case scenario for his rest-of-season fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Giants are serious suitors for Jonathan Taylor, while the Broncos and Vikings might be less inclined to acquire him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: All three teams have inquired about Taylor’s trade cost. Per Breer, the Colts either want a first-round pick or a draft pick package similar to what the Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2023. The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan pulled up lame following a kick return at the end of the first half and was deemed questionable to return when the two teams came out after the break. Jonathan Taylor appears to be in line to operate as a true workhorse for the remainder of the game after McGowan had carved out a meaningful role the previous two weeks. McGowan managed seven yards on three carries and caught his lone target for one yard prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan will see “heavy usage” in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: A week after the Colts went ultra run-heavy in a win over the Dolphins — they were 9.3 percent below their expected pass rate — Boyd anticipates a similar approach on Thursday night against Houston. Taylor and McGowan over the past two games have split carries, 29-18, while Taylor takes on almost all the pass-catching work out of the backfield. “It doesn’t matter what I envision. It’s effective,” Taylor said of sharing the backfield workload with McGowan. “It helped us get a win. If we gotta win doing that and that’s what it takes, then I’m all for it. Seth has been growing each and every single day.” McGowan over the past two weeks has the highest EPA per rush in the NFL while Taylor ranks 44th. Unless the Colts face runaway negative game script against the Texans, look for McGowan to see around a dozen touches. Houston ranks 14th in running back fantasy points per opportunity allowed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan eclipsed his previous career-high with 12 carries in the Colts’ win. He continues to be involved, eating into Jonathan Taylor’s workload with a few red zone carries and a four-yard rushing touchdown to open the second quarter. McGowan was not involved in the passing game and Taylor still saw 23 more snaps. However, it seems like McGowan is here to stay as a playmaker for the Colts offense with a rushing score for the second straight game. He should be on fantasy rosters as a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, losing three yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan came on in relief of Jonathan Taylor on third-and-goal from the two late in the first quarter, cashing in on the opportunity for his first touchdown this season. a 36-yard scamper in the fourth quarter pushed his yards per carry mark to a healthy 7.5, dwarfing the 3.5 of Taylor. McGowan should not be on waiver wires ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with the looming possibility that Taylor has played his final snap for the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor remains on the Colts roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Steichen mostly dodged questions about why the Colts would play Taylor in Week 9 if the team was in talks with contenders who might want to acquire the star running back before the NFL’s trade deadline. “Teams call all the time,” Steichen told reports. He said the team was focused on the Cowboys, their opponents in Week 9. Taylor seems more than likely to be dealt to another team in the coming weeks. That could be the Vikings, Bengals, Seahawks, or another contending team in need of backfield help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan actually out-gained Jonathan Taylor on the ground in a game the Colts trailed 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 heading into the fourth quarter. No. 3 back DJ Giddens was called upon for six carries, which he turned into 43 yards. Fantasy managers are stuck in a holding pattern as they await Taylor’s Colts fate ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but McGowan remains worth a speculative stash in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: The Colts this week dealt DeForest Buckner to the 49ers and Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks in what looks like a fire sale ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline. Taylor could be next if the Colts are ready to go all in on a rebuild in 2027 and beyond. A contender would likely have to part with a second round draft pick if they want Taylor in the coming weeks. Teams that could be suitors for Taylor include the Bengals, Vikings, and Seahawks, all of whom have backfield issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 11 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding one reception for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: With Jonathan Taylor trade possibilities swirling, McGowan quietly saw an increase in usage against the Vikings. He turned 12 touches into 48 yards, seeing 20 offensive snaps to Taylor’s 41. Though Taylor is still the definitive RB1, it is notable that the rookie 25-year-old is getting more opportunities, including a couple red zone snaps. McGowan has not quite achieved standalone fantasy value but should be added as a bench stash. He would be the Colts’ RB1 should Taylor be traded later this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts declared CB Sauce Gardner, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, LT Bernhard Raimann, DT Jerry Tillery, RT Jalen Travis and CB Charvarius Ward inactive for Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner and Ward are the Colts’ starting perimeter cornerbacks, and Raimann and Travis are the Colts’ starting offensive tackles. Losing all four for this game will be consequential. The Texans’ wide receivers and pass rushers should play efficiently in this week’s Thursday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable for Week 11 against the Texans.
