https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner did not practice at all this week, which usually guarantees that a player will not suit up. However, the Colts playing on Thursday night instead of Sunday makes things a bit murkier. The team has already ruled out Charvarius Ward because of a knee injury. Expect C.J. Stroud to keep cooking this week, even if Gardner manages to suit up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) did not practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Both Gardner and Charvarius Ward (knee) were listed as DNP on Tuesday after DNPs on Monday. They suffered the injuries in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins and are trending out for a Thursday game this week. Texans receivers get a boost for Week 11 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: So, too, was Charvarius Ward with a knee injury, the latter of whom departed the team’s Week 10 contest and did not return. The team has already announced quarterback Daniel Jones as the starter for Thursday Night Football, with no other massive news early in a short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner exited the game with a leg injury in the third quarter. He headed to the locker room and the Colts listed him as questionable to return. Gardner had dealt with a calf injury earlier this season, so it is possible he is dealing with a re-aggravation of the same injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Sauce Gardner (calf) will be active for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner missed last week’s game after suffering a calf strain in Week 6 against the Titans, but will return after getting in a limited session on Wednesday and a full practice on Thursday. We’re assuming that means he’s in line for another full practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner is considered week-to-week because of the calf strain he suffered in Week 6. He’s not expected to miss an “extended period”, but it’s safe to assume Gardner is out for Week 7. Maybe that will help kickstart the Vikings’ sluggish passing attack, though we doubt it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sauce Gardner is considered week-to-week after suffering a calf strain in Week 6’s loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: According to Rapoport, an MRI revealed a mild calf strain for Gardner, who is expected to be week-to-week with the injury. While he is expected to miss some time, Rapoport also notes that Gardner is not expected to miss “an extended period,” which suggests he won’t be placed on injured reserve. Gardner sounds like a virtual lock to miss Week 7’s game against the Vikings, so we’ll see if a week away gives him enough time to be ready for Week 8’s game against the Jaguars. Gardner has totaled 17 tackles and four pass breakups for the Colts this season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 62.6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner did not return to the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans after suffering a calf injury in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner injured his left calf today, which is concerning because he injured the same calf twice last year. The first injury occurred in Week 13. He resumed playing in Week 17, lasting 35 snaps before re-injuring it. Gardner was labeled questionable to return following today’s injury, but he never made it back onto the field. He will likely undergo imaging on Monday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans declared Marvin Harrison, EDGE Danielle Hunter, RB Woody Marks, TE Brevin Jordan, C Jake Andrews, OG Wyatt Teller and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison (hamstring) and Marks (concussion) are both out this week, condensing the Texans’ skill position corps for fantasy football purposes. Both players can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though neither player is a must-stash option. David Montgomery should handle a sizable workload with Marks out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans ruled out Marvin Harrison (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Unfortunately, the Texans’ mid-season acquisition will miss another game. Harrison’s absence helpfully condenses the pass-catching corps for fantasy football purposes, though. Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson will likely lead their position group, followed by Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be sidelined for Week 11’s TNF game after back-to-back missed practices. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell should be the main fantasy beneficiaries of Harrison’s absence. This will make two weeks in a row on the shelf for Harrison and no practices since ahead of Week 9’s game, making it feel dicey that he’ll be able to get active for Week 12 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It appears highly likely that Harrison Jr. will miss his second consecutive game with a hamstring injury considering the team is on a short week. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte are likely to continue forward as the top two wide receivers behind Nico Collins, with Tank Dell likely to be held around half of the offensive snaps in this third game back from over a year of missed time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison is tentatively on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns, but hamstring strains can be tough for wide receivers to immediately bounce back from, and we do not know whether the injury occurred today or last Sunday. Harrison’s practice participation tomorrow will tell us more. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison was fairly quiet today, though CJ Stroud picked on Chargers CB Duke Shelley on the Texans’ seventh drive, and Harrison did manage to get in on the fun, beating Shelley for a 15-yard, tip-toe catch along the right sideline. Harrison remains a boom-bust FLEX against the Browns next week, as he continues adjusting to the Texans’ offensive scheme.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M Alexander reports Jaylin Noel (toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a rough blow for Noel, who had been extremely efficient on his targets. It does clear up space for some of Houston’s other receivers. The recently-activated Tank Dell and recently-acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. will benefit a bit from one fewer mouth to feed after the Texans come off bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 1-of-4 targets for six yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison had to come back to the ball in the end zone, one that was placed to his back shoulder by C.J. Stroud to fit it around a zone defender. That was the good. Harrison also added an egregious drop while playing just 13 snaps. Your guess is as good as ours about fantasy value here as we sort through the names. Harrison doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered through his Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers released RB Pierre Strong.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: We take this move as a good sign for Josh Jacobs’ (finger) health. Strong could end up being signed to the Packers’ practice squad. He played a rotational role for Green Bay this season, leading the team with 17 opportunities in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Pierre Strong rushed five times for seven yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding three receptions for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Making his Packers debut, 27-year-old journeyman Strong slid into Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) vacated role. Although it’s a potential concern for MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson — any new face in this makeshift backfield would be — it appears to be a bigger issue for Johnson, as Strong was playing ahead of him until garbage time. Ominous for Johnson managers, though Strong has little shot at carving out 12-team league value of his own.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers released Pierre Strong.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Strong was released right after it was reported that the team was acquiring Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers. He spent the 2025 season on the Packers’ practice squad and was elevated for two games. Strong will likely find work on another practice squad once rosters are settled.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers RB Chris Brooks took first-team reps to begin 11-on-11 drills at organized team activities on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Brooks opened team drills as the Packers’ starting running back on Wednesday. Fellow backup RB Pierre Strong then subbed in, taking first-team reps as well. Starting RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on Tuesday for domestic abuse and was not present. Presumed RB MarShawn Lloyd practiced on Tuesday, but was limited to individual drills for an undisclosed reason on Wednesday. Injuries derailed Lloyd’s first two NFL seasons, so his absence is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd (undisclosed) sat out during team drills at organized team activities on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: It’s possible this is just a maintenance-related coaching decision, but it is still slightly concerning. Injuries have limited Lloyd to just 10 offensive snaps through two NFL seasons. Packers starting RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on Tuesday and was not present on Wednesday, allowing the backups to take first-team snaps. Per ESPN’s Rob Demovsky, Lloyd “took part in team drills during Tuesday’s closed session but did only individual work Wednesday.” Packers RB Chris Brooks began team drills with the first-team offense before subbing out for RB Pierre Strong. The Packers had the day off on Thursday and will resume practicing tomorrow. The Packers “remain optimistic that the powerful and speedy Lloyd can repay the team for their patience,” but he needs to retake the field soon if he hopes to prove his reliability. Hopefully, Lloyd is back in action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Releasing Josh Jacobs would result in a $6.25 million dead cap hit for the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Jacobs this week was arrested in Wisconsin on domestic abuse chargers. The 28-year-old back was booked in jail for battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, and intimidation of a victim. Jacobs denies the allegations. If the Packers were to release Jacobs — who has two years and $25 million remaining on his current deal — they would absorb a doable $6.2 million hit to the salary cap for 2026. Jacobs could be facing team and/or league discipline in the coming months, and could miss part of the regular season if the NFL’s investigation into the domestic abuse allegations warrants a suspension. Other running backs on the Packers depth chart include Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Pierre Strong.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers signed K Lucas Havrisik, OT Brant Banks, DL Dante Barnett, OG Karsen Barnhart, DL Anthony Campbell, TE McCallan Castles, OT Dalton Cooper, TE Drake Dabney, DL James Ester, CB Tyron Herring, LB Jamon Johnson, RB Damien Martinez, S Mark Perry, WR Will Sheppard, RB Pierre Strong Jr. and TE Messiah Swinson to reserve/futures contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Havrisik hit 4-of-4 field goals and 7-of-9 extra points this year, and the Packers seemed to be developing him as kicker of the future — whatever that means in the NFL — while letting him stay on the practice squad. With Brandon McManus’ job officially under scrutiny, it’s possible he eventually gets the Packers kicker gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers added RB Emanuel Wilson (illness) to the injury report Saturday with a questionable designation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: The team elevated RB Pierre Strong from the practice squad in an associated move, which comes as both Josh Jacobs and Wilson are listed as questionable. Stay tuned ahead of the team’s inactives Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers K Brandon McManus (quad) is inactive for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Also inactive for the Packers are RB Pierre Strong Jr., G Donovan Jennings, T Anthony Belton, TE Ben Sims, DL Lukas Van Ness, and DL Devonte Wyatt. McManus will miss another game due to his quad issue, meaning Lucas Havrisik will kick for Green Bay against the Cardinals. Strong was elevated from the practice squad, but with Josh Jacobs (calf/illness) active, he is inactive this week. Meanwhile, Van Ness will miss this game due to a foot issue that kept him out of practice all week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Ray Davis (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Davis is still worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues. He is James Cook’s primary backup. Passing down specialist Ty Johnson (knee) is practicing in full this week and should be good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: James Cook rushed 13 times for 57 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans, adding three catches for 12 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Cook had twenty yards on the game’s first drive, but the game eventually skewed pass-heavy for the Bills and Josh Allen had the game’s only two rushing touchdowns. Per PFF’s early charting data, Cook had 41 of the 57 snaps and almost all the work ahead of Ray Davis and Frank Gore Jr. Assuming Ty Johnson remains out on a short week against the Lions in Week 2, Cook will remain a touch-dominator on the RB1 line and will have a chance for a better touchdown runout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said the team will know more about RB Ty Johnson’s (leg) injury next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Johnson went down while running a route in practice on Saturday and immediately grabbed at the back of his right leg. He appeared to be grabbing at the lowest section of his hamstring, but both the back of his knee and the highest point of his calf are possible. Johnson logged a 65 percent third-down snap share and a 56 percent two-minute-drill snap share last season. Starting RB James Cook (19 percent and 31 percent) and fellow backup RB Ray Davis (16 percent and 13 percent) were also involved in both scenarios. If this is a serious injury that causes Johnson to miss time, it could meaningfully raise Cook’s fantasy-scoring ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Ray Davis caught both of his targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Divisional Round loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Davis was technically the Bills’ backup running back, handling the second-most carries and gaining 275 rushing yards on 4.7 yards per carry over the season. However, Ty Johnson was used far more often in the red zone and had 24 catches to Davis’ 10. Davis did emerge as an elite kick returner, leading the NFL in yards per return at 30.4. That just won’t provide much fantasy value heading into next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (ankle) is questionable for Buffalo’s Divisional Round game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Johnson got in a limited session on Thursday, which is very similar to his Friday limited last week after two DNPs that also got him to the questionable line. Our guess is that he’s on the pessimistic side of questionable. If Johnson doesn’t play, Ray Davis will be a threat for a higher snap count than usual again and be a potential DFS play for the Divisional Round slate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Ray Davis rushed 21 times for 151 yards in a Week 18 win over the Jets, adding 23 yards and a touchdown on two catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Davis had 174 all-purpose yards on Sunday, while the Jets’ entire team had just 122 yards against the Bills’ backup defense. Davis had a near split in carries with Ty Johnson today, but Davis was the far more effective back, ripping off some huge runs through the middle. Davis hasn’t had as big of a role this season with James Cook leading the NFL in rushing yards and Ty Johnson having a larger third-down role; however, Davis has looked good when given a chance. He’s also been one of the best kick returners in the NFL and remains a solid backup to Cook.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Ray Davis rushed nine times for 62 yards in the Bills’ Week 13 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Davis had, this is not a joke, -2 total yards rushing on two carries combined in the four weeks before this, so this effort came out of nowhere. Davis got his chance in the first quarter when James Cook was forced off the field due to an issue with his helmet. Davis proceeded to break off two rushes for 30 yards, which clearly prompted the Bills to give him more work on a day when they were gashing the Steelers on the ground. We would not anticipate this leading to an expanded role for the second-year back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Bills RB James Cook (ankle/foot) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: He’s officially only a limited participant, but his return puts him on track to play in Week 10 against the Dolphins, whose run defense is among the league’s worst. Backup RBs Ray Davis and Ty Johnson are still worth stashing on benches, just in case Cook’s injury flares up, but at this time, neither one appears to be a locked-in FLEX-worthy starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Bills RB Ray Davis (illness) is not on Buffalo’s final Week 9 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Davis has 18 carries in two games against the Bills and Panthers in which Buffalo has generated huge leads and four carries in his other five games combined. He shouldn’t be in consideration for a standalone FLEX start, but can be held as a hedge against a James Cook injury in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.headline: Bills RB Ray Davis (illness) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/remahn-davis/0.analysis: Sounds like a 24-hour bug. Davis won’t hold a standalone-worthy role in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but has some fantasy upside in the event that James Cook misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: The Bengals’ stud right guard is dealing with injuries to both knees. Hopefully, the extra day of rest leading up to this week’s Monday Night Football game allows him to get healthy enough to play. The offense is better with him active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Offensive tackle Myles Hinton is also questionable with an illness. It looks like something is going around the Cincy locker room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (knee) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Risner is one of the Bengals’ best offensive linemen, profiling as an all-around talented run blocker and pass protector. He sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in full on Friday. He seemingly has a chance to play. Having him on the field would be very helpful against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Dalton Risner (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Risner signed a one-year, $5 million contract extension with the Bengals in the offseason. He has started all three games at right guard this year. Risner has allowed just three pressures this year and has been a solid contributor in the run game as well. Jalen Rivers took his reps in practice today, meaning he is the next man up if Risner can’t go on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Bengals have agreed to a one-year, $5 million extension with OG Dalton Risner.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Risner joined the Bengals last offseason after he was let go by the Vikings after training camp. The veteran guard appeared in 14 games for the Bengals last season while making 11 starts, and did more than enough to warrant an extension this offseason. Risner played on 768 snaps last season and allowed only two sacks, per TruMedia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Bengals signed G Dalton Risner.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: He’ll probably step in as an instant starter at right guard, with the Lucas Patrick and Cody Ford tandem struggling in the preseason. Risner had a 67.0 PFF blocking grade in 2024 and has been roughly an adequate guard over his six NFL seasons. That makes him a huge upgrade on what the Bengals had in-house. Risner took visits with the Bengals and Seahawks before picking Cincinnati.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Seahawks will host OG Dalton Risner for a visit.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Risner visited the Bengals on Tuesday and will continue his visits with the Seahawks. Seattle just added first-rounder Grey Zabel to the interior offensive line, but is looking to add depth to a group that struggled last season. Fowler also reports Risner is considering visiting the Steelers. The 30-year-old wants to take multiple visits as the preseason winds down before making a decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Bengals will host OG Dalton Risner for a visit on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Risner, 30, has 81 career starts to his name and spent last season with the Vikings. The veteran guard earned a PFF blocking grade of 67.0 last season while starting all eight games he appeared in after returning from a back injury that kept him out for the first 10 weeks of the season. Risner would provide plenty of experience to an interior offensive line whose current projected starters include a rookie third-round pick and a 32-year-old vet in Lucas Patrick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Vikings activated OG Dalton Risner from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: The veteran guard will make his team debut in Week 9 and could force his way back into the starting lineup after starting 11 games in 15 appearances for the Vikings a season ago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.headline: Vikings OG Dalton Risner (back, injured reserve) is inactive for Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-ris.analysis: Like T.J. Hockenson (knee, injured reserve), Risner was ruled out earlier Thursday. The hope is that he is ready for Week 9. Joining Risner and Hockenson on the shelf are QB Brett Rypien, CB Akayleb Evans, CB Dwight McGlothern, RB Myles Gaskin, DL Levi Drake Rodriguez, LB Blake Cashman and OT Walter Rouse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas is seemingly on track to play in Week 11’s Monday Night Football game against the Commanders, but he does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins (knee), Chase Brown and Mike Gesicki are playing very well in the receiving game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve, though he practiced in full today. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals placed Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor said Iosivas is expected to return at some point this year. Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will both be in the running for the WR3 role, though it’s not a role that produces fantasy points unless one of Tee Higgins or Ja’Marr Chase goes down.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught his only target for seven yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: He played 32-of-60 snaps as the Bengals have spread the ball around, letting Colvie Young (1/7 on one target) and Dohnte Meyers (0/0 on one target) also get involved against the Texans. Iosivas looks like a poor FLEX risk in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals WR Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas was on the field for two drives, taking 10 of the first 13 snaps and playing alongside QB Joe Burrow. Fourth-round rookie WR Colbie Young subbed in, taking one snap on the second drive and remained on the field after the starters left. He looked good hauling in a 20-yard gain on 3rd-and-16 from QB Joe Flacco. The battle for the Bengals’ WR3 role continues with Iosivas seemingly ahead of the rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports that WR Colbie Young and WR Andrei Iosivas are still competing for the Bengals’ WR3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Young, the rookie, “has seemingly stacked at least one impressive catch per day.” Iosivas has had “a few notable drops,” but he reportedly “appears as polished and athletic as ever at getting open.” Both players could be worth late-round picks in best ball formats, but neither one is likely to return FLEX value in re-draft without WR1 Ja’Marr Chase or WR2 Tee Higgins missing time. Iosivas is entering a contract year, and the team just spent a fourth-round pick on Young. An in-season breakout from the rookie would make things easier from a salary cap perspective. Dehner also notes that former CFL WR Dohnte Meyers “has been a talk of camp” thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes the Bengals will add competition for Andrei Iosivas’ No. 3 receiver role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: This isn’t a front-page headline or anything, but OC Dan Pitcher did say that Iosivas “would probably tell you that there were points last year that he was happy with his play and points where he felt he needed to be better.” Entering the final year of his rookie contract, Iosivas could be pushed by Mitchell Tinsley or a draft pick for playing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas proved to be a capable depth option in 2024, but there wasn’t much room for his role to grow this year. He appeared in all 17 games and totaled 34 grabs for 435 yards. His 2025 stat line was nearly identical to 2024’s, except for a notable drop in touchdowns. He scored six times last year compared to two touchdowns this time around. For fantasy purposes, Iosivas only cracks the weekly FLEX ranks when one of Ja’Marr Chase or Tee Higgins is sidelined. He won’t be on the redraft radar for his fourth NFL season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (knee) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins injured his knee in Week 10 against the Steelers, but apparently it is only a minor injury. The Bengals’ No. 2 wide receiver is having an excellent season, and that top-tier performance should continue against a beatable Commanders’ pass defense. Higgins is a borderline WR1/2 with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins’ six targets finished third on the team behind Ja’Marr Chase (14) and Chase Brown (nine) while his receiving output was dwarfed by the 231 yards of Chase. The matchup against the zone-heavy Steelers likely played a significant role in the target breakout, with Higgins much more dangerous against man coverage this season. Higgins remains an elite WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 10-of-11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins led the team in receiving yards while trailing Ja’Marr Chase in receptions and targets. He was Joe Burrow’s primary target over the middle of the field in the intermediate and deep areas. Higgins caught a pair of second half touchdowns, catching an 18-yard score to tie the game towards the end of regulation. Pass-heavy game scripts will lead to a high amount of fantasy production for Higgins and Chase, who saw a combined 56-percent target share from Joe Burrow. Higgins is a high-end WR2 for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins came up big multiple times for the Bengals in the second half after they were shut out 13-0 in the first half. He hauled in passes of 10 and 19 yards on the Bengals’ opening drive in the second half to help set up an eventual six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and hauled in a 13-yard touchdown of his own on the following drive. He would also make two catches of 40-plus yards, and came up six yards short of a second touchdown on an impressive 44-yard grab — his longest play of the day. Higgins has gone for 140-plus yards in two of his last three games and has topped 90 yards in four of six games this season. He profiles as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is questionable for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins missed the first two practices of the week but practiced in full on Friday. We would consider him to be truly questionable given his one day of practice, meaning fantasy managers will want to check his official game status when the team announces inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. If he can’t go, Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, could be on the fantasy radar as a WR4 in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (illness) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow should be able to face the Commanders in this week’s Monday Night Football game without issue. Fortunately, his No. 2 wide receiver, Tee Higgins (knee), is also practicing in full this week. Burrow is an elite QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 38-18, Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding eight yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow cruised to his fifth consecutive game of four total touchdowns or more, passing for 302 yards and three scores in the first half alone. The Steelers were completely unable to move the ball consistently while managing only 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters, allowing Burrow and the Bengals to build an insurmountable lead through the first 45 minutes of play. The win sends Cincinnati to the top of the AFC North with a 7-2 record after splitting the season series with the Steelers, now in the driver’s seat for the division title with two months remaining in the regular season. Burrow will look to keep the elite play going in a Week 11 meeting with the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football, where he remains a top tier QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground. Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 38-of-48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions in the Bengals’ 43-36 win over the Titans, adding three carries for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow and the Bengals passing offense started off slow, ending the first quarter scoreless. A first quarter interception from Burrow in Titans territory led to a Tennessee score the other way. He finished the half on a better note, tossing a 30-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase and a one-yard score to Jack Endries. The second half saw many more possessions between both teams, with Burrow throwing two more interceptions to give the Titans increased opportunities. He was able to lead several scoring drives regardless, tossing three touchdowns in the second half and scrambling for the go-ahead touchdown in overtime. A high-scoring game script leads to very productive days for Burrow and the Bengals offense. Burrow profiles as a fantasy QB1 once again for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 35-13, Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: After throwing for just 55 scoreless yards in the first half, Burrow and the Bengals came out firing on all cylinders in the second half. Trailing 13-0 at halftime, Burrow immediately orchestrated a nine-play, 66-yard drive that ended with a six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and followed that up with four more touchdown drives on his team’s next four possessions to jump out to a 35-13 lead. Burrow was as sharp as could be in the second half, completing 16-of-18 attempts while also completing two passes of 20-plus air yards. Burrow has now thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games and has four multi-touchdown games this season. He’ll be on the QB1 radar next week when the Bengals play host to the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bengals’ 22-17, Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense struggled to finish drives for much of this game, with Burrow throwing his first touchdown to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter. He also added a rushing touchdown on a fourth-quarter quarterback sneak. Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early didn’t help as Burrow threw two interceptions and nearly had a third. He threw one to Travis Hunter in the first quarter, though it was nullified by a roughing the passer penalty. He later threw one with under two minutes left in the first half, leading to a Jaguars score the other way. The final interception came in the fourth quarter in the red zone, ending a promising drive. Burrow made great plays under pressure, often finding Tee Higgins downfield. However, the interceptions proved to be back-breaking and the Bengals’ comeback attempt ultimately fell short. Burrow is a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 5 against a soft Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 281 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 30-27, Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow came out hot in this one, completing his first 14 passes while throwing a three-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase on the Bengals’ opening drive. Burrow would throw his second touchdown of the day late in the second half when he connected with Tee Higgins for a 28-yard score and found Mike Gesicki 25 yards downfield on a fourth-and-two for his third touchdown of the day. Burrow led his offense on multiple long drives in this one, but with his team trailing 30-27 and driving late in the fourth quarter, he would cough up the ball on a strip-sack, which was recovered by Pittsburgh to seal the win for the Steelers. Burrow has attempted 30-plus passes in every game this season while throwing for six touchdowns to just one interception. He’ll be on the QB1 radar for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in Cincinnati’s 20-6, Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was under pressure quite a bit in this one, as he took five sacks, but the Bengals were able to establish enough of a lead on a few incredible out-of-structure plays by Burrow that they took the air out of the ball in the middle of the third quarter. Both touchdown passes were to Ja’Marr Chase, the second as Burrow drifted out of his pocket to the right. It’s full-steam ahead in the QB1 tiers as Burrow heads to Pittsburgh in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back) is active for Cincinnati’s Week 2 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: It never seemed like there was a real chance Burrow would miss this game, even after Josh Johnson was elevated from the practice squad yesterday. Burrow will be on the QB1 line against a Texans defense looking to rebound. Inactive for the Bengals are: Johnson, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OL Myles Hinton, DT B.J. Hill (Achilles), and DT Landon Robinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo left last Thursday night’s game against the Giants briefly with an injury scare, but had returned by the end of the game. This listing tells us he’s in no danger of missing Monday Night Football and, assuming Ben Sinnott isn’t suddenly usurping him as the starter after his nice game, Okonkwo can be played as a fringe TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo is one of many fringe TE1/2 candidates on any given week. He does not need to be in fantasy football lineups, but he can act as a serviceable fill-in, though his upside is most touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: That ought to put him firmly in the mix to play on Thursday against the Giants. Okonkwo is coming off a 6/57 game on seven targets against the Rams and figures to again be a reasonable low-end TE1 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo’s seven targets tied Van Jefferson for the team high in this one. Okonkwo hauled in a 15-yard reception on the Commanders’ opening drive, and on the final play of the game, he caught a 16-yard pass and then tossed it to Rachaad White in hopes of keeping the play alive after time had already expired. Okonkwo has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and is seeing enough work in the passing game to be on the streaming radar for Week 10’s game against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo flashed his athletic ability with a full-stretch reception in the second half but it was not enough to overshadow a first quarter fumble. The spry veteran has now been held to four receptions or fewer in four of five appearances in the low volume Washington pass offense, unable to return consistent fantasy value through the absence of Terry McLaurin. He is best left on fantasy benches in a Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Pretty much all the smoke here is that he’ll be activated and ready to go for Monday Night Football and the injury report does not disagree with that assertion. We’re expecting to see him as questionable on the final injury report because that is just generally how teams label players returning from IR, but ‘Bill’ is looking like a reasonable FLEX play against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders designated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Ben Standig reports that he’s expecting Croskey-Merritt to be active for Monday night barring a setback. We’re expecting a pass-happy Commanders offense as they try to keep pace with Cincinnati’s high-flying offense, but given how many teams are on bye there’s certainly worse FLEX starts out there than a returning “Bill.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending in the right direction” to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Quinn declined to commit to opening “Bill’s” 21-day return window, but sounded optimistic about doing so later in the week. The Commanders’ RB1 has missed the last four games with a groin injury he picked up in Week 5 and would be eligible to return as early as Week 11 if he were to be designated to return this week. The Commanders have struggled on the ground without JCM this season, as their running backs have combined to average just 3.7 YPC since Week 6 while finding the end zone once. If he’s able to play against the Bengals, JCM would have some appeal as an RB3/FLEX in a week that has six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders placed Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to get the majority of the work from Weeks 6-9. The Commanders also brought Jeremy McNichols off injured reserve and signed him to the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through soft tissue injuries for weeks now. He played through a groin injury last week, and the same issue is still bothering him today. Regardless, Croskey-Merritt still has a chance to play this week and today’s absence could actually benefit the starting running back. The Commanders face the 49ers on Monday night, so Croskey-Merritt has extra time to rest and rehab. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 11 times for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt’s 82 rushing yards set a new season high. Nearly half of his yards came in the first quarter when “Bill” broke free for a 33-yard touchdown to give the Commanders a 7-0 lead on their opening drive. On the final play of the third quarter, Croskey-Merritt would rip off a 22-yard run on a drive that eventually ended on a 26-yard touchdown run by Jayden Daniels. JCM continues to be the unquestioned leader in Washington’s backfield, but he remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option due to his lack of receiving upside. He’ll be a boom-or-bust RB2 in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Saints plan to release S Justin Reid at his request.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: Reid’s having his worst season in the league per PFF’s charting data, having compiled a 49.1 PFF defensive grade and his second-worst coverage grade as a pro at 47.8. That said, Reid has plenty of versatility and wants to seek work with a contender. It sounds like he’ll likely find a new home in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints restructured TE Juwan Johnson, EDGE Chase Young and S Justin Reid’s contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: The Saints are working to become cap-compliant entering next week. Johnson earned 100 targets last year, hitting triple digits for the first time in his career. Young led the team with 49 quarterback pressures and ranked second in sacks with 10.0. Reid totaled 53 solo tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints declared S Justin Reid, RB Alvin Kamara, RT Asim Richards, DT John Ridgeway, DT Khristian Boyd, CB Rejzohn Wright and TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden inactive for Week 15 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: Kamara and Richards were ruled out on Friday. Reid seemingly had a chance to return from his knee injury, practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday. He will try again next week. Reid accounts for 45 tackles, two quarterback pressures, one sack, two pass breakups and one interception. Saints RB Devin Neal (abdomen) will start again in Kamara’s stead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints S Justin Reid (knee) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 15 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: He didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the veteran probably has enough savvy to make it on to the field on Sunday if his knee cooperates. Reid had missed Week 14 and four straight practices before re-appearing on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints S Justin Reid (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: It’s his first practice since injuring his knee in Week 13, and a sign that he has a chance to be active against the Panthers in Week 15. We’ll check in on Reid again tomorrow, but this is at least an encouraging sign that he could make the questionable line on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints S Justin Reid (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 14 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: He suffered a knee injury in Week 13, one that Kellen Moore said will “not send him to injured reserve.” But it doesn’t appear that Reid will be back any time soon. Terrell Burgess will likely be called upon for most of the snaps at safety on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Justin Reid (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 5 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: Reid suffered the injury in the first quarter, so the Saints will need to find someone to fill his shoes. The defense has been using Reid all over the field as both a safety and a pseudo big nickel corner. With him out, the Giants’ tight ends have been feasting, so this is a situation to monitor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Saints agreed to terms with S Justin Reid, formerly of the Chiefs, on a three-year, $31.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: Adam Schefter notes that Reid will get $22.25 million fully guaranteed. It’s a strong contract for the 28-year-old safety, who finished 2024 with a career-best 78.2 PFF grade and is versatile enough to play in the box, over the top, and at slot if necessary. He’ll give defensive coordinator Brandon Staley some pre-snap versatility. Reid will replace Will Harris, who the Commanders signed earlier today, as New Orleans’ starting safety next to Tyrann Mathieu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Chiefs activated S Justin Reid (quad) from the non-football injury list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: Reid opened training camp on the non-football injury but is now back with the team. The veteran safety totaled 95 tackles, three sacks, and one interception in his second year with the Chiefs and has been instrumental in the team’s last two Super Bowl runs. At just 27 years old, Reid is a staple in a secondary that lost star corner L’Jarius Sneed earlier this offseason. With a little less than a month before the season gets underway, his return is a welcomed one for the Chiefs and their top-flight defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.headline: Chiefs placed S Justin Reid (quad) on the NFI list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-rei.analysis: The report comes from Arrowhead Pride’s Pete Sweeney. Reid is considered day-to-day with the injury and has been a steady presence for the Chiefs safety unit since signing with the team in 2022. His 1,560 coverage snaps over the last two years are more than twice as many as the next closest current Chiefs safety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes that the Titans or Chargers would host “an auction” for the 2027 NFL Draft’s No. 1 overall pick if either team gets it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans are currently in position to receive the No. 1 overall pick, and the Chargers are right behind them. Schefter spent much of the segment discussing the Titans, who Schefter says have “enough conviction” in Cam Ward that they would pass on the opportunity to draft Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker. He cites the Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals and Browns as potential suitors. Poor play from Ward could still change minds in the Titans’ front office, but for now, it seems as though his job is secure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said the Titans shifted the offensive philosophy to give Cam Ward “an opportunity” to prove he’s a franchise quarterback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “A few weeks ago we made a shift on how we’re letting Cam Ward run the offense, let him be a field general. ... He’s looking more comfortable, his footwork is improving, and he’s doing a nice job playing quarterback. Still things he can clean up,” Saleh added. Ward over the last two weeks has four touchdown passes and his two highest passing-attempt totals of the season. We’re not exactly excited to fire up Ward as a QB1 streamer at this point, even against the Cowboys in Week 11, but given how many NFL offenses are currently trending down it’s worth pointing out that the Titans are actually taking a step forward of late.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 28-of-39 passes for 231 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Titans’ 40-23, Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also led the Titans with 39 rushing yards. He got off to an ugly start by throwing an interception to Travis Hunter. Ward attempted a throw across his body to a receiver with very little separation. He didn’t lead Elic Ayomanor enough and Hunter made a great play on the ball. Ward improved throughout the contest, but not enough to make this an awfully competitive game. Still, he threw two touchdown passes for the second time this year. The first was in Week 8 before Tennessee’s bye. Ward will be worth a look as a streamer when he takes on the Cowboys next week, though only as a low-end QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 26-of-40 attempts for 304 yards, two touchdowns, and a fumble in the Titans’ 43-36, Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding seven carries for 41 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also added a two-point conversion on the ground. The Titans offense got off to a fast start, leading 13-0 after one quarter. Ward finished the day passing for 304 yards, averaging 7.6 yards per attempt and surpassing 300 yards for the first time in his career. He made plays with his legs, scrambling for multiple first downs on short-yardage situations. A sack-fumble from Ward led to a Bengals score the other way in the third quarter and the 24-year-old also took a long sack towards the end of regulation to send the game into overtime. The Titans could not convert a fourth down in overtime to close the game. Ultimately, Ward had one of the best games of his season against the Bengals but came up short. For fantasy purposes, Ward’s work on the ground is encouraging for his elevated floor and an improved passing skillset makes him a fantasy QB2 heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 attempts for 181 yards and an interception in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward did his best game manager impression in this one and made a handful of solid high-leverage throws using various arm angles. He had a positive EPA per drop back and was slightly over his expected completion rate, small victories at this point but still victories. The Titans deployed no-huddle for much of the game and operated at a quick pace — a strategy that seemed to get Ward into some sort of rhythm early on. Ward’s accuracy issues showed up on the fourth quarter when he sailed a pass over the head of a wide open tight end who had beaten the entire Cleveland secondary. It would’ve likely been a game-winning touchdown. Ward has now cracked 200 passing yards just once through Week 7 and should only be rostered in superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 11-of-22 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Titans’ 26-20, Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward added just three carries for seven yards. Ward got the “quarterback win” as the Titans finally broke their five-game losing streak to begin the season, but this was more about the Colts imploding and setting up one short Titans field after another with turnovers. Ward did keep his connection with No. 4 overall rookie Carnell Tate going, finding him for 6/70/1 on seven targets. Ward didn’t find veteran Calvin Ridley for what would have been a wide open end zone grab, but we digress. His interception was a second quarter sail job as he was getting leveled by the blitz. Ward’s increasing chemistry with Tate is the Titans’ first real good news of the season, but today was not a particularly inspiring victory. They now get the Browns for a Week 7 home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said he had a “cool conversation” with Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s head, per Saleh, is in a “good place” ahead of the Titans’ Week 6 game against the Colts. Ward has been dreadful through five weeks, ranking 24th in EPA per drop back and 27th in drop back success rate. Only five quarterbacks have a lower adjusted yards per attempt than Ward this season. Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent are the only QBs who average fewer fantasy points per drop back. Saleh has defended his second-year QB at every turn and does not seem close to benching him in favor of journeyman backup Mitchell Trubisky.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 170 scoreless yards and an interception in Tennessee’s Week 5, 26-3 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans led off the day with a 58-yard field-goal drive that fell apart from a red zone first-and-5. They would not even flirt with crossing 30 yards in a drive for the rest of the game and crossed into Texans territory on only 11 more snaps all game, including just one inside the Houston 40. Ward took four sacks and avoided several others by turning Tyjae Spears into a PPR hero. The closest he came to actually putting points on the board was a double-covered bomb to Carnell Tate’s general area. It was, well, what you would have expected from both sides in the preseason. Ward remains a last gasp supeflex QB2 heading into Week 6’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 passes for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Titans’ 24-18, Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding four carries for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s second pass of the game resulted in an interception, but he would settle in to put together his most productive outing of the season. Ward linked up with rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate on multiple long gains and ended the day with four completions of 20-plus yards. The two would connect on a 33-yard pass late in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-10, and on the next play, Ward would find Wan’Dale Robinson for a three-yard score to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-18. Ward did a good job at evading pressure in this one. Despite being pressured on 11 dropbacks, per PFF, only one of those resulted in a sack. Ward has been sacked just once over the last two weeks, but will have a tough challenge ahead of him next week when the Titans play host to the Texans. Ward projects as a low-end QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Titans pass catchers and the team’s defense are to blame for Cam Ward’s sloppy footwork.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Asked about Ward’s continuing footwork disaster, Saleh said the second-year quarterback “usually starts off good then fades into old habits.” Titans beat writer Terry McCormick then asked Saleh “why if his footwork gets worse as the game goes on, why the offense has had such slow starts. [Saleh] said it has been dropped passes vs. Giants and defense not getting off field vs. Eagles.” Saleh has made a point to shield Ward from all criticism throughout the preseason and through three horrific regular season outings. Ward ranks 20th in accuracy and 29th in EPA per drop back this season. He’s fresh off throwing a game-deciding end zone interception against the lowly Giants in Week 3. Mitchell Trubisky will probably get a couple starts this season if Ward can’t turn things around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said he considered leaving the Cowboys after being stripped of play-calling duties.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Parker was demoted after the Cowboys got rocked by the 49ers in Week 10. Defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call plays on defense for now. When asked about his future in Dallas, Parker could only say he will cross that bridge when he gets there. It sounds like he and the Cowboys will part ways after the season. Parker was a defensive backs coach in Denver and Philadelphia for five seasons before landing the Dallas defensive coordinator gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker will cede play-calling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: After getting thrashed by Brock Purdy and the 49ers in Week 10, the Cowboys now allow the second highest yards per play and the highest EPA per play. The Dallas defense has given up a touchdown on 31 percent of their opponents’ offensive possessions this season, the third highest rate in the NFL. Pettine will try to stop the bleeding beginning this week against a Titans offense that has shown signs of life in recent weeks. Pettine was last a defensive coordinator with the Packers in 2020, when Green Bay allowed the fewest points in the league and the fifth fewest yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, asked directly about Christian Parker’s status as defensive coordinator and if changes are being made, said “I’m not saying that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: “I’m saying we’re still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today,” Schottenheimer concluded, notably not conclusively answering the question after the Cowboys allowed 46 points to the 49ers in what has been another lost season purely due to defensive lapses. The 34-year-old Parker was regarded as a hot coaching prospect, but the early returns have been rough. The Cowboys have allowed 282 points, the third-most in the league, and are allowing a league-worst 5.2 yards per rushing attempt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe believes Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is on a “direct path” to being a head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Wolfe said he heard this sentiment from multiple sources around the league. Dallas hired him as their defensive coordinator this offseason after two years as the Eagles’ defensive backs coach and pass game coordinator. He also held the title of DBs coach in Denver for three seasons. Parker has a tall order ahead of him with the Cowboys. They ranked dead last in scoring allowed in 2025, giving up a franchise-record 511 points. Expect several teams to give him a look in the next hiring cycle if he can turn this unit into even a league-average one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Cowboys requested an interview with Vikings DL coach Marcus Dixon for their potential defensive line coach vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Cowboys DL coach Aaron Whitecotton is “drawing interest” from the Titans as they search for a defensive coordinator under new head coach Robert Saleh. Rather than waiting to find out if Whitecotton leaves, the Cowboys are proactively starting their own search for his potential replacement. ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that Dixon coached the Broncos’ defensive line from 2022-2023, while new Cowboys DC Christian Parker coached Broncos defensive backs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Cowboys hired Eagles DB coach and pass game coordinator Christian Parker as their defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The deal was finalized shortly after multiple national and local reporters said that the Cowboys were ready to bring him aboard. Parker, 34, has studied under Eagles DC Vic Fangio, in his current roles, for the past two seasons. He spent the 2022-2023 seasons as the Broncos’ defensive backs coach, notably working under Broncos DC Vance Joseph in his second season with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Packers will interview Eagles defensive backs coach Christian Parker for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
