https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Parker will interview with the Cowboys on Wednesday before heading straight to Green Bay to interview for the same defensive coordinator position. Viewed as a “rising star” in many inner circles, Parker appears to have a good chance at his first defensive coordinator gig at the NFL level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Cowboys “plan to bring in” Eagles defensive passing game coordinator and DBs coach Christian Parker for an in-person interview.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It looks like the Cowboys are gearing up for the second phase of their defensive coordinator interviews, this time in-person. They requested Parker a few days ago initially. Parker with join Jonathan Gannon and Daronte Jones as in-person interviews with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Cowboys requested to interview Eagles DB coach and pass game coordinator Christian Parker for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that Parker is the seventh known candidate for the position. Parker interviewed for the Saints’ defensive coordinator vacancy last year, after his first season in his current roles with the Eagles. He previously coached the Broncos’ defensive backs from 2021-2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports the Saints are interviewing Eagles DB coach Christian Parker for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Newly-minted head coach Kellen Moore continues to bring in familiar faces. Like former Chargers head coach Brandon Staley, who worked with Moore in 2023, Parker and Moore served on the Eagles’ championship coaching staff this season. Moore has been a defensive backs coach for the last four seasons and was hired as the Eagles’ DB/pass game coordinator last season after previously working with the Broncos from 2021 to 2023. He played a key role in reshaping an Eagles secondary that ranked among the worst in 2023 to one of the best in 2024 and ultimately proved capable of shutting down Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs in the Super Bowl. If he’s hired, this would mark the first time in his career that Parker has served as a defensive coordinator.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos signed CB Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: The former third-round pick played almost exclusively on special teams as a rookie. He took over a starting role in his second season and never looked back. Moss has eight pass breakups and one interception this year. He led the league in PBUs in 2025. Moss was set to hit free agency next offseason. Instead, the Broncos got out ahead of him hitting the open market and kept him in town on a relatively affordable deal. Moss is just outside the 20 highest-paid corners on a per-year basis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Hufanga nearly played pre-bye in Week 9 against the Panthers, but he was unable to do so. He has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in Week 5 against the Chargers. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Riley Moss (concussion) are also practicing. Check back on Friday for their official statuses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss suffered a concussion in Denver’s Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Attempting to help out in run defense, Moss took a second quarter knee to the hit and went down in extremely concerning fashion. He was ruled out after the break. The Broncos’ thinned out pass defense has been struggling since Moss’ departure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss, one of the Broncos’ starting cornerbacks, returns from a one-game absence. He injured his ribs in Week 4 against the 49ers. The Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Jordan Jackson and DL Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 6 against the Seahawks. Ehlinger will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss was ruled out of Week 5 against the Chargers but has a chance to play Week 6 against the Seahawks with back-to-back limited practice listings. Meanwhile, S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was a DNP for the second straight day. With Patrick Surtain (ankle) still out in the short term, the Broncos’ banged-up secondary may have a tough time against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and company on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Neither Surtain or Riley Moss (ribs) practiced on Wednesday. Head coach Sean Payton said the Broncos don’t anticipate placing Surtain on injured reserve. The injuries to both corners look to be shorter-term; Surtain is week-to-week while Moss’ return timeline is not disclosed yet. Both are on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Patrick Surtain’s ankle injury is not believed to be season-ending.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: According to Rapoport, there are no longer any concerns that this is an Achilles injury for Surtain, who left Week 4’s game against the 49ers with a non-contact injury. Surtain could be looking at a multi-week absence and will undergo an MRI soon to confirm the severity of his injury, but it sounds like he avoided anything too serious. In addition to Surtain, the Broncos are also evaluating the status of CB Riley Moss, who is dealing with a rib injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos HC Sean Payton said the injury Riley Moss suffered in Friday’s preseason game is not considered serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss exited Friday’s game with an apparent rib injury, but Payton said the team is choosing to make the smart decision by not practicing him. Moss totaled 57 tackles and one interception last season and has started all 31 games he has appeared in since 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: The Baltimore Ravens sent Marlon Humphrey home and he will be inactive for Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey was asked what the city of Baltimore was good at making on his personal podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show. He jokingly responded, “They’re the best at making criminals.” Humphrey has since apologized for the disparaging remark, but the team is dismissing him for the week after a wave of backlash. He could potentially return in Week 12 against Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey logged one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable for Week 5. He’s one of several key defenders dealing with an injury heading into Sunday Night Football. EDGE Trey Hendrickson has already been ruled out, while S Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a groin injury. Even with some missing names, this defense still looks like a true test for Michael Penix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said CB Nate Wiggins and CB Marlon Humphrey “are trending very well to potentially be back next week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Wiggins was carted away on Tuesday, and Humphrey walked off with trainers on Wednesday. Minter’s phrasing is obviously non-committal, but it does seem like the Ravens’ starting cornerbacks will return before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (illness) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 18 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Bateman hasn’t practiced all week, but John Harbaugh said he believes both Bateman and Marlon Humphrey (illness — also questionable) to be cleared by game time on Sunday. Bateman has barely cracked the fantasy radar all season and would be hard to trust if he was healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey (finger) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: He didn’t even miss a practice after being sidelined ahead of Week 11’s game with the Browns. Humphrey will return and help limit the Jets’ new-look passing game in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said he is optimistic that Marlon Humphrey (finger) will be able to play in Week 12 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey underwent a minor procedure last week that sidelined him for Week 11 against the Browns. He was never expected to miss more than a game or two, so Harbaugh’s early optimism that he could return in Week 12 doesn’t come as a surprise. Humphrey has played on 272 coverage snaps this season, per PFF, breaking up four passes while also forcing one interception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said Marlon Humphrey (finger) may need surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: According to Harbaugh, Humphrey would likely miss one or two games if he did need surgery. The team is still weighing that decision, but with games against the Browns and Jets on tap over the next two weeks, it’s safe to say the Ravens can afford to be without Humphrey if he does opt for surgery. Humphrey has struggled in coverage this season, allowing 32 receptions for 461 yards and two touchdowns on 45 targets, but did notch his first interception of the season in Week 10’s win over the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens S Kyle Hamilton (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Neither are CB Chidobe Awuzie (hamstring), ILB Roquan Smith (hamstring), or CB Marlon Humphrey (illness) — and outside of Humphrey missing Wednesday’s practice all four of those players got in full sessions all week. Baltimore’s defense finally looks to mostly be recovered from their early October swoon. Will they actually play better in Week 8? That’s the real question.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Kirk underwent a successful meniscus surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rapoport didn’t give any details on Kirk’s timeline to return. We suspect he is done for the season. Kirk missed most of the season with a hamstring injury. He returned for one game, didn’t record any stats, and then injured his knee. Kirk signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in the offseason. He will be stuck taking another prove-it deal if he’s healthy when free agency starts in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk missed the start of the year with a calf issue and immediately injured his knee in Week 7. The 49ers have already burned several injured reserve return designations this year, including one on Kirk himself. He could ultimately be stuck on IR for the remainder of the year, even if he’s not dealing with a catastrophic knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers ruled out Christian Kirk (knee) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: At this point, Kirk probably does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He returned from his lengthy calf injury only to injure his knee. It’s a tough break for the veteran wide receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was not spotted at the open portion of Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited Wednesday with his knee issue, and it’s possible he’ll get that designation again in the closed portion of practice. The 29-year-old still has a decent chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders, but even with the litany of injuries for the 49ers in their receiving corps, it’s hard to trust Kirk from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk comes out of the 49ers’ bye as a limited practice participant due to a knee issue. He was not targeted in Week 7 after returning off a calf injury and should remain off fantasy rosters even if he plays in Week 9 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk was not targeted in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was activated off the injured list this week after missing the first six games of the season with a calf injury. He played on just 20 of the team’s 66 snaps and ran a route on 14 of their 43 dropbacks. Kirk was always likely to be eased back into things, and the 49ers have a bye next week to get him more up to speed. That being said, he doesn’t figure to be a huge part of this passing game if the 49ers can get more of their receivers back healthy after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers activated Christian Kirk (calf) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The 49ers would normally have Kirk on a pitch count for his first game of the year. With their top four receivers unavailable for today’s game, Kirk may be thrust into a full-time role right away. He will be in the mix for WR1 duties in San Francisco alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Kirk is a long-shot FLEX option for his first game as a 49er.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus after being activated from injured reserve Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited all of last week but starts out this week listed as a full participant for the 49ers’ Wednesday walkthrough practice. He remains on injured reserve, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7. A full practice listing is a good start and Kirk could see WR3 volume immediately with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Commanders signed WR Malik Heath to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Heath worked out for the Commanders Wednesday and signed to the practice squad. He caught 31 passes for 308 yards and three touchdowns over the past three seasons with the Packers and spent some time with the Falcons as well last season. The Commanders add Heath as receiving depth for the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Falcons did not tender restricted free agent WR Malik Heath, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Heath finished last year with a 6/86 line for the Packers and was a healthy scratch after signing with the Falcons in December. The 25-year-old offers special teams experience and will likely look to catch on as a veteran depth piece somewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Falcons WR Drake London (knee) is active for Week 16 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: We last saw London play in Week 11 against the Panthers, when he caught 7-of-9 targets for 119 yards before suffering a PCL sprain. He practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday and Thursday this week before sitting out on Friday. We really would have preferred to see him practice fully at the end of the week, though it is entirely possible that the team gave him the day off for rest and rehab. London’s target-earning ability keeps him in the WR1 tier, though his range of potential outcomes is far wider than normal. The Falcons declared CB Mike Hughes, RB Nathan Carter, LB JD Bertrand, OL Michael Jerrell, WR Casey Washington, DL Elijah Garcia and WR Malik Heath inactive for Week 16 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Falcons declared WR Drake London, WR Jamal Agnew, ILB JD Bertrand, OL Michael Jerrell, WR Casey Washington, WR Malik Heath and DL Elijah Garcia inactive for Week 15 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Falcons WR Darnell Mooney is, unfortunately, just a dart-throw FLEX option with London sidelined. Mooney has totaled 45-plus receiving yards just twice this season. Falcons TE Kyle Pitts will continue operating as the No. 1 pass catcher. He should be started as a high-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Falcons claimed WR Malik Heath off waivers from the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: The 25-year-old receiver has a career 31/308/3 slash line in 37 games with the Packers and can be involved on special teams. The Falcons are at a point where they’re relying on David Sills every weekend. The waiver claim makes some sense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Packers waived WR Malik Heath
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: With Jayden Reed (hamstring) activated off injured reserve, the Packers clear the needed room with the waiving of Heath. The 25-year-old will likely revert to the practice squad if he goes unclaimed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Packers WR Dontyavion Wicks (calf) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 1 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Ditto Savion Williams, as both got in three limited sessions and are likely on the optimistic side of questionable. Malik Heath could get involved if one of these two receivers gets ruled out ahead of the action on Sunday. As it is, Wicks profiles as a FLEX dart throw and Williams probably shouldn’t be started without either Wicks or Jayden Reed being ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Malik Heath did not catch any of his four targets in Green Bay’s Wild Card Round loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Most notably, he failed to catch a sideline ball from Jordan Love on a fourth-down pass where one of Heath’s feet clearly came down on the out-of-bounds line. Heath started against the Rams in Week 5, playing 76 percent of the snaps and drawing just three targets. Otherwise he was just a depth outside option for the Packers, only seeing extended playing time in Week 18. Heath will compete for a depth role with the Packers in August.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Malik heath hauled in his only target for a three-yard touchdown in the Packers’ Week 17 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Efficient. Heath caught his only target for a score to make it a 27-16 game late in the fourth. He saw no other targets, and likely will see a scarce few — if any — in Week 18 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.headline: Malik Heath caught 2-of-2 targets for 15 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 12 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-heat.analysis: Heath handled his typical, small workload this week but was fortunate enough to earn one of them in the green zone. His score from three yards out iced the Packers’ 38-10 win over the 49ers. He is a WR6 against the Dolphins in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle exited the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers with a concussion. He had time to work through the protocol with a Week 10 bye and is now back to practicing at the start of Week 11. Given his full participant listing, Waddle is trending to play this week against the Raiders. He has had a disappointing fantasy season and should be in the WR3 ranks for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Starting with the positive, Waddle found the end zone for the second time this year and got going over the middle of the field with a 35-yard missile from Nix early in the second quarter. It’s his longest catch since Week 2, when he erupted for 138 yards on eight receptions, including a 49-yarder. On the downside, Waddle managed a pedestrian 19 percent target share and finished third on the team in receiving. He found the end zone and still scored a grand total of 12.9 PPR points. The Broncos’ offense is still a work in progress, even if today was a step in the right direction. Waddle will get another week in the WR3 mix when the Broncos take on the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is no longer listed with a back injury, and is practicing in full post-bye. Both factors are extremely encouraging. The veteran running back is an RB1 against the Steelers this week, likely with an uptick in touches compared to the 13-carry workload he handled in Week 9 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: It was a horribly inefficient day for the Eagles’ superstar back, but there was not a whole lot he could do with the Giants understandably not respecting the “threat” presented by No. 3 Philly quarterback Joe Milton. Barkley at least saved face with his three-yard scoring plunge in the first quarter. Having his snaps and touches rationed for this injury-ruined and tanking team, Barkley will probably have a hard time getting back into the RB1 ranks when Philly comes off bye in Week 11 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley played through the pair of injuries last week, turning 13 carries into 30 yards and a score. While this could just be maintenance for a banged-up veteran, the Eagles are waving the white flag on 2026 by starting Joe Milton at quarterback. If they’re worried about making Barkley’s injuries worse, the team may simply shut him down for the year at some point. Elijah Mitchell is the next man up for Philly if Barkley doesn’t play in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley said the Eagles informed him that they don’t intend to trade him ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Speaking with the media early Monday morning, Barkley said he was informed that the team would not be trading him despite falling to 2-6 on the season after Sunday night’s loss to Washington. Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the loss while catching one pass for another 24 yards. The soon-to-be 30-year-old back could have decent trade value for the Eagles in what is shaping up to be a lost season, but it sounds like he’s in the team’s future plans heading into 2027. Barkley is playing through injuries and has just 56 carries for 274 yards and two touchdowns this season, and has caught seven passes for another 41 yards. Assuming he can get in another week of practice this week, he’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in Week 9 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding 24 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley showed clear limitations as he played through hamstring and back injuries, routinely spotted on the sideline riding the stationary bike and getting stretched out by trainers as he rotated with Elijah Mitchell. The Philadelphia offense remained largely ineffective as they gained only 268 yards of total offense, while Barkley’s longest carry of the game went for only five yards against a solid Washington run defense. Fantasy managers will want to consider their alternatives when the Eagles face the Giants in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Saquon Barkley “will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Though teams can change their minds in very short periods of time, Rapoport’s wording on this matter is rather definitive. Sitting at 2-5 with Jalen Hurts out for the year, it makes sense for the Eagles to be sellers at the trade deadline. Players including Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Hollywood Brown have also been the subject of trade rumors. All three are more likely than Barkley to land with new teams over the next week. Barring a change of heart from GM Howie Roseman, Barkley will continue to be the focal point of a failing offense for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley gave a cryptic response when asked if he would play earlier in the day, ultimately ready to gut out multiple injuries as the Eagles continue to trudge forward in an injury-decimated season. The veteran back added that the injuries are both something he will need to manage throughout the game but that he feels as if he can play through them. That leaves fantasy managers in a sticky situation, likely forced to start Barkley if he’s on the roster. Barkley is a middling RB2 in a difficult matchup on the ground against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens activated Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall is practicing in full and should be good to go for Week 11. He is set to make his NFL debut against the Panthers. With Derrick Henry hogging most of the carries and Justice Hill handling the passing downs, Randall will likely be limited to special teams for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Adam Randall (neck) is questionable for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall is currently on injured reserve, so the Ravens will have to activate him tomorrow afternoon if they plan on him playing. He will compete with Rasheen Ali for the RB3 role if he’s ready to return to the field this week. There isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens designated Adam Randall to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall was placed on injured reserve at the end of training camp with an undisclosed injury. The team now has three weeks to officially activate him from injured reserve. Once healthy, Randall will be contending with Rasheen Ali for the Ravens’ rarely used RB3 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue. He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens signed fifth-round pick RB Adam Randall to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Per Spotrac, the deal is worth $4.62 million and includes a $379,480 signing bonus. Randall is the team owner, Steve Bisciotti’s first handpicked player. He converted from wide receiver to running back for Clemson’s 2025 season and posted a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens’ Ryan Mink reports that team owner Steve Bisciotti was allowed to draft a player for the first time ever this year and chose former Clemson RB Adam Randall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens drafted Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft’s fifth round yesterday. Bisciotti has been the Ravens’ majority owner since 2004 and was reportedly “begging” general manager Eric DeCosta for the chance to draft a rookie this year. According to DeCosta, Bisciotti “did his research and studied the tape, talked to people.” Bisciotti notably has a really good relationship with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney. Swinney moved Randall (6’3/232) from wide receiver to running back for the 2025 season after Randall showcased shifty moves when given the chance to run the ball and contribute as a returner late in 2024. Whether Randall can earn the No. 2 or No. 3 running back role remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens selected Clemson RB Adam Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall could be the next big-bodied WR-to-RB convert to earn an NFL roster spot. He suffered a torn ACL during a 2022 spring practice and recovered in time to resume playing in Week 3 that year. Randall’s splash plays in the run game and return game late in 2024 inspired coach Dabo Swinney to move Randall from WR to RB for the 2025 season. Built to handle a three-down workload, Randall, 21, measured 6’3/232 at the NFL Scouting Combine. In his lone season at running back, Randall produced a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line. Randall is still learning how to play running back, so he comes with a very low floor, but his frame and dual-threat profile make him a name to know for fantasy purposes. He will likely get a crack at replacing Keaton Mitchell’s part-time role as a rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Omarion Hampton has reestablished himself as the team’s lead running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado asked Harbaugh why it took Hampton so long to reestablish himself as the team’s top running back. Harbaugh said, “he’s there (now). He’s showing it, proving it. And that’s all. That’s what’s important to me.” Hampton totaled 22 carries and one catch in Week 10. It sounds like he has a chance to continue handling a high-volume workload in the coming weeks, though the game script could hurt him if he fails to increase his passing game usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding one reception for zero additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton tallied just his second game of 100 yards from scrimmage in the team’s first win of the season, which was also his first game this year hitting the century mark on the ground. The only other game in which Hampton surpassed 100 yards came against the Raiders way back in Week 2, which was also the only other game this season with 20 or more touches. The typically backfield timeshare tilted heavily in Hampton’s favor through positive game script, hinting at his upside potential in games the Chargers are able to control, something that has not been routine this season. Hampton could carry legitimate RB2 upside against the Jets in Week 11, pending the status of quarterback Geno Smith.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that Omarion Hampton would get more touches. Surprise. The Chargers continued their three-player backfield rotation for much of the day, though Kimani Vidal was somewhat phased out in the second half. That said, Hampton at least totaled double-digit rushing attempts for the first time since Week 5. He clearly looked like the most powerful, explosive Chargers running back on a 32-yard run late in the game, jump-cutting his way into an open hole before exploding down the right side of the field. Hampton is a FLEX option against the Ravens in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had nine rushes for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding two catches for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: It was business as usual for the plodding Hampton, who breaks no tackles and does nothing beyond what is blocked for him. Hampton, who now has less than 50 rushing yards in five games this season, was third in pass routes among LA running backs on the day and tied with Keaton Mitchell with three targets. Hampton’s role doesn’t offer much: Coming into Week 8, he ranked 31st among running backs in expected fantasy points per game (and 37th in actual fantasy points per game). With no ceiling of which to speak, Hampton should stay on benches in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed nine times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton’s late touchdown that still left the Chargers down by 10 in the middle of the fourth quarter is the only positive of the day. Los Angeles clearly isn’t enamored with the second-year tailback — or at the very best, is concerned about keeping him healthy — right now, and he was clearly in a timeshare again with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. He’s at best a FLEX play for Week 5 against the tough Denver defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings missed the past two games with the calf injury. A full practice today puts him on track to return for a revenge game against the 49ers. Jordan Addison is sidelined with a thumb injury, meaning Jennings will likely return to the No. 2 receiver role. He is worth a look in deeper formats, though he’s still a high-risk WR5 for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings would have been useful additional depth to have with Jordan Addison suddenly questionable. Tai Felton will likely see more work in Week 10, and perhaps Odell Beckham Jr. will be elevated off the practice squad if Jordan Addison (thumb) also sits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings missed Week 9 against the Bills with the calf issue and looks likely to sit for at least one more game. Myles Price ran ahead of Tai Felton last week, putting him in line for another round of No. 3 duties in Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the uptick in snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been the subject of trade rumors. Since is able to practice, even in a limited capacity, this injury is unlikely to alter a potential suitor’s interest. Regardless, Jennings is not on the FLEX radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings “would be a name for me to keep an eye on” for the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been a major disappointment in Minnesota, falling behind Tai Felton on the depth chart. A small stakes trade could make sense for the 49ers, who are down to hoping Brandin Cooks can provide for Brock Purdy in a major rash of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman should be able to face Miami this weekend. The Bills will likely employ a run-heavy approach, though with Kyle McCord starting on the other side. Coleman is only a boom-bust FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-3 passes for 11 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman did make an impressive second catch in traffic, but the play was called back due to an illegal shift penalty. He also took a hit to his helmet on the same play and had to go into the blue medical tent. He was eventually cleared and returned to play, but it’s a situation to watch at practice this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman’s fantasy-scoring outlook has been hurt by his teammate’s improving health. At this point, Coleman is more so a single-game DFS FLEX rather than a starter in 12-team re-draft formats. He should be good to go for Week 9’s Monday Night Football game though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey at today’s practice. His limited session to begin the week puts him on track to face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. With DJ Moore (shoulder) back in the lineup, Coleman is just a WR4/FLEX. Joshua Palmer (hamstring) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 4-of-6 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman’s six targets tied for second-most on the Bills with Khalil Shakir, who also found the end zone in this one. Coleman scored on an impressive 12-yard play by Josh Allen, who appeared ready to take off and run with the ball before spotting Coleman open in the end zone and flipping a shovel pass to him for the score. Coleman has now scored in three straight games and has been targeted six or more times in two of his last three. With the Bills now heading into their Week 7 bye, Coleman could face more target competition when they return in Week 8 against the Ravens if DJ Moore (shoulder) is active. Moore was questionable entering this week and ruled out 90 minutes before kickoff, so it wouldn’t be surprising if he was a full-go after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was largely erased by the lockdown corner play of the Rams but had a receiving line also heavily influenced by a ground-heavy game plan from a Bills team that attempted only 19 passes in almost 70 minutes of football. It was quite the letdown fantasy performance for managers looking to take advantage of the absences of both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Coleman is a borderline FLEX play in Week 6 against the Raiders, pending the status of Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was added to the injury report on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Palmer seemingly injured his shoulder in practice today. The Bills may already be without WR DJ Moore (shoulder) on Monday night. While Palmer is not relevant in 12-team leagues, his potential absence would improve Keon Coleman’s stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Rams this week. He had a career day in Week 4, with a 6/116/1 receiving line. We have seen Coleman produce solid outings in the past, so caution is advised if one is to consider believing the hype. That said, he rose to the occasion last week and could do so again in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: This was the best game we’ve seen from Coleman in a long time. Not only did he show up in the box score, but two of his catches were unbelievable sideline grabs that showed the type of hands that made him an intriguing draft pick out of Florida State. He played on 46 of the team’s 59 snaps and ran a route on 31 of their 40 dropbacks. With D.J. Moore leaving this game with a shoulder injury, Coleman is a priority add on waiver wires before next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said WR Keon Coleman (ankle) “should be good to play” for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was limited on Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and apparently will avoid a questionable tag. He was questionable last week and played through the injury, though he doesn’t draw enough targets to be fantasy-relevant outside of the deepest leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions activated S Kerby Joseph (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph was designated to return from the PUP list exactly three weeks ago, so they had to activate him today. He got in a full practice last week but did not travel to Germany with the team. Practicing in full once again, Joseph looks likely to make his 2026 debut in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph got in a full practice session with the Lions on Thursday, but will not travel to Munich with the club. It sounds like he’ll have a real chance to play in Week 11 when the Lions head back to the states.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: The Lions are at their best when the offensive line is in good health. Mays missed multiple games early in the year with a wrist injury. He is now sidelined by an ankle injury. Hopefully, he can resume practicing before long. Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Brian Branch (hip) were both limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) will not play in Detroit’s Week 8 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Dan Campbell said Joseph has been used only in individual and group practices so far and that he’s handled that well. Next week he’ll get in on real practice. Joseph probably stands a decent chance of being active for Week 9 assuming he acclimates well to that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph dealt with a cartilage issue in his knee last year and has spent the entirety of 2026 working his way back from it. As of a month ago, Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic that Joseph would be able to play at any point this year. Joseph is currently on the PUP list. His return to practice means the team has opened his 21-day practice window. We expect them to use most of the window to ramp Joseph up to full speed, but it’s still a great sign for the playmaking safety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) is hopeful he’ll be available later this season, reports NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Lions HC Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic about the prospects of Joseph, who is dealing with a potentially career-threatening knee cartilage issue, helping the Lions this year. In two separate media appearances in the last week, Campbell said that there wasn’t anything he could say about Joseph that would make anyone “feel good.” Pelissero reported Saturday morning that Joseph, who missed all of training camp and hasn’t played since last year’s Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, is hopeful he’ll be available to help the Lions down the stretch. While that may be the case, whether Joseph is able to return to play this year remains an open question. Without Joseph and S Brian Branch (Achilles), the Lions are severely shorthanded in the backend heading into Week 3’s home matchup against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph is still nursing a knee injury that hampered him last season. He will remain on the PUP list to open the season, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the active/PUP list with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (ankle/foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Fellow starting CB DaRon Bland will miss time with injuries in both ankles, but at least Porter’s health is trending upward. Cowboys OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), OG Tyler Booker (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is active for the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter and fellow corner DaRon Bland are both active for this one, giving the Cowboys their top two corners against a good 49ers offense. We’ll see if Porter and Bland can slow Brock Purdy and company at home in Jerry World as the Cowboys look to move to 5-5 this season. The Cowboys ruled out S P.J. Locke, LB Donovan Ezeiruaku, WR Jonathan Mingo, S Juanyeh Thomas, OT Ajani Cornelius, TE Jake Ferguson, and DB Derion Kendrick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is “trending towards playing” in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Fellow Dallas cornerback Daron Bland is also expected to play. We don’t foresee the Cowboys putting up much of a fight against the 49ers offense, but having both corners available will at least help them slow San Francisco down a bit. Porter has appeared in four games for the Cowboys this year. He has three pass breakups and eight combined tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter reportedly told reporters that his “whole foot is jacked up.” That sounds bad. He was able to run today, and hadn’t in a while, but declined to say whether he will play in Week 10 against the 49ers. We suspect he will sit out this weekend’s contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter Jr. was on the practice field with his helmet on, but he ultimately watched as the rest of the defense went through the session. He was playing through the ankle issue for a while before missing Week 9 against Arizona. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 10, but things could change if he manages a limited session on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler Jr. (ankle) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: JPJ was downgraded to a limited participant in Friday before being hit with the questionable tag, causing some concern about his Week 6 availability. It looks like the light practice session may have been a precaution. The newly-minted Cowboys should be good to go versus Green Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is questionable for Dallas’ Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter downgraded from full to limited on Friday and wound up with this status despite practicing all three days this week. Peculiar. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson would be better off on Sunday if Porter wasn’t able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Cowboys declare CB Joey Porter, LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, OLB James Houston, OG Ajani Cornelius, OT Drew Shelton and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter’s bumpy 2026 campaign takes another surprising turn. The Cowboys’ new cornerback was set to expand his involvement this evening, but he is evidently unable to play due to an illness. Fortunately for the Cowboys, the Buccaneers’ offense is hamstrung by Baker Mayfield’s (thumb) absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (back/conditioning/contract) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on Friday, “we actually think Joey Porter will get snaps.” ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that prior to the mid-week trade, Porter was ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Steelers and Browns, saying his back was tight. He practiced the last two days “without issue.” Porter might be on a snap count this week, but it looks like he will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo returned to action last week after missing one game with the hamstring injury. He ran for 78 yards and scored twice while adding 44 yards on three grabs. Whether they want to or not, the Giants are treating Skattebo like a workhorse back once again. He is pushing to the top of the RB2 ranks heading into his Week 11 matchup with Jacksonville.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 44 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo immediately returned to a workhorse role following the shortcomings of Devin Singletary in Week 10, the latter of whom saw but one opportunity to the 22 of Skattebo. The Skatt-man bookended halftime with a score from one yard out on the team’s final possession of the first half and a score from 13 yards out on the team’s first possession of the second half, earning two backflips in the process. The second-year back also escaped down the sideline for a 34-yard reception in the first quarter to pad his counting stats. Despite the resurgence in workload, Skattebo will be a borderline FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said to “expect a lot of Cam Skattebo” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The Giants host the Commanders for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. The open-air stadium is currently experiencing heavy rain, and Fowler indicates the rainfall will continue this evening. Devin Singletary will back up Skattebo, but the touch distribution will heavily “slant” toward Skattebo, solidifying his status as an RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9. He reportedly pushed to play, but the team smartly chose to hold him out. He logged two full practices this week and is good to go for Thursday’s game. Without much competition for touches, Skattebo is back in the RB2 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports the Giants inquired about Bijan Robinson’s availability before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: He should be good to go and handle low-end RB2 duties against the Commanders. Seemingly always at his best after a week off — which makes sense due to how physical he plays — don’t be surprised if Skattebo puts up some major fantasy points on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier Monday that Skattebo would be “full go” for Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. It’s good news for a New York football team that struggled mightily to run the football consistently with veteran journeyman Devin Singletary spearheading the backfield against the Eagles in Week 9. Skattebo appears likely to reclaim lead back duties moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will be “full go” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Harbaugh said Skattebo was “very close” to playing in Week 9 against the Eagles, but they opted to sideline him, focusing on the second game they would play four days later. With the Giants set to face the Commanders on Thursday, Skattebo should be well rested and ready to play in his first game since Week 7, when he first suffered his injury. Skattebo totaled 71 scoreless yards on 15 touches in Week 5 against the Commanders and will be in the RB2 mix upon returning this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said DaRon Bland (ankle) will “miss some time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Bland entered the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers with a left ankle injury. Unfortunately, he suffered a high-ankle sprain in his right ankle mid-game and could miss “the bulk” of the remaining schedule. Bland’s absence will make this weak defense even weaker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Cowboys S DaRon Bland (ankle) will not return in Week 10’s game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Bland could be seen having his right ankle tended to on the sideline in the second quarter of Sunday’s game. The 27-year-old corner was ruled out at the beginning of the second half and entered the game with an ankle injury that had him listed as questionable entering the weekend. Hopefully this isn’t an issue that plagues him for too long, as Dallas can ill-afford to lose its top defenders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is active for the Cowboys’ Week 10 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Porter and fellow corner DaRon Bland are both active for this one, giving the Cowboys their top two corners against a good 49ers offense. We’ll see if Porter and Bland can slow Brock Purdy and company at home in Jerry World as the Cowboys look to move to 5-5 this season. The Cowboys ruled out S P.J.
