Locke, LB Donovan Ezeiruaku, WR Jonathan Mingo, S Juanyeh Thomas, OT Ajani Cornelius, TE Jake Ferguson, and DB Derion Kendrick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is “trending towards playing” in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Fellow Dallas cornerback Daron Bland is also expected to play. We don’t foresee the Cowboys putting up much of a fight against the 49ers offense, but having both corners available will at least help them slow San Francisco down a bit. Porter has appeared in four games for the Cowboys this year. He has three pass breakups and eight combined tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, the Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space this year. They also reworked DT Kenny Clark and CB DaRon Bland’s deals. Ferguson’s $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. For fantasy purposes, this does not alter Ferguson’s standing. The front office could have a personnel move in mind, though. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that Cowboys CB DaRon Bland (foot) is expected to be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Back in January, Bland said he expected to be ready for organized team activities. Unfortunately, that has not been the case. That said, Archer thought Bland was “moving very well laterally,” and expect the Cowboys to “be patient with how they bring him along.” Bland was injured in Week 15 last year. He tallied five pass breakups, one interception, 54 tackles and two quarterback pressures.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Cowboys CB DaRon Bland (foot) said he expects to be fully healthy for Dallas’ offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: Bland will undergo foot surgery later this week after missing the final three weeks of the season with the foot ailment. Signed to an extension during training camp, Bland had a career-worst (though still fairly solid) 64.5 PFF coverage grade in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: Cowboys activated CB Trevon Diggs (knee) ahead of Week 16 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: The team also placed fellow cornerback DaRon Bland (foot) on injured reserve in an associated move. As has been the case for most of the season, the Cowboys continue forward without pieces from their secondary. Diggs pushed his return up to the limit, meaning we might not see him play a full allotment of snaps in his first game in over two months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Cowboys CB DaRon Bland “is facing surgery on his left foot” and is “likely going to end up on injured reserve.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-blan.analysis: This is unfortunate. Bland broke out in 2023, breaking up six passes and recording nine interceptions. He fractured his foot during the 2024 training camp and has struggled to return to form ever since. This season, Bland has broken up five passes, intercepted one pass, totaled 53 tackles and two quarterback pressures.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, this is the first time Stribling has worked off to the side at practice since injuring his ankle in Week 1. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant, but this is still a great sign for his availability in the coming weeks. Stribling must be rostered in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers WR De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: According to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco, the 49ers are “hopeful he can return this season,” which is a tad confusing, given the 10-week return timeline. Regardless, 10 weeks, plus a little wiggle room, should allow Stribling to return late in the regular season, potentially in time to help fantasy managers make a playoff push. That said, he should probably only be kept on managed re-draft rosters with an injured reserve spot. Veteran WR Demarcus Robinson filled in for Stribling last week and may be FLEX-viable moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the 49ers placed De’Zaun Stribling (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering a serious ankle injury in Week 1’s win over the Rams. It’s a disappointing start for the rookie, who can safely be dropped in most fantasy leagues. Deebo Samuel, who led the Niners in slot routes last week, could see an uptick in playing time and targets over the next month. Samuel had 48 yards on six receptions against the Rams. He should be rostered in 12-team PPR formats ahead of the Niners’ Week 2 game against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is out “at least a month.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling suffered a deltoid sprain in his ankle. He is not expected to undergo surgery at this time, though Rapoport notes it is still a possibility. The fact that Rapoport noted that Stribling is “still seeking opinions” suggests surgery is very much on the table. With the rookie sidelined, Demarcus Robinson will slide into the three-receiver rotation. He scored a long touchdown versus the Rams in Week 1, though he profiles as a boom/bust WR6 going forward. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel will see the majority of targets in most weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said De’Zhaun Stribling’s Achilles was intact after Week 1’s win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling was carted from the game late in the second quarter after briefly attempting to play through the ankle injury he suffered earlier in the game. While there was some concern that his injury was Achilles-related, Shanahan’s comments after the game suggest there’s little reason to be concerned about his Achilles at this time. Stribling played 21 snaps in the first half of Thursday’s game but was held without a catch. We’ll likely get more clarity on his status in the coming days, but hopefully the worst was avoided here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) has been ruled for the remainder of Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling was carted off during Friday’s contest, and finished without a catch in his NFL debut. He’ll get a little longer to potentially return for Week 2 against the Dolphins, but obviously his status for that contest is very much in doubt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) exited Week 1 against the Rams on a cart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling hurt the ankle earlier in the contest, and while he was able to return shortly after, the rookie wideout was unable to continue and exited on the vehicle. It’s likely he won’t return to Friday’s game, but there should be an update on his status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes “the plan” is for WR De’Zhaun Stribling to be the primary slot receiver and WR Mike Evans’ “understudy” at X-receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In his projected depth chart, Barrows lists Stribling as both the starting slot receiver and the No. 2 X-receiver. He does not place Stribling on the Z-receiver depth chart, which could mean the rookie wide receiver has not yet earned a role in two-wide receiver sets. Veteran WR Deebo Samuel is the starting Z-receiver, though Barrows already reported that Samuel will take only “a portion” of the overall Z-receiver snaps. It would be surprising to see Nos. 2-3 Z-receivers, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing, play ahead of Stribling when Samuel needs a breather, but the season is long and Stribling can always change Barrows’ mind. Early in the year, Stribling is likely best treated as a WR4/FLEX candidate. Were Evans to miss time, Stribling would seemingly slide into a full-time starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said he hopes Mike Evans (adductor) will practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Evans’ Week 1 status is starting to look iffy after missing most of the past few weeks with various injuries. Entering his age-33 season, Evans will need to log at least a couple practices next week if he’s going to suit up against the Rams in the season opener. Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans is “ahead of schedule doing good. But we know with Mike and where he is at in his career, we’ll definitely have to treat him differently.” An Evans absence would be a marked boost for De’Zhaun Stribling and perhaps Deebo Samuel. Evans will be a name to watch in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers WR De’Zhaun Stribling (shoulder) resumed practicing in a non-contact jersey on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team labeled Stribling as “day-to-day” yesterday. His limited return is a good sign for his Week 1 availability. Hopefully, the 49ers’ impressive rookie is back in pads before long. He can still be drafted as a FLEX starter with WR3 upside at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Mike Jackson (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters that he thinks Jackson, his team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, is “ready” to return. He will slightly upgrade the Panthers’ secondary if so. Jackson has been sidelined since injuring his groin in late September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Mike Jackson (core muscle surgery) will be sidelined for around eight weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Canales said fellow corner Jaycee Horn faces a similar timeline. He suffered a torn quad in Week 3 but did not need surgery. Both players were placed on injured reserve earlier today. The Panthers will now be without their top two corners for most of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Panthers placed Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Horn, who suffered a quad tear in Week 3’s loss to Cleveland, could miss most of the season while Jackson’s groin injury is likely less severe. Even so, Carolina’s suspect defense will be without both starting corners for now — a potential boon for opposing passing attacks, including the Lions in Week 4. Carolina has allowed the 12th lowest drop back EPA and the 15th lowest passing success rate through Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Panthers CB Mike Jackson suffered a groin injury in Carolina’s Week 3 game against the Browns and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Jackson was injured on a first quarter play where he was called for pass interference. He’s an every-snap player for the Panthers’ defense, so this will require dipping into the team’s depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Panthers re-signed CB Mike Jackson to a two-year, $14.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Jackson was acquired just before the start of the 2024 regular season in a trade with the Seahawks and now remains with the Panthers on a new two-year deal. He played all but 13 defensive snaps for the Panthers a season ago and should remain the team’s other perimeter option next to Jaycee Horn.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Panthers acquired CB Michael Jackson from the Seahawks in exchange for LB Michael Barrett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: Jackson has appeared in 34 games for the Seahawks over the last two seasons while making 21 starts. The fifth-year corner earned a PFF coverage grade of 76.9 while playing on 474 defensive snaps last season and provides nice depth for a Panthers secondary that is in need of help. In return, the Seahawks get rookie linebacker Michael Barrett, who the Panthers selected in the seventh round of this year’s draft. Barrett has totaled two tackles this preseason and will likely contribute on special teams to start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Patriots waived CB Michael Jackson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: It’s a mild surprise after the Patriots traded Jackson earlier in camp. Clearly, it was a conditional pick contingent on Jackson making the team. The second-year fifth-rounder quickly developed a reputation for going toe to toe with N’Keal Harry, but the wideout had started getting the better of him of late. Jackson is only 23, but he is fast becoming a journeyman.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.headline: Patriots traded a 2022 draft pick to the Lions for CB Michael Jackson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-jacks.analysis: The trade came hours after the Lions announced they would cut Jackson, who played in just one game for Detroit in 2019. Jackson was drafted by Dallas in the fifth round of the 2019 NFL draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young has played through lower-body injuries for much of the season already. Late in October, coach Dave Canales admitted that Young’s knee issue may be limiting his mobility. While we fully expect Young to play this week, he may be a little less likely to scramble than he normally would. Regardless, it doesn’t alter his ranking much. Today, Canales said Young’s “foot was sore coming out of the game Sunday, but it’s been getting better and better.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 17-of-30 attempts for 200 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding one rush for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It was one of Young’s worst performances of the season considering the middling competition. He posted a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent under his expected completion rate against New Orleans. His statistical day would have been a little less bleak if Darren Waller had been able to hang on to what would have been a 30-yard score in the first half. Young, who regular missed open wideouts in the intermediate areas, has struggled for most of the past month. Young will be a superflex option in Week 11 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 28-of-39 passes for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in the Panthers’ 26-21, Week 9 loss to the Broncos, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young’s three-score start was his first since Week 2, though the two turnovers really put a damper on things. Young’s fourth quarter fumble short-circuited a potential game-winning drive, while his interception came in the end zone. Now, it was one of the more unlucky plays we have ever seen in the NFL — a ball seemingly everyone thought bounced off the ground actually bounced off a player into Devon Key’s arms — but Young put too much on the negative side of the ledger for the Panthers to pull this one out. They’ve now lost three straight games to fall to 3-5 on the season. Young at least snapped a streak of three straight starts with a sub-60 completion percentage. He also converted a late 4th-and-18 with an amazing throw. Young remains a frustrating option on the QB1/2 borderline heading into a golden Week 10 matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said after Week 8’s loss to the Packers that Young’s knee injury could be limiting his mobility. The team didn’t list the knee issue on this week’'s injury report, instead adding an ankle injury to the mix. It’s not something that will prevent Young from playing on Sunday, but another lingering ailment could further hamper his mobility. Already in the midst of a two-game slump, Young is back in the middle of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers. Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers listed Bryce Young (knee) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was listed with the same knee injury last Friday but remained a full participant and was good to go in Week 7. Whatever issue he’s dealing with appears minor, especially if the team is still listing him as a full participant. At this point, there’s no reason to think he won’t be active for Week 8’s game against the Packers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 14-of-27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Panthers’ Week 7 game against the Bucs, also losing a fumble-six.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: With the Panthers somehow losing 43-6 in the fourth quarter, Young gave way to Kenny Pickett for the final 10:11. Pickett immediately engineered a garbage time touchdown drive. This was by far Young’s worst performance of what had so far been a legitimate breakout campaign, as he short-circuited one drive after another and set up Bucs short fields with turnovers. The fumble-six was the most costly mistake, but Young’s second interception was probably his worst throw. He was fooled by the coverage under pressure and threw the ball right to Tykee Smith. Young’s first pick came after Jalen Coker fell down. In between all the miscues, Young could get nothing going with either Coker or Tetairoa McMillan. It was hard to see this coming — especially against the Bucs — but it is even harder to see it continuing for Thursday’s short-week date with the Packers. With that contest likely to feature shootout game script, Young will remain in the low-end QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It’s the first time we’ve seen Young o the injury report with this knee issue, though a full practice today is nothing to worry about. He will be good to go for his date with the Bucs. Young is currently the QB4 by fantasy points per game. Even if he does cool down this week, Young should be in most starting fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans ruled out Danielle Hunter (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter will now miss his second game due to a hamstring injury. He is replaced in the lineup by veteran pass rusher Jadaveon Clowney. Fortunately, Will Anderson returned from his ankle injury last week. Kamari Lassiter (wrist) is expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter popped up on the report with this injury on Thursday as limited and wound up ruled out after a DNP on Friday. Rough scenes for the $40 million-a-year edge rusher. This will be the first game he has missed since the 2021 season. Houston’s pass rush looks tenuous against the Browns with Will Anderson Jr. also on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans signed EDGE Danielle Hunter to a one-year, $40.1 million contract extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: The two sides did the same thing last March via a $35.6 million deal. Hunter’s new one-year extension includes a $30.7 million signing bonus. Per PFF, Hunter totaled 83 quarterback pressures and 16 sacks last season. Both figures rank in the top five in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans signed EDGE Danielle Hunter to a one-year, $35.6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Hunter is now the NFL’s second-highest paid defensive end and will make $32 million this season, a $12.5 million bump from his previous contract. His deal becomes a two-year, $55.1 million agreement with $54.1 million guaranteed. Hunter initially signed a two-year deal with the Texans last offseason and now gets one more season in Houston with a pay bump after tallying 12 sacks and a Pro Bowl in 2024. With Will Anderson opposite Hunter, the Texans keep a menacing pass rush through 2026. This sets another price point in an expensive edge market with pass rushers like Trey Hendrickson and Micah Parsons next to cash in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans agreed to terms with EDGE Danielle Hunter, formerly of the Vikings, on a two-year, $49 million deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: The Texans essentially swap edge rushers with the Vikings, adding the veteran Hunter after reportedly losing Jonathan Greenard to Minnesota. One of the top edge rushers on the market, Hunter totaled 16.5 sacks for the Vikings in 2023. The former third round pick will spend his first career snaps outside of Minnesota in 2024, lining up opposite of Defensive Rookie of the Year Will Anderson. It’s a reported two-year deal worth $49 million with a max value of $51 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports the Vikings “made an effort” to re-sign EDGE Danielle Hunter earlier this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: This doesn’t mean a deal with Hunter won’t get done before free agency opens up, but with the team also attempting to re-sign Kirk Cousins and extend Justin Jefferson, it’s possible Hunter at least makes it to the open market. Jeremy Fowler added that teams are expecting Hunter to seek a deal that pays “well north of $20 million per year,” which would make him amongst the highest paid EDGE rushers i the league. Hunter tallied a career-high 16.5 sacks with the Vikings last season and has totaled 87.5 sacks through his first eight seasons in the league. Hunter will be 29 at the start of next season, and should have no trouble fetching a lucrative deal should he and the Vikings not come to terms on a contract in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings are “receiving calls” about EDGE Danielle Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter has been the subject of trade rumors for years, but the Vikings have always worked things out with their star pass-rusher. That includes giving him a one-year, $20 million contract that features a no-tag clause this offseason. Hunter leads the NFL with eight sacks but his team sits at 2-4. With Minnesota’s season circling the drain, it would be smart for them to get something for Hunter instead of holding onto him for a lost season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Vikings signed DE Danielle Hunter to a one-year $20 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter’s contract includes $17 million in guaranteed money, a no-tag clause, and ultimately ends his brief hold-in with the team. Dating back to 2022, Hunter and the Vikings have gone back and forth in contract negotiations, which led to Hunter being the subject of trade rumors earlier this offseason. Since entering the league in 2015, Hunter has totaled 71 sacks, 85 TFLs, and three Pro Bowls. The no-tag clause gives the veteran pass rusher a chance to earn a significant payday in 2024 — either from the Vikings or via free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Danielle Hunter has reported to Vikings training camp but that he isn’t expected to practice until “his situation gets resolved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter skipped the Vikings’ mandatory minicamp earlier this offseason after being the subject of trade rumors earlier. The veteran pass rusher is also in search of a new extension, which he’s been hoping to secure dating back to last year. Hunter totaled 10.5 sacks and 12 TFLs for the Vikings in 2022 and was named to his third Pro Bowl. Because he reported to training camp, Hunter can’t be fined, but there are multiple ways he can stay off the field while he and the team figure out what to do next.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Vikings EDGE Danielle Hunter is planning to skip the team’s mandatory minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter has been the subject of trade rumors for the last two offseasons. The veteran pass rusher was in search of a contract extension last offseason but ultimately played on his deal. Now in the final year of his contract, Hunter, who totaled 10.5 sacks and 12 TFLS last season, is still in search of a new deal. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported last week that teams have already begun contacting the Vikings about a potential trade for Hunter, but little has materialized since then. Set to earn just $5.5 million this season, Hunter is more than deserving of a new deal, whether it’s from the Vikings or another team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans ruled out Woody Marks (concussion) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: David Montgomery (groin) is expected to return for tomorrow’s game. Emari Demercardo will serve as Montgomery’s backup. The Texans’ run game has been unable to establish itself as a reliable unit, but Montgomery’s workload and matchup against the Colts’ defense put him in the RB2 tier. The Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Should Marks return to action, he will likely be relegated to PPR FLEX status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: His ruleout on Wednesday is basically just a formality at this point. David Montgomery looks likely to lead the Texans backfield against the Colts on Thursday night. Marks should have a real chance to suit up for Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: It is highly unlikely that Marks will clear concussion protocol on a short week, likely leaving Emari Demercado to split work with David Montgomery, the latter of whom was listed as a full participant as he aims to return from his own injury. Fantasy managers can consider Demercado a viable waiver target in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion evaluation) left Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: He was sandwiched between a pair of defenders on a third-quarter run and eventually walked off between trainers. Marks had 65 total yards before leaving, including one catch for 15 yards. With the short week ahead of them, the Texans will likely not have Marks available on Thursday night, leaving fantasy managers ignoring Emari Demercado and Dare Obungowale unless David Montgomery can play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks should be good to go for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns, though this backfield is awfully banged up. Marks totaled 18 carries and four targets last week, and should again handle a sizable workload this week. Unfortunately, he has not proven to be an efficient player and may need to score a touchdown to return RB2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 18 times for 70 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was able to earn four targets in this one, but he caught only one of them. He was heavily involved as a rusher, regularly churning out short-to-intermediate ground gains, but without steady receiving production, he is stuck in the low-end RB2 tier with touchdown-dependent upside. He will qualify as such next week against the Browns if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Per head coach DeMeco Ryans, Montgomery remains week-to-week. He did not practice today and we assume he won’t get on the field in any capacity this week. Woody Marks will make another start. Facing a down-horrific Chargers squad, Marks should finally get going after two underwhelming starts in Montgomery’s absence. He is a locked-in RB2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.headline: Steelers placed LG Mason McCormick (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports this morning that McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle but not a fracture. That gives him a shot at returning in the postseason, though he will miss at least the rest of the regular season. Spencer Anderson took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and will likely do so going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.headline: Mason McCormick (lower leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 10 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.analysis: McCormick stayed down on the field with his head in his hands following a pass protection rep late in the second quarter against the Bengals. Training staff placed an air cast on his lower leg and loaded him onto the cart to be removed from the field. He was immediately taken to the locker room for x-rays and is likely looking at an extended absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.headline: Steelers selected South Dakota State OG Mason McCormick with the No. 119 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-mcco.analysis: Mason McCormick (6'4/309) was an unranked interior offensive lineman in the 2018 recruiting class who decided to play just up I-29 from his hometown of Sioux Falls at South Dakota State. McCormick’s biggest knock may be the level of competition he played against at SDSU, where he received all-conference honors four times, was named a consensus All-American twice, and had the distinction of being a team captain for three years in 57 career starts. In terms of build, there is almost no width difference between his shoulders and hips. McCormick is probably maxed out on physical development, but at 24 years old that is to be expected. He uses his mature frame with reckless abandon in the run game. When blocking downhill, he has good aim in nailing his facemask to defenders on the second level. When blocking in the trenches, he has a deft understanding of digging out the lower leverage on shorter Defensive Linemen, while attacking the midsection of taller three techs. McCormick has decent agility on pulls, though he shows some stiffness when pulling square around tackles. Ultimately, McCormick is a ready-made prospect who can plug into a lineup at a position of weakness.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison underwent successful surgery on his thumb after suffering a “freak” injury in practice last week. He is still expected to miss multiple games, but not placing him on IR means the Vikings don’t foresee him missing an entire month. He will be out for Week 11 and likely Week 12, but fantasy managers should still try to hold onto him ahead of the fantasy postseason. Myles Price and Tai Felton will be in the mix for extra targets if Jauan Jennings remains out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will undergo surgery and could miss “a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: He called it a “freak” injury and didn’t dismiss the possibility of Addison heading to short-term injured reserve. Fantasy managers in a rough bye week squeeze without injured reserve spots can move on from Addison if need be. He hasn’t cleared 100 yards in a game all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Week 10 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: After injuring his thumb in Friday’s practice, Addison has officially been ruled out for Sunday’s pivotal NFC North tilt against the Packers. With Jauan Jennings (calf) and T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) also sidelined, Kirk Cousins will be forced to rely on Myles Price, Tai Felton, and Jeshaun and his other receivers behind Justin Jefferson. Jefferson could be in line for a big day in his first game with Cousins since 2023. The Vikings also ruled out QB Kyler Murray, QB Max Brosmer, LB Blake Cashman, and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jordan Addison (thumb) “will have his status determined closer to game time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison injured his thumb in practice on Friday and the team listed him as questionable for today’s game. The team elevated wide receiver Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad yesterday, casting some doubt on Addison’s availability. With Jauan Jennings also out, Tai Felton and Myles Price could be in line for larger roles today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Kevin O’Connell described it as Addison getting “dinged” in practice today. Not ideal. Addison would have been in for a workload bump with T.J. Hockenson out, as it stands it looks like Kirk Cousins will just throw to Justin Jefferson 25 times like it’s 2022 again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison and the rest of the primary Minnesota pass catchers struggled through some of the worst quarterback play you will see all season, with Carson Wentz leading an offense that gained only 126 yards while failing to pick up a single first down through 55 minutes of play. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the struggling veteran late in the fourth quarter and made a few really nice throws, but the team maintains one of the worst quarterback rooms in the league. Fantasy managers are left wishing the team addresses those shortcomings ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline to revive an anemic pass offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 3-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Kyler Murray targeted Addison deep a few times in this one and connected with Addison on a 51-yard deep shot over double coverage in the injury-riddled Lions secondary. It was good to see signs of life from Addison, who entered Week 8 averaging fewer expected fantasy points per game than Cooper Kupp and Kendrick Bourne. The team’s primary downfield threat, Addison’s role in the run-heavy Minnesota offense makes him a boom-bust weekly play. That won’t change in a good matchup in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison also got a carry for three rushing yards. His usage involved designed touches in the shallow area, with the Vikings trying to get him out into space. His utilization dropped in the second half and he did not see many looks downfield. Addison is the clear No. 3 pass-catching option in the Vikings offense, a role that warrants WR4 consideration for Week 8 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison, well-rested coming off his team’s Week 6 bye, is ready to go. The Colts’ defense has played poorly, and they will likely be without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf). Addison can be a volatile producer at times, but he warrants WR3/FLEX treatment this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bo-richter.headline: Vikings placed EDGE Bo Richter on injured reserve with a foot injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bo-richter.analysis: Richter is a capable special teams player. Hopefully, he can return later this year. The Vikings also signed WR Jeshaun Jones to the active roster and WR D’Wayne Eskridge to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bo-richter.headline: Vikings re-signed EDGE Bo Richter to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bo-richter.analysis: Listed as an outside linebacker by Minnesota, Richter sees nearly all of his work on special teams. He logged the 20th-most special teams snaps in the entire league last year and over half of his eight combined tackles came on special teams. Richter appeared in all 17 games last year desite his limtied role on defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) will not play in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Right tackle Jalen Travis is also out with a knee injury. That’s both of Indy’s starting tackles on ice for their date with the Texans. While Houston’s defense has been one of the most disappointing units of the season, this looks like a get-right spot for Demeco Ryans’ squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) was ruled out of Week 10 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Raimann headed to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion in the first half of the Colts’ Week 10 game agains the Dolphins. The Colts promptly ruled him out for the game later in the second quarter. Luke Tenuta comes in at left tackle for Raimann.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said he expects LT Bernhard Raimann (elbow) to “give it a go” in Indianapolis’ Week 17 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: The Colts will likely be forced to throw often against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in Week 17, so whatever Raimann give them could be an upgrade on Luke Tenuta in a game where they’ll need to keep Jacksonville’s pass rushers away from Statue Phil Rivers. It does sound like there’s a chance he will sit or that he’s at a re-aggravation risk based on this wording.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts LT Bernhard Raimann (elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Raimann missed Week 16’s game with the elbow issue. A limited practice to open the week is a good sign for his Week 17 availability. Center Tanor Bortolini is currently in the league’s concussion protocol and did not practice today. He is likely out for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts LT Bernhard Raimann (right elbow) will not play in Week 16 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Raimann got in one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable for Monday’s game. Downgrading him to out this early means he wasn’t that close to suiting up. Raimann will eye a Week 17 return. Luke Tenuta took over for Raimann in Week 15 and could be the next man up once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts T Bernhard Raimann (elbow) did not practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: He hasn’t practiced on either Thursday or Friday ahead of Monday Night’s game against the 49ers. Raimann left Week 15’s game against the Seahawks, giving way to Luke Tenuta at left tackle. Indianapolis worked out several offensive linemen this week. It would not be surprising if Raimann were placed on IR ahead of Monday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts signed OT Bernhard Raimann to a four-year, $100 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: The mega-deal catapults Raimann into the top seven in highest total value contracts amongst active offensive linemen, with the team locking him up through the 2029 season. Raimann received Pro Football Focus’ eighth highest overall grade during the 2024 season, highlighted by one of the top pass blocking grades in the league after allowing just 20 total pressures on 471 pass blocking snaps. The deal includes $60 million in guaranteed money, a staggering mark that stands as the second most in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts LT Bernhard Raimann (knee) will play in Week 13 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Raimann missed two games with the knee issue but is good to go for Week 13. Matt Gonclaves had been starting in his place and could stay in the lineup, only at right tackle. Braden Smith is out for personal reasons this week, leaving an opening for Gonclaves on the right side.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts LT Bernhard Raimann (knee) was limited in practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: He hadn’t practiced since suffering a knee injury on the Wednesday leading up to Week 11. The Colts need all the help they can get on the offensive line with Tanor Bortolini (concussion) likely to miss the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.headline: Colts declared T Bernhard Raimann, TE Will Mallory, DE Isaiah Land, S Darren Hall, WR Anthony Gould, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Indianapolis’ Week 12 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bernhard-r.analysis: Raimann still has not practiced since injuring his knee in practice a couple Wednesdays ago. His Week 13 status is probably up in the air at this point. The rest of this list is the usual inactives for Indianapolis, with three repeats and third quarterback Ehlinger joining Land — who had played in 10 of 11 games so far for the Colts this year despite just one tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills activated WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs last year and began the season on the PUP list. He was active for all 17 games last year and played a mix of offense and special teams. Shavers caught 23 passes for 245 yards and a touchdown in 2025. He will mix in as a depth option for Buffalo over the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills placed Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season after tearing his ACL in the playoffs. No surprise there. Shavers will likely be a late-season reinforcement, if that, in 2026 after coming on strong when the Bills needed receiving help last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills placed WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: After tearing his ACL in early January, Shavers is a good bet to wind up on reserve/PUP at the conclusion of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills coach Sean McDermott said WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the playoffs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers actually played 22 of the team’s snaps in the second half on the torn ACL, which is absurd. The 26-year-old heads to the offseason as unlikely to play early in the season due to how late this knee injury was suffered. He had a career-best 15/245/1 receiving line on 23 targets in the 2025 season, starting nine games and being sporadically useful when the team got annoyed with mercurial second-year receiver Keon Coleman. The Bills will need to rely on Coleman to give them something in the Divisional Round.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) returned to the Bills’ Wild Card Round game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers left in the second quarter with the knee issue. He went to the locker room and the team listed him as questionable to return. Shavers was back on the field coming out of halftime, giving the Bills some extra receiver depth for the final two quarters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) is questionable to return in the Wild Card Round against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers injured his left knee while on punt coverage in the second quarter. He quickly left for the locker room and was listed as questionable to return. With Josh Palmer now on IR, the Bills would be forced to lean on Keon Coleman, Gabe Davis, and Brandin Cooks for wide receiver snaps if Shavers is done for the day. Bills S Jordan Poyer (hamstring) is also questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers caught 2-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Bills’ 13-12, Week 17 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers made a massive 32-yard catch in traffic down the sideline to put the Bills in the red zone late in the third quarter. They would wind up getting stuffed on the one-yard line and turning the ball over on downs, but it was a really nice catch in traffic for the young receiver, who has emerged as a key part of the Bills’ wide receiver corps due to his run blocking and special teams ability. He may be the only receiver, in addition to Khalil Shakir, who feels like a lock to be on the Bills next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills declared WR Keon Coleman, TE Dalton Kincaid, WR Curtis Samuel, DT Phidarian Mathis, OL Chase Lundt and DB Ja’Marcus Ingram inactive for Week 12 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: This will be Coleman’s fourth occasion missing game time due to disciplinary reasons in less than two years in the NFL. Kincaid (hamstring) and Samuel (elbow/neck) are both out due to injury. With Coleman out last week, the Bills relied on a wide receiver rotation including Khalil Shakir, Tyrell Shavers, Gabe Davis, Mecole Hardman, Joshua Palmer and Samuel. Hardman has since been placed on injured reserve. A heavy rotation is still expected against the Texans’ elite pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers caught 4-of-5 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a Week 11 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: With Keon Coleman inactive for disciplinary reasons, it was Shavers who saw the biggest increase in playing time and usage. The 26-year-old did most of his damage on a 43-yard broken play touchdown, where he got behind the defense, but he also caught a few huge 20-plus yard passes throughout the game. We can’t expect this moving forward, but he’s certainly worth an add in deeper formats in case Keon Coleman’s disciplinary punishment lasts beyond one week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills WR Joshua Palmer (knee/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Palmer was forced from play after injuring his knee and ankle while being tackled by a Falcons defender in Week 6. His continued sidelining post-bye indicates he may need another week to rehab the two injuries. Fellow Bills WR Curtis Samuel (ribs) was limited on Wednesday. WR Tyrell Shavers should see increased opportunities this weekend. He is not a reliable FLEX option, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni announced Joe Milton will start in Week 11 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton struggled in the Eagles’ loss to the Giants before their bye. Maybe an extra week of prep will result in a better performance, though we don’t have our hopes up. Milton threw for 169 scoreless yards on 34 attempts. He took seven sacks and lost a fumble. On the bright side, Milton added 64 yards with his legs. That will keep him in the QB2 mix for Superflex purposes this week, but nothing more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton completed 18-of-34 passes for 169 yards in the Eagles’ 19-11, Week 9 loss to the Giants, adding nine carries for 64 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Making the first official regular season start of his career, third-year pro Milton also took a whopping seven sacks for 41 yards and a lost fumble. He never felt Arvell Reese’s pressure when he was obliterated in the second quarter and put the ball on the ground. It was, unsurprisingly, a somewhat ugly day, though Milton was also victimized by drops, including a really awful muff late in the fourth quarter by Makai Lemon. Elijah Mitchell also scrambled a potential game-scoring drive when he failed to get out of bounds to stop the clock. All in all, today would not be surprising to anyone familiar with Milton’s game. He flashed arm strength, running ability, and highly questionable game management skills. Now headed on bye before a Week 11 date against the Steelers, Milton is not a must hold in superflex leagues where other QBs actually find themselves on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Joe Milton will be the Eagles’ starting quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton, 26, has spent time with three different teams since the Patriots drafted him in the 2024 NFL Draft’s sixth round. He is a towering, mobile, cannon-armed quarterback with enticing traits. His erratic play can also be frustrating. Milton can be added in two-quarterback leagues, though his range of potential outcomes in his first start is extremely wide. He replaces Tanner McKee after a three-game starting stint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Eagles signed Joe Milton, formerly of the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton on the Eagles’ 53-man roster. This move comes a day after it was revealed that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot that could sideline him for the next several weeks. Milton will likely serve as the Eagles’ emergency third QB on game days and seems unlikely to see any playing time at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys signed QB Joe Milton to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton initially made the 53-man roster but was let go after the initial wave of waiver claims. He went unclaimed when waivers ran Tuesday and now returns to the Cowboys on the practice squad. With Sam Howell winning the QB2 job, Milton will be QB3 heading into the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton was not claimed on waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He’ll likely catch on with a practice squad in the next day or two, perhaps with the Cowboys again. Milton had initially made the 53-man roster in Dallas but lost his spot when they claimed Emari Demercado off waivers. The 26-year-old has an arm that was made to play quarterback and a decision-making process that was made to play quarterback in 1975.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Sam Howell and Joe Milton will compete for the No. 2 quarterback job this summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: This is mostly just a housekeeping item for dynasty managers, but re-draft managers can still file it away for a potential rainy day in Dallas. Things could change via the 2026 NFL Draft, but these two are set to duke it out for now. Milton flubbed his second-half opportunity in Week 18 last year, perhaps prompting the Cowboys to search for a more reliable No. 2 option. The team certainly has a type. Both Howell and Milton possess very strong arms, which should allow the Cowboys to continue attacking downfield if starting QB Dak Prescott were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton III completed 7-of-13 passes for 73 yards and an interception in the Cowboys’ 34-17, Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: A year after destroying the Bills’ backups in the final game of the 2024-25 season, Milton failed to deliver the same kind of fireworks here. He started the second half for the Cowboys and led five drives, only one of which resulted in points. He’ll finish the season 15-of-24 for 183 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, while adding four rushes for 45 yards. He will return as Dak Prescott’s backup in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-31 passes for 188 yards and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 44-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He was benched with eight minutes left in the game and Dallas down by 27 points, Joe Milton led a touchdown drive with things out of hand. Both of Prescott’s picks were pretty weird, one of them by dropping edge player Deondrea Tillman. He was hit hard today, taking 14 pressures in 38 dropbacks per PFF. Obviously, this wasn’t the QB1 game you were promised — it didn’t look like the Cowboys had a real answer for their easy underneath stuff getting poached. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 9 against the Cardinals and should remain on the QB1 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 31-of-40 passes for 251 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 31-14 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Testing the limits of what an all-Jake Ferguson offense could deliver to the world, one of Prescott’s picks deflected off George Pickens’ hands, and the other got him benched for Joe Milton in a 17-point deficit the Cowboys were obviously not overcoming. (Milton went 3-of-5 for 41 yards and a pick of his own.) The pass offense lost a lot of oomph without Lamb, and now Prescott gets to deal with an absolutely livid Packers front seven on Sunday night next week. If Lamb misses Week 4, it would be hard to fire up Prescott as more than a borderline QB1. The Dallas defense has forced plenty of passing situations for the Cowboys, as Prescott has 126 pass attempts in three games, but it would be a tough sell against a great defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said offensive coordinator Frank Reich would continue calling plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Glenn was asked about whether he had considered switching play callers after the Jets went nine straight quarters without a touchdown. “I have a lot of confidence in Frank,” Glenn said. Since Week 7, the Jets rank 19th in EPA per play and 11th in offensive success rate. They have a league-low 38 percent red zone touchdown rate on the season. This week they play an improving Chargers defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini said he “would be a little surprised” if the Jets draft Alabama QB Ty Simpson with the No. 16 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft “because they have so many other needs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Cimini also believes the Jets do not feel “pressured” to draft a quarterback in 2026 because they have three first-round picks in 2027. That said, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, general manager Darren Mougey, OC Frank Reich and QB coach Bill Musgrave had dinner with Simpson last night and hosted him for a private workout today. The Jets hold the second, 16th, 33rd and 44th picks in this year’s draft. We certainly agree that the Jets have many needs, but finding a starting quarterback tops the list. Simpson could still end up in a Jets uniform next month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: Jets hired former Panthers head coach Frank Reich as their offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Reich was Stanford’s interim head coach last year in what felt almost like a favor to former quarterback Andrew Luck. Now he finds himself in a different unenviable position with the Jets. Breece Hall is a free agent. There is no real hope of grabbing a franchise quarterback in the draft or finding one in free agency, and the only quarterbacks the team have under contract for 2026 that started games are Justin Fields and Brady Cook. Reich will have to rise well above his station to get this offense to any semblance of “average” in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: Jets announced they completed an in-person interview with former Panthers head coach Frank Reich for their offensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: The Jets completed an in-person interview with Reich, indicating he is a finalist for the team’s offensive coordinator role. A former head coach of the Panthers and Colts, Reich was Stanford’s interim head coach briefly in 2025. should he join Aaron Glenn’s staff, Reich would be the offensive play-caller and a senior leader of the coaching staff. Rumors have had Reich attached to the job and a hire could be completed soon, pending other interviews.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: Jets interviewed former Panthers head coach Frank Reich for their offensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Reich has been heavily rumored to take over as the Jets’ offensive play-caller since the team let go of offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand. The 64-year-old was head coach of the Colts for five seasons, followed by one season at the helm of the Panthers, making history as the first head coach to be fired midseason in back-to-back seasons. He was Stanford’s interim head coach for a bit in 2025 and is currently a senior advisor for the program. While Reich looks to be the favorite, the Jets also interviewed former Chargers OC Greg Roman, Dolphins quarterbacks coach Darrell Bevell, Bills quarterbacks coach Ronald Curry, and Cowboys tight ends coach Lunda Wells for their offensive coordinator vacancy. A decision could be expected soon, though given the tumultuous nature of Aaron Glenn’s head coaching tenure, we would not be surprised if the process is lengthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: Jets fired OC Tanner Engstrand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Well, it really made no sense to keep Engstrand and find a new playcaller, so we guess from that point of view it makes sense. Engstrand’s run game was versatile and varied and he probably deserves a role as someone’s run game coordinator at the very worst next year — perhaps he’ll head back to Detroit. The Jets will do whatever it is the Jets do from here, which from the looks of their defensive coordinator search probably means they’ll wind up paralyzed by overanalyzing 10 different candidates. Frank Reich has been the rumored playcaller replacement for the Jets in recent days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: SNYTV’s Connor Hughes reports the Jets could hire former Panther head coach Frank Reich as the team’s offensive play caller.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Reich, if he’s hired by the Jets, is expected to call plays for the team’s offense, per Hughes. That would mean current offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand would be demoted following a 2025 season in which the talent-bare Jets offense had the NFL’s fourth lowest EPA per play and third lowest success rate. Hughes said Engstrand could maintain his OC title. Reich, a former NFL quarterback, served as offensive coordinator for the Chargers and Eagles before becoming the Colts’ head coach and then the Panthers’ head coach. Both head coaching tenures proved disastrous.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports Jets OC Tanner Engstrand is not expected to call plays in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: An offensive coordinator not calling plays for a defensive-minded head coach certainly evokes a strong whiff of “what would you say you do here?” Hughes added that former Colts and Panthers HC Frank Reich is “among the names” he’s heard linked to the Jets. This is certainly an out-of-left-field development as the Jets’ run game was mostly praised last year despite what looked to be a pretty elementary passing game. Perhaps they’re trying to find someone who can assist with the passing part.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: NFL Insider Josina Anderson reports the Panthers are expected to be interested in Lions OC Ben Johnson for head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Frank Reich was recently fired as head coach of the Panthers, who are 1-10 after drafting QB Bryce Young first overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson received head coaching interest from the Panthers last off-season, but had declined an interview and chose to stay in Detroit. Reich, who was hired by the Panthers instead, is now out after 11 games and the 37-year-old Johnson is expected to receive interest for the Panthers’ head coaching vacancy again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Panthers have fired HC Frank Reich.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/frank-reic.analysis: Heading into Week 11, FOX’s Jay Glazer reported Reich was on the “hottest seat in the league.” A Week 12 loss to the Titans was likely the boiling point for the front office and owner David Tepper, who was reportedly heard shouting expletives while leaving the locker room. We may not ever fully know who was responsible for the disaster that has unfolded in Carolina this season, but No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young’s struggles have been well documented and amplified by the fact that No. 2 overall pick C.J. Stroud has thrived early with the Texans. Rumors are Stroud was the preferred pick over Young by Reich and the staff, but the selection of Young came directly from Tepper. Still, Carolina’s issues extend beyond their rookie quarterback. The Panthers are among the worst pass-blocking units in the league and boast a defense that’s allowing the third-most points per game (26.5). Special teams coordinator Chris Tabor is expected to take over as interim head coach for the remainder of the season, with the Panthers expected to make a run at Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson in the offseason. A premium head coaching candidate could be tough to come by with the Panthers not having a first round pick in 2024, and Tepper now moving on to his third head coach in four seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL insider Dianna Russini reports Brandon Aiyuk passed the 49ers’ physical.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: “He’s 100% healthy right now, in shape, and working out full force,” Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk’s agent, told Russini. Passing the team’s physical was a key step in the two sides parting ways after years of conflict. Aiyuk reportedly hopes to sign with another team once the 49ers release him. Whether that happens in the coming weeks is anyone’s guess. Aiyuk had been linked to the Commanders in the summer before a series of questionable social media posts from Aiyuk squelched those rumors.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, he owes th e 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture. The two sides met today, but evidently, things were not resolved. The saga continues. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers “roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture,” which could delay his return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Pelissero calls this a “potential complication in [Aiyuk’s] efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” While it’s possible both sides reach a deal for Aiyuk to pay back that money, which would make this a non-issue, Pelissero said this could also end up going to arbitration, which may delay things. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers’ facilities today, so we could have our answer in the next few hours about when this situation is resolved and Aiyuk has been granted his release. Aiyuk recently hired Drew Rosenhaus with the hopes of being reinstated into the league and with a new team soon. The 28-year-old last played in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Brandon Aiyuk submitted paperwork to the NFL for his reinstatement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed the development on Wednesday, and said Aiyuk would report to the 49ers on Friday. That could expedite his release from the team so he could seek employment with another, presumably wideout-needy NFL team. Aiyuk’s erratic behavior over the past year and questions about his conditioning could prevent some teams from pursuing him. “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said. He had been closely linked to the Commanders before a series of online meltdowns in the offseason. The Rams could be in the market for Aiyuk with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined indefinitely. Aiyuk is still unlikely to have any fantasy value this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk “is close to hiring new representatives in an effort to get back to the NFL and on a team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: An entire offseason spent creating goofy Instagram videos in hopes of willing himself onto the Commanders’ roster didn’t go as Aiyuk had hoped. Instead, the 28-year-old receiver, who last played a snap in 2024, remains under contract with the 49ers after failing to apply for reinstatement, which remains the first step he would need to take if he hopes to be made available to other teams. The 49ers put a “left squad designation” on Aiyuk back in July, meaning while he remains under contract with the team, he does not count against the team’s 53-man roster. It seems unlikely he will remain with the Niners if/when he applies for reinstatement, meaning the team will either have to release him or find a trade suitor for him before this month’s deadline. It would be surprising if Aiyuk played a snap for any team in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Nick Wagoner reports that 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson has been initially diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain “that could cost him extended time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Although Robinson will apparently undergo more testing, the “initial diagnosis” aspect seems like a formality at this point. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he is “sure” the team will have to sign a wide receiver, “whether it’s a practice squad or to the roster.” For those curious, Shanahan was asked whether there was any chance of bringing back WR Brandon Aiyuk. Per Wagoner, Shanahan responded simply, “No.” That’s that. Expect Robinson to miss time, likely increasing WR Deebo Samuel’s involvement. No. 1 WR Mike Evans suffered a hip injury, though Shanahan did not seem to think it was serious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Stefon Diggs “remains a player of interest” for the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Perhaps more notable is that Keim pointed out “other free agents don’t appear to be on their radar,” with Brandon Aiyuk presumably the “other” in this scenario. Diggs has long been linked to the Commanders as a potential fit, and ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported last week that “Washington is intriguing” to Diggs, so there’s a good chance some mutual interest exists. The Commanders’ receiver room is headlined by Terry McLaurin, but behind him is an unproven group in Jaylin Lane, Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, and rookie Antonio Williams. It feels like only a matter of time before the Commanders eventually make a move to upgrade their receiving corps, and Diggs would provide a solid option opposite McLaurin after going for 85-1,013-4 with the Patriots last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said Brandon Aiyuk “is on a left squad designation” as the team opens training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: For those who continue to follow the Niners/Aiyuk saga, this is no surprise. Aiyuk’s designation means he does not count against the 49ers’ 90-man roster for camp, and the designation requires him to apply to the NFL for reinstatement before he can be released or traded. Aiyuk has been active on his Instagram account, and appears to be trying to manifest a move to the Commanders to play with long-time friend and former college teammate Jayden Daniels, but the ball is ultimately in his court to take the steps necessary for anything to be facilitated. It was reported earlier this month by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler that he “doesn’t think” the Commanders would be interested in Aiyuk if he were to come available. Aiyuk last played in 2024, posting a 25-374-0 line in seven games before suffering a torn ACL in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season.
