Losing Hutchinson would make this team even more reliant on explosive offensive performances than it already is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is expected to be out “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: Hutchinson injured his knee while celebrating a sack in the first quarter of Detroit’s Week 10 win over the Patriots. He jumped into the air and his right knee buckled as he landed. He will undergo more testing, but it looks like the Lions will be without their top pass-rusher for a while. Hutchinson has six sacks in nine games this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: Hutchinson jumped in the air to celebrate a sack in the first quarter. His right knee buckled when he landed and the star pass-rusher stayed on the field for a while. He was eventually able to walk off under his own power but headed straight into the locker room. Hutchinson would be a massive loss for a Detroit defense that hasn’t played particularly well this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (elbow) is not on Detroit’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: Good thing, too, because the entire rest of the Lions defense found their way on to this report. Terrion Arnold (concussion), Kerby Joseph (knee) and Josh Paschal (back) were all ruled out. D.J. Reed (hamstring) and Amik Robertson (hamstring) are questionable. Both A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith should see slight matchup uggrades given the CB injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (elbow) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: Hutchinson leads the NFL with 57 quarterback pressures, and his eight sacks tie for seventh, so an absence against the Eagles this weekend would be significant. The Lions’ star defensive lineman still has time to get right, but this is one worth watching. Lions EDGE Al-Quadin Muhammad is second on the team with just 37 quarterback pressures.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: Lions signed EDGE Aidan Hutchinson to a four-year contract extension worth $180 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: The mega-deal includes $141 million in guarantees, according to NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero. It’s the most guaranteed money ever for a non-quarterback in the NFL. Hutchinson, 25, who’s now signed with Detroit through 2030, has been stellar in 2025, recording six sacks and forcing four fumbles through seven games. He has 34.5 sacks in 46 NFL games since entering the league in 2022. Pro Football Focus grades Hutchinson as the league’s second best pass rusher behind Micah Parsons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson “looks destined for a new deal” that will keep him in Detroit.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-hutc.analysis: Fowler is unconvinced that Hutchinson will beat the four-year, $186 million deal signed by Packers EDGE Micah Parsons, but it should be plenty lucrative and on par with “quarterback money.” The Lions’ 25-year-old pass rusher currently ties for a positional high in quarterback pressures (31) and ties for second in sacks (six). The Lions face off against the Chiefs in Week 6’s Sunday Night Football game on NBC, and Chiefs EDGE George Karlaftis is the player with whom Hutchinson is tied in the former category. Karlaftis signed a four-year, $93 million extension through 2030 in July.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku was not targeted in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku briefly saw his role in the offense grow after fellow tight end Oronde Gadsden departed in the first quarter with an eye injury. Gadsden would return in the second half after the team deemed him questionable earlier, shifting Njoku back to a complimentary role behind Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. Njoku’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy score comes in Week 11 against the Jets, although fantasy managers are better off leaving him on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers activated TE David Njoku from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku will try to fight for fantasy relevancy going forward, but there’s no need to pretend he has it at the moment with all three Chargers tight ends healthy. They also activated LB Denzel Perryman off the same list and sent G/T Branson Taylor to injured reserve in their place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is still within his 21-day practice window and has remained limited for five straight practices. He could end up playing on Monday night, but he does not need to be rostered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is not worth rostering whenever he officially returns to the active roster, but he theoretically can contribute offensively. He will likely be a mildly productive member of the Chargers’ three-player tight end rotation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers did not activate David Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku entered the contest listed as doubtful, although he practiced in a limited capacity all week. He might be able to return next week, but he does not need to be added in 12-team leagues. The Chargers declared LG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Kendall Williamson (calf), CB Deane Leonard (concussion), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and WR Theo Wease inactive for Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku’s return is probably a good thing for the offense as a whole, but the Chargers’ tight end rotation makes for a fantasy-unfriendly situation. Njoku does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku had his practice window opened this week, giving the Chargers 21 days to activate him off injured reserve. He has been out since Week 3 and is now nearing a return, getting in limited work with a fibula injury on Wednesday. WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) was a DNP on Wednesday. Neither Njoku nor Thompson need to be on fantasy rosters just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Jim Harbaugh said the team will open the 21-day practice window for David Njoku this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku has been on the shelf since being placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 3, with the potential to return following five missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. The team will have 21 days to activate him from short-term injured reserve, meaning Njoku is not guaranteed to be activated in time for Week 9 against the Texans. Fantasy managers that have held Njoku through his time on injured reserve can continue patiently waiting for his return while those in shallower leagues can consider adding him from waivers before he is activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 3-of-5 targets for 42 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman saw his route structure altered with the change at quarterback, running a high percentage of his routes over the middle of the field. He was able to run free in the intermediate areas against the heavy zone coverage rates of the Chargers for much of the game, with Brissett instead targeting tight end Mark Andrews and alpha wide receiver Zay Flowers at elevated rates. Bateman remains a shaky Flex play ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman is firmly on track to play in the Ravens’ Monday Night Football game against the Chargers. Bateman will provide new QB Jacoby Brissett with a downfield option, but the veteran wide receiver is almost entirely reliant in ripping off one or two big plays, which has proven to be a difficult proposition for him on a weekly basis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman left the Ravens’ Week 6 game against the Browns and did not return, though head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was going to be fine. Expect the team to manage his reps in practice this week with an eye on getting him ready for Sunday. Bateman has made a handful of splash plays this year, but his production is low-volume and high-variance. He will be a low-end FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said there’s optimism that Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will “be fine.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Sounds like another week of managed reps in practice is ahead for Bateman, but he’ll likely have a reasonable chance to suit up in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will not return in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We’re not quite sure when this injury occurred, but Bateman was dealing with a shoulder injury throughout the week. He was removed from the final injury report on Friday. Bateman’s day ends without a reception on one target.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman was a surprise DNP on Thursday, but got in a full session today. He remains an uninspiring FLEX option against the Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane handily led the team with 11 targets but struggled through inconsistent play, the most glaring of which came on a drop on a routine target inside the five. It won’t be often that lane leads the team in targets while playing alongside Zay Flowers and the recent resurgence of tight end Mark Andrews, the latter of whom should benefit greatly from the historically high tight end target rate from new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Lane is an upside Flex ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught his lone target for 13 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane hauled in a 13-yard reception from Joe Fagnano in the second quarter after Fagnano came in to replace Tyler Huntley (toe). Lane has yet to live up to the training camp hype he drew all offseason and seems even less likely to hit his stride with Lamar Jackson’s (thumb) in jeopardy. Fantasy managers stashing Lane in deeper leagues can move to drop him at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane had a relatively forgettable day through the air, but just missed finding the end zone on a short pass from Tyler Huntley in the second quarter. The rookie receiver ran 30 routes, which were second only to Zay Flowers, but he’s caught just seven passes for 65 scoreless yards in his two games since returning from injury. Lane’s involvement in the offense is encouraging, but there’s not enough here to warrant starting him in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 4-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane was immediately involved in the offense after missing the previous four weeks with a wrist injury. The rookie third-rounder caught two of his four passes on the Ravens’ opening drive that ended with a short touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and ran 22 routes on the day. Zay Flowers (34) and Devontez Walker (26) both ran more routes than Lane on the afternoon, but Lane has been targeted on 21.1 percent of his routes in limited action this season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to start him in Week 7 against the Bengals, but the early volume is encouraging for a player who was hyped up throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Lane has “a shot” to face the Browns in Week 6. His full participation furthers that notion. The talented rookie drew rave reports all summer before suffering an unfortunate wrist fracture in Week 1. While he makes for a dicey FLEX if Tyler Huntley is under center, Lane should at least be safely stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has “a shot” to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lane, who injured his wrist in the season opener against the Colts, will return to practice this week and could suit up this weekend against the Browns. Lane had impressed Ravens coaches and beat writers through training camp and in Week 1 he caught one of three targets for 11 yards before exiting with the wrist injury. Lane’s return to the Baltimore lineup could limit snaps and routes for Rashod Bateman Devontez Walker. Lane should be picked up in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane on injured reserve with a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane underwent surgery to address a fracture in his wrist and will now miss at least four games on short-term injured reserve. He will be eligible to return in Week 6. Ravens No. 1 WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is also nursing an injury. Theoretically, fellow rookie WR Elijah Sarratt should be active in Week 2 against the Saints, though it is unclear if he would have a meaningful role if Flowers plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-7 targets for 74 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers carried only two receptions on two targets into the fourth quarter as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching fire in the final frame before losing a costly fumble on the team’s penultimate possession with under three minutes remaining in a three-point game. Even so, it was a solid rebound effort after Flowers had struggled mightily with poor quarterback play the previous weeks, with veteran Jacoby Brissett providing enough stability for Flowers to remain an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 0-of-5 targets in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Lamar Jackson exited after one play due to a thumb injury. Midway through the second quarter, backup Tyler Huntley left the game with a toe injury, forcing Flowers into a nightmare situation with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center. Flowers saw four of his five targets come from Fagnano but was unable to convert any of them into catches, even if they were within his range to do so. With the Ravens now set to face the Jaguars on a short week, and Fagnano possibly set to make his first career start, Flowers needs to be adjusted down to WR3 rankings. With a full week to install a game plan with Fagnano, it’s fair to assume he’ll offer more than the donut we saw here today, but the Ravens’ offense, which was already struggling with Huntley under center, is unlikely to fare any better with Fagnano.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers’ biggest play of the day came on the Ravens’ opening drive. The star receiver turned a screen pass on third-and-nine upfield for a 48-yard touchdown to give the Ravens an early lead on what would be their only touchdown drive of the day. Despite another low-scoring day for the Ravens’ offense, Flowers continues to be one of the most profitable wide receivers in fantasy. He’s averaged over 10 targets per game in three starts by Tyler Huntley and has caught six or more passes in his last four games. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) expected back for Week 8’s game against the Bills, things are looking up for Flowers and the Ravens’ offense as a whole. The good news for Flowers’ managers, however, is that he’s a must-start regardless of who is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-11 targets for 66 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers has yet to find the end zone in back-to-back games with Tyler Huntley under center, but the 10 targets per game he has averaged over that span is still encouraging. Flowers led the Ravens in targets by a wide margin in this week’s loss, with his biggest play coming on a 31-yard reception in the third quarter. Scoring opportunities were scarce in this one, as the Ravens managed just 10 points on their first two drives and were shut out for the rest of the game. Flowers will be in the WR1 conversation next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) makes the start, but would be more of a WR2 if Huntley gets the nod for a third straight week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers played through a foot injury last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards and rushing once for 13 yards. This injury could be related, but we really don’t know. Flowers’ productivity took a hit with Tyler Huntley running the offense last week. Huntley is currently in line to start again, though Lamar Jackson’s (ankle) status is still up in the air. If the toe injury limits Flowers, that further complicates things, but he still must be started if active. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 13 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was largely confined to short area work with Tyler Huntley under center and also saw a 26-yard reception erased from his ledger due to a 29-yard pass interference penalty on the play. It was a weird situation in which the penalty yardage was greater than his reception. Fantasy managers might be forced to continue waiting on the return of Lamar Jackson after it was reported this week that the All Pro starter could be forced to miss another week. Flowers is a locked-in WR2 against the Browns in Week 6 with Huntley under center and an elite WR1 should Jackson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was limited in practice throughout the week but never appeared at risk of missing Sunday night’s game. The bigger issue for him will be the absence of Lamar Jackson. Flowers has been the most efficient receiver in the league on a per-route basis this year. That will come back to Earth sans Jackson, but he remains on the WR1/2 border, even with Tyler Huntley under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: The presence of Jacoby Brissett and his elevated tight end target rate benefited Andrews, leading to a season-high 82 receiving yards on eight receptions. Andrews suddenly has the profile of a back end TE1 after nine weeks of poor performances and gets a solid matchup against the reeling Panthers in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews has been playing through the hand injury for a few weeks without any issues. He logged three full practices this week. With Joe Fagnano making his first career start for the Ravens tomorrow, we wouldn’t advise playing any Ravens outside of Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was listed as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: That keeps the veteran tight end on track to suit up in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Andrews has struggled to return usable fantasy weeks throughout his age-31 season, with the team now down to their third, potentially fourth, quarterback for Thursday’s game. he can safely be left on fantasy benches on the short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was another day at the office for Andrews, who has now gone six straight games with 28 or fewer receiving yards. Any hope that he might see a slight increase in production with Lamar Jackson back under center can be put aside after Jackson suffered a severe injury to his throwing hand that will require surgery and force him to go on injured reserve. Andrews isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 9 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was business as usual for Andrews, who can be consistently relied on for a solid 20-yard game. Andrews has gone for 28 or fewer yards in five straight games and will not be on the fantasy radar in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews ran 11 more routes than rookie tight end Josh Cuevas but was out-targeted by Cuevas 5-to-3. Andrews continues to underwhelm in the passing game and has now failed to surpass 28 yards in four straight games. He can be left on waivers ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews practiced in full with the hand injury last week before posting a 5/27/1 receiving line. He should be good to go again this week, though he is a low-end TE1, with backup QB Tyler Huntley likely starting in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews continues to see most of his work come in the short area of the field. He’s gone for less than 30 yards in each of his last two games, but did manage to haul in a three-yard score in the second quarter of Sunday’s win for his first touchdown of 2026. Lamar Jackson also missed Andrews in the end zone on a high throw earlier in the game, but he remains a very touchdown-dependent option as far as fantasy is concerned. He’s a boom-or-bust play in Week 5 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers, adding 10 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: It was the fifth straight game in which Henry was held to 58 yards on the ground or fewer, all five of which were Baltimore losses. Henry salvaged an otherwise poor showing with two rushing scores and a season-high five receptions, marking his 35th career game with multiple touchdowns in the loss. Now playing with Jacoby Brissett under center, Henry has fallen to a middling RB2 in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a more enticing matchup against the Panthers in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens aren’t expected to trade RB Derrick Henry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Citing league sources, Schefter says the Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him. While speculation about a trade is understandable given Baltimore’s injuries at the quarterback position, the Ravens are said to have never even considered it, according to Schefter. With the newly acquired Jacoby Brissett likely to be under center in Week 10 against the Chargers, Henry will be in the RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as to call numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Playing more than half of the game with emergency QB Joe Fagnano under center didn’t do much to help Henry or the Ravens’ offense. Fortunately, after being gifted a short field in the first quarter following an interception by Josh Allen, Henry was able to convert the opportunity into a two-yard rushing touchdown two plays later. It was Henry’s first rushing touchdown since Week 4, but he’s shaping up to be little more than a volume-based RB2 in Week 9 against the Jaguars if Fagnano is forced to start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 45 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals, adding one reception for four additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry has rushed 34 times for 93 scoreless yards in his last two games, and has seen 10 of those carries go for zero yards or a loss. Injuries to the Ravens’ offensive line continue to plague the running game, and the loss of rookie RG Vega Ioane (knee) in the first quarter didn’t do anything to help the Ravens’ rushing woes. Henry has just one touchdown in the three starts by Tyler Huntley and has just six carries inside his opponents’ 10-yard line over that span. Baltimore’s sluggish offense under Huntley hasn’t boded well for Henry’s fantasy upside, but with Lamar Jackson (ankle) expected back for Week 8’s game against the Bills, Henry should be in line for more scoring opportunities. He will be a fringe RB1 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 58 scoreless yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry continues to struggle on the ground, as this marks the third time in four games that he has been held under 4.0 YPC. In fairness to the Big Dog, he averaged less than one yard before contact per attempt in this one, and six of his 17 rush attempts went for no gain or a loss of yards. Henry totaled 28 rushing yards on his first two carries on a drive that eventually ended with a Ravens touchdown, but yards were hard to come by the rest of the way. He’s now gone two-straight weeks without a rushing touchdown, but will hopefully be in better position to score next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is back under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry also tacked on a successful two-point conversion to further pad his counting stats. The King erupted for 59 yards in the first half before being largely held in check for the final two quarters with the Ravens playing from behind. He would watch from the sidelines for the duration of the team’s final possession in the two-minute drill but came on the field to tie the game with a two-point conversion on a direct snap. The Falcons were no match for Henry in the extra frame, with the bruising back tacking on an additional 32 yards on the ground on the team’s lone overtime possession. Henry continues to turn back the clock while notching his eighth touchdown in five appearances, having scored in every game to start the season. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans, adding two receptions for six additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: This week marks the second straight game in which Henry averaged less than 4.0 YPC. Fortunately for fantasy managers, he did manage to find the end zone on a five-yard score on the Ravens’ first drive and was relied on heavily in the second half when Lamar Jackson exited the game with an ankle injury. This wasn’t a flashy game for Henry, who was held to three or fewer yards on 16 of his 23 rush attempts. That said, he continues to be the only Ravens RB of note and remains in the RB1 mix for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at the production Henry provided their lineups in Sunday’s win over the Cowboys, but the Big Dog was largely bottled up against a suddenly stingy defensive front. Henry’s longest run came on a 29-yard burst in the third quarter that helped set up a Chris Moore receiving touchdown, but that run also accounted for 32.6 percent of Henry’s yards on the ground. He averaged a very underwhelming 2.4 YPC on his other 25 carries on the day and was tackled for a three-yard loss on a fourth-and-goal from the Cowboys’ one-yard line. The good news is Henry remains the unquestioned bell cow in the Ravens’ backfield, and he has a Week 4 revenge game against the Titans on tap. He’ll be a must start RB1 in what should be a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints, adding three receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry didn’t provide his signature explosive plays in this one, with his longest carry of the afternoon coming on an eight-yard run. On the Ravens’ second drive of the game, Henry turned seven touches into 45 yards from scrimmage, thanks in part to a screen pass he took for 19 yards, and capped the drive with a one-yard score to give the Ravens an early 7-0 lead. He averaged a respectable 4.3 YPC on the day, but the Saints were able to hold Henry in check for much of the afternoon. That said, fantasy managers won’t be mad at the production. He gets a plus matchup next week on the road against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 33-of-49 passes for 340 yards and one interception in the Ravens’ 23-20, Week 10 loss to the Chargers, adding two yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett and the Ravens played from behind throughout against the only team without a win through the first nine weeks of the 2026 season, but the veteran’s performance through the air kept the team within striking distance late into the fourth quarter. The defense did its job and gave the ball back to the Ravens with under three minutes remaining and Brissett had the team driving the field down by three before a Zay Flowers fumble cost them the game. For his part, Brissett settled into the game in the second quarter after three straight three-and-out possessions, ultimately falling just short in the defeat. Brissett will remain the starter under center for the next 6-10 weeks as Lamar Jackson recovers from surgery on his thumb, with his next opportunity to return a viable fantasy outing coming in Week 11 against the Panthers in what is a must-win game for the Ravens, losers of five straight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter released a statement saying Lamar Jackson (thumb) will be out for the next 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: On the short end of this timeline, Jackson could return in Week 16 against the Browns. On the long end, Jackson would be looking at returning around the Wild Card or Divisional Round of the playoffs if the Ravens make the postseason. This timeline closely aligns with the 6-9 week absence NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier in the week. If this isn’t a season-ender for Lamar, it will be close, and how the Ravens perform over the next several weeks with Jacoby Brissett under center will likely determine whether the Ravens dress him for the final few weeks of the season, even if he is ready to go. Minter said that Jackson is “doing well” after suffering his injury in Week 8 against the Bills, which is encouraging, but we’re a long way from knowing if a return for Jackson is truly in the cards. The 4-5 Ravens have lost their last four games but hope to turn things around on Monday night when they play host to the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he expects Jacoby Brissett to start in Week 10 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: The Ravens wasted little time in trading for Brissett after he lost his starting job with the Cardinals. The 33-year-old journeyman is familiar with Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork and was acquired in part because the team believed he could quickly become the starter. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in his eight games with the Cardinals this season, and will now look to save the Ravens’ season after they fell to 4-5 last week. With Lamar Jackson (finger) hoping to come back in the next six to nine weeks, if Baltimore can string together a few wins, it’s possible he will be back in time for the playoffs should they make the postseason. Brissett being under center should also provide some stability to Zay Flowers’ and Derrick Henry’s fantasy stocks after a rough few weeks sans Lamar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals in a deal that is expected to be completed this weekend.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Schefter adds that this trade will not be completed in time for Brissett to play in Week 9’s Thursday Night Football game for the Ravens, but he will make his debut in Week 10 against the Chargers. Brissett’s impending arrival in Baltimore immediately stabilizes the pass-catching corps’ fantasy value. The trade compensation has not yet been revealed, but we expect to know more soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett will serve as the Cardinals’ emergency QB3 in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: After holding out part of the offseason for a new deal that was fitting for a starting QB in the league, Brissett now finds himself as the QB3 of the Cardinals entering Week 9. There’s a good chance this is the end of the road for Brissett as far as his time with the Cardinals is concerned, as a handful of dire QB situations around the league could warrant a trade to a contender who is looking to upgrade at QB before the trade deadline. Brissett was solid last season for a three-win Cardinals team, throwing for 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in 12 starts. He currently sports a 1,719-10-7 line this season but has struggled in his last three starts, throwing just one touchdown to two interceptions. With Brissett being demoted to QB3, rookie Carson Beck will be elevated to QB2 on game days, and draws ever closer to making his first career start at some point in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 10-of-23 passes for 119 yards and an interception before being benched for Gardner Minshew in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: He took four sacks, including back-to-back sacks to kill a third-quarter drive, before being replaced. Brissett hasn’t necessarily played this poorly all season, but we’d been getting plenty of questions at press conferences about if he’d remain the starter so we’re ultimately unsurprised by this move. Minshew took over and we assume Carson Beck will also be mentioned ahead of Week 9. Full Mike LaFleur press conference coverage to come, naturally.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ 30-16, Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett struggled to get the deep ball going in this game and was largely stuck dinking and dunking his way down the field. He averaged a measly 5.7 yards per attempt while completing 56.3 percent of his passes. Brissett hasn’t averaged seven yards per attempt in a game since Week 1. Even worse is the fact that he’s taking bone-crushing hits more than ever. Brissett injured his non-throwing hand while taking a sack late in the second quarter but never missed any time with the issue. We expect him to make an appearance on the injury report this week. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters after the game that Brissett remains the starter, meaning he’ll take on a terrible Dallas defense next week. He will be a priority streamer for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-35 passes for 218 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ 18-16, Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett threw an interception to Rams S Quentin Lake while targeting Trey McBride on the Cardinals’ third play from scrimmage but managed to play mistake-free and touchdown-free football from there on out. Brissett took zero sacks for the first time this season and linked up with four different players for explosive gains. That said, the box score results obviously disappoint. Brissett nearly linked up with Michael Wilson for a 36-yard touchdown on the Cardinals’ seventh drive, but the ball glanced off Wilson’s fingertips as he dove for it in the end zone. The drive ultimately resulted in a field goal, as did five others. Brissett will be a high-end QB2 against the Broncos in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught his only target for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston was a complete afterthought in a game quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the team playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. Fellow receiver Tre’ Harris handily led the team with five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards, with no other pass catcher seeing more than three looks, catching more than two passes, or going for more than 16 yards. Johnston is completely off the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-4 targets for 58 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding one rush for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: If you didn’t start Johnston, we can’t blame you. It’s been a rough go. Johnston deserves credit for his long score. He caught a pass on a slant route and took off downfield via a post pattern, churning his legs through a shoestring tackle attempt. It’s the type of play we expected Johnston to be featured on in OC Mike McDaniel’s offense, rather than the deep routes he is frequently stuck running. Johnston also earned an end zone target, but was unable to secure it. With Justin Herbert (left hand) ailing, Johnston is tough to trust as a FLEX against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnston, who did his work underneath in this one. He now has one game this season with more than two receptions in a Chargers offense that can be described as utterly dysfunctional on every level. Johnston should not be rostered in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston (chest) will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh added. Johnston practiced on both Thursday and Friday so he likely has the best chance of being active among Los Angeles’ main three wideouts. Unfortunately this passing game is in rough shape, and even a higher volume, healthy load probably wouldn’t get Johnston above the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris’ five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards were all team highs on a night quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the Chargers playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. The highlight of the game on either side was Harris’ 31-yard reception in the first quarter, with the veteran receiver shaking free on a deep crosser and getting his hand under the ball on a sliding catch. Fantasy managers will want to track the status of Ladd McConkey entering a Week 11 meeting with the Jets as a return to action could send Harris back to the nether realm as far as fantasy value is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team in targets last week, but somehow managed just six yards on three catches. With Ladd McConkey (back) ailing, Harris could lead the team in targets again. He would only be a boom-bust FLEX in this case, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team with seven targets last week, catching just three of them for six yards. Although he is not fantasy-relevant on his own, his presence theoretically helps Justin Herbert and Harris is on track to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 3-of-7 targets for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Being this inefficient ain’t easy. Trainers examined Harris’ lower left leg after an eighth-drive incompletion in which Harris twisted as he unsuccessfully tried to high-point a pass and came down hard on his feet. Harris does not need to be in fantasy football lineups against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was the team’s WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, as usual. When McConkey is healthy, Harris operates as a part-time player without much of a fantasy floor. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of LA’s Week 9 game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was labeled week-to-week early in Week 6 and was unable to face the Chiefs that weekend. After resting and rehabbing through the Chargers’ Week 7 bye, Harris has a chance to resume playing in Week 8. We expect to see him listed as a limited participant, but an update will be provided if he practices in full. Brenen Thompson (quad) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is “more of a week-to-week [thing].”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris will probably have a real chance to play in Week 8, after the Chargers’ Week 7 bye. He thudded to a 16-yard outing in his big chance last week with Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey out and doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered if you’re in a bye week crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 12-of-18 passes for 129 yards in the Chargers’ 23-20, Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding 51 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was not called on often after the Chargers jumped out to a 10-point lead in the first quarter, attempting under 30 passes for the fifth time this season. Two key turnovers were the difference in this one, the first a deflected pass off a Los Angeles defender that fell into the arms of linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips and the second a fourth quarter fumble recovery after Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers with under three minutes to play. Herbert padded his counting stats with a 22-yard touchdown run on the team’s first possession but it still wasn’t enough for the veteran signal caller to return his first QB1 week of the season. Herbert remains a fantasy dud ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Chargers “immediately shut down all inquiries” for Justin Herbert at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schultz reports the Vikings called on Herbert, but the Chargers had no interest in moving on. It’s hard to understand what Herbert’s market value would have been — this has been one of the most disgusting outlier seasons for a previously good quarterback in recent memory — but the Chargers appear ready to move forward with him as their franchise quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert may have suffered a left-hand fracture in the Chargers’ 22-44, Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Last year, when Herbert injured his left, non-throwing hand, his trainers stabilized the hand, with extra padding and tape applied to his middle finger. The exact same thing happened today. Herbert fended off a pass rusher with his left hand before bracing himself with the same hand as he fell. Fortunately, he remained in the game long enough to complete a 58-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. After a trip to the blue medical tent, Herbert was on the sideline, helmet on, with his left hand and middle finger heavily taped and padded. However, he did not return. The Chargers’ pass protection remains a huge problem, allowing eight sacks on the day. Before exiting, Herbert completed 13-of-23 passes for 193 yards, one touchdown and one interception, rushing once for seven yards. Herbert told reporters post-game that he does not expect his left middle finger to be an issue going forward. We will know more once he undergoes imaging. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert entered the blue medical tent in Week 9 against the Texans after suffering an apparent left hand injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert appeared to injure his left hand, and specifically his left middle finger, while fending off a pass rusher in the fourth quarter. He fractured the same hand, and seemingly the same digit, last year and underwent surgery to stabilize it in-season. We tentatively expect him to return after getting it taped up, but he will be playing hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 24-of-32 attempts for 257 yards and two interceptions in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding four rushes for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Coming off their bye week, the Chargers looked worse than ever on offense, with Herbert apparently confused as to where to throw the ball or how to conduct OC Mike McDaniel’s complex pre-snap motion scheme. Herbert had a negative EPA per drop back. Both of his picks were of the mind blogging variety, thrown directly to Rams defenders in the open field. Frustrated and dejected, Herbert continues his worst pro season for the winless Bolts. As usual, Herbert — who ranks 33rd in fantasy points per game — won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 22-of-37 attempts for 205 yards and one interception in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding five rushes for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert’s hellish season continued unabated on Sunday against a Kansas City defense that swamped the beleaguered Bolts quarterback on seemingly every drop back. After throwing exactly one touchdown in each of his first five outings, Herbert didn’t have any against the Chiefs. He had a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent below his expected pass rate in the loss. Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a head injury in the first half, further complicating OC Mike McDaniel’s efforts to stop the bleeding for the LA offense. The team’s wideout injuries and the predictability of the offense means Herbert should be dropped in most one-QB fantasy formats ahead of the Chargers’ Week 7 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Chargers would not consider trading Justin Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schefter reached out to the team after a league source told him the Chargers could get upwards of three first-round draft picks in exchange for Herbert. The Chargers source told Schefter the team has “never” discussed the idea of dealing Herbert, even as the Chargers start the season 0-5 and rank near the bottom in almost every offensive category. It would seem unlikely that the Chargers would consider trading Herbert even if they go all in on a rebuild following the 2026 season. Herbert, 28, who ranks 33rd out of 34 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per drop back this year, is signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues with a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rashawn Slater suffered a high ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The injury, sustained during the Bolts’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, will cost Slater between four and six weeks, Rapoport said. It’s yet another massive blow for the struggling Chargers offense. Through Week 4 the Chargers rank 30th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and fifth in run blocking win rate. Justin Herbert’s weekly prospects take a hit with the oft-injured Slate sidelined, as do the prospects of LA’s pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden (eye) caught his only target for seven yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden was injured on a run-blocking rep in the first quarter. He was checked out in the medical tent before being taken to the locker room after appearing to be poked in the eye, eventually deemed questionable to return by the team. He would return in the second half to catch his lone target for a meager seven yards in a game in which quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes. Gadsden remains off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Justin Herbert gave Gadsden a chance to get going downfield early on, but the pass clanged off his hands. The incompletion may ultimately have been erased by a penalty. Herbert looked his way again later, on the Chargers’ late two-point conversion attempt, but it failed. Charlie Kolar, meanwhile, caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and rushed once for three yards. Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught all five of his targets for 52 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden led LA tight ends in targets and trailed only Ladd McConkey in receiving yards on the day. Operating as a big slot receiver, Gadsden could have some fantasy value if he were to get more snaps and routes in the Chargers offense. In Week 9 against the Texans he’ll be a decent streaming option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day. (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards.) Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either player to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden did make a spectacular catch on fourth down to set up a touchdown, but oustide of that, the tight end — while finishing tied for the most catches on the day with Keaton Mitchell — was unable to find any room against the Seahawks’ defense. The 23-year-old was more involved than he has been in previous weeks, but that’s less compliment to this effort than insult to the first few. He’ll be back at it in Week 5 against another tough defense in the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. We guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught both of his targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: David Njoku left the game early with a knee injury and Charlie Kolar followed him to the locker room much later because of a forearm injury. As a result, Gadsden’s route rate jumped from 14 percent in Week 1 to 48 percent today. He still managed just two catches, but Gadsden at least found the end zone for the first time this year. The Chargers offense has looked defunct through two weeks, so even a full-time role for Gadsden could result in middling fantasy numbers. Still, he is worth a look off the waiver wire for teams in need of tight end production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Charvarius Ward (knee) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward departed the team’s Week 10 win over the Dolphins with a shin injury and did not return, listed as a non-participant one day later on the team’s estimated practice report. It would appear unlikely he is able to play on a short week against the Texans on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Charvarius Ward (shin) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward went down with a leg injury after a couple of pass-breakups in the third quarter. He limped to sideline and was later carted to the locker room. The Colts declared Ward questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts declared CB Charvarius Ward (groin) active for Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward was the only questionable Colts player, but got in a full practice on Friday. Ashton Dulin (ankle) was ruled out on Friday. The other Colts inactives, all healthy scratches, are RB DJ Giddens, DE George Gumbs Jr., QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts CB Charvarius Ward (back) is sidelined indefinitely.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward was contemplating retirement this offseason due to a scary amount of documented concussions, but gave it a go at training camp only to wind up missing tons of time due to this back injury. The 30-year-old will start for the Colts if he’s healthy for Week 1, but that sounds like an open question at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts CB Charvarius Ward (concussions) is contemplating retirement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward is quoted as saying that even a small bump on his head in normal day-to-day activity recently left him with a debilitating migraine, and adds: “I do know going into next season, if I do come back and play again, if I get one more (concussion), I’ll for sure probably retire.” A big-name free agent addition by the Colts this past offseason, Ward was only able to play seven games while dealing with brain injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said CB Charvarius Ward is in concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Again. As in: For the third time this season. Woof. It would not be surprising if this was a season-ender for Ward. He did play 61 of 64 snaps against the Jaguars, so he apparently either played through symptoms or they developed after the game. It’s become a lost season for Ward, one of the Colts big-money signings this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said CB Charvarius Ward (concussion) has cleared protocol and will be activated from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward sustained his concussion in pre-game warmups ahead of Week 6’s game with the Cardinals. His return should give the Colts a lot of versatility at cornerback as they can now boast a triumvirate of Sauce Gardner, Ward, and Kenny Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts CB Charvarius Ward (concussion) practiced fully on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward is firmly on track to play in Week 12 against the Colts. The Colts’ secondary has been banged up this year, so Ward’s return is a positive occurrence. Colts slot CB Kenny Moore II is also fully healthy after dealing with an Achilles injury for much of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts opened the 21-day practice window for CB Charvarius Ward (concussion).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward sustained a concussion during pre-game warmups ahead of the Colts’ Week 6 game against Arizona and was placed on injured reserve.
