He could suit up as soon as this week against the Chiefs if he clears the NFL’s concussion protocol and gets the green light from Colts trainers. Ward will be a welcome addition to a Colts secondary that has struggled of late.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.headline: Colts placed CB Charvarius Ward (concussion) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charvarius.analysis: Ward suffered a concussion in pre-game warmups in Week 6 and has now been placed on injured reserve, marking a massive blow to the secondary in Indianapolis. The freak accident will keep him out of the game-day lineup for the next four games, at minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, G/T Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Chandler Rivers, and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive for Week 10 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: No surprises here as Hawkins had already been ruled out earlier in the week, with the remaining five players all normal healthy inactives. The Ravens look to right a sinking ship against the only remaining winless team in the league, with quarterback Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Cornerback Nate Wiggins is questionable with an illness. He did not practice today. Hawkins missed Week 8 with the knee issue and wasn’t able to practice once this week. The Ravens play on Thursday this week and then get an extended break until Monday of Week 10, when they’ll take on the Chargers. The extra time off might help Hawkins get back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is out for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was unable to practice all week as he tends to a knee injury, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 Friday. It will go down as his second consecutive absence, with his next opportunity to take the field to come in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) missed practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was absent for the second consecutive day, requiring some level of participation Friday to avoid a designation for the team’s showdown against the Bills in Week 8. The team got good news on other fronts as Lamar Jackson, Ioane Vega, Kyle Hamilton, and Roquan Smith were all present Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens agreed to terms with S Jaylinn Hawkins, formerly of the Patriots, on a two-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins signed with the Pats as a backup two years ago. He was elevated to a starting role in 2025 and put some of his best play on tape. Hawkins totaled six pass breakups, four interceptions, and 1.5 sacks across 15 games. He will likely serve as Jesse Minter’s third safety in Baltimore’s new defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots released S Jabrill Peppers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Peppers has $4.32 million in guaranteed money remaining on his contract for this season. The 29-year-old safety started 26 games over the last three seasons with the Patriots. New England could be looking to start Jaylinn Hawkins and rookie Craig Woodson now, according to ESPN’s Mike Reiss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots re-signed S Jaylinn Hawkins to a one-year, $2.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins will handle backup safety duties while primarily contributing on special teams. He earned a 69.5 PFF special teams grade last year, though he does not return punts nor kicks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Chargers claimed S Jaylinn Hawkins off waivers from the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was primarily a special teams contributor for Atlanta to start the season. He saw a handful of defensive snaps in each of his first three games but has only played on defense one time in the past three weeks. Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Chargers were not the only team to put in a claim on Hawkins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: The Falcons waived S Jaylinn Hawkins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was a 2020 fourth-round pick by the Falcons, starting 16 games in 2022. He has four career interceptions and was in the last year of his rookie contract, but Hawkins has now been cut loose by Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jordan Burch (knee) will miss the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch suffered an MCL injury in Week 10’s loss to the Rams and will now miss the remainder of the season. The second-year linebacker and former third-rounder has appeared on 235 defensive snaps this season, totaling nine pressures and one sack while earning a PFF defensive grade of 54.8. Assuming his recovery goes well, he should be in line to return in time for training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: Cardinals selected Oregon EDGE Jordan Burch with the No. 78 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: A former five-star recruit, Burch (6’4/279) finally put it all together in 2024 after a career that included three seasons at South Carolina before transferring to Eugene. He posted career-highs in TFLs (11.0), sacks (8.5), and pass breakups (5) despite missing four games due to injury. A smooth-moving edge rusher in a power end’s frame, Burch is a heavy-handed disruptor whose favorite tool is brute strength, bull-rushing blockers into reverse or uncorking a violent club-rip to soften edges. He posted an 83.9 pass rush grade — best of his career — and an 81.2 tackling mark, missing just one tackle all season. His athletic testing wasn’t full-spectrum, but his 4.67 forty was a 91st percentile mark, flashing the juice needed to win early in reps. However, Burch’s tape is often feast-or-famine. He lacks a diverse counter arsenal, and inconsistent get-off timing lets linemen gain leverage. He is more reactive than instinctual versus the run and will be 24 as a rookie, with multiple injuries in his college history. That said, Burch offers high-floor traits and scheme versatility as a power end with pass-rush upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: South Carolina signed five-star 2020 DE Jordan Burch.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) committed to South Carolina in December and reaffirmed his commitment on Wednesday’s National Signing Day, but the Gamecocks then went through an anxious 24-plus hours after the program failed to receive his signed National Letter of Intent. LSU was pushing hard for the flip, here. The drama finally ended on Thursday evening, when South Carolina officially announced him as a signed member of their 2020 class. Columbia native Burch, now staying home, hits the 247Sports composite board as the No. 8 overall prospect in the 2020 class and makes for the program’s highest-ranked signee since Jadeveon Clowney in 2011.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: South Carolina has yet to receive five-star verbal DE commit Jordan Burch’s NLI.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: More drama with Burch. The 6-foot-6, 255-pound defensive end initially committed to South Carolina in December and announced on Wednesday that he would be playing his college ball in Columbia. However, it has become clear that Burch’s NLI has not yet reached South Carolina, with HC Will Muschamp essentially saying as much in his press conference on Wednesday afternoon. That doesn’t necessarily mean that Burch won’t end up with the program, but LSU had been pushing very hard to flip the five-star stud over the past month-and-a-half. At the very least, the delay, here, is an interesting one. We’ll continue to track this one until it reaches resolution.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: South Carolina five-star 2020 verbal DE commit Jordan Burch is taking an official visit to the Gamecocks this weekend.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) committed to the Gamecocks in December but did not sign with them at the time, leaving the door open for a potential February flip. LSU drew an unofficial visit from the Columbia native last weekend, but South Carolina will have the last chance to make a closing pitch, here. That should be considered an encouraging sign for the program, though even with the OV locked in, this one is not a done deal for HC Will Muschamp and staff. Earlier this week, 247Sports’ Steve Wiltfong predicted that LSU would win out for Burch come National Signing Day. Burch will be announcing his final decision at 1 EST on Wednesday. On the 247Sports’ composite board, Burch lands as the No. 8 overall prospect in the 2020 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: 247Sports’ Steve Wiltfong predicts that South Carolina five-star 2020 verbal DE commit Jordan Burch will sign with LSU next Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) committed to South Carolina at the start of the early signing window in December, but because he did not sign his NLI at the time, teams like LSU will have a chance to swing him over come National Signing Day next Wednesday. Per Wiltfong, South Carolina is trying their darnedest to lock Burch in for a visit this coming weekend, which would allow them one final in-person opportunity to seal the deal. The five-star defensive end hits the 247Sports composite board as the No. 7 overall prospect in the 2020 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: South Carolina five-star 2020 verbal DE commit Jordan Burch could take January visits to other schools.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) committed to South Carolina to much fanfare at the start of the early signing period, but crucially did sign his NLI at the time. Per Rivals’ Chad Simmons, all of his earlier finalists beyond the Gamecocks -- Clemson, Georgia, Alabama and LSU -- have been in touch with the Columbia native. If the star prep edge rusher does ultimately set up a few visits for January, we’ll pass along word. Rivals ranks Burch as the No. 8 overall prospect in the 2020 class. It would be a killer blow for the Gamecocks if they ended up losing this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: South Carolina signed five-star 2020 DE Jordan Burch.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) was choosing between South Carolina, Alabama, Clemson, Georgia and LSU. The Columbia, South Carolina, native had been on campus a number of times and the Gamecocks had the hometown edge for this one, but even so, they fought through the toughest of competition to get the job done on Wednesday. Burch is South Carolina’s biggest prep signing since Jadeveon Clowney and currently ranks on the 247Sports composite board as the No. 5 overall prospect in the 2020 class. In his ESPNU post-decision interview, Burch said that he styles his game after the likes of Julius Peppers and Khalil Mack. As the kids say, let’s go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: Updating a previous item, South Carolina five-star 2020 verbal DE commit Jordan Burch has not yet sent the program his signed letter of intent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: This per The Athletic’s Josh Kendall. Burch (6'6/255) announced his South Carolina commitment earlier on Wednesday, opting in with the Gamecocks over Alabama, Clemson, Georgia and LSU. We’ll pass along word when the five-star defensive end officially inks up on his NLI. Kendall, it should be noted, passes along that Burch is not expected to sign before the end of Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.headline: Uncommitted five-star 2020 DL Jordan Burch will announce his college decision on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-burch/0.analysis: Burch (6'6/255) will make his decision public in front of a national audience, as his ceremony will be broadcast on ESPNU. The five-star defensive lineman originally planned to make the announcement on December 19, but it’s been moved up a day for television reasons. Burch, ranked the top strong-side defensive end in the 2020 class by 247Sports, is considering Alabama, Clemson, Georgia, LSU and South Carolina heading into his decision day. Also a talented basketball player, Burch has been compared to former Ohio State DE Joey Bosa by some recruiting analysts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik Willis (groin) is not having surgery at this time but a final decision has not been made on if he’ll have it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “We’ll see how he feels,” Hafley said. “If he needs surgery, he will have surgery.” Well, hard to make it less complex than that. Willis is definitely out for the next three games and it sounds like there’s at least a reasonable chance he’ll be done for the season. In the meantime, Kyle McCord will play the role of bottom-five superflex starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he hopes Malik Willis (groin) can return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley told reporters on Wednesday that Willis would seek second opinions on the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. It sounds like season-ending surgery is a possibility for Willis, who would end his 2026 campaign. Through Week 9, Willis ranks 26th in passing yardage and 29th in passing touchdowns. He’s dead last in EPA per pass attempt and ranks 28th out of 38 qualifying QBs in EPA per drop back. Kyle McCord will get a chance at quarterback for the Dolphins in Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins placed Malik Willis (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: He had clearly been laboring since the bye week and this will give Willis some time to heal. This is not regarded as a season-ending injury and Willis will be eligible to return in Week 14. In the mean time, it appears we’re all about to see how well the roster cutdown Kyle McCord trade works out for the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 13-of-25 passes for 128 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 19-9, Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis only added seven yards on two carries. He was on the injury report with a groin injury this week. Despite practicing in full three times, Willis appeared to be severely limited by the issue. He turned down several opportunities to scramble, instead opting to throw the ball away when the Lions’ pass-rush got close. Without the rushing production to bail him out of tough spots, the offense collapsed despite facing one of the league’s worst defenses. His passing output was already weak, but a lack of rush attempts will pull him out of the QB2 ranks entirely. He will be downgraded to a low-end QB2 for his Week 10 matchup with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis did the same during Week 8 practices and ended up running just once against the Patriots. Hopefully, the groin injury continues to improve and his rushing usage returns. Willis remains a QB2 this week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 21-of-32 passes for 211 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the Dolphins’ 19-24, Week 8 loss to the Patriots, adding one rush for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full this week despite being listed with a groin injury. Perhaps the soft tissue issue made him play a little more restrained than we would have liked him to. The Dolphins’ quarterback continues to hold the ball too long. He took five sacks today. His interception was not totally his fault. He was hit by a pass rusher, altering the pass’s trajectory, which bounced off a defensive lineman’s helmet before flying 29 yards downfield, where a Patriots defender picked it off. Willis had another interception called back due to defensive offsides, which was lucky. The Dolphins’ young wide receivers are learning the ropes and could help him churn out usable fantasy line as the season progresses. Willis will be a high-end QB2 against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said it’s too early to know if Laremy Tunsil (triceps) will return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Quinn said Tunsil is progressing well in his recovery from the torn triceps he suffered in training camp and has moved on to the next phase of his recovery. Tunsil was always expected to miss all or most of the season with his injury, so it’s no surprise to hear that Quinn is unsure if he will be able to return with eight weeks left to go in the regular season. We’ll likely get more updates on his status in the coming weeks, but until the Commanders designate him for return, we can safely assume he will be out for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn said Laremy Tunsil will undergo surgery to repair his torn triceps.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Tunsil suffered a torn triceps on Saturday and is at risk of missing most or all of the regular season. Quinn said the team hopes to have a better sense of his recovery timeline after his surgery, but for now, the Commanders are set to move forward with third-year lineman Brandon Coleman as their starting left tackle. Coleman has spent all of camp competing with Chris Paul for the starting left guard spot, but started 12 games at left tackle for the Commanders in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil has been diagnosed with a torn right triceps and will miss a “significant” portion of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Fresh off becoming one of the highest paid offensive linemen in the history of the league, Tunsil suffered the injury in Saturday’s practice. He is expected to undergo surgery, and his absence will be measured in months, probably a minimum of 3-4 of them. It’s possible he misses the entire campaign. It appears the initial plan is for last season’s swing tackle, Andrew Wylie, to step in on the blindside, leaving 2025 first-rounder Josh Conerly to remain on the right. Brandon Coleman is another less-than-great in-house option. We wouldn’t be surprised if Conerly eventually kicks left, however. Whatever happens, it’s a monumental downgrade, one that will have Washington scouring the remains of the free agent market and perhaps angling for a trade to add some depth. It’s not the news Jayden Daniels needed as he himself looks to stay healthy after an injury-cursed year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil (shoulder/neck) will undergo testing for injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: The news was first reported by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Tunsil will be evaluated and tested for injury, but Garafolo says he’s not sensing huge panic about the injury. Still, Garafolo also said he wouldn’t be surprised if Tunsil has to miss some time. Stay tuned as the tests will ultimately show the severity of Tunsil’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders signed LT Laremy Tunsil to a two-year, $60.2 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Tunsil had one year remaining on his previous deal but will now remain under contract through the 2028 season. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tunsil will receive $61.5 million in guaranteed money, which includes a record $32.5 million signing bonus for an offensive lineman. In his first season with the Commanders, Tunsil appeared on 802 snaps while allowing just 15 QB pressures and two sacks, per PFF. He’ll protect Jayden Daniels’ blindside for the foreseeable future and should continue to play at a high level throughout the duration of this deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders GM Adam Peters said the team has had “good talks” with LT Laremy Tunsil on an extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: There’s no deadline and Peters “feels good about the direction.” It was an open secret that Tunsil wanting a new extension helped guide him to Washington in trade last offseason, and he enters 2026 on the final year of his contract. With as great a year as Tunsil had for the Commanders last year — a career-best 84.7 PFF grade — we’d be surprised if this wasn’t eventually done. That said, the Commanders haven’t exactly worked fast to extend their own players, as the Terry McLaurin saga taught us in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil (oblique) will not play in Washington’s Week 18 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Tunsil ends the year with a career-best 84.7 PFF offensive grade in 802 snaps. The trade for Tunsil was largely successful for the Commanders — it’s just that one man is not a whole offensive line and Jayden Daniels got hurt anyway. He enters the final year of his contract in 2026 and, given that extension concerns were what sent him to Washington in the first place, probably will have some work done on his deal this offseason. This oblique injury is not expected to linger.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Comanders LT Laremy Tunsil (oblique) will not play in Week 17 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Tunsil suffered a strained oblique in Week 15 and hasn’t practiced or played since. Josh Johnson will make his first start of the year without his left tackle. Our hopes for the Washington offense are not high this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders delared QB Jayden Daniels, RB Chase Edmonds, T George Fant, T Laremy Tunsil, TE Colson Yankoff, and DT Eddie Goldman inactive for Week 16 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: The Commanders will be without both starting offensive tackles in a game started by backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, potentially opening the door for defensive dominance from a relentless Eagles defense. Expect a reliance on the ground game to start while getting back Chris Rodriguez from a one-game absence, but that stance could quickly shift should the Commanders fall behind early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.headline: Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil (oblique) will not play in Week 16 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laremy-tun.analysis: Tunsil strained his oblique in Week 15. Now Marcus Mariota will draw another start, this time without his left tackle. Brandon Coleman took over for him mid-game last week and will likely keep that gig into Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “that’s my plan” when asked if Micah Parsons (knee) could return in Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: LaFleur did note that his plan has “been different than everybody else’s” throughout Parsons’ recovery, and said the star pass-rusher still has “a couple more hurdles” to clear before they can commit to him returning. Parsons has been practicing with the team since November 4th and would need to come off injured reserve by Week 12 in order to avoid being shut down for the season. With the Packers now entering their Week 11 bye, we will likely get more news on Parsons’ Week 12 status closer to the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 12 when the Packers return from their bye week, assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slow-played his return and have been rewarded, as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons was cleared to resume individual activities but was never likely to play against the Pats this week. The next chance for Parsons to play will be Week 10 against the Vikings, and there’s at least a smidgen of optimism he could be back for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) is a “full go” to do individual work at practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: That doesn’t mean Parsons is a “full go” for Week 9 against the Patriots, however, as the pass rusher comes back from a season-ending knee injury in 2025. Parsons could return soon for a Green Bay defense that ranks 12th in pressure rate and 16th in quick pressure rate on the season. Look for the team to ease Parsons into action to make sure he’s OK for the final stretch of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Micah Parsons (knee) to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is not expected to suit up in Week 9 against the Patriots, but this is the next step in his recovery as he looks to return to the field. On Sunday, it was reported that the Packers were targeting a Week 12 return for Parsons, which would mean he plays on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams if all goes according to plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons (knee) is targeting a Week 12 return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is still working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered late in the 2025 season. Per Rapoport, Parsons is expected to return to practice this week, meaning he will be designated to return from injured reserve in the coming days. He will then ramp up for a few weeks before hopefully returning in Week 12 against the Rams. Green Bay’s Week 11 bye will give him some extra time to get fully up to speed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Micah Parsons (knee) is expected to practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: If Parsons returns to practice next week, the Packers will have a 21-day window where he can practice before activating him to the 53-man roster. Pelissero also reported that Parsons’ most likely return date is in Week 11 against the Rams. Including the playoffs, Green Bay is 5-8 since Parsons tore his ACL last December.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “there’s a chance” Micah Parsons (knee) practices next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: When asked about Parsons’ chances of practicing next week, LaFleur said, “I sure hope so.” He followed that up with, “I’m saying there’s a chance.” Parsons opened the season on the PUP list after an ACL tear late last season. The Packers have a Thursday game for Week 8, leading to a mini-bye where Parsons’ door to practice is at least cracked open.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports George Holani (knee) has an MCL sprain and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The “hope” is that Holani is not an IR candidate. His absence left Zach Charbonnet playing most of the third-down snaps yesterday, adding to his RB2 case going forward. Holani can be dropped in most leagues ahead of Seattle’s Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani (knee) has been ruled out in Week 10.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani picked up the knee injury in the first half against the Raiders and did not return. The Seattle rushing offense has revolved around Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price in recent weeks, leaving Holani out of the backfield fold. He can remain on waivers ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani split primary change of pace duties with recent practice squad call-up Velus Jones Jr, the latter of whom turned four carries into 20 yards while losing one yard on his lone reception. Both backs appear unlikely to return fantasy value as Zach Charbonnet nears a return from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed four times for seven yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding four receptions for 24 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani put the ball on the turf twice in this one, but it was his fumble with 13 seconds left in the first half that proved to be one of the more costly mistakes of the game. With the Seahawks simply looking to get to halftime, Holani took a handoff from Sam Darnold for what should have been the final play of regulation. Instead, the third-year back had the ball knocked out and into his own end zone, which resulted in a Niners touchdown after it was recovered by DT Gracen Halton for the score. Holani hasn’t emerged as the late-round value fantasy managers hoped for this offseason and is fully off the fantasy radar for Week 6 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani is active for Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani is good to go for Sunday’s game after entering the weekend as questionable. Holani rushed seven times for 18 scoreless yards last week and shouldn’t be relied on in any fantasy format this week. While Holani is active, the Seahawks declared QB Jalen Milroe, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, WR Montorie Foster Jr., and TE Nick Kallerup inactive for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was nursing a ribs injury on Wednesday and Thursday, but he is now listed with a knee injury as well. This is concerning. He clearly picked up a new injury during the practice week. Velus Jones is the current RB3. Jones is not viable as a FLEX starter if Holani sits, but Emanuel Wilson should take on an RB2-worthy workload regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani should be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 5 game against the 49ers, but he is certainly working through a decent little injury. The trusted passing game specialist should handle his normal workload, although he is only a touchdown-dependent PPR FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was listed as a limited practice participant due to a rib injury on Wednesday. The 26-year-old operated as a passing-down backup to Emanuel Wilson in Week 4 with Jadarian Price out. Unless he misses practice later this week, he is still on track to play in Week 5, though Holani does not have a large enough role to achieve fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Seahawks Week 4 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In the first week without Jadarian Price, Holani operated as a lightly used backup behind Emanuel Wilson, who rushed for 21-81-1, and added another 3-39-1 through the air on four targets. Any hope that Holani could see an increased workload sans Price needs to be put on hold for now. He can be left on fantasy benches in Week 5 when the Seahawks host the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn revealed that DC Brian Duker called defensive plays on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: Last February, Glenn said that calling plays was his “superpower.” The Jets are 28th in defensive DVOA per FTN and have allowed the most rushing attempts in the league along with 1,353 yards on the ground, third-most in the league. Glenn did not say whether he or Duker would call plays going forward. We’re not sure it really matters. The second-year coach is running out of road as the Jets have stumbled to a 2-8 start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini said he “would be a little surprised” if the Jets draft Alabama QB Ty Simpson with the No. 16 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft “because they have so many other needs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: Cimini also believes the Jets do not feel “pressured” to draft a quarterback in 2026 because they have three first-round picks in 2027. That said, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, general manager Darren Mougey, OC Frank Reich and QB coach Bill Musgrave had dinner with Simpson last night and hosted him for a private workout today. The Jets hold the second, 16th, 33rd and 44th picks in this year’s draft. We certainly agree that the Jets have many needs, but finding a starting quarterback tops the list. Simpson could still end up in a Jets uniform next month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said he’ll call plays on defense in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: It confirms one of the worst-kept secrets in the league after the Jets passed up on numerous other coordinator options to land on unheralded Brian Duker as their defensive coordinator. Glenn said “play calling is my superpower, really.” Well, it’s good to have one of those. We’ll see how it lasts with this Jets roster. It certainly can’t be worse than it was last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: A former NFL general manager said Jets head coach Aaron Glenn “did nothing” to change the team’s culture of losing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: The former front office official told ESPN’s Rich Cimini that the lackluster effort on the part of Jets players was a telltale sign of a head coach who had not done anything to shift the team’s miserable culture, like his former boss, Dan Campbell, did in his first year with the Lions. Glenn “talked about swagger and toughness, but I didn’t see any of that. They played like a bunch of guys punching time clocks; they didn’t want to be there,” the former GM said. Glenn’s Jets struggled through a hopeless 3-14 season in 2025, posting one of the most lopsided scoring margins in recent NFL history. Glenn, a defensive specialist, gave total control of the defense to Steve Wilks, who was fired late in the season. New York was the first team in NFL history to go an entire season without an interception. Jets owner Woody Johnson will give Glenn another season to turn things around, Cimini said, because he was very much involved in hiring Glenn last offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: NFL Network’s Judy Battista reports Jets owner Woody Johnson “remains committed” to head coach Aaron Glenn.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: Despite sitting at 3-13 with one game left to play, the Jets will give Glenn a second chance in 2026. The former Lions defensive coordinator was brought in to turn the team around this year. Instead, the Justin Fields experiment flopped and Glenn’s side of the ball failed to contribute anything to the cause. The Jets currently rank 30th in points allowed. As Battista notes, Glenn is expected to make some changes to his staff during the offseason. Offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand could be asked to fall on his sword after a dismal season from the offense. Defensive coordinator Steve Wilks was fired in the middle of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is expected to keep his job beyond the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: Rapoport weaved the news into a segment where he explains that the Jets “next move” is to find a franchise quarterback by using the 2026 and 2027 NFL Draft picks haul that the team acquired before this season’s trade deadline. Rapoport indicates that a franchise quarterback could be found via the draft or by trading away picks. While Rapoport’s phrasing suggests the Jets plan to acquire a franchise quarterback this offseason, it is worth noting that the segment was backdropped by a graphic showing two first-round picks and two-round picks in 2026, plus three first-round picks and one second-round pick in 2027. Rapoport narrates by saying “Glenn is expected to be there” with GM Darren Mougey, “making those picks.” Given the Jets’ 2025 failures under Glenn, we assume the first-time head coach does not actually have guaranteed job security through 2027, though Rapoport’s phrasing leaves room for interpretation. Expect Glenn to get another shot in 2026 at the very least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: Jets owner Woody Johnson said the Jets offense “would look good” if “we can just complete a pass.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: Welp. That’ll be one for the career obituary on Justin Fields. It seems clear that the Jets owner has not soured on Aaron Glenn and instead believes that the Fields play was simply a mistake. The Jets have not announced anything about who their quarterback will be this week, but ownership doesn’t usually just say something like this about a pass offense with a quarterback they intend to keep starting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: Jets owner Woody Johnson received an F from players who responded to an NFLPA survey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: The NFLPA report card, which included responses from nearly 1,700 active NFL players, had Johnson as the only owner to get a failing grade. Patriots owner Robert Kraft, Cardinals owner Michael Bidwell, and Panthers owner David Tepper were the only owners to get a D on the NFLPA’s report card. Johnson received a B- grade in 2023. “Rather than addressing concerns, players believed that management responded to feedback by making conditions worse,” the report said about Johnson and the Jets higher ups. It’s hardly a surprise that Johnson would get such low marks after another failed season, his commitment to Aaron Rodgers, and reports that Johnson’s children had made roster decisions based on Madden ratings. Johnson, who reportedly took control over the Jets front office midway through the catastrophic 2024 season, would do well to step aside and let head head coach Aaron Glenn take charge of the organization.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Jets are hiring Lions DC Aaron Glenn as their head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: The connection of Glenn to the Jets has been made for months and came into focus earlier this week when the team brought him into New York for an interview with the plan of hiring him on the spot. Glenn’s ties to the franchise run deep. The Jets drafted Glenn, a former cornerback, in the first round 30 years ago and he even spent time in the organization as a scout after his playing days were over. Glenn served as a DBs coach in New Orleans and followed Dan Campbell to Detroit in 2021, accepting the position of defensive coordinator. In 2024, Glenn led the Lions to top-10 ranks in EPA per play and total points allowed despite the team being bombarded by injuries on the defensive side of the ball. He now joins a Jets team with plenty of talent on defense including Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. The offensive side of the ball is the bigger issue, meaning Glenn’s choice of offensive coordinator will be crucial.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt reports “barring anything unexpected” the Jets will hire Lions DC Aaron Glenn as their new head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-glen.analysis: The Jets and Aaron Glenn have been flirting with each other through the coaching cycle and the Divisional Round elimination of Glenn’s Lions is speeding things up. He interviewed with the Jets on Tuesday and is expected to be named their head coach soon. Rosenblatt adds the Jets’ staff “has been operating as if it will get done” and the team is “informing candidates that they are going in another direction.” Glenn has been the Lions’ defensive coordinator since 2021, keeping the team afloat through major defensive injuries this season, prior to the playoff exit. The 52-year-old will be a first-time head coach, faced with rebuilding the Jets after a short-lived Aaron Rodgers era.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Drake London was evaluated for a concussion against the Chiefs and cleared the protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: We didn’t mention this in the blurb streets yesterday as it happened late in the fourth quarter. London should be fine to start in Week 12 after Atlanta’s Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 6-of-12 targets for 109 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also drew an 18-yard DPI. The 100-yard game was somehow London’s first in five weeks. It was also just his third of the season. After starting off on a high note with Michael Penix, London has been reduced to scrounging for volume of late. Things aren’t going to get any better coming off the Falcons’ bye in Week 12, where they must venture to Minnesota to take on the Vikings’ elite defense. That figures to be more of a WR2 day for London before the WR1 times are good again in Week 13 vs. the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-5 targets for 68 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London bounced back after being held to one reception and eight yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. He caught all five of his targets for 68 yards, but still has only one touchdown on the year after being held scoreless again. After dominating with Michael Penix in the lineup last season, London has just been okay with Penix under center this year. Likely facing a pass-heavy game script in Week 10 against the Chiefs, London will be a low-end WR1 again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 1-of-6 targets for eight yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Bucs defenders caught more passes on London’s six targets than he did. It was that bad of a day. Michael Penix was intercepted four times and only completed eight attempts. He managed just 125 yards, over half of which came on a 76-yard throw to Jahan Dotson that was the result of a coverage miscue. There’s simply not much to take away from a game where London’s quarterback plays this poorly. London had gone for at least 60 yards on four catches in every previous Penix start. We fully expect him to get back on track as a WR1 versus the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London fought through a tackle on a 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter for his first touchdown catch of the season. He was also open for a touchdown earlier in the game, but Michael Penix Jr. sailed the pass over his head. London had twice as many targets as any other pass catcher in Atlanta and should continue to get elite usage in this offense. He did leave the game to be evaluated for a concussion, and while he was able to return to the field, it’s a situation to monitor for early practice reports next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London couldn’t get much going against Chicago’s middling secondary outside a 39-yard grab in the second half, with the Falcons abandoning the run game as they faced a three-touchdown deficit. Michael Penix missed London in the first half on what could have been a fairly easy 30-yard score with a better-placed throw from Penix. London almost came down with an end zone target too. No other Atlanta pass catcher had more than seven targets on the day. London will remain a top-10 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London started slow along with the rest of an Atlanta offense that gained just 37 total yards on their first three possessions before a 78-yard scoring drive to end the half. He would add six receptions after the break to push his season average to 127 yards per game in games started by Michael Penix. Penix departed late in the fourth quarter with a ribs injury, suddenly making London’s fantasy managers skittish after the veteran receiver managed a meager 80 total yards in two games without Penix to begin the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Atlanta’s starting quarterback’s status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears, where London will be a WR1 with Penix or an upside WR3 in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London turned in his second consecutive usable fantasy week with Michael Penix under center. The low volume can primarily be attributed to just 20 Penix pass attempts in a game Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 yards and five touchdowns on the ground on 33 carries. London could be tasked with more volume when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5, for which he will remain an unquestioned WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 9-of-10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: To make the stat line more impressive, London didn’t catch his first pass until three minutes into the second quarter following a 1-of-5 start from Michael Penix. He would catch his final nine targets on his way to a massive fantasy day, combining with Bijan Robinson to set the NFL record for a wide receiver and running back duo to both go over 150 yards in the same game with three such occurrences. London continues to excel with Penix under center and returns to the WR1 ranks in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also had a 25-yard grab called back by penalty. As expected, the Falcons simply rolled out a dead-on-arrival offense with Cooper Rush under center. Rush turned the ball over three times before being benched in the third quarter. Things didn’t get any better with Jack Strand under center. He threw an immediate pick-six and the Falcons promptly pulled the bulk of their starters from the game. With Michael Penix expected to play next week, London should return to the WR2 ranks next time we see him. If Penix isn’t available once again, London will barely register as a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said he is “really optimistic” that Sam Darnold (quad) will be able to start after the team’s Week 11 bye.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Macdonald also reaffirmed Darnold as the starter after Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10’s win over the Raiders. Lock has been solid for the Seahawks in four games this season, throwing for 837-7-0 while completing a career-high 73.1 percent of his passes. With the Seahawks now entering their bye, Macdonald said he his hopeful Darnold can log enough reps in time to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. We’ll see where things stand a week from now, but it’s clear there will be no QB controversey in Seattle whenever Darnold is ready to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald said Darnold will need at least one more week to recover from the quad injury that sidelined him in Week 9. While Drew Lock (oblique) is dealing with his own injury, Macdonald said he believes the team can manage it and expects him to start next week against the Raiders. The Seahawks will have their bye in Week 11, so hopefully three straight weeks off will give him enough time to recover before Week 12’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks declared QB Sam Darnold, WR Rashid Shaheed, T Charles Cross, G Quenton Nelson, LB Uchenna Nwosu, DT Brandon Pili, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold was ruled out earlier in the week while Shaheed misses his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Drew Lock gets the start under center for the second time this season while veteran receiver Cooper Kupp could see a slight uptick in usage with Shaheed sidelined. Injury trouble along the offensive line could lead to a more ball-out-quick offensive game plan as the Seahawks look to keep pace in the NFC West.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Per Macdonald, Darnold also suffered a rib injury early in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Bears, though that doesn’t appear to be the reason he’s out this week. Darnold is considered week-to-week. Per Macdonald, he won’t go on injured reserve. It’s possible this quad issue is related to the glute issue that sidelined Darnold earlier in the season. Either way, Darnold’s health concerns are now becoming an issue for a Seahawks team that was already struggling to live up to the hype. Drew Lock will draw the start versus Arizona this week. He’ll likely start in Week 10 as well. With two successful appearances under his belt this year, Lock is a somewhat safe QB2 bet for Superflex managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 17-of-34 passes for 188 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 34-17, Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding 20 yards on two rushes.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold really struggled through consistent pressure from Dennis Allen’s aggressive defensive front as the Seahawks gained just 252 yards of total offense. Things looked manageable in the first half while Darnold leaned heavily on alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, feeding his top option for 92 yards before the break. Allen’s second half adjustments all but removed JSN from the offense, holding him to just 26 yards after the break. Week 8 went down as only the third game of the 2026 season in which Darnold threw multiple touchdowns, leaving him outside QB2 range and on waiver wires ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 20-of-28 passes for 257 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 20-3, Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold continued to flaunt his connection with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba with zero regard to the naysayers, feeding his alpha 12 targets on 28 pass attempts, the latter of whom accounted for 150 of the 257 pass yards for Darnold. As you probably guessed, Smith-Njigba was also the recipient of Darnold’s lone touchdown throw, which was a dime down the left sideline on a corner route that the veteran signal caller dropped into the bread basket. The two would connect on another similar play later in the same quarter in which Smith-Njigba was forced out at the two, with the result of that drive Darnold’s interception in the end zone. Darnold continues to do just enough for his team and not enough for fantasy managers that thought they could grab cheap production late in drafts. He’s better sent back to the waiver wire than inserted into starting lineups. The Seahawks next face the Bears on the second half of back-to-back Monday Night Football games, where Darnold remains a shaky fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 17-14, Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding 19 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks struggled to move the football throughout against the tenacious situational play calling from Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, scoring only three points until just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. A late-game surge saw them punch on in and a successful two-point conversion drew the team within three points. They would stop the Broncos on the subsequent possession but an interception in Denver territory put the game in jeopardy. The defense would do their job and force a three-and-out that took only 15 seconds off the clock, giving the ball back to Darnold to lead a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime through a chip shot field goal. Darnold would throw his second interception in overtime, watching from the sideline as the Broncos walked it off with a 53-yard Will Lutz field goal. The loss sends the Seahawks to 3-3, matching the total number of losses from a season ago through only six weeks of the 2026 season. The Seahawks have work to do to make up ground in the NFC West, now 2.5 games behind the undefeated 49ers through the first third of the regular season. Darnold and the Seahawks now have a long week to prepare for the now-undefeated Chiefs at home in Week 7, where Darnold will be a fringe QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Patriots “are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: According to Schultz, the Patriots could look into free agents like Jimmy Garoppolo and may also consider signing a QB from a team’s practice squad. Garoppolo, who last threw a regular-season pass in Week 18 of the 2024 season, worked with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniel from 2014 to 2017 during their time together in New England, and also spent the 2023 season with McDaniels during a brief stint with the Raiders. It’s hard to imagine Garoppolo coming off the couch to save the Patriots’ season, but he could offer a little more upside than Tommy DeVito did in relief of Drake Maye during Sunday’s loss to the Lions. For now, DeVito is expected to start in Week 12 when the Patriots return from their bye, but it’s clear they would prefer an upgrade if one were available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports Steston Bennett is getting the “first crack” with the ones when Matthew Stafford rests.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: Atkins doesn’t seem impressed with Bennett (who has “fallen victim to a couple of greedy mistakes”) or Ty Simpson (“isn’t going downfield much”) early in camp and suggests that the unsigned Jimmy Garoppolo could just be a phone call away if Simpson isn’t able to win the QB2 job. We’ll see what happens, but Garoppolo lingering as a free agent could keep some upside injury runouts off the table for Simpson this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports QB Jimmy Garoppolo will play football this season for “the right situation.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: Garafolo adds that Garoppolo “has not decided to retire” and will continue to play. Nothing is imminent and the “right situation” may take an injury to a starter around the league. The 34-year-old had contemplated retirement earlier in the offseason but instead is open to continuing his playing career. Garoppolo is a free agent to keep an eye on as training camp battles and injuries start to unfold.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said that the team wants Jimmy Garoppolo to return but “are letting him figure out his future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: There is no timeline on that decision, per McVay. Ian Rapoport reported yesterday that Garoppolo was considering retirement, something that makes his slow-developing market make more sense. McVay wanting Garoppolo back makes perfect sense when you consider the alternative is currently Stetson Bennett as Los Angeles’ QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports free agent QB Jimmy Garoppolo is considering retirement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: Garoppolo, 34, is the preferred backup for Matthew Stafford and the Rams after he spent the last two seasons serving as the Rams’ QB2. If he opts to continue playing, he will most likely return to the Rams on a one-year deal, but Garoppolo is reportedly considering hanging things up. The former second-round pick has started 64 games in his career, with 55 of those starts coming with the 49ers. He’s attempted just 41 passes over the last two seasons and did not attempt a pass in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: ESPN’s Sarah Barshop believes it’s “likely” the Rams will “take a modified approach with the number of throws [Matthew Stafford] takes leading up to the season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: In other words, like last year, expect Stafford to not be given all of the reps in training camp or (likely any of them) in preseason. This is mentioned as Barshop notes that the Rams have yet to address backup quarterback. Kirk Cousins, who was mentioned as a potential backup option, signed with the Raiders late last week. McVay said at the meetings that Jimmy Garoppolo’s return is “less likely than likely.” As things currently stand, Stetson Bennett would be getting a lot of training camp reps with the 1s. We expect there’ll be a different answer than that when it’s actually August, but that’s where things stand now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports free agent QB Jimmy Garoppolo is “weighing a few options.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: Garoppolo was linked to the Dolphins and Cardinals in early March, but both teams have brought new quarterbacks aboard since then. Per Atkins, the Rams’ “sights for a backup” have refocused on Garoppolo, now that the Raiders have signed QB Kirk Cousins. The Rams would reportedly “really would like an experienced former starter in that role.” Garoppolo spent the last two seasons in said role and turns 35 in November.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said Kirk Cousins could be a backup option they consider if Jimmy Garoppolo signs elsewhere.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: McVay said Garoppolo is “working through his process right now,” as the veteran QB remains unsigned nearly a month into free agency. McVay added that Garoppolo’s return “feels less likely than likely.” Cousins and McVay spent five seasons together in Washington, with McVay serving as Cousins’ offensive coordinator for three of those seasons. As Cousins seems more and more unlikely to land a starting job before the start of this season, a reunion with McVay in Los Angeles as Matthew Stafford’s backup could make a ton of sense for both sides, and give the Rams two solid veteran options at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports the Rams are interested in bringing back Jimmy Garoppolo, “but the market for him is fluid.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jimmy-garo.analysis: From the outside, it’s been a very puzzling free agency for Garoppolo. He was a rumored fit in Arizona and Miami, and it seemed like it was assumed that he’d return to the Rams when the Cardinals inked Gardner Minshew. But it’s been weeks since then and there’s been no clarity on his status. It sure doesn’t seem like there are better options for him out there than returning as the Rams backup — perhaps the Cardinals are considering trading Jacoby Brissett? — but the report of a fluid market suggests that maybe there are more teams interested than we know about.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Buccaneers signed QB Cooper Rush, formerly of the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush’s signing comes a day after it was reported that Baker Mayfield could miss Week 11’s game against the Lions due to a leg injury he suffered in Week 9. The decision to sign Rush suggests Mayfield is trending in the wrong direction early in the week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when they take the practice field. Rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels would be the favorite to start in the event Mayfield is sidelined, but Rush could be in line to serve as his backup. The 32-year-old vet struggled during his brief stint in Atlanta, throwing for 229-1-4 in two games while completing only 56.4 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons released Cooper Rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush’s release came after the Falcons signed Andy Dalton. Rush had a rough stretch with the Falcons, throwing for 229-1-4 in his two starts while completing 56.4 percent of his passes. Once regarded as one of the better backup quarterbacks in the league, Rush has struggled mightily in his two seasons away from the Cowboys, going 0-4 in his starts since 2024 while throwing one touchdown to eight interceptions. He could catch on elsewhere as a practice squad option in the coming days, but he seems like a long shot to start another game in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons declared Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB Malcom DeWalt IV, CB Roger Longerbeam, DE Jared Iven, and OL Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 4 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush will serve as the emergency quarterback over Jack Strand. LB Samsom Ebukam, who came into the weekend listed as questionable, will play against the Saints. The Falcons look to move into a tie atop the NFC South against their divisional opponent after beating the Packers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB Malcolm Dewalt, CB Robert Longerbeam, EDGE Samson Ebukam and OT Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 3 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush sits ahead of Strand on the depth chart and has been labeled as this evening’s emergency third quarterback. Hopefully, it doesn’t come to that. Week 3 marks QB Michael Penix’s return to action following last year’s season-ending knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Speaking Monday, Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski did not commit to naming a starting QB for Week 3’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: With the Falcons set to play on Thursday night, Stefanski will have little time to prepare his starter for the week. It’s hard to imagine the team going back to Cooper Rush after back-to-back disastrous starts to open the season, which could pave the way for rookie UDFA Jack Strand to make the start of Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) still aren’t ready to go. Strand completed 8-of-15 passes for 59 yards and an interception in his first taste of NFL action. Stefanski did say he had a “decent idea” of who he thinks he will be starting this week, so we’ll likely have our answer soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Cooper Rush completed 10-of-17 passes for 86 yards and two interceptions before being benched in the third quarter of the Falcons’ Week 2 game against the Panthers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush opened the game with a lost fumble on Atlanta’s first offensive play of the day. Things somehow got worse from there. He was intercepted twice and nearly threw a third, but it went through the hands of Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke. Rush was arguably the worst starter in the league in Week 1 and nothing changed in Week 2. With Michael Penix expected to make his 2026 debut next week, Rush may have just finished his final career start. Jack Strand will close this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons QB Cooper Rush will start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: It was reported earlier that Rush was expected to draw the start, but with Michael Penix Jr. (knee) officially ruled out, it will be Rush getting the ball against the Panthers. Rush struggled in last week’s game against the Steelers, throwing for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions on 22 attempts. Drake London shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR2 in fantasy this week with Rush under center, while Kyle Pitts profiles as a boom-or-bust TE1 after putting up zero fantasy points in Week 1. Jack Strand will serve as Rush’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cooper Rush is expected to start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush is taking all of the first-team reps with the Falcons in Friday’s practice, and according to Rapoport, sources familiar with the situation expect Rush to get the nod on Sunday. With Rush under center, all Falcons pass-catchers receive a substantial downgrade after he struggled to move the ball in Week 1 against the Steelers. Fantasy managers hoping Drake London and Kyle Pitts can be of some value against a Panthers defense that allowed 269 yards and two passing TDs to the Bears last week should approach both players with caution. London is best trusted as more of a WR2, while Pitts, who saw one target on 21 routes last week, shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in what figures to be a run-heavy game for the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons QB Cooper Rush (back) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush told reporters that he and QB Michael Penix (knee) split first-team reps, though the coaching staff already said Penix is not yet ready to take the field on game day. Rush or rookie QB Jack Strand will likely start, with QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said QB Cooper Rush is getting treatment for a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Stefanski on Wednesday wouldn’t rule out any of his four quarterbacks of the apocalypse, including rookie QB Jack Strand, who flashed in preseason action against second and third-team defenses. Rush as abysmal in the Falcons’ Week 1 loss to the Steelers. He was 10.5 percent below his expected pass rate, throwing for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two picks. There’s almost no way Strand would be a downgrade for Week 2 if he gets the nod. Michael Penix (knee) will continued to be sidelined and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is questionable at best. Strand should be picked up in superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins waived K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Shortly after being named the Dolphins’ full-time kicker, Gonzalez is once again looking for work. The 31-year-old had a rough outing against the Colts, going 1-for-3 on field goal attempts, missing on 47 and 51-yard attempts. He also missed an extra point in the 24-22 defeat. Gonzalez has made 6-of-10 field goals on the season and is 6-for-7 on extra-point tries. It wouldn’t be surprising if he found work elsewhere at some point in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Zane Gonzalez converted 1-of-3 field goal attempts in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez just recently became the Dolphins’ full-time kicker, but he missed two field goals and one extra point against the Colts. He had the opportunity to kick the go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter, but missed from 51 yards. He also missed a 47-yarder earlier in the game while making a 53-yarder and missing an extra point in the third quarter. In a game the Dolphins lost by two points, Gonzalez leaving seven points on the field certainly contributed towards the outcome of this game. If he is still on the team next week, Gonzalez should not be a fantasy option in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins signed Zane Gonzalez, formerly of the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez reportedly beat out Justin Tucker in a tryout for Miami and will sign with the team pending a physical. Gonzalez, a journeyman who has played for five teams since entering the NFL in 2017, will replace Riley Patterson, who has missed two of his seven field goal attempts in 2026. Gonzalez will not be a fantasy option in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins released K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez’s release seemingly bodes well for K Riley Patterson. The two veteran kickers were competing to replace K Jason Sanders, who signed with the Jets this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins agreed to terms with K Zane Gonzalez, formerly of the Falcons, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez converted 19 of his 22 field goal attempts and was 7-of-9 from 50-plus yards.
