https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Rico Dowdle is making progress in his attempt to return from a toe injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: McCarthy said he expects Dowdle and Jaylen Warren to be a “one-two punch” once Dowdle returns to the field. Warren has totaled 34 rushes over the last two weeks while rushing for 220 scoreless yards, but had a 21-89-0 line during the first two weeks of the season when Dowdle was active. Both backs will likely fall in the RB3/FLEX range if Dowdle suits up for Week 5’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns, adding 33 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren’s six targets combine with his 17 carries to give him his second consecutive game with more than 20 opportunities in the absence of Rico Dowdle, seeing all but two running back opportunities in the process. More impressive was the fact that he once again maintained elite efficiency on the ground through the additional touches, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt against a solid Browns run defense. The veteran back appears likely to revert to a strict timeshare with Dowdle expected back for Week 5 after the long week, bringing him back to the RB3 range for a meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, adding eight yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle played sparingly in the first half as the Steelers were completely incapable of moving the ball. In fact, Pittsburgh managed just 40 yards of total offense in the first half before losing 17 yards in the third quarter, leaving them with a putrid 23 yards of total offense through three quarters. The extremely negative game script clearly limited the backfield’s opportunities and production, with Dowdle unable to escape the onslaught. His next opportunity to return usable counting stats comes in Week 11 against the Eagles, where he’ll remain off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle looked good in this one, and while he didn’t hit the home run play that Jaylen Warren did, he was ripping off big gains throughout the day. Dowdle played just six fewer snaps than Warren, ran four fewer routes, and had two fewer carries, so he needs to be rostered as an RB3 who would have low-end RB2 value if Warren were to get hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed nine times for 48 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding six catches for 45 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was the clear backup to Jaylen Warren, but he was able to have a solid day thanks in large part to checkdowns from Aaron Rodgers. The 28-year-old had a long rush of 16 yards, and the toe injury that sidelined him earlier in the campaign doesn’t appear to be bothering him. Dowdle is a FLEX option for Week 8 against the Browns, at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is active for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The knee issue was new for Dowdle and limited him to three partial practices this week. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 on Friday. Dowdle will once again form the 1B portion of Pittsburgh’s backfield committee. He’s a low-end RB3 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s a new injury that popped up on Wednesday, but with two limited sessions we’re not overly concerned about Dowdle missing Sunday morning’s Civil Unrest Bowl in Paris. He’ll be in the RB3/FLEX discussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The Steelers will likely limit Dowdle’s reps for a few weeks as he manages the toe injury that cost him three games. He should be good to go for Sunday’s game by Friday. Dowdle saw 10 touches in his first game back and looked relatively explosive, running for 40 yards on seven attempts. He is in the RB3 mix for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed seven times for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was active for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. He initially formed a near 50-50 committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter pulled away in the fourth quarter and overtime. Warren racked up four carries and one catch in overtime alone, bringing his touch total from 11 to 16. Dowdle saw a single carry in the extra frame. Dowdle’s role should grow in the coming weeks, but it’s clear that Warren is the top option in the backfield, leaving Dowdle as a low-end RB3 for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle is back after missing three games with the toe issue. He will form a committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter’s elite play last week likely earned him a larger split of the backfield in Week 6. Dowdle will primarily operate between the tackles, pushing him to the back of the RB3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 15-of-29 passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Steelers’ 38-18, Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The final score doesn’t seem as bad as it was for Rodgers and the Steelers, who managed just 34 yards of total offense through three quarters as they fell to their division rivals in a game that decided the current division leader. Rodgers failed to complete his first eight passes, a mark that tied the longest stretch of incompletions to start a game of his illustrious career. Two fourth quarter touchdowns with the game already well out of reach padded Rodgers’ counting stats as well as making the game appear slightly closer than it played. The abysmal performance drops the Steelers to 6-3 and one game behind the Bengals for the lead in the AFC North, with the fact that the two teams split the season series the only saving grace as the Steelers look to make a second half push toward the postseason. Up next for Rodgers and the Steelers are the reeling Eagles on the road in Week 11, where Rodgers will remain a middling QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 13-of-25 passes for 172 yards and an interception in the Steelers’ 26-6, Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers wasn’t asked to do much in this game with the Steelers dominating on the ground, but he didn’t deliver many big plays on the chances he did have. Darnell Washington had a nice catch-and-run for a 58-yard gain, but the Steelers didn’t threaten down the field much throughout the game. The interception was certainly not Rodgers’ fault, however. He threw a great pass that hit DK Metcalf in the chest, but Metcalf popped the ball up into the air, and it was picked off. Rodgers is going to be a low-ceiling option in fantasy because the Steelers want to win with their defense and running game, but he should have better days than this. They won’t be in Week 9 though, since the Steelers are on a bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-30 passes for 219 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ 16-10, Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers dinked and dunked for the overwhelming majority of the game with over half of his completions coming to his running backs. He did connect with DK Metcalf for a 51-yard connection on a beautiful deep ball, and he found Darnell Washington for his lone scoring play. Outside of that passing touchdown, the biggest play for Rodgers was a scramble on third-and-six just before the two-minute warning that essentially cemented the game. Rodgers and the Steelers move to 5-2 with the win in Paris, and they’ll face the Browns in Week 8. He’ll be a QB2 for that contest, on paper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 33-of-49 passes for 253 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers and the Steelers couldn’t get anything going through three quarters. They had just three points on the board and Germie Bernard check-downs were their only method of moving the ball. Even that was barely working. Running out of options, Rodgers simply started forcing the ball to DK Metcalf. He targeted Metcalf 12 times in the fourth quarter and overtime. The Steelers scored 16 points in the fourth quarter and another seven in the extra frame. Rodgers now has at least 230 yards and multiple touchdowns in four straight games. The Steelers’ pass-crazed approach under Mike McCarthy has kept him in the QB2 mix so far, and it will do so again when he faces the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22, Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Steelers seemed worried about the Colts’ pass rush today, so there were a lot of quick-hit passes from Rodgers. The vast majority of them went to running backs or tight ends. Only nine of Rodgers’ 22 completions went to wide receivers, and 80 of his 235 passing yards came on a short pass to Jaylen Warren that the running back took up the sideline for a long touchdown. That’s not to say Rodgers didn’t play well. He did a good job avoiding sacks and not taking negative plays, but the Steelers’ offense didn’t look very potent outside of two explosive plays from Jaylen Warren. They may find things a little bit tougher against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-40 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Steelers’ 27-24, Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers was under constant pressure from an unrelenting Cleveland pass rush, taking five sacks while throwing two interceptions in the loss. The offense struggled to maintain consistent efficiency as the Steelers fell into a 21-7 hole in the second quarter, eventually requiring more Rodgers fourth quarter heroics to knot the game at 24 with under two minutes to play. That would be enough time for Deshaun Watson to get the Browns into field goal range for the go-ahead kick with 10 seconds remaining. With just one timeout in hand, the Steelers were forced into downfield aggression on the final play of the game, which resulted in the second of two Rodgers interceptions. The Steelers have now been involved in three one-score games through four weeks, something both Steelers fans and those familiar with head coach Mike McCarthy are all too familiar with - two of those games resulted in wins. Up next for Rodgers and the Steelers are the reeling Colts in Week 5, against whom Rodgers will remain a middling QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-34 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 30-27, Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers’ first throw of the game came on a 30-yard dump-off to Jaylen Warren, but three plays later, Rodgers would connect with a wide-open Roman Wilson down the left sideline for a 38-yard touchdown. That would be the first of two touchdowns Rodgers would throw in the first quarter, with his second coming on a play-action pass to Ben Skowronek for a 23-yard score. Rodgers and the offense would stall a bit in the second quarter, with an interception on a dropped pass by Roman Wilson highlighting their struggles, but in the second half, the Steelers would rip off four plays for 20-plus yards to keep the pressure on the Bengals’ defense. Rodgers threw a six-yard touchdown pass to DK Metcalf in the third quarter to put the Steelers up 24-20, and benefited from a long catch-and-run by Darnell Washington on a 47-yard play that helped set up an eventual field goal by Chris Boswell. This was easily the best game of the season for Rodgers, who averaged a solid 7.1 ADOT on his completed passes against a Bengals defense that was solid through the first two weeks. Despite the strong outing, Rodgers shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a QB2 in Thursday’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy “plans to pare down the game plan with the goal of executing the staple plays more consistently.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo penned a rather pessimistic assessment of the Steelers’ current state on Sunday night. We can’t necessarily blame him. The results have been disappointing. Perhaps thinning out the playbook will pay off. McCarthy believes QB Aaron Rodgers “could play with any volume of game plan, but at the end of the day, it’s a team game.” DeFabo notes that the Steelers moved WR DK Metcalf into the slot at times, attempting to avoid Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez’s coverage, but Gonzalez surprisingly trailed him, and Metcalf turned in an inefficient outing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 23-of-39 passes for 189 yards, an interception and a fumble in the Steelers’ 20-3, Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers led an anemic offense in a defense-heavy matchup with the Patriots for Week 2. The Steelers began the day with a couple of three-and-outs and were unable to find chunk plays the whole game. Rodgers fumbled in the second quarter on a play that pushed the Steelers back 37 yards due to a game of pinball in an effort to scoop up the ball; the play kicked the Steelers out of field goal territory. He later fumbled for a Pats scoop-and-score in the fourth quarter. Rodgers’ second turnover was an interception coming off a Germie Bernard bobble in the fourth quarter. A 4.8 yards per attempt mark indicates an offense that cannot push the ball downfield. Fantasy managers will not see chunk gains from Rodgers, who should be a fantasy QB3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 24-of-40 passes for 221 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ 20-13, Week 1 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers averaged just 5.5 yards per completion and didn’t complete a single pass over 20 yards downfield, going 0-for-6. He was also just 4-for-14 for 64 yards when he was under pressure. That being said, he also didn’t make many bad decisions and threw a couple of beautiful passes in tight windows over the middle of the field. It’s a new season, but this doesn’t really feel much like a new Steelers’ offense, which means the ceiling might be low when it comes to fantasy production. Rodgers remains just a QB2 option next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 6-of-7 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the Niners.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy’s seven targets were good for third-most among all Cowboys pass-catchers in this one. The third-year receiver hauled in a 23-yard catch in the third quarter, and broke free from his defender in the end zone on a fourth-and-six in the fourth quarter for an 11-yard touchdown as the Cowboys were hoping to mount a comeback. Flournoy continues to prove himself as a reliable option whenever Dak Prescott looks his way, but his usage remains hard to predict as long as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are healthy. Fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance entering Week 11 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-3 targets for 53 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy had just one catch for seven yards until the final drive of the game, where he caught a 46-yard pass on the first play of the drive to instantly place the Cowboys into the red zone while trailing by three points. A Javonte Williams touchdown and Caleb Downs interception on the subsequent possession would be enough to send the Cowboys to 4-5 with a win. Fantasy managers must be left disappointed with the outing considering George Pickens was unable to go with a hamstring injury. Flournoy will be a shaky FLEX option in Week 10 against the 49ers, regardless of the status of Pickens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: He added a DPI at the two-yard line to set up another score, and dropped another pass in the red zone. It’s clear that he’s cutting into George Pickens’ production at this point; Flournoy has gone over 90 yards or scored in three of his last four starts. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play next week against the Colts, although the Cowboys may abandon the pass at some point in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught all four targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is not typically going to see elite volume while playing alongside two true alphas in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but he continues to outproduce tight end Jake Ferguson as the preferred third option through the air. His big play potential showed against the Eagles as he caught a 35-yard dime early. Flournoy is, at minimum, worthy of a bench spot and could work his way into viable FLEX territory with another solid outing against the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 7-of-9 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: While the yardage totals continue to remain modest for the third-year receiver, his emergence as a trusted WR3 in the offense has led to him out-targeting tight end Jake Ferguson in five of six games through the first third of the season. That’s a role that can return usable FLEX production in the right matchups in the typically high-powered Cowboys offense, adding to his high-end handcuff value. Fantasy managers can continue to stash FLournoy ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the division rival Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy continues to operate as the clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, typically incapable of returning viable fantasy production in their shadows. He hit for a 48-yard reception at the end of the second quarter to set up a go-ahead field goal entering the break, otherwise remaining about as quiet as we would expect. This was the first game in 2026 over a modest 37 yards for Flournoy, who could be tasked with additional emphasis in the immediate future after Lamb departed with a quad injury in the fourth quarter. He could be worth a speculative add ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy has been held to exactly 22 or 23 yards in each of his first three games of the season, but the trend of Dallas passing more is pretty good for him. He’s got 21 targets over his last three games. It’s not anything beyond FLEX production yet but Thursday night games can be weird and that’s where Dallas will be next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: The veteran receiver inked a one-year contract extension this offseason to retain his supporting role in the high-powered Dallas offense, but the early returns were less than inspiring. Flournoy played 41 of 58 snaps, nearly every-down work, but the Cowboys just didn’t get enough play volume to let him spike a ceiling week. It’ll be hard for Flournoy to return consistent fantasy production for as long as both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remain healthy. He’ll be a boom-bust WR4 in a plus matchup against the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys signed Ryan Flournoy to a one-year, $6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is now under contract through the 2027 season. The 26-year-old receiver caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, while finishing third among Cowboys receivers in routes run (273) and fourth on the team in targets. It was reported earlier this summer that he was seeing more snaps in the slot, but it’s hard to imagine Flournoy making enough of an impact to be fantasy-relevant as long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Ryan Flournoy “has worked in the slot more” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Archer mentioned Flournoy as the biggest surprise for the Cowboys so far this offseason. The third-year receiver totaled 40 catches for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, and played 34.4 percent of his snaps in the slot. The Cowboys ran the fourth-most plays from 11 personnel last season, per TruMedia. While it’s possible that Flournoy’s increased slot role leads to more production, fantasy managers should take this with a grain of salt. As long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy, Flournoy will face an uphill climb to improve on the 3.8 targets per game he averaged last season. That said, if either Lamb or Pickens were to miss time, Flournoy could have some streaming upside in deeper leagues after he posted a few 100-plus yard games last season in games where either Pickens or Lamb were sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 16 times for 59 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason’s 16 carries and 59 yards both led all Vikings players. It was his first double-digit touch game since Week 7 against the Colts, but despite the encouraging touch share, he still lacked the high-value touches near the goal line. Aaron Jones handled all four of the Vikings’ goal-to-go rush attempts, leaving Mason to rely on long scores. Mason will be hard to trust as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed six times for 35 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings managed only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, completely incapable of moving the football with Carson Wentz under center. Those shortcomings confined Mason to only eight touches for the second consecutive week. Mason is not a starter-worthy fantasy asset until, or unless, the quarterback situation in Minnesota drastically improves ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason had eight rushes for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in carries, as Aaron Jones — who came into the game with a knee issue — saw five rushing attempts on the day. Jones remained the team’s pass-catching option out of the backfield while Mason could not get anything going on the ground against a middling Lions rush defense. Mason, who had 15 carries last week, will remain a touchdown-dependent RB3 option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason did not start for the Vikings, but out-touched and out-snapped Aaron Jones. He was the primary early-down back and saw two targets as well, though he did not catch either of them. Jones (knee) exited the game in the fourth quarter, leading to Mason finishing out the game for the Vikings. Even before the Jones injury, Mason was the the back with the highest utilization. Mason is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions; he could emerge as a top-15 option if Jones misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. He should tentatively be expected to lead the backfield in carries right away, with Aaron Jones potentially settling into a 1B role. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings designated Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open; most of the reporting is that the Vikings expect him to play in Week 7. Assuming that’s the case, we expect to see him hit the ground running on the Wednesday practice report with at least a limited session and perhaps a full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s cold streak continued in a miserable game for Tyler Shough, who averaged 5.3 yards per attempt with an average depth of target of 4.5. The emergence of Jordyn Tyson, who led the Saints with 13 targets against Carolina, is going to take away targets from Vele. He might hold some PPR appeal in Week 11 against the Bears, but not much. Vele has more than four catches in a game just once in the past five weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: As expected, the return of Jordyn Tyson brought about the end of Vele’s time as a WR3 fantasy option. Though Vele got his normal complement of routes, Tyson out-targeted him 5-4. He also went for more yards on two extra catches. Tyson’s role is only going to grow as he gets more practice reps under his belt. Fantasy managers can thank Vele for the good times and send him to the waiver wire on this week’s run. He will be buried in the WR5/6 range for Week 10 versus the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele brought in a one-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal late in the second quarter to tie the game at 10-10. It would be the last points the Saints would score. Vele has hovered around these numbers through the first half of 2026, and while he provides Shough with a nice safety valve, it’s not exactly what fantasy managers should be chasing. He’ll be a WR4 in Week 9 against the Browns after the Saints “enjoy” their bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The Saints offense has not pushed the ball downfield over the past two weeks, leading to low-scoring outputs for Vele. He caught three passes on the day, and nearly reeled in a fourth catch on a Tyler Shough sideline overthrow in the second quarter. When the Saints aren’t in a pass-happy game script, Vele is relegated to touchdown-dependent FLEX value. He will be in the WR4 ranks against the Steelers for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 4-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Tyler Shough managed a dismal 96 passing yards in this game, so there simply wasn’t enough production for any New Orleans wideout to post usable fantasy numbers. Vele still tied Chris Olave for a team-high in targets. He has at least four catches and six targets in every game this year. Even after a quiet Week 5, Vele remains a solid WR4 option headed into a Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s nine targets ranked behind only alpha Chris Olave, although he was headed for another modest fantasy outing before a garbage time touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the blowout loss. Vele has yet to eclipse 69 yards through the first month of play as he continues to operate in an intermediate role for a Saints team struggling to attack downfield. Fantasy managers could consider sitting Vele against the ferocious Vikings defense in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints’ loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele nearly added a decent first-down pickup to his box score, but he was unable to secure the pass as he was diving to the ground. Aside from that, he had a nice 17-yard gain in which he ripped his leg away from a would-be tackler and scampered away for a few extra yards. Vele is a boom-bust FLEX against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It was another solid outing for Vele, who has now caught 12 passes for 133 yards and one touchdown in his first two games this season. Vele’s biggest play came on a third-and-eight when he hauled in a 29-yard reception to extend a drive that ended with a Daniel Carlson field goal. Vele is the clear-cut WR2 for the Saints at this point and could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues next week as a WR3/WR4 in Week 3 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-4 targets for 19 yards in the Packers Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: That makes it back-to-back one-catch weeks for Kraft, who has totaled just two receptions for 20 yards on seven targets. While this can partly be blamed on a tough matchup against a stout Vikings defense, it’s worth remembering that Kraft often produces for fantasy managers despite lacking elite volume at times. His 52 routes run over the last week are tied with Dalton Schultz for 11th-most among tight ends, but the ball just hasn’t been finding him as of late. Despite the frustrating usage, he should be in the mix when the Packers return from their bye as a fringe TE1 in Week 12 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Interestingly, Kraft had a more productive day on the ground (2-8-0) in what was a quiet day for the 26-year-old tight end. His quiet day can be partly blamed on a hyper-efficient passing attack that saw Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combine for 335 of the 372 receiving yards the Packers managed on the day. The three targets Kraft saw tied a season low, and he averaged 6.7 targets per game over his last six games. He will look to bounce back next week at home against the Vikings and will profile as a low-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-6 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft found the end zone on a 14-yard touchdown near the end of the second quarter, giving him his second touchdown of the season and his first since Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Kraft has seen six or more targets in four of his last five games and has posted double-digit PPR points in three of his last four. Even when he isn’t finding the end zone, his volume, coupled with his big-play ability, is enough to keep him in the TE1 conversation. Kraft gets a nice matchup next week against the Panthers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were also his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-7 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Jordan Love made it a point to get Kraft going in this game, peppering him with easy-button targets throughout the contest. Kraft led the team with a 23 percent target share. His six grabs also led the team and are a new season high. He found the end zone with an impressive toe-dragging catch at the goal line. Kraft is still looking for the explosive play, but the team is getting him more involved every week. He is back in the TE1 ranks after a slow couple of weeks to start the season. Kraft will look to stay hot versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft, who tore his ACL in Week 9 last year, told reporters he would not be on a snap count in Week 1. He was. Kraft ran 20 routes to Jonnu Smith’s 18. The good news is that Kraft looked as explosive as ever, racking up gains of 30, 23, and 12 yards. Even with the weak route rate, this goes down as a win for a player whose game is built around big plays. His route rate should climb in the coming weeks, keeping him in the TE1 mix versus the Jets next Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-2 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed ran a route on 17 of 25 Seattle drop backs but was again not a part of the passing attack. Cooper Kupp and Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught touchdowns from Drew Lock as Shaheed ran empty routes. Headed into the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye, Shaheed has two games on the season with more than three receptions and he has not scored a receiving touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: He’ll return to his boom/bust fantasy role as Seattle’s field-stretcher and punt returner after missing a few weeks due to this knee injury. Shaheed practiced in full all week and should not have any real limitations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed has missed the last two weeks with a knee injury, but he was able to practice in full to open Week 10. A full practice participation is a good sign we’ll see Shaheed on the field for Week 10 against the Raiders. He has been splitting WR2 opportunities with Cooper Kupp this year and belongs on fantasy benches until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Also not practicing is OT Charles Cross (ankle). Both missed Week 8 against the Bears and are still out with their respective injuries to open the week. They will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at returning for the Seahawks offense in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) remained sidelined for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable heading into Monday evening’s game against the Bears. If he was in your third receiver or second FLEX spot in a 14-team league, it is time to start making other plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the “early returns are positive” on Rashid Shaheed’s knee injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Macdonald didn’t elaborate on how much time Shaheed could miss, if any, but it doesn’t sound like this is expected to be a long-term injury based on what he had to say on Monday. Shaheed’s impact is largely felt in the punt and kick return game, as he has just 16 receptions for 163 scoreless yards on the season for Seattle. We will update his practice status throughout the week, but Shaheed won’t have any fantasy relevance even if he does suit up next week against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Myles Price caught 4-of-4 targets for 49 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price scored his first career touchdown in the first quarter when he hauled in a 38-yard pass from Kirk Cousins on a third-and-23 to put the Vikings up 10-0. Cousins displayed good anticipation on the throw to Price, who found a hole between three defenders. Price hauled in the pass, bounced off a defender, and turned upfield for the long score to give Cousins his first touchdown pass in a Vikings uniform since 2023. Price has now run 20-plus routes in back-to-back weeks while lining up in the slot over 70 percent of the time. He won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Vikings agreed to terms with WR Myles Price.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The 23-year old Price played four seasons at Texas Tech before transferring to Indiana in 2024. He caught 38 passes for 466 yards with three touchdowns in his final collegiate season. His 289 punt return yards ranked fifth most in FBS in 2024, while he forced a Power 4-best 24 missed tackles on punt returns per Pro Football Focus. He went undrafted last week but will compete for a roster spot in Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas freshman WR Myles Price (ankle) and sophomore WR Loic Fouonji (undisclosed) have both been ruled out for Saturday’s game against Baylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'10/180) has been one of the Red Raiders’ most productive pass-catchers this season, so his absence will have an impact. The freshman has caught 35 passes for 451 yards and two touchdowns this season. As for Fouonji (6'4/220), he’s been comparatively quiet, recording a 8-168-1 receiving line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas Tech freshman WR Myles Price (ankle) is considered a game time decision for the Red Raiders’ season finale at Baylor this Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'10/175) was injured on his first reception last Saturday against Oklahoma State when he caught a screen pass behind the line of scrimmage and was rolled up on during the ensuing tackle. It’s a tough break from the promising freshman who had just recorded his career-high with nine receptions for 175 yards and a touchdown the previous week in an upset against Iowa State. Price has steadily improved as the season progressed finishing with 35 receptions, 451 yards, 12.9 yards per reception and two touchdowns. His presence will be sorely missed against the ninth ranked Bears if hi is unable to suit up this Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas Tech freshman WR Myles Price caught nine passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in a 41-38 victory over Iowa State this Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'10/175) gave the Iowa State secondary fits all afternoon, leading both teams with 11 targets while averaging 19.4 yards per reception. He was instrumental in keeping the chains moving, running precise routes that got him consistently open. His best play was on a slant route where he used his savvy to turn the cornerback’s hips and gain five yards of separation, allowing Donovan Smith to hit him in stride for the 39-yard touchdown catch. This marks Price’s first 100-yard game of his young career with just his second touchdown. He will look to post another big game next week against Oklahoma State.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas Tech freshman WR Myles Price was carted off the field after suffering an apparent left lower leg injury during the first half of Saturday’s game vs. Baylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'10/175) was initially taken to the team injury tent, but shortly thereafter he was carted to the Texas Tech football facility for further evaluation. No official declaration has been made regarding his status for the remainder of Saturday’s game, but the odds of a return appear to be slim. Price was responsible for six rushing yards (one carry) and five receiving yards (one reception) prior to his exit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas Tech freshman WR Myles Price brought in seven receptions for 79 yards in a 34-27 win over West Virginia on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price wasn’t able to find the end zone, but it was easily the best game of the 5-foot-10, 175-pound wideouts young career. He had a long gain of 44, and made a couple more key catches for the Red Raiders to give Texas Tech a much-needed victory. Price appears to have a bright future, and he should be a part of the game plan next Saturday against Oklahoma.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Texas Tech received a verbal commitment from three-star 2020 ATH Myles Price, who had previously been committed to Oklahoma State.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'8/161) had committed to the Cowboys in the middle of June, but it was a short engagement, as he’s decided instead that he’ll be playing in Lubbock. For now, anyway. He also had offers from schools like Arizona State, Boston College, Boise State and several more institutions. He’s rated the 39th best “athlete” in the class -- he’ll likely play wideout on Saturdays for the Red Raiders -- and 81st among all players in the always loaded state of Texas in the 247Sports rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma State received a verbal commitment from three-star 2020 ATH Myles Price.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price (5'8/161) is a smaller but explosive player who recorded a 4.59-second 40-yard dash at The opening regional on March 3rd. He chose Oklahoma State over Arizona State, Boise State, and Boston College among others. He’s the 45th ranked athlete in the country and 94th ranked player in Texas. Oklahoma State now has the 24th ranked recruiting class for 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnson in the flailing New Orleans offense. Johnson, who doesn’t have more than 40 yards in a game since Week 4, ran a pass route on 31 of 46 Saints drop backs. His involvement hasn’t led to much in the way of production. Johnson should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson split reps with Noah Fant and Oscar Delp once again. He had one catch headed into overtime but made the most of the extra drive with a game-winning touchdown grab. It was his first touchdown since Week 3. This was also his first multi-catch game since Week 5. With Jordyn Tyson set to take on a larger role in the coming weeks, Johnson’s days as a high-end TE2 appear to be over. Fantasy managers can do better off the waiver wire in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was solid over the first four weeks of the season, but this was another clunker for the 30-year-old tight end. After going over 50 yards in his first four games and bringing in three touchdowns, Johnson has just 23 total yards without a score in the next three. Because of positional value Johnson can’t be completely ignored, but the Saints haven’t paid much attention to him lately, so it’s time to look for alternatives, at least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch either of his two targets in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was silent in a low-efficiency passing day for the Saints offense. The tight end position in general was a non-factor as a pass-catching group on the day. As Tyler Shough deals with broken bones in his non-throwing hand, the Saints’ passing game is tightening up and has less room for Johnson. He is a fantasy TE2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 6-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson saw a slight uptick in snaps and routes after Noah Fant was inactive with an abdominal injury but returned a modest receiving line while being kept out of the end zone. The towering veteran finished third on the team in targets behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, the latter of whom scored the only receiving touchdown in a game that saw the two teams combine for seven rushing scores. Johnson remains a back-end TE1 for as long as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined, which appears likely to persist for another few weeks, at minimum. That holds true ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the vaunted Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 8-of-8 targets for 53 yards, two touchdowns and one lost fumble in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was getting open at will on out routes and shallow crossers. He and Noah Fant, along with the two Raiders tight ends, combined for six touchdowns, tying an NFL positional record. Johnson fumbled while trying to make a big play for his team late in the game. He attempted to stiff-arm Nakobe Dean, who cleanly punched the ball out for Eric Stokes to recover. Tyler Shough threw a bad pass to Johnson earlier on, which CB Hezekiah Masses easily picked off and returned downfield. Johnson raced after him and successfully punched the ball out with a diving hammer-fist, but the Raiders ultimately recovered that fumble, leading to a turnover for the Saints. Johnson remains a reliable TE1 against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 targets for 66 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was on the receiving end of two big plays in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. Johnson hauled in a short pass on a third-and-13 in the third quarter and turned it upfield for a 25-yard gain. In the fourth quarter, Johnson again picked up 25 yards on a short pass on third-and-eight, taking it to the Ravens’ five-yard line and setting the Saints up for a touchdown a few plays later. Johnson has caught seven passes in his first two games and is averaging an impressive 17.1 YPR on said catches. He’ll be on the TE2 radar for next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson posted a 3/54/1 receiving line last week and can be treated as a TE1 again in Week 2. Saints WR1 Chris Olave is nursing a hamstring strain, though the team is telling reporters that the injury is not concerning. Johnson could take on a slightly larger workload if Olave is at all limited, though we won’t know if that is the case until the dust settles and the game ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Meanwhile, Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for a meager 18 yards and again took all the pass-catching work out of the Raiders backfield. Washington will see decent rush volume when the Raiders see neutral or positive game script. How often that will happen in the coming weeks is another matter entirely. Washington should not be played in most fantasy formats next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: At least for one week, the Raiders formalized Washington’s early-down takeover, as the rookie out-carried a doghoused Ashton Jeanty 25-2. However, Washington got routinely stood up on his ample goal-line opportunities, and only out-gained Jeanty 83-73 thanks to Jeanty’s involvement in the passing game. A 45-yard reception where Jeanty literally fell down to catch an inaccurate Kirk Cousins pass only to get up and rumble nearly half the length of the field was by far the biggest play by a Raiders running back in this one. Although Washington now has to be considered the favorite for early-down work, he was uninspiring enough this afternoon that it’s not going to be an open-and-shut case against the 49ers. We would still rather start Jeanty in fantasy because of his pass catching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As usual, Washington was far more efficient than lead back Ashton Jeanty, who had 15 yards on eight carries while catching eight passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. Washington can be stashed for now in case Jeanty misses time in the second half of the season. Washington likely won’t get the pass-catching work if Jeanty misses time, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is active for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whether Washington plays all that much remains to be seen. He is not a recommended FLEX starter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has misdirected at times with injury-related comments. The Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker IV, DE Cian Slone, S Dalton Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, G Bryan Cabeldue, S Tristin McCollum and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 7 against the Rams. O’Connell will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers will be reevaluated on Monday after suffering an ankle injury in Las Vegas’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Kubiak told reporters that the team has not yet determined the injury’s severity. Tomorrow’s tests will provide more info. Bowers injured his ankle in the first quarter and was taken into the blue medical for examination. He managed to return for Fernando Mendoza’s 10-yard touchdown run, but was taken to the locker room after that. Bowers then returned to the field early in the second quarter, catching a 12-yard pass on third down. Unfortunately, his ankle wasn’t feeling right and he was again taken back to the locker room before later being ruled out. His day ended with two catches for 18 yards. The Raiders face the Broncos and Browns before going on bye in Week 13. Hopefully, he is able to return before then. Michael Mayer will be a TE1 if Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: The Vegas passing attack was snuffed out from start to finish by an elite Seattle defense. Mayer could see a marked increase in targets if Brock Bowers misses time with the ankle injury he sustained in the first quarter. Mayer, who was productive earlier this season when Bowers was sidelined with injury, would be a legit streaming option in Week 11 against Denver if Bowers is out. The Broncos allow the tenth most fantasy points per target to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was second on the team in pass routes behind Brock Bowers. He nearly had not one, but two touchdown catches on the day. Mayer had the ball knocked out of his hand as he reached for the goal line in the first half, and was called for pass interference on a short touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. It was a tough luck day for the Raiders’ TE2. With 15 receptions over the past three games coming into Week 9, Mayer is usable in deeper formats going forward. He gets the Seahawks in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This was Mayer’s fourth five-catch outing of the season. Only Brock Bowers caught more passes this afternoon. It could have been a bigger day in fantasy, but Mayer’s unconverted look was an inaccurate goal-line pass he short-armed. Mayer has a reasonable enough PPR TE2 floor, but his spiked week potential remains limited enough that he is not a very exciting streamer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer benefited from a pass-heavy second half for the Raiders as they once again faced a big deficit. He ran a pass route on 38 of the Raiders’ 49 drop backs. With four games of at least five targets, Mayer profiles as a desperation play in tight end premium games and a 12-team option if Brock Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer and the rest of the Vegas pass catchers took a backseat to Brock Bowers, who had a team-leading ten targets for 110 yards and a touchdown before the Raiders pulled their starters in the fourth quarter of this blowout loss. Mayer was fresh off an 82-yard outing (on ten targets) against Kansas City. He should remain on waivers ahead of Week 6’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 8-of-10 targets for 82 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer’s 10 targets were just one fewer than what Brock Bowers (11) saw on the day. Mayer made the most of his opportunities, racking up 82 yards—the second most in his career and saw four of his receptions come on the Raiders’ first four drives of the game. On the Raiders’ fourth drive, Mayer hauled in passes of two, seven, and 17 yards, with his longest catch setting up a 48-yard field goal just before halftime to put them up 13-10. We shouldn’t expect this level of production from Mayer on a weekly basis, but the Raiders’ underwhelming WR corps could pave the way for more opportunities for Mayer going forward after this solid outing. There’s a lot to like here, but Mayer will be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Patriots until we see reliable target totals on a more consistent basis, while he shares the field with Brock Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer scored with just under six minutes left in the first half. Coach Klint Kubiak sent Brock Bowers in motion, back and forth across the formation, behind the line of scrimmage, before Kirk Cousins executed the play-action fake. Mayer ran an out route from the slot and shook Saints defender Justin Reid on the cut before quickly hauling in the pass. Mayer’s other two catches both went for double-digit yardage gains. He will be a viable TE2 moving forward, with defenses focused on stopping Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Brock Bowers missed his second game of the year while recovering from a mensicus trim procedure, giving Mayer another opportunity to start. He led the Raiders in routes but failed to make a big impact in the box score, logging a measly 14 percent target share. Mayer is generally in the TE2 mix when Bowers is out, but even then he isn’t a particularly high-upside option. With Bowers expected to return next week, Mayer can be sent back to the waiver wire on the upcoming waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for 18 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, adding four catches for 46 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty was the Raiders’ leading receiver with Brock Bowers sidelined with an ankle injury. His 38-yard catch and run was by far the biggest play of the day for a lifeless Vegas offense with Fernando Mendoza under center for his first start of his NFL career. As usual, Jeanty operated as the primary pass catcher out of the backfield, running 26 routes to just eight routes for Mike Washington, who had a meager 23 yards on eight carries. Jeanty will be a top-24 PPR option next week against Denver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best.
