It continues to appear as if Kupp’s fantasy-relevant days are far behind him, with the veteran best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 7 showdown against the Chiefs on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 4-of-5 targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp took advantage of the Commanders double-teaming Jaxon Smith-Njigba and walked into the end zone on the fourth touchdown throw from Sam Darnold. It’s his first score of the season, and it’s a season high in receiving yards for the former star. Kupp will try and build on this in Week 4 in a matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will not be fantasy-relevant in 12-team managed leagues this week, but he could be an option in single-game DFS tournaments. If QB Sam Darnold (glute) can play, he will appreciate having Kupp on the field with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp got involved on the Seahawks’ fifth and sixth drives, but was quiet outside of that. The 33-year-old wide receiver entered the game with a back injury, though he logged two full practice sessions, so it is unlikely to have meaningfully impacted him. He nabbed his second reception during the Seahawks’ two-minute drill at the end of the first half, but he was unable to get out of bounds, allowing precious seconds to tick away. Kupp is a WR5/FLEX against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Ronnie Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Rivers functioned exclusively as a special teams player right up until the Rams’ final drive, which began with 12 minutes and 15 seconds remaining in the game, at the Rams’ four-yard line. Rivers ran the ball on 15 consecutive plays, with carry results ranging from minus-one to 16 yards, while taking exactly 11 minutes off the clock. Matthew Stafford knelt it out from there. Rivers will not be on the fantasy radar in Week 12 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye, but it was an encouraging performance for the team’s No. 3 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams placed Ronnie Rivers (calf) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Sean McVay said Rivers will miss 4-6 weeks. The team will call up one of Dean Connor or Jordan Waters from the practice squad for Week 3. Rivers doesn’t play much on offense, but he would normally be in line for backup duties if something happened to Kyren Williams or Blake Corum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams signed RB Ronnie Rivers to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Rivers has been Los Angeles’ third back for most of the last four years, rushing 72 times for 295 yards in the process. He has not crossed the 100-snap threshold on offense, but does play plenty on special teams. Rivers probably won’t ever be a fantasy cog, but he’s a useful depth back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams waived OL AJ Arcuri.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: The 2022 second-round pick will seek work elsewhere. The Rams also waived OL A.J. Arcuri, OL Wyatt Bowles, WR Tru Edwards, DT Jack Heflin, S Tanner Ingle, CB Derion Kendrick, CB Cam Lampkin, OL Dylan McMahon, OLB Jamil Muhammad, ILB Elias Neal, DL Bill Norton, ILB Chris Paul Jr., WR Brennan Presley, RB Ronnie Rivers, RB Cody Schrader, S Nate Valcarcel, CB Charles Woods, WR Britain Covey, OLB Brennan Jackson, TE Mark Redman, WR Drake Stoops, WR Jordan Waters, OL Willie Lampkin IV and CB Shaun Jolly. The Rams released CB A.J. Green.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said WR Konata Mumpfield (ankle) won’t miss any time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Great news. Mumpfield earned McVay’s praise with his “smart and conscientious” play last week. It will be difficult for him to make his way onto the re-draft radar this year but he is a name to know for dynasty leagues. McVay added that RB Ronnie Rivers (ribs) and TE Anthony Torres (ankle) will both miss “a little bit of time.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams re-signed RB Ronnie Rivers to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Rivers joined the Rams as a UDFA in 2022 and has appeared in 34 games over the last three seasons. The former Fresno State Bulldog rushed 22 times for 99 scoreless yards last season, and has a career rushing line of 63-249-0. Rivers has also caught 15 passes for 85 scoreless yards. He got some late-season run after Blake Corum went down for the remainder of the season with a forearm injury, but Rivers enters the 2025 season again needing injuries ahead of him to be a factor in the backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Rams signed RB Royce Freeman to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: The 28-year-old back got in to 14 games for the Rams in 2023 and will be Los Angeles’ replacement for Blake Corum in the playoffs. Ronnie Rivers is expected to get most of the RB2 reps for the Rams behind Kyren Williams in the playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Ronnie Rivers had 12 rushes for 49 yards in the Rams’ Week 18 loss against the Seahawks, adding four catches for 33 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Rivers operated as the team’s lead back with Kyren Williams resting alongside other Rams starters and Blake Corum sidelined with a forearm injury he sustained in the first half. Rivers was third on the team in targets and had a nearly every-down role in the final two quarters. He won’t see postseason action unless Williams and Corum go down to injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Blake Corum (forearm) exited the Rams’ Week 18 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: He’s listed as questionable to return but has next to no chance to see another snap in a meaningless game for LA. Entering the game as the Rams’ top back with Kyren Williams inactive alongside other LA starters, Corum had two carries for ten yards before leaving the game. Ronnie Rivers is in line to be the Rams’ lead back for the rest of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.headline: Ronnie Rivers rushed six times for 26 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ronnie-riv.analysis: Rivers rotated into the backfield as the Rams’ No. 2 back in the second quarter of the team’s loss to the Bears. His best run went for 11 yards and he totaled 26 yards on six carries. Meanwhile, Blake Corum was not heard from at all this week. Rivers can be left on fantasy benches heading into Week 5 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-10 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba, as usual, accounted for well over half of the Seahawks’ receiving yardage, with no other Seattle pass catcher seeing more than three targets on the day. JSN’s catch-and-run touchdown came on a perfectly placed ball from Drew Lock after he was flushed out of the pocket. This marked JSN’s eighth 100-yard receiving performance in 2026; he has at least ten targets in all but two games this season. JSN has the strongest fantasy profile in quite some time. The Seahawks are on bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 7-of-10 targets for 51 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over he Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: The fact that 54 yards is something to talk about says enough about the year Smith-Njigba is having, still handily leading the league in receiving despite the down performance. He remained the clear top dog through the air, receiving 10 targets on only 28 Lock pass attempts, largely confined to short area work as the Seahawks struggled to decipher the zone-heavy and two-high-heavy Arizona defense. Lock suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter that could place his Week 10 status in doubt, despite not missing an offensive snap, meaning fantasy managers of Smith-Njigba will want to monitor the situation ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders considering Sam Darnold remains unlikely to play with a multi-week injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6-of-11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba was the entire offense in the first half, accumulating 92 yards through the air while the rest of the offense managed only two, including his receiving touchdown. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made adjustments after the break that confined JSN to only 26 additional yards the rest of the way. Smith-Njigba now has seven 100-yard receiving games in eight appearances as he extended his league-leading yardage totals, far and away the top overall wide receiver in fantasy circles. That position will not change ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Is there anyone in the league doing it better than Smith-Njigba at the moment? The reigning receiving leader put on an absolute show in this one, making two nearly identical bread basket catches down the left sideline in the second quarter, the first of which he snuck inside the pylon for his touchdown. He was forced out at the two on the second, resulting in an end zone interception from Sam Darnold two plays later. Those two long receptions before the break helped push Smith-Njigba to 126 yards and a touchdown before halftime, and he added an additional 24 yards on three more receptions in the final two frames as the Seahawks transitioned to a more ground-heavy attack while playing with the lead. Fantasy’s early-season cheat code has now gone over 100 yards in six of seven games while notching a league-leading eight receiving touchdowns. It goes without saying, but Smith-Njigba remains the overall WR1 in a solid matchup against the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury in Week 5 and was limited in practice this week before getting a full designation on Wednesday. Despite the short week ahead of a Thursday matchup against the Broncos, he is off the injury report and good to go. Smith-Njigba is once again a top-three wide receiver option for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba gets a second-straight “limited” practice designation. The Seahawks have technically not practiced yet this week but it is notably the 24-year-old receiver gets back-to-back limited designations. With a Thursday matchup against the Broncos on the horizon for Week 6, the Seahawks are leaving the door open for Smith-Njigba to play; he battled the ankle injury in Week 5 and the short week makes this a tougher evaluation. For now, we still expect Smith-Njigba to play against the Broncos on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks listed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: With the Seahawks preparing to face the Broncos on a short week, it would be a bit more concerning if JSN were listed as a DNP. The team listing him as limited on the first day of the week is encouraging after he clearly battled through an ankle injury in Week 5’s loss to the 49ers. Smith-Njigba still topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time this season and made several big plays despite being in visible pain. We’ll continue to update his practice status throughout the week, but as long as he’s active come Thursday, JSN should be in your fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-8 targets for 102 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding one rush for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: JSN appeared to be playing through a bit of an ankle injury in this one, but he looked perfectly fine when he turned what would have been a short two-yard reception upfield for a 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks were attempting a comeback, JSN hauled in a 35-yard reception, evading multiple defenders to get the Seahawks to the 50-yard line. A few plays later, he would drop a wide-open pass that may have set the Seahawks up for a game-winning field goal opportunity, but JSN did his part to keep the Seahawks in what proved to be a sloppy game for the offense as a whole. He’s gone for 100-plus yards in four of his first five games of the season and will look for his fifth 100-yard game on Thursday night when the Seahawks visit the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-6 targets for 78 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: For the first time this year, Smith-Njigba was held out of the end zone. It was a quiet day fore the star wideout, but if 78 yards is your worst day (so far), well, you’ve had a pretty good season. JSN and fantasy managers will hope for a return to the end zone and a little more volume against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Tutu Atwell caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell’s lone catch came via a crisp corner route from the slot on the Rams’ first drive. His gaffe came via a post route on the Rams’ fifth drive that probably should have resulted in a 32-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, Atwell bricked it, mimicking a volleyball set while trying to high-point the pass inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line. He will be a boom-bust FLEX in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams OC Nate Scheelhaase wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell earned four targets last week, catching two for 52 yards. Increasing his workload could only mean one or two more targets, so Atwell does not need to be quickly picked up in 12-team formats. For those struggling at the wide receiver position, Atwell simply enters the boom-bust FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Tutu Atwell caught 2-of-4 targets for 52 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell made the biggest play of the day for the Rams, catching a perfectly placed 40 yard pass from Matthew Stafford. Atwell was second on the team in targets behind Puka Nacua, who had 12 targets on the day. Atwell should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, WR CJ Daniels, OL Bill Murray, TE Max Klare and QB Ty Simpson inactive for Week 1 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: The Rams acquired Atwell via trade in August. Although he already knows the system, coach Sean McVay evidently feels that Atwell is unnecessary for this one. Incumbent QB Stetson Bennett has officially defeated Simpson for the QB2 job. Simpson is inactive, but has been labeled the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams acquired WR Tutu Atwell from the Dolphins in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Back with his old team, Atwell is highly unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season, but he provides the Rams with a speed element that the offense was somewhat lacking. The move also indicates that TE Terrance Ferguson will not be asked to stretch the field as much as he did last year, freeing him up for a potential breakout campaign. Last week, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that Hunter has had a good training camp, showing “many of the rushing skills that had the Rams enamored enough to trade up and draft him in the fourth round last year.” He will likely compete for the No. 2 running back job in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Dolphins signed WR Tutu Atwell, formerly of the Rams, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: This will be Atwell’s first time playing for a team other than the Rams, who drafted him in the 2021 NFL Draft’s second round. Atwell spent time on injured reserve last season, dealing with a hamstring injury. Although he is unlikely to be a full-time, fantasy-relevant player with the Dolphins, his speed will help stretch the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, CB Derion Kendrick, RB Jarquez Hunter, TE Nick Vannett, OL Beux Limmer, QB Stetson Bennette, and DE Larrell Murchison inactive for Sunday’s NFC Championship Game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell is again a healthy scratch for the playoffs. The Rams did not have a player listed on their final injury report for the week and enter a tough road environment at near full strength as they look to win their third conference championship game under Sean McVay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, CB Derion Kendrick, RB Jarquez Hunter, S Tanner Ingle, TE Nick Vannett and OT DJ Humphries inactive for the Divisional Round against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Typically a valuable, role-playing field stretcher, Atwell just hasn’t been able to crack the Rams’ loaded skill corps rotation this season. Now 26 years old, it’s possible healthy-scratched Atwell has played his final game for the Rams as he heads to free agency this spring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Tutu Atwell (hamstring) will be activated from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell has been back at practice for a few weeks and is finally ready to return to action. He will play a part-time role on offense unless something happens to Puka Nacua or Davante Adams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams WR Tutu Atwell (hamstring) will not be activated off injured reserve for Week 14 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell remains on injured reserve despite practicing fully for two weeks. The team evidently feels comfortable with their current wide receiver corps, and we can’t really blame them. Still, keeping Atwell’s downfield speed on injured reserve rather than wielding it on occasional shot plays is surprising. It remains to be seen whether he will return for Week 15 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: CJ Daniels caught 1-of-2 targets for 22 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Daniels earned an end zone target on the Rams’ first drive, but Matthew Stafford unfortunately overthrew him. Daniels then snagged a 22-yard catch via a nine-route down the left sideline on the following drive. Unfortunately, his biggest impact on the game was a false start penalty that erased a five-yard receiving touchdown from Kyren Williams on the Rams’ fourth drive. The rookie wide receiver does not need to be held on rosters through the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue believes the Rams may take a committee approach to the WR3 role this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Rodrigue listed WR Konata Mumpfield and WR Jordan Whittington as candidates for the gig, notably excluding rookie WR CJ Daniels. Daniels was viewed as the potential WR3 due to his blocking ability earlier this year. Rodrigue says it is instead Whittington who could serve as the “3B” blocker. Mumpfield reportedly “looks the part” as the “3A” receiving component. Will he return fantasy value reliably? Probably not. Earlier this month, Rodrigue’s colleague, Nate Atkins, said Mumpfield could be the next man up on the perimeter if WRs Puka Nacua or Davante Adams miss time. Rodrigue’s comments seemingly confirm this.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams WR Konata Mumpfield “could be the primary backup on the perimeter” if WR Puka Nacua or WR Davante Adams miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Mumpfield enters his second NFL season after posting a 10/92/1 receiving line in the regular season last year. He chipped in three catches for 22 yards in the playoffs. Were he to get a spot start, he is not guaranteed to be fantasy-relevant. Atkins lists sixth-round rookie WR CJ Daniels as the most likely player to assume No. 3 wide receiver duties, primarily due to his blocking. He also has some contested-catch ability. Mumpfield is a name to know for 2026, but he is unlikely to meaningfully contribute in the box score if Nacua and Adams are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams WR CJ Daniels “is a strong fit for a third receiver role after blocking in one of college football’s most physical offenses.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: The statement comes with positives and negatives. On the one hand, Atkins believes the sixth-round rookie is the favorite to start in three-wide receiver sets. On the other hand, Daniels’ fit is due partially to his blocking ability. Getting on the field is the first step toward fantasy-relevance, though. Daniels is a player to watch closely in the coming months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Rams selected Miami WR CJ Daniels with the No. 197 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Daniels (6’2”/202) is a sixth-year prospect who made stops at Liberty (2020-2023) and LSU (2024) before finishing his career at Miami in 2025. What Daniels lacks in speed (4.58 40-yard dash), he makes up for with creative route running and an impressive ability to pull off contested catches (62.3 percent contested catch rate, per PFF). He’s a good downfield threat and broke out for 55/1,067/10 in 2023 at Liberty, but Daniels’ production fell off in his final two seasons when the level of competition was ramped up while playing for LSU and Miami. Given what we saw from Daniels in his post-Liberty career, it seems unlikely he will look like the player we saw in his breakout season when he’s facing NFL-caliber talent on every snap. He has very limited experience on special teams, returning just three punts in his career and never logging a single snap on the kick/punt coverage units. Despite his sixth-round pedigree, he’ll face an uphill battle to make a 53-man roster in his rookie season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that the Jaguars had a virtual meeting with Miami WR CJ Daniels.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: The Jaguars do not use top-30 visits. They prefer to keep their pre-draft information gathering under wraps. Jaguars general manager James Gladstone during his nine-year run with the Rams. Daniels revealed his meeting with the team in a recent interview. He has also met with the Titans, Broncos and Panthers. Daniels posted a 50/557/7 receiving line in his fifth and final college season. Shipley believes Daniels (6'2/202) could provide a big-bodied, physical element that is currently missing in the Jaguars’ wide receiver room. The Jaguars notably tried to sign Seahawks WR Jake Bobo (6'4/207) earlier this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Liberty redshirt freshman WR CJ Daniels WR caught eight receptions for 118 yards in Saturday’s loss to Army.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: This was not a good day for the Liberty offense as a whole. Army was able to keep quarterback Malik Willis one-dimensional for the most part having to rely on the passing attack. Daniels (6'1/195) and Willis had a good connection today as they had a couple of plays for some big yards, but the Army defense was good at making adjustments, putting pressure on Willis, especially on third and fourth downs, and stopping the drives. It’s certainly been a rough last stretch for Liberty as they end the season with three straight losses. The Flames will wait for their fate in the bowl season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Liberty redshirt freshman WR CJ Daniels caught seven passes for 135 yards and two touchdowns in Liberty’s 35-26 win over North Texas on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Daniels (6'1/195) found the end zone twice in this one, first on a 39-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Johnathan Bennett in the second quarter, and then again on a 20-yard touchdown pass from Malik Willis in the third quarter as Liberty attempted to rally from a 12-point deficit. This was Daniels’ best game of his career, as he eclipsed 100+ receiving yards for the first time on the season, and caught a season-high seven passes. Liberty plays host to UMass in Week 9 on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Liberty redshirt freshman CJ Daniels caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown in a 24-21 loss to Syracuse Friday night.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Daniels (6'1/195) continued the momentum from his strong performance last week against Old Dominion. After catching only 11 passes last season, Daniels is proving himself to be a great running mate for Demario Douglas. Liberty plays at UAB next Saturday which is shaping up to be a high-scoring affair.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.headline: Liberty redshirt freshman WR CJ Daniels scored twice while picking up 70 yards on five catches in a 45-17 clobbering of Old Dominion on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-daniels.analysis: Daniels caught two of the four touchdown passes from Malik Willis, with Kevin Shaa procuring the other two scores. The 6-foot-1, 195-pound wideout was an afterthought in the first two games with all of two catches for 21 yards, but was a big part of the game plan against the Monarchs on Saturday. It’ll be interesting to see if Daniels gets as many looks next week against Syracuse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock completed 14-of-17 attempts for 240 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders, adding six rushes for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock, as he has been in every spot start this season, was efficient in the run-first Seattle offense, averaging 14.1 yards per attempt and finishing 15 percent over his expected pass rate against a Raiders defense that ranks among the NFL’s worst. Lock fought through an elbow issue and an oblique injury in another win as Sam Darnold works his way back from injury. Visibly grimacing at time, Lock was his usual aggressive self, connecting with Cooper Kupp and Jaxson Smith-Njigba for touchdowns. Seattle has its bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will not “take every rep and throw” during Week 10 practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock was a limited practice participant through Week 9 practices before starting on game day. We expect that to be the case again this week. Fellow backup QB Jalen Milroe will take some first-team reps to help preserve Lock for the Seahawks’ Week 10 game against the Raiders. Given the injuries, Lock is likely just a mid-to-low QB2 despite the soft matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team expects Drew Lock (oblique) to start in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Speaking on Monday, Macdonald said that tests on Lock’s oblique injury were “good” and that they believe his injury is something the team can manage. Lock has been solid in three games for the Seahawks this season, throwing for 597-5-0 while completing 71.1 percent of his passes. He draws a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Raiders and could be on the radar as a mid to low-end QB2 that may have some stream appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. The team passed an update on Lock’s oblique injury following the game, indicating that the veteran journeyman would undergo follow-on testing but that his status for Week 10 could be in doubt. He’ll be nothing more than a deep-league potential streamer against the Raiders, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Seahawks QB Drew Lock (elbow) has severe tendonitis in his elbow.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Pelissero reiterated that Lock looked good in practice and will start against the Cardinals in Week 9. Still, Lock has been dealing with this since earlier this season and at one point wasn’t able to throw because of it. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said earlier this week he didn’t know how much Lock will be able to throw. Despite his play in relief of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) earlier this year, Lock isn’t a priority in 1QB leagues. Jalen Milroe could even be worth stashing in deeper formats given that Lock’s tendonitis could flare up at anytime.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding two receptions for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams was the clear-cut starter, as usual, touching the ball on the first four plays, but Blake Corum played so well that Rams coach Sean McVay just kept calling his number. Williams had a five-yard receiving touchdown called back due to a false start committed by rookie WR CJ Daniels. Williams’ five targets also led the pass-catching corps. The Rams go on bye in Week 11, but Williams will be back in the RB1 ranks against the Packers in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams was bottled up for most of the afternoon, with his longest gain coming on a nine-yard run. Williams’ 15 rush attempts narrowly edged out Blake Corum (11), but Corum found the end zone when he punched in a one-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Williams continues to see reliable work, but now that he’s in a near 50/50 split with Corum, the high-ceiling games could be few and far between compared to what we are used to seeing. He will profile as a fringe RB1 in next week’s game against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: After complaining about the team’s backfield split last week, Williams was out-carried by Blake Corum, 17 to 16, with Corum scoring a touchdown and having two others called back on penalties. Though Williams lost a fumble in the second half, the Rams leaned on him late in the fourth quarter following a short-lived Vegas comeback. He ran 18 pass routes to eight routes for Corum — a season long trend that makes Williams less sensitive to game script than Corum. Williams will be a locked-in top-15 running back option next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 10 times for 50 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams played for the duration of the first and third drives, ceding the second to Blake Corum, who played well right out of the gate. The duo rotated during drives thereafter. Williams looked like his normal, capable self, showcasing a slick spin move off contact on the Rams’ fourth drive. Unfortunately for him, Corum fought hard to convert a first down just inside the red zone and coach Sean McVay kept him out there for the scoring-position sequence, which ended in a 15-yard receiving score for Corum. Williams quietly continued his high-end receiving involvement, earning six targets against the Cardinals today. Williams belongs in the RB1 tier next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 27 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has yet to see more than the 16 carries he saw against the Bills this season but the team’s recent pass-heavy nature has left the veteran lead back with six or more receptions in three straight games, including 27 total targets in that span. The elite-level aerial volume made it three consecutive games with 20 or more opportunities for Williams, who continues to return RB1 fantasy weeks while playing in one of the league’s top offenses. Williams remains a middling RB1 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding 10 receptions for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 10 receptions were a new career high, while his 26 touches were tied for his seventh most. This, as Blake Corum handled the ball only six times. With Matthew Stafford having trouble against a stout Eagles defense in the rain, he focused on Williams checkdowns, and the strategy actually paid off as the Rams erased a 20-10 halftime deficit. Williams now has 47 touches over the past two weeks after that number was 28 for Weeks 1 and 2. With the Rams off to a shaky start, it’s not surprising they’ve started concentrating touches on their most established weapons. Corum is going to hang around as a nuisance, but Williams has returned himself to the low-end RB1 mix ahead of a likely Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-7 targets for 61 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Despite a short week to acclimate himself to his new team, Allen made a seamless transition to his new team. He caught 2-of-3 targets on third down for 31 yards, with one of those plays resulting in a 23-yard gain while Brock Purdy was scrambling around to extend the play. Allen’s 21 routes run narrowly trailed Deebo Samuel (27) and Jordan Watkins (22), but it wouldn’t be surprising if he saw more involvement going forward. Still one of the premier receivers in the league when it comes to finding separation and getting open, Allen already looks like a perfect fit in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. He will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next Week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen wasn’t targeted until late in the second quarter but picked up two receptions on back-to-back plays to tease fantasy managers in an otherwise poor outing. Things can’t get much worse in Indianapolis, with their decisions in the coming days ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline potentially allowing Allen to step into a more featured role in the second half of the season. Stay tuned as the Colts limp into a Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 7-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: As is now the case every week, Allen easily lead the Colts in most every receiving category. That did not include targets — a returning Tyler Warren commanded 10 looks — but Allen out-gained him 67-18. Now Allen and fantasy managers must sit and wait to see what kind of moves the tanking Colts make ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That could include non-roster changes like the benching of Daniel Jones. For now a low-end WR3, Allen could be valued much differently 10 days from now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was second on the team in targets while leading in receptions and yards against the Vikings. He saw just 30 snaps but operated as a quick release valve over the middle of the field for Daniel Jones against a blitz-happy Vikings defense. In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ onslaught of blitzes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) is active for Week 5 against the Steelers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen got in a full practice on Friday, so he seemed to be trending towards being active, but now we know for sure. With Jamel Dean out this week and Joey Porter Jr. now in Dallas, the Colts’ passing game gets a slight bump, which is good news for Daniel Jones, who really needs to get back on track. The Colts inactives are: LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin, QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton, and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-9 targets for 74 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle’s nine targets led all Niners players in this one. His 20-yard touchdown on the Niners’ opening drive set Deebo Samuel up nicely for an 11-yard touchdown on a screen pass on the following play, and in the fourth quarter, Kittle caught a 10-yard pass to move into the Cowboys’ red zone and positioned Christian McCaffrey for a 16-yard touchdown run soon after. Kittle continues to impress in his return from a late-season Achilles injury. He has gone for 58 or more yards in four straight games while averaging 8.5 targets per game over that span. He draws a tough Week 11 matchup against the Vikings, but will still profile as a low-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-7 targets for 58 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a fairly low volume day for Brock Purdy and the Niners passing offense. The team had 25 pass attempts to 34 designed rushes against a miserable Vegas defense. Kittle ran a route on 28 of the team’s 32 drop backs and led the Niners with seven targets. His biggest play came on a patented catch and run through the Vegas secondary — one of a few long YAC plays for the San Francisco offense. Kittle should remain in all lineups next week against a porous Dallas coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 8-of-10 passes for 88 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Unfortunately, Kittle also lost a fumble on the team’s final drive of the game as he was trying to earn extra yardage and set the team up for a better shot at the end zone. Even with that mistake, Kittle was tremendous on the day and the clear top option in the passing attack. The 49ers will be on a bye in Week 8, and then some of their injured receiving corps should return in Week 9, which might impact Kittle’s usage a bit. He will remain a rock-solid TE1 in fantasy leagues though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, which managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 72 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evans is expected to miss the team’s Week 7 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into additional volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a quiet day for Kittle before a fourth quarter screen pass went for a 58-yard score that sealed the game for the Niners. Displaying explosiveness less than a year after tearing his Achilles tendon, Kittle outran the Broncos secondary for his second touchdown in as many weeks. His six looks from Brock Purdy was second most among Niners pass catcher, trailing only Mike Evans (eight targets). Kittle’s big play upside and his role in the red zone make him a potential matchup flipper in fantasy. He gets the Seahawks in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle saw a season-high seven targets in the 49ers’ win, becoming the team’s No. 1 pass-catcher after Mike Evans (rib) left the game. He caught a 10-yard touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter and later sealed the win with a 20-yard score with under two minutes left. Kittle seems to be all the way back from his Achilles tear, leading all 49ers offensive skill players in snaps, only trailing Brock Purdy and the offensive line. With Evans’ status in the air, Kittle is the team’s top receiver and is squarely in the fantasy TE1 conversation for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle looked good in this one, finding space over the middle of the field and showing good burst after the catch. That’s important considering he’s still working his way back from last year’s Achilles injury. The veteran played just three fewer snaps than Mike Evans and was fourth on the team in routes run, just one behind Christian McCaffrey. His playing time will continue to increase as the year goes on, but he looks pretty close to the George Kittle we’ve gotten used to.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown, adding three carries for 78 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel, 30, turned back the clock to score not one, but two touchdowns in the Niners’ route of the Cowboys. Samuel would find the end zone on an 11-yard bubble screen in the first quarter to give the Niners their first points of the day. Then, in the third quarter, Samuel took an end around 70 yards upfield for a touchdown, and at one point had to walk a tightrope along the sidelines to stay in bounds before finding a clear path to the end zone. The run set a new career-high for Samuel, whose previous long was a 51-yard run back in 2022. Things went about as well as they could have for Samuel, who was playing in his first game since Week 5. Despite the strong outing, Samuel has averaged just 6.0 opportunities per game in his last three games, and his three targets in this one tied Jordan Watkins for fourth-most on the team. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a WR4 next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will resume practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel now has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense. The 49ers could play things cautiously and give him more time off, but an early-week return is usually a good sign. With much of the 49ers’ pass-catching corps still banged up, Samuel could return to a WR3/flex-worthy workload right away. He should be added wherever he is available. Samuel later told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was not seen at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) was seen at the practice, and the same goes for Christian Kirk (knee). Kirk still has a chance to play, but it seems very unlikely that Brock Purdy will have Samuel lined out wide for Week 9 against the Raiders. His next chance to play will be Week 10 against the Cowboys, barring something unforeseeable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Lynch said the same about Mike Evans. Samuel hasn’t played or practiced since going down with a hamstring injury in Week 5. It’s unclear when he will return to the field. The fact that the 49ers didn’t place him on injured reserve when he suffered the injury suggests they expected him to miss fewer than four games. Week 9 will be his third absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel remains sidelined by his Week 5 hamstring strain. He still has a chance to resume practicing in time to face the Raiders this weekend, but it would have been nice to see him take the field today. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-13 passes for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t be disappointed with the end result, but this was a frustrating game for Lamb. It became apparent early on that he would be taking a backseat to George Pickens, who saw six targets on the Cowboys’ first two drives of the game. Lamb saw nine of his 13 targets in the second half, and he was particularly productive in the fourth quarter, catching five passes for 49 yards and hauling in a one-yard touchdown pass with less than a minute to go in regulation. Despite Lamb needing every last second of this one to hit his expectations from a fantasy perspective, we don’t expect that to be the case for him most weeks. He’ll remain in the high-end WR1 conversation next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 10-of-16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s day was inches from being one of the top fantasy outings for any player this season, with the talented veteran unable to get his second foot down in the end zone in the third quarter, forcing the Cowboys to settle for a field goal. Even so, Lamb has now seen double-digit targets in each of his previous four games and five of his last six, averaging 13.8 targets per game in that span. His production in Week 9 also marked the third time this season in which Lamb has gone for more than 150 yards, handily leading the league in targets while trailing only Jaxon Smith-Njigba in yardage. Lamb and the Cowboys get a more difficult matchup against the 49ers in Week 10, where Lamb will remain an elite WR1 at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 58 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s most memorable play from this game was evading three tacklers on a screen to finally find a first down. He had two of Dallas’ six red zone targets but turned them into just one catch for four yards. Arizona’s aggressive defense simply clouded Lamb and dared the other receivers to win. He’ll remain on the WR1 line next week against the hapless Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-12 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: It wasn’t a clean game for the alpha wide receiver by any stretch, who committed two drops and caught only five of his team-leading 12 targets. Despite the poor efficiency, Lamb made the plays he needed to when it mattered most, scoring from nine yards out on a fade to the back corner of the end zone and from 16 yards out on a similar play to the opposite sideline. Lamb has now seen 56 targets in his previous four games, with 12 or more in three of his last four. That level of volume keeps him in elite company near the top of rest-of-season wide receiver rankings in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through an up-and-down connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb played through a quad bruise last week but exacerbated the issue and left the game late in the fourth quarter. The injury is not believed to be serious and a full practice today means Lamb isn’t at risk of missing Week 6. Despite burning fantasy managers with two catches for nine yards last time around, Lamb remains one of the best fantasy football wideouts in play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports CeeDee Lamb’s quad injury is not believed to be serious after Week 5’s loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was on the field for a few more plays in Thursday’s loss to the Buccaneers after his injury was announced. Rapoport reports that Lamb is believed to be dealing with a quad bruise, which is not believed to be serious. Lamb and the Cowboys now have over a week to rest up before facing the Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Barring an unexpected development, we would expect Lamb to be good to go for next week’s game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb departed in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He tried to return but managed one snap before making his way back to the sideline, coming back on the field later in the drive for a two-point attempt. He was shown on the sideline in visible discomfort following the additional two snaps. Lamb managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for nine yards prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming week, although the additional recovery time could allow him to avoid any missed games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: He simply could not be stopped the way the Texans were playing defense. Lamb feasted on the sideline and against zone coverages — his longest catch went just 30 yards — and he had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left that had FOX’s Greg Olsen wondering why any defense would play him that way when he’d been that productive over the course of the game. He’d never managed more than 17 targets in a game before today. Obviously he won’t do this again, but Lamb has delivered for those who lucked into him in the late first-round mix and will again be a plug-and-play alpha WR1 against the Bucs on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-8 targets for 112 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: That makes it back-to-back games of 100-plus yards for Lamb. Lamb didn’t officially find the end zone on this one, but he did come up with a catch on a two-point reception in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21. He came up with a few big plays in the fourth quarter, with his biggest being a 49-yard reception on a drive that ended with a KaVontae Turpin rushing touchdown to briefly give the Cowboys the lead. Despite being out-targeted 11 to 8 by George Pickens in this one, Lamb has looked like the unquestioned WR1 for the Cowboys through the first three weeks. He’s totaled 15 receptions for 265 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks and is a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers, adding one reception for four additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams wasn’t particularly efficient in this one, averaging just 3.9 YPC, with his longest run coming on a nine-yard gain late in the game. Williams saw half of his rush attempts come on the Cowboys’ first two drives of the game, but was mainly an afterthought in the second half when the Cowboys entered the fourth quarter trailing 31-19. The negative game script certainly didn’t help Williams in this one, but his volume continues to keep him in the RB2 conversation. He’ll look for better results in Week 11 when the Cowboys take on the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts, adding 23 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams notched his second 100-yard game of the season, tacking on a fourth quarter score with less than two minutes remaining to push his fantasy production into RB1 territory. Week 9 also marks the third straight week in which the Cowboys utilized a new-look, run-heavy game plan, this time utilizing Tyler Goodson to soak up carries behind Williams. Williams has now seen 20 or more carries in three straight and will remain a volume-based RB1 in a difficult matchup against the 49ers at home in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 24 times for 56 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Woof. The Cardinals simply overwhelmed the line of scrimmage with run blitzes and dared the Cowboys to do something about it; they often didn’t. Williams also fumbled away a goal-line tote only for it to wind up as a Cowboys touchdown by landing in the hands of journeyman tight end James Mitchell. Things should be easier next week against the Colts, where Williams will remain a reasonable RB1/high-end RB2 tweener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams churned out consistently positive gains against the injury-riddled Eagles but took off in the fourth quarter, gaining over 60 yards in the final frame. He cashed in for fantasy managers with a touchdown with just over two minutes remaining on the clock to push his line into elite territory, despite failing to notch any receptions. The career high in yardage on the ground comes after the Cowboys averaged the fewest rush attempts per game during the first six weeks of the new season. Williams gets a sparkling matchup against the Cardinals at home in Week 8, where he’ll return to RB1 status in fantasy circles following the eruption against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding nine yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now been held to 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in five of six games and 45 yards on the ground or fewer in four of six games, with seven combined touchdowns keeping his fantasy value afloat through the first third of the regular season. Williams has now seen 12 or fewer carries in four of six contests to start the year. The good news is that the Cowboys have no choice but to keep riding Williams until the wheels fall off considering the general lack of depth in the backfield, meaning there are likely to be better days ahead for the veteran back. He gets another middling matchup on the ground against the division rival Eagles in Week 7, where he will be a volume-driven RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers, adding 17 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now averaged 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in four of five games, keeping his fantasy value afloat via six combined touchdowns through five weeks. While the touchdown equity is solid in one of the league’s most potent offenses, we’re liable to see more down weeks like the one he put forth against the Buccaneers unless, or until, the Cowboys can fix their woes on the ground. Williams did see all but one running back opportunity in this one, keeping him in the top six in backfield opportunity rate through Week 5. Consider Williams a volume-aided and touchdown-aided RB2 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 4 win over the Texans, adding five catches for 21 yards on his only five targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams had a very easy rushing score — his first one where he only had to beat one defender to the outside after a pair of pulls. He also had a very hard one, where he dragged several Texans defenders into the red zone. The Cowboys didn’t run the ball much, but when they did it was effective. Williams was averaging 5.1 yards per tote before the second half, where he simply lived in the goal-to-go set. He’ll be on the low-end RB1 line in Week 5 against a Jalon Daniels-led Bucs outfit on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 98 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens, adding two receptions for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys drew up a lot of carries for Williams early in this one. The 26-year-old back totaled seven carries for 45 yards on his team’s first two possessions, and punched in a two-yard score late in the fourth quarter to put the Cowboys up 10-0. Williams would mostly be bottled up by the Ravens after his score, but he did break free for a 22-yard run in the third quarter that helped set up a Brandon Aubrey field goal — which was blocked. This is undoubtedly the best game of the season for Williams, who hadn’t gone for more than 41 yards in either of his first two games. That said, he still struggled at times to get going on the ground, as seven of his carries went for two or fewer yards. His volume remains reliable enough to keep him in the RB2 conversation for next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 30 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 20 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys dominated through the air on Sunday, but the same can’t be said of their efforts on the ground. Washington bottled up Williams all afternoon, with his biggest play coming on a nine-yard run on the Cowboys’ final drive. Williams has just 71 rushing yards on 24 attempts (3.0 YPC), but has also seen nine targets in his first two games. He remains the unquestioned leader of the Cowboys’ backfield and will be a volume-based RB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding five receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown.
