https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams understandably operated as a clear workhorse for a Cowboys team with little depth at the position following Malik Davis’ season-ending injury earlier in the week. His two second half scores and five receptions masked poor rushing efficiency on a night the Cowboys ran only 52 offensive plays, although a robust 32.7 percent total opportunity share foreshadows the potential for continued elite counting stats for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers can continue to start Williams as a volume-driven RB1 as the team prepares to host the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was the star of today’s show. He got involved partway through the Rams’ first drive, lining up in a two-running back set alongside Kyren Williams. The Rams’ immediate successes out of this formation led to a whole lot of it for the rest of the game. The shifty third-year running back hogged touches for stretches, playing so well as a rusher and receiver that having an eight-yard run erased by a penalty was a non-issue for fantasy purposes. Corum is a locked-in RB2 with RB1 upside. Treat him accordingly against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum continued to split drives with Kyren Williams, but he was easily the better back in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Corum ripped off several strong runs on the opening drive of the third quarter and capped a 69-yard offensive drive with a two-yard score to put the Rams up 13-10. He failed to haul in either of the two targets that came his way, but this was the kind of fantasy week we have come to expect from Corum, who has now had double-digit carries in three straight games. He has also found the end zone in each of those games and will be a boom-or-bust RB2 in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Kyren Williams led the LA backfield with 16 carries for 56 yards. Corum was much more efficient as a rusher against the Chargers, regularly bursting through the line of scrimmage and shedding tacklers on a couple second half runs. The Rams have been run heavy since Davante Adams went down with a serious hamstring injury a few weeks ago. That’s generated more opportunity for Corum, who last week had 17 rushes. He ranks 44th among running backs in expected fantasy points per game in 2026. That kind of usage should make Corum flex-viable for now. He gets the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 17 rushes for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum had the lead in carries until the final drive of the game, when the Rams turned to Kyren Williams to seal the victory following a short-lived Raiders comeback. Corum’s fantasy day could have been much bigger if he hadn’t had two touchdowns called back on penalties along with another chunk gain. Despite running cold on luck, Corum’s role continued to grow even after Williams complained publicly about the backfield workload split last week. Williams logged 18 routes against the Raiders while Corum ran just nine. Look for the Rams to be more run heavy in the coming weeks with Davante Adams out indefinitely with a hamstring injury, putting Corum in play as a weekly flex. He gets the Chargers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 1-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta’s slump continued with another quiet outing today. Backup tight end Brock Wright out-produced him in PPR formats with two catches for 11 yards, albeit on just two targets. He has nine catches for 99 yards over his past four appearances. With so many mouths to feed in the Detroit offense, LaPorta is increasingly looking like the odd man out. He will get one more week in the TE1 ranks. If things don’t turn around versus the Bucs in Week 11, fantasy managers might need to explore other options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the only Lion outside of Amon-Ra St. Brown to catch more than two passes. He accounted for a fifth of Jared Goff’s targets, but the team’s low-volume passing approach meant there wasn’t much volume to go around. LaPorta has gone cold in recent weeks with three straight games under 40 yards. He’ll look to get back on track as a mid-range TE1 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta had a quiet day against a Minnesota defense that has shut down opposing tight ends for much of the season. He had at least 80 receiving yards in each of that past two Detroit games. LaPorta had been a serviceable starting tight end headed into Week 8, and should have a better outlook in Week 9 against the Bills. He’s been targeted on 18 percent of his routes on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 1-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: While Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams combined for 244 yards and two touchdowns, LaPorta was an afterthought in the Lions’ offense on Sunday. LaPorta’s first target didn’t come until late in the fourth quarter, and his first catch came in the fourth quarter on an 18-yard play. It was an uncharacteristically underwhelming game by LaPorta, who entered the day coming off two-straight games in which he topped 80 yards and found the end zone. Despite the dud performance, LaPorta will be in the TE1 ranks next week at home against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-5 targets for 88 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta got involved on the Lions’ third drive, making a clutch 12-yard grab on 4th-and-3 while suffering what the officials deemed an unnecessarily rough hit by LB Mack Wilson at the end of the play. He chipped in two catch-and-run plays on the following drive. The first being an 11-yard play that was controversially ruled down in front of the sticks. Coach Dan Campbell called his number on the next play, resulting in an effortless 38-yard touchdown down the right side of the field. LaPorta tacked on an eight-yard catch and a 19-yard catch in the second half as the Lions cruised to a blowout win. He goes on bye next week but returns to the TE1 ranks in Week 7 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the primary beneficiary against the single-high-heavy Panthers, which was interesting considering both of Carolina’s top two corners were absent from this game. The 13 targets were easily a season high for the veteran tight end, primarily the result of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts in what would become a negative game script. LaPorta routinely found space behind the linebackers as the primary outlet through pressure for Goff, and while it remains unlikely he repeats the lofty target totals, LaPorta’s red zone acumen keeps him a fantasy TE1 ahead of a very different matchup in the two-high-heavy Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam LaPorta and the Lions “have broken off contract talks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Rapoport did note that the Lions could make another push to sign LaPorta later this year, so the door isn’t entirely closed. LaPorta is set to become a free agent next offseason. The team could, however, place the franchise tag on him. He has gotten off to a quiet start with 14 catches for 144 yards and one score. LaPorta is currently on pace for a career-low in yards per game. He would still have plenty of suitors in free agency, even if the counting stats don’t improve this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was a secondary piece of the passing attack in this game, taking a backseat to Jhamyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The two superstars combined for 16 targets while LaPorta and Jameson Williams were held to a combined eight looks. LaPorta has at least 44 yards in every game this year but no more than 52. With a solid floor established, all that’s left is for LaPorta to hit on a ceiling game. He remains a mid-range TE1 for Week 4 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson was barely involved today, though he nearly scored a touchdown on the Rams’ sixth drive. He successfully high-pointed a red zone pass, but tumbled out of bounds at the one-yard line, tangled up with a Cardinals defender. Parkinson will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Parkinson would be a DNP on Wednesday. The 27-year-old has been dealing with a rib injury since Week 7, missing the Rams’ Week 8 game against the Chargers. Starting out DNP puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 3-of-4 targets for 17 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee earned an end zone target on the Rams’ opening drive, but Matthew Stafford overthrew him, resulting in an incompletion. The two did manage to link up for a score on the Rams’ fourth drive, though. Rams coach Sean McVay dialed up a play where Higbee motioned from in-line to out wide on the left side. He ran right past his coverage defender, and Stafford hit him streaking toward the back of the end zone for a five-yard touchdown. Higbee will likely be a low-end TE1 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.

Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 1-of-2 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: It was another disappointing outing for Higbee. This one came with Colby Parkinson (ribs) sidelined. Davis Allen had two catches on two targets for eight yards. Higbee now hasn’t had more than 25 yards receiving in a game since the beginning of October, and has lost opportunities with the Rams going run heavy in recent weeks. Higbee won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Davis Allen caught 4-of-5 targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: The Rams in Week 7 resorted to a heavy dose of three tight end sets with Davante Adams sidelined with a long-term hamstring injury. That led to 12 pass routes for Allen, fewer than both Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. He caught two red zone touchdowns from Matthew Stafford, however, seeing a look on 33 percent of his routes. Allen will be tough to trust as a fantasy option unless or until his snaps and routes increase. He could be a deep league option in Week 8 against the Chargers, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 1-of-1 targets in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen played a small role, but made a big impact today, scoring from 19 yards out on a nice catch-and-run on the Rams’ seventh drive. Allen lined up in-line on the right side before slipping across the field mid-play, seemingly without any Cardinals defenders noticing. He easily hauled in the pass and turned upfield for the score. Allen will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, post-bye, in Week 12.

Fresh off catching two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford on just 12 routes in Week 7, Allen didn’t get so lucky in Week 8. He shouldn’t be rostered in 12-team formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen is dealing with a foot injury and is listed as a DNP on the Rams’ estimated practice report. Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as limited, though he has been dealing with the shoulder injury for a few weeks now and the Rams are likely managing his workload. Parkinson is trending to play. Allen’s potential absence may lead to the Rams activating rookie Max Klare to play alongside Parkinson and fantasy streaming option Tyler Higbee in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught 2-of-2 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Smith could have scored a 72-yard touchdown on the Rams’ third drive, but he was brought down by a shoestring tackle while trying to turn upfield. He made up for it with a 22-yard screen pass touchdown on the Rams’ fifth drive, in which he weaved through the middle of the field before cutting north into the end zone. The Rams go on bye next week, before facing the Packers in Week 12. He does not qualify as a much-stash player at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams signed WR Xavier Smith off the 49ers’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: With all the injuries at wide receiver, the Rams decide to bring back a familiar face in Xavier Smith in lieu of trading for a receiver. Smith was on the 49ers’ practice squad after the Rams waived him earlier this season. He caught 18 passes for 303 yards for the Rams last year, seeing the bulk of his opportunities as kick returner. Smith figures to operate as receiving depth with special teams utility once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is considered a “pre-game decision” for the Rams’ Week 2 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Nacua was added to the injury report on Friday as a DNP. He failed to get in any reps on Saturday but still received the questionable designation. Given that the game is on Monday, fantasy managers won’t have many contingency options left. With Jordan Whittington also expected to miss Week 2, the Rams’ No. 2 receiver will be either Konata Mumpfield or Xavier Smith if Nacua doesn’t suit up. Both players would be WR5/6 options in the event of a Nacua absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams tendered OL Justin Dedich, K Harrison Mevis, WR Xavier Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: The team will maintain control of three players that surprised in 2025, including “thiccer kicker” Harrison Mevis. The tendering of exclusive rights free agents ties the three to the franchise through the 2026 season considering they are unable to negotiate with other teams. At least for now, it appears as if the Rams will continue forward with Mevis as their place kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: What Smith did do was lose his footing on a punt return, letting the ball bounce off his chest and arms and right to the Seahawks. It immediately led to a touchdown in what finished as a four-point loss. Kyren Williams replaced Smith afterwards. Smith battled Tutu Atwell for a roster spot all season and eventually won out because of his work on special teams. Welp. An exclusive rights free agent in 2026, Smith was mostly a shot-play weapon and doesn’t figure to have a real fantasy role next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught 4-of-6 targets for 67 yards in the Rams’ Week 17 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Smith operated as the WR2 with Davante Adams out of action, a role that would have likely been far less conducive to fantasy production had the Rams not been playing from behind throughout after going down 21-0 at the half. The significantly negative game script forced the Rams away from a 12 and 13-personnel base offense, allowing for more snaps for the speedy youngster. Adams is reportedly due back to the game-day roster in Week 18, meaning Smith is likely headed back to a situational role when the Rams take on the Cardinals to end their regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught both of his targets for 57 yards in the Rams’ Week 16 overtime loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Smith was wide open for a 48-yard connection with Matt Stafford to set up a score. The 28-year-old certainly has some speed, but even with Davante Adams not available, there just aren’t enough targets to make him fantasy relevant at this stage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught 3-of-3 targets for 82 yards in the Rams’ Week 13 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Entering the day with just 85 yards on the season, Smith unexpectedly led the Rams with 82 yards through the air in Sunday’s defeat. His longest gain on the afternoon came on a 51-yard catch thanks to a beautifully thrown deep ball by Matthew Stafford. It was a good outing for Smith, but with the low target count, we can chalk this performance up as a one-off.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught his only target for 14 yards in Los Angeles’ Week 10 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: He and Konata Mumpfield (33 snaps, zero catches) led the Rams’ WR3 platoon with Jordan Whittington only playing seven snaps. None of these players are worthwhile roster spots in this current incarnation of the Rams’ offense, though perhaps if a team thoroughly game-scripted the Rams they’d pop up. Nobody has really stepped up to fill the Tutu Atwell role to this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Whittington is scheduled to resume practicing, in a limited capacity today. While the return is good, he is seemingly on the wrong side of questionable for this divisional matchup. Whittington was out-targeted by rotational WR Xavier Smith 3-0 last week, and currently does not need to be rostered in re-draft formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 3-of-4 targets for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield had a decent game today, producing catches of 10, 27 and 45 yards, notably adding decent yardage post-catch on his two longest receptions. He was also targeted on Matthew Stafford’s interception, but it was simply an off-target throw. Mumpfield generated his longest gain with a slick hitch-and-go, leaving his defender in the dust on the false step. The Rams go on bye in Week 11 and face the Packers in Week 12. Davante Adams (hamstring) is targeting a Week 13 return. Mumpfield should be FLEX-viable in Week 12, though he will likely become quite volatile when Adams returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 1-of-2 targets for 15 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield saw a bump in snaps and routes but not so much in actual targets and receptions as the Rams went all in on three tight ends sets with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the foreseeable future. Mumpfield doesn’t need to be rostered in fantasy leagues for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-8 targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield managed just one grab before erupting for 78 yards and a touchdown on a single drive in the fourth quarter with the Rams trailing for the first time in the game. His touchdown came on a double move against Riley Moss down the sideline for a walk-in score from 48 yards out. Mumpfield stepped into a growing role the previous two weeks in the absence of Puka Nacua and could remain a starter at wide receiver should Nacua miss additional time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is considered a “pre-game decision” for the Rams’ Week 2 game against the Giants.

Both players would be WR5/6 options in the event of a Nacua absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue believes the Rams may take a committee approach to the WR3 role this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Rodrigue listed WR Konata Mumpfield and WR Jordan Whittington as candidates for the gig, notably excluding rookie WR CJ Daniels. Daniels was viewed as the potential WR3 due to his blocking ability earlier this year. Rodrigue says it is instead Whittington who could serve as the “3B” blocker. Mumpfield reportedly “looks the part” as the “3A” receiving component. Will he return fantasy value reliably? Probably not. Earlier this month, Rodrigue’s colleague, Nate Atkins, said Mumpfield could be the next man up on the perimeter if WRs Puka Nacua or Davante Adams miss time. Rodrigue’s comments seemingly confirm this.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams WR Konata Mumpfield “could be the primary backup on the perimeter” if WR Puka Nacua or WR Davante Adams miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield enters his second NFL season after posting a 10/92/1 receiving line in the regular season last year. He chipped in three catches for 22 yards in the playoffs. Were he to get a spot start, he is not guaranteed to be fantasy-relevant. Atkins lists sixth-round rookie WR CJ Daniels as the most likely player to assume No. 3 wide receiver duties, primarily due to his blocking. He also has some contested-catch ability. Mumpfield is a name to know for 2026, but he is unlikely to meaningfully contribute in the box score if Nacua and Adams are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes wideout could be “a strong spot for the No. 13 pick in the draft.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: He also adds that a Day 2 selection is in play. Neither Davante Adams nor Puka Nacua are likely going to see their 2026 production threatened by a rookie wideout, but Adams is in the final year of his contract and the depth at the position hasn’t shown much for the Rams. Konata Mumpfield, who played outside while Adams was dealing with a hamstring injury late in the season, would figure to lose major dynasty stock if the Rams spent an early pick on a wideout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield failed to catch either of his two targets in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield had an eight-target game in Davante Adams’ hamstring-related absence and certainly appears to be the main backup wideout on the outside after the Rams picked him in the seventh round of last year’s draft. He finished the year with a 10/92/1 line. There’s not an obvious fantasy vacuum for him to step into even if he managed to be the main third receiver in 2026 — especially given how successful three tight-end looks were for the Rams this year. Still, he’s an interesting dynasty bench stash after making good progress in his rookie year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 3-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Rams’ Week 16 overtime loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: With Davante Adams out due to a hamstring injury, Mumpfield was given a chance to make some plays. He didn’t make enough of them, as Matthew Stafford just missed on a few connections with the seventh-round pick of this year’s draft. If Adams can’t go in Week 17 against the Falcons, Mumpfield will be in the conversation for fantasy relevance in that contest. If Adams can go, there’s not enough upside for consideration in redraft formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 11-of-18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: In his first game since owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys needed to focus more on getting the ball to Pickens, the 25-year-old receiver saw passes funneled to him early and often. Pickens was targeted six times on the Cowboys’ first two drives and capped the second drive with a 35-yard touchdown to give the Cowboys their first touchdown of the day. Pickens would find the end zone two more times in this one, with his second score coming on a 39-yard play on a long catch-and-run. His last score would come on a five-yard pass from Dak Prescott as the Cowboys aimed to keep pace with the Niners late in the fourth quarter, but it ultimately proved to not be enough in the end. Despite his struggles at various points this season, Pickens was far from an underutilized receiver, as he entered the day averaging a solid 7.8 targets per game. It goes without saying that we shouldn’t expect this kind of performance every week from Pickens, but he will be on the fantasy radar next week as a mid-to-high-end WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said George Pickens (hamstring) is expected to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens missed Week 9 with the hamstring issue. He was limited in practice throughout the week, but the team ultimately chose to hold him out for Sunday’s game. We expect one week off to be enough for the veteran wideout. Assuming things go well in practice, Pickens will be back in the WR2 ranks when the Cowboys take on the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The 25-year-old still seems to be on target to play in Week 9 against the Colts, but fantasy managers would obviously like to see Pickens get in a full session before that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: On the plus side, Pickens is no longer listed with a shoulder injury. Hopefully, Pickens upgrades to full participation tomorrow, and puts this hamstring strain behind him. Team owner Jerry Jones told reporters earlier this week that Pickens needs to get the ball more. The squeaky wheel often gets greased. The Cowboys’ Week 9 game against the Colts looks like a solid bounce-back spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren’t trading George Pickens.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Rapoport added that “as of right now, there’s nothing there,” as far as a potential trade is concerned. Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn’t produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production. Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys’ disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East. With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it’s safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and one touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys, adding four receptions for 161 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was at his best in what can only be described as a legacy game for the 30-year-old running back. A relatively pedestrian line on the ground (12-62-1) proved to be nothing but a footnote in the box score for McCaffrey, who needed just four catches to set a new career high with 161 receiving yards. McCaffrey ripped off scores of 74 and 66 yards through the air, doing most of his damage after the catch. Of his 161 receiving yards, 141 of those yards came after the ball was in his hands, and his second score went virtually uncontested by a helpless Von Miller in man coverage. McCaffrey’s 223 yards from scrimmage were just 14 off his career high, and marked the fifth time in his career that he has gone for 200-plus yards from scrimmage. He will look to follow up this elite performance in Week 11 when the Niners “host” the Vikings in Mexico City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey had 18 rushes for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey didn’t have much trouble against a Vegas run defense that has been one of the league’s worst over the past month. His rushing score was his ninth of the season, while his receiving score was his first of 2026. CMC logged 28 routes on the day while Kaelon Black had just five routes and did not see a target from Brock Purdy. McCaffrey, with at least 15 carries in five games this year, has a spectacular Week 10 matchup against a miserable Dallas defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kaelon Black had 11 rushes for 70 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Christian McCaffrey, meanwhile, had 18 rushes on the day and scored two touchdowns. Black had just five pass routes against the Raiders while CMC ran 28 routes. Black’s 70 rushing yards marks a season high and shows he can be a fantasy factor when the Niners have game script in their favor. It didn’t help that he faced an abysmal Raiders front seven. Black should have some flex viability in deeper leagues next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday. Even though today’s activity only resulted in a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: That explains McCaffrey’s brief departure in the team’s Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when the veteran alpha missed most of the second quarter but returned for the second half. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan added that he believes McCaffrey will be fine when the team comes out of their Week 8 bye. “We’re pretty optimistic,” he said Monday. Fantasy managers appear to have dodged a bullet with the first-round fantasy powerhouse but will want to continue to monitor reports from the team through their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons, adding 61 receiving yards on six catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game and had six touches, which seemed to set the tone for a massive workload. However, he also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and didn’t return again until the third quarter. The 49ers seemed to give him a few extra breaks in the second half, but McCaffrey didn’t look any less explosive. He was also half a yard away from catching a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter, but he was ruled down short of the end zone, and then Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk on the next play. The 49ers have a bye next week, so we doubt McCaffrey’s thigh injury will be an issue when we see them next in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returned to the game in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was injured on the first drive of the game when the 49ers scored a touchdown. The training staff was working on his thigh before he jogged into the locker room in the second quarter and was listed as questionable to return. It was a 14-3 49ers lead when McCaffrey went into the locker room, and it’s 19-14 in favor of the Falcons now, so the team is going to see if their star running back can get them back in front.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 30-of-51 passes for 343 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 46-40, Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Facing a Niners offense that scored a touchdown on six of its 11 possessions, Prescott and the Cowboys needed to be nearly perfect if they hoped to keep pace. Dak orchestrated an 11-play, 71-yard drive on the Cowboys’ second drive of the game, capping it with a 35-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens, who found the end zone a career-high three times in this one. Prescott’s two touchdown passes in the first half had the Cowboys trailing 17-16 at halftime, but after being outscored 14-3 in the third quarter, Prescott and the company aired it out 24 times in the fourth quarter as they aimed to keep pace. Prescott threw a five-yard touchdown to Pickens to get the Cowboys within seven points, and responded on the following drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy to cut the Niners’ lead to 38-32. Unfortunately, that would be as close as the Cowboys would get, as the 49ers would need just two plays to go up by double digits, which proved to be too much for Dallas to overcome, even after a one-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb. This is the kind of game the Cowboys are capable of posting any given week, especially if they are being pushed by the opposing team. We wouldn’t expect Cam Ward and the Titans to push them next week in the way the Niners did this week, but Prescott will be in the QB1 mix in what looks to be a plus matchup at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 21-of-34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 27-23, Week 9 win over the Colts, adding one yard on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The two teams played to a maddening field position battle through the first three quarters in what was one of the least disciplined games in recent memory, including a multitude of penalties on key downs, two turnovers, and a missed field goal from the Cowboys. A poor fourth quarter saw the Colts snatch the lead with a late field goal, but a 46-yard deep connection with Ryan Flournoy on the play of the subsequent possession allowed the Cowboys to take the lead with just over a minute remaining in the fourth quarter. A Caleb Downs interception ended the game, allowing Prescott and the Cowboys to escape with a win to send them to 4-5 as they chase the Giants in the NFC East. Up next is a home test against the 49ers in Week 10, where Prescott will remain a back end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ 33-30, Week 8 loss to the Cardinals, adding seven carries for 20 yards and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: If you’re wondering, it was Prescott’s first rushing touchdown since Week 12 of the 2025 season against the Eagles, and his first game with seven carries since Week 5 of the 2025 season. The gist of it is: The Cardinals big blitzed a lot and vacated several underneath zones to allow Prescott to run. Dallas often tried to solve things pre-snap, and they often did — but not often enough to win. Dallas was either throwing haymakers or quickly finding themselves going three-and-out, as they did in overtime. Prescott will get to rebound quickly in Week 9 against a Colts outfit that barely qualifies as a serious football team amid what has the look of a fire sale.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 15-of-27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 38-21, Week 7 win over the Eagles, adding eight yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Prescott made the throws when they counted while connecting on three touchdowns to his two alpha receivers, two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens. After averaging the fewest rush attempts per game through the first six weeks of the regular season, the Cowboys leaned heavily on Javonte Williams against a battered Eagles team; Williams set a career high with 155 yards on the ground. Even so, Prescott did not look his best, nor did the pass offense. Lamb committed two drops and the team benefited from multiple first downs due to penalty. Prescott gets another sparkling matchup against the Cardinals at home in Week 8, where he remains a fantasy QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 23-13, Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding seven yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Prescott and the Cowboys were completely unable to get anything going prior to the half, managing just 92 yards of total offense while taking a 17-point deficit into the break. They would force a three-and-out to start the third quarter and follow it up with a touchdown drive to get on the board, but a punt and two turnovers on downs left them trailing by 16 until a late score inside of two minutes remaining in the final frame. Prescott’s two interceptions occurred deep in Green Bay territory in the second quarter, removing much needed points from the scoreboard in what was then a tight game. The loss drops the Cowboys to 2-4 and looking up at the Giants for the division lead through a third of the regular season. Prescott will be a back-end QB1 on the road against the division rival Eagles in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 24-of-42 passes for 316 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 24-16, Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The two interceptions on Dak’s ledger were both in-and-out of his receivers’ hands, the second of which hit tight end Jake Ferguson in the face mask to allow the Buccaneers to ice the game in the fourth quarter. The first “pick” bounced off the hands of Ryan Flournoy to allow the Buccaneers to establish an 11-point lead at the beginning of the third quarter, a deficit the Cowboys would be unable to overcome. That said, Prescott wasn’t at all at his sharpest, missing numerous throws wide in addition to a few badly under-thrown balls in the second half. To make matters worse, alpha wide receiver CeeDee Lamb departed the game in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. The Cowboys fall to 2-3 and find themselves looking up at both the Giants and Eagles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Packers at Lambeau. Prescott returns to QB1 status in what has become a soft matchup, pending the health of Lamb.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 32-of-45 passes for 335 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-30, Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: He had just 87 passing yards at halftime, but the Cowboys turned up in a major way in the second half by peppering CeeDee Lamb with targets and getting George Pickens matched on Kamari Lassiter to their benefit. Prescott was surgical against the blitz and led a game-winning drive after C.J. Stroud briefly put the Texans up 30-27, leading the Cowboys 74 yards in 1:43 by brutalizing the Texans’ zone coverage. Dak should remain in the QB1 ranks next week against the woeful Buccaneers on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 25-of-40 passes for 276 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-31, Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys came out with a run-heavy approach early, but Prescott was efficient through the air when given the chance. He was able to get both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens involved in this one, with the two receivers combining for 14 receptions for 194 yards on the day. Prescott’s lone touchdown pass came on a 19-yard strike to Jake Ferguson in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21, but on the Cowboys’ final drive in the fourth quarter, he would go 3-of-6 passing for 36 yards while adding another nine yards on the ground to help set up a game-tying field goal by Brandon Aubrey. A literal last-second field goal moments later would give the Ravens the win, but Prescott and the Cowboys have now gone for 30-plus points in back-to-back weeks. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 26-of-31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 37-20, Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys faced little resistance from the Commanders’ defense in this one. The Cowboys came out firing from the start, as Prescott orchestrated a 10-play, 66-yard opening drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb, who had three receptions on the drive. Prescott threw his second touchdown of the game to Jake Ferguson, who broke free in the end zone for a 10-yard score, and in the third quarter, the two connected again for a 12-yard score. Dak found Lamb for a 24-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to set the Cowboys’ franchise record for career touchdown passes (249), putting the finishing touches on what was an impressive day. Prescott will be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens in Rio De Janeiro.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passes for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 28-20, Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: A first half in which Prescott was victimized by drops and penalties from his supporting cast was completely overshadowed by a defensive performance that saw the Giants go 9-of-10 on third down and amass 394 yards of total offense. The Cowboys saw the ball only twice in the second half, scoring touchdowns on both drives, but it was ultimately not enough as they fell to 0-1 for the second consecutive season. Prescott’s lone interception came on a prayer ball down the sideline on third down at the end of the first half, eventually leading to a go-ahead touchdown for the Giants as they took a 14-7 deficit into the break, one they would not overcome. The Cowboys now turn the page to Week 2 as they prepare to host another division opponent in the Commanders in what has quickly become a near must-win game for both teams. Prescott will look to return to the QB1 ranks in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 46-40, Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Facing a porous Cowboys defense, Purdy and the Niners delivered just about everything fantasy managers could have hoped for in this one. Despite taking five sacks on the day, Purdy was nearly perfect, throwing just six incompletions while coming up with multiple big plays. Purdy’s first touchdown pass came on an 11-yard bubble screen to Deebo Samuel, with his other two coming on long catch-and-runs by Christian McCaffrey. In the second quarter, Purdy tossed a 14-yard pass to McCaffrey, which CMC immediately turned upfield for a 74-yard score, and in the fourth quarter, another six-yard pass to CMC in the face of a blitz resulted in a 66-yard score after the Cowboys left Von Miller in coverage against McCaffrey. Purdy’s three touchdowns resulted in 151 passing yards, but came on passes that combined for just 20 air yards. That’s the benefit of playing with elite playmakers like CMC. Purdy and the Niners will get a true test in Week 11 when they take on the Vikings in Mexico City. We cautiously project Purdy as a QB1 despite the tough matchup on paper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 attempts for 232 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 40 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy made quick work of a Raiders defense that has ranked as one of the NFL’s worst over the past month. The Niners tormented the Vegas defense with well-timed screens and quick hits to the middle of the field. Purdy used his legs in a couple high leverage situations in the first half and scored his second rushing touchdown of the season. He connected with Christian McCaffrey and Jordan Watkins for his throwing scores. The ultra-efficient Purdy will take on the generationally bad Dallas defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the 49ers’ 29-20, Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: After losing seemingly every wide receiver to injury, it was only a matter of time before we finally had a down Purdy game. The truth is, he didn’t even play poorly. His first interception was on a pass that he was trying to throw away when safety Jesse Bates made an incredible toe-drag interception. The second pick was on a really nice play by linebacker Kendal Daniels over the middle. Purdy looked good and gave his team a chance to win despite a depleted offense. The 49ers will have a bye next week and then hopefully get back at least one of their primary receivers before a Week 9 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break. The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-30 attempts for 218 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding ten rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy’s ten rushing attempts were a season high, and the product of Denver’s secondary blanketing Niners pass catchers for much of the game. Injuries to both starting Broncos corners eventually loosened things up for Purdy and the 49ers. He connected with George Kittle on a fourth quarter screen pass that went for a 58-yard score — the biggest play of the game. Purdy, who now has 11 touchdown passes through four games, is a weekly top-10 fantasy play even on his less-than-efficient days. He gets a tough matchup against Seattle in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 15-of-27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns in the 49ers’ 36-30, Week 3 win over the Cardinals, adding two carries for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers offense had another fruitful fantasy day despite injuries haunting the team once again. Purdy showcased his mobility and athleticism, often making throws on the run and scrambling out of pressure. His first score was a completion to Mike Evans, who lateraled it to Deebo Samuel for the score. Purdy then threw a more traditional touchdown to Evans later in the first half, then threw two scores to George Kittle to seal the game in the second half. Despite losing Evans and LT Trent Williams by the third quarter, Purdy was still able to gash the Cardinals defense and surpass 300 total yards. Though the offense keeps losing pieces, Purdy in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme is a fantasy QB1 until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-13, Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding 30 yards rushing and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Dolphins’ defense didn’t put up much of a fight, but Purdy was tremendous in this one. He bought extra time in the pocket when he needed to, made plays with his legs if the opportunities were there, and found open receivers over the middle of the field all game long. He may find the going a little bit tougher next week against the Cardinals, but probably not much. The bigger question will be who else can step up in the receiver room with Demarcus Robinson leaving this game with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the 49ers’ 27-7, Week 1 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy also added 29 yards on his five attempts. The veteran signal-caller did throw a terrible interception, but outside of that pick he played exceptionally well; even if most of his completions were for short yardage. All three passing scores came to different players, with his best throw being a perfectly placed touchdown to Deebo Samuel between two Rams’ defenders to cement the blowout. Purdy will look to keep it going in Week 2, and gets a friendly matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that 49ers QB Brock Purdy said he is “prepared to use his mobility more this year if needed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers’ quarterback is not a straight-line burner, but he is more agile than he is given credit for. Purdy adds that he won’t constantly be looking for opportunities to run, however, he believes he can help the offense by scrambling for 10-12 yards from time to time. Purdy has racked up 113 carries over the past two NFL seasons, including the playoffs, proving himself an efficient scrambler with a 47.8 percent conversion rate that ranks first among quarterbacks with at least 50 attempts. He’s a borderline QB1/2. Scrambling more often could get him into the weekly low-end QB1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 18-of-26 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Rams’ 34-6, Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams lost two centers to injury today, but Stafford navigated the resulting offensive line shuffling without issue, completing passes to nine different pass catchers. Stafford probably should have had a fourth touchdown added to his box score, but he overthrew Tyler Higbee and CJ Daniels in the end zone on the opening drive, which ultimately resulted in a field goal. A touchdown pass thrown to Kyren Williams was called back due to a false start on the Rams’ fourth drive, but Stafford linked up with Higbee for a score a couple of plays later. A similar sequence occurred in which Stafford threw a touchdown pass to Xavier Smith on the following drive, after Tutu Atwell failed to secure what should have been a 32-yard touchdown. Stafford’s second-drive interception was on him. He threw an off-target pass to Konatha Mumpfield, which a Cardinals defender easily caught. All in all, Stafford dealt with the Rams’ offensive personnel issues well. He will be a low-end QB1 against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 26-of-43 passes for 228 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ 20-13, Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an uneven day for Stafford and the Rams, who managed just six points in the first half of this one. Stafford threw 19 of his 43 targets to Puka Nacua, who was unsurprisingly his most reliable receiver of the day, as the two connected 14 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Stafford’s lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Nacua in the back of the end zone, which gave the Rams a 20-13 lead early in the fourth quarter. This marks back-to-back pedestrian outings for Stafford, who has thrown for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games. Stafford will be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week on the road against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 17-of-25 attempts for 157 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford wasn’t asked to do much against the Chargers, as the Rams once again went ultra run-heavy with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. Averaging a meager 6.3 yards per attempt, Stafford mostly checked down to his short-area targets. His touchdown came on a well-designed screen pass to Puka Nacua. Stafford will have some fantasy appeal in Week 9 against the pass-funnel Washington defense. Coming into Week 8, Stafford ranked 13th in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 23-of-29 attempts for 195 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was a fairly clean game for Stafford against a Raiders defense that rarely pressures the passer and has proven vulnerable in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. Stafford picked apart the Vegas secondary in the first half, with heavy three tight end-set usage and a more run-heavy game plan than usual with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. The Rams had 35 rushing attempts to 29 passes on the day. Stafford connected with Puka Nacua for one score and Davis Allen for two others. Though Stafford’s ceiling is going to be lower with Adams out, he profiles as a safe option in Week 8 against the Chargers. He now has six multi-touchdown games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Puka Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams.
