Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua (groin) will play in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua, who missed Monday night’s game against the Giants, will be able to suit up against Denver next week. The Rams offense was fine without Nacua on Monday against an injury-ravaged Giants team. LA had the week’s fourth highest EPA per play on the way to a 28-6 win. Another game with Nacua sidelined will mean more target domination for Davante Adams and more involvement for Terrance Ferguson, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Joey Slye converted all three of his field goal attempts in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Slye also connected on both of his PATs. Most importantly, he laid out Josh Cameron in kick coverage. The bone-crunching hit knocked the ball out of Cameron’s hands, though the Jags ultimately fell on the loose ball. Slye isn’t a reliable fantasy option, but he deserves his flowers for two combined tackles and a forced fumble on top of the solid kicking performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans re-signed K Joey Slye to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Slye missed time with a calf injury early in the season, but went 28-of-35 on field-goal attempts. His job status is tenuous on a one-year contract, but the Titans are set to open the season with him as their kicker as things currently stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans K Joey Slye (calf) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: This was telegraphed earlier when the Titans waived Matthew Wright. Those of you looking for a chance at a zero from your fantasy kicker can happily start Slye against the Patriots in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans declared K Joey Slye, DB Marcus Harris, OLB Arden Key, OL Blake Hance, OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, WR Bryce Oliver, and TE Thomas Odukoya inactive for Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Slye will miss the game with a lingering calf injury. That leaves veteran journeyman Matthew Wright as the Titans’ kicker against Vegas. He won’t be a fantasy option in most formats as the Titans don’t create the sort of game script that leads to consistent field goal tries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans K Joey Slye (calf) will not play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Calf injured his calf in the Titans’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals and was a DNP all week. The veteran kicker will be sidelined for Sunday’s game against the Raiders as a result, giving way for Matthew Wright to see his first action of 2025. Wright split time between three teams in 2024, including the Titans, going 15-for-16 on his field goal attempts while making all tries inside of 50 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans K Joey Slye (calf) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Slye is listed with a right calf injury for Wednesday. It is unclear when he suffered the injury as the 29-year-old kicked the game-winner in the Titans’ win over the Cardinals in Week 5. The Titans may look to add a kicker to the practice squad should Slye not practice the rest of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Titans signed K Joey Slye, formerly of the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: It’s possible this spells the end for 40-year-old Nick Folk, who has spent the last two seasons with the Titans. Slye kicked last season for the Patriots, converting on 26-of-33 attempts while going 6-for-9 on distances of 50 or more yards. He hit a career-long 63-yard field goal in last season’s Week 4 game against the 49ers. Slye is a career 81.7 percent field goal kicker, and could have the inside edge to win whatever kicker competition comes his way once training camp starts up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Patriots signed K John Parker Romo, formerly of the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Parker Romo will be on the team’s practice squad until the Pats activate him to the game day roster. Parker Romo made 11 of his 12 field goal attempts in four games with the Vikings this season before the team released him in Week 14, with Will Reichard returning from IR. Parker Romo could be New England’s starter soon rather than later. Joey Slye has missed three field goals over the team’s past two games and has converted a lowly 78 percent of his attempts in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Patriots waived K Chad Ryland.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Something of a swan song terrible pick for erstwhile GM Bill Belichick, Ryland suffered through an ineffective rookie campaign and saw Joey Slye added as veteran depth in May. Slye has now presumably won the job. Kickers tend to begin their careers strangely slow in the NFL, so 24-year-old former fourth-rounder Ryland could quickly revive his fortunes on the workout circuit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.headline: Patriots sign K Joey Slye, formerly of the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-slye/.analysis: Slye will serve as camp competition for second-year kicker Chad Ryland, who converted on 16-of-25 field goals in his rookie season. Ryland missed 7-of-14 attempts from 40-plus yards out, a range that Slye converted on at a 71.4 percent rate last season. Slye has converted 82.3 percent of his field goals for his career and has spent the last two seasons with Washington. While he was most recently with the Jaguars, Slye never attempted a field goal for them, as he was signed back in mid-March as a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers declared QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar ,RB Eli Heidenreich, S DeShon Elliott, and CB Sean Murphy-Bunting inactive for Week 10 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Elliott suffered a knee injury in warmups and was announced as out just 15 minutes prior to inactives being released. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback while rookie running back Eli Heidenreich is inactive for the seventh consecutive contest. The absence of Elliott is a massive blow, leaving defensive coordinator Patrick Graham to scramble to adjust his game plan mere hours before first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: T.J. Watt (calf) was removed from the Steelers’ Week 7 injury report and will play against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Watt popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a calf injury and was listed as limited. On Friday, he was upgraded to a full participant in what was an estimated report, but he does not carry an injury status heading into the weekend. S DeShon Elliott (knee) is listed as questionable but was listed as a full participant throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers placed S DeShon Elliott (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Elliott was considered week-to-week with a knee injury he suffered in Week 8 against the Packers. However, with the Steelers acquiring Kyle Dugger from the Patriots, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Elliott will be placed on injured reserve. He will miss a minimum of four games and could return later in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers S DeShon Elliott (knee) was carted to the locker room in the third quarter of Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Elliott’s knee got caught under Packers tight end Tucker Kraft while attempting a tackle in the third quarter. He remained on the field before being helped to the medical tent, eventually carted to the locker room while in visible pain. The team ruled him out for the remainder of the game and it appears as if he is headed for an extended absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers declared WR Calvin Austin III, OG Andrus Peat, DL Logan Lee and DE DeMarvin Leal inactive for Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Austin remained sidelined all week by his shoulder injury, and the Steelers do not have an adequate replacement for the speedy receiver on the roster, once again solidifying a large target share for WR DK Metcalf. Fortunately, the Steelers will have S DeShon Elliott, who missed two practices this week due to a personal issue. The Steelers (4-1) sit atop the AFC North, with the Bengals (2-4) in the No. 2 spot, now led by veteran QB Joe Flacco, who joined his new team via trade just last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers S DeShon Elliott (personal) “will be upgraded to not have a game status designation” and is expected to play in Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: The news comes directly from the Steelers’ senior director of communications, Burt Lauten, so we read the “expected to play” line as a formality. Elliott missed practice on Tuesday and Wednesday due to a personal issue, but he has now arrived in Cincinnati and is evidently good to go. The Steelers defense is tasked with containing the Joe Flacco-led Bengals on Thursday Night Football this evening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers ruled out WR Calvin Austin (shoulder) for Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Austin has not yet returned to practice after injuring his shoulder in the Steelers’ Week 4 game against the Vikings. The team had a Week 5 bye and declined to put Austin on short-term injured reserve, which would have required him to sit out until Week 10. The Steelers face the Bengals on Thursday Night Football this week. The short week undoubtedly hurt Austin’s chances of returning in time. The Steelers also ruled out S Miles Killebrew (knee) and listed S DeShon Elliott (personal) and LB Malik Harrison (knee) as questionable. Elliott missed Weeks 3-4 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers DT Derrick Harmon (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: Harmon’s return to practice could not have come at a better time. Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin already said CB Joey Porter Jr. (hamstring) is “questionable at best” to play in Week 3 against the Patriots. He was unable to practice, as was S DeShon Elliott (knee). Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) is likely due for an extended absence, though he was able to avoid being placed on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports S DeShon Elliott (knee) will miss “a couple weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: The team hopes to have Elliott back for their Week 4 game against the Vikings in Ireland, according to Schultz. Elliott will be replaced by some combination of Jalen Ramsey and Jabrill Peppers, who signed with the Steelers on Tuesday. The loss of Elliott is a blow for a Pittsburgh defense that allowed the fourth highest drop back success rate in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.headline: Steelers S DeShon Elliott (knee) left Pittsburgh’s Week 1 game against the Jets and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshon-ell.analysis: He walked off the field on his own, though he was surrounded by trainers, and went directly to the blue medical tent. Elliott had five solo tackles before leaving. Jalen Ramsey has been playing more safety with Elliott sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-rob.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, T Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-rob.analysis: Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and the team is missing contributing tight ends, but the Bengals enter the second half of the season as one of the healthier teams in the league. The winner of this game will move into sole possession of the division lead in what has become the most competitive division in the AFC.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-rob.headline: Bengals selected Navy DT Landon Robinson with the No. 226 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-rob.analysis: Robinson (5’11"/293) was recruited to Navy as a linebacker but made the transition to defensive tackle while sitting out as a freshman. He saw the field for the first time as a sophomore and was immediately a wrecking ball, tallying four sacks, albeit on just nine pressures. He earned a starting role for the next two years and totaled 10.5 sacks, 14 TFLs, and two forced fumbles as an upperclassman. Pro Football Focus charted him with a top-10 pass-rush grade among defensive linemen, though his run defense grade was nothing to write home about. Robinson crushed his Pro Day with a 4.87 40-yard dash (95th-percentile) and 7.32-second three-cone drill (94th-percentile), among other impressive measureables. Robinson is not particularly close to being an NFL-sized defensive tackle, but his elite pass-rush production can’t be ignored. He will be eyeing a rotational role in the pros, though his 2026 opportunities will likely come on special teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.headline: Andrew Armstrong caught a 43-yard touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.analysis: Armstrong’s fourth quarter score was his only target, and just his third catch of the season. It was certainly notable in that it came on a freelance, somewhat broken play with Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs really had their down-field attack cooking in Atlanta, and it could remain a theme for Week 11 against the Cardinals. Fun for fantasy, but 26-year-old, second-year UDFA Armstrong remains nothing more than a deep, deep Dynasty league curiosity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell believes Chiefs WR Andrew Armstrong “appears” to have a chance to make the final roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.analysis: This isn’t exactly breaking news, but it is always worth keeping track of the players who might have a chance to catch passes from QB Patrick Mahomes. Newell compares Armstrong to WR Tyquan Thornton, who signed with the Chiefs in November 2024 before earning Mahomes’ trust the following offseason. Armstrong has spent the entire offseason training with the Chiefs and was allowed to take “numerous” first-team reps on Thursday. In his 2024 senior season at Arkansas, Armstrong (6'4/202) led the SEC in catches (78), receiving yards (1,140) and receiving yards per game (103.6). Newell believes “it would be an underdog tale if he makes the team,” so set your expectations accordingly, but feel free to track his progress this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.headline: Dolphins signed WR Andrew Armstrong.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-arm.analysis: Armstrong (6’4/202) redshirted as a freshman at Texas A&M Commerce, didn’t play as a sophomore because of COVID-19, and was a backup as a junior. Finally in a starting role as a senior, he topped 1,000 yards and scored 13 times in just 11 games. The breakout season caught the eye of Arkansas’s coaching staff via the transfer portal and he joined the Razorbacks for two seasons. He went for 764 yards and five scores in his first season at Arkansas and then led the SEC with 78 catches and 1,140 yards in 2024. He did, however, only bring down one touchdown. For better or worse, Armstrong plays at every bit of 6’4. He won 18-of-29 contested targets in his final season, but nearly a quarter of his total targets were contested. Armstrong is lanky and doesn’t create separation with his routes, but he does win the looks thrown his way. The lack of separation and a late breakout make him a high-risk pick for NFL teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: The Chiefs finally got their deep passing attack going and Allen was a big part of it, catching a 39-yard touchdown where he took advantage of a “stutter and go” to beat A.J. Terrell in 1-on-1 coverage. It was the kind of play the Chiefs have been dying for from one of their role players since Tyquan Thornton was lost for the season. Allen, Rashee Rice, and Andrew Armstrong all had long “air yards” conversions this afternoon, perhaps signaling the arrival of a new-look attack with Josh Downs’ addition hopefully improving the Chiefs’ spacing and timing. Good stuff for them, but not terribly relevant for Allen in fantasy, who remains miles from 12-team league relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 1-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Allen was the recipient of Patrick Mahomes’ first target of the game, which he took down the right sideline for a tidy 18-yard gain. He would disappear into oblivion the rest of the way as he continued to play behind Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals, with Justin Watson also worked into the game plan in this one. Allen played just 16 offensive snaps. Head coach Andy Reid has a long history of taking his time to develop rookies, meaning fantasy managers are likely forced to be patient. In other words, keep Allen on fantasy benches, for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught both of his targets for 27 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Rashee Rice’s absence didn’t translate into more playing time for Allen, who logged a mere five pass routes against the Chargers. He can remain on waiver wires until his playing time increases, which is unlikely if Rice is able to return in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: When asked about Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen, WR coach Chad O’Shea said rookie wide receivers are “always a work in progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: You don’t say, Chad. Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp. Beat reporters celebrated his ability to beat man coverage and win over the middle of the field — two aspects that help wide receivers thrive in fantasy. Unfortunately, Allen has logged just four offensive snaps this season. O’Shea adds that Allen is improving every day, both “fundamentally and schematically.” Good for him. The once-intriguing rookie is droppable in 12-team formats, though an in-season breakout remains possible. Theoretically.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said the team is going to continue building up WR Cyrus Allen to a bigger workload “the right way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Apparently, that means barely using him on game day, at least in the short term. Allen played one snap in the Chiefs’ season opener, despite starting WRs Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy combining for a just 5/37/1 stat line. Bieniemy also said that Allen is “going to be a part of our success moving forward. I guarantee that.” Given Allen’s Week 1 usage, becoming fantasy-relevant could take quite some time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 1-of-2 targets for 12 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: The Chiefs let most of their starters take the field in this game and Allen wasn’t among them. He didn’t see a snap until after Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton had all left the contest. His first target didn’t come until the third quarter, and it was a drop on a high throw. The rookie rebounded with a 12-yard gain for a first down on the very next play. After playing well into the second half of the team’s final preseason game, Allen is, at best, the Chiefs’ WR4 entering the season. Despite the strong training camp, he shouldn’t be in starting fantasy lineups for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen’s “ability to be a quality route runner should make him one of the Chiefs’ top answers” against man coverage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Taylor stops short of declaring Allen a starter in three-wide receiver sets, so he is likely still stuck in the No. 4 wide receiver spot. The fifth-round rookie has at least carved out a role for himself, and Taylor dubs him “the biggest winner in camp.” Allen is a worthwhile late-round pick at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 3-of-5 targets for seven yards in the Chiefs’ preseason loss to the Buccaneers on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Allen saw action through the first three quarters of play. His 29 snaps were the third-most of any Chiefs receiver, while his 23 routes run were the second-most on the day. All three of his catches came in the short areas of the field, as evidenced by the -1.7 ADOT he averaged on his three receptions, per TruMedia. One of the most hyped players of this training camp season, the rookie fifth-rounder has a 5-27-0 receiving line on 10 targets in his two preseason games thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a hamstring strain at practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Thornton headed into the medical tent and was subsequently carted to the locker room at Tuesday’s practice. Now it’s been revealed that he suffered a hamstring strain. It’s unclear how long Thornton might be out, but his injury further opens the door for camp standout Cyrus Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-5 targets for 20 yards in Kansas City’s first preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: The good news is that Allen worked with the starters in the slot. The bad news is that he worked well into the second half in the first preseason game while leading the team in targets. He’s clearly the highest-upside stash receiver of the group, but playing deep into the first preseason game isn’t a great sign for his chances of early playing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Although this was only Dotson’s second three-catch performance of the season, this has rather amazingly become something of his weekly statline. Not that it is amounting to anything in fantasy football. It definitely won’t when the Falcons come off bye to face the Vikings in Week 12. Dotson can remain firmly affixed to 12-team league waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons passing attack was a mess against the Bengals in Week 9. Michael Penix threw 31 times, but for just 162 yards. Dotson was a non-factor by product, totaling just 16 yards on two receptions. He’s Atlanta’s WR2, but is merely a WR5/6 heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-5 targets for 95 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The bulk of Dotson’s production came on a single, 76-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Michael Penix lobbed him a ball on the boundary and two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson uncovered with room to run. He bolted down the sideline but didn’t have the speed to take it to the house. That play alone accounted for over half of Penix’s passing output. Dotson has made the occasional splash play while running as Atlanta’s WR2, but his fantasy prospects are not that intriguing headed into Week 9. He will be in the WR5/6 range when the Falcons take on the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties. That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route on 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce missed large chunks of the first and second quarter with injury, but returned to finish the game without incident. It initially appeared Kelce aggravated his pre-existing ankle issue, but coach Andy Reid said afterward it was a calf ailment. That likely means cramps. That also means it’s not a big concern for Week 11 against the Cardinals, but with Josh Downs in tow to finally provide another legitimate target for Patrick Mahomes, Kelce’s TE1 floor is probably lowering for the stretch run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle, questionable) returned for the second quarter of Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce ended up missing about a quarter of action. He figures to be on a snap count for the rest of the afternoon, but we would have to imagine he will be a point of targets emphasis when he is on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Already nursing an ankle issue, Kelce got rolled up at the end of a first quarter reception and hobbled gingerly to the sideline. He tried to re-enter, but ran off the field after briefly checking back in. He then headed to the locker room. We would assume veteran Kelce is genuinely questionable, and that he could get taped up/receive a pain-killing injection and return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: The Chiefs have been limiting Kelce’s participation on Wednesdays in recent weeks. His return to full participation to begin the week is great to see. Kelce, 37, remains a locked-in TE1 at this point in his career. Treat him accordingly against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-6 targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding a rush for one yard and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce scored on a goal line tush push in the first half. It was a nice little treat for fantasy managers starting the old guy in Week 9. Kelce was second among KC pass catchers in targets, trailing Rashee Rice, who saw seven targets on the day. Kelce remains a reliable floor option in PPR formats. He’s had at least four receptions in five games this season, though his after the catch production has (predictably) cratered. Kelce should be in 12-team league lineups against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: This time last week, Kelce was still a limited participant. Today’s upgraded status is a good sign for his overall health. The Chiefs’ stalwart tight end earned eight targets last week despite the ailment. He can be treated as a fantasy football TE1 against the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce looked slightly hobbled by the ankle issue in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, but he played through it and never missed a meaningful number of snaps. A limited session today means he should be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Kelce’s numbers are down over the past month, but he’s still seeing enough work to be considered a low-end TE1, especially against a weak Jets defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: The Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season as they struggled to move the football against the tenacious Seattle defense. Their offense lacked any downfield threat in the absence of their top two receivers, while Xavier Worthy drew primary coverage. Much of Kelce’s aerial work remains tethered to the short areas of the field in his age-37 season, lacking the burst and YAC ability that once defined his game. Kelce moved into sole possession of the No. 5 spot on the NFL’s all-time receptions list, and achieving such a lofty accomplishment is a testament to his standout career. That said, fantasy managers are sure to be disappointed with his early-season production, as the veteran tight end has surpassed a modest four receptions just once through six games. He gets another difficult matchup on the interior against the swarming Broncos defense in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed nine times for 33 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars, adding eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was bottled up on the ground throughout this contest, but Cam Ward leaned on him for easy completions as the Titans played from behind. Pollard eventually cashed in on one of them with a 32-yard score on a simple check-dowk. Pollard broke several tackle attempts from Jagaurs defenders that could only be descried as effortless. The return of Tyjae Spear had no impact on his role, though that could change as Spears gets healthier. Pollard remains a volume-based RB2 for his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans are holding on to Tony Pollard at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Keeping a 29-year-old running back on the final year of his contract on your 1-7 cellar franchise is certainly a choice a team is allowed to make. We don’t know if it’s the one we’d make, but Pollard will be here to hover around RB2 value in games the Titans are pesky and RB3 value in games where the Titans offense plays as we’ve come to expect.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding three receptions for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard had his second-straight multi-touchdown game, scoring the first touchdown of the game on a 40-yard scamper with multiple missed tackles and a stiff-arm in the first quarter. With Tyjae Spears out, Pollard was the only Titans running back that got touches. He recovered his own fumble in the second half and added a one-yard score in the third quarter. He was also dropped for a safety in the third quarter on a head-scratching delayed hand-off to give the Bengals two points. Pollard enters the Titans’ Week 9 bye with several trade rumors swirling; if he is still in Tennessee, Pollard is a fantasy RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy was held without a reception on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Josh Downs making his Chiefs debut, Patrick Mahomes had his best game since 2022. Worthy, sadly, could not get in on the fun, turning in his first 2026 “zero ball” while only really popping up during the broadcast when he failed to corral a fourth quarter onside kick attempt. Worthy was playing through a hamstring injury, but he did not look much worse for the wear. Today was sad confirmation that what little WR4 value Worthy had left is probably now gone with Downs’ arrival. That includes even for plus dates like next week’s contest with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Patrick Mahomes will have his speedy wide receiver on the field this weekend. Unfortunately for Worthy, he may be operating in a reduced role with Josh Downs now in Kansas City. Worthy can still be rostered in 12-team formats, but his play could be even more volatile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Head coach Andy Reid told reporters Worthy is “actually feeling pretty good.” Worthy went down with a hamstring injury late in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets on Sunday. The fact that he’s able to practice in any capacity today suggests he will be good to go for Week 10 against the Falcons. With Josh Downs now in the mix for targets, Worthy’s days as a relevant fantasy option appear to be over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy hobbled off the field after a fourth quarter reception in the KC victory. It appeared to be the serious kind of hamstring injury but we won’t know the extent of it until the team tests the speedy receiver. Worthy had caught all six of his targets for 48 yards before exiting the game. An absence of Worthy would likely free up more targets for Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. The team’s running backs could also see an uptick in targets if Worthy misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Rashee Rice back after missing two games because of a hamstring issue, Worthy was relegated to WR2 duties once again. Per usual, he didn’t do much while Rice racked up PPR-friendly receptions. Worthy was, however, the intended target on a pair of red zone attempts in the third quarter. Pat Surtain easily broke up one pass that was left a bit short and Worthy actually fought to knock another one down that should have been intercepted by Riley Moss. Worthy has topped 25 yards in one game with Rice again. He’s simply not a part of the Chiefs’ plans on offense when they’re at full strength. Fantasy managers can feel free to cut him loose on this week’s run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy struggled to separate from primary coverage of the Seahawks throughout, also committing a drop in a crucial situation in the second half. The Chiefs continue to show hesitancy in utilizing Worthy in a downfield role, which is of particular concern for his fantasy managers considering the absence of Tyquan Thornton. Worthy is better left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the stingy Broncos, particularly if Rashee Rice returns from injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 4-of-7 targets for 70 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy saw a season-high seven targets in this one after Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited just a few plays into the game. Worthy came up with a handful of key plays for the Chiefs, with his biggest coming on a 41-yard reception that put the Chiefs in position for a short touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton a few plays later. The Chiefs now head into their Week 5 bye, but they could be down multiple receivers, with Rice and Thornton (ankle) both suffering injuries in this one. While we don’t yet know the extent of Rice’s injury, Thornton’s ankle injury looked like a potential season-ender. Worthy could well be worth a stash in leagues where he is still available, as he could soon be the top receiver for the Chiefs when they return in Week 6 to face the Chargers. Second-year receiver Jalen Royals, who ran 21 routes in this game, could also see an expanded role in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Daniel Bellinger caught 2-of-3 targets for six yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Belinger caught a goal line touchdown in the second quarter. It was his first touchdown as a Titan. It was also the first receiving touchdown for any Titans tight end this year. Bellinger isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 11, but his presence should preent fantasy managers from having interest in Gunnar Helm.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Titans agreed to terms with TE Daniel Bellinger, formerly of the Giants, on a three-year, $24 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Bellinger reunites with former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who was hired as the Titans’ OC earlier this offseason. Bellinger totaled a career-high 286 receiving yards on just 19 receptions with the Giants last season and started 10 of the 16 games he appeared in. Bellinger is a solid blocker but is unlikely to add much to the Titans’ passing game. We wouldn’t expect this to turn into a fantasy-relevant any time soon, but he’s a good depth piece for an offense that’s in the middle of a rebuild.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Daniel Bellinger caught both of his targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in a Week 18 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Bellinger’s touchdown catch was on a shovel pass from Jaxson Dart. Dart was under heavy pressure and evaded a sack by throwing a back-handed toss to Bellinger, who caught the ball just inches off the ground and rumbled 29 yards for a touchdown. The 25-year-old had some moments of success earlier in the season when the Giants’ receiving room was really banged up and will finish with 19 catches on 26 targets for 286 yards and two touchdowns. He’ll be a free agent in the offseason, and it remains to be seen if he’ll return to his committee role in New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (illness) won’t play in New York’s Week 18 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Two weeks missed with an illness is rather unusual. We hope Johnson is alright and the story about the illness isn’t too gruesome. Johnson returned five touchdowns with a 45/528 line, becoming more involved with the offense when Jaxson Dart took over against the Chargers in Week 4. It’s possible that Johnson exits the 2026 offseason with a TE1 case, but he feels more like a high-end TE2 from where we sit today. His absence in Week 18 gives Daniel Bellinger a chance to feast against Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Daniel Bellinger caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Giants’ Week 17 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: On the Giants’ first drive, Bellinger nearly secured a pass more than 15 yards downfield, but could not hold onto it after getting leveled by a Raiders defender. He earned just two targets after that, though one occurred late in the game on 3rd-and-8, from the Raiders’ nine-yard line. He caught the pass and was stopped two yards shy of the end zone. Bellinger returns to TE2 status against the Cowboys next week if TE Theo Johnson (illness) is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Giants declared TE Theo Johnson, WR Jalin Hyatt, RB Dante Miller, CB Cor’Dale Flott, OLB Caleb Murphy, DL Rakeem Nuñez-Roches and QB Russell Wilson inactive for Week 17 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: The Giants threw the ball 13 times in a losing effort against the Vikings last week, so even if Johnson were to play today, his target volume would be difficult to project. His absence gives No. 2 TE Daniel Bellinger a chance to operate as a full-time player, though, putting him on the touchdown-dependent TE1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Theo Johnson caught 3-of-5 targets for 77 yards in the Giants’ Week 12 loss against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Johnson nearly caught not one but two touchdowns in this one. He was targeted on a pedestrian 17 percent of his pass routes but remained involved in the red zone as the Giants’ biggest pass catcher. Jameis Winston has not looked to Johnson the way Jaxson Dart did before his Week 10 concussion. Dart’s potential return in Week 13 should be a boon for Johnson. Giants TE Daniel Bellinger ran just eight routes to 33 routes for Johnson against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Giants ruled out WR Darius Slayton (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: This is unfortunate, but it was expected. Slayton aggravated his nagging hamstring injury after catching 4-of-4 targets for 89 yards in Week 10 against the Bears. Watching the Giants’ downfield wide receiver work with the cannon-armed QB Jameis Winston would have been fun. Slayton’s absence against the Packers condenses the Giants’ reliable pass catchers to slot WR Wan’Dale Robinson and the tight ends. Robinson is a strong bet to lead the team in targets and can be started as a WR3 in an albeit tough matchup. No. 1 TE Theo Johnson warrants TE1 treatment. No. 2 TE Daniel Bellinger (groin) is best-suited to deep leagues as a touchdown-dependent bet. Keep an eye on possession WR Isaiah Hodgins, who the team brought back earlier this week. He is not worth starting this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Giants TE Daniel Bellinger (groin) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Bellinger cannot catch a break. The 25-year-old tight end has been an injury report mainstay for some time, most recently dealing with a neck injury. His continued participation suggests he will play this weekend, though it is worth monitoring his Friday participation. The Giants’ pass-catching corps is already short-staffed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.headline: Daniel Bellinger caught 1-of-2 targets for eight yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-bel.analysis: Bellinger, returning from injury, ran a route on 25 of the Giants’ 45 drop backs but played well behind Theo Johnson, who had 75 yards on seven catches. The Giants run enough two tight end sets to make Bellinger somewhat interesting in deeper formats. He’s better left on your waiver wire ahead of the Giants’ Week 11 matchup against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 4-of-5 targets for 50 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The four catches were Pitts’ most in three weeks, while the 50 yards were his second most of the season. Unfortunately, that latter stat tells you all you need to know about Pitts’ TE1 viability right now — he doesn’t have any. He’s also now been held scoreless in 7-of-10 appearances. Headed on bye before returning against the Vikings’ shutdown defense, Pitts is a drop candidate in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Three receptions for 23 yards is a disappointing line and unfortunately it represents the most receiving yards Pitts has had in his last three games. Pitts has four touchdowns on the season, but is unusable in fantasy unless he finds the end zone. The definition of touchdown-dependent, Pitts is a low-end TE2 in Week 10 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts’ 20 percent target share would have been good for at least TE2 fantasy numbers on a normal day. This game was anything but normal. Pitts and Jahan Dotson were the only Falcons pass-catchers with multiple receptions. Michael Penix only completed eight passes, so there simply wasn’t enough production to go around. He was intercepted four times and the Falcons were shut out. Pitts’ role as a PPR merchant should tick back up in Week 9 versus the Bengals. He will be back in the TE2 mix for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all five of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The touchdown is nice to see, and Pitts finished tied for second on the team in both catches and targets. However, preliminary snap counts say he played on 37 of the team’s 67 snaps and ran a route on 20 of their 37 dropbacks. Charlie Woerner ran a route on 11 dropbacks and Austin Hooper ran a route on 10 dropbacks, so the Falcons continue to get tons of tight ends on the field. That makes Pitts more of a high-end TE2 option, really solely because of good touchdown equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 25-of-35 attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panther, adding six rushes for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough continued his wildly inefficient ways. He faced constant pressure from a Carolina front seven that entered the week with the league’s sixth lowest QB pressure rate, and missed short and intermediate throws throughout. Shough had a miserable aDOT of 4.5 and had a -8 total EPA on the day. The disjointed Saints offense doesn’t make things easy for Shough, but his total inability to make routine throws is having a real impact on Saints pass catchers. Shough should be considered a superflex-only option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 21-of-35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ 23-22, Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough got off to a dreadfully slow start, throwing for a measly 156 scoreless yards over the first three quarters. The Browns weren’t pushing the Saints to play fast or pass often, resulting in a noticeable lack of volume for Shough. A 64-yard touchdown for the Browns in the middle of the fourth quarter finally forced the Saints to pick up the pace. Shough responded with a 55-yard touchdown drive two series later, though Audric Estime found the end zone on the ground. Shough eventually closed out the game with a 15-yard touchdown strike to Juwan Johnson in overtime. Shough’s fantasy output is tied directly to his passing volume. He’ll remain at the top of the QB2 ranks as long as his defense keeps giving up points, which should happen versus the Panthers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-38 passes for 273 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Saints’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough’s seven rushing yards led the team, which isn’t ideal. The 27-year-old was mostly accurate and on-time with his throws, but he should have had three turnovers in the first half — one dropped interception, one strip-sack that was overturned and one fumble that luckily went out of bounds — in addition to the one costly red-zone interception that actually made the stat sheet. It wasn’t Shough at his best, but there were some flashes of brilliance in the loss. Shough will get a bye week before he faces the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Saints’ 34-27, Week 6 win over the Giants, adding five carries for 32 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints had their usual slow start on offense, going scoreless in the first quarter. Shough then did what he does best and led an effective offensive effort the rest of the way. He is dealing with broken bones in his non-throwing hand and it arguably impacted some of his throws, missing open receivers and struggling to push the ball downfield. Though he averaged 4.8 yards per attempt, he totaled three touchdowns on the day. Shough was also impactful as a runner, totaling 32 yards and a tush push touchdown on the day while also getting tackled inside the five-yard line on another rush. Two straight games have been impacted by Shough’s hand injury but the post-first quarter volume continues to elevate his fantasy floor. Shough is a high-end QB2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As expected, he’ll start and be on the QB1/QB2 borderline against an extremely pesky and attacking Vikings defense that has held down quarterback scoring quite well so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As a right-handed quarterback, Shough should be fine despite his surprise appearance on the injury report. Even in a blowout loss on Monday, the second-year passer racked up 286 yards and a touchdown on 48 attempts. As long as the volume is there, Shough is good for low-end QB1 numbers. He will remain inside the top 12 at his position for Week 5 against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 45-24, Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding five yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough and the Saints stayed true to recent form as they quickly fell into a 14-point hole in the first quarter, with the team now averaging an almost eight point deficit at the half since head coach Kellen Moore took over to start the 2025 season. The team was unable to reproduce the second half magic they so frequently muster behind an overmatched offensive line. Shough needed a late touchdown toss to Devaughn Vele with less than two minutes to play to give fantasy managers something of value. Moore and Shough have their work cut out for them with Brian Flores’ relentless defense coming to town in Week 5, where Shough will be on the QB1/2 border in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Coming off a 5-71-1 receiving line versus the Bengals, Dike appeared to be taking on a larger role in the absence of Carnell Tate. That wasn’t the case versus Jacksonville and he finished fifth on the team in targets. Even desperate fantasy managers can send him back to the waiver wire ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-6 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike saw 58 snaps with Carnell Tate out, second among Titans wide receivers. He scored on an 11-yard reception in the fourth quarter. It was Dike’s first game with over three receptions and second game over one target this season. Dike is mostly utilized as a kick returner but is in line to see increased opportunities on offense if Tate misses additional time. For now, Dike should be off the fantasy radar heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 55 yards in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike also had a carry of seven yards and drew a 50-yard defensive pass interference. He finished the day tied for team-highs in catches and yards. With some help from his punt and kick returns, Dike set the record for all-purpose yards by a rookie at 2,344. Dike has his limitations as a receiver, but he is a force to be reckoned with when the ball is in his hands. He will be in the FLEX mix for his Week 18 date with the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: In addition to his fourth receiving score of the season, Dike set the Titans’ single-season record for kick return yardage. The 24-year-old has been a legitimate all-purpose weapon, even if it hasn’t quite translated to weekly WR4 value. Maybe that will be on tap for 2026, but Dike still lacks either the floor ceiling to be a trusted fantasy option for finals week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Titans’ Week 15 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had the most targets of any Titans wide receiver, but that’s not much to write home about. The Titans love to run screen passes, and Dike is really shifty after the catch, so you figure he’d be a good option on those plays. The Titans don’t seem to agree. The rookie also had a brutal drop in the fourth quarter on a play where Cam Ward evaded three rushers and escaped to the sideline before throwing a dart that hit Dike in the chest. He needs to make those catches, and the drop is a good example of why he’s hard to trust in fantasy leagues right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-8 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 14 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: That’s a highly disappointing yardage total considering Dike’s catches and targets, but the looks matched a season high. The score was also his second in three weeks. The Titans have followed through on their pledge to get Dike more involved down the stretch. It has been difficult for it to translate to real fantasy value because of Cam Ward’s ongoing struggles, but Dike is still looking like someone who could be an eventual fantasy WR3. That will not include for Week 15 against the 49ers. Fantasy managers simply have too many other higher-ceiling options with the playoffs beginning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 14 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike has been quite the volatile scorer as of late. In his late six games, he has finished as the half-PPR WR15-18 three times. In his other three showings, he finished as the WR75 or worse. Facing the Browns’ elite defense, he makes for a very risky FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had a calamitous Week 13 showing with just eight yards on four targets, as well as a fumbled kick return. He’s not a super desirable FLEX option against a strong Browns defense in Week 14.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike has delivered volatile results while playing through small injuries in recent weeks. Although his limited session on Wednesday puts him on track to play, he faces the Browns’ elite defense in Week 14. He is not a recommended FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is up to 16 catches over his past four games, but he’s still looking for his first touchdown of the year. Daniel Bellinger stole a short score in this game. Helm also has just one game over 30 yards to his name. He’s developed a modest PPR floor, but there’s no ceiling to be had headed into his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.
