https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 5-of-9 targets for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm saw career-highs in targets and receiving yards in a high-scoring game against the Bengals. He saw a few targets in the flats but was targeted downfield multiple times, catching two passes of at least 24 yards. Helm also caught a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter. He is the Titans primary pass-catching tight end and saw heavy usage in a pass-heavy game script. Fantasy managers should not anticipate more game scripts like this for the Titans but Helm is a deep league streaming tight end option once the Titans come out of a Week 9 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 3-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Running a route on 23 of the team’s 34 drop backs, Helm was a little more involved than usual in the Titans’ low-octane passing attack. With fewer than 30 receiving yards in every game this season, Helm should not be rostered in any fantasy format for now. He’s been targeted on just 12 percent of his routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm continued to split reps with Daniel Bellinger, who also caught two passes today. Helm hasn’t topped 30 yards in a game this year and his four catches in Week 1 remain a high-water mark. He isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now sitting on a scoreless 6/41 through the Titans’ first two contests. Helm is an intriguing second-year pro, but there’s not going to be much intrigue in the Titans’ offense for the time being. 24-year-old Helm is best left on 12-team league waiver wires head of Week 3 vs. the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm finishes a successful rookie season with a 44/357/2 slash line, and looked to be making a climb up Tennessee’s target pecking order before injuries largely derailed his final month. It’s hard to rely on anything in Tennessee’s offense until we see exactly what happens with the coaching staff, but there are offseason runouts that will put Helm as a high-end TE2 with Chig Oknokwo slated for free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now on the wrong side of questionable, which benefits TE Chig Okonkwo, who has scored a touchdown in consecutive weeks. Okonkwo is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season and has a chance to earn a decent payday with another strong showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 1-of-6 targets for six yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman was second on the Dolphins with six targets on the day, though he caught just one for six yards. He also drew a key defensive pass interference against Sauce Gardner in the second quarter. With Chris Bell (knee) out, Coleman was No. 3 in wide receiver snaps for the Dolphins. He can be rostered in 14-team leagues as a desperation boom-or-bust play for Week 11 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 3-of-3 targets for 46 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman led the Dolphins in receiving yards today. Although that outcome may be unlikely in the coming weeks, he looks like a capable contributor. Coleman scored a 35-yard touchdown on the Dolphins’ 10th drive, shaking his coverage defender along the sideline with a false step and a dramatic upper-body fake, before racing downfield and hauling in the pass in stride before crossing the plane. He nearly scored earlier, on the Dolphins’ fifth drive, snagging a six-yard pass on a quick out route on 1st-and-goal from the Patriots’ six-yard line, but he was unable to stay inbounds. Coleman could warrant boom-bust FLEX treatment in 14-team leagues against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 3-of-7 targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman was heavily involved in the Dolphins’ second-half gameplan, seeing the second-most targets among Miami pass-catchers on the day. He scored on a Malik Willis red zone pass in the fourth quarter and was tackled at the one-yard line on a reception towards the end of the game. Coleman is a fifth-round rookie and unlikely to see this much volume moving forward but is an intriguing deep-league stash in case Malik Washington were to suffer an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 1-of-4 targets for three yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: This is Coleman’s second consecutive week catching 1-of-4 targets for three yards. He earned two targets on the second drive, which was encouraging. He should have had a double-digit gain on the fifth drive, but Malik Willis’ off-target throw was far too low. Willis targeted him again on the sixth drive, but the pass clanged off Coleman’s hands as he slid toward the sideline in the end zone. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, but he is worth keeping an eye on for later in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said there will be no “pitch count” for starting receiver Chris Bell, and that he trusts both Bell and fellow rookie starter Caleb Douglas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: “We believe those guys deserve to start, and we’re gonna start them,” was Hafley’s matter-of-fact Wednesday statement. His words come after the ‘Fins officially listed the third-round rookies as starters on Tuesday. His “pitch count” comments pertain to Bell’s summer stint on the NFI list as he completed his recovery from torn ACL suffered last season at Louisville. Starting a pair of Day 2 receivers in Week 1 is far from ideal for anybody, but no less so than trotting out Jalen Tolbert. The Dolphins are fully committed to their rebuild, and rookies like Bell, Douglas and Kevin Coleman are the biggest potential beneficiaries. Bell and Douglas belong on 12-team league watch lists, with Coleman worth a dynasty stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: The Miami Herald’s Omar Kelly believes Dolphins rookie WR Kevin Coleman Jr. should be the team’s starting slot receiver this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Responding to readers on social media this week, Kelly said he believes Coleman is the Dolphins’ best rookie wide receiver, and linked to an article of his from May 8. In the piece, Kelly argues that Coleman should be the team’s front-runner for the starting slot role. If Coleman can pull it off, he may only get on the field when the Dolphins are in three-wide receiver sets, giving him a limited upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Dolphins selected Missouri WR Kevin Coleman Jr. with the No. 177 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman (5’10/179) spent his college career with four teams in four seasons, starting at Jackson State with Travis Hunter and Deion Sanders. After Hunter and Sanders left for Colorado, he hopped to Louisville and Mississippi State before finishing at Missouri. Coleman spent much of his college career as a slot receiver with some punt return ability mixed in. He is undersized but has acceleration and agility to make him an effective ball-carrier in space. Coleman is limited in his route tree with shallow receptions littered across his college production. Despite the lack of vertical receptions and touchdown production, Coleman got the ball a combined 153 times on offense between Mississippi State and Missouri in his final two seasons. He has a chance to stick on an NFL roster as a gadget slot receiver and special teams return man.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 5-of-10 targets for 79 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor didn’t do much in Carnell Tate’s absence the last time he took the field. He stepped up as the Titans’ clear WR1 in this game. Ayomanor led the team in all receiving categories except touchdowns. He nearly led the way in scoring as well, but the Jags tracked him down inside the five-yard line on his 50-yard catch. Ayomanor will move into the FLEX mix if Tate remains out for Week 11 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor has shown signs of life of late in a Titans offense operating quickly in recent weeks. Against the Browns he tied Carnell Tate for the team lead in targets while running a route on nearly 90 percent of the team’s drop backs; it seems that Cam Ward trusts him more than Calvin Ridley (hip), who missed this game. Even with more involvement in the Tennessee offense, Ayomanor should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy formats ahead of the Titans’ Week 8 matchup against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: It goes down as his second one-catch, three-target, 11-yard game of the season. He posted those exact numbers in Week 1, though with a touchdown for good measure. Ayomanor popped for 69 yards in Week 2 but failed to find the big play in this game, cratering his numbers. As the WR3 on one of the worst offenses in football, he is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 2-of-3 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: One week after finding the end zone, Ayomanor led the Titans in receiving as they nearly upset the Birds. 41 of his yards came on an impressive leaping grab over Marcus Epps. Good stuff, but there’s not going to be much “good stuff” in this limited attack. Ayomanor should also routinely be out-targeted and out-gained by both Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson. Even in 14-team leagues, Ayomanor is probably off the re-draft radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for an 11-yard touchdown in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor’s score came deep into garbage time with the Titans trailing 23-3. 23-year-old Ayomanor had an impressive rookie year for a fourth-round pick in 2025, but he’s now buried behind Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson in the Titans’ receiver corps. This is not an offense that is going to be producing consistent production out of the No. 3 receiver spot. We’ll let you know if Ayomanor becomes 12-team league relevant, but don’t count on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Titans WR Elic Ayomanor (shoulder) resumed practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Per ESPN’s Turron Davenport, Ayomanor was in the huddle early at today’s practice, which is a good sign. The second-year wide receiver left practice early yesterday after seemingly injuring his left shoulder. He appears to be good to go and will now resume competing for a starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 4-of-7 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor secured touchdown No. 4 of his rookie season by leaving his defender in the dust for a seven-yard score. His seven targets tied Chig Okonkwo for a team-high in pass-game opportunities. Ayomanor hasn’t caught more than four passes in a game this year and that’s unlikely to change versus the Jags next week. He will be a splash-play WR5 for the season finale.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-4 targets for 58 yards in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Today was the first time since November 2 Ayomanor caught more than two passes, while those receiving yards were actually a new season high. Not bad, if not terribly notable. Chimere Dike remained the more impressive young wideout against the Chiefs. Ayomanor is a young player who has shown something in an offense displaying subtle signs of progress, but he’s not on the radar for fantasy finals week, while his 2026 rank remains very much to be determined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara had two rushes for four yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara somehow came up with both Saints touchdowns on the day even with Travis Etienne returning from injury and operating as the de facto RB1. Kamara didn’t even lead the backfield in routes, logging 13 pass routes to 14 for Etienne, who had three grabs for 20 yards. Fantasy managers would do well not to chase Kamara’s Week 10 touchdown production when the Saints take on the Bears in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Travis Etienne had eight rushes for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints wasted a few first half plays trying to get Etienne involved in his first game back from an extended injury absence. Those plays predictably went nowhere, and it was Alvin Kamara who had the big fantasy day, scoring both Saints touchdowns — one through the air, the other on the ground. Etienne logged 13 routes to 12 routes for Kamara. The Saints backfield is among the least appealing for fantasy purposes and has been for some time. Etienne will be a desperation deep league option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: As usual, Kamara’s back listing has not prevented him in any real way from playing. A potential Travis Etienne activation off injured reserve could cut into his FLEX value in Week 10, but if Etienne stays on IR, Kamara will be a reasonable play against a rough Panthers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: We expect to see Kamara listed with his typical NIR-rest/back designation when the team’s official injury report is released later today. An update will be provided if this is not the case. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) now practicing and Audric Estime playing well, Kamara is barely fantasy-relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints added Audric Estime via waivers on Monday and he went on to lead the team in carries today. He saw 15 rushes plus one target. Estime also found the end zone after Kamara was tackled at the two-yard line. Kamara was the team’s primary back on passing downs, but his role between the tackles remained incredibly limited. With Travis Etienne potentially returning next week, his role could take another hit in Week 10. He remains a low-upside RB4 for his upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara has no injury designation for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for five yards in the Saints’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers, adding seven receptions for 57 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Tyler Shough ended up leading the Saints with seven rushing yards. Yikes. Kamara was effective as a receiver out of the backfield, but to say that New Orleans struggled to run the ball is quite the understatement as they finished with 18 yards on 17 attempts. The good news for fantasy managers that used Kamara is that he was effective out of the backfield as a receiver, but it’s a modest day for the 31-year-old. Kamara and the Saints will try and get something going after a bye against the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich failed to catch either of his two targets in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich saw just two targets on the day but did not reel either of them in. Kyle McCord targeted him on a red zone fourth down in the second quarter, but the ball was tipped and fell incomplete. Six teams going on bye in Week 11 means Dulcich still nets low-end TE2 consideration against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Despite the quiet fantasy outing, Dulcich finished second on the team in catches and yards. If you couldn’t tell, it was not a productive day for Miami’s passing attack. Dulcich had stacked a few usable weeks over the past month, but Week 9 was his breakout spot against a dreadful Detroit defense. Having missed his big opportunity, he’ll return to the back of the TE2 ranks for Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Three of Dulcich’s catches occurred on the final two drives, and his first catch occurred in the two-minute drill at the end of the first half. Malik Willis seemingly only looks his way when playing quickly. Maybe the coaching staff should address that, because Dulcich played effectively in those situations. The Dolphins face the Lions’ fantasy-friendly pass defense next week, potentially elevating Dulcich to high-end TE2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The fringe TE2 life awaits Dulcich against the Patriots on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The Dolphins’ tight end finally had a decent game, only to tweak an ankle along the way. He should be fine for Week 8 against the Patriots, but he is barely in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich made the most of National Tight Ends Day with a 32-yard catch on the Dolphins’ opening drive and two more gains of 15+ yards throughout the contest. He led the team in catches and targets. Dulcich now has at least four receptions in three of his past four games. Miami’s run-first approach is preventing him from finding spike weeks, but Dulcich has worked himself into the TE2 conversation ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich also added a two-point conversion to his total. It was a low-efficiency passing offense for the Dolphins once again, leading to Dulcich averaging under 10 yards per reception. The 26-year-old tight end is a fantasy TE3 as the Dolphins head into a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 5-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Held under 20 yards in each of the Dolphins’ first two games, Dulcich finally had something of a pop-up effort as the ‘Fins tried in vain to match points with the Chiefs. It was nice to get some proof of TE2 concept, but it is going to be exceptionally difficult for Dulcich to carve out streamer value in a low-volume passing attack focused on seeing what it has in its intriguing rookie receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 1 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Both of Dulcich’s targets occurred on the third drive. One was a six-yarder via play action. The other was a delayed screen pass, which Dulcich admirably ran for 12 yards, picking up a first down along the way. The fact that he was barely involved in a pass-heavy game script bodes poorly for his TE1 viability. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Jalen Tolbert caught 2-of-2 targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Tolbert caught the Dolphins’ sole receiving touchdown of the day on a trick play pass from Malik Washington. He was wide open for a 34-yard score in the second quarter. Tolbert caught his only other target and was otherwise quiet with just 11 offensive snaps. Despite the score, Tolbert should be left on fantasy benches heading into Week 11 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, LB Willie Gay, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., CB Reese Taylor, DE Rob Beal Jr., OL DJ Campbell, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: With Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell both healthy, Tolbert doesn’t have a spot on the game-day roster and is a healthy scratch this week. Douglas is back after missing a month because of an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared QB Brady Cook, DE Chop Robinson, WR Jalen Tolbert, OL DJ Campbell, CB Marcellus Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Robinson remains in concussion protocol and was ruled out earlier in the week. Interestingly, Jalen Tolbert remains unable to be active on a Dolphins team that is hurting for weapons on offense. A lot of it has to do with him not having a clear role on special teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, QB Brady Cook, CB Reese Taylor, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 1 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Tolbert is listed as a second-stringer on the Dolphins’ depth, reinforcing coach Jeff Hafley’s confidence in rookie WRs Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas. Those two are listed as starters alongside slot WR Malik Washington. A wait-and-see approach is probably smart for the rookies, but they can be started in the FLEX spot as needed. Cook will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones believes Jalen Tolbert “appeared to be” one of Malik Willis’ top targets in OTAs and minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Furones also lists Greg Dulcich as a player that was a primary receiver for Willis, but we’ve done plenty of offseason hype on Dulcich. Tolbert appears to be a potential “someone has to catch a ball here” deep league pick, as he’s well off the fantasy radar at this point. He’s not off the board among the top-100 wideouts in ADP. The ceiling is likely low, but if he can emerge as the top option amongst Miami’s wideouts, Tolbert could be a viable WR3/WR4 at points this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: The Miami Herald’s Omar Kelly reports that Dolphins WR Jalen Tolbert distanced himself from his peers, but believes the receiver unit “doesn’t have a single player who would start for another NFL team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Oh, boy. Kelly giveth and taketh away. On the one hand, Kelly believes Tolbert “seems ready to handle the split end, possession receiver role.” On the other hand, Kelly thinks Tolbert is a replacement-level player. Tolbert has cleared 275 receiving yards just once in his four-year career. Kelly is probably right. If Tolbert can become the clear-cut No. 1 target, he might be able to return FLEX value, but he could be an extremely volatile producer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team’s passing offense is “a work in progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Malik Willis, Hafley said during a Tuesday presser, is still building chemistry with the team’s pass catchers in OTAs and working on timing. That presumably includes Malik Washington, who had 46 catches for 317 yards and three scores last season, and Greg Dulcich, who’s expected by Miami beat writers to “figure heavily” into the team’s passing attack in 2026. Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell could also see heavy snaps in the Miami passing game this season. Tolbert, who flashed in Dallas in 2024 with 610 yards and seven touchdowns, could emerge as the Dolphins’ top pass-catching option with a solid training camp. There likely won’t be much target volume to go around, however, considering the team’s plans to operate a run-heavy offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins signed WR Jalen Tolbert, formerly of the Cowboys, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schlutz reports Tolbert is “close with Malik Willis,” who was signed by the Dolphins earlier this week. A former third-round pick of the 2022 NFL Draft, Tolbert never emerged as a top option in the Cowboys’ passing game. Last season, the 27-year-old had his least productive season since his rookie year, catching 18 passes for 203 yards and one touchdown despite appearing on 464 offensive snaps. With Jaylen Waddle being the only starter of note in Miami’s receiver room, it’s possible Tolbert carves out a more meaningful role this season, but we wouldn’t bet on there being much fantasy value here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Jalen Tolbert failed to catch his only target in a Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: We’re just a couple of years away from Tolbert being thought of as a potential fantasy sleeper. Instead, the 26-year-old will finish with 18 catches on 34 targets for 203 yards and one touchdown. He’ll enter free agency this offseason, but doesn’t figure to command a lot of interest as anything other than a depth option to round out a team’s wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Cowboys declared DE Jadeveon Clowney, WR Jalen Tolbert, RB Jaydon Blue, DT Jay Toia, DT Perrion Winfrey and OT Tyler Guyton inactive for Week 14 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Clowney (hamstring) attempted to give it a go in warmups after practicing once, a limited session on Wednesday, this week. He will be missed against the Lions’ top-notch offense. The Cowboys have once again declared Blue, the once-exciting rookie, inactive this week. He does not need to be stashed at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime had seven rushes for six yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding one catch for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was shockingly ineffective a week after he led the Saints backfield with 15 rushing attempts for 72 yards and a touchdown. Travis Etienne returned from injury this week and operated as the nominal RB1 for the disastrous New Orleans offense. Estime won’t hold any fantasy value as long as Etienne is healthy and active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was waived by the Browns on Monday. The Saints claimed him on Tuesday and he was their starting back by Sunday. Life comes at you fast. Kellen Moore made it a point to get Estime going early with three carries for him on their first three plays of the game. He gashed the Browns 32 yards on those three attempts alone. He would later punch in a goal line touchdown to give the Saints the lead in the fourth quarter. Estime will be the Saints’ lead runner until Travis Etienne is activated from injured reserve. That could happen as soon as Week 10, so fantasy managers shouldn’t count on another usable week from Estime anytime soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It wasn’t an overly impressive day for Estime, who was on the Vikings’ practice squad earlier in the week. But in the fourth quarter, with the Browns trailing 10-3, Estime took back-to-back carries for six yards, with his second resulting in a two-yard touchdown that would tie the game with just over eight minutes left in regulation. Estime could see a similar role in next week’s game against the Titans if Quinshon Judkins (ankle) misses another game, but he’ll be hard to trust as far as fantasy is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns signed RB Audric Estime from the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime’s signing comes as Quinshon Judkins is dealing with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5. Estime, who is only 23 years old, already feels like an NFL journeyman as he now heads to his fifth team in three seasons after brief stints with the Broncos, Eagles, Saints, and Vikings. The former fifth-round pick has rushed for 508 yards and three touchdowns in his career and rushed for 76-310-2 as a rookie with the Broncos. Estime could see snaps in Week 6 against the Ravens if Judkins is unable to play, but we wouldn’t expect to see anything close to a meaningful workload at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed Kelvin Banks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and reached an injury settlement with running back Audric Estime in corresponding moves. Banks is undergoing surgery for a severe high-ankle sprain. He could return later this year, but the team will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games, and likely much longer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is questionable to play in Week 1 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara logged two limited sessions to begin the week, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill said he thinks Kamara will play, barring a setback. We do not yet know Kamara’s practice participation level on Friday, but he is traveling with the team, which is a good sign. Kamara would be a PPR FLEX if active. He is expected to play on passing downs while starting RB Travis Etienne leads the team in carries. Etienne is the best bet to handle the primary red zone role, but Kamara has been a prolific touchdown scorer over his career and could factor in. The Saints ruled out RB Audric Estime (thigh).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints’ backup running back statuses continue to change. Veteran No. 2 RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least one month, and RB Audric Estime is now sidelined with an undisclosed injury. Miller and RB Devin Neal (hamstring) both returned this week, though. Beat reporter Jeff Nowak notes that Miller, Neal and RB Ty Chandler were all allowed to rotate in for first-team reps today, as coach Kellen Moore presumably seeks out a viable primary backup for starting RB Travis Etienne. Per Nowak, Miller “looks sharp despite the time missed.” This is worth tracking for short-term bench stash purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 21 times for 63 yards in the Saints’ Week 18 loss to the Falcons, adding five receptions for 43 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing out the string for the Saints’ injury-ruined backfield, Estime reached 100 yards from scrimmage for the first time in his career after posting 98 the week before. Not a bad end to the year for a player who spent the first half of the season on practice squads. Still only 22 years old, Estime is buying himself time to get established in the NFL, but he still probably mostly profiles as a special teamer if he’s going to make a 53-man roster out of camp. Considering the Saints’ issues at running back, it could very well be in New Orleans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 3-of-3 targets for 50 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, completing his sole passing attempt for 34 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington led all Dolphins wide receivers in snaps, but fell behind Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman in targets. He caught all three of his targets, including a circus catch to reel in a dangerous throw from Kyle McCord in the third quarter. The Dolphins also dialed up some trickery in the second quarter with Washington taking a toss and finding Jalen Tolbert downfield for a 34-yard passing touchdown. Ultimately, Washington is on the field a lot for the Dolphins and still ranks in the WR4 range for Week 11 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington wasn’t awfully involved in this game, even if you account for the Dolphins’ low-volume passing approach. He earned a 12 percent target share and added one carry for zero yards. Caleb Douglas, on the other hand, was the runaway WR1 for Miami. He earned eight targets and led the team with six grabs for 70 yards. Already completely out of the playoff race, the Dolphins are in evaluation mode with their young receiver corps. That could mean increasing workloads for Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman. Washington will get another week in the WR4 ranks, but he could be waiver wire fodder if he posts another quiet game against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington continues to play well as a short-area pass catcher, though he did haul in a 23-yarder downfield. He got leveled on the Dolphins’ fifth drive, and Patriots LB Christian Ellis received an unnecessary roughness penalty for the act. It briefly seemed like Washington’s day might be over, but he returned a few plays later to score a one-yard touchdown via a quick out route after going in motion pre-snap. Today’s stat line allowed Washington to clear the century mark in career catches (103). Among NFL wide receivers with at least 100 receptions from 2021-26, Washington’s 8.4 yards per reception ranks dead last. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s WR4 status will continue aplomb against the Patriots in Week 8, though Caleb Douglas’ return probably has capped his ceiling case for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington has cooled off in recent weeks. Although his knee injury is unlikely to keep him out of the Dolphins’ Week 8 matchup against the Patriots, he is barely a WR5 in fantasy football. Washington does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets, adding two carries for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s previous season-low in targets was five. He had also reached at least 43 receiving yards in every game before today. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that his worst box score of the season came in Caleb Douglas’s first game back from a month-long absence. With more competition for targets on a team that doesn’t want to pass the football, Washington is trending in the wrong direction headed into Week 8. He will be a low-end WR4 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington was the most involved Dolphins receiver, leading the team in targets and receiving yards. He started things off with an 18-yard rush and saw a steady peppering of low-depth targets. Though he led all Dolphins skill-position players in snaps, Washington doesn’t see many scoring opportunities in the Miami offense. After a Week 6 bye, The 25-year-old is a volume-based FLEX play Week 7 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-5 targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington remains one of the Dolphins’ primary returners despite his increased receiving involvement. His day began with a muffed punt that he successfully recovered in the end zone for a touchback. Things improved from there. Washington delivered multiple double-digit gains, functioning effectively as a weapon behind the line of scrimmage and in the flats. He also turned in a 17-yarder via a corner route on play action. Rookie WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) may return for next week’s game against the Saints. If he remains sidelined, Washington should be FLEX-viable, though his ceiling is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson added four receptions for six yards. The Chiefs’ defense wasn’t set on Robinson’s three-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. Robinson has now found the end zone in back-to-back games after somehow previously going four straight weeks without a score. So it goes in what is becoming an increasingly dysfunctional offense. Robinson and company are now headed on bye before returning in Week 12 against the imposing Vikings. You won’t be benching Robinson for that one, of course, but you will be limiting your high-end RB1 expectations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals, adding six receptions for 47 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson bounced back nicely after posting 76 scoreless yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. The 24-year-old running back had 100 rushing yards and score while adding six catches for 47 yards through the air. Robinson’s touchdown gives him six in nine games this year after scoring 11 times in 17 games last season. Still an elite fantasy option despite the offense around him, Robinson is a locked in RB1 against the Chiefs in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson dropped his only target of the day. He has quietly been held under 100 rushing yards in four straight games. Robinson normally papers over that with strong receiver numbers, but that disappeared today as well. Michael Penix only completed eight passes and threw four interceptions. Robinson should have better luck in Week 9 against the Bengals, but the odds of him repeating as the RB1 overall are shrinking by the week. He will sit just outside the top tier of fantasy options in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did add 59 yards receiving on five catches to help salvage his fantasy day, but this is the third straight week he has delivered a modest fantasy return after explosive performances in Weeks 3 and 4. In fact, this is now five of seven games this season that Robinson has been held under 90 yards rushing. He’s contributing as a pass-catcher, and he looks elusive when he can get beyond the line of scrimmage, but the Falcons may need to make an adjustment on offense with defenses clearly keying on stopping Robinson. We’d expect them to focus on getting him going next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson had nine rushes for 61 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for -8 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson couldn’t get anything going against a Chicago defense allowing the fifth highest rate of yards before contact. The Bears were intent on snuffing out the Atlanta rushing attack and forcing Michael Penix to move the ball through the air. It worked for much of the game. Robinson, who had 425 rushing yards in his previous three games, remains the engine of the run-heavy Falcons offense and should get back on track in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens, adding 32 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson suffered through poor offensive efficiency in the first half, finally breaking loose for a 38-yard carry on the team’s first possession of the third quarter. Although the receiving production and yardage total were enough to salvage a usable fantasy week, it was only the second time in five games in which Robinson failed to find the end zone. Robinson remains an elite fantasy RB1 ahead of a Week 6 showdown against the Bears in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints, adding two yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Week 4 marked Robinson’s second consecutive game going over 100 yards with two touchdowns on the ground, this time aided by a 59-yard touchdown run on his first touch of the game. The Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, with backfield mate Brian Robinson adding three to the two of Bijan. The return of quarterback Michael Penix has given the Falcons the threat of passing after dropping their first two games of the season behind suboptimal play from the position, and nobody has benefited more from reduced numbers in the box than Robinson. He’ll look to keep the momentum going as a top-tier RB1 when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson single-handedly out-gained the Packers in the first half after clearing the century mark on the ground early in the second quarter. His patience and burst through the gap were on full display, routinely gaining chunk yardage on first down while making the Green Bay defensive front look like Swiss cheese. A 55-yard scamper on a wide zone carry in the first quarter got the All Pro back off to a blazing start, adding his first of two touchdowns to cap the drive. He would take on a second score late in the fourth quarter to send the Packers to their first home opener loss in 14 years. Robinson remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the division rival Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne had eight rushes for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: The Saints wasted a few first half plays trying to get Etienne involved in his first game back from an extended injury absence. Those plays predictably went nowhere, and it was Alvin Kamara who had the big fantasy day, scoring both Saints touchdowns — one through the air, the other on the ground. Etienne logged 13 routes to 12 routes for Kamara. The Saints backfield is among the least appealing for fantasy purposes and has been for some time. Etienne will be a desperation deep league option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: He did practice again today, finally hitting a full session, so he at least has cleared a full week of practices if nothing else. If Etienne does play he could be a reasonable FLEX option. There are reports that he could be on a snap count if he does play, and that mixes with the early-season usage to create a situation that isn’t necessarily guaranteed to smash. That said, the Panthers are an enticing matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Travis Etienne’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Raiders. The 27-year-old back will need to have his 21-day return window opened before he can take the practice field, so we’ll see if Moore and the staff elect to designate him for a return ahead of Wednesday’s practice. Until that happens, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, and CJ Donaldson will continue to operate as the Saints’ top options, with Kamara the likely leader in what has been an underwhelming backfield this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: We do not yet know today’s participation level, but Etienne logged two limited sessions to begin the week. Hopefully, we get a report pre-game revealing the injury’s severity, so we can better assess his potential usage. Given the Saints’ prior backfield workload splits and Etienne’s soft-tissue strain, he should probably be viewed as a low-end RB2/FLEX starter right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron was on the receiving end of a pair of deep shots from Trevor Lawrence. The first was a long contested catch on the boundary and the second was a layup touchdown. Cameron was completely uncovered for a 25-yard touchdown strike. It was his third score of the year. Cameron is a better real-life player than a fantasy option, but he’ll at least be on the radar as a high-risk FLEX play for Week 11 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Brian Thomas Jr. played only 23 snaps in Week 3 because the Jaguars “were playing in a little bit more 12 and also some of the things that we had Josh [Cameron] on specifically were things that we felt good about him doing within a role that he has.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that Cameron’s usage (23 snaps) could make it “stand[s] to reason Thomas could quickly become the fourth option instead” in a column that says he believes a “new start would be best for both parties.” It sounds like there’s a non-zero chance that Thomas is on the trade block at the deadline, as weird as that seems given how good the Jaguars have been on offense. Thomas isn’t necessarily someone who has to be rostered in shallow leagues given how things are trending.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught his lone target for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: He caught one of Trevor Lawrence’s three touchdown throws on the day. Cameron has begun to eat into Brian Thomas Jr.'s snap share. Against the Patriots Cameron logged ten routes to 16 routes for Thomas while Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers each ran 31 routes. If the Jaguars part ways with Thomas in the coming weeks, Cameron would likely step into a bigger role in the potent Jags passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron was thought to be buried on the Jaguars depth chart as a rookie, but Liam Coen found opportunities for him in Week 1 nevertheless. He caught a touchdown pass in the first half and saw increased snaps with Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) exiting the game briefly in the first half. Despite the touchdown, fantasy managers still should not expect Cameron to get fantasy-relevant opportunities unless one of the Jaguars’ top three wide receivers are injured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes WR Josh Cameron would be the fill-in starter if a Jaguars starting wide receiver misses time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: This might not matter, but it is worth noting. The Florida Times-Union recently reported that Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers ( thumb ) is sidelined, as is WR Brian Thomas (shoulder). Both picked up minor injuries recently, but according to Shipley, the team does not “seem overly concerned” about either issue. Cameron and fellow sixth-round rookie WR CJ Williams have had good training camps. Cameron is evidently the name to know for waiver wire purposes in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes Jaguars WR Josh Cameron “has the size and traits to work his way into the outside receiver rotation sooner rather than later.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron injured his ankle during the draft process, so he only recently began practicing with his new teammates. He participated in special teams drills last week and made his offense debut today, on Tuesday, at mandatory minicamp. Per Shipley, Cameron arguably had the best day of any receiver. The Jaguars’ wide receiver corps is very deep, so it is tough to see how Cameron could become a meaningful contributor in year one. He is probably worth adding in dynasty formats, though. Keep an eye on him this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Jaguars selected Baylor WR Josh Cameron with the No. 191 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: With a bulky frame, Cameron (6’1/220) profiles best as a physical, contested-catch receiver. He started almost exclusively on the outside at Baylor, operating as the Bears’ No. 1 wideout his last two seasons. Totaling 19 touchdowns over that span, Cameron also led the Big 12 with 5.8 receptions per game in 2025. Cameron lacks the burst and route-running skills to separate consistently and is not a yards-after-catch player. However, he possesses good ball skills, rarely tallying drops while his physical presence often bullied college cornerbacks. The Athletic’s Dane Brugler also notes Cameron is a “competitive blocker and can be an asset in the run game.” An NFL team can build upon Cameron’s physical toolset to develop him as a blocker and big-bodied receiver at the next level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed 3 times for a loss of two yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding 2 receptions for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is still the Dolphins’ backup running back, though this has led to limited opportunities behind Ollie Gordon. He saw 12 snaps on the day and only has fantasy value as a handcuff to Gordon moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright missed last week with the quad issue. Kaytron Allen played through a quad issue of his own, though he only saw one carry. Allen practiced in full today as well. Wright will return to a distant RB2 role for Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright, WR Jalen Tolbert, TE Justin Joly, G Christian Haynes, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., and CB Reese Taylor inactive for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Both Wright and Kaytron Allen were questionable because of quad injuries. Allen is active and will serve as Ollie Gordon’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaylen Wright (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright had been backing up Ollie Gordon before going down with the quad injury. Kaytron Allen is the next man up for RB2 duties, though he’s also dealing with a quad issue. Needless to say, we’re expecting a large workload for Gordon this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) was limited. At some point, Allen might get a chance to overtake Wright for the No. 2 role, though Wright remains a capable special teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed two times for five yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright failed to catch his lone target and returned five kicks for 142 yards. Wright is just a bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon operating in a featured offensive role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot/quad) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is a mediocre bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon playing well in the lead role. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he may be able to slightly improve his efficiency if his health continues to improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright managed just six touches, even with Miami running the ball 41 times today. Wright is the only running back seeing work outside of Ollie Gordon, but the latter is pushing for workhorse status, leaving Wright without much to do. He is somewhere well beyond the RB4 ranks for his Week 8 matchup with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 3-of-7 targets for 35 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: None of the Carolina pass catchers did much in a game that saw the Panthers go ultra run-heavy. McMillan led the team in targets but was never on the same page with Bryce Young, who had one of his worst games of the season. On the season McMillan has four games with at least 75 yards, along with five games of at least five receptions. McMillan will be a WR2 option in Week 11 against a shaky Ravens secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan’s four-yard touchdown with the Panthers attempting to complete a fourth quarter comeback was his first since Week 4 and only his third of the season. He has also now been held below 60 yards receiving in three straight games as Bryce Young has been mired in a slump. If there’s good news, it’s that McMillan has maintained a decent floor, and we know the next spiked week can’t be far away. It could come as early as Week 10 against the Saints’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Feel lucky McMillan even reached those marks, as the Panthers simply did not compete in a game where they committed four turnovers and trailed 33-6 at halftime. The first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. McMillan had a better go of it than Jalen Coker, who caught one pass and fell down to create an interception. A shambles, though one the Panthers have to move on from quickly, as they are headed to Green Bay for a potential short-week shootout on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14-of-16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan set career highs in both receptions and yardage in the first half with nine catches for 147 yards before the break. He operated as the clear alpha in a pass attack without both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, routinely dusting everyone the Lions had at their disposal in an injury-ravaged secondary. While the receiving line surely turns heads, fantasy managers were left even more ecstatic about the way in which he was utilized, with the second-year receiver catching six passes for 94 yards and both touchdowns while aligned in the slot. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is providing structure, sequencing, and situational tendencies unlike anything fans had grown accustomed to when head coach Dave Canales was helming the offense, resulting in quarterback Bryce Young leading the league in passing while averaging more than 30 points per game through the first month of play. McMillan’s ceiling remains sky-high as a legitimate WR1 when the Panthers square off against the Eagles fin Week 6 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: By far McMillan’s quietest outing of the young season came with Jalen Coker departing midway through with a quad injury. No. 3 Xavier Legette didn’t even suit up as he battled a knee issue. That allowed the Browns’ defense to key in on T-Mac, and key they did. Fill-in No. 2 Brycen Tremayne took advantage with four receptions for a team-leading 83 yards. Heinous stuff for McMillan managers, but he has an immediate Week 4 bounce-back spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan took a backseat to Jalen Coker last week. The opportunities were distributed more evenly this time around. McMillan led the team with 10 targets and a 28 percent target share. Coker wasn’t far behind with nine targets. McMillan easily led the team in yards, though Coker caught eight balls and Darren Waller popped up for a two-score game. This offense may ultimately be too spread out for McMillan to reach his full potential, but Week 2 reaffirmed his status as the team’s top dog. He will be in the WR2 mix when the Panthers take on the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-8 targets for 75 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan played distant second fiddle to Jalen Coker, who cooked the Chicago secondary for 138 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Panthers in air yards and targets. A bulked-up McMillan appeared a little slower than he was as a rookie in 2025, and had trouble separating for most of the game. Coker’s involvement and Bryce Young’s trust in his WR2 might be a problem for McMillan’s upside this season. He should, however, remains a decent weekly floor option, including next week against a gettable Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Panthers will “likely” decide whether to offer QB Bryce Young an extension in the 2027 offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Young has two years remaining on his contract, but is currently eligible for an extension. According to Wolfe, Young needs to improve in three areas. First, Young must check down when it’s the responsible thing to do, in turn elevating his completion rate to the “high 60s, low 70s” range. Second, Young must be comfortable playing with tempo and diverse personnel formations, including WR Tetairoa McMillan lining up in the slot more often. Third, Young must play quickly and decisively. Whether he can accomplish these feats is up in the air. He’s a mid-to-low QB2 for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding four receptions for 39 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continues to operate as the Dolphins’ workhorse back, getting 20-of-23 running back carries on the day. He also saw five targets out of the backfield, operating as a useful target in the flats for Kyle McCord. Passing game utilization as a an easy-button target elevated his fantasy production on a day he did not score a touchdown. Gordon will continue to see a heavy workload en route to RB2 fantasy viability for Week 11 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon caught his only target for nine yards. Jaylen Wright was out this week. Kaytron Allen was active but entered the weekend with a quad injury. He saw one touch. Gordon earned another bell-cow workload but failed to do much with it for the second week in a row. Things should turn around for him when Miami takes on the equally down-bad Colts in Week 10. Gordon will remain in the RB2 mix despite the consecutive bust weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 19 times for 69 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continues to look like a powerful, capable interior runner, deserving of the Dolphins’ starting role. He, frustratingly, had a 15-yard run erased by a holding penalty and failed to catch his lone target. Gordon celebrated a bit too enthusiastically after a five-yard run on the Dolphins’ seventh drive and was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The young player was extremely upset about the call and required one-on-one conversations with coach Jeff Haffley, another unidentifiable coaching staff member and Malik Willis before regaining composure. Gordon will likely end up in the mid-to-high RB2 ranks against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: The Dolphins took an early lead and never looked back, allowing them to lean on their ground game for the better part of four quarters. Gordon, in turn, set new career highs in rushes and yards. In four starts sans De’Von Achane, Gordon has 69 carries for 332 yards and four touchdowns.
