He has finished as a top-20 fantasy option at his position in all four starts. Gordon’s role on one of the most run-heavy offenses in the league is too good to ignore. He will be in the RB2 mix when the Dolphins take on the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continued to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 running back, scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. He took all of Miami’s red zone backfield touches and was tackled at the one yard line in the third quarter, coming close to his second touchdown of the day. He lost two yards the next play and the Dolphins did not convert. Gordon saw 42 snaps on the day and will be a low-end fantasy RB2 for Week 7 against the Jets after a Week 6 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon entered the game on the Dolphins’ second drive, generating one yard and two receptions on three touches during that possession. Things improved from there. After letting nominal starting RB Jaylen Wright and Gordon each play their own drives, the Dolphins eventually began rotating them in and out until Gordon separated on the first drive after halftime. Gordon notched three carries in a row, breaking off a 53-yarder on the second one by navigating traffic and making his way to the left sideline, shedding a jersey grab along the way. On the seventh drive, he had what could have been a breakaway touchdown run blown dead by officials, who thought Gordon was down by contact as he stumbled through the box. It was a close call. He then touched the ball on two-of-four plays on the ensuing drive, including a touchdown run up the middle from 12 yards out, in which Gordon acrobatically vaulted over a downed lineman. Tentatively expect Gordon to be the Dolphins’ starter in Week 5 against the Bengals and treat him as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones reports that Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright is lining up with the first-team offense during pre-game warmups.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon is rotating in behind Wright, confirming Wright is the team’s current starter. That said, the Dolphins could still split the backfield workload almost evenly. We won’t know what the plan is until the game is underway. For now, Wright should be viewed as the slightly safer FLEX, though both running backs could get bottled up by the Vikings’ defense today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Jaylen Wright (foot) should be good to go for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright was a full participant in Thursday’s and Friday’s practices, which is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. If he doesn’t draw a questionable tag later in the day, we’ll go ahead and assume that the third-year back will be on the field when the Dolphins visit the Vikings. Wright should be in line for a decent day as far as volume is concerned, but it’s hard to invest much hope in him or Ollie Gordon, who will split work with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the remainder of the season. It’s hard to know how the touches could be distributed here, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be rushing to put either back in their lineups against a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright should be rostered in 12-team leagues. He is now on track to play in Week 4 against the Vikings and is still listed ahead of RB Ollie Gordon on the Dolphins’ depth chart. The Vikings’ defense could bottle up this running back, but things might get a tad easier in Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 23-of-43 passes for 286 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception in the Falcons’ 35-13, Week 10 loss to the Chiefs, adding four rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix now has just one total score over his past three starts. Although the 286 yards look nice in the box score, Penix had only 86 at the break. A huge chunk of his production came with the Falcons in frantic fourth quarter comeback mode, and the “comeback” was never particularly realistic. No longer looking like a solid matchup-based streamer, Penix now goes on bye before coming off the open date vs. the Vikings’ ferocious defense. Things do get better in Week 12 against the Lions, but that’s a long time from now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 20-of-31 passes for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Falcons’ 34-17, Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix has now gone back-to-back weeks without eclipsing 200 yards. He found Charlie Woerner for a one-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but couldn’t get much going for the rest of the game. Wide receiver Drake London dominated in a small sample with Penix healthy last year, but he’s had just two games with at least 100 yards and only one touchdown this season. Penix is a low-end QB2 heading into Week 10’s home matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 8-of-24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions in the Falcons’ 16-0, Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix got off to a poor start and his play spiraled from there. He threw a pass directly at Bucs linebacker Alex Anzalone’s chest on the first play of Atlanta’s second drive for an easy interception. Anzalone then took the ball away two Penix throws later by, again, simply standing in the throwing lane. Penix wasn’t seeing the field and nothing changed as the game went on. He threw two more interceptions and had several other passes that could have been caught by the Bucs. Even his best play, a 76-yard toss to Jahan Dotson, was a throw into double coverage where two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson wide open at the last second. This looked like an homage to Cooper Rush’s two catastrophic starts to open the season. Penix should rebound in Week 9 versus the Bengals, but his fantasy stock is undoubtedly on the decline. He is shuffling to the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ 29-20, Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The stats may make it seem like Penix had his way with the 49ers, but it didn’t seem like a seamless performance in reality. He missed some deep passes and overthrew Drake London on a clear touchdown in the second half. He really wasn’t able to get much going down the field, but the Falcons’ defense forced four turnovers, which set up some short fields that Penix was able to take advantage of. He gets a good matchup against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 19-of-33 for 225 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was a mess in the first half, missing Drake London on what should have been an walk-in 30-yard touchdown. The Falcons abandoned the run game in the second half, facing a three touchdown deficit, and Penix threw three touchdowns in hurry-up mode. Taking five sacks on the day, Penix targeted London and Jahan Dotson heavily, connecting with Dotson on a nicely thrown 41-yard gain in the second half. This was the first multiple-TD game of Penix’s season. He’ll be a low-ceiling superflex play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was able to practice this week and will start for Atlanta in a potentially high scoring game against the Bears. Penix should be considered a streaming option in most formats. Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB C.J. Henderson, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, LB Christian Harris, OL Ethan Onianwa, and DE Drake Jackson inactive against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was reported the day after the Falcons’ overtime loss to the Ravens that there was “optimism” that Penix would start in Week 6. After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice, he seemed like a lock to be ready to go by Sunday, so Friday’s news isn’t all that unexpected. Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception this season, throwing one touchdown in each of his first three games. He’ll be on the fantasy radar in 2QB/Superflex leagues against a Bears defense that has allowed just two top-12 fantasy finishes to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is great news for the Falcons’ offense, which can barely function with Tua Tagovailoa at the helm. Penix is firmly on track to play in Week 6 against the Bears, as long as he gets through the week setback-free. Penix can be viewed as a high-end QB2 with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “We’ll see how he’s feeling,” head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Wednesday morning, adding that Penix should be able to play through the injury. Even if it’s a limited practice session for Penix, it’s good news for his Week 6 availability following his Sunday night rib injury against the Ravens. Penix, operating under center at a much higher rate than last season, is among the most efficient quarterbacks in the league through Week 5. If Penix is out, Tua Tagovailoa would represent a major downgrade for all Atlanta pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports there’s “optimism” that Michael Penix (ribs) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix said after Sunday’s loss that he didn’t believe his injury would be long-term. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime because of his injury, but he also added that he likely would have gone back on the field had the Falcons received the ball to start the extra quarter. Instead, Penix said his pain worsened the longer he sat, which was why he ultimately didn’t go back in. Penix’s status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he can’t start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would be in line to start his first game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans, adding one rush for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter’s highlight of the day came on defense when he made a diving interception in the first quarter. He played sparingly on offense once again. Hunter is a starting corner who sees a few snaps on offense every week. He is not on the fantasy radar for his Week 11 game against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter was held without a catch in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter did add a 5-yard “rush” on what sure looked like a pass attempt from Trevor Lawrence, but that’s neither here nor there. What is here is a rather predictable letdown after Hunter went into the Jaguars’ Week 7 bye with a pop-up effort in London. Although it was good to see Hunter contribute at all on offense, his role is too limited in an attack with too many mouths to feed to treat him as even a boom/bust WR4. That includes for Thursday’s short-week date with a Ravens team now missing starting quarterback Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught 4-of-4 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: In London, where Travis Hunter’s best games live, Hunter both caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud (his first of the season), becoming the first player to do both in the same game since Brian Dawkins in 2002. Hunter did all this on just nine offensive snaps. The skill is there to do this on offense, but the Jaguars have really been defense-first with his snaps this year. Depending on the post-bye buzz, Hunter could be a reasonable pick-up in fantasy leagues ahead of Week 8’s games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the Jaguars are “looking at continuing to find different ways” to get Travis Hunter involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Coen talked about getting Hunter involved more on both sides of the ball, so it’s unclear how much of an uptick in offensive snaps we can expect in Week 3. Hunter has a 58 percent snap share on defense and a pitiful nine percent snap share on offense through two games. Even if he isn’t likely to hit the fantasy radar anytime soon, it would be shocking for the No. 2 overall pick to play this infrequently every week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught his lone target for eight yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns, adding one carry for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter saw just four offensive snaps to 39 defensive snaps against the Browns. With a good wide receiver room, Hunter was not playing offense as much and his utilization overlapped with Jakobi Meyers. It’s unlikely the 23-year-old achieves much fantasy relevancy without an injury to Meyers moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Travis Hunter “is expected to be the Jaguars’ No. 1 cornerback in Week 1 and beyond.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley leaves the light on for offensive contributions, entertaining the idea that Hunter can chip in “a few hundred yards and a few touchdowns” this season as well. That said, the early indications for Hunter’s FLEX viability in managed leagues are pretty bleak. Stash him if you wish, but understand that starting him in Week 1 against the Browns could result in zero points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter has taken reps “almost exclusively at cornerback” for the last two weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley estimates that Hunter has logged fewer than 10 reps at wide receiver in team drills during that span. Shipley said, “it seems like” the Jaguars are treating Hunter like their CB1. He also still thinks “there will be games where he logs 50 percent of the offensive snaps,” though. The biggest takeaway is that Hunter has an extremely wide range of potential outcomes, and he cannot be counted on to be FLEX-viable at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: ESPN’s Mike DiRocco reports that Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. and CB/WR Travis Hunter “have shared reps” in 11 personnel packages.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: To be clear, Thomas is the starting X-receiver and Hunter is rotating in behind him. Hunter has also been taking more defensive snaps lately, so if he is going to maintain an offensive role, a simplified downfield role makes sense. Regarding Thomas, DiRocco adds that he “was arguably the best player on the field” during organized team activities, has had a “great” training camp and is “showing some of the toughness and ball security that seemed to be missing last season.” With all of that in mind, losing snaps in three-wide receiver sets is a bit surprising. Thomas is extremely talented, but obvious questions remain as to his usage in the upcoming season. A boom-bust WR3 season could be on the way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter took zero 11-on-11 reps on offense on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: It was suggested by Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley that the Jaguars could be “tipping their hand” here, as he writes “it is clear the Jaguars believe they need to devote more practice time with Hunter before Week 1 at cornerback, which could be the biggest signal yet that the majority of his snaps against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13 will be at cornerback.” Hunter will likely still be involved in the offense — he has worked with the offense every day before this — but it is notable that there was a shift here. Hunter will likely be just a dart throw WR5/WR6 in most standard leagues this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe believes Brian Thomas Jr. will play the X receiver role in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: That would mean Thomas is set to play on the outside at the line of scrimmage. Parker Washington will presumably play in the slot with Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter fighting for flanker duties. As Wolfe notes, Liam Coen learned last year that going over the middle of the field and taking hits isn’t BTJ’s thing. Instead, he will likely be tasked with winning deep and beating man coverage. Wolfe noted Liam Coen’s roots in the Rams’ offense and compared BTJ’s role to that of Brandin Cooks and Sammy Watkins when they played in LA. Cooks topped 1,200 receiving yards in his first season with the Rams but fell below 600 in his second and final season with the team. Watkins, meanwhile, played just one season in LA and was also held under 600 yards. All signs point to Washington being the team’s No. 1 receiver this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for nine yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange saved an otherwise bust of a fantasy outing with a touchdown in the third quarter. Liam Coen schemed him open via a rub route at the goal line for an easy three-yard score. Strange has seven targets over his past three games. After a promising start to the year, he’s fallen to the middle of the TE2 pack headed into Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange had a 46-yard first quarter catch-and-run that went down as the Jags’ longest gain of the day in a 42-7 demolition of the pathetic Colts. Strange was really rumbling, looking out of gas at the end of his journey. Strange actually tied for the team lead in receiving yards, but that’s because Trevor Lawrence attempted all of 14 passes. Strange has done enough to keep himself in the TE2 mix, but he is not an ideal TE1 streamer heading into a short-week Thursday night date vs. a Ravens team that will be without Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: The Jaguars did have a tight end touchdown, but unfortunately for fantasy managers it went to Nate Boerkircher on a ridiculous one-handed stab on a pop pass at the goal line. Strange has now gone for 23 targets in three games and appears to be crowding out Brian Thomas Jr. He’s a reasonable low-end TE1, albeit one on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: After a quiet three games to start the year, Strange has heated up over the past two weeks. He led the team with seven catches last week and did so again today in London. Strange had seven catches in his first three games combined. He can’t be expected to pace the Jags in receiving, but Strange is back on the TE1/2 border for his Week 6 date with Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was Trevor Lawrence’s primary target against a Bengals defense that has struggled against tight ends. Many of his targets were middle-of-the-field intermediate passes as he tallied 95 total receiving yards on the day. The Jaguars offense has a variety of pass-catchers that can find success based on defensive matchup. The game environment aligned perfectly for Strange, who rarely came off the field with 53 total snaps. The Eagles are a tougher matchup for tight ends, but Strange is a good streamer option in the high-end TE2 territory for a Week 5 matchup in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers dominated looks from Trevor Lawrence on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Strange played his usual role as a check down option for Lawrence, rumbling for yards after the catch on two of his three grabs. Strange, with seven catches on the year, could be a streaming play in Week 4 against the Bengals if the game turns into a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange ran a pass route on 30 of the team’s 36 drop backs but was invisible for most of the game. For now Strange can be treated as a desperation streamer in 12-team formats ahead of the Jags’ Week 3 matchup against the Patriots. He should remain on waiver wires in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange operated as the Jaguars’ primary receiving tight end, seeing three targets on the day. In a loaded passing attack, he still found opportunity in what was a very fantasy-friendly offense. Strange caught a 14-yard touchdown in the second quarter and was mostly quiet in a second half where the Jaguars were already up by four scores. The Jaguars wide receivers will take much of Lawrence’s targets but Strange has a role over the middle of the field; he profiles as TE2 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth “up to” $48 million. A chunk of that figure is presumably based on incentives. The contract includes $25 million guaranteed. Strange posted a minor breakout in 2024 with 411 yards on 40 grabs. He upped the ante in 2025 to 46 catches for 540 yards despite missing five games. Strange was heading into the final year of his rookie deal before this extension and the team spent multiple draft picks on tight ends, making it look like they were considering letting him walk next offseason. Instead, Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol will primarily see the field for heavy offensive looks, something the team talked about after the draft. Strange will sit on the TE1/2 border in early fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: J. Michael Sturdivant caught 2-of-4 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sturdivant found the end zone in the third quarter when Jordan Love connected with him on a 32-yard score. Sturdivant broke free behind his defender and found a hole to secure the long catch, giving the rookie UDFA his first career touchdown. Sturdivant was the only Packers player to score in a game that was dominated by the Vikings’ defense for most of the afternoon. He won’t be on the fantasy radar when the Packers return from their bye in Week 12 to face the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Skyy Moore (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: We’re Skyying less and less. Assuming Savion Williams (ankle) isn’t activated off injured reserve, J. Michael Sturdivant could become a deep-league stab or DFS punt against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers signed Florida WR J. Michael Sturdivant.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sturdivant, 23, flashed high-end athleticism at the NFL Scouting Combine, while measuring 6’3/207. The 65/755/7 receiving line he posted as a redshirt freshman in 2022 ended up being a career-best. The Athletic’s Dane Brugler notes Sturdivant led all FBS freshmen in receiving that year. He spent two seasons at Cal before transferring to UCLA for two more, and ended up at Florida for a one-off campaign. He will need to contribute via special teams to have any short at the 53-man roster in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cal received a verbal commitment from four-star 2021 WR J.Michael Sturdivant.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sturdivant announced his commitment on social media Saturday morning. The 6-foot-2, 183-pound wideout was always considered a strong lean towards the Golden Bears, but he also had interest in schools like LSU, Oklahoma and UCLA. Gabe Brooks of 247Sports cites his ability to track the ball and that he can make plays with the ball in his hands. The recruiting website ranks Sturdivant the 27th best wideout in the 2021 class. A very big get for Justin Wilcox and the Cal coaching staff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed 10 times for 42 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Johnson’s 10 carries and 42 rushing yards both led the Packers, who also mixed in MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks throughout the day. While Johnson failed to replicate the 14-68-1 performance he had in Week 9 against the Patriots, his 10 carries were more than double those of the next closest back. The Packers are now entering their Week 11 bye, but if Josh Jacobs (thumb) is unable to go in Week 12 against the Rams, Johnson could have some boom-or-bust RB3/Flex appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed 14 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: An early injury to Josh Jacobs (finger) opened the door for Johnson to have a career day. The former third-round pick rushed for a career-high 68 yards in this one while leading the Packers in carries and managed to find the end zone on a two-yard touchdown in the second quarter. In addition to Jacobs leaving the game early, Johnson also benefited from MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive. Half of his rushing production came on a 34-yard run, and fantasy managers should exercise caution before adding him off of waivers this week. The Packers have already said that they are going to see if Jacobs can play through his fractured finger, and it’s possible Lloyd will be active next week after entering this weekend carrying a questionable tag. If both Jacobs and Lloyd are sidelined, Johnson could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues as a boom-or-bust RB3 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed seven times for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Even with Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve, Johnson remain mired in a three-man committee, as veteran journeyman Pierre Strong slid seamlessly into Brooks’ vacated “role.” In fact, it was worse than that, as Johnson could also only watch as MarShawn Lloyd and Strong formed an early 1-2 punch. Johnson wasn’t really involved before garbage time. Before that, Lloyd had the advantage in short-yardage situations, notching the first two rushing touchdowns of his star-crossed career. Yet to handle more than eight carries in a game, it just isn’t happening for Johnson in 12-team league fantasy. He’s a distant FLEX bet ahead of Week 6 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Brooks suffered the ankle injury in Week 4. He went down in the first half and did not return. Brooks underwent testing on his ankle after the game, though the exact nature of his injury has yet to be reported. He does appear to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he can’t go, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield. Johnson led the team in carries last week but also gave up a goal line fumble. We expect Lloyd to get the start versus Chicago on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Chris Brooks is undergoing tests on his ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Brooks left the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs with an ankle injury in the first half. He did not return after the break and LaFleur didn’t have any definitive answers about the injury on Monday. It sounds like his status for Week 5 is very much up in the air. After coughing up a goal line fumble, Kaleb Johnson would likely take a backseat to MarShawn Lloyd once again. Lloyd has some low-end RB3 appeal as the potential lead back, but this is ultimately a backfield to avoid for fantasy purposes if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A week after breaking out for 171 yards and a score, Watson and the rest of the Packers’ explosive passing game were grounded by the physical Vikings defense. Jordan Love and company failed to generate many downfield plays on the day and were instead forced to settle for more short and intermediate throws, which the Vikings immediately shut down. Watson’s biggest play came on a 15-yard reception in the first quarter on a drive that ended with a missed field goal by Trey Smack. He will be on the fantasy radar as a high-end WR2 in Week 12 when the Packers return from their bye week to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson and fellow receiver Matthew Golden combined to catch 14 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, as both receivers attacked downfield at will against an overmatched Patriots secondary. Watson saw four of his seven receptions go for 20-plus yards, and found the end zone on a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter, one play after the Packers’ defense forced a turnover. Watson has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has four games of 100-plus-yard performances on his resumé this season. He draws a tough Week 10 matchup against the Vikings and will be in the mix as a high-end WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is off the injury report for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got in a pair of limited practices after leaving in Week 8 against the Panthers with a rib injury that required a trip to the hospital. The 6-foot-4 wideout is a WR1 for the upcoming battle against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson appears to just be being managed at this point as Matt LaFleur said there are no concerns on him playing in Week 7. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Watson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Jordyn Tyson, in his second NFL game, took over for at least one week as the team’s clear WR1, drawing 13 targets and finishing with 80 yards on 11 grabs. Olave, who did not record a reception until late in the third quarter, saw nothing downfield as Tyler Shough was under constant duress against a Carolina defense that entered the week with one of the lowest QB pressure rates in the NFL. Olave entered Week 10 with a 27 percent target share and a 47 percent air yards share. Tyson’s emergence could be a major issue for Olave if this sort of usage continues in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 7-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: It was business as usual for Olave, who has seen at least 10 targets in 6-of-8 games this year. He earned an astounding 38 percent target share today, and his 229 air yards are the second-most of the week, pending the two remaining games. The return of No. 8 overall pick Jorydn Tyson had no impact on his role, though Tyson was limited to 16 routes in his NFL debut. Tyson should see more work next week, but that will primarily come at the expense of Devaughn Vele. Olave will remain in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Panthers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 6-of-10 targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was once again a shorter-yardage target with a long gain of just 14 yards in the contest. Tyler Shough missed the 26-year-old on what would have been a walk-in touchdown from deep on a disappointing day for the top target in the Saints’ passing attack, at least based on expectations. He’ll remain one of the top fantasy receiving options in his next game, but that won’t come for two weeks as the Saints get a bye before facing the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave finished as the Saints’ leading receiver after coming into the weekend questionable with an illness. He was able to salvage his fantasy day with an 18-yard score at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Despite a season-low 43 yards receiving, Olave is still averaging just under 100 yards receiving per game this season. There is no question he belongs in the fantasy WR1 ranks heading into a Week 7 showdown against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Unless we get word that it’s an exceptionally rough illness, we’d expect no worse than a questionable listing on Friday despite the two missed practices. Olave should remain a smash WR1 against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: We expect Olave to be fine for the Saints’ Week 6 game against the Giants. There is currently no cause for concern, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Olave experienced blood clots in his lung last season, and spent much of the offseason recovering. We are not doctors and cannot opine on the matter. For now, expect him to play, but keep an eye out for his hopeful return to practice tomorrow or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was averaging over 120 yards per game before today’s contest. The Saints’ extreme play volume and tilt to toward passing the ball turned his great role into elite fantasy production. That finally came to a halt with Brian Flore’s defense shutting down Tyler Shough. The second-year passer completed just 16 throws for 96 yards. Shough and the entire passing attack should improve drastically versus the Giants next week. Fantasy managers can keep treating Olave as a WR1 despite this speed bump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell is the de factor WR1 for the Colts with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen dealt at the trade deadline. He led all receivers in snaps while scoring the team’s sole receiving touchdown in the red zone towards the end of the second quarter. The Colts passing game won’t generate many scoring opportunities with a depleted receiving corps and Daniel Jones’ constant struggles. However, Treadwell is the best bet to roster for fantasy purposes. He is a fantasy WR4 for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 2-of-8 targets for 34 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell was third on the team in targets, but he’s seeing most of his work on deep passes down the field, which Daniel Jones has had a hard time connecting on. Treadwell did play only three fewer snaps than Josh Downs and ran 39 routes on 47 dropbacks. We should note that Keenan Allen (groin) was not playing a full snap share in his first week back from injury, so Treadwell could see his role slip a bit next week. Even so, he’s a downfield threat on a team that has struggled to pass the ball, which makes it hard to roster him outside of the deepest formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell has taken over Alec Pierce’s role with the latter now on IR. Though he isn’t as productive as Pierce, Treadwell is still capable of moving the chains every now and then. He somehow led the Colts in targets this week, which may ultimately be a sign of the dysfunction in their passing game. Even after the solid performance, fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to play Treadwell in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts waived/released DE Genard Avery, CB Chris Lammons, WR D.J. Montgomery, TE Eric Tomlinson, WR Laquon Treadwell, CB Micah Abraham, LB Austin Ajiake, LB Liam Anderson, QB Jason Bean, DE Levi Bell, S Marce Dabo, RB Demetric Felton, OG Arlington Hambright, RB Evan Hull, DT Eric Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, DE Titus Leo, TE Jordan Murray, C Mike Panasiuk, RB Zavier Scott, CB Jaylin Simpson, CB Ameer Speed, S Michael Tutsie, OT Jake Witt, LB Craig Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell caught 10-of-11 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown this preseason. The former first-round pick played a handful of snaps on offense for the Ravens last season but hasn’t done anything of note since 2021, when he went for 33-434-1 with the Jaguars. At 29 years old, Treadwell could still garner some interest as a practice squad body, but he’s unlikely to stick on a 53-man roster this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts signed WR Laquon Treadwell, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Indy waived WR Xavier White in a corresponding move. Treadwell bounced between the Ravens’ practice squad and active roster throughout the 2023 season. He appeared in five games and caught one pass for 16 yards. The former first-round pick will be a depth option for the Colts if he makes their 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens signed WR Laquon Treadwell to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell had been on Baltimore’s practice squad for much of the season, catching just one pass for 16 yards in five games. He was released on Monday to make room for Dalvin Cook. Now, just two days later, the Ravens have added Treadwell back to the practice squad and released Tarik Black to make room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens waived WR Laquon Treadwell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell caught just one pass for 16 yards in five games with the Ravens this season. The former first-round pick has struggled to find a home in the league since being drafted by the Vikings in 2016 and will likely be playing for his fifth team in as many seasons if he catches on elsewhere in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens signed WR Laquon Treadwell, formerly of the Seahawks, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: The Ravens continue to bolster their wide receiver corps heading into this season, but Treadwell is little more than added depth on a roster that boasts Odell Beckham Jr., Rashod Bateman, Laquon Treadwell, and Nelson Agholor. After being released by the Jaguars last August, Treadwell caught on with the Seahawks last December, appearing in six games while catching six passes for 42 yards. He’ll compete with Devin Duvernay, James Proche, and a slew of players hoping to crack the 53-man roster at the conclusion of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: 49ers hosted free agent WR Chris Conley for a visit.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: The team also brought in Laquon Treadwell for a visit. Conley re-signed with Texans last offseason. He was cut, re-signed, and cut again before the start of the season. He had a cup of coffee with the Chiefs and then closed out the year by bouncing between the Titans’ practice squad, free agency, and their active roster. Conley is nothing more than a depth option at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-2 targets for 3 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq is becoming buried on the Jets’ depth chart. He did run a route on 23 dropbacks in this one, compared to 28 for Mason Taylor, but Taylor played 23 more snaps, and Sadiq also has to compete with three receivers for targets. He can’t be trusted in fantasy leagues right now and should not be on redraft rosters unless there’s an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor played 52 of the team’s 70 snaps in this game, with Kenyon Sadiq only playing 29. Sadiq did run a route on 23 dropbacks compared to 28 for Taylor, but it’s clear that Taylor is the top tight end on the Jets. It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught a 22-yard pass in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq’s third quarter reception went down as one of just two targets for the rookie tight end. He was once again out-caught by Mason Taylor, though Taylor provided just 19 yards across his three grabs. Sadiq’s reception was an impressive, leaping catch against single coverage, but therein lies part of the problem: It’s taking spectacular acts for Sadiq to create fantasy value. He is sadly off the radar for the time being in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught his only target for six yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The first-round rookie was held to one catch for the second week in a row. He has four catches over his past four games. It wouldn’t be surprising for his role to expand as the season wears on, but there were no signs of that happening this week. He isn’t worth holding onto in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: BTJ split the WR3 duties with Josh Cameron once again. Cameron, however, racked up 67 yards and a touchdown on three grabs. https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz’s only grab of the game was Houston’s only score of the second half, a ball C.J. Stroud lofted over zone coverage in the end zone to find Schultz at the back of it. It was a low-end outcome for Schultz, who had his lowest target count of the season. He’ll remain a high-end TE2 play against the Colts in Week 11 on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz’s box score is a tad inflated by two throwaway targets. CJ Stroud aimed passes Schultz his way while pressured, in order to avoid intentional grounding penalties. Schultz did make a great toe-tapping catch along the right sideline on the Texans’ seventh drive, and later hauled in a 28-yard pass downfield against busted coverage. Schultz is a borderline TE1/2 against the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 5-of-6 targets for 45 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Nothing groundbreaking here, though this was more like reasonable low-end TE1 work than reasonable low-end TE2 work. Schultz heads into the Week 8 bye with 137 yards in six games against non-Bengals defenses this year and unless you’re in a TE-premium league likely does not need to be on the roster while on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz never left the Texans’ Week 6 game against Jacksonville, but he was spotted with a limp after taking a knee to the leg. It’s possible the injury was worse than initially expected. If he were to miss Week 7, Foster Moreau, who scored twice last week, would be the next man up. Given that Schultz was barely putting up TE2 numbers as the starter, our hopes for Moreau as a streaming option would not be high.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: If you’re thinking all Dalton Schultz lines have started to blur together, you’re not wrong. He’s had eight catches for 69 yards since his Week 2 explosion against the Bengals. There’s not much upside here, but at least he’s providing a safe TE2 floor for those of you who get five points per TE reception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-2 targets for nine yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Not the most inspiring entry of #RevengeGame lore. Schultz was outgained by Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan. He’s trending towards TE2 usage with Nico Collins back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz told the CBS booth before the game that he “hopes to not have stat lines” like he had in Week 2, an anecdote they related as he had just one catch in the fourth quarter. Sounds like news that fantasy managers wish they had heard yesterday. He didn’t have a catch in the first half and yielded a red zone touchdown to spoiler Foster Moreau. Schultz has low-end TE1 status in a classic #RevengeGame against the Cowboys in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor played 52 of the team’s 70 snaps in this game, with Kenyon Sadiq only playing 29. Sadiq did run a route on 23 dropbacks compared to 28 for Taylor, but it’s clear that Taylor is the top tight end on the Jets. It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: It’s likely a maintenance day for Taylor, who tallied three catches on five targets in Week 8. He has been running ahead of rookie Kenyon Sadiq in recent weeks, though his own fantasy has been hit or miss. Taylor has been held under 40 yards in three of his past four appearances. He erupted for 62 yards and two scores in the fourth. Barring a setback in practice, Taylor will be a low-end TE2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s five targets were third on the team behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, while fellow seam stretcher Kenyon Sadiq mustered only two looks. Taylor has become a weekly volume presence in an offense that attempts a lot of passes, but he has not established a particularly high floor while his spiked week odds remain practically nonexistent. He’s a TE2 by the letter of the law but not one we would be looking to start in Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor got off to a hot start on National Tight Ends Day by mossing Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr in the end zone. Not content with just one score, Taylor double-dipped with a leaping touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter. He also scored the two-point conversion after the play. Taylor is running well ahead of first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq right now and there’s no reason to expect anything different in Week 8 versus the Raiders. Taylor will be in the TE2 mix next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 7-of-9 targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington was unstoppable in the first half with three gains of 30 or more yards plus a short touchdown. He entered halftime with six grabs for 148 yards. The fact that he was on pace for nearly 300 yards and finished with “only” 152 is a slightly disappointing outcome, but there wasn’t much of a reason for the Jags to keep airing it out in the second half. The Titans weren’t putting up much of a fight on offense and the Jags leaned on their ground game, preventing Washington from having a truly insane day. Fantasy managers will have to live with their 28.2 PPR points. Washington is pushing for a WR1 ranking as he heads into a Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added a 10-yard rush. Extremely disappointing volume coming out of the Jaguars’ bye week, but no Jag commanded more than three targets in a contest where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 throws before taking a fourth quarter breather in a 42-7 blowout. Washington is going to be subject to this kind of risk when the deep-and-dangerous Jags take on more overmatched foes, including now for Week 9 as the Ravens come to town for Thursday Night Football with their No. 2 or 3 quarterback under center. You always fire up Washington as a WR2, but he’s probably not going to stuff the stat sheet on Thursday evening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 4-of-11 targets for 64 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: A lot of these incompletions were balls Washington got a hand on but couldn’t quite reel in as was breaking to the sideline. Washington displayed his speed and shiftiness on a 27-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter where he cut through both Texans linebackers for a big gain. He is a fantasy WR2 as the Jaguars enter their bye week. Washington is #onpace for a near-1,200 yard season with 14 touchdowns even after this dud.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for 7 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added three yards with one carry on the ground. After a hot start to the season, Washington was relatively quiet against the Bengals. The Jaguars receivers combined for just 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 23 targets and Washington saw three of those. His first reception came in the fourth quarter on a 40-yard catch-and-run that would have sealed the game, but was called back after replay showed he stepped out of bounds after seven yards. Game script and the Bengals’ tight end weaknesses played a factor in this game, with Brenton Strange the primary target on the day. Washington should still be the Jaguars’ No. 1 receiver and is a fantasy WR2 for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Trevor Lawrence, as always, targeted Washington heavily, as no other Jacksonville pass catcher saw more than eight targets on the day. Washington came within half a yard of a touchdown in the first half after scoring in Week 1 against the Browns. Clearly the team’s No. 1 wideout, Washington should have a rock-solid weekly floor with upside to spare, especially when the Jaguars have to operate a more pass-heavy offense. Washington will be a top-15 play next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington saw elite usage in the first half, making the first Jacksonville catch of the game and ending the Jaguars’ first drive with a diving 30-yard touchdown reception. He followed it up with a one-handed sideline catch on the second drive and tallied five receptions in the first half. His usage was that of a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver for the Jaguars’ fantasy-friendly offense. The game was out of hand in the second half, leading to no more receptions the rest of the day, but fantasy managers will be happy with Washington’s utilization and production as he adds to his elite box scores from the end of last season. Washington is a fantasy WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Jaguars are “unlikely” to extend Parker Washington before Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jags explored a deal similar to that of Michael Wilson, who just landed a three-year, $75 million extension. The two sides couldn’t agree to terms, and Washington will now start his contract year. It’s a highly risky move for a largely unheralded player who caught lightning in a bottle at the end of last year. Washington caught 29 passes for 507 yards and three touchdowns in his final five games, including one postseason appearance. If he repeats anything close to those numbers over a full season this year, Washington will make far more than Wilson as a free agent next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: One of the incomplete passes was one that hit Mitchell in the hands, and he had two feet in bounds, but he let go of the ball to readjust his grip and was unable to remain in bounds, wiping out a 15-yard gain. With Omar Cooper Jr. leaving this game with an ankle injury, Mitchell could have a more dependable role next week against the Chargers, which would put him on the FLEX radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell was expected to play, but now we have confirmation that he will. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also active, it’s unclear which Jets receiver will be most productive in a good matchup. That makes Mitchell a boom-or-bust FLEX option in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.
