https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The consecutive limited showings seems to indicate Moore is on track to return from a two-game absence, something we should get further fidelity on after Friday’s practice. There remains a possibility that Moore carries a questionable designation into the weekend if he is unable to upgrade to a full participant Friday, leaving fantasy managers hopeful yet uncertain as we near the weekend. Moore would return to a WR2 profile when the Bills take on the Ravens, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore missed the Bills’ past two games because of the recurring shoulder injury. He got in one limited practice in Week 6. The team listed him as questionable but ultimately held him out. A Week 7 bye could not have come at a better time, and he now appears likely to return for Buffalo’s upcoming date with the Ravens. In a likely shootout with Baltimore, Moore will be back in the WR2 mix once he gets the green light to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons, adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Making a spot start in place of Kenneth Walker III (groin), fifth-round rookie Johnson was electric from the opening whistle, routinely tacking on extra yardage by either dragging tacklers or simply juking them out of their cleats. Johnson almost never took a negative play, and was so, so slippery in the open field or with any steam whatsoever. He was the Chiefs’ No. 2 receiver with 6/70/2, and actually the most targeted with seven looks. It was the kind of all-around performance we knew was possible from Johnson’s pre-draft profile but that we just have not seen because of Walker’s dominance. With Walker truly questionable for Week 11 against the Cardinals until we hear otherwise, Johnson would be an RB1 if given another start against the lowly Birds. Even if Walker goes, Johnson’s FLEX standing is now on much firmer ground.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is out for Week 10’s game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Reid added “we’ll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow.” Not exactly a glowing endorsement for Walker playing, though we expect the injury report later today to at least read questionable. If Walker were unable to go, Emmett Johnson would probably find himself with a low-end RB1 workload against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had six rushes for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson, fresh off a big receiving day in Week 8 against the Broncos, didn’t see much involvement until the Chiefs were up multiple scores in the fourth quarter. He ran in his first NFL touchdown on a goal line carry after Ken Walker — who had three touchdowns on the day — was resting on the sideline. Johnson remains one of the game’s most important and upside backup running backs and should be rostered in every league in case Walker misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: He added one carry for 15 yards. Johnson racked up the bulk of his production on a 73-yard touchdown grab in the first half. The Broncos sent pressure and Patrick Mahomes perfectly lofted the ball to Johnson, who saw nothing but green grass ahead of him. The turf monster nearly took him down at the 10-yard line, but Johnson stayed upright enough and lost one final defender on his way into the end zone. He also picked up a 38-yard catch just before halftime to set up a last-second field goal. Johnson had more than two touches in just one of his previous three games headed into Week 8. Though he’s not going to challenge Kenneth Walker for RB1 duties anytime soon, this breakout performance should earn him a few more touches in Week 9. He will be have some value as a boom/bust FLEX play versus the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had three rushes for six yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: It was another Ken Walker explosion game (128 yards, two touchdowns on the ground) with Johnson serving as the breather back. Johnson should be rostered as a high-upside contingency option in case Walker misses any time in the coming weeks or months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson was not targeted in the passing game. His six carries were nothing to sneeze at on an afternoon where the Chiefs were limited to 49 total plays, but that was compared to 20 Kenneth Walker touches. Johnson will have some pop-up standalone value behind workhorse Walker, but he is primarily a contingency option heading into the meat of the fantasy campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: The Bills leaned on Cook heavily in this one, not showing much of a belief that the Jets were going to pile up many points on offense. It was a solid day overall for Cook, but he then ripped off a career-high 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter that not only sealed the win for the Bills but also made it a big fantasy day for Cook. The 27-year-old could have had an even bigger day, but he dropped what likely would have been a 15-yard touchdown catch. Cook should be a rock-solid RB1 next week against the Dolphins as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook struggled to 2.7 yards per carry through the first three quarters but made his mark felt in the final frame, adding his lone rushing score in the fourth quarter to bring his season total to eight. The yardage total also pushed him over 5,000 career rush yards, doing so in the same game as Josh Allen to become the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. Cook has now scored in seven straight games as he continues his bid for one of the top fantasy running backs in the league. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens, adding two receptions for 21 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook paced the Bills on the ground all afternoon, picking up one key first down after another in a game where the offense struggled a bit in the first half. On the Bills’ first possession of the second half, Cook rushed three times for 20 yards, capping the drive with a five-yard rushing touchdown to bring his season total to seven scores on the ground. He exited briefly in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but was able to return. Cook will be in the RB1 conversation next week despite a tough road matchup against the Vikings in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders, adding three receptions for 58 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook had a much-needed bounce-back game in Sunday’s win over the Raiders. A week after he fumbled twice in an overtime win over the Rams, Cook secured the football for all four quarters and broke off multiple explosive plays while handling 22 of the Bills’ 24 running back carries. His lone rushing touchdown came on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter, and came one play after Cook ripped off a 26-yard reception on a third-and-three to keep the chains moving. Concerns about ball security may follow Cook for the remainder of the season, but his role in the Bills’ offense continues to provide valuable production in both real and fantasy football. He will be locked in as an RB1 in Week 8 against the Ravens when the Bills return from their Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said James Cook needs to protect the ball or he’s going to get fewer carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: “At some point, there has to be consequences,” Brady said about his lead back, who has fumbled four times in five games this season, including twice on Monday night. Cook has played 67.3 percent of the team’s snaps, and this probably isn’t a threat to his lead back status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if he sat on the bench for a spell if he fumbled in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook’s elite rushing line was overshadowed by two fumbles, the second of which was a lost fumble on the team’s first possession of overtime, placing the Rams in position to complete the comeback and steal away the victory. A blocked field goal on what would have been the game-winning kick breathed new life into the Bills, who demonstrated confidence in their lead back by throwing him right back out there on the following possession to eventually win the game. The 26 touches go down as a season high for the veteran back, who found paint for the fourth consecutive game in the thrilling overtime win. Cook remains a top-tier RB1 for fantasy purposes ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders in Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: He added two catches for either yards. This game was never more than a one-score game, so it’s pretty shocking that Cook only had 14 touches. The Patriots did a good job containing him early in the game, apart from his touchdown run, but the Bills simply moved away from the running game too quickly. Cook was gaining huge chunk yards in the second half and should have been fed more carries during the game. With the Bills having their second straight mediocre offensive performance, you have to wonder if they will make it a point to lean on Cook more next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook was the only running back to get a carry on the day, and he ripped off over six yards per rush. He got the Bills down inside the two-yard line twice but watched as Josh Allen ran it into the end zone each time. On the third trip deep into the red zone, Cook rushed it in from four yards out. With Ty Johnson back, Cook did cede some passing game work; however, Cook also played 42 of the team’s 62 snaps, compared to just 15 snaps for Johnson. The lack of receiving may prevent Cook from being a top-five running back, but he’s a clear RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook jumped out to a scorching start on the ground, reaching the century mark in rushing before the half. Still, fantasy managers were left scratching their head as they watched Josh Allen account for three touchdowns from inside the five, two on the ground and one through the air. It wasn’t until a 22-yard carry that was down at the one late in the fourth quarter that the team rewarded Cook with a short-yardage touchdown, finally allowing fantasy managers their first taste of sweet touchdown copium from their first-round draft pick on the young season. Cook is likely to remain busy when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3, where he will remain a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Bills “want to get that running game recharged” in Week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Bills RB James Cook totaled 57 yards on just 13 rushing attempts last week, adding three catches for 12 yards. Per Fowler, the Bills plan to use him a lot more in primetime this evening. Cook can be treated as a locked-in RB1 in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment on Thursday Night Football. The Bills notably elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. from the practice squad, which could indicate that RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) will be inactive tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 35-13, Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Breaking Josh Downs into the Chiefs’ undermanned receiver corps, Mahomes ended up having his first five-score passing effort since Week 1 of the 2022 season. Heavens to Betsy. The 348 yards were also his fourth most since that MVP campaign for years ago. All this when the only addition was Josh Downs. Of course, it helped that Mahomes was facing a downtrodden, disinterested Falcons side, but it really did seem like the presence of another legitimate wideout was creating more space for everybody. That even included Rashee Rice, who caught a legitimate down-field bomb, and Andrew Armstrong, who housed a late 43-yard score where Mahomes just kind of chucked it up. Two of Mahomes’ touchdowns went to spot-starting running back Emmett Johnson, who was electric in the open field. This had the feel of a sort of deliverance for the Kansas City side, and it should continue in Week 11 against the Cardinals. The schedule stiffens after that, if not really the opposing defenses. Mahomes is back to every-week QB1 status, and should frequently be a high-end option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Patrick Mahomes suffered a “very small sprain of his UCL” and a muscle strain in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes’ right arm was clobbered by a Jets defender while attempting to throw a pass late in the first half of Week 9. It looked like a serious issue at first, but he managed to finish the game and didn’t even miss any practice time this week. Per Schefter, the Chiefs consulted with physicians from the Rangers and Royals, who are among the world’s best doctors when it comes to shoulder and elbow injuries. Both doctors cleared him to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This comes directly from Andy Reid, though we’ll have to wait until the team’s injury report officially drops to be sure it’s actually a full session. Either way, Mahomes is playing on Sunday despite suffering an ugly elbow injury in Week 9. He told reporters it’s simply a matter of pain management for now. The Chiefs may opt to lean on their ground game against the Falcons, but even that won’t knock Mahomes out of the QB1 mix after the addition of Josh Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is considered “day-to-day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This news comes less than 24 hours after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that an MRI “did not reveal a major injury” to Mahomes, who was able to finish out the game in Sunday’s win over the Jets. Reid said Mahomes is dealing with some soreness that he will have to rehab a bit, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing any time. Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets and will be on the QB1 radar next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patrick Mahomes’ (elbow) MRI “did not reveal a major injury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Rapoport adds that Mahomes’ “elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling.” Without getting too deep into the weeds, there are a few things to note. First off, Rapoport sometimes reports injury news optimistically. It would have been nice to see him actually report a “minor” injury, rather than not “major.” Secondly, “strain” typically refers to muscles and tendons, while “sprain” is often used for ligaments. Using both is a tad confusing. That said, Rapoport’s follow-up statement suggests Mahomes may have a chance to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Updates will be provided as soon as news breaks. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-41 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding two rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was pulled with a few minutes to go in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs up multiple scores and the Jets not all that interested in staging a comeback. Mahomes overcame an injury to his right forearm in this one. He sustained the injury on a hard hit from a blitzing New York defender who bent Mahomes’ arm back awkwardly. After getting some treatment on the sideline, Mahomes re-entered the game and seemed fine, though he was seen grimacing and shaking his arm at times. This marked Mahomes’ sixth multi-touchdown game of the season. He should remain in starting lineups as a top-12 option in Week 10 against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 28-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes posted a strong box score for fantasy managers and took care of the football with zero turnovers. He also took just two sacks, but the second was one that will haunt Chiefs fans for a while. After marching the offense down to the goal line under the two-minute warning, the Chiefs found themselves on fourth-and-goal. They initially got the score via a strike to Rashee Rice, but the play was blown dead via a false start. The Broncos’ pass-rush got to him on the second try, taking Mahomes down for a game-ending sack. On the whole, it was another dink-and-dunk game plan from Mahomes, who failed to get the deep ball going once again. Luckily for him, Emmett Johnson averaged 25.6 yards per catch and turned a short toss into a 73-yard touchdown in the first half. The Chiefs get a bounce-back spot against the Jets next week in a game where Mahomes will be just inside the QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 19-of-33 passes for 165 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ 20-3, Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: The three points tied the fewest scored in a start in Mahomes’ career as the Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season. Mahomes faced consistent pressure and a shrinking pocket as the Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. Mahomes also had an ill-advised turnover as he tried to escape pressure, over-throwing his intended receiver on the run. The Chiefs fall to 5-1 with the defeat, leaving only the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team through seven weeks. Mahomes gets little time to lick his wounds with the division rival Broncos on the horizon in Week 8, where he’ll be a low end QB1 in another difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-30 attempts for 272 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding five rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes had multiple touchdown tosses in every game this season headed into Week 6. Kansas City’s offense didn’t have to do much against a sleepy Chargers offense that could barely move the ball once again on Sunday. The Chiefs leaned on Ken Walker, who went for 128 yards and two touchdowns on the day. With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton out, Mahomes relied heavily on Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. Until Rice is back and fully healthy, Mahomes will be more of a top-15 option. He gets the Seahawks in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 30-27, Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was under duress throughout this one. He took multiple hits and was sacked twice, but managed to come up with just enough plays to pull off the road win against a spry Raiders team. Mahomes threw his first touchdown of the day in the first quarter, finding Tyquan Thornton for a two-yard score, then connected with Thornton again in the fourth quarter for an eight-yard touchdown near the back of the end zone. Mahomes’ longest play of the game also went to Thornton, when the speedster broke free down the left sideline to make a 55-yard catch. Unfortunately, Thornton exited the game with a gruesome ankle injury after the play, but he did set up Kenneth Walker for a two-yard touchdown run on the ensuing play. Mahomes and the Chiefs are now 4-0 as they enter their Week 5 bye week. They’ll play host to the Chargers, who are 0-4 when they return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He added three catches for 33 yards on five targets as part of a robust screen game. Judkins has continued to see reasonable usage on the ground for a team that runs plenty, but he has yet to crack 100 yards in a game and this was just his fourth touchdown of the season. He actually was outsnapped by Dylan Sampson today, though it’s clear that happened because the Browns fell behind 17-0 before making their comeback. He’ll head into the bye as a borderline RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 11 times for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins added two catches on just two targets for 24 yards. The Browns’ offense could get nothing going against the Steelers’ defense, and the Browns’ offensive line was pushed around all day. Judkins also had two carries from inside the five-yard line, including a carry from the one-yard line with 22 seconds left, but he couldn’t convert on either. The Browns should have a bit of an easier time moving the ball against the Saints next week, but if Judkins has a good day, that might be the chance to trade him away. Judkins actually played 11 fewer snaps than Dylan Sampson in this one with the Browns trailing all game, so that gives Judkins a low fantasy floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins had 17 rushes for 96 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins took full advantage of a Titans defense that has struggled to stop the run in recent weeks. He broke tackles on a couple of his longest runs and made decisive cuts in the open field on well-designed rushing attempts. It was Judkins’ second career 100-yard day and his second and third touchdowns of the season. Dylan Sampson, in his first action of the 2026 season, saw six carries for 45 yards and ran 19 routes to 13 routes for Judkins. As long as game script remains neutral or positive, Judkins should be a viable flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He should carry his usual load in a good matchup against the Titans. That will put Judkins in the mid-to-low RB2 range this week, even with Dylan Sampson getting a chance to come back off injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Earlier today, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ availability for Week 7 against the Titans. Today’s limited session puts him on track to play, though it would be nice to see him practice in full. If active, he would be a FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s “optimistic” Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Monken sounded like Judkins and Dylan Sampson will be active and ready to go against Tennessee. Judkins had been the locked-in lead back for Cleveland before his Week 5 ankle injury, seeing 71 percent of the team’s designed rushing attempts. The potential return of Sampson, a good pass catcher, could complicate things for Judkins’ involvement in the pass game going forward. Judkins will be a touchdown-dependent flex play against a Titans defense allowing the NFL’s ninth lowest rushing success rate in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins tested out his ankle in pregame warmups, with the team deciding afterward that he would not play in this AFC North battle with the Ravens. With backup Dylan Sampson still sidelined and Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve, the Browns will look to Jaleel McLaughlin and the recently signed Audric Estime to lead their backfield in Week 6. This is looking like a backfield to avoid for this week, but McLaughlin could have some value in deeper leagues. The Browns also ruled QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Igbinoghene, DT Mike Hall Jr., C Parker Brailsford, OG Teven Jenkins, and DT Mason Graham inactive for this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.headline: Cade Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards and an interception in the Jets’ 31-12, Week 10 loss to the Bills.

His ability to be able to come out and operate with the first group the way he did, I thought, was outstanding.” Given how Jets quarterbacking has gone over the past few years and Geno Smith’s age, Klubnik will likely find himself in a starting lineup at some point this season if he can stay healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the team is not concerned about Smith’s foot soreness, writing, “if this was a regular-season game, he’d be a go.” Smith has reportedly been pushing the ball downfield in practice. https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said there is an “open competition” between Bailey Zappe, Cade Klubnik, and Brady Cook for the team’s backup quarterback position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.analysis: Glenn added that Zappe took the second-team reps behind Geno Smith in practice on Wednesday. Zappe has the most NFL experience of the bunch, so that shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. It also doesn’t mean he will hold the QB2 job into Week 1. Since entering the NFL, Zappe ranks 78th out of 84 qualified quarterbacks in EPA per play (min. 150 plays). The good news for him is that Cook holds spot No. 84. As a fourth-round pick, Klubnik does have some potential, and his competition for the QB2 job is exceptionally weak. No matter who earns the backup gig, the hope for Jets fans will be that we never see them in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes the Jets’ decision to “slow-play” their pursuit of another veteran option is an indication they’re giving Cade Klubnik “the chance” to win the backup quarterback job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.analysis: (Deep sigh.) “The word ‘“aura”’ has been thrown around — including by running back Breece Hall — after a slo-mo video of Klubnik walking out to practice on Thursday,” Rosenblatt writes. Klubnik also gathered Jets rookies at the team hotel to run through plays in a weight room even though the receivers were running “three-yard routes” in Klubnik’s words. We suppose there’s a low bar for excitement on the Jets quarterback front. It’s plausible that Klubnik rebounds from a down final season at Clemson that claimed the draft stock of both himself and several of his teammates. We’d be surprised if he made a real push to play this year without injuries ahead of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.headline: Jets traded up with the Bengals to select Clemson QB Cade Klubnik with the No. 110 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/cade-klubnik/0.analysis: The Jets traded No. 128 and No. 140 to the Bengals for this pick and No. 199. Klubnik (6’2/207) was the No. 1 QB of the 2022 recruiting class per 247Sports’ composite rankings. The former Clemson Tiger peaked in 2024, throwing for 3,642-36-6 while leading his team to a 10-4 record, but he regressed to a 2,946-16-6 line in 2025, completing 65.2 percent of his passes. He’s an undersized but mobile QB who totaled 878 rushing yards and 17 rush touchdowns in his career, but managed just 94 rushing yards last season. Some of that can be attributed to the decline in designed runs he saw from 2024 to 2025. When Klubnik was at his best, he operated in an offense that ran RPOs at a 20.8 percent clip, per TruMedia, so the dip to a 13.8 percent RPO rate last season may explain some of his struggles. His career 5.7 ADOT on completed passes, along with his underwhelming big-time throw rate of 3.8 percent, per PFF, offers a behind-the-scenes look at Klubnik’s career adjusted completion percentage of 74.9 percent, but the numbers fall off drastically when he pushes the ball into the short and intermediate parts of the field. His traits and former five-star pedigree will warrant a further look, but Klubnik seems destined for a backup QB role at the next level. However, he’ll get the chance to compete against Geno Smith for the Jets’ starting job this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Bills’ 31-12, Week 10 win over the Jets, adding two rushing touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The Bills leaned heavily on James Cook in this one, with Allen dropping back to pass just 21 times. When the Bills did pass, they took a few big shots down the field, which resulted in a long touchdown pass to D.J. Moore, but also a long interception on third down in what was ultimately an “arm punt.” Of Allen’s two rushing touchdowns, only one of them was on a tush push. The Bills quarterback has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in four straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a quarterback in NFL history, and he has 324 total touchdowns in his career, which is now the most by any player in their first 10 seasons in NFL history. He will look for another big fantasy day in Week 11 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 21-of-31 passes for 234 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 23-6, Week 9 win over the Vikings, adding 15 yards on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The career accolades continued to pile on for Allen, who became the fifth quarterback in NFL history to rush for 5,000 yards in his career with 15 yards on the ground against the Vikings. Furthermore, in one of the more wild statistics you will ever see, Allen and running back James Cook each surpassed 5,000 career rush yards on the same drive, becoming the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. The Bills surge to 7-1 with the win and extend their lead on in the AFC East following the loss by the Patriots on Sunday. Allen and company earned every bit of it in this one, fighting through consistent pressure from the aggressive and tenacious Minnesota defense, the latter of whom kept the game within reason deep into the fourth quarter. Allen remains the top overall fantasy quarterback ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 21-of-34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Bills’ 36-10, Week 8 win over the Ravens, adding seven carries for 30 additional yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen set the Bills’ franchise record for passing touchdowns in the fourth quarter when he completed an 11-yard pass to DJ Moore to put the Bills up 29-10. He added to his total a few minutes later when he connected with Dalton Kincaid down the right sideline for a 23-yard score, as the Bills trounced the hapless Ravens, who were down to their third QB midway through the second quarter. Allen and the Bills’ offense struggled at times, but eventually made the most of multiple possessions, thanks in part to three Ravens turnovers and multiple short drives. Allen also found the end zone on the ground in this one, and came up short of a second rushing score in the second quarter when he was tackled for a three-yard loss while trying to break a run to the outside. Allen and the Bills draw a tough road matchup against the Vikings in Week 9, but Allen is a must-start QB regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 255 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 33-30, Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The Raiders did their part to keep Allen in the pocket in this one. He managed just one rushing yard on five carries, but did plenty of damage through the air to put the Bills in position to pull out their fifth win of the season. Allen threw his first touchdown of the day to Khalil Shakir in the second quarter on a nine-yard screen pass, and flipped an impressive shovel pass to Keon Coleman in the third quarter for his second touchdown pass of the day. Allen and the Bills have scored 30-plus points in four of their first six games this season, with Allen totaling four touchdowns in his last two games. The Bills punted just twice in this one, and Allen led his team on three straight scoring drives to start the game. While there’s plenty to figure out on defense, Allen and the offense are clicking on all cylinders even with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. The Bills now head into their Week 7 bye week and will return in Week 8 to play host to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 12-of-19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 37-34, Week 5 win over the Rams, adding 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The two teams mustered only 20 combined points in the first half as they felt each other out. There were only two punts after the break between the two sides, who combined for seven touchdowns on nine combined possessions including five straight touchdowns in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime. Allen and the Bills took the ball first in the extra frame and quickly found themselves deep in enemy territory following a 57-yard, catch-and-run pass to Khalil Shakir. A James Cook fumble on the next play appeared to shatter Allen’s chances of earning his first career win in overtime, but a blocked 48-yard field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis gave the ball back to the Bills with a chance to win. Two Josh Allen scrambles set up a game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. Allen ended with the second most yards on the ground of his career as the Bills moved to 4-1 with the wild win. Allen remains the top overall quarterback in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 253 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 29-26 Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen did score a rushing touchdown, but he had just four rushing yards on five carries, making this the second straight game that he was contained as a rusher. Every time Allen rolled out, the Patriots had a defender in the lane, and Allen wasn’t able to make his usual big plays with his arm. Once D.J. Moore left the game with a shoulder injury, it felt like none of the Bills’ receivers were able to create space with their defenders, much like we saw for all of 2025. Allen’s interception was an egregious decision on the final drive of the game, where he made an impressive spin move to avoid a sack and then chucked an unnecessary Hail Mary into double coverage. You’re still starting Allen in fantasy leagues, but it’s a bit concerning that we’ve seen the Bills’ offense look scattered and out of sync for two straight games. It won’t get easier on Monday against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 16-of-26 passes for 204 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 24-16, Week 3 win over the Chargers, adding 22 yards rushing and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen certainly wasn’t good in this one, but he wasn’t alone. The Bills turned the ball over five times, committed 10 penalties, and allowed four sacks and somehow won this game. His first interception was on a truly bad read over the middle of the field. The second was on a deep pass into coverage when Allen thought he had drawn an offside. The pass managed to hit the safety in the back and then land in his stomach when he rolled over after hitting the ground. Allen would also fumble on a sack later in the game. The Chargers did a good job of taking Allen’s scrambles away, and this entire Bills team was in disarray, so nobody was consistently open down the field. That being said, Allen’s two rushing touchdowns give him 85 for his career, which means he’s now tied with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. The Bills and Allen will look to get things straightened out against the Patriots next week, and Allen will clearly be in your lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Bills’ 41-31, Week 2 win over the Lions, adding 69 yard and two touchdowns on 14 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Was it ever a doubt that Super Josh would make an appearance in the franchise’s first game in their new stadium? To the utter dismay of James Cook fantasy managers, Allen accounted for three touchdowns from inside the five against the Lions, two with his legs and one with his arm, extending his NFL-record for games with multiple rushing touchdowns and multiple passing touchdowns to 10 in the process. The unquestioned overall QB1 in fantasy circles continues to prove the doubters wrong as the Bills surge to 2-0 atop the AFC ahead of a home meeting with the Chargers in Week 3. Allen remains a top-tier fantasy asset until pigs fly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 36-31, Week 1 win over the Texans, adding 23 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Some had suggested you might want to bench Josh Allen against the Texans defense this week. Instead, Allen absolutely decimated last year’s top defense with a game-winning stick throw to the post for Josh Palmer to take a late five-point lead. He did his typical witchcraft out of structure, the best of which was probably a floater in his own end zone with a man in his face that landed directly on Dalton Kincaid’s hands. He also owned the ground game in the red zone. It was the first Bills win in Houston since the JP Losman Era. Allen, as always, will be in the QB1 overall discussion against the Lions in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia said he would not be surprised if DJ Moore is “on the field constantly and for [Josh] Allen to default to looking his way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Buscaglia called Moore, who was acquired from the Bears this spring, the “crown jewel of the offseason” for the Bills front office. “Moore’s contributions to the offense within training camp were immediate and obvious,” Buscaglia said. “Allen routinely pushed the ball downfield to Moore, making a concerted effort all summer to build on-field chemistry with the Bills’ new No. 1 receiver. ... The days of ‘everybody eats’ seem to be in the rearview mirror.” It’s a bullish report — one that could mean Moore is among the best values in redraft leagues this season even after being among the NFL’s most inefficient wideouts in 2025. Moore should be in all 12-team lineups for Week 1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 5-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
Matthew Golden caught 10-of-10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden appeared to be on pace for a historic performance after the first quarter. The second-year receiver hauled in two receptions of 40-plus yards, along with a five-yard touchdown, and ended the quarter with a 6-126-1 receiving line on six targets. Golden obviously didn’t sustain that pace for the remaining three quarters, but fantasy managers won’t be mad with the one highly productive quarter he offered up. Golden continues to dazzle in his second season and has now gone for 100-plus yards in four different games this season. He’s both a target hog and an air-yards king, which makes for a deadly combination as far as fantasy football is concerned. He will be a fringe WR1/WR2 next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue his recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden was estimated as a DNP for two walkthroughs this week before being limited in the Packers’ only real session. The short turnaround to Thursday Night Football likely forced the Packers to take an extra cautious approach with him in practice. While he almost certainly isn’t at 100 percent, Golden looks like a good bet to play in a sneaky shootout with the Panthers tonight. He will be on the WR1/2 border if he gets the green light.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: The Packers held two walkthrough practices to start the week. Golden was estimated as a DNP for both. He was limited in the team’s final practice before being hit with the questionable tag. Fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-time decision for tomorrow’s game. Savion Williams has been operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver over the past two weeks. He would presumably be the next man up if Golden can’t go, though Williams would still be a high-risk FLEX bet for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team is “still working through it” when asked if WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) will play Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky relayed LaFleur’s noncommittal response to questions on Golden’s status. LaFleur said the team hopes Golden plays, but the 23-year-old has been an estimated DNP for the first two practices of the week due to shoulder and foot injuries. With the Packers playing on a short week against the Panthers, Golden’s status will likely rely on the final practice report before a Week 8 Thursday showdown against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: This does not have us optimistic that Golden will play on Thursday night. If he’s sidelined, Savion Williams will be a candidate for more work on offense and perhaps a worthwhile FLEX streamer, while Tucker Kraft will likely ascend to the No. 2 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers listed Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) as a DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden has been dealing with the shoulder injury since last week, but the foot injury is a new one. While this is only an estimated injury report, the DNP is still mildly concerning for Golden, with the Packers playing on a short week. His status will be one to monitor in the coming days, but hopefully this is a minor issue. Golden played the entirety of the game in Week 7’s loss to the Lions and didn’t appear to be hampered by any nagging issues. We’ll see if he get upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden’s 12 targets led all Packers receivers, but the speedster was unable to convert them into anything meaningful. Of the 12 targets Golden saw, four came on passes of 20-plus air yards. He managed to secure one of those passes for a 22-yard gain, but that was all he could manage in what ended up being a relatively low-scoring game despite the two teams combining for over 700 offensive yards. The 39 yards Golden posted on Sunday were good for his second-lowest total of the season, but he’s an air-yards king who is seeing the kind of volume we expect of a true WR1. He’s primed for a bounce-back in next week’s game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 9-of-13 targets for 74 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: “The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 3-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: It was a game to forget for Jefferson and the Vikings, who gained only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession. Jefferson also failed to secure what was initially ruled on incomplete pass on a screen attempt in the first half, later overturned to a Carson Wentz fumble after being ruled a backwards pass. Furthering the pain for Jefferson’s fantasy managers is the fact that 19 of his yards came on the team’s final possession with Max Brosmer under center, leaving arguably the most talented wide receiver in the league completely bereft of a viable option at quarterback considering Wentz’s struggles. His fantasy contingency are best off saying their prayers that the team decides to address the quarterback position in the next 17 hours ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. Jefferson would be a middling WR2 if the position remains unchanged ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 5-of-9 targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson once again led the Minnesota offense in targets but it was Jordan Addison and TJ Hockenson who had bigger statistical days in what was Kyler Murray’s best game as a Viking. Jefferson secured a short touchdown in the first half and was mostly invisible in the second half. He was seen shouting at no one in particular on the Minnesota sideline late in the fourth quarter. With just two games of more than 60 receiving yards, Jefferson is somewhat touchdown-reliant in the low-volume, run-first Vikings offense. He’ll face a porous Bills secondary in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson led the Vikings in targets and yards on a low-volume day for the passing game. He hit a career milestone, crossing 600 career catches with a four-catch day. The Vikings’ offense continues to post low-efficiency outings as the defense lifts the team to an undefeated record. Jefferson is still the No. 1 wide receiver but banks on high volume usage and touchdowns to be a fantasy WR1. A lack of touchdown opportunities and red zone usage will be an issue in the Vikings offense, but Jefferson has a soft matchup against the Lions for Week 8. He should be back in the WR1 rankings next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is just a maintenance day for the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver. Jefferson has an excellent matchup this week against the struggling Colts’ defense. The unit will likely be without No. 1 CB Sauce Gardner (calf), further enhancing Jefferson’s WR1 outlook for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson didn’t miss a beat after returning from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. He made several spectacular grabs in this game, the most amazing of which was a toe-tapping catch in the back of the end zone with three defenders covering him. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson is simply one of the best receivers in the league. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when the Vikings face the Colts after their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 11 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was out-rushed by Jordan Mason in this one, but he still managed to get 12 touches and found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. It was the first touchdown for Jones since Week 5, which was also the last time he rushed for more than 26 yards in a game. His lone target in the passing game resulted in an eight-yard gain, but this was an otherwise forgettable performance for Jones were it not for the touchdown to get fantasy managers over the hump. Jones has not been the reliable pass-catcher fantasy managers have come to count on over the years and shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a fringe RB2/RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed five times for 16 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ six opportunities were three behind backfield-mate Jordan Mason, despite the former getting the start on paper. The Vikings were unable to move the football consistently with Carson Wentz under center, gaining just 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, both of which heavily influenced the veteran back’s opportunities and output. Jones is far from a usable fantasy asset while sharing the workload with Mason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones had five rushes for 22 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions, adding two catches for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jordan Mason led the Minnesota backfield with eight rushes (for 20 yards) while Jones remained the team’s preferred pass-catching option out of the backfield. Jones was battling a knee injury headed into the game and did not appear to be 100 percent against Detroit. He’ll be a deep league flex option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is active for Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was able to practice in full on Friday after battling the lingering knee issue all week. He could be somewhat limited against Detroit, creating a potentially bigger workload for Jordan Mason, who profiles as a flex option in 12-team leagues. Vikings declared Jakobe Thomas, Charles Demmings, Demond Claiborne, Caleb Tiernan, Elijah Williams, and Max Brosmer inactive against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones departed the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts after aggravating an existing knee issue. He was held out of practice Wednesday before retaking the practice field on consecutive days to end the week, ultimately deemed healthy enough to play against the division rival Lions in Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best off finding a suitable alternative considering Jones is struggling through a sprained MCL and the team got Jordan Mason back a week ago, although managers in a bind can safely expect him to be on the field come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was forced from the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts due to an aggravation of an existing knee injury. The fact he was able to return to the practice field in any capacity after missing Wednesday’s session is good news for his potential availability against the Lions. We would expect him to form a loose committee with Jordan Mason, if active Sunday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his level of participation Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones has reportedly been playing through a sprained MCL in one knee since Week 2. He seemingly aggravated it in Week 7 and left the game early in the fourth quarter. On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Jones is considered “day-to-day.” Jones could once again play through the issue this week against the Lions. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 26 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts, adding one reception for zero yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones got the start in the Vikings backfield, ripping off four straight carries for nine yards on Minnesota’s first possession. Outside of the opening possession, Jones took a backseat to Jordan Mason, seeing a mix of passing-down snaps and short-yardage carries. He caught his only target in the red zone but had it punched out for a fumble out of bounds. Jones left in the fourth quarter with a knee injury; he had been playing through an MCL injury and may have aggravated the issue. Prior to the injury, Jones was getting out-snapped by Mason and ends with 15 snaps to Mason’s 38, while getting six fewer touches. Jones is a low-end fantasy RB2 if healthy for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is questionable to return Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones suffered a knee injury after a fourth quarter run against the Colts. He has notably been playing through an MCL injury and may have re-aggravated it here. Jones struggled to walk and spent time in the medical tent. Jordan Mason is the team’s top running back while Jones is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 17-of-27 passes for 220 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 30-10, Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was under relentless pressure for most of this one. According to the early data from PFF, Love was pressured 19 times on his 35 dropbacks, which feels about right for a player who was sacked a season-high eight times. Love and the Packers went three-and-out on two of their offensive drives and also saw a promising drive late in the second quarter end after giving up back-to-back sacks after two long completions to Matthew Golden. Love and the Packers would eventually string together a 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive in the third quarter, with the lone touchdown coming on a 32-yard pass to rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, but that was as close as the Packers would come to mounting any sort of a comeback. Love and the Packers now head into their bye week and will return in Week 12 to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots, adding one carry for 13 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 27-of-45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 20-17, Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Even with Josh Jacobs back in the mix, the Packers still struggled to get the ground game going. As a result, Love aired it out early and often, throwing a ridiculous 10 passes for 20-plus yards, but only three were completed. Love’s first touchdown pass came on a third-and-nine when he connected with Tucker Kraft for a 14-yard score, and in the third quarter, a short pass to Jacobs was turned upfield for a 25-yard touchdown after Jacobs tight-roped along the sideline to find pay dirt. Love nearly connected with Jacobs for another score late in the fourth quarter, but Jacobs was unable to complete the diving catch in the end zone for the go-ahead score. On the next play, Trey Smack had a 35-yard field goal blocked, which ultimately set the Lions up for the game-winning field goal on the ensuing drive. Love continues to play an aggressive style of football, airing it out to his speedsters in Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. He and the Packers now have a short turnaround to prepare for the Panthers in Week 8, where he will be on the QB1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s limited session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Love was “pretty beat up” after Sunday night, but Love doesn’t appear to be in any danger of missing the game. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jordan Love (back) was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love got checked out by the team’s chiropractor after the game and was listed as limited for yesterday’s practice. LaFleur told reporters they haven’t determined whether he will be limited for today’s session. Either way, he said yesterday that there is no chance Love misses Week 7, so the practice reports are a moot point. Love is a top-half QB1 for his date with Detroit this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Wednesday’s session was a walkthrough, so this is just an estimate from the team. We don’t believe it will be much of an issue for Love in Week 7. Barring a setback, Love will remain in the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Lions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 25-of-31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ 31-7, Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: With the Packers’ backs against the wall in a rivalry grudge match, Love had one of the best starts of his NFL life by simply cutting it loose. His 367 yards passing were the third most of his career, and accompanied by zero turnovers. He found each of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft for at least one 46-yard gain, including a 53-yard touchdown to Watson. That does not include an earlier 42-yard scoring strike to Watson. Each score had serious air underneath them. This really was Love airing it out, something less competent quarterbacks had been struggling to do vs. the Bears’ vulnerable defense. We have seen this Love and Packers movie before — a step forward not followed by another move in the right direction — but neither Packers fans nor fantasy managers could have asked for more this afternoon. Love will have a good shot at keeping the good vibes going vs. the Cowboys’ struggling defense in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Vikings’ 30-10, Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins didn’t exactly stuff the box score in this one, but his performance provided a noticeable upgrade for the Vikings’ passing game. Getting the start on a short week following his trade to the Vikings, Cousins struggled early on, but eventually found his footing on the road against a solid Packers defense. His first big play of the game came on a 38-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price, where he placed the ball perfectly between three defenders to find Price, who then turned the ball upfield for the long score. In the fourth quarter, Cousins would connect with Gavin Bartholomew for his second touchdown pass of the day, which all but put the game out of reach for the Packers. With a full week to get ready for Week 11’s game against the Niners, we would expect Cousins and the offense to look a little more in sync. Cousins profiles as a mid-QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said there is “always potential” for Kirk Cousins to remain in Minnesota beyond 2026, but acquiring him was about this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: It seems that the Vikings just love to move on from quarterbacks who successfully adapt to their system. It is fair to wonder how much Cousins, 38, has left in the tank, but the fact that Teasley actually said this out loud is a little perplexing. At worst, Cousins should be able to serve as a mentor for whichever young quarterback coach Kevin O’Connell decides he wants to whisper to in 2027. Cousins is currently playing on a one-year, $11.3 million contract and could likely be retained on a one- or two-year deal at a similar value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues.
