Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kirk Cousins is a “prime trade candidate” for the Vikings ahead of today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: This would, of course, have multiple fantasy impacts. Fernando Mendoza would take over as Las Vegas’ starting quarterback if Cousins were traded, and Kyler Murray would likely take a backseat to Cousins sooner rather than later in Minnesota. We unfortunately must recommend that you stay tuned for the next couple of hours. Click the ads, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-32 attempts for 216 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: The statuesque Cousins was under duress from start to finish, often falling back as he threw the ball into tight windows. That led to three picks, which should have been four or five picks if 49ers defenders had been a little more sure handed. As usual, Cousins targeted Brock Bowers relentlessly, once again connecting with the superstar tight end for a touchdown. He nearly threw a second touchdown to Bowers in the second half. Cousins also had a touchdown to Michael Mayer called back on an offensive pass interference penalty. This was only Cousins’ second game of the year with less than two TD passes. Cousins will be a superflex option in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in the Raiders’ 38-33, Week 8 win over the Jets, adding a rushing score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: With the Fernando Mendoza chatter increasing as the Raiders were mired in a four-game losing streak, Cousins responded with his fourth three-touchdown effort through the air, albeit his first since Week 3. Cousins has now provided multiple scores in 7-of-8 starts, and is up to 20 overall on the season. This, with Tre Tucker as his No. 1 receiver. Of course, Tucker is merely Cousins’ No. 1 wideout. Brock Bowers is his No. 1 pass catcher, and the elite tight end stacked up 7/92/2 in the new Meadowlands. Cousins seemed to look Bowers’ way on all the most critical downs, and he was richly rewarded. Fantasy managers also continue to be rewarded with Cousins in streamer spots, though that will be put to the test in Week 9 against the 49ers on the road. With only two teams on bye, we would be looking elsewhere in our quarterback spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said “Kirk Cousins is our quarterback,” when asked about the possibility of making a change at QB ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Rather than let any speculation linger, Kubiak was quick to shut down any idea of a switch at quarterback heading into Week 8’s game against the Jets. Kubiak said, “There is no controversy” at quarterback at this time, while also adding that “Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football” at some point this season. Kubiak said the team does not have a timeline for when Mendoza could eventually make a start, and said Cousins continues to play well despite the team’s recent struggles. Cousins will be firmly on the streaming radar this week against a Jets team that just allowed 28 points to the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said the team is “thinking about everything” in regards to the team’s QB situation after Week 7’s loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Kubiak was asked about the possibility of switching from Kirk Cousins to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and said the team is considering “everything” while also making it sound like their struggles were more of a team issue. Cousins struggled in the early part of Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but managed some late touchdowns in garbage time to save his stat line. If the Raiders are considering a switch, it’s possible we’ll learn their decision by Wednesday, when they begin preparing for their Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Dorian Williams is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Jets due to a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: Williams was hurt at the beginning of the fourth quarter and was taken to the blue medical tent. The Bills are up 24-12 with under eight minutes to go, so they may hold Williams out even if he is cleared to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Dorian Williams is out for the game after a neck injury after the opening kickoff of the AFC Division Round against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: He was able to walk off the field on his own but was then carted to the locker room. Williams tackled Marvin Mims on the opening kickoff, and their helmets collided. Williams’ arms went limp, and he was down on the turf for an extended period of time. With Terrell Bernard (ankle) inactive for this game, the Bills will be without key linebacker depth with Williams missing the rest of this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Bills ruled out LB Dorian Williams (knee) for Week 5 vs. Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: The Bills also ruled out CB Dorian Strong (neck), who was added to the injury report on Thursday. Williams suffered his knee injury in last week’s win over the Saints, putting the Bills down a key defender. Williams has totaled 18 tackles and one pass breakup in four starts for the Bills this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Dorian Williams (elbow) returned to the game against the Lions in Week 15.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: Williams had missed almost half game after suffering an elbow injury in the second quarter of the game; however, with Matt Milano suffering a groin injury in the fourth quarter, the Bills made sure to get Williams back on the field. There’s no indication yet how serious Milano’s groin injury is, but if it were to keep him out, Williams look step back into the starting lineup for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Dorian Williams is questionable to return to Week 15 against the Lions with an elbow injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: Williams has been bumped from the starting lineup with Matt Milano back from injury, but the Bills do use him on some early downs. His backup, Baylon Spector, immediately allowed a touchdown on the next play, so that could be an issue if Williams can’t get back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.headline: Bills selected Tulane LB Dorian Williams with the No. 91 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dorian-wil.analysis: Williams (6’1/228) was a nondescript, low three-star prospect who worked his way up to become a Tulane program legend and three-time All-AAC honoree. After finishing fourth nationally in FBS with 16.0 TFL in 2020, he racked up 132 tackles, 5.0 sacks, seven PBU and two interceptions for the Green Wave last year. His career on a high note, recording 17 tackles and winning the MVP in Tulane’s dramatic Cotton Bowl victory over USC. The team captain verified his wheels at the Combine with a sensational 4.49s 40-yard dash (98th%) and 1.52 10-yard split to go with an 8.76 RAS. While he likely doesn’t have the requisite bulk and take-on skills to consistently play in the box at the NFL level, Williams received PFF coverage grades of 87.0 and 90.2 which are elite scores that should translate well to the NFL. A verified athlete who has the chops to stay with the majority of running backs and tight ends in space, Williams will get a chance to help replace the loss of ex-Bills LB Tremaine Edmunds to free agency this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon caught his only target for six yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coming off a six-target game in Week 9, Raridon’s role all but evaporated today. He could pop up for another TE2 week down the line, but fantasy managers don’t need to hold him through the Pats’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Henry could ultimately get in a limited session later in the day, but this certainly looks like a DNP. The veteran tight end injured his foot early in the Pats’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins and did not return. Rookie Eli Raridon will take his spot in the lineup if Henry is unable to play this week. Raridon is averaging an impressive 13.3 yards per catch while mixing in behind Henry this year. He would immediately be in the TE2 mix if Henry is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon caught 1-of-4 targets for five yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots’ rookie tight end got involved early, chipping in a five -yard catch on the team’s first drive. He earned a target at the Dolphins’ five-yard line on the next play, but the pass was thrown inaccurately by a scrambling Drake Maye. Hunter Henry suffered a foot injury in the first half, which allowed Raridon to run as the Patriots’ top tight end. Although he earned a few more targets as the game progressed, unfortunately, Raridon’s lone box score contribution thereafter was a false start on the Patriots’ eighth drive. Despite Raridon’s quiet Week 8 outing, he will warrant streaming TE1 treatment next week against the Packers if Henry is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon caught 5-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon, who was out last week, was very much involved in the revived New England passing attack. Hunter Henry, meanwhile, had three grabs for 44 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots have used two tight end sets at a high rate when Raridon is healthy. Unless Henry misses time, Raridon should remain on waiver wires in most 12-team formats. He had been targeted on ten percent of his routes headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Bills with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon was questionable coming into this game with a thigh injury. He caught one of two targets for 12 yards before leaving this game with another injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon (thigh) is active for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon was questionable heading into the weekend, but he was able to get in three limited practice sessions this week, so he had been trending towards a return. He will back up Hunter Henry but could cut into Henry’s snaps enough to make Henry just a TE2 in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable for New England’s Week 4 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He got in three limited sessions this week. If active, Raridon would cut into Hunter Henry’s ceiling a bit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots’ rookie tight end has a chance to play this week. He is not yet involved enough to warrant TE1 treatment though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon is tentatively on track to play in Week 4 against the Bills, though he cannot be started as anything more than a touchdown-dependent TE2. His return could squeeze TE Hunter Henry’s access to targets though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry couldn’t get anything going while catching passes from Tommy DeVito for the better part of four quarters. DeVito averaged 3.4 yards per attempt on 24 throws in the blowout loss. Henry would tumble down the TE2 ranks if DeVito starts the Pats’ next game. With a bye week on tap, the hope will be that Drake Maye is available when New England takes on the Chargers in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry played through the foot issue last week despite a severely limited practice regimen throughout the week. He only caught three passes for 35 yards, though the Pats failed to get much going on offense while the game was competitive. He should rebound as a high-end TE2 for his Week 10 date with the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was playing through a foot injury in this one, but still ended up leading all Patriots tight ends in routes run (22). Prior to his injury-shortened outing in Week 8, Henry was riding a four-game streak of double-digit PPR performances, but he wasn’t able to get there this week. Hopefully, he didn’t suffer any setbacks this week and will be a viable streaming option in what could be a plus matchup next week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Henry had a “realistic” shot at suiting up this week after he managed to log a limited practice on Friday. Henry will profile as a high-end TE2 with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) out this week. In addition to Brown being out, the Patriots also declared RB TreVeyon Henderson, CB Charles Woods, OT Dametrious Crownover, and QB Behren Morton inactive for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Hunter Henry (foot) has a “realistic chance to play” in Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry only practiced once this week but still received a questionable designation on Friday. Eli Raridon would have taken his spot in the lineup, but it sounds like Henry will give it a go. He will be a high-end TE2 for his matchup with the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders declared WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, G Bryce Cabeldue and DT Thomas Booker IV inactive for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers will function as the only viable pass catchers for Fernando Mendoza in his first NFL start against a tough Seattle defense. The Raiders will be without two key safeties, making the matchup slightly better for Drew Lock and his pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Dont’e Thornton (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton’s injury woes continue. The young wide receiver spent much of the year on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He had a back injury last week, and now another back injury threatens his availability. Thornton does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he provides the team with a downfield element when active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders activated WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: It was his last possible day to be reinstated in his 21-day window. The fact that Klint Kubiak spent much of Thornton’s 21-day window talking about how he had to go show us something makes us think Thornton will probably just be a depth piece for the time being. The Raiders waived Jonah Laulu to make room for Thornton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) has “got to go show us something” in the final week of his 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: This is rough. Currently on injured reserve, Thornton began practicing in Week 5, activating his 21-day practice window. The young wide receiver told reporters that he was “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” Two weeks later, the team has not yet officially removed him from injured reserve. Per Kubiak, Thornton “had a good first week, had a good second week,” but he still has to go “out there to practice to show us that he’s ready.” He’s been practicing in full for two weeks. The fact that the wide receiver-needy Raiders have not yet activated him is not encouraging. Thornton does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders ruled out Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders activated Thornton’s 21-day practice window this week. Despite the young wide receiver saying he feels “ready to play,” the team has determined that he needs more time. With Jalen Nailor (concussion) also ruled out, Cody White (ankle) and Malik Benson will round out three-wide receiver sets behind Tre Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice and feels “ready to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been on injured reserve since late August, practicing in full for the first time on Wednesday. He told Raiders media that he is “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” With Jack Bech on injured reserve, there is room for the 23-year-old speedster to earn targets if he plays in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks declared RB Emanuel Wilson, QB Sam Darnold, CB Avery Smith, LG Quenton Nelson, LT Charles Cross, NT Deven Eastern, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson will be a healthy scratch once again now that Zach Charbonnet is healthy. Both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price profile as legit fantasy plays against a Raiders rush defense that has been the worst in the league by most metrics over the past six weeks. Look for the Seahawks to be particularly run heavy with Drew Lock banged up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald declined to say whether or not Zach Charbonnet (knee) would play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Macdonald said the team will continue to stick to their plan regarding Charbonnet’s return. The 25-year-old running back was activated from the PUP list last week, only to be ruled out before the weekend as the Seahawks were preparing to face the Chiefs. It’s worth noting that Charbonnet was a full participant in practice last week, so we would assume he will log another full week of practices this week. Should the Seahawks opt to sideline Charbonnet next week, Emanuel Wilson would again assume the role as lead back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 24 times for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding 15 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson handily outperformed former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker in the latter’s return to Seattle, spiking his fantasy production with a 21-yard touchdown scamper late in the fourth quarter with the Seahawks in ice mode. The outburst went down as the second time in Wilson’s career in which he hit the century mark in rushing, pleasing fantasy managers that were forced into his services in Week 7 through both byes and injuries. Wilson’s days as the lead back in Seattle are likely numbered with veteran Zach Charbonnet reportedly nearing a return from his 2025 torn ACL. That could occur as early as Week 8 when the Seahawks face the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 14 times for 52 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson is now down to just 3.4 yards per carry while filling in for numerous key injuries in the Seattle backfield, with the team clearly waiting with bated breath for the return of Zach Charbonnet. Charbonnet continues to inch closer to a return from injured reserve and appears likely to bring an end to the Wilson experiment, relegating the latter to bench fodder in fantasy circles in the process. That could come a early a Week 7 when the Seahawks host the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 20 times for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding two receptions for 11 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson again led the Seahawks in rushing sans Jadarian Price. He handled all but four of the team’s running back carries in this one and found the end zone on a two-yard plunge in the first quarter to tie the game at 7-7. Wilson coughed up a key fumble in the second quarter that gave the Niners the ball on Seattle’s 11-yard line. On the following play, the Seahawks would allow an 11-yard touchdown run to Christian McCaffrey to put the Niners back out in front. Assuming Zach Charbonnet (Achilles) is at least one more game away from returning, Wilson will be on the RB2 radar in Week 6 when the Seahawks take on the Broncos on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Holani was nursing a ribs injury on Wednesday and Thursday, but he is now listed with a knee injury as well. This is concerning. He clearly picked up a new injury during the practice week. Velus Jones is the current RB3. Jones is not viable as a FLEX starter if Holani sits, but Emanuel Wilson should take on an RB2-worthy workload regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown while adding three catches for 39 yards and a score in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson picked up his first score on a screen pass from San Darnold. His second touchdown came on an untouched stroll from eight yards out. Wilson doesn’t have anything close to elite burst, but he’s tough to bring down and has good-enough vision to take advantage of the holes he receives. He was clearly the bellcow as George Holani received just seven carries for 18 yards and only one catch in the contest. He’ll be a RB2 for Week 5 against the Broncos and as long as Zack Charbonnet/Jadarian Price remain out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: It’s possible that this is just a precautionary rest day, but those typically occur on Wednesdays. Price should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 4 against the Chargers. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald favorite, Zach Charbonnet (knee), returned as a limited participant. Backup RB Emanuel Wilson would likely get the start if Price and Charbonnet are both out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: Demario Douglas caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas finished third among the team’s wideouts in targets behind A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins. Brown left the game with a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter and did not return. His absence could open up more work for Douglas, but the Pats are on bye after their trip to Germany. Fantasy managers don’t need to hold Douglas through their week off.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 5-of-9 targets for 102 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The Patriots trailed throughout this one, which resulted in Drake Maye airing it out a season-high 38 times. The nine targets Douglas saw in this one also set a new season-high for the 25-year-old receiver, who reeled in two passes for 30-plus yards. Douglas has had a productive few games as of late, topping 60 receiving yards in four of his last five outings while also finding the end zone four times. He’ll be in the WR4/Flex range in Week 10 in what could be a high-scoring game against the Lions in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-3 targets for 76 yards and one touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The Patriots rolled with 12 personnel on their first play from scrimmage, so Douglas began his day on the sideline. Hunter Henry suffered an apparent foot injury early on, which likely afforded Douglas extra snaps via 11 personnel. He made his opportunities count. Douglas critically picked up a first down, powering through contact on 4th-and-2 on the Patriots’ eighth drive. He showed up again on the Patriots’ ninth drive, securing a play-action pass along the right sideline before juking a Dolphins safety and slipping a shoestring tackle attempt from JuJu Brents before racing into the end zone for a 48-yard touchdown. Douglas is a FLEX option against the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas followed up his best game of the season with another best game of the season, as well as the third most receiving yards of his career. His touchdown was a nine-yarder in the second quarter where the Jets’ defense simply afforded Drake Maye too much time. Things could not have been going better for “Pop” until his fourth quarter fumble at the end of a 39-yard catch-and-run. He was the victim of a classic “Peanut punch” from behind. Rather ominously, he was not targeted thereafter, though the Patriots were also in ball-control mode as they worked on draining the clock. That today’s effort came as A.J. Brown was returning from a five-week absence was promising, but the reality is that Douglas’ big box scores are likely to remain pop-up efforts rather predictable and/or weekly occurrences. He’s a shaky WR4 even with byes and injuries in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas had his first two touchdown grabs of the season as Drake Maye sliced and diced a lifeless Vegas defense from start to finish. Douglas was wide open standing in the end zone by himself for his first score, and broke out of a bunch formation inside the ten yard line for his second score. Douglas has run significant routes in the New England offense since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down to injury. When Brown returns — perhaps this week — Douglas will take on a smaller role in the Pats pass game. He should remain on waiver wires in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas was second on the team in targets behind only Mack Hollins, who saw nine looks from Drake Maye. Douglas got open and made a nice grab for his 38-yard gain — one of the only big plays for the struggling New England offense on Sunday. Though Douglas is playing a decent snap share, he should remain on waivers in most formats ahead of the Patriots’ Week 4 game against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett and Aaron Donald should have productive outings against a Cardinals offensive line that will be playing with a third-string left tackle and a backup center. Rookie QB Carson Beck will also be making his first career start. The Rams D/ST unit should put up points today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that he expects Garrett to play. This is unfortunate news for the Cardinals, who will be led by rookie Carson Beck in his first NFL start. Garrett played very well last week against the Commanders, but his preseason knee issue is apparently still bothering him. Hopefully, he can get healthy before the season’s end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett returned from injured reserve and played in Week 9 against the Commanders. A limited listing indicates the 30-year-old will be managing his practice reps as he ramps back up from the knee injury. Expect Garrett to play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams activated EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: No surprise here as Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Garrett is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. The Rams are 4-4, but will finally have Garrett and Aaron Donald on the same defensive line. That could cause problems for opposing offensive lines, starting with Washington’s on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was able to practice again Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has now been able to participate in back-to-back practices. The 30-year-old star defender appears to be ready to roll for Week 9 against the Commanders, but a decision on Garrett’s availability likely won’t be made until Friday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Garrett will be limited today. The team could still give him another couple of weeks to ramp up, but he at least has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. Garrett underwent surgery on his injured knee back in September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie sat out in Week 9 after injuring his back in Week 8. He missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury. Getting him back in the lineup provides the Rams’ secondary with a serious boost. He should play very well against a Cardinals wide receiver corps made up of backups. Myles Garrett (knee) and S Kam Curl (toe) are also active. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, S Maximus Pulley, LS Joe Cardona, OLB Darryl Peterson, OL Steve Avila, OL Keagen Trost and OLB Desjuan Johnson. Simpson will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: The Rams were optimistic about McDuffie practicing on Thursday and playing on Sunday. The former did not happen. It sounds like he has a chance to play this weekend, but his recovery appears to be going slightly slower than expected. Rams S Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable to play, though LG Steve Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Yesterday, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that the Rams were hopeful that McDuffie would play in Week 10 against the Cardinals. He is tentatively on track to do so with today’s return to practice. The Rams will potentially morph into a run-heavy team that relies on the defense to generate turnovers with their top-two wide receivers and top tight end sidelined. McDuffie can help them accomplish that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Trent McDuffie (back) will not practice on Wednesday, but the Rams are hopeful he will play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Groin and back injuries have plagued McDuffie for some time, but it sounds like he has a chance to face the division-rival Cardinals in Week 10. With the Rams’ receiving corps ailing, Los Angeles could turn into an old-school team, featuring a high-volume run game and a lockdown defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is inactive for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie was a DNP in practice all week but still managed to get a questionable designation entering the weekend. That said, the team’s decision doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the fact that he was unable to get on the field last week. Fortunately for the Rams, they faced a depleted Commanders receiving corps, and they will have both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for the first time together.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie played through a groin injury in Week 8 and seemingly picked up a new back injury during the game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie will be a DNP Wednesday, indicating the 26-year-old’s back issue is more than a minor flare-up. It’s possible he is getting the day off to rest the groin and back injuries, but Rams fans should keep an eye on his practice status the rest of the week. It’s safe to say McDuffie is truly questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said he did not have an official update on Trent McDuffie (back), adding, “he looks like he’s feeling OK.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury that he suffered in practice. He played through a questionable tag this week after three straight limited practices. Until we get an official update, McDuffie should probably be considered questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is active for the 49ers’ Week 10 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams is active despite only logging one limited practice this week. The future Hall of Famer will man his normal spot at bookend left tackle against the Cowboys. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw is also active, giving the Niners two of their key starters in this one. The 49ers have declared QB Kurtis Rourke, WR Mike Evans, OL Enrique Cruz Jr., LB Tatum Bethune, and WR Brandin Cooks inactive for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Trent Williams (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams injured his shoulder during Thursday’s practice. The team then held him out of Friday’s session before listing him as questionable. It was likely a precautionary move as Williams is good to go for today’s game, which is great news for a 49ers offense that is very banged up otherwise.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams evidently injured his shoulder during the 49ers’ practice on Thursday, as did LB Dre Greenlaw (knee). 49ers OT Vederian Lowe would be Williams’ replacement if he cannot play. 49ers starting perimeter CBs Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot), and slot DB Upton Stout (shoulder) are also questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that Williams was expected to resume practicing today. The fact that he is on track is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (bruised quad) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (neck) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams still has a chance to play in Week 4 against the Broncos, and he does not necessarily need to practice. The 49ers could choose to play it conservatively by sitting him until he is fully ready to go, though. We will see how the week unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Trent Williams (stinger) “should be good to go by Thursday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: The 49ers don’t play until Sunday, so we’re assuming Shanahan is referencing when we should first expect Williams to take the practice field this week. Williams suffered what was classified as a stinger in Week 3’s win over the Cardinals, but appears to have avoided any serious injury. Shanahan said the team plans to manage he and LB Dre Greenlaw (quad) throughout the week, and didn’t rule out either player playing in Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team is still gathering information on WR Mike Evans’ (ribs/oblique) injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, “it was unclear exactly what happened to Evans.” He got hit hard in the sternum on a catch over the middle, but remained in the game for a few plays before needing help from the training staff to get off the field. Shanahan said the team couldn’t tell if Evans broke a rib or injured his oblique, but he believes those questions will be answered tomorrow, indicating Evans will likely undergo imaging. He entered the game with a hip injury. Wagoner adds that LT Trent Williams (stinger) and LB Dre Greenlaw’s (quad) injuries “seemed less severe” than Evans’ injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: Trent Williams (stinger) is questionable to return Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams left in the third quarter, taking the cart to the 49ers locker room. The veteran left tackle was officially diagnosed with a stinger and is questionable to return. Vederian Lowe is in at left tackle with Williams out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers listed RB Christian McCaffrey, OT Trent Williams, LB Dre Greenlaw, and EDGE Nick Bosa as resting non-participants for Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: McCaffrey and Williams were listed as DNP simply for rest, while Bosa had a rest/knee designation and Greenlaw had a rest/Achilles designation. This is notable as the 49ers have several key veterans who have dealt with injuries throughout their career and practice reps will be managed for these players, especially coming off a Week 1 in Australia. McCaffrey reportedly dealt with cramps in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams; though he is not injured, his experiences with Achilles tendinitis will certainly lend to rest days throughout the season. We expect the 49ers to continue to rest veterans in practice throughout the season in an effort to remain healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: A.J. Brown left this game late with a hamstring injury but was struggling before getting banged up. With the WR1 doing nothing, Hollins stepped up with team-highs in catches and yards. He was, however, catching passes from Tommy DeVito, who took over for an injured Drake Maye. Hollins could see more work if Romeo Doubs remains on IR and Brown is out once again, but we won’t know much about either player until after the Pats’ upcoming bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Playing in his first game since Week 4, Hollins ran a season-high 34 routes and tied Eli Rairdon for the second-most targets among Patriots pass-catchers on the day. Hollins found the end zone on a 22-yard score in the third quarter with the Packers already well ahead, which gave Hollins his first touchdown of the season. Hollins has been targeted five or more times in three of his five games this season and could be a deep league streaming option next week against the Lions if A.J. Brown (knee) misses next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins is firmly in the questionable column with one practice left in Week 9. If active, he would be a boom-bust FLEX. The Patriots’ healthy wide receivers have played well in Hollins’ absence, though the team would probably like to get their field-stretcher back in action before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots place Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: The Patriots snuck Hollins onto the injured reserve list over the weekend. He will be eligible to return after sitting out for four games. The Patriots also placed FB Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: It sounds like Efton Chism, Kyle Williams, and Demario Douglas will all work more than usual next to Romeo Doubs in Week 5. Chism might be the most interesting FLEX play of the three after putting up 2/42/1 in relief of Hollins against the Patriots, though all of them have cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Normally a wind-sprinter and a blocking specialist, Hollins became shockingly important at work after A.J. Brown went on IR with an ankle injury. He currently leads the team in targets, tied with Romeo Doubs at 20 apiece. Hollins holds the lead outright in catches (15) and yards (209). His absence would free up downfield opportunities for Kyle Williams. Efton Chism and Demario Douglas would likely see an uptick in routes as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins injured his calf in Week 4 and was listed as questionable to return. He immediately went to the locker room and did not return. Hollins is unlikely to play in Week 5. Romeo Doubs finally broke out last week with six catches for 58 yards and two scores. He will be in line for another sizable role once Hollins is ruled out. Kyle Williams will take on a starting role, though he is only worth a stash in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.headline: Roy Lopez (toe/ankle) is active for Week 10 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.analysis: Lopez, the Cardinals’ starting nose tackle, will play through a questionable designation after suffering toe and ankle injuries last week. The Rams’ ground game should still play well, but Lopez will make them work a little harder for yardage than they otherwise might have had to. Cardinals S Andrew Wingard (groin) and CB Max Melton (knee/hand) are also active. The Cardinals declared QB Joey Aguilar, CB Starling Thomas, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines and C Hjalte Froholdt inactive for Week 10 against the Rams. Playing without Froholdt, their starting center, and Williams, their current starting left tackle, is unfortunate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.headline: Cardinals agreed to terms with DT Roy Lopez, formerly of the Lions, on a two-year, $11.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.analysis: The deal includes $7 million guaranteed. 28-year-old Lopez is returning to Arizona after a one-year sojourn in Motown. A space clogger in the middle of the defense, Lopez will find a rotational role on early downs in the desert, but nothing more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.headline: Lions agreed to terms with DT Roy Lopez, formerly of the Cardinals, on a one-year, $4.65 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.analysis: A 2021 sixth-round pick of the Texans, Lopez was cut by Houston on the eve of the 2023 season. He then managed to become a Cardinals mainstay as a rotational interior lineman. That is what he will remain in Detroit during his age-28 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.headline: Texans waived DT Roy Lopez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.analysis: Per ESPN’s Field Yates, Lopez was waived with an injury settlement and is free to sign with any team if he goes unclaimed on waivers. The former sixth-round pick has appeared in 33 games for the Texans since 2021, totaling 67 tackles, 11 TFLs, and two sacks. With 29 starts under his belt, Lopez can provide valuable depth and experience to any defensive line looking to improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.headline: Texans selected Arizona DT Roy Lopez with the No. 195 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roy-lopez/.analysis: Lopez (6’2/304) was only a two-star prospect from Tempe, AZ who received scant interest on the recruiting trail and ended up enrolling at New Mexico State over the Utah State Aggies. A highly productive player at NMSU, Lopez racked up 63 tackles and 12.5 TFL in 2018 before getting injured in 2019 and transferring to Arizona as a graduate for the 2020 season where he started all five of the Wildcats’ games. As a two-time state wrestling champion whose father is a football coach, Lopez knows how to use leverage to maximize his strength and hold the point of attack. He plays with a relentless motor and upper body power, as his 36 bench reps show. He tested well in his pro day workout, posting a credible 7.48 RAS. His straight-line speed and burst are a little slow, but his agility is exceptional for a player his size. He has the potential to develop into a dependable interior lineman at the next level. PFF graded the Texans as having the worst run-stopping defense in the league last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.headline: Lan Larison caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.analysis: Larison, New England’s third-string running back today, only ran the ball once. He found the end zone on a 20-yard catch-and-run late in the fourth quarter, but the play was nullified by a penalty. Refusing to be denied, Larison got in on a 10-yard checkdown from Tommy DeVito a few plays later. Larison will see a handful of weekly snaps with TreVeyon Henderson on IR, but we don’t foresee him being a relevant fantasy option afte New England’s upcoming bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.headline: Patriots team reporter Evan Lazar reports that RB Lan Larison “appears to be an early leader” for the RB3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lan-lariso.analysis: Larison, 24, was a 2025 undrafted free agent. He is apparently competing for a role as a kick returner as well as the backup rushing role. He will need to contribute on special teams if he is going to make the final roster. Lazar notes that rookie RBs Jam Miller and Myles Montgomery “have flashed explosiveness and lateral quickness,” and he thinks one or both could make a “push” after showing off burst in the outside zone scheme that the Patriots have been working on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 10 times for 25 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner was the first Patriots running back to touch the ball, even with Rhamondre Stevenson active. He out-carried Stevenson 10-6, though New England pulled Stevenson in the fourth quarter. Kiner saw three rush attempts in the final frame, though it was third-string running back Lan Larison who found the end zone. Stevenson’s role should improve after the Patriots’ Week 11 bye. Kiner will tumble to the back of the RB3 ranks when he takes on the Chargers in two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Despite some belief that Stevenson could miss a short period of time due to a knee injury he suffered late in Week 9’s loss to the Packers, the 28-year-old back will have an outside chance at suiting up against the Lions after logging back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Backup Corey Kiner is expected to step into an expanded role if Stevenson is unable to go, but will be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/FLEX play if Stevenson does suit up. With the Pats and Lions set to face off at 9:30 AM EST in Germany, fantasy managers will want to check early inactives before setting their lineups if they either player on their roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stevenson is expected to miss some time because of the knee issue. With their bye next week, it makes sense for the Pats to hold him out on Sunday and give him an extra week of rest. With TreVeyon Henderson already ruled out, Corey Kiner is the next man up in this backfield. As the only game in town for touches, he will push for an RB2 ranking this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots lost Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) late in this one, but it’s still worth noting that nearly all of Kiner’s production came when the backups were on the field. Kiner punched in a nine-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter with the game well out of reach, and broke off a 20-yard run on the second-to-last play in regulation. While it’s possible Kiner finds himself in a lead role when the Patriots take on the Lions next week, fantasy managers will want to temper expectations for Week 10 if either Stevenson (knee) or TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s most notable usage note is that he was trusted with a carry on 3rd-and-1 during the Patriots’ eighth drive. He was unable to convert it for a first down. Kiner was involved today because TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive. Kiner does not need to be stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Even with Rhamondre Stevenson active and TreVeyon Henderson surprisingly playing through his ankle injury, Kiner was called on as the Patriots’ “closer,” with all 11 of his handles coming in the final 16:30 of the contest. The Patriots were winning, but the game was still in doubt. Kiner responded by continually turning his short-yardage opportunities into first downs, while he ended up leading the team in rushing. It wasn’t easy to see that one coming, but it might be difficult for coach Mike Vrabel to un-see it as neither Stevenson nor Henderson impress in their No. 1 or 2 jobs. Kiner is worth an end-of-bench stash in 14-team leagues but is not yet 12-team league relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for four yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was initially expected to miss multiple weeks because of the knee injury he suffered in Week 9, so it was rather surprising that he suited up at all today. He was on the field for the Pats’ first play of the game but then immediately gave way to Corey Kiner, who went on to tally 10 carries. The team eventually pulled Stevenson entirely once the game was out of hand. He did not play a snap in the fourth quarter. Stevenson should see more work after resting over the bye week, but he may be relegated to committee duties for a few more weeks. Stevenson will be a low-end RB2 when he takes on the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: There’ll be no Corey Kiner SZN then. I’ll tell the children. Stevenson is somewhat shockingly active after injuring his knee in Week 9. Initial reports had him missing multiple weeks. Instead, he’s good to go, though we should still expect Kiner to mix in for a few touches. Inactive for the Pats are QB Behren Morton, OG Ben Brown, OG Walter Rouse, OT Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis, and S Brenden Schooler.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: A.J. Brown is also expected to play. We will get confirmation from the team within the hour, but fantasy managers who are already rising and grinding can get Stevenson and Brown back in their lineups. Stevenson will shuffle back into the RB2 mix. We will expect to see some Corey Kiner touches to keep Stevenson fresh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Despite some belief that Stevenson could miss a short period of time due to a knee injury he suffered late in Week 9’s loss to the Packers, the 28-year-old back will have an outside chance at suiting up against the Lions after logging back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Backup Corey Kiner is expected to step into an expanded role if Stevenson is unable to go, but will be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/FLEX play if Stevenson does suit up. With the Pats and Lions set to face off at 9:30 AM EST in Germany, fantasy managers will want to check early inactives before setting their lineups if they either player on their roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Post-Week 9 reports had Stevenson with a chance to miss a short period of time, but a limited session at least points to the idea that he could play in Munich on Sunday morning. Fantasy managers reliant on Stevenson or dabbling with Corey Kiner will want to keep an eye on Friday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson is expected to miss some time because of the knee issue. With their bye next week, it makes sense for the Pats to hold him out on Sunday and give him an extra week of rest. With TreVeyon Henderson already ruled out, Corey Kiner is the next man up in this backfield. As the only game in town for touches, he will push for an RB2 ranking this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) could miss a “short period of time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Reporting Monday, Schefter relayed that Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that could “sideline him for a short period of time.” While the report is about as vague as possible, fantasy managers will want to begin exploring alternatives for a running back that has outperformed his preseason draft capital through the first half of the season. TreVeyon Henderson remains sidelined indefinitely with what is being called an illness, which could leave Corey Kiner atop the depth chart in the backfield in the immediate future. The Patriots next play the Lions in Week 10, where Kiner would be a viable FLEX play, should Stevenson and Henderson miss. Schefter adds that the tendon issue is not expected to require surgery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) will not return in the Patriots’ Week 9 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson suffered his knee injury late in the third quarter, but was eventually able to make it to the field under his own power. After spending a few moments in the blue medical tent, Stevenson went to the locker room and was ruled out soon after by the team. The 28-year-old back managed just 32 scoreless yards on six carries, but hauled in a 30-yard reception from Drake Maye in the second quarter, finishing the day with a 3-46-1 line on four targets. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined with neurological concerns, the Patriots could be looking at using Corey Kiner as their top back entering Week 10 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (undisclosed) exited in the third quarter of Week 9’s game against the Patriots and went to the locker room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was slow to get up after a play late in the third quarter and was seen going to the locker room shortly after leaving the field. He spent some time in the blue medical tent, but the team has not disclosed what he is dealing with. Stevenson has rushed six times for 32 yards so far and has caught another three passes for 46 yards and a touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 19 times for 82 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding three receptions for eight yards.
