https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was held out of the end zone against the Dolphins, but comfortably paced his team with 22 touches and was handed the ball on each of the Patriots’ first three plays. Stevenson ran hard on inside runs and played well as a receiver, as usual. A fake pitch from inside the Dolphins’ five-yard line had at least one Dolphins defender convinced that Stevenson was headed for the end zone, but Drake Maye kept the ball and ran it into the end zone himself. Stevenson remains firmly in play as an RB2 next week against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Tommy DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Patriots’ 35-10, Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito took over for an injured Drake Maye in the first quarter. He could not get anything going despite facing a Detroit defense that has been extremely beatable this year. DeVito threw a ghastly interception right at Roger McCreary late in the second quarter. He had Kyle Williams wide open for a touchdown but didn’t see him sprinting down the field uncovered. DeVito did eventually find the end zone on a check-down to Lan Larison late in the fourth quarter. DeVito would be the next man up if Drake Maye isn’t healthy after New England’s Week 11 bye, though we hope it doesn’t come to that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots re-signed QB Tommy DeVito to a two-year, $7.4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito spent all of last season with the Patriots but never took a snap for the team. The former UDFA served as the team’s QB3 behind Joshua Dobbs and will likely have a chance to compete with Dobbs for the team’s QB2 spot now that both are slated to return in 2026. For his career, DeVito has thrown for 1,358-8-3 on 222 passes while completing 65.3 percent of his attempts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots declared WR Efton Chism, CB Kobee Minor, OLB Bradyn Swinson, OT Marcus Bryant, G Caedan Wallace, TE C.J. Dippre and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Super Bowl LX against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Chism, an undrafted free agent rookie, was active in the Divisional Round and Wild Card Round but did not play in the AFC Championship Game. He caught 3-of-3 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown in the regular season and caught his lone postseason target for a 20-yard gain. DeVito will serve as the Patriots’ emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots declared QB Tommy DeVito, G Jared Wilson, S Brenden Schooler, T Marcus Bryant, OLB Bradyn Swinson, TE CJ Dippre, and DT Khyiris Tonga inactive for Week 13 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant is probably the most notable inactive for the Patriots considering he was expected to serve at the swing tackle against the Giants. DeVito will be inactive, as has been the case since being claimed by the team in August.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots claimed QB Tommy DeVito off waivers from the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito threw for 198 yards and three touchdowns against the Patriots in the preseason finale and now he’ll join New England’s active roster. The 27-year-old started six games with the Giants in 2023, but he’ll serve as New England’s third quarterback behind Drake Maye and Josh Dobbs. New England also claimed DB Charles Woods off waivers from the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Giants released QB Tommy DeVito.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: While DeVito was competing for the backup quarterback job in camp, he had little chance of making the Giants roster after New York brought in Russell Wilson, Jameis Winston and Jaxon Dart this offseason. The 27-year-old started six games with the Giants in 2023, throwing for eight touchdowns and three interceptions. DeVito is unlikely to be claimed by another team on waivers, meaning he’s destined for a practice squad. While carrying a fourth quarterback on the practice squad may be a little excessive, Wilson and Winston aren’t exactly spring chickens either and DeVito’s best path forward for his career may be to remain in the Giants organization.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Giants re-signed QB Tommy DeVito to a one-year, $1.030 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: According to Stapleton, DeVito will sign his ERFA tender over the weekend, making DeVito the first quarterback to be rostered by the Giants for the start of the 2025 season. DeVito has thrown for 1,358-8-3 in two seasons with the Giants but played just 91 offensive snaps last season. He’ll have a chance to compete for the backup quarterback job in camp but is more likely to serve as an emergency QB3 most weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Giants coach Brian Daboll said Drew Lock (shoulder) will get an MRI and a decision on who will start against the Colts in Week 17 has not yet been made.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Someone with more time to pursue this should come up with a stat on Giants touchdowns thrown against MRIs received since Daniel Jones was released. After clearing concussion protocol it seems likely that Tommy DeVito would be the starter against the Colts if Lock was unable to go. Either way, the Giants will be a target for Colts D/ST streamers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Tommy DeVito (concussion) will be active for New York’s Week 16 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito cleared protocol and will back up Drew Lock as the NFL’s worst quarterback room tries to make it through the last three weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Dylan Parham is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Bills with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: The Jets’ starting left guard went down with a knee injury in the second quarter. The injury didn’t look good, but he was able to walk off the field and into the blue tent on his own. We’ll see what further testing reveals, but he’s been one of the Jets’ best linemen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Dylan Parham suffered a knee injury in the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Parham signed a two-year deal with the Jets in the offseason. Jordan Meredith has taken his spot at left guard. Needing a flurry of points to get back in this game, things are looking bleak for Gang Green.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Jets agreed to terms with OG Dylan Parham, formerly of the Raiders, on a two-year, $20 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Parham has been a starter for the Raiders since the team drafted him in 2022. The former third-round pick appeared in 15 games in 2025. He played exclusively at left guard this year but has previously pitched in at center and right guard. Parham will take on a starting role with the Jets and his versatility will allow them some freedom with other free agent or rookie offensive linemen decisions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Raiders signed OG Alex Cappa, formerly of the Bengals, to a two-year, $11 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Cappa was a cap casualty for Cincinnati earlier this week. The age-30 guard has 96 career starts during his time with the Bengals and Bucs. Dylan Parham started at right guard for the Raiders last year but missed a handful of games with an injury and was even benched for a week. Cappa could push him for the starting role in training camp. Even if the Raiders stick with Parham, Cappa gives them a second option as Parham heads into a contract year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Raiders OG Cody Whitehair (ankle) exited Week 9 against the Bengals and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Whitehair went down in the third quarter with an ankle injury, marking the third Raiders offensive lineman ankle injury on the day. Kolton Miller was ruled out, but Andrus Peat came back in. Dylan Parham entered the game for Whitehair, though Parham was already not starting due to a foot injury that kept him out the last few games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Andre James (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: The Raiders’ offensive line is one of the team’s core strengths so losing the starting center could be a big deal. The team has also been without G Dylan Parham (foot), who returned to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. The offensive line could be compromised if both players are absent on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Raiders RG Dylan Parham (foot) ruled out for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: The Raiders’ offense is in a bad state with Davante Adams now a Jet, Jakobi Meyers doubtful to play and no long-term answers at quarterback. Hopefully, Parham can return soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: Raiders LT Kolton Miller (knee/shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: The Raiders had multiple lineman listed on the injury report Wednesday, starting with Miller, who was listed as a non-participant due to knee and shoulder injuries. OT Thayer Munford (knee/ankle) was a full participant while OG Dylan Parham (foot) was a non-participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.headline: RG Dylan Parham (Achilles) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-parh.analysis: Raiders RT Thayer Munford Jr. (knee/ankle) was also absent during the portion of practice open to the media. The news bodes poorly for the unit’s chances of fending off the Broncos’ blitz-happy pass rush in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa beat his man off the line of scrimmage for a 12-yard score early in the second quarter. He was surprisingly involved in this contest, logging just his third game with more than three targets on the year. TeSlaa hadn’t seen more than two targets in a game since Week 4. We don’t expect this to be the new norm, so fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa did not have a catch in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa has been effectively phased out of the Detroit passing attack. he has one catch over his past three games, and against the Vikings on Sunday he ran 13 routes on 35 Lions drop backs and did not see a target. He can be dropped in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-2 targets in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: Jared Goff gave TeSlaa two chances to contribute today. The first was a 3rd-and-13 pass on the Lions’ second drive, just beyond the sticks, in which TeSlaa went aerial and fully horizontal, trying to make the diving catch. The pass, unfortunately, fell incomplete. Goff went back to him on the fifth drive, firing a pass — just a touch too high — to the second-year wide receiver who was wide open on a crossing route, racing across the back of the end zone. TeSlaa leapt for it and got a hand on it, but he couldn’t come down with it. TeSlaa takes his goose egg into the Lions’ Week 6 bye. With any luck, it hatches into a FLEX-relevant stat line against the Packers in Week 7, though he remains a boom-bust pass catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa led the Lions in receiving on the back of a 49-yard grab late in the game. He was otherwise an afterthought in the offense, finishing the game with a nine percent target share. TeSlaa is averaging three targets per game, which simply isn’t enough to get him into the FLEX mix. He is buried in the WR6/7 range headed into Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa failed to catch his only target in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa did his usual wind sprinting in this game and failed to bring in his only target on the day. With stars at nearly every skill position in Detroit, there simply isn’t any room for a meaningful TeSlaa role. He is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell told reporters WR Isaac TeSlaa is going to be just fine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: Even after TeSlaa’s training camp struggles extended into the Lions’ first preseason game, Detroit doesn’t seem worried about the 24-year-old receiver. TeSlaa had his first target go through his hands and off his helmet for an interception and later couldn’t hang on to a fourth down pass in the loss to the Bengals on Thursday. Still, his only competitor for the WR3 role is Greg Dortch, a journeyman receiver who also failed to catch a pass in the first preseason game. The Lions WR3 isn’t likely to be a fantasy-relevant role when everyone else in the offense is healthy, but Detroit would still like to see more development from their third-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lionis WR Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-3 targets in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: The Lions’ established starters did not play. Lions WR Greg Dortch could be challenging TeSlaa’s WR3 role, although Dortch went 0-for-1 as a receiver as well. TeSlaa out-snapped him 15-7 on the first three drives. TeSlaa took two more snaps on the fourth drive, sans Dortch, which ended in a turnover. This is a position battle to keep an eye on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy reports a lot of targets to Isaac TeSlaa in the early portion of training camp have been broken up “due to a lack of separation.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: We weren’t expecting a major target share for TeSlaa anyway in this offense, and he makes his living making contested catches, but it’s still a little disappointing that he hasn’t taken more of a step forward from his rookie season so far. TeSlaa is probably only a consideration in deeper leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Isaac TeSlaa has “looked like a consistent veteran this offseason” and he is “excited about where he’s trending.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa looks to be penciled into the three-wide set next to Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown. It’s hard to understand how TeSlaa will generate much in the way of targets — he sure didn’t last year when he was on the field — but the Lions could have a good enough offense that TeSlaa finds his way on the WR4 radar this year either way. TeSlaa notched six touchdowns on 27 targets last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy believes Isaac TeSlaa should be a “full-time starter” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa played sparingly for most of the season until Kalif Raymond started dealing with an ankle injury near Thanksgiving. TeSlaa’s numbers boomed to an average of 44 snaps a game for the rest of the season. The target rate wasn’t exactly fantasy-friendly, but TeSlaa managed six touchdowns on just 27 targets last year and figures to be an interesting fantasy football player in 2026, if not a downright useful one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki rushed six times for 28 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki operated as the RB2 once again. Three of his carries came on the Lions’ penultimate drive, though Jared Goff was still on the field. Dan Campbell pulled his starters for the team’s final possession and Jacob Saylors closed out the game. Vaki is the backup fantasy managers should roster as Jahmyr Gibbs insurance, but he doesn’t hold any standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: No surprise here. St. Brown is good to go as a mid-range WR1 for Week 10. Sione Vaki is also active. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, C Cade Mays, DB Keith Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DT Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He remains a worthwhile stash as the Lions’ No. 2 running back. His backup, Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring), is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki played through the injury last week, and should be expected to do so again against the Patriots this week. Fellow backup RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) is practicing in full. Vaki is the team’s top backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Isiah Pacheco (back) could return in early December.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: According to Rapoport, Pacheco “had surgery to remove a body that was pressing on a nerve in his back.” The 27-year-old back is looking at a 12-week recovery, but if all goes well, he could return for the final month of the season. If the Lions don’t add anybody to their backfield in the coming days/weeks, Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors will continue to serve as the primary backups behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could both push for RB2 touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It’s hard to imagine either Vaki or Saylors having meaningful fantasy value at this point in the season, but it sounds like both will be on the field while Isiah Pacheco (back) is sidelined for at least the first four games of the season. Judging by how Campbell sounded when discussing each player, it sounded like Saylors might be closer to the official RB2, but Campbell didn’t mince words when he said, “I see Vaki getting some reps, too.” Fantasy managers interested in taking a shot on a Lions running back not named Jahmyr Gibbs can consider both Saylors and Vaki as late-round dart throws until we see how their snap shares look in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 50 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams didn’t post an elite box score, but he did earn his highest target total since Week 7. The speedster earned a healthy 22 percent target share and finished second on the team in receptions, tied with Amon-Ra St. Brown. Williams has generally been a boom/bust wideout, but he has at least 40 yards in all but two games this year. He’ll remain at the top of the WR3 ranks when he takes on the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: We’re not sure if a player can be due for a catastrophic bust of a fantasy week, but “Jamo” was probably due for a catastrophic bust. He came into this game red hot, with 208 yards and five touchdowns over his past three games. Given Williams boom/bust nature, a flop was always right around the corner. He also dropped one of his two targets, which didn’t help his cause. The Lions get a potential shootout with the Patriots next week, meaning fantasy managers can safely keep Williams in their lineups as a WR3 despite today’s quiet outing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams scored the Lions’ lone passing touchdown on a short corner-of-the-end-zone grab in the first half. Williams was second behind Amon-Ra St. Brown in targets, functioning as the primary downfield threat with a nice 46-yard catch on a Jared Goff shot down the middle. Williams, who came into Week 8 with the 16th most air yards among wide receivers this season, should remain in lineups next week against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary that has struggled against boundary wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 5-of-9 targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams wasted little time getting involved early in this one. On the Lions’ fifth play of the game, he ripped off a 24-yard gain to the Packers’ 16-yard line. On the next play, Williams came in motion and snuck out of the Lions’ backfield to turn a short pass into a 16-yard score, giving the Lions their first points of the day. Williams would find the end zone again in the third quarter on a 10-yard touchdown, and on the following drive, he nearly scored again. Were it not for a Packers defender knocking him out of the back of the end zone on a catch, we would have seen a hat trick. Williams’ big-play ability was on display all night, as three of his five receptions went for 15-plus yards. Williams now has back-to-back two-touchdown performances to his name and has gone for 90-plus yards in two of his last three games. His volume continues to be inconsistent, but Williams is capable of breaking any game open at a moment’s notice. He will be a fringe WR2 in what could be a tough Week 8 matchup against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The Lions’ speedster only caught two passes today, but he made them count. Williams’ first catch was a nine-yard, fourth-down touchdown on the Lions’ fifth drive. He nearly hauled in a 25-yarder via a play-action target on the sixth drive, but Cardinals CB Max Melton batted it away. He was open for an explosive gain on the next drive, but Jared Goff checked down to Sam LaPorta about 10 yards beneath Williams. A few plays later, Williams dusted his coverage defender for a 39-yard score from bunch formation, hauling in the touchdown pass in stride in the end zone. Goff later gave him another touchdown chance on a downfield throw targeted inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line, but Williams couldn’t secure it. He’ll now take a week off with the Lions’ Week 6 bye, but return as a WR2 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Fantasy managers had suffered through three down games with the middle-round pick before Williams was able to take advantage of a Carolina secondary missing its top two corners. He was kept out of the end zone for the fourth consecutive contest to start the 2026 season but returned his first fantasy-viable outing on the backs of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts. While that level of volume is unlikely to be the norm for the Lions, a Week 5 meeting with the Cardinals provides another opportunity for Williams to return value in a potential shootout. Williams will be an upside WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: The Detroit Free Press’s Dave Birkett reports Jameson Williams will not face assault charges stemming from an incident with a woman on August 6th.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The incident was reported to the police earlier this month. Jeff Wattrick, spokesman for the Oakland County Prosecutor, told Birkett, “Based on the facts presented to us at this time, the Novi Police and our office jointly concluded that there is no cause to file charges against Mr. Williams.” Williams has been an off-field headache for the Lions since entering the league, but it doesn’t sound like this latest incident will be an issue. He will be on the field for the team’s Week 4 date with Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Drew Petzing schemed up a few short and intermediate looks for Williams, but he still finished with a measly 12.5 percent target share. Both Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown saw eight targets. Williams has topped out at four catches through three weeks. His 49 yards today are a season-high. Williams closed the 2025 season as an every-week WR2, maybe even more. That usage has all but disappeared to start the 2026 season. He is tumbling back into the WR3 ranks heading into the Lions’ Week 4 game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams continues to be primarily utilized as a deep threat in the Detroit offense, which is not the development fantasy managers were expecting following offseason reports that his route tree would be expanded in the new year. The mounting injuries along the offensive line have limited Goff’s time in the pocket to the point where Williams rarely has enough time for his routes to develop, leading to the down production through two weeks. Whether either of those two variables changes in the immediate future remains to be seen, leaving us to treat Williams as nothing more than an upside WR3 in the interim. He will be a difficult start in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he’s “not concerned” with Jameson Williams’ drops.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: At least a couple times a year Campbell has to tell reporters that he’s not worried about Williams’ sometimes-egregious drops, and that his playing time won’t suffer as a result. “I mean, look, nobody’s more frustrated than he is about it, but what I love is this just shows his growth,” Campbell said. “He bounced back, he gets back in the huddle. He’s not sulking, he’s not pouting about it, he’s not letting it go in the tank.” Williams in Week 1 against the Saints had two drops, one of which could have gone for a long score. He led the Lions with 128 air yards (a 56 percent share) and was second on the team with a 23 percent target share. Williams ran a route on 37 of Detroit’s 40 drop backs. He should be locked into lineups for Thursday night’s matchup against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 20-of-31 passes for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Lions’ 35-10, Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions’ offense faced almost no resistance from New England. Goff averaged 9.8 yards per attempt and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for seven yards per carry. Goff did, however, force two throws that simply weren’t there. Both came in the second quarter, and the second pick was in the back of the end zone, costing the Lions at least three points. On the whole, it was still business as usual for one of the league’s best offenses. Goff gets a tough matchup versus the Bucs next week, but that won’t knock him out of the QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: That should alleviate any concern that he’d miss Sunday morning’s Munich kickoff against the Patriots. Goff will be a low-end QB1 for that one assuming no major negative news hits on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff had his worst game of the year in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins. Perhaps this injury was bothering him. On the plus side, Goff is already practicing in a limited capacity, so we do not expect it to impact his availability for Week 10 against the Patriots. It is worth monitoring his practice participation level this week, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 17-of-25 passes for 170 yards and an interception in the Lions’ 19-9, Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions undoubtedly played down to their opponents in this game, putting up six points in the first half before finding slightly more success after the break. Things got off to a rocky start with an easy interception for Dolphins defensive back Chris Johnson. Goff was hit as he threw the ball and it wobbled right into Johnson’s arms. The Lions had one drive go for more than 50 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs punched in the score at the end of the drive, taking home the only Lions touchdown of the day. Goff should have no issues turning things around against the Patriots next week. He will remain near the top of the QB1 ranks for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 18-of-25 attempts for 176 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff, like all quarterbacks against the Vikings, seemed lost from start to finish, unable to decipher to intricate Vikings blitz scheme. He was sacked four times and saw pressure on seemingly every drop back before the Lions abandoned the pass game for the run game in the second half. Sunday marked only the second game this season in which Goff did not have multiple touchdown throws, and the first time he has not eclipsed 200 passing yards. Goff should be able to get back on track next week against a bad Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 22-of-32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 20-17, Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: In a game that felt like it should have featured far more points, Goff and the Lions narrowly walked away with the win. He led an explosive opening drive that included a 28-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown and a 24-yard pass to Jameson Williams, and ended with a 16-yard touchdown pass to Williams to put the Lions up 7-0 early. Goff would again connect with Williams for a 10-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter, and narrowly missed linking up with him for a third touchdown when Williams was forced out of the end zone on a catch on fourth-and-five from the Packers’ six-yard line. Goff did lose a fumble in this one on a botched snap exchange with his center, but it was an overall strong outing for the Lions’ signal-caller. Goff has yet to throw an interception this season and has now thrown for over 300 yards in three of his six games this season. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week at home against the 6-0 Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 19-of-30 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ 45-21, Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for a one-yard touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Sacks and a few errant throws under pressure derailed the Lions’ first three drives. Goff got things back on track after that, guiding the offense to seven straight scoring drives, including six touchdowns. He even punched in a one-yard rushing touchdown via a quarterback sneak, marking his first rushing score since 2023. Goff could have boosted his passing yards total with a likely explosive gain by targeting an open Jameson Williams on the first drive after halftime, but he instead checked down to Sam LaPorta in the flats for an eight-yard pickup. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but Goff will be a locked-in QB1 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 32-of-52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ 32-26, Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff has now thrown a touchdown pass in 27 straight contests, a streak that started in the team’s Thanksgiving day contest against the Bears in 2024. He could move into sixth on the all-time list for consecutive games with a touchdown pass should he throw for at least one touchdown in each game this season. He came within four minutes of breaking that streak against the Panthers, needing a late touchdown to tight end Sam LaPorta to keep it alive in a game the Panthers dictated with their defense throughout. Goff also maintained his clean sheet of no interceptions thrown to start the season but it wasn’t enough to overcome a defense that ceded 445 yards of total offense to a Panthers team without two of their top three wide receivers in Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. The Lions fall to 2-2, now two games behind the division-leading Vikings through the first month of play. Goff remains a surefire QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-24, Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff and the Lions got off to a slow start with just three points over their first three drives. Things started to click before halftime and Goff rode that momentum to 21 points after the break. Excluding a few kneel-downs to end the game, Detroit scored on five of their final six drives. The Lions have scored exactly 31 points in all three of their games this year. That may be a bit higher than their projection for Week 4 against the Panthers, but not by all that much. Goff will remain in the QB1 mix versus Carolina next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 26-of-38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns in the Lions’ 41-31, Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions staked the Bills to a 21-point lead early in the second quarter, eventually taking a 27-10 deficit into the break. The closest they would get the rest of the game was a 10-point deficit, but the offense finally came alive in the final two frames. Goff tossed a pair of touchdowns to alpha wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and one each to Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs, salvaging the poor team performance with an elite fantasy score for managers brave enough to start him on the road in the elements. The Lions fall to 1-1 ahead of a much more forgiving home matchup against the Jets in Week 3, where Goff will look to return another QB1 performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-5 targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown got things started early with a 56-yard catch-and-run that saw him make nearly half of the New England defense miss. Not content with one score, St. Brown plowed into the end zone on a 22-yard screen early in the third quarter. It was an electric homecoming of sorts for ARSB, who spent part of his childhood in Germany and holds German citizenship. St. Brown hadn’t scored since Week 3, so the double-dip today will be much appreciated by fantasy managers. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when Detroit takes on Tampa Bay next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: No surprise here. St. Brown is good to go as a mid-range WR1 for Week 10. Sione Vaki is also active. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, C Cade Mays, DB Keith Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DT Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown played through the rib injury last week. He remained limited in all three practices before this week’s game. He’s likely not at full strength, but there was never much risk of him missing today’s game. He remains a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was listed as questionable in Week 9 after practicing in a limited capacity all week. He managed to suit up on game day, posting an 8/86 receiving line. He was limited in all three practices this week and once again got hit with the questionable tag. We expect him to play. He should be treated as a WR1, as usual, assuming he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: He played through this last week, managing an 8/86 line against the Dolphins. We’d be surprised if he wasn’t removed from the injury report tomorrow after getting in two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown played through the injury without issue last week, catching eight passes for 86 yards. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver should be treated as a WR1, as usual, against the Patriots in this week’s international game. St. Brown will likely upgrade to full participation on Thursday or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was questionable for today’s game with a rib issue. You wouldn’t know it by his usage. He ran circles around the rest of the Lions’ pass-catchers with a 38 percent target share. He led the team in yards from scrimmage and accounted for just shy of half the team’s passing production. St. Brown remains a strong WR1 option ahead of his Week 10 game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was limited in practice throughout the week. He has a knack for getting it out through injuries and will do so again today. Even at less than full strength, St. Brown shouldn’t face much resistance from Miami’s weak secondary. He remains a top-end WR1 for his Week 9 game in South Beach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots, adding seven catches for 99 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs gashed the Pats for chunk gains at will, averaging seven yards per carry and over 14 yards per catch. The Lions’ line bludgeoned New England and Gibbs was untouchable in open space. Gibbs could have posted even better numbers had the Patriots’ offense pushed the pace of this game more. Even without much pushback from New England, Gibbs racked up 44.2 PPR points, which is just shy of the highest mark in a single game this year. He’s running away with the RB1 overall crown, especially with Kenneth Walker banged up. Per usual, Gibbs will be the top-ranked option at his position when he takes on the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: This was easily Gibbs’ worst fantasy outing of the year, though that largely speaks to just how incredible he has been in 2026. The big difference today was a lack of receiving usage. Gibbs was only targeted once and failed to catch a pass for the first time since Week 4 of the 2024 season. Jared Goff only attempted 25 passes, but that would still result in more than one target for Gibbs on a normal day. We’re willing to write this off as the product of a low-scoring rock fight with the Dolphins. Gibbs will be back at the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 10 date game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs had 23 rushes for 153 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Like all Minnesota opponents this season, the Lions got nothing going through the air. They resorted to a run-heavy game plan and shredded the Vikings defense on the ground for 228 yards. The rushing attack was led by Gibbs, who popped a handful of chunk runs in the second half after the Lions had mostly given up on attacking the Vikings through the air. This is Gibbs’ third 100-yard rushing effort of the 2026 season. His centrality in the Detroit offense makes Gibbs an elite play every week. He’ll take on the Dolphins in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Like teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, Gibbs started the week off with a missed practice before upgrading to a full participant in both sessions to end the week. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will be ready for a normal workload against the division rival Vikings Sunday. Fantasy managers are clearly starting Gibbs, regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: The return to practice comes on the heels of a missed practice Wednesday for the veteran workhorse, immediately putting fantasy managers at ease for Week 8. Managers will want to confirm his practice status Friday before making final preparations for the weekend, but it certainly appears as if Gibbs will be good to go for a normal, and massive, workload when the Lions take the field against the division rival Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 29 times for 116 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers, adding five receptions for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at what was an overall solid performance, but they probably would have liked to see Gibbs rush in a touchdown; the Packers were more than willing to give him one late in the fourth quarter. Gibbs intentionally fell short of the end zone twice on the Lions’ final drive to ensure Jake Bates’ game-winning field goal attempt would be the final play in regulation, which worked to the Lions’ advantage in the 20-17 win. Gibbs ripped off multiple chunk gains in this one, with 13 of his 29 carries going for five or more yards. He did lose a fumble deep inside Packers territory near the end of the second quarter, which likely cost his team at least three points, but as usual, Gibbs was a big reason why the Lions constantly found themselves in position to win. It’s worth noting that on his final play of the game, Gibbs appeared to suffer a knee injury when his left leg bent awkwardly as he attempted to stop and fall to the turf to keep the clock running, but he was able to jog off under his own power. We would ultimately expect him to be fine, but his practice status will be one to monitor this week as the Lions prepare to take on the Vikings. Assuming he is good to go, Gibbs will be an obvious RB1 candidate next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding five receptions for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs scored twice today, bringing his career touchdown total up to 57, breaking the NFL record set by former Lions RB Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored by a player under 25 years old. The exceptionally talented player gets a boost from his sharp coaching staff, who continue to maximize Gibbs’ strengths. OC Drew Petzing dialed up a trick-play screen pass for Gibbs after the two-minute warning, in which Gibbs took the handoff, pitched it to Amon-Ra St. Brown, who pitched it back to Jared Goff, who then chucked it back to Gibbs with three offensive linemen in front of him on the left side of the field. An 18-yard gain ensued. Gibbs later produced a season-long 22-yard run. Although he scored two touchdowns today, he could have had a third. On the Lions’ ninth drive, Gibbs got two chances from the one-yard line on the ninth drive before the coaching staff greenlit a successful QB sneak for Goff. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but he returns to the top of the running back ranks against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers, adding 31 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs had eclipsed 100 combined yards against all three opponents to start the season before the Panthers held him largely in check, with fantasy’s top asset cashing in on a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to avoid a disastrous outing. The two teams were knotted at 16 entering the half but it was the Panthers that dictated terms following the break, winning the time of possession battle by over six minutes. Gibbs maintained an elite workload by seeing all but two backfield opportunities and every available carry on the evening, keeping his fantasy value sky-high ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, RB AJ Dillon, DT TeRah Edwards, C Sam Hecht, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee, and LB Bobby Okereke inactive for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders will be out against the Saints, meaning Tommy Tremble will get a decent number of snaps and routes. He’ll be the TE2 behind Darren Waller, coming off his biggest game of the season. The Saints this season have allowed the third highest fantasy points per target to opposing tight ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, OLB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, G Damien Lewis, G Torricelli Simpkins, and DT Bobby Brown inactive for Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: The Panthers are extremely shorthanded along the offensive line and on the defensive side of the ball, most notably in the secondary and with the pass rush. That could spell trouble against the high-powered Green Bay passing game, particularly with wide receiver Matthew Golden active. The Panthers look to halt their recent skid on the road in hostile territory at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, WR John Metchie, QB Haynes King, S Zakee Wheatley, OT Albert Reese, OLB Patrick Jones II, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders, who worked through a lingering ankle injury this offseason, won’t suit up for the team’s season opener. That leaves Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble as the Panthers’ top two tight ends against Chicago. Waller will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 option who probably won’t run many routes in the run-first Carolina offense. Tremble should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person reports Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) looked good running around in the early offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders broke his ankle in Week 17 against the Seahawks, ending his season. It would seem that he’s on track to participate in training camp, and this report doesn’t really dwell on if he’ll be a possibility for the PUP list. In theory, Sanders could still emerge as the preferred pass-catching option at the position for the Panthers. In actuality, the 2024 fourth-rounder probably would have made more strides in either of the past two years if that was going to happen. He’s simply a TE3 hold in deep leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person believes the Panthers could target TE Kenyon Sadiq in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Person said the Panthers, who hold the 19th pick in the 2026 draft, could target two Oregon players: Sadiq, who had 51 receptions for 560 yards and eight touchdowns in his final collegiate season, and safety Dillon Thieneman, one of the most sought-after secondary options in this year’s draft. The team would likely have to trade up to make sure they have a shot at Sadiq, who would join Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders in the Carolina tight end room if he lands with the Panthers. The Panthers in 2025 targeted the tight end position at a 21 percent clip, the seventh lowest mark in the NFL. “Could that change with Brad Idzik taking over the play calling and the addition of offensive specialist Darrell Bevell, who was in Seattle with Canales when the Seahawks traded for All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham?” Person said. “Possibly.” Sadiq, who ranks 11th in yards per route run among tight ends in the 2026 draft class, would probably be a rotational player in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers GM Dan Morgan says he believes Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) will be ready for the team’s offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders underwent season-ending ankle surgery late last season and was placed on injured reserve before the Week 18 finale. Sanders, who was selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, caught just 29 passes for 190 yards and one touchdown last season while starting five of the 13 games he appeared in. The third-year tight end will likely battle with Tommy Tremble for playing time this season, but the Panthers could also look to add to their tight end room through the draft with a talented rookie class incoming.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) would undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 18’s game against the Buccaneers. Sanders broke his ankle on Carolina’s first play from scrimmage yesterday against the Seahawks. The 2024 fourth-rounder enters the 2026 offseason in the third year of his rookie contract having not taken a noticeable step forward in his sophomore year while struggling through a midseason high-ankle sprain. He doesn’t figure to offer a lot in fantasy leagues in 2026 from where we sit at the end of the 2025 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders suffered an ankle injury in Carolina’s Week 17 game against the Seahawks and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders’ right foot got rolled up run blocking on the literal first play of the game. He was in a world of pain before being carted to the locker room. It’s quite possible the 22-year-old’s season is through. The second-year pro entered today sitting on a 29/190/1 line, with the touchdown coming last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught both of his targets for nine yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 16 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders was targeted just twice, but one of those targets was a six-yard touchdown catch. The other one was an attempted hurdle for a three-yard gain in the first half. Rookie Mitchell Evans caught three passes for 23 yards as well. The tight end spot in Carolina is a mix of multiple players. Sanders ran 20 routes and saw 31 snaps, while Tommy Tremble saw 23 snaps and Evans saw 16 snaps. Sanders is the pass-catching tight end while Evans is more of the blocker, but neither should be on fantasy radars for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught all four of his targets for 22 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders led the team’s tight ends in targets and catches, but Tommy Tremble was the hero of the day with a 54-yard reception to set up a game-winning field goal. Rookie tight end Mitchell Evans also caught a pair of passes. With all three tight ends seeing some work every week, Sanders is barely in the TE2 mix ahead of Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Colts declared QB Riley Leonard, LS Luke Rhodes, LB Jaylon Carlies, OT Jalen Travis, TE Will Mallory, and DT Jerry Tillery inactive for Week 10 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: The Colts already declared several players out prior to Sunday’s game against the Dolphins. Leonard will be the emergency third quarterback while Rhodes (hamstring), Carlies (neck), Travis (knee), Tillery (calf) and Mallory (hamstring) are dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Colts TE Will Mallory (lung) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 18 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Buried with Tyler Warren in the mix, Mallory played in just two games and had one catch in 16 snaps. He enters the final year of his rookie deal on the borderline of the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Colts declared TE Will Mallory, LB Cameron McGrone, QB Anthony Richardson, OG Dalton Tucker, and DE Isaiah Land inactive for Week 18 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Anthony Richardson is the big name here. He was ruled out on Friday. Mallory’s second season ends with four catches for 29 yards. He went for 207 yards on 18 grabs as a rookie, so 2024 was a step back for the young tight end. He will be fighting for a roster spot when the Colt’ offseason program starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Will Mallory caught 4-of-4 targets for 47 yards in the Colts’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: The Colts tight ends led the team in yardage, with Mallory totaling 47 yards and Kylen Granson totaling 62 yards. The rookie Mallory saw usage over the middle of the field as a big target to fight for yards. Gardner Minshew and the Colts were slow in moving the ball, so Mallory had a big piece of a small pie against the Falcons. It was only Mallory’s second career-game of at least four catches, though that trend is unlikely to continue when Michael Pittman returns to action. Mallory is best left off the fantasy radar the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Colts selected Miami TE Will Mallor with the No. 162 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Mallory (6’4/239) was a consistent producer at Miami, hovering around 300 receiving yards for three years before posting a 42-538-3 line as a fifth-year senior. He led the Canes in catches and yards while spending most of his time as an inline tight end. Despite being attached to the line or in the slot on occasion, Mallory struggled as a run-blocker, ranking just shy of dead last in run-blocking grade among Power Five tight ends according to Pro Football Focus. At the combine, Mallory cruised to a 4.54 Forty and excelled in the broad (122 inches) and vertical (36.5 inches) jumps. Mallory may need to put on weight to improve as a blocker at the next level, but that could sap his difference-making speed. He will likely be viewed as a part-time player in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Miami senior TE Will Mallory (shoulder) is ready to return to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Mallory (6'5/245) had surgery back in March for his shoulder, but the team has announced he’s ready to return to practice and will play when the season starts. The fifth-year senior is coming off his best season, where he had a career-high 30 catches and 347 receding yards. The bulk of those numbers came when Tyler Van Dyke took over at quarterback, and with him being the Day 1 starter this year, we should see Mallory getting consistent opportunities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Miami junior TE Will Mallory said on Monday that he’s “basically a full-go” after missing the spring due to shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: “The shoulder’s doing good,” Mallory said, according to 247Sports. “I’m basically full-go now. It’s good to be back. I missed being out there in the spring with the guys, but if feel good now and we’re getting after it summer workouts.” Due to the shoulder issue Mallory was left to do a lot of “mental reps” during the spring, which was also the case for starting QB D’Eriq King (torn ACL). According to the junior tight end, who will be of even greater importance the Hurricanes with Brevin Jordan in the NFL, he and King have been able to strengthen their bond during the offseason. Mallory finished the 2020 season with a 22-329-4 receiving line, and he should be a part of the conversation for the Mackey Award during the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Miami junior TE Will Mallory (shoulder) will not be available for spring practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Mallory (6'5/245) underwent minor shoulder surgery earlier this offseason. This past season, the junior logged a 22-329-4 receiving line. Presumably, he’ll be good to go for August camp, but if that’s not the case, we’ll pass along word. Mallory is a prime candidate to see a statistical bump this coming season, as TE Brevin Jordan is draft-bound and there will be catches available in the fall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Miami junior TE Brevin Jordan is back to full strength after missing time due to a shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Jordan (6'3/245) has not appeared in a game since he injured his shoulder during the Hurricanes’ October 10 loss at Clemson. With the junior sidelined for wins over Pitt and Virginia fellow junior Will Mallory ascended into the starting role, and he caught four passes for 109 yards and two touchdowns in those games. Both Mallory and Jordan will be available for the Hurricanes’ matchup with NC State Friday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.headline: Miami junior TE Brevin Jordan is listed as a co-starter for Saturday’s game vs. Virginia after missing this past week’s game with a shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mallo.analysis: Jordan (6'3/245) injured his shoulder during the Hurricanes’ October 10 loss at Clemson, and he was held out of this week’s 31-19 win over Pitt as a result. The junior tight end’s absence opened the door for Will Mallory, who caught two passes for 51 yards and two touchdowns on Saturday. Should Jordan not be able to play against Virginia, Mallory would be in line for another start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) is active for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson was questionable and did not practice on Friday, so he’s presumably gutting it out as the Texans go without Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) in what looks like a must-win game. Also ruled out on Friday and Saturday were Marvin Harrison (hamstring), TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), C/G Keylan Rutledge (neck) and David Montgomery (groin), and they’re joined by G Wyatt Teller (back/illness) on the inactives list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Will Anderson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson was added to the injury report on Thursday, then downgraded to a DNP on Friday. He was on the report earlier this year with the ankle injury. We suspect it flared up on him mid-week. The good news for Texans fans is that it won’t stop him from facing the Browns. With 9.5 sacks to his name through eight games, Anderson is in the midst of another elite season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson (ankle) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson was added to the report as limited on Thursday and did not practice on Friday, throwing his status into major doubt ahead of Houston’s game in Cleveland. He has been listed with an ankle before this year, and with Danielle Hunter suddenly out, Cleveland’s pass offense could see some efficiency boosts against the Texans without their star rushers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (ankle) is not on Houston’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: It wound up being a DNP-Limited-Full workload progression for Anderson, who should remain a terror against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson popped up on the injury report with an ankle issue to open the week. As one of the league’s elite pass-rushers, the 25-year-old is a key cog to the Texans defense. He did not practice Wednesday, putting his Week 5 status in jeopardy. Anderson still has chances to practice later this week and play against the Titans, but any time missed puts the 0-4 Texans in an even deeper hole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans signed DE Will Anderson to a three-year, $150 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson’s deal will make him the highest-paid non-QB in NFL history. The star pass rusher will receiver $134 million in guaranteed money on his new deal and is now under contract with the Texans through the 2023 season. Anderson entered the league in 2023 after molding himself into the nation’s top pass rusher at Alabama. He has shown steady growth during each of his three seasons and has posted double-digit sack totals in each of his last two seasons, earning First-team All-Pro honors in 2025 while finishing second in Defensive Player of the Year voting. With Anderson now extended, the Texans can now shift their focus to C.J. Stroud, whose fifth-year option they recently picked up to keep him under contract through 2027. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , Anderson’s deal will also include a no-trade clause.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer believes “it would be a stunner” if Texans EDGE Will Anderson signed for less than $50 million per season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: The Texans and Anderson have been mutually interested in an extension for most of the offseason, though it hasn’t happened yet. The sticker shock is surely there reading "$50 million a year,” but it’s essentially no different than the $46 million that Micah Parsons got per season as part of his trade to the Packers given inflation. It shouldn’t surprise anyone when the deal comes in this high, but the rest of Houston’s offseason maneuverings (how much cap space do they still need available for 2026, etc) could be holding the extension up given just how large the contract will be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans exercised the fifth-year option for EDGE Will Anderson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson has been a star pass rusher since being drafted No. 3 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. He totaled 23 sacks over the past two seasons and was a First-Team All-Pro in 2025. With the fifth-year option, Anderson is now set to make $21.512 million in 2027. The Texans will certainly want to extend the 24-year-old as a cornerstone of the defense, but they get him under contract for an additional year for now. Anderson will be headed to reset the pass-rushing market with a prospective extension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports extending Will Anderson “is a priority” for the Texans this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson has totaled 23 sacks over the last two seasons and has wasted little time establishing himself as a premier pass-rusher in the league. The former No. 3 overall pick is entering the fourth-year of his contract and will have his fifth-year option picked at some point in the coming weeks. When he signs his deal, Anderson, 24, could reset the market for pass rushers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson (chest/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 14 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: He practiced in full on Friday and should be fine. In IDP leagues, it would be a disappointment if Anderson did not provide at least a half-sack or so against a Chiefs offensive line that looks likely to be down several starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Zachariah Branch, QB Andy Dalton, LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell WR, QB Jack Strand, CB Robert Longerbeam and OL Cameron Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It has been a disappointing rookie season for third-rounder Branch, who seemed like he might be in line for some first-year targets. Instead he has under 100 yards receiving and is now injured. A first-year washout like this makes Branch something of a dicey long-term prospect in Dynasty leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and enters Atlanta’s Week 11 bye off two completely lost weeks. The rookie hasn’t made much of an impact so far and doesn’t necessarily need to be kept on rosters in non-dynasty leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered the hamstring injury in Week 8 and missed last week’s game because of it. He appears to be on pace to miss another game. With just 10 catches to his name after nearly as many weeks, 2026 is shaping up to be an underwhelming start to Branch’s career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8’s shutout loss to the Buccaneers and will miss next week’s game against the Bengals in Madrid. The rookie third-rounder has caught just 10 passes for 64 scoreless yards this season and has also served as the Falcons’ primary kick and punt returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch’s primary duties still come on kick and punt returns, but Kevin Stefanski made it a point to get him more involved this week. He was held without a catch or even a target in Week 1. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but dynasty managers can be pleased with his role taking a step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch had no targets in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: On one hand, no targets is bad. On the other hand, Branch played one more snap than Olamide Zaccheaus and ran only three fewer routes. This is not a passing attack that you want pieces of right now, but there is a chance that Branch could take the WR3 role by the middle of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks is active for the Packers’ Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Running backs Josh Jacobs (thumb) and Pierre Strong are both out for this one, meaning the Packers will rely on the trio of Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson to handle backfield duties against a stout Vikings defense. Johnson “broke out” for 14-68-1 on the ground in last week’s win over the Patriots, but will be hard to trust this week given the multiple injuries it took for him to become fantasy relevant in Week 10. It could be best to avoid this situation altogether, especially with the Packers boasting one of the most explosive passing games in the league. The Packers declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OG Kevin Zeitler, and OL Sean Rhyan inactive for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers activated RB Chris Brooks and WR Skyy Moore from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks returns to a backfield once again without Josh Jacobs, appearing likely to serve as the preferred passing down back while Kaleb Johnson handles early-down duties. Moore remains unlikely to be consistently involved in the offense but brings a sizable boost to the special teams unit. The top duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should continue to dominate targets through the air for one of the most pass-heavy offenses in the league.
