https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks would have a chance to assume passing-down duties if he is activated off injured reserve. That would probably quash Pierre Strong’s value more than Marshawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson’s, but Brooks would probably be the favorite to see the most snaps among Green Bay’s runners if active. It would be a rough FLEX play against a good Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is questionable for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Lloyd popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the knee issue, and now appears to be a game-time decision. Chris Brooks (ankle) is also questionable for the Week 9 tilt, so there could be depth issues for the Pack behind Josh Jacobs, who has struggled in his return to action as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers designated Chris Brooks (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks is back at practice and could be officially activated from IR ahead of the Packers’ Week 9 matchup with the Patriots. He would likely take Pierre Strong’s spot in the lineup as Green Bay’s RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers placed RB Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks had been the most consistent contributor to a Green Bay backfield working to find their way in the absence of Josh Jacobs. The team appears likely to utilize journeyman Pierre Strong as the preferred passing down specialist, likely keeping the backfield in a maddening timeshare without Brooks. None are worthy of legitimate fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 5 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: This was foreshadowed a bit by the appearance of Pierre Strong Jr. on the roster. It’s unclear how the Packers will handle third-down reps between Strong, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd on Sunday. Strong was on the field for 138 passes of his 192 snaps in 2024 with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Matt LaFleur said earlier this morning that they were going to “give him another day and see where he’s at tomorrow and make a decision after that.” It sounds like there’s still a chance Brooks could play in Week 5, but he’ll likely be on the questionable line on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Spencer Brown (ankle) will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown had been questionable to play after not getting in any full practices during the week. The Bills’ right tackle went through an extensive pre-game workout before he and the team declared himself good to go. The Bills will have their full offensive line healthy for this matchup against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) is not on the Bills’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are both good to go this weekend. Bills RT Spencer Brown (ankle) is unfortunately doubtful to play. Overall, the Bills’ offensive line health is trending in the right direction, though. Bills CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Spencer Brown (back) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against Baltimore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown has a history of not practicing and getting up for the game on Sunday, so we wouldn’t necessarily read too far in to his two DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. That said, it also wouldn’t be surprising if Brown had to sit against the Ravens on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Spencer Brown (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown initially suffered the back injury in Week 5. He missed most of that game but was back on the field for Week 6. Coming out of the bye with a DNP today suggests the issue isn’t getting better. If Brown isn’t able to play this week, Tylan Grable will take his spot at right tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills TE Dawson Knox is not on Buffalo’s final Week 15 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Neither are Joey Bosa (hamstring/wrist) or Spencer Brown (shoulder) as the Bills look to be healthy in the trenches against the Patriots in a must-win game if they want any hope at the AFC East title this year. Joshua Palmer (ankle) is questionable after three limited sessions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills declared WR Joshua Palmer, OT Spencer Brown. OT Chase Lundt, DE Joey Bosa, DT Phidarian Mathis, LB Terrel Bernard, and S Darnell Savage inactive for Week 14 vs Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: The Bills’ offensive line held up well last weekend, even with Brown and left tackle Dion Dawkins (concussion) out. Dawkins is back for this one, but the Bills will still be down their starting right tackle in a snow game, where they could rely on James Cook and the rushing attack a lot. Joey Bosa continues to be week-to-week, but his loss is a big one for this pass rush, and Shaq Thompson will start again with Terrel Bernard out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 14 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown was limited in practice all three days this week. Buffalo has tended to be fairly conservative with Brown compared to how some teams treat their tackles — being limited is not a guarantee that Brown will play. Still, we’d bet on him being on the optimistic side of questionable after showing up at practice three days this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: He did, however, shed his non-contact jersey, so he may be closer to clearing concussion protocol. Dawkins and Spencer Brown (shoulder, limited for the second day in a row) are both trending towards playing on Sunday, or at least hitting the questionable line on Friday. It would do wonders for Buffalo’s offense to have their bookend tackles back on Sunday against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) also upgraded to limited. Both players were sidelined for the entirety of Week 13. The Bills face the Bengals’ pushover pass-rush unit in Week 14. Although the offense can likely get by without their starting offensive tackles, having them on the field would give Buffalo a significant edge in the trenches. Bills LB Terrel Bernard (elbow) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) will not play in Week 13 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Head coach Sean McDermott also ruled out RT Spencer Brown (shoulder), LB Terrel Bernard (elbow), and WR Curtis Samuel (elbow/knee), for Sunday’s contest. With both bookend tackles sidelined, the Bills will likely roll with Ryan Van Demark at left tackle and Chase Lundt at right tackle, which could make life tough for Josh Allen against a defense that has the fourth-highest blitz rate and fifth-highest sack total (34) this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Morgan Moses (knee) returned to the Patriots’ Week 10 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Moses limped off the field in the first quarter and immediately left for the locker room. He was briefly listed as questionable to return but managed to get back on the field in the second quarter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Morgan Moses (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Things are going from bad to worse for the Pats. Drake Maye left the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Moses then followed him to the locker room a few minutes later. Both are questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots ruled out Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: The Patriots will also be without RG Ben Brown (knee). The Bears’ defense is not an elite unit, but losing two starting guards is rough. Backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse will start instead. The Patriots listed RT Morgan Moses (foot) as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots RT Morgan Moses suffered an ankle injury in New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Moses went down early, but the Patriots waited until midway through the second half to rule him out. The move comes after LG Alijah Vera-Tucker was ruled out earlier with a hamstring issue. Not ideal, to put it mildly. Rookie first-rounder Caleb Lomu is finishing the game in Moses’ place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots C Garrett Bradbury (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Patriots OLB Anfernee Jennings (illness) and OT Morgan Moses (illness) resumed practicing in full. Patriots OT Vederian Lowe (illness) remained sidelined, and did DT Khyiris Tonga (foot). All ill players have a chance to play in the Patriots’ Wild Card Round game against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots C Garrett Bradbury (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Bradbury joins OLB Anfernee Jennings, OT Vederian Lowe, and OT Morgan Moses as players out with illness on Wednesday. The only non-illness absence on the active roster for the Pats was DT Khyiris Tonga (foot). Sitting with illness this early in the week generally does not mean the players will miss the game, but it is certainly a situation to keep an eye on for the Pats’ offensive line heading into the Wild Card round against the Chargers. Tonga is a key run stuffer that will have a couple more chances to practice ahead of Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots RT Morgan Moses (illness) is questionable to return to New England’s Week 12 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: The Patriots already lost starting left guard Jared Wilson to an injury on the first drive, so this would be a big blow to their offensive line. The Bengals have been able to get pressure on Drake Maye often to start this game, and that could continue if Moses can’t come back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots RT Morgan Moses (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: The last thing Drake Maye needed was to lose one of the bookends to his offensive line. Moses was brought in as a free agent to help improve one of the league’s worst lines in 2024. Though the veteran tackle is a few years past his prime, he was still set to be a stabilizing force for the unit. Losing Moses would be a tough blow for a New England offense that already came out flat-footed in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots OT Morgan Moses has been limited in OTAs after undergoing offseason knee surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: According to ESPN’s Mike Reiss, Moses had surgery to help correct a knee injury he suffered in Week 3 of last season. Moses missed two games as a result of the injury, but played through it for much of the year. In March, it was reported that Moses “was given a clean bill of health” by the Jets shortly before the team allowed him to hit free agency. Moses signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the Patriots this offseason and said he’s “just pacing things out” when asked about his limited participation in OTAs thus far. For now, this seems like a non-issue as training camp nears, but it will be something worth monitoring if the 34-year-old continues to be limited late into the summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots agreed to terms with OT Morgan Moses, formerly of the Jets, on a three-year, $24 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth up to $28.5 million. The Patriots fielded arguably the worst offensive line in the league last year, so it’s no surprise to see them spending big to improve that unit. Protecting Drake Maye has to be a priority for the rebuilding Pats this offseason. Even at 34 years old, Moses is a solid right tackle option for a team desperate to improve both bookends to their offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL and will undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: This was the expectation after Minshew severely injured his elbow in Week 9 against the Seahawks. His season is over after one incomplete start. Minshew threw for 354 yards and three scores in 2026. The surgery could sideline Minshew for over a year, meaning he may not play in 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals placed QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Officially he’ll miss at least four weeks, but Adam Schefter reports he’s not expected to play again this season, which essentially confirms that he tore his UCL without actually confirming it. There’s no current timeline for his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he did not consider benching Gardner Minshew for Carson Beck at any point in Arizona’s Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: We don’t believe him. But it really doesn’t matter because Beck will get his chance at some point in the coming weeks. The Cardinals’ rookie looked good in the preseason Hall of Fame game, though it is unclear whether he can do enough to warrant QB2 treatment as a pure pocket passer. The Cardinals’ schedule softens after matchups against the Rams and Chiefs over the next two weeks. Beck should have a chance to play in Week 12 against the Commanders, if not sooner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 21-of-30 passes for 166 yards in the Cardinals’ 17-3, Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, adding four yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: To be fair, the matchup in Week 9 was far different than the one Minshew erupted in last week, with the Seattle defense placing the clamps on the Cardinals from the first kick, holding them to just 198 total yards of offense on the down night. The only points mustered came on the team’s first possession, with three of their five first half possessions resulting in three-and-outs. The Cardinals saw the football only thrice following the break, getting stopped after achieving first and goal from the four on their final possession of the game. It was an outing to forget for all parties. Minshew remains likely to be the starting quarterback, at least in the immediate future, but the looking presence of rookie Carson Beck could be accelerated if the former returns more games like this one. Up next for the Cardinals are the Rams in Week 10, where Minshew will be nothing more than a streamer in two-quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew will start in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: After leading a second-half comeback against the Cowboys in which he threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-23 passing, the move to Minshew felt inevitable. Now, the eighth-year journeyman will have a chance to make his first start for the Cardinals in what’s sure to be a tough road matchup against the Seahawks. Minshew has long proved his value as a serviceable backup in the league and should provide enough to keep the fantasy stocks of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson up, but he could be in for a tough outing against a top-flight Seahawks defense. He shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation streamer in 2QB/superflex leagues, while Wilson’s expectations should fall somewhere in the WR3 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 17-of-23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns in Arizona’s 33-30, Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew appeared to get better blocking and be more accurate and on-time with his passes than Jacoby Brissett. He also got a few major long gains from Tyler Allgeier en route to rallying the Cardinals from a 17-3 deficit. Minshew should have had a walkoff 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds left, but kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point. In overtime, after an initial three-and-out, Minshew completed just one pass as Wilson and Allgeier ran the Cardinals into field-goal range for the win. Hard to see how the Cardinals would bench Minshew after how this looked, though he certainly shouldn’t be considered a firm rest-of-season starter just yet. Minshew Mania will likely figure into the QB2 superflex mix in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. One of Carolina’s biggest offseason additions, Phillips was off to a solid start to the year before going down. He had 2.5 sacks in five games, two of which he left early. Getting Phillips back will be a big win for the Panthers’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Carolina also ruled out left guard Damien Lewis, who is dealing with a knee issue. Phillips also missed last week’s game because of a hamstring injury. The hope is that the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football is enough to get him back for Week 9. Phillips has 2.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, after missing the previous two, with what the team is calling neurological symptoms. Whatever it is that Henderson is currently going through is clearly bigger than football. Rhamondre Stevenson is currently listed as questionable for Week 10 but is not expected to play, leaving the backfield in the hands of Corey Kiner in the immediate future. Here’s hoping for a speedy recovery for the electric running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson is dealing with an unexpected medical emergency right now. We would imagine he did not travel to Germany with the team. It’s unclear when he will return. With Rhamondre Stevenson also expected to miss Week 10, Corey Kiner is in line to see the bulk of the team’s backfield touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes TreVeyon Henderson’s illness might be related to the “adversity” he has faced this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Reiss was asked about Henderson’s status during his weekly appearance on the local radio show, Toucher & Hardy. According to Reiss, Henderson has faced a lot of new challenges this season, including recurring ankle issues and limited playing time, and the adversity has been tough for Henderson to deal with. Some might remember that similar reports surfaced regarding Bucky Irving, beset by multiple injuries, last season. Henderson might need more time before he resumes playing. Stay tuned. He was officially listed as a non-participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s rare for a player to miss even one game with an illness. It’s even more unheard of for them to miss the next practice. It’s possible Henderson is dealing with something more severe than the flu or a stomach bug. If he isn’t able to play in Week 9, Rhamondre Stevenson will handle the bulk of the backfield touches once again. He touched the ball 22 times on Sunday and would be in line for a similar workload against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson first popped on the injury report with a missed practice Thursday before maintaining that status to end the week, ultimately unable to play through the ailment while being ruled out Saturday. Rhamondre Stevenson steps into a potential workhorse role against the downtrodden Dolphins, where he will be an upside RB2 in Week 8. Expect the team to elevate another back from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game to play behind Stevenson and Corey Kiner, the latter of whom is expected to serve as the primary change of pace option with Henderson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is questionable for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson missed practice Thursday with an illness, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for the team’s Week 8 divisional clash with the Dolphins. That places fantasy managers in a precarious position considering the team plays in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate. It would be prudent to make alternate plans at FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers activated WR Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette will make his return to a passing offense currently dominated by Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, and tight end Darren Waller, unlikely to return a usable fantasy score in his first game since Week 2. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the plus matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette has missed the past six games but could join the active squad for the first time since Week 2. Even if he returns this week, the third-year wideout may have trouble carving out a fantasy-relevant receiving role every week behind Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble, and running back Chuba Hubbard. However, even in this crowded picture, the 25-year-old could warrant a stash in some deep leagues for those craving anyone with upside at wide receiver. His added presence could help Bryce Young’s fantasy value as the season goes on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the team is weighing whether or not to open Jonathon Brooks (core) return window this week
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Canales said the oft-injured Brooks still has “some things to clear recovery-wise” but noted that he could still have his practice window opened this week. Brooks suffered a core muscle injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and handled just 11 touches in his first two games of the year. Given his injury history, it’s hard to know how close he could truly be to dressing on game day, but even when he does return, we would still expect Chuba Hubbard to handle the majority of touches given how efficient he has been this season. In addition to Brooks, Canales said the team is also weighing when to open the return window for Xavier Legette, who has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers placed WR Xavier Legette (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette was already ruled out for Week 4, which marks his second straight absence. He will now be forced to miss the next four games while on injured reserve, making his absence a total of five games, at minimum. John Metchie and Brycen Tremaine will continue to operate as the WR3 in the interim.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) will not play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette will miss a second straight game with his knee injury. He has caught just two passes for 64 yards on six targets this season and wouldn’t be on the fantasy radar even if he were active. In addition to Legette, the Panthers also ruled out OG Damien Lewis (elbow) for Week 4 against the Lions while OT Monroe Freeling (concussion), DT Lee Hunter (foot), and DT Cam Jackson (knee) were all listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales said WR Xavier Legette (knee) is week-to-week, while Coker “is more day-to-day.” Canales adds that the team “has to see Coker move around before he returns to action.” Coker remains firmly in the questionable camp at this time. He might have a chance to play in Week 4 against the Lions, but fantasy managers should make a serious backup plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is inactive for Week 3 vs. the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Jalen Coker (ankle), meanwhile, is active. Legette made a big catch in Week 2, but he’s one of the only boats not rising with the tide of the Panthers’ ascending offense. He is off the radar in 12-team league fantasy, especially now that he’s injured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Coker (ankle) “should play” in Week 3 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Xavier Legette (knee) remains a game-time decision. Both players were officially listed as questionable on Friday. Coker has gotten off to a red-hot start this year with 16 grabs for 204 yards and a pair of scores through two weeks. Even if he’s limited by the ankle issue, the production is too good to keep on the bench. He is, at worst, a WR3 for his date with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Xavier Legette (knee) will likely be a game-day decision for Week 3 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a DNP and was limited on Friday. The third-year receiver underwent an MRI, but it doesn’t sound like it revealed anything too concerning given his practice status for Friday. Even if he is active, Legette isn’t on the fantasy radar this week. He’s managed just two receptions for 64 yards on four targets so far this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys placed RB Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: It’s yet another blow to the depth of a backfield devastated by injuries this season, leaving lead back Javonte Williams again positioned well to see a workhorse role against the 49ers. The team elevated running back Israel Abanikanda in an associated move, who is likely to serve as the primary change of pace option in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys ruled out Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: The Cowboys will be without their No. 2 running back, removing what little threat there was to Javonte Williams’ workload. Goodson should remain stashed on 12-team benches if possible, though he could miss next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said RB Tyler Goodson (knee) is expected to miss some time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys’ RB2 this season, and rushed 12 times for 77 yards in Week 9’s win over the Colts. He played through the knee injury he suffered in the second quarter. The fact that he played through the injury suggests this isn’t anything too serious, but it’s not uncommon to see players be sidelined in the following weeks once the adrenaline has worn off and the game is over. We’ll likely get a clearer timeline for his return in the coming days, but for now, it looks like Israel Abanikanda and/or Jashaun Corbin will be promoted from the practice squad, with Javonte Williams being the only healthy back on Dallas’ roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Tyler Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson saw solid work early against the Colts, effectively rotating drives with starter Javonte Williams before injuring his knee in the second quarter. He was deemed questionable to return by the team after amassing 44 yards on seven carries, but returned to rotate in with Williams in the third quarter, adding an additional 33 yards after the break. Goodson could carry viable FLEX value if the Cowboys continue forward with a run-heavy approach, as they have the previous three games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Tyler Goodson rushed seven times for 14 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona, adding two catches for 19 yards on his only two targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: He found 20-of-74 running back snaps against the Cardinals; not bad work but nothing that is making you consider a waiver claim either. Goodson should be held in deeper leagues as a contingency stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Tyler Goodson has had the RB2 role for the past couple of weeks and is set to continue now that Demercado was waived to make room for Tyler Smith to come off injured reserve. Demercado has now been waived twice in two months, and though he may be claimed again, he could also wind up on a practice squad next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports the Cowboys are signing RB Tyler Goodson off the Falcons’ practice-squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson will backfill the roster spot lost to placing Malik Davis on IR at the end of last week. It’s unclear whether Emari Demercado or Goodson would be the head of a committee if Javonte Williams were injured, as both of them showed up with the Cowboys after last cuts. Neither player is a must-roster as things stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons released RB Tyler Goodson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson made an impact as part of the Falcons’ running back room in the preseason but ultimately Brian Robinson Jr. will keep the backup job. Also waived/released by the Falcons were CB Darnay Holmes, DT Eric Johnson II, TE Nick Muse, OLB Azeez Ojulari, DE Cam Sample, LB Channing Tindall, DT Marlon Tuipulotu, OL Brandon Walton, DL Chris Williams, LB Josh Woods, DT Carlos Allen, WR Vinny Anthony, OL James Brockermeyer, CB Cobee Bryant, RB Nate Carter, OL Kam Dewberry, WR Dylan Drummond, RB Cash Jones, OL Riley Mahlman, WR Keelan Marion, DT Devonnsha Maxwell, OT Wanya Morris, LB Daveren Rayner, OL Jaeden Roberts, TE Joshua Simon, DB Keidron Smith, OL Andrew Stueber, LB Bralen Trice, TE Jack Velling, WR Antwane Wells Jr., and CB A.J. Woods.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons signed RB Tyler Goodson, formerly of the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson was slated to be a restricted free agent, but the Colts balked. He’s a decent third-down back, but behind Bijan Robinson he figures to offer little fantasy value in his age-26 season. At least his last name isn’t also “Robinson,” unlike some backups in this backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: DJ Giddens rushed eight times for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 18 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: It was the first time Giddens saw any real work since Week 1, where he spelled Jonathan Taylor late in a blowout win over the Dolphins. With Tyler Goodson (one carry, three yards) set to become a restricted free agent in 2026, Giddens will enter the offseason No. 2 on the depth chart. He hasn’t shown much so far, but how could he? He had only 18 carries all season before this game as Taylor stayed incredibly healthy, and those 18 carries were the most among Indy’s backup runners.
